## Multi-Gesture Interactions — Pinch, Zoom, and Long Press  [community]

Beyond `browser.swipe()`, several gestures require the W3C Actions API or WDIO v9's high-level
mobile gesture helpers.

```typescript
// test/helpers/gestureHelper.ts — production-grade gesture utilities

/**
 * Perform a pinch-to-zoom gesture on an element.
 * Uses the iOS mobile:pinch XCUITest command or WDIO v9 W3C pointer actions on Android.
 *
 * @param element - Target element to pinch
 * @param scale   - Pinch scale (< 1 = zoom out / pinch in, > 1 = zoom in / spread)
 * @param speed   - Animation speed in ms (default: 500)
 */
export async function pinchElement(
  element: WebdriverIO.Element,
  scale: number,
  speed = 500,
): Promise<void> {
  if (browser.isIOS) {
    // iOS: use mobile:pinch XCUITest command for reliable simulator gesture
    await driver.execute('mobile: pinch', {
      element: element.elementId,
      scale,
      velocity: scale < 1 ? -1 : 1,  // negative = zoom out, positive = zoom in
    });
  } else {
    // Android: WDIO v9 element.pinch() translates to W3C pointer actions
    await (element as any).pinch({ scale, speed });
  }
}

/**
 * Long-press an element for a specified duration.
 * Normalises iOS (seconds) and Android (ms) semantics.
 *
 * @param selector   - WDIO selector string
 * @param durationMs - Hold duration in milliseconds (minimum 800ms on Android)
 */
export async function longPressElement(
  selector: string,
  durationMs = 1000,
): Promise<void> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  await el.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

  if (browser.isIOS) {
    await driver.execute('mobile: touchAndHold', {
      element: el.elementId,
      duration: durationMs / 1000,  // XCUITest uses seconds, not ms
    });
  } else {
    // Android: W3C pointer actions for precise duration control
    const { x, y } = await el.getLocation();
    const { width, height } = await el.getSize();
    const cx = Math.round(x + width / 2);
    const cy = Math.round(y + height / 2);

    await browser.action('pointer', { parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' } })
      .move({ x: cx, y: cy })
      .down()
      .pause(durationMs)
      .up()
      .perform();
  }
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/map-gestures.spec.ts — map zoom test using pinch helper
import { pinchElement, longPressElement } from '../helpers/gestureHelper.js';

describe('Map screen gestures', () => {
  before(async () => {
    await $('~map-tab').click();
    await $('~map-container').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
  });

  it('should zoom in on the map with a spread gesture', async () => {
    const map = await $('~map-container');
    const zoomLevelBefore = await $('~zoom-level-label').getText();
    await pinchElement(map, 2.0, 600);  // spread (zoom in)
    await browser.waitUntil(async () => {
      const zoomAfter = await $('~zoom-level-label').getText();
      return zoomAfter !== zoomLevelBefore;
    }, { timeout: 5_000, timeoutMsg: 'Map zoom level did not change after pinch gesture' });
  });

  it('should show context menu on long press', async () => {
    await longPressElement('~map-container', 1500);
    await expect($('~context-menu')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
  });
});
```

**[community] `mobile: pinch` on iOS Simulator with Xcode 15+ requires the Simulator window to be
in focus — background Simulator sessions silently skip the gesture without error:** WHY: XCUITest's
gesture synthesis requires the Simulator UI window to be the frontmost application. In headless CI
on macOS GitHub Actions runners, gestures may be silently ignored. Fix: verify the Simulator is
responsive by checking for animation completion rather than polling a zoom level numeric value;
add `await browser.pause(300)` after app foreground to ensure focus before performing gestures.

**[community] W3C pointer action `durationMs` on Android must be ≥ 500 ms for UIAutomator2 to
register a long press — 800 ms is the safest cross-device minimum:** WHY: UIAutomator2's long-press
threshold varies by manufacturer — Samsung defaults to 600 ms, stock Android to 500 ms. A 300 ms
hold that passes on Pixel will be treated as a tap on Samsung S24. Fix: use 800–1000 ms as the
default and define it as a named constant in a shared `GESTURE_CONSTANTS` object.

## Sauce Labs — GitHub Actions Full CI Workflow  [community]

```yaml
# .github/workflows/mobile-sauce.yml — Sauce Labs real-device CI
name: Mobile E2E — Sauce Labs

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'release/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  upload-app:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      ios_app_id: ${{ steps.upload_ios.outputs.app_id }}
      android_app_id: ${{ steps.upload_android.outputs.app_id }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Upload iOS app to Sauce Storage
        id: upload_ios
        run: |
          APP_ID=$(curl -sf -u "${{ secrets.SAUCE_USERNAME }}:${{ secrets.SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY }}" \
            -X POST \
            "https://api.us-west-1.saucelabs.com/v1/storage/upload" \
            -F "payload=@./build/MyApp.ipa" \
            -F "name=MyApp-${{ github.sha }}.ipa" \
            | jq -r '.item.id')
          echo "app_id=$APP_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Upload Android app to Sauce Storage
        id: upload_android
        run: |
          APP_ID=$(curl -sf -u "${{ secrets.SAUCE_USERNAME }}:${{ secrets.SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY }}" \
            -X POST \
            "https://api.us-west-1.saucelabs.com/v1/storage/upload" \
            -F "payload=@./build/MyApp.apk" \
            -F "name=MyApp-${{ github.sha }}.apk" \
            | jq -r '.item.id')
          echo "app_id=$APP_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  e2e-sauce:
    needs: upload-app
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        platform: [ios, android]
      fail-fast: false  # run both platforms even if one fails
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.19.0'
          cache: 'npm'

      - run: npm ci

      - name: Run E2E on Sauce Labs (${{ matrix.platform }})
        env:
          SAUCE_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.SAUCE_USERNAME }}
          SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY }}
          SAUCE_APP_ID: ${{ matrix.platform == 'ios' && needs.upload-app.outputs.ios_app_id || needs.upload-app.outputs.android_app_id }}
          PLATFORM: ${{ matrix.platform }}
          GITHUB_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: npx wdio run wdio.conf.sauce.ts --suite ${{ matrix.platform }}

      - name: Upload test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: test-results-${{ matrix.platform }}
          path: ./test-results/*.xml
```

**[community] Sauce Labs `storage:` app reference (`storage:<app_id>`) is permanent but app files
expire after 60 days of inactivity — long-lived feature branches may reference expired app IDs:**
WHY: Sauce Storage has a 60-day inactivity TTL. An app uploaded for a feature branch 3 months ago
will 404 on revival. Fix: always upload a fresh build at workflow trigger time rather than reusing
a cached ID from a previous run; treat the app hash as a build artefact that lives and dies with
the CI run.

**[community] `fail-fast: false` in the GitHub Actions matrix is critical for mobile CI — a single
device cloud outage should not cancel all platform runs:** WHY: Sauce Labs occasionally has regional
incidents affecting one device type (e.g. iOS real devices) while Android remains healthy. With
`fail-fast: true` (the default), the Android job is cancelled as soon as the iOS job fails, giving
you no signal on Android regressions. Fix: always use `fail-fast: false` for cross-platform mobile
CI matrices so you get full signal on every PR.

## Appium 2.x Plugin System — Installation, Usage & Custom Plugins  [community]

Appium 2.x introduced a first-class plugin architecture. Plugins intercept and extend Appium's
command handling without forking the server. They install into the Appium server process (not
into test code) and are declared at server startup.

### Plugin CLI quick reference

```bash
# List all installed plugins
appium plugin list

# Install an official plugin from npm
appium plugin install --source npm appium-wait-plugin
appium plugin install --source npm @appium/device-farm
appium plugin install --source npm appium-gestures-plugin

# Install a plugin from a local path (development)
appium plugin install --source local /path/to/my-plugin

# Install a plugin from a GitHub repo
appium plugin install --source github appium/appium-wait-plugin

# Uninstall a plugin
appium plugin uninstall appium-wait-plugin

# Update a plugin to the latest version
appium plugin update appium-wait-plugin
```

### Activating plugins at server startup

Plugins must be explicitly activated with `--use-plugins` — installing alone is not enough:

```bash
# Start Appium with one plugin
appium --use-plugins=appium-wait-plugin

# Start with multiple plugins (comma-separated)
appium --use-plugins=appium-wait-plugin,appium-gestures-plugin
```

In `@wdio/appium-service`, pass plugins via `appiumArgs`:

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — activate plugins via the WDIO Appium service
export const config: Options.Testrunner = {
  services: [
    ['appium', {
      appiumArgs: {
        port: 4723,
        'base-path': '/',
        'use-plugins': 'appium-wait-plugin,appium-gestures-plugin',
        // If a plugin requires allowInsecure, add it here:
        // 'allow-insecure': 'appium-wait-plugin:*',
      },
    }],
  ],
};
```

### `appium-wait-plugin` — automatic implicit waiting

The wait plugin removes the need for `waitForDisplayed()` in every test. It intercepts
`findElement` calls and retries automatically until the element appears or the timeout expires.

```typescript
// Without plugin (explicit wait required every time):
await $('~submitButton').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
await $('~submitButton').click();

// With appium-wait-plugin active (no explicit wait needed):
await $('~submitButton').click();  // plugin handles the wait automatically

// Override wait settings per-test at runtime:
await driver.execute('plugin: setWaitPluginProperties', {
  timeout: 20_000,          // ms — override server default for this session
  intervalBetweenAttempts: 500,  // ms between retries
});
```

Server startup for the wait plugin:

```bash
appium --use-plugins=appium-wait-plugin \
  --plugin-element-wait-timeout=15000 \
  --plugin-element-wait-interval-between-attempts=300
```

**[community] `appium-wait-plugin` masks root-cause flakiness — elements that require explicit
waiting are often symptoms of race conditions or animation timing issues in the app itself:**
WHY: The plugin hides missing waits by retrying silently. A test that passes only because the
plugin waited 14 seconds for an element is inherently slow. Fix: use the plugin as a safety net
during initial test authoring, but profile slow tests with `trackSelectorPerformance` and add
targeted `waitForDisplayed` calls to the worst offenders.

**[community] The wait plugin does NOT apply to `$$()` (multi-element queries) — only single
element `$()` finds are intercepted:** WHY: The plugin hooks `findElement` (W3C singular) but
not `findElements` (W3C plural). Calling `$$('~item').length` will return 0 immediately if
elements haven't appeared yet. Fix: call a single `$()` first to wait, then call `$$()` to
collect all matching elements.

**[community] Plugins must be re-activated after upgrading Appium — `appium plugin update`
updates the plugin package but does NOT add it to `--use-plugins` if the startup flags changed:**
WHY: The `--use-plugins` flag is ephemeral (CLI-only). If your CI startup script hardcodes
plugin names, adding a new plugin requires updating both `appium plugin install` and
`--use-plugins`. Fix: manage plugins in `.appiumrc.json` using the `"plugin"` key so
installation and activation stay in sync.

### `appium-gestures-plugin` — higher-level mobile gestures

The gestures plugin exposes high-level gesture commands not available in the standard Appium
protocol, avoiding the complexity of raw W3C pointer actions.

```typescript
// Scroll to an element by accessibility ID (iOS + Android unified)
await driver.execute('gesture: scrollToElement', {
  elementId: await $('~targetItem').getElement().then(el => el.elementId),
  direction: 'down',
  maxScrolls: 10,
});

// Perform a free-form swipe gesture (plugin handles W3C actions internally)
await driver.execute('gesture: swipe', {
  direction: 'left',        // 'left' | 'right' | 'up' | 'down'
  percent: 0.75,            // swipe 75% of the screen width/height
  speed: 1000,              // pixels per second
});

// Long-press on an element with precise duration control
await driver.execute('gesture: longPress', {
  elementId: await $('~contextMenuTrigger').getElement().then(el => el.elementId),
  duration: 2000,           // ms
});
```

**[community] `appium-gestures-plugin` requires `appium:automationName` to be either
`UiAutomator2` (Android) or `XCUITest` (iOS) — it does NOT work with Espresso or other drivers
because it uses driver-specific scroll primitives under the hood:** WHY: The plugin maps
`gesture: scrollToElement` to `mobile: scroll` on iOS (XCUITest) and `mobile: scrollGesture`
on Android (UiAutomator2). Both commands are driver-specific. Fix: check your `automationName`
capability before enabling the plugin; on Espresso, use `mobile: scrollToPage` directly.

### Custom Appium plugin skeleton (TypeScript)

For teams that need to extend Appium with project-specific behavior (e.g. custom logging,
test fixture injection, or proprietary device management):

```typescript
// my-custom-plugin/index.ts
import type BasePlugin from '@appium/base-plugin';

// Custom plugin that logs all click commands with a timestamp
export default class TimestampLogPlugin extends (require('@appium/base-plugin') as typeof BasePlugin) {
  static pluginName = 'timestamp-log';

  // Intercept 'click' before it reaches the driver
  async click(
    next: () => Promise<unknown>,
    driver: unknown,
    ...args: unknown[]
  ): Promise<unknown> {
    const start = Date.now();
    console.log(`[timestamp-log] click started at ${new Date(start).toISOString()}`);
    const result = await next();
    console.log(`[timestamp-log] click completed in ${Date.now() - start}ms`);
    return result;
  }
}
```

```json
// package.json for the custom plugin
{
  "name": "my-appium-timestamp-plugin",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "appium": {
    "pluginName": "timestamp-log",
    "mainClass": "TimestampLogPlugin"
  }
}
```

```bash
# Install and activate the local plugin
appium plugin install --source local ./my-custom-plugin
appium --use-plugins=timestamp-log
```

## Mobile Accessibility Testing — iOS VoiceOver & Android TalkBack  [community]

Accessibility testing ensures your app is usable by people with visual, motor, and cognitive
disabilities. On mobile, this means verifying your app works correctly with iOS VoiceOver and
Android TalkBack screen readers.

### Checking accessibility labels and roles natively

```typescript
// test/specs/accessibility.spec.ts
describe('Accessibility label validation', () => {
  it('should have accessible labels on all interactive elements', async () => {
    // iOS: accessibilityLabel maps to the ~accessibility-id selector
    // Android: contentDescription maps to the ~accessibility-id selector

    const submitBtn = $('~submit-button');
    await submitBtn.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    // Verify the accessibility label is meaningful (not empty, not the raw ID)
    const label = await submitBtn.getAttribute('label');      // iOS
    const desc  = await submitBtn.getAttribute('content-desc'); // Android

    const accessibleText = browser.isIOS ? label : desc;
    expect(accessibleText).toBeTruthy();
    expect(accessibleText).not.toMatch(/^\d+$|^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/i); // not a UUID/raw ID
  });

  it('should have correct accessibility role for the login button', async () => {
    const role = await $('~login-button').getComputedRole();
    // Computed role uses WAI-ARIA roles derived from the element type
    expect(role).toBe('button');
  });

  it('should report all interactive elements as enabled', async () => {
    const interactiveElements = await $$('android.widget.Button');
    for (const el of interactiveElements) {
      const enabled = await el.getAttribute('enabled');
      // Fail if a visible button is unexpectedly disabled
      expect(enabled).toBe('true');
    }
  });
});
```

### iOS: Verifying element traits (by.traits equivalent via `mobile: getElementAttribute`)

On iOS, XCUITest exposes accessibility traits (`.button`, `.link`, `.selected`, `.header`, etc.)
that screen readers use to describe elements. Verify them to catch regressions in accessibility
markup:

```typescript
// iOS-specific accessibility trait verification
async function getElementTraits(element: WebdriverIO.Element): Promise<string[]> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) return [];
  const traitsRaw = await element.getAttribute('traits') ?? '';
  // XCUITest returns a comma-separated list: "button,selected"
  return traitsRaw.split(',').map((t) => t.trim()).filter(Boolean);
}

it('should have button trait on the CTA', async () => {
  const cta = $('~call-to-action-button');
  const traits = await getElementTraits(await cta);
  expect(traits).toContain('button');
});

it('image decorations should have none trait (not interactive)', async () => {
  const decoration = $('~decorative-illustration');
  const traits = await getElementTraits(await decoration);
  // Decorative images should have 'image' but NOT 'button' or 'link'
  expect(traits).not.toContain('button');
  expect(traits).not.toContain('link');
});
```

### Android: Verifying content descriptions are not empty for images

```typescript
// Android accessibility audit: check all ImageViews have content descriptions
it('should have content descriptions on all images', async () => {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) return;

  const images = await $$('android.widget.ImageView');
  const missing: string[] = [];

  for (const img of images) {
    const cd = await img.getAttribute('content-desc');
    const resId = await img.getAttribute('resource-id');
    // Some images are decorative and legitimately have no CD (check importantForAccessibility)
    const importanceAttr = await img.getAttribute('important-for-accessibility');
    if (!cd && importanceAttr !== 'no') {
      missing.push(resId ?? 'unknown-resource-id');
    }
  }

  expect(missing).toEqual([]);
});
```

### axe-core integration for WebView accessibility scanning

For hybrid apps with WebView components, integrate `axe-core` to run WCAG 2.1 AA audits:

```typescript
// test/helpers/axeHelper.ts
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/webdriverio';

/**
 * Run an axe accessibility audit on the current WebView context.
 * Returns the violations array — empty means no issues found.
 */
export async function runAxeOnWebView(
  contextSelector?: string,
): Promise<import('axe-core').Result[]> {
  // Must be in WEBVIEW context before calling this
  const axeBuilder = new AxeBuilder({ client: browser as never });

  if (contextSelector) {
    axeBuilder.include(contextSelector);
  }

  // Focus on WCAG 2.1 AA
  axeBuilder.withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa']);

  const results = await axeBuilder.analyze();
  return results.violations;
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/webview-accessibility.spec.ts
import { runAxeOnWebView } from '../helpers/axeHelper.js';

describe('WebView WCAG accessibility', () => {
  before(async () => {
    await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');
  });

  after(async () => {
    await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
  });

  it('should have no WCAG 2.1 AA violations on the dashboard', async () => {
    await browser.url('/dashboard');
    await $('[data-testid="dashboard-content"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    const violations = await runAxeOnWebView();

    if (violations.length > 0) {
      const report = violations
        .map((v) => `[${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description}`)
        .join('\n');
      throw new Error(`axe found ${violations.length} WCAG violations:\n${report}`);
    }
  });

  it('should have no colour-contrast failures on product cards', async () => {
    const violations = await runAxeOnWebView('[data-testid="product-card"]');
    const contrastViolations = violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'color-contrast');
    expect(contrastViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

Install dependencies:

```bash
npm install --save-dev @axe-core/webdriverio axe-core
```

**[community] `@axe-core/webdriverio` version must match `axe-core` version exactly — version
skew causes silent false negatives (no violations reported even when issues exist):** WHY:
`@axe-core/webdriverio` injects the `axe.min.js` script from the `axe-core` package. If the two
packages are at different minor versions, the injected script API doesn't match the results
parser, and analysis returns `violations: []` silently. Fix: always pin both to the same version:
`"axe-core": "4.9.x", "@axe-core/webdriverio": "4.9.x"`.

**[community] axe runs inside the WebView context — you MUST call `switchContext('WEBVIEW_...')`
before `axeBuilder.analyze()` or you'll get `TypeError: browser.executeScript is not a function`:**
WHY: `@axe-core/webdriverio` uses `browser.executeScript()` which is a web context command. In
native Appium context, WebDriver protocol doesn't expose `executeScript`. Fix: always switch to
the WebView context before running axe, and switch back afterward.

**[community] Long axe analyses time out on large WebView pages — default WDIO `commandTimeout`
(30 s) is too short for complex single-page apps:** WHY: axe traverses the full DOM including
shadow roots and iframes. On a dashboard with hundreds of components, the `analyze()` call can
take 40+ seconds. Fix: increase `connectionRetryTimeout` in `wdio.conf.ts` to 120 s for tests
that include axe scans.

## BrowserStack Real Device Testing — Full WDIO v9 TypeScript Configuration  [community]

BrowserStack App Automate provides 3000+ real iOS and Android devices. The `@wdio/browserstack-service`
handles session tagging, test observability, and local tunnel management.

### Installation

```bash
npm install --save-dev @wdio/browserstack-service
```

### Complete `wdio.conf.browserstack.ts`

```typescript
// wdio.conf.browserstack.ts
import type { Options } from '@wdio/types';
import { uploadAppToBrowserStack } from './test/helpers/bsUpload.js';

const BS_USER = process.env.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME!;
const BS_KEY  = process.env.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY!;
const BUILD   = process.env.CI_BUILD_NUMBER ?? `local-${Date.now()}`;

// Upload app once and share the bs:// URL across all parallel sessions
const IOS_APP_URL     = process.env.BS_IOS_APP_URL     ?? await uploadAppToBrowserStack('./build/MyApp.ipa');
const ANDROID_APP_URL = process.env.BS_ANDROID_APP_URL ?? await uploadAppToBrowserStack('./build/MyApp.apk');

export const config: Options.Testrunner = {
  user: BS_USER,
  key:  BS_KEY,
  hostname: 'hub-cloud.browserstack.com',
  port: 443,
  protocol: 'https',
  path: '/wd/hub',

  services: [
    ['browserstack', {
      browserstackLocal: false,       // set true for localhost/staging APIs
      testObservability: true,        // enables BrowserStack Observability dashboard
      testObservabilityOptions: {
        projectName: 'My Mobile App',
        buildName:   `CI Build #${BUILD}`,
        buildTag:    process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME ?? 'local',
      },
      sessionNameFormat: (config, capabilities, suiteTitle, testTitle) =>
        `${testTitle} | ${(capabilities as WebdriverIO.Capabilities)['bstack:options']?.deviceName}`,
    }],
  ],

  maxInstances: 5,   // BrowserStack parallel concurrency (adjust per subscription tier)

  capabilities: [
    // iOS — real iPhone
    {
      platformName: 'iOS',
      'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
      'appium:app': IOS_APP_URL,
      'bstack:options': {
        deviceName:      'iPhone 15 Pro',
        osVersion:       '17',
        projectName:     'My Mobile App',
        buildName:       `CI Build #${BUILD}`,
        sessionName:     'iOS E2E',
        debug:           true,   // enables visual logs on BrowserStack dashboard
        networkLogs:     true,
        appiumLogs:      true,
      },
    },
    // Android — real device
    {
      platformName: 'Android',
      'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
      'appium:app': ANDROID_APP_URL,
      'bstack:options': {
        deviceName:      'Samsung Galaxy S24',
        osVersion:       '14.0',
        projectName:     'My Mobile App',
        buildName:       `CI Build #${BUILD}`,
        sessionName:     'Android E2E',
        debug:           true,
        networkLogs:     true,
        appiumLogs:      true,
      },
    },
  ],

  specs: ['test/specs/**/*.spec.ts'],

  mochaOpts: {
    timeout: 120_000,  // BrowserStack sessions have network latency — increase timeout
  },
};
```

### App upload helper

```typescript
// test/helpers/bsUpload.ts
import { readFileSync } from 'fs';
import { basename } from 'path';

/**
 * Upload an app binary to BrowserStack App Storage.
 * Returns the bs:// URL to use as the `appium:app` capability.
 * Caches results to avoid re-uploading on retries.
 */
export async function uploadAppToBrowserStack(localPath: string): Promise<string> {
  const user = process.env.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME!;
  const key  = process.env.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY!;

  const body = new FormData();
  body.append('file', new Blob([readFileSync(localPath)]), basename(localPath));

  const response = await fetch(
    'https://api-cloud.browserstack.com/app-automate/upload',
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${user}:${key}`).toString('base64')}`,
      },
      body,
    },
  );

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`BrowserStack app upload failed: ${response.status} ${await response.text()}`);
  }

  const data = await response.json() as { app_url: string };
  console.log(`[BrowserStack] Uploaded app: ${data.app_url}`);
  return data.app_url;
}
```

### Using regex for flexible device selection

```typescript
// BrowserStack supports regex in deviceName and osVersion for flexible allocation
capabilities: [
  {
    platformName: 'Android',
    'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
    'appium:app': ANDROID_APP_URL,
    'bstack:options': {
      // Any available Samsung Galaxy S series running Android 13 or 14
      deviceName: 'Samsung Galaxy S.*',
      osVersion:  '1[34]',
    },
  },
],
```

**[community] BrowserStack sessions time out after 300 s of inactivity — set
`appium:newCommandTimeout: 0` in capabilities to disable the driver-level timeout and rely only
on BrowserStack's session-level limit:** WHY: With two independent timeouts, the shorter one wins.
If your test has a `browser.pause(30000)` debugging line left in, the Appium server times out
first (default 60 s), not BrowserStack's 300 s. Fix: set `'appium:newCommandTimeout': 0` in
your BrowserStack capabilities to disable the Appium-level timeout and use only BrowserStack's
session timeout as the upper bound.

**[community] BrowserStack `testObservability: true` requires `@wdio/browserstack-service >= 8.x`
— older v7.x service versions silently ignore the `testObservabilityOptions` block:** WHY: The
Observability API was added in service v8. If you upgraded `webdriverio` to v9 but left
`@wdio/browserstack-service` at v7, the options are valid TypeScript but do nothing at runtime.
Fix: always upgrade all `@wdio/*` packages together: `npm install @wdio/browserstack-service@latest`.

**[community] `bs://` app URLs expire after 60 days (same as Sauce Labs storage) — automation
pipelines that cache app URLs across branches will fail after expiry with `App not found` error:**
WHY: BrowserStack's App Storage lifecycle is 60 days from last access. An app uploaded for a
long-lived feature branch may reference an expired ID when the branch is rebased months later.
Fix: always re-upload the app binary at pipeline start time; treat `bs://` URLs as ephemeral
build artefacts, not long-term references.

**[community] `browserstackLocal: true` starts a BrowserStack Local tunnel process — if the tunnel
binary is not in PATH or the firewall blocks the tunnel port (45691), sessions fail with
`Could not connect to BrowserStack Local`:** WHY: The `@wdio/browserstack-service` downloads and
launches `BrowserStackLocal` as a subprocess. Corporate firewalls often block the tunnel port.
Fix: pre-download the tunnel binary as a CI artefact; verify port 45691 is open on the CI network;
set `opts.forceLocal: true` to force all traffic through the tunnel even for publicly accessible URLs.

### Pattern 238 — Appium 3.4.0: Global Privacy Control + Storage Access WebDriver Endpoints

Appium 3.4.0 (released 2026-05-06) added three new WebDriver extension endpoints defined by
W3C External Specifications: `getGlobalPrivacyControl`, `setGlobalPrivacyControl`, and
`getStorageAccess`. These allow tests to verify and manipulate privacy/storage-access state in
mobile browsers and WebViews — completing full WebDriver spec compliance.

```typescript
// Global Privacy Control: verify GPC header is respected by the app's WebView
it('should honour Global Privacy Control opt-out', async () => {
  // Navigate to a WebView page that reads the GPC signal
  await driver.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');

  // Set GPC signal to opt-out (true = user has requested no tracking)
  await driver.setGlobalPrivacyControl(true);

  // Reload to let the page re-read navigator.globalPrivacyControl
  await driver.url('https://privacy.example.com/status');

  const gpcStatus = await driver.$('#gpc-status').getText();
  expect(gpcStatus).toContain('opted-out');

  // Restore for next test
  await driver.setGlobalPrivacyControl(false);
  await driver.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});

// Storage Access: test that third-party content requests storage access
it('should detect storage access request in embedded iframe', async () => {
  await driver.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');

  // getStorageAccess returns whether the current browsing context
  // has been granted storage access by the user
  const hasAccess: boolean = await driver.getStorageAccess(
    'https://thirdparty.example.com',
    'https://firstparty.example.com'
  );
  expect(hasAccess).toBe(false); // first load — no grant yet
});
```

**[community] `setGlobalPrivacyControl` only affects the browser/WebView context — calling it
in `NATIVE_APP` context throws `UnsupportedCommandError`: WHY: GPC is a WebDriver BiDi-level
signal that applies to browser-land, not native app code. Always switch context before calling
it. Add a guard: `if ((await driver.getContext()).startsWith('WEBVIEW'))` before calling.**

**[community] `getGlobalPrivacyControl` returns the *Appium driver's* current setting, not the
device OS privacy preference — it cannot read the system-level "Global Privacy Control" toggle
in iOS 18 Settings Privacy Tracking:** WHY: The WebDriver spec endpoint is per-session
state only. To test OS-level GPC signals, use `mobile:simctl` privacy commands on iOS or
Android's `PackageInstaller` consent flows instead.

**[community] `getStorageAccess` requires Appium 3.4.0 + a driver that supports the Storage
Access API — UIAutomator2 v7.2+ and XCUITest v11.2+ are required; older drivers return
`UnknownCommandError` silently treated as `false` by some test runners:** WHY: The command is
proxied through to the underlying driver. Mismatched Appium server + driver versions silently
degrade. Always pin `appium` server and driver packages together with matching semver ranges in
`package.json`.

### Pattern 239 — XCUITest v11.4.0: `resignTask` for Real-Device App Re-signing

`resignTask` is a new Appium XCUITest server-side task (v11.4.0) that automates re-signing an
`.ipa` bundle with a different provisioning profile without rebuilding from source. This is
essential for enterprise distribution pipelines where QA teams receive a build signed for one
profile but need to install on devices registered under a different team.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — trigger resign via appium:options at session create time
const resignCapability = {
  'appium:resignApp': true,
  'appium:resignProvisioningProfile': process.env.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_PATH,
  'appium:resignSigningIdentity': process.env.IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY,
  // The full path to the .ipa that will be re-signed before install
  'appium:app': path.resolve(__dirname, 'builds/MyApp.ipa'),
};

// Or trigger via execute mobile command for an already-installed session
async function resignInstalledApp(
  driver: WebdriverIO.Browser,
  bundleId: string
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: resignApp', {
    bundleId,
    provisioningProfile: process.env.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_PATH!,
    signingIdentity: process.env.IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY!,
  });
  // Wait for the re-signed app to be ready
  await driver.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const state = await driver.queryAppState(bundleId);
      return state !== 6; // 6 = reinstalling
    },
    { timeout: 60_000, timeoutMsg: 'resignTask timed out' }
  );
}
```

**[community] `resignTask` requires `codesign` and `xcrun` to be available on the Appium host
machine — it silently fails on Linux CI runners that lack Xcode command-line tools:** WHY:
Re-signing is a macOS-only operation. If your Appium server runs on Linux (common with Docker
CI), resignTask will fail with `ENOENT: codesign not found`. Gate the capability: only set
`appium:resignApp: true` when `process.platform === 'darwin'`.

**[community] Resigning with a wildcard provisioning profile (`com.example.*`) breaks
associated-domains entitlements — Universal Links and App Clips stop working after resign:**
WHY: The resignTask strips entitlements that reference specific bundle IDs unless the signing
profile also includes those entitlements. Use explicit bundle-ID profiles for tests that
exercise deep links or App Clips. Store profiles as CI secrets and mount them in the runner.

**[community] `resignTask` does not update `CFBundleVersion` — installing a re-signed IPA
over the same bundle ID that already has the same version silently skips the install on iOS 17+
real devices:** WHY: iOS 17+ enforces version-based install idempotency. Bump the micro version
as part of the resign step, or use `appium:noReset: false` to force full reinstall.

### Pattern 240 — XCUITest v10.x: `remotexpc` for iOS 18+ Real-Device Operations

XCUITest driver v10.x progressively migrated from `appium-idb` and `py-ios-device` to Apple's
native `remotexpc` protocol for real-device communication. On iOS 18+, remotexpc handles app
installation, AFC (file system), crash reports, certificates, and port forwarding — removing
the requirement for `libimobiledevice`.

```typescript
// No code change required — remotexpc is automatic when iOS >= 18
// But these patterns become reliable on real devices:

// 1. Push files to device's app container (uses AFC via remotexpc on iOS 18+)
async function pushTestFixture(
  driver: WebdriverIO.Browser,
  localPath: string,
  remotePath: string
): Promise<void> {
  const fileBuffer = fs.readFileSync(localPath);
  await driver.pushFile(remotePath, fileBuffer.toString('base64'));
}

// 2. Retrieve crash reports (uses remotexpc crash-report path on iOS 18+)
async function getLatestCrashReport(driver: WebdriverIO.Browser): Promise<string> {
  return await driver.execute('mobile: getCrashReports', {
    bundleId: 'com.example.app',
    since: new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000).toISOString(), // last 5 min
  }) as string;
}

// 3. CI GitHub Actions — no need to install libimobiledevice on iOS 18+ runners
// steps:
//   - name: Install Appium + XCUITest driver
//     run: |
//       npm install -g appium@latest
//       appium driver install xcuitest
//       # No brew install libimobiledevice needed for iOS 18+ real devices
```

**[community] `remotexpc` is only active when the connected device is iOS 18 or newer —
iOS 17 and below still fall back to `appium-idb` paths, which require `libimobiledevice` on
the CI runner:** WHY: XCUITest driver uses an OS version check at session creation to select
the communication layer. If you run a mixed-iOS-version device farm, your CI runner must still
have `libimobiledevice` installed for the older devices.

**[community] `remotexpc`-based certificate installation (v10.16.0) installs the cert in the
system keychain but does NOT automatically trust it for apps — you still need UI-level
interaction to tap "Trust" in Settings:** WHY: Apple's security model prevents programmatic
certificate trust escalation. Plan a one-time manual trust step on new real devices before
automation runs, or use supervised MDM profiles.

**[community] App installation via `remotexpc` on iOS 18+ is significantly faster than the
`appium-idb` path (~40% reduction for 50 MB+ IPAs) but fails silently when the device's Trust
dialog has not been accepted for this Mac host:** WHY: `remotexpc` requires the device-to-host
trust pairing file (`~/.pymobiledevice3/` lockdowns). On a fresh CI runner or newly wiped
device, the first session will hang at install until the "Trust This Computer" dialog is
dismissed. Pre-pair devices with `pymobiledevice3 lockdown pair` in CI setup steps.

### Pattern 241 — UIAutomator2 v7.2.0: Bluebird Removal and Native Promise Migration

UIAutomator2 v7.2.0 removed the Bluebird promise library. This only affects projects that
imported or interacted with Bluebird directly. Modern async/await code is unaffected, but
legacy `Promise.resolve(val).spread()` patterns or custom `promisifyAll` utility calls will
break at runtime with `TypeError: promise.spread is not a function`.

```typescript
// BEFORE (Bluebird-dependent pattern — breaks in UIAutomator2 v7.2+)
// import Bluebird from 'bluebird';
// return Bluebird.all([getDeviceTime(), getDeviceInfo()])
//   .spread((time, info) => [time, info]);

// AFTER — native Promise, no Bluebird dependency
async function getDeviceMetrics(driver: WebdriverIO.Browser): Promise<[string, string]> {
  const [time, info] = await Promise.all([
    driver.getDeviceTime(),
    driver.execute('mobile: getDeviceInfo', {}) as Promise<string>,
  ]);
  return [time, info];
}

// Audit for indirect Bluebird usage:
// npx depcheck | grep bluebird
// npm ls bluebird  -- look for any non-empty output
// If found, replace .spread() with destructuring, .promisifyAll() with util.promisify()
```

**[community] Some older `@wdio/*` packages (particularly `wdio-allure-reporter` pre-v9.20)
still import Bluebird transitively — after upgrading UIAutomator2 to v7.2+ these packages may
re-introduce Bluebird as a separate instance causing `.spread is not a function` errors even
after your own migration:** WHY: Two Bluebird instances in the same process don't share
prototype methods. Pin all `@wdio/*` packages to >=v9.20 and run `npm ls bluebird` to confirm
no transitive copies remain.

**[community] `Promise.promisifyAll()` pattern used in some WDIO community helper libraries
(e.g., custom `adb-helper.ts` wrappers) is Bluebird-only — these libraries fail silently when
Bluebird is absent and `promisifyAll` is called on plain objects:** WHY: `promisifyAll` is not
a native Node.js API. Replace with explicit `util.promisify()` calls or native async wrappers.
Audit all `helper/` and `support/` directories for Bluebird imports before upgrading.

### Pattern 242 — UIAutomator2 v7.3.0: Strict TypeScript Mode Impact

UIAutomator2 v7.3.0 enables strict TypeScript compilation (`"strict": true`) internally. This
affects consumers if you import UIAutomator2 TypeScript types directly or extend its internal
interfaces. Most WDIO test projects interact via the `browser` / `driver` globals and are
unaffected — but projects using declaration-merging to extend UIAutomator2 capability types
must update their type extensions to satisfy strict mode's stricter null checks.

```typescript
// Pattern: capability interface declaration merging — ensure null-safe types
// BEFORE (may cause compilation issues after UIAutomator2 v7.3.0):
// declare namespace WebdriverIO {
//   interface Capabilities {
//     'appium:avdArgs': string; // non-nullable — strict mode flags if you pass undefined
//   }
// }

// AFTER — use optional + null-safe:
declare namespace WebdriverIO {
  interface Capabilities {
    'appium:avdArgs'?: string | undefined;
    'appium:adbListenAllNetwork'?: boolean | undefined;
    'appium:setStylusHandwriting'?: boolean | undefined; // v7.1.0 new cap
  }
}

// Type guard helper for UIAutomator2-specific capabilities:
function isAndroidCaps(
  caps: WebdriverIO.Capabilities
): caps is WebdriverIO.Capabilities & { platformName: 'Android' } {
  return caps.platformName === 'Android';
}

// tsconfig.json — match UIAutomator2 v7.3 strict mode in your project:
// {
//   "compilerOptions": {
//     "strict": true,
//     "strictNullChecks": true,
//     "noImplicitAny": true
//   }
// }
```

**[community] Strict TS mode in UIAutomator2 v7.3.0 causes `@wdio/appium-service` type
definitions to emit new compilation errors if you have `"strict": false` in your project's
`tsconfig.json` and import from `@wdio/appium-service` — the mismatch between strict and
non-strict declaration files can cause `Type 'X' is not assignable to type 'Y'` errors:**
WHY: TypeScript strict-mode type declarations use `NonNullable<T>` constraints that are
stricter than non-strict equivalents. Fix: enable `"strict": true` in your project
`tsconfig.json` and resolve any resulting type errors — this is the long-term recommendation.

**[community] Projects using `ts-expect-error` suppressions to work around UIAutomator2 type
issues will see those suppressors silently become unused after v7.3.0 fixes the underlying
types — with `"noUnusedLocals": true` this causes CI compilation failures not runtime failures:**
WHY: `ts-expect-error` becomes a compile error when the annotated line no longer produces an
error. Clean up suppressors when upgrading to UIAutomator2 v7.3+.

### Pattern 243 — UIAutomator2 v7.1.0: `mobile:setStylusHandwriting`

`mobile:setStylusHandwriting` enables or disables handwriting recognition on Android devices
that support a stylus (e.g., Samsung S-Pen, Chromebook stylus). It is gated behind a security
flag (`appium:allowInsecure: ['setStylusHandwriting']`) because it modifies system-level input
settings.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — enable the security flag in @wdio/appium-service appiumArgs
// appiumArgs: { allowInsecure: ['setStylusHandwriting'] }

// Test: toggle handwriting mode and validate stylus input field
it('should accept handwriting input on stylus-enabled device', async () => {
  // Enable handwriting recognition
  await driver.execute('mobile: setStylusHandwriting', { enable: true });

  // Tap on a text field that supports S-Pen / stylus input
  const inputField = await driver.$('~handwriting-input');
  await inputField.click();

  // Verify handwriting keyboard appeared (Samsung devices)
  const handwritingIndicator = await driver.$(
    '//android.widget.ImageView[@content-desc="Handwriting"]'
  );
  await expect(handwritingIndicator).toBeDisplayed();

  // Disable handwriting after test to restore default state
  await driver.execute('mobile: setStylusHandwriting', { enable: false });
});

// Type-safe execute wrapper:
async function setStylusHandwriting(
  driver: WebdriverIO.Browser,
  enable: boolean
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: setStylusHandwriting', { enable });
}
```

**[community] `mobile:setStylusHandwriting` is a no-op on Android emulators that don't have
stylus hardware simulation — the command succeeds (no error) but the system setting is not
actually changed, causing test assertions about the handwriting keyboard to fail silently:**
WHY: The UIAutomator2 driver applies the setting via the Android Settings provider API, but
AVDs without a stylus profile ignore the value. Test this feature exclusively on physical
stylus-equipped devices (Samsung Galaxy S-series, Galaxy Tab with S-Pen, Pixel Fold).

**[community] Without `appium:allowInsecure: ['setStylusHandwriting']` the command returns HTTP
500 `SecurityError: setStylusHandwriting is not allowed` — some older `@wdio/appium-service`
versions (pre-v9.15) do not pass `allowInsecure` array items to the Appium CLI correctly,
causing the flag to be silently ignored:** WHY: The `appiumArgs.allowInsecure` config must be
serialised as a comma-separated string in the Appium CLI invocation. Verify with
`appium --allow-insecure=setStylusHandwriting` manually on the CI runner to confirm.

### Pattern 244 — `@wdio/mcp`: AI-Assisted Mobile Test Authoring

`@wdio/mcp` (released February 2026) is a Model Context Protocol server that exposes
WebdriverIO/Appium automation to AI assistants (Claude, Copilot, Cursor, VS Code Agent). It
uses an efficient 2-HTTP-call XML page-source strategy (rather than 600+ queries) to let AI
tools inspect the current app state and generate test actions without flooding the Appium server.

```typescript
// Setup: add @wdio/mcp to Claude Desktop / Claude Code
// ~/.claude/claude_desktop_config.json:
// {
//   "mcpServers": {
//     "wdio-mcp": {
//       "command": "npx",
//       "args": ["-y", "@wdio/mcp"]
//     }
//   }
// }

// Pin the version in package.json to avoid version drift between CI runs:
// "devDependencies": { "@wdio/mcp": "^1.0.0" }

// MCP server capabilities exposed to AI tools:
// - getPageSource()        -> returns XML page source in 2 HTTP calls
// - tapElement(selector)   -> AI generates accessibility-ID or XPath selector
// - swipe(direction)       -> directional swipe on current context
// - switchContext(name)    -> switch between NATIVE_APP and WEBVIEW contexts
// - screenshot()           -> compressed PNG (max 1 MB) for visual inspection

// Cross-platform selector priority used by @wdio/mcp when generating code:
const MCP_SELECTOR_PRIORITY = [
  '~accessibility-id',            // iOS + Android — highest priority
  '-android uiautomator:...',     // Android-specific fallback
  '-ios predicate string:...',    // iOS-specific fallback
  '//XCUIElementType...',         // XPath — last resort
] as const;

// AI-assisted test generation workflow:
// 1. Launch app + Appium session
// 2. Connect AI tool (Claude) to @wdio/mcp
// 3. Describe the scenario: "Test that login form validates empty password"
// 4. @wdio/mcp generates WDIO TypeScript test code with correct selectors
// 5. Review generated tests and commit
```

**[community] `@wdio/mcp` only supports a single active session — if you have multiple
`multiRemoteBrowser` sessions (e.g., two devices for push notification testing), the MCP
server attaches to an unspecified session, potentially sending commands to the wrong device:**
WHY: MCP's single-session model predates multiRemote. Use `@wdio/mcp` for single-device
exploration and scaffolding only; run actual multi-device tests without MCP involvement.

**[community] `@wdio/mcp` does not support cloud providers (BrowserStack, Sauce Labs) out of
the box — it creates its own local WebdriverIO session and attempts to connect to a local
Appium server. Attempts to use it with `bs://` app URLs fail with `SessionNotCreatedException`:**
WHY: The MCP server creates sessions using local capabilities. Cloud sessions require
BrowserStack/Sauce credentials not passed through the default MCP config.

**[community] `@wdio/mcp` screenshot auto-compression to 1 MB causes visual regression misses
when pixel-level differences (less than 2% of image) are significant — JPEG compression
artefacts introduced by size reduction obscure small UI changes:** WHY: The 1 MB limit applies
lossy compression. For visual regression testing, use `@wdio/visual-service` directly rather
than routing screenshots through `@wdio/mcp`.

**[community] Running `npx -y @wdio/mcp` installs a fresh copy on every invocation — this means
the AI tool may use different `@wdio/mcp` versions between sessions, causing selector generation
style inconsistencies across CI runs:** WHY: `npx -y` always fetches the latest. Pin the version:
`"@wdio/mcp": "^1.0.0"` in devDependencies and use `npx @wdio/mcp` after `npm install`.

### Pattern 245 — XCUITest v11.0.0 Upgrade Checklist

XCUITest v11.0.0 (released 2026-04-14) has significant breaking changes. Use this checklist
when upgrading from v10.x.

```typescript
// 1. Node.js version gate — verify before appium driver install
// node --version  # must be >= 20.19.0
// npm --version   # must be >= 10
// appium --version  # must be >= 3.0.0

// 2. Remove deprecated capabilities from wdio.conf.ts:
//    REMOVED (UnrecognizedCapabilityError if present):
//    - 'appium:waitForQuiescence'        -> use explicit waitUntil() instead
//    - 'appium:appInstallStrategy'       -> default strategy used automatically
//    - 'appium:calendarAccessAuthorized' -> use mobile:setPermissions instead
//    - 'appium:useSimpleBuildTest'       -> removed without replacement
//    - 'appium:launchWithIDB'            -> idb removed, remotexpc used on iOS 18+
//    - 'appium:simpleIsVisibleCheck'     -> use isDisplayed() built-in

// 3. Remove deprecated mobile execute commands from test code:
//    - mobile:startPcap / mobile:stopPcap      -> use native packet capture tools
//    - mobile:listXCTestsInTestBundle          -> use xcodebuild CLI

// 4. Replace appium.contextUpdated BiDi event (removed from XCUITest v11):
//    BEFORE: await driver.on('bidi:appium.contextUpdated', handler)
//    AFTER:  poll via getContext() in beforeEach or use switchContext() callbacks

// Capability migration validator helper:
const REMOVED_V11_XCUITEST_CAPS = [
  'appium:waitForQuiescence',
  'appium:appInstallStrategy',
  'appium:calendarAccessAuthorized',
  'appium:useSimpleBuildTest',
  'appium:launchWithIDB',
  'appium:simpleIsVisibleCheck',
] as const;

function validateXCUITestV11Caps(caps: Record<string, unknown>): void {
  for (const removedCap of REMOVED_V11_XCUITEST_CAPS) {
    if (removedCap in caps) {
      console.warn(
        `[XCUITest v11] Removed capability used: ${removedCap} — remove from your config`
      );
    }
  }
}
```

### Pattern 246 — Appium 3.3.1: Plugin-State Isolation Between Sessions

Appium 3.3.1 (2026-04-23) fixed a bug where plugin state was shared across sessions in some
concurrent execution scenarios. The fix ensures plugin state is fully scoped to the creating
session — critical for parallel device testing where two sessions may run the same plugin
simultaneously.

```typescript
// Pattern: verify plugin isolation in parallel runs by asserting independent plugin state
// This pattern catches regressions if you ever downgrade Appium below 3.3.1

describe('parallel session plugin isolation', () => {
  let session1: WebdriverIO.Browser;
  let session2: WebdriverIO.Browser;

  before(async () => {
    [session1, session2] = await Promise.all([
      remote(capsIOS),
      remote(capsAndroid),
    ]);
  });

  it('plugin wait state should be independent per session', async () => {
    // Set a wait plugin property on session 1 only
    await session1.execute('setWaitPluginProperties', {
      elementWaitTimeout: 10_000,
    });

    // Session 2 should still have its own default timeout (5000 ms)
    const s2Props = await session2.execute('getWaitPluginProperties', {});
    expect((s2Props as { elementWaitTimeout: number }).elementWaitTimeout).toBe(5_000);
  });

  after(async () => {
    await Promise.all([session1.deleteSession(), session2.deleteSession()]);
  });
});
```

**[community] Pre-3.3.1 Appium versions exhibit plugin-state bleeding between parallel iOS
and Android sessions in CI — manifesting as `appium-wait-plugin` using iOS-configured timeout
values on Android sessions, causing `TimeoutError` on fast Android actions:** WHY: Plugin
instances were keyed by plugin name, not session ID. Fix: upgrade to Appium >=3.3.1. If you
cannot upgrade, run iOS and Android sessions in separate Appium server processes on different
ports.

**[community] The 3.3.1 plugin caching fix applies at session-create time only — hot-reloaded
plugin config via `setWaitPluginProperties` mid-session is still not isolated between
concurrent sessions on Appium <3.4.0:** WHY: The cache invalidation fix was applied at session
init, not at plugin command dispatch. For full safety, combine Appium >=3.4.0 with
session-scoped `beforeEach` calls to reset plugin state to known values.

### Pattern 247 — UIAutomator2 v2.29+: Multi-Display Screenshot in CI

UIAutomator2 v2.29.0 added support for capturing screenshots of specific virtual display IDs,
enabling testing on foldable Android devices and multi-window CI emulators without the
screenshot defaulting to the primary display.

```typescript
// Capture screenshot from a specific virtual display (foldable inner screen)
async function screenshotDisplay(
  driver: WebdriverIO.Browser,
  displayId: number
): Promise<string> {
  // Returns base64-encoded PNG of the specified display
  return (await driver.execute('mobile: screenshots', {
    displayId,
    format: 'png',
  })) as string;
}

// Usage: test layout on foldable inner display (displayId = 1)
it('should render correctly on inner display', async () => {
  // Ensure we are in landscape / unfolded state
  await driver.execute('mobile: setOrientation', { orientation: 'LANDSCAPE' });

  // List available displays first to guard against missing displayId
  const displays = (await driver.execute('mobile: listDisplays', {})) as number[];
  expect(displays).toContain(1);

  const innerDisplayBase64 = await screenshotDisplay(driver, 1);
  expect(innerDisplayBase64).toBeTruthy();

  // Save for visual regression baseline
  fs.writeFileSync(
    path.join('screenshots', `inner-display-${Date.now()}.png`),
    Buffer.from(innerDisplayBase64, 'base64')
  );
});

// GitHub Actions CI: use pixel_fold system image with secondary display flags
// avdArgs: '-display-size 2208x1840 -secondary-display 1840x2208'
```

**[community] `mobile: screenshots` with a non-existent `displayId` silently returns the
primary display screenshot (displayId = 0) on API 29 and below — no error is thrown, causing
screenshot assertions to always pass even when the secondary display failed to render:**
WHY: Virtual display creation API on older APIs returns a success code but does not populate
the display registry used by UIAutomator2. Guard: call `mobile: listDisplays` first and assert
your target `displayId` appears in the list before capturing.

**[community] CI Android emulators in `-no-window` mode do not create virtual displays for
foldable simulation by default — `displayId: 1` screenshot always returns the primary display
base64 on headless AVDs without explicit `-display-size` and `-secondary-display` AVD flags:**
WHY: Foldable displays require special emulator image support. Use
`@reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` on `ubuntu-22.04` with the `pixel_fold` system
image and set `avdArgs: '-display-size 2208x1840 -secondary-display 1840x2208'`.

### Pattern 248 — UIAutomator2 Server v10.0.0: ESM-Only Migration

UIAutomator2 Server v10.0.0 (released May 8, 2026) migrated to ESM-only, removing CommonJS
support and all default exports. Projects that reference this package (directly or transitively
through UIAutomator2 driver) must update their module system and import syntax.

The practical impact for WDIO test authors is limited — the UIAutomator2 driver wraps the
server package — but if you have custom Appium plugins or direct server integrations, this is
a breaking change. Also triggers `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` in older Node/CJS test harnesses.

```typescript
// BEFORE v10.0.0 (CJS default import — breaks in v10+)
// const UIAutomator2Server = require('appium-uiautomator2-server');

// AFTER v10.0.0 — named ESM import only
import { UIAutomator2Server } from 'appium-uiautomator2-server';

// In wdio.conf.ts: ensure your project is ESM-compatible
// package.json: "type": "module"  OR use .mts extension
// tsconfig.json: "module": "NodeNext", "moduleResolution": "NodeNext"

// v10.1.0 also added dedicated type exports — import types cleanly:
import type { UIAutomator2ServerOptions } from 'appium-uiautomator2-server';

// Validate your project's module setup before upgrading UIAutomator2 driver
// to a version that depends on server v10:
function checkEsmReady(): void {
  // In CommonJS context this will fail at parse time with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM
  // Run: node --input-type=module -e "import('appium-uiautomator2-server')"
  // to pre-validate before CI upgrade
  console.log('ESM check passed');
}
```

**[community] Upgrading `appium-uiautomator2-driver` to a version that pulls in
`appium-uiautomator2-server` v10+ silently breaks CJS test harnesses with
`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` at session-creation time — not at `npm install`:** WHY: npm resolves
the semver range and installs v10 without warning if you are on UIAutomator2 driver >=X.
The error surfaces only when Appium attempts to start the server subprocess. Guard: pin
`appium-uiautomator2-server` explicitly in `package.json` or add an
`engines.node` check. If staying on CJS, pin `appium-uiautomator2-server` below v10.

**[community] `module: "CommonJS"` in `tsconfig.json` does not prevent runtime
`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` when a dependency is ESM-only — TypeScript compilation succeeds but
the compiled JS crashes at runtime:** WHY: TypeScript does not transform dynamic
`import()` calls for ESM-only packages when targeting CommonJS; the runtime
module loader enforces the package's `"type": "module"` contract. Solution: migrate
to `"module": "NodeNext"` or use a dynamic `import()` wrapper for the server package.

**[community] `appium-uiautomator2-server` v10.1.0 added explicit type exports but the
`exports` map in `package.json` requires the `types` condition — projects using
`"moduleResolution": "Node10"` will not resolve type exports and get `any`:** WHY:
`Node10` (classic) resolution ignores `exports` map conditions. Switch to
`"moduleResolution": "NodeNext"` or `"Bundler"` to correctly resolve the new type
exports.

### Pattern 249 — XCUITest v11.4.0: `sign-wda` CLI for Real-Device WDA Re-Signing

XCUITest v11.4.0 (released May 13, 2026) adds the `sign-wda` task — a CLI command
invoked via `appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda` that re-signs the WebDriverAgent app
bundle with your own certificate after downloading it with the `download-wda` task
(added in v11.3.0). This is the new canonical workflow for real-device CI without
full Xcode present.

```bash
# Step 1: Download WDA (v11.3.0+)
npx appium driver run xcuitest download-wda -- \
  --wda-path ./WebDriverAgentRunner.app

# Step 2: Re-sign WDA with your certificate (v11.4.0+)
# P12_PASSWORD must be set as an environment variable — not a CLI arg (security)
export P12_PASSWORD="$WDA_CERT_PASSWORD"

npx appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda -- \
  --wda-path ./WebDriverAgentRunner.app \
  --p12-file ./certs/dev-cert.p12 \
  --profile-dir ./certs/profiles/

# Verify signing without actually signing (dry-run):
npx appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda -- \
  --wda-path ./WebDriverAgentRunner.app \
  --p12-file ./certs/dev-cert.p12 \
  --inspect

# Also supports separate cert + key instead of p12:
npx appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda -- \
  --wda-path ./WebDriverAgentRunner.app \
  --cert-file ./certs/dev.cer \
  --key-file ./certs/dev.key \
  --profile-dir ./certs/profiles/
```

```typescript
// GitHub Actions CI workflow pattern: cache downloaded WDA, re-sign per run
// .github/workflows/ios-real-device.yml (YAML excerpt as comment):
//
// - name: Download WDA (cached)
//   id: wda-cache
//   uses: actions/cache@v4
//   with:
//     path: ./WebDriverAgentRunner.app
//     key: wda-xcuitest-${{ env.XCUITEST_VERSION }}
//
// - name: Download WDA if not cached
//   if: steps.wda-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
//   run: npx appium driver run xcuitest download-wda -- --wda-path ./WebDriverAgentRunner.app
//
// - name: Re-sign WDA
//   env:
//     P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WDA_P12_PASSWORD }}
//   run: |
//     npx appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda -- \
//       --wda-path ./WebDriverAgentRunner.app \
//       --p12-file ./certs/dev-cert.p12 \
//       --profile-dir ./certs/profiles/

// WDIO capability: point to pre-signed WDA
const caps = {
  platformName: 'iOS',
  'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
  'appium:deviceName': 'iPhone 16',
  'appium:udid': process.env.IOS_DEVICE_UDID,
  'appium:usePreinstalledWDA': false,        // use downloaded+signed WDA
  'appium:webDriverAgentUrl': undefined,     // let Appium install from wda-path
  // If using usePreinstalledWDA = true after manual install:
  'appium:updatedWDABundleId': 'com.mycompany.WebDriverAgentRunner',
} as const;
```

**[community] `P12_PASSWORD` passed as a CLI argument (`--p12-password`) is intentionally
not supported in sign-wda — the password is only read from the `P12_PASSWORD`
environment variable:** WHY: CLI arguments are visible in process listings (`ps aux`)
and shell history. Always inject the password through the environment. In GitHub Actions,
use `env:` block with a secret: `P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WDA_P12_PASSWORD }}`.

**[community] `--inspect` (dry-run mode) validates the signing configuration without
modifying the WDA bundle, but it does NOT verify that the provisioning profile covers
the physical device's UDID:** WHY: The inspect step only checks certificate validity and
profile format, not device entitlement. Add a separate preflight step using
`security cms -D -i <profile>` to extract and check the `ProvisionedDevices` array.

**[community] Caching the signed WDA bundle across CI runs can cause `INSTALLATION_FAILED`
on real devices when the signing identity's provisioning profile expires — the cached
binary retains the expired entitlement:** WHY: The cache key only tracks XCUITest driver
version, not the certificate expiry date. Include the certificate fingerprint (or expiry
month) in the cache key: `wda-${{ env.XCUITEST_VERSION }}-${{ env.CERT_FINGERPRINT }}`.

### Pattern 250 — WDIO v9.25.0: `no-floating-promise` ESLint Rule

`eslint-plugin-wdio` v9.25.0 added the `wdio/no-floating-promise` rule, which detects
WebDriverIO command calls that are not `await`ed. Floating promises in WDIO tests cause
silent test failures — the command runs asynchronously, the test proceeds, and assertions
execute before the browser action completes.

```typescript
// .eslintrc.cjs (or eslint.config.js for flat config)
// Install: npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-wdio

// Legacy .eslintrc.cjs:
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['wdio'],
  extends: ['plugin:wdio/recommended'],
  rules: {
    // Explicitly enable (included in recommended since v9.25.0):
    'wdio/no-floating-promise': 'error',
    // Keep existing WDIO rules:
    'wdio/no-pause': 'warn',
  },
};

// Flat config (eslint.config.js — required for ESLint v9+):
import wdioPlugin from 'eslint-plugin-wdio';

export default [
  {
    plugins: { wdio: wdioPlugin },
    rules: {
      ...wdioPlugin.configs.recommended.rules,
      'wdio/no-floating-promise': 'error',
    },
  },
];
```

```typescript
// INCORRECT — floating promise, assertion runs before click completes:
it('should submit form', async () => {
  browser.url('/login');          // ❌ missing await
  $('#username').setValue('joe'); // ❌ missing await
  await $('#password').setValue('secret');
  await $('button[type=submit]').click();
  await expect($('.dashboard')).toBeDisplayed();
});

// CORRECT — all commands awaited:
it('should submit form', async () => {
  await browser.url('/login');
  await $('#username').setValue('joe');
  await $('#password').setValue('secret');
  await $('button[type=submit]').click();
  await expect($('.dashboard')).toBeDisplayed();
});

// ALSO CATCHES: promise assigned to variable but never awaited:
it('bad promise variable', async () => {
  const p = browser.url('/page'); // ❌ caught by rule: p never awaited
  await $('h1').waitForDisplayed();
});
```

**[community] The `wdio/no-floating-promise` rule does not catch floating promises
inside `Promise.all()` array literals where one entry is missing `await` — only
top-level unawaited WDIO calls are flagged:** WHY: ESLint AST analysis cannot track
whether an expression is consumed inside an array being passed to `Promise.all`. Use
TypeScript's `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` rule alongside WDIO's rule for
comprehensive coverage.

**[community] `browser.pause()` calls without `await` are caught by both
`wdio/no-pause` (warns about usage) and `wdio/no-floating-promise` (errors on unawaited
call) — double-triggering on the same line can cause confusing ESLint output:** WHY:
The rules are independent; `no-pause` fires on any pause call, `no-floating-promise`
fires because the returned Promise is not handled. Resolve both by removing the pause
and using `browser.waitUntil()` instead.

**[community] ESLint flat config (`eslint.config.js`) requires the plugin to be imported
as an ES module — the legacy `require('eslint-plugin-wdio')` syntax will throw
`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` if you upgraded eslint-plugin-wdio to a version that is ESM-only:**
WHY: eslint-plugin-wdio follows the same ESM migration trend as the rest of the WDIO
ecosystem. Use `import wdioPlugin from 'eslint-plugin-wdio'` in your flat config file.

### Pattern 251 — WDIO v9.26.0: Appium 3 Protocol Command Rename Compatibility Layer

WDIO v9.26.0 added systematic renaming of deprecated Appium protocol commands to their
Appium 3 `appium:`-prefixed equivalents. This is primarily a WDIO internals change, but
it affects custom Appium command wrappers and any code that calls raw protocol commands
directly via `browser.execute()` or custom locator strategies.

The Appium 3 protocol rename table (37 commands) was documented in iteration 29. WDIO
v9.26.0 ensures the WDIO protocol layer dispatches the new command names to Appium 3
servers while providing compatibility wrappers for older servers.

```typescript
// Pattern: detect Appium server version and use appropriate command set
// WDIO v9.26+ handles this automatically, but for custom browser.execute() calls:

async function getDeviceInfo(driver: WebdriverIO.Browser): Promise<{
  appiumVersion: string;
  isAppium3: boolean;
}> {
  const status = await driver.status();
  const appiumVersion: string =
    (status as { build?: { version?: string } }).build?.version ?? '2.0.0';
  const isAppium3 = appiumVersion.startsWith('3.');
  return { appiumVersion, isAppium3 };
}

// Use version-aware command dispatch for raw protocol calls:
async function getScreenRecording(driver: WebdriverIO.Browser): Promise<string> {
  const { isAppium3 } = await getDeviceInfo(driver);
  // WDIO v9.26+ mobile commands handle this automatically via wrappers,
  // but for direct execute() calls, use the correct command name:
  const commandName = isAppium3
    ? 'appium:stopRecordingScreen'   // Appium 3 prefixed name
    : 'stopRecordingScreen';         // Appium 2 legacy name
  return (await driver.execute(commandName, {})) as string;
}

// WDIO high-level API (recommended — version-transparent):
// await driver.startRecordingScreen();
// const video = await driver.stopRecordingScreen();
// ↑ These work correctly on both Appium 2 and Appium 3 via WDIO v9.26+ wrappers.

// Validate your wdio.conf.ts appium service version setting:
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  services: [
    ['appium', {
      // Explicitly state Appium 3 for correct command dispatch:
      command: 'appium',
      args: {
        // Appium 3 is the default when installed globally >= 3.0.0
      },
    }],
  ],
});
```

**[community] WDIO v9.26.0 `queryAppState` rename was reverted in v9.27.0 because
the wrapper caused regressions — if you upgraded to v9.26.0 and saw `queryAppState`
failures, update to v9.27.0 which restores the original non-prefixed dispatch:** WHY:
The Appium 3 rename for `queryAppState` conflicted with the WDIO high-level
`driver.queryAppState()` method, causing duplicate dispatch. The v9.27.0 revert uses
the pre-existing WDIO method as the canonical interface instead of a protocol wrapper.

**[community] Raw `browser.execute('stopRecordingScreen')` calls (without `appium:`
prefix) fail silently on Appium 3 servers — they return `null` instead of the base64
video string, because Appium 3 only recognises the prefixed command name:** WHY: Appium
3 made the `appium:` prefix mandatory for extension commands. The WDIO high-level
`driver.stopRecordingScreen()` is the safe API — it handles prefix routing. Never use
raw `execute()` for Appium extension commands in Appium 3 environments.

### Pattern 252 — WDIO v9.27.0: `queryAppState` Revert and `AppState` Enum Best Practice

WDIO v9.27.0 (March 2026) reverted the `queryAppState` protocol rename introduced in
v9.26.0. The high-level `driver.queryAppState()` method remains the canonical interface.
This pattern documents the correct TypeScript usage with the `AppState` enum and guards
against the v9.26.0 regression.

```typescript
import { AppState } from 'appium'; // Appium 3 exports AppState enum

// Correct WDIO v9.27+ pattern for app state checking:
async function waitForAppForeground(
  driver: WebdriverIO.Browser,
  bundleIdOrPackage: string,
  timeoutMs = 10_000
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const state = await driver.queryAppState(bundleIdOrPackage);
      // AppState enum values: NOT_INSTALLED=0, NOT_RUNNING=1,
      // RUNNING_IN_BACKGROUND_SUSPENDED=2, RUNNING_IN_BACKGROUND=3,
      // RUNNING_IN_FOREGROUND=4
      return state === 4; // AppState.RUNNING_IN_FOREGROUND
    },
    {
      timeout: timeoutMs,
      timeoutMsg: `App ${bundleIdOrPackage} did not reach foreground in ${timeoutMs}ms`,
      interval: 500,
    }
  );
}

// Typed AppState constants if Appium package is not installed:
const APP_STATE = {
  NOT_INSTALLED: 0,
  NOT_RUNNING: 1,
  RUNNING_IN_BACKGROUND_SUSPENDED: 2,
  RUNNING_IN_BACKGROUND: 3,
  RUNNING_IN_FOREGROUND: 4,
} as const;
type AppStateValue = (typeof APP_STATE)[keyof typeof APP_STATE];

// Cross-platform app lifecycle test:
describe('app lifecycle', () => {
  const APP_ID = process.env.PLATFORM === 'ios'
    ? 'com.example.myapp'
    : 'com.example.myapp';

  it('should reach foreground after deep link', async () => {
    await driver.terminateApp(APP_ID);
    expect(await driver.queryAppState(APP_ID)).toBe(APP_STATE.NOT_RUNNING);

    await driver.deepLink('myapp://dashboard', APP_ID);
    await waitForAppForeground(driver, APP_ID);
    expect(await driver.queryAppState(APP_ID)).toBe(APP_STATE.RUNNING_IN_FOREGROUND);
  });
});
```

**[community] The `queryAppState` revert in v9.27.0 means projects that explicitly
imported the raw Appium 3 command name (`appium:queryAppState`) in custom commands
must remove the prefix — but projects on v9.26.0 that worked around the bug by calling
`appium:queryAppState` directly will break again on v9.27.0:** WHY: The revert
creates a bidirectional migration: v9.26.0 → v9.27.0 requires removing `appium:`
prefix workarounds. The canonical form is always `driver.queryAppState()` — never
the raw protocol command.

**[community] `queryAppState` returns `0` (NOT_INSTALLED) on Android when the app is
installed but the process was killed by the OS memory manager — the kernel removes the
process entry before Appium checks, making it indistinguishable from uninstalled apps:**
WHY: Android's low-memory killer can terminate app processes without updating the
package manager. Use `driver.isAppInstalled(packageName)` separately to distinguish
between "killed process" and "not installed" states.

### Pattern 253 — Appium 3.4.0: Storage Access WebDriver Endpoint

Appium 3.4.0 (May 2026) added three new W3C WebDriver extension endpoints aligned with
the Privacy Community Group specifications:

1. `GET /session/{id}/gpc` — `getGlobalPrivacyControl()`
2. `POST /session/{id}/gpc` — `setGlobalPrivacyControl(gpc: boolean)`
3. `POST /session/{id}/storage-access` — request/grant storage access permission

These enable testing of privacy-aware web features inside WebViews without manually
manipulating browser settings or injecting JavaScript.

```typescript
// Pattern: test WebView GPC compliance in a hybrid app
// The GPC signal tells websites the user opts out of data sale/sharing

async function testWebViewGpcCompliance(driver: WebdriverIO.Browser): Promise<void> {
  // Switch to WebView context first
  const contexts = await driver.getContexts();
  const webviewCtx = contexts.find((c) => String(c).startsWith('WEBVIEW'));
  if (!webviewCtx) throw new Error('No WebView context found');
  await driver.switchContext(String(webviewCtx));

  // Enable GPC signal — signals opt-out to the page
  await driver.execute('appium: setGlobalPrivacyControl', { gpc: true });

  // Verify the page received the GPC signal via navigator.globalPrivacyControl
  const gpcValue = await driver.execute(() =>
    (navigator as Navigator & { globalPrivacyControl?: boolean }).globalPrivacyControl
  );
  expect(gpcValue).toBe(true);

  // Verify analytics opt-out logic triggered:
  await expect($('[data-testid="analytics-opt-out-banner"]')).toBeDisplayed();

  // Disable GPC (default — user has not opted out):
  await driver.execute('appium: setGlobalPrivacyControl', { gpc: false });
  const gpcDisabled = await driver.execute(() =>
    (navigator as Navigator & { globalPrivacyControl?: boolean }).globalPrivacyControl
  );
  expect(gpcDisabled).toBe(false);
}

// Storage Access API pattern:
// Test that a cross-origin iframe can request storage access in a WebView:
async function testStorageAccessRequest(driver: WebdriverIO.Browser): Promise<void> {
  // Navigate to page with cross-origin iframe
  await driver.url('https://app.example.com/payment');

  // Switch to the cross-origin iframe context
  const frame = await driver.findElement('css selector', 'iframe[src*="payment-provider"]');
  await driver.switchToFrame(frame);

  // Trigger the storage access request (calls document.requestStorageAccess())
  await $('[data-testid="enable-cookies-btn"]').click();

  // Appium 3.4.0 can intercept and grant via the new endpoint
  // (driver-level grant without user gesture requirement in test context):
  await driver.execute('appium: grantStorageAccess', {});

  // Verify the embedded payment form is now functional:
  await expect($('[data-testid="card-number"]')).toBeEnabled();
}
```

**[community] `appium: setGlobalPrivacyControl` has no effect on native app contexts —
the command must be called after switching to a WebView context; calling it in
`NATIVE_APP` context silently succeeds but the GPC header is never injected:** WHY:
GPC is a browser-level HTTP request header (`Sec-GPC: 1`). It only applies in contexts
where WebKit/Chromium is rendering. The Appium endpoint proxies to the underlying
WebDriver implementation which requires an active WebView context.

**[community] The Storage Access endpoint (`grantStorageAccess`) is not supported by
all XCUITest WebView implementations — WKWebView must have been built with
`WKPreferences.isSiteSpecificQuirksModeEnabled = false` to respect W3C storage
access behavior; otherwise the grant silently has no effect:** WHY: Older WKWebView
builds (iOS < 17.2) use site-specific quirks that bypass the W3C Storage Access API.
Test on iOS 17.2+ simulators and set the preference explicitly in your app's WebView
configuration for consistent behavior.

**[community] `getGlobalPrivacyControl()` returns `null` (not `false`) when the GPC
preference has never been set in the current WebView session — GPC is opt-in and has
no default value:** WHY: Per the GPC spec, absence of the signal is not the same as
`false`. Your app's privacy compliance logic must handle both `null` (no preference
declared) and `false` (explicitly opted in) as "user has not opted out" states.
