### Pattern 254 — BrowserStack Self-Healing AI Agent: Integration with WDIO TypeScript

BrowserStack's App Automate introduced a self-healing AI agent that automatically
detects flaky element selectors and attempts to locate the element using alternative
strategies (accessibility ID, text, XPath) when the primary selector fails. This
reduces CI test failures caused by minor app UI updates without requiring selector
maintenance.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — BrowserStack self-healing configuration
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  user: process.env.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME,
  key: process.env.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY,
  hostname: 'hub.browserstack.com',
  port: 443,
  protocol: 'https' as const,
  path: '/wd/hub',

  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'Android',
    'appium:deviceName': 'Samsung Galaxy S24',
    'appium:platformVersion': '14.0',
    'appium:app': `bs://YOUR_APP_HASH`,
    'appium:automationName': 'UIAutomator2',
    // Enable self-healing:
    'bstack:options': {
      projectName: 'My Mobile App',
      buildName: `CI Build ${process.env.BUILD_NUMBER ?? 'local'}`,
      sessionName: 'E2E Suite',
      // Self-healing options:
      selfHeal: true,                    // enable AI-powered self-healing
      // Optional: tune healing aggressiveness:
      // selfHealScore: 0.8,             // confidence threshold (0-1, default 0.8)
    },
  }],

  services: ['browserstack'],

  // Log healed selectors for post-run review:
  afterTest: async (test, _context, { error }) => {
    if (!error) return;
    // BrowserStack SDK emits healed selectors in the session JSON report
    // Review at: app.browserstack.com → App Automate → Session → Self-Heal tab
    console.log(`Test "${test.title}" had selector issues — check BrowserStack self-heal log`);
  },
});
```

```typescript
// Page Object pattern compatible with BrowserStack self-healing:
// Self-healing works best with accessibility IDs (most stable anchor)
class LoginPage {
  // Primary: accessibility ID (most stable — self-healing rarely needed)
  get usernameField() { return $('~username-field'); }
  get passwordField() { return $('~password-field'); }
  get loginButton()   { return $('~login-button'); }

  // If accessibility IDs are not available, use text-based selectors:
  // BrowserStack self-healing can fall back to text matching when ID changes
  get forgotPasswordLink() {
    return $('android=new UiSelector().text("Forgot Password?")');
  }

  async login(username: string, password: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.usernameField.setValue(username);
    await this.passwordField.setValue(password);
    await this.loginButton.click();
  }
}

// TypeScript utility: extract self-heal events from BrowserStack session API
interface BrowserStackSelfHealEvent {
  selector: string;
  healedSelector: string;
  confidence: number;
  timestamp: string;
}

async function getSelfHealEvents(sessionId: string): Promise<BrowserStackSelfHealEvent[]> {
  const response = await fetch(
    `https://api.browserstack.com/app-automate/sessions/${sessionId}/selfheal`,
    {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Basic ${Buffer.from(
          `${process.env.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME}:${process.env.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY}`
        ).toString('base64')}`,
      },
    }
  );
  return response.json() as Promise<BrowserStackSelfHealEvent[]>;
}
```

**[community] BrowserStack self-healing fires for ALL failed selectors, not just
transient ones — if your selector is permanently broken (e.g., after a major app
redesign), self-healing will use a low-confidence alternative and the test will pass
incorrectly, masking a real regression:** WHY: Self-healing is not aware of semantic
intent, only visual/structural similarity. After a major release, disable self-healing
for one run to identify all genuinely broken selectors: `'bstack:options': { selfHeal: false }`.

**[community] `selfHeal: true` does not apply to WebView contexts — self-healing only
works for native app elements (NATIVE_APP context):** WHY: WebView elements are
resolved by the Chromium/WebKit engine, not UIAutomator2/XCUITest, so BrowserStack's
server-side element resolution layer cannot intercept and heal WebDriver WebView
selector lookups.

**[community] Self-healed selectors reported in the BrowserStack session are
suggestions, not automatic source-code updates — you must manually update the Page
Object to use the healed selector to permanently fix the test:** WHY: BrowserStack has
no access to your source code. The self-heal event is purely a runtime rescue. Treat
healed-selector reports as a prioritised fix backlog — address them before the next
major app release when the healing fallback may no longer find the element either.

### Pattern 255 — WDIO Multiremote: TypeScript Declaration for Cross-Platform iOS + Android

WDIO's multiremote feature is the standard approach for cross-platform tests that
interact with both iOS and Android simultaneously (e.g., push notification end-to-end,
cross-platform chat). The TypeScript declaration pattern ensures type safety when
accessing platform-specific drivers.

```typescript
// Type augmentation for multiremote cross-platform mobile testing
// Place in: test/types/wdio-multiremote.d.ts

declare namespace WebdriverIO {
  interface MultiRemoteBrowser {
    iOSDriver: WebdriverIO.Browser;
    androidDriver: WebdriverIO.Browser;
  }
}
```

```typescript
// wdio-multiremote.conf.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  capabilities: {
    iOSDriver: {
      capabilities: {
        platformName: 'iOS',
        'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
        'appium:deviceName': 'iPhone 16',
        'appium:udid': process.env.IOS_UDID,
        'appium:app': process.env.IOS_APP_PATH,
        'appium:wdaLocalPort': 8100,
      },
    },
    androidDriver: {
      capabilities: {
        platformName: 'Android',
        'appium:automationName': 'UIAutomator2',
        'appium:deviceName': 'Pixel 9',
        'appium:udid': process.env.ANDROID_UDID,
        'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH,
        'appium:systemPort': 8200,
      },
    },
  },
  // Single Appium server manages both sessions:
  services: [['appium', { command: 'appium', args: { port: 4723 } }]],
});
```

```typescript
// Cross-platform push notification e2e test (TypeScript):
import type { MultiRemoteBrowser } from 'webdriverio';

describe('cross-platform push notification', () => {
  it('iOS sender triggers Android receiver notification', async () => {
    const ios = (browser as MultiRemoteBrowser).iOSDriver;
    const android = (browser as MultiRemoteBrowser).androidDriver;

    // iOS: send a message via the chat app
    await ios.$('~compose-button').click();
    await ios.$('~recipient-field').setValue('android-user@example.com');
    await ios.$('~message-field').setValue('Hello from iOS!');
    await ios.$('~send-button').click();

    // Android: wait for push notification to arrive (up to 10s)
    await android.waitUntil(
      async () => {
        await android.openNotifications();
        const notif = await android.$('android=new UiSelector().textContains("Hello from iOS!")');
        return notif.isDisplayed();
      },
      { timeout: 10_000, interval: 1_000 }
    );

    // Tap the notification on Android to deep-link into the chat thread
    await android.$('android=new UiSelector().textContains("Hello from iOS!")').click();
    await expect(android.$('~chat-thread-header')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```

**[community] Both multiremote driver sessions must use different Appium ports
(`wdaLocalPort` for iOS, `systemPort` for Android) even when sharing a single Appium
server — failing to set distinct ports causes the second session to inherit the first
session's port assignment and both fail to start:** WHY: Appium runs the drivers in
parallel processes; port collision causes a bind error that surfaces as a cryptic
`EADDRINUSE` in Appium logs, not a clear WDIO error.

**[community] `browser.getInstance('iOSDriver')` (string-based access) is not
type-safe in TypeScript — prefer the declaration-merged `(browser as
MultiRemoteBrowser).iOSDriver` which gives full `WebdriverIO.Browser` type
inference:** WHY: `getInstance()` returns `WebdriverIO.Browser | undefined` and
requires a null check. The declaration merge approach fails at compile time if the
key name is wrong, catching errors earlier.

**[community] Multiremote tests run sequentially within a `it()` block — there is no
built-in parallel step execution. If iOS and Android steps need to interleave
concurrently (e.g., real-time chat), use `Promise.all([ios.fn(), android.fn()])` to
run browser commands in parallel:** WHY: WDIO executes multiremote commands
sequentially by default; simultaneous actions require explicit `Promise.all()`.

### Pattern 256 — UIAutomator2 v7.3.0 Strict TypeScript Mode: Impact on Test Code

UIAutomator2 driver v7.3.0 (released May 13, 2026) enables strict TypeScript mode
internally. While this is a driver-internal change, it surfaces through stricter type
exports and improved type accuracy that benefits WDIO test code. Specifically,
capability types are now more precise, and `mobile:` command return types are more
accurately typed.

```typescript
// WDIO capability types are now stricter: boolean caps no longer accept strings.
// BEFORE (v7.2.x tolerated this):
const caps = {
  'appium:disableWindowAnimation': 'true',   // ❌ string instead of boolean — tolerated
  'appium:noReset': 'false',                  // ❌ string instead of boolean
};

// AFTER (v7.3.0+ will emit a TypeScript compile error with strict caps typing):
const caps2: WebdriverIO.Capabilities = {
  'appium:disableWindowAnimation': true,     // ✅ correct boolean
  'appium:noReset': false,                   // ✅ correct boolean
};

// If you use a typed config helper, leverage defineConfig() from @wdio/config:
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'Android',
    'appium:automationName': 'UIAutomator2',
    'appium:deviceName': 'Pixel 9',
    // Type errors are now caught at config-write time, not session-start time:
    'appium:disableWindowAnimation': true,    // ✅ TypeScript validates this
    'appium:ignoreUnimportantViews': true,    // ✅ boolean validated
    'appium:newCommandTimeout': 120,          // ✅ number validated
  }],
});

// mobile: command return types are also more precise in v7.3.0:
// Before: (await driver.execute('mobile: getDeviceInfo', {})) was typed as unknown
// After: typed utilities can leverage the stricter exported types

// Helper with strict typing for getDeviceInfo result:
interface DeviceInfo {
  androidId: string;
  apiVersion: string;
  bluetooth: { state: string };
  brand: string;
  carrierName: string;
  displayDensity: number;
  locale: string;
  manufacturer: string;
  model: string;
  networks: Array<{ type: string; state: string }>;
  platformVersion: string;
  realDisplaySize: string;
  timeZone: string;
}

async function getDeviceInfo(driver: WebdriverIO.Browser): Promise<DeviceInfo> {
  return (await driver.execute('mobile: getDeviceInfo', {})) as DeviceInfo;
}
```

**[community] The strict TS mode in UIAutomator2 v7.3.0 only affects the driver's own
TypeScript codebase — your test code is not automatically recompiled with strict mode.
To benefit from stricter cap typing, you must upgrade the `@wdio/types` package
alongside the UIAutomator2 driver:** WHY: `@wdio/types` publishes the capability
type definitions used in test code. The UIAutomator2 driver update alone does not
change the type definitions available in your test project.

**[community] String-typed capability values (`'true'`/`'false'` as strings) that
passed before v7.3.0 now cause TypeScript errors at compile time — but still work at
runtime via Appium's capability coercion:** WHY: Appium coerces string `'true'`/
`'false'` to booleans server-side for backward compatibility. The TypeScript error is
a linting-level improvement, not a runtime change. Fix the types in your config without
worrying about functional regression.

### Pattern 257 — WDIO v9.24.0: Appium Service Selector Performance Optimisation

WDIO v9.24.0 (February 2026) shipped Appium service selector performance improvements.
The enhancement (`trackSelectorPerformance` beta, which graduated to stable in this
release) now automatically profiles how long each selector strategy takes to resolve,
allowing teams to identify slow selectors in CI without manual instrumentation.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — enable selector performance tracking (stable since v9.24.0)
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  services: [
    ['appium', {
      command: 'appium',
      args: {
        port: 4723,
        logLevel: 'info',
      },
      // Selector performance profiling (graduated to stable in v9.24.0):
      trackSelectorPerformance: true,
    }],
  ],
  // Selector performance results are emitted to the WDIO reporter after each spec:
  reporters: [['spec', { addConsoleLogs: true }]],
});
```

```typescript
// Interpreting selector performance output:
// After test run, WDIO emits a table like:
//
//   Selector Performance Report:
//   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬────────┐
//   │ Selector                                         │ Avg (ms) │ Count  │
//   ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼────────┤
//   │ android=new UiSelector().text("Submit")          │    823   │   47   │
//   │ //android.widget.Button[@text='Submit']          │    612   │   23   │
//   │ ~submit-button (accessibility ID)                │     42   │   71   │
//   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────┴────────┘
//
// Selector priority recommendation from this output:
//   1. accessibility ID (~)     → fastest (native OS lookup)
//   2. id (resource-id/name)   → fast
//   3. class chain / predicate string → medium (iOS only)
//   4. XPath                   → slow (full DOM traversal)
//   5. UiSelector text()       → slow (full text scan)

// Refactoring pattern: replace slow UiSelector text() with accessibility ID
class CheckoutPage {
  // BEFORE (slow — 823ms avg per selector report):
  // get submitButton() { return $('android=new UiSelector().text("Submit")'); }

  // AFTER (fast — 42ms avg):
  get submitButton() { return $('~submit-button'); }

  // Where accessibility ID is unavailable, use resource-id:
  get priceLabel() {
    return $('android=new UiSelector().resourceId("com.example.app:id/price_label")');
  }
}
```

**[community] `trackSelectorPerformance: true` adds ~5-10% overhead to test run
time in CI due to the per-selector timing instrumentation — disable it in production
CI runs after the initial profiling sweep:** WHY: The feature is designed for one-time
audits, not permanent enablement. Profile in a dedicated "selector audit" CI workflow,
fix the slow selectors, then disable the flag.

**[community] The selector performance report aggregates across all `it()` blocks in
the spec — if a selector appears in both a fast path and a slow path (e.g., inside
`waitUntil()` polling), the average obscures the worst-case latency:** WHY: The report
uses arithmetic mean. For selectors used in polling loops, the per-call time is low
but cumulative cost is high. Manually time `waitUntil()` blocks to capture total
wait time.

### Pattern 258 — WDIO v9.26.1+: BrowserStack Exit Signal Fix for Unix CI

WDIO v9.25.0 fixed an exit signal handling issue in the `@wdio/browserstack-service`
that caused CI processes on Unix/Linux to hang after test completion. When Appium
sessions on BrowserStack finished, the WDIO runner sometimes received `SIGTERM` but
did not propagate it to worker processes, leaving CI jobs suspended indefinitely.

```typescript
// Defensive CI pattern: always set a hard timeout on the WDIO runner process
// to prevent CI job hang even if exit signals are not correctly propagated.

// package.json scripts:
// "test:mobile:ci": "timeout 900 npx wdio run wdio.conf.ts || true"
//
// GitHub Actions step:
// - name: Run mobile tests
//   timeout-minutes: 15          # ← hard ceiling for the GitHub Actions step
//   run: npx wdio run wdio.conf.ts
//   env:
//     BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BS_USER }}
//     BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BS_KEY }}

// WDIO config: ensure afterSession cleans up connections explicitly
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  afterSession: async (_config, _caps, _specs) => {
    // Explicit session cleanup reduces the chance of dangling connections
    // that cause the exit signal hang:
    try {
      await browser.deleteSession();
    } catch {
      // Session may already be deleted by service teardown
    }
  },

  // Use WDIO's built-in connection timeout to avoid indefinite hangs:
  connectionRetryTimeout: 120_000,
  connectionRetryCount: 3,

  // BrowserStack service configuration:
  services: [
    ['browserstack', {
      // Ensure the service respects the runner exit:
      forcedStop: true,   // kill any lingering Appium/BS processes on exit
    }],
  ],
});
```

**[community] The BrowserStack exit signal bug primarily affects Ubuntu 20.04 and
22.04 runners on GitHub Actions — macOS runners (`macos-14`/`macos-15`) are not
affected because `launchctl` handles process cleanup differently:** WHY: Linux sends
`SIGTERM` to the runner process, which the old BrowserStack service handler did not
relay to WDIO worker subprocess. Upgrade `@wdio/browserstack-service` to >=9.25.0
for the fix.

**[community] Setting `forcedStop: true` in the BrowserStack service causes any
in-progress test session to be marked as `FORCE_STOPPED` in the BrowserStack
dashboard — if your CI pipeline monitors for `FORCE_STOPPED` sessions as a failure
signal, it will false-positive on normal `afterSuite` teardowns:** WHY: `forcedStop`
terminates the Appium subprocess immediately rather than waiting for graceful session
deletion. Use it only in CI exit handlers, not in normal test teardown.

### Pattern 259 — WDIO v9.27.1: BiDi Network Data Capabilities + SPA Shadow Root Memory Leak Fix

WDIO v9.27.1 (released April 30, 2026) delivered two significant stability improvements for
modern web/hybrid-app testing.

**BiDi network data support** extends the existing `networkAddIntercept` / `networkContinueRequest`
family with typed data-payload access — captured request and response bodies are now available
via the `NetworkDataResponse` type exposed from `webdriverio`.

**Shadow root memory leak fix**: When an Angular or React SPA navigated between routes, orphaned
shadow root references accumulated in WDIO's element cache. The fix deregisters shadow roots on
page navigation, preventing the heap from growing unboundedly in long test suites.

```typescript
// WDIO v9.27.1+: typed BiDi network data interception
import type { NetworkDataResponse } from 'webdriverio';

// Register a network intercept for API calls
const interceptId = await browser.networkAddIntercept({
  phases: ['responseStarted'],
  urlPatterns: [{ type: 'string', pattern: '**/api/v1/**' }],
});

// Listen to response data events
browser.on('bidiResponseStarted', async (event: NetworkDataResponse) => {
  const { request, response } = event;
  // Inspect response body before it reaches the app
  console.log('Status:', response.status);
  console.log('URL:', request.url);
});

// Perform action that triggers the API call
await $('~searchButton').click();

// Always clean up intercepts to prevent memory leaks in long suites
await browser.networkRemoveIntercept(interceptId);
```

**[community] Failing to call `networkRemoveIntercept()` after each test in a long SPA test
suite causes WDIO's BiDi intercept registry to grow unboundedly — each registered intercept
subscribes to a Node.js `EventEmitter` channel, and Node's default `MaxListenersExceededWarning`
fires after 11 registered listeners:** WHY: WDIO does not auto-clean intercepts between tests;
the BiDi channel persists for the full browser session. Call `networkRemoveIntercept` in
`afterEach` or use `using` resource management with a wrapper.

**[community] The shadow root memory leak in WDIO < v9.27.1 only manifests in SPA navigation
(React Router / Angular Router) — apps that reload the page between tests are not affected
because the full document reload already discards shadow roots:** WHY: Page reload triggers a
new browsing context document, which clears all element handles. Shadow roots orphaned by
client-side navigation (without a document reload) were the only leaking case.

**[community] BiDi `bidiResponseStarted` events on iOS WebView require `appium:webviewConnectRetries`
set to ≥ 3 and `appium:includeSafariInWebviews: true` to be reliably fired — the WebView context
must be fully attached before the intercept is registered:** WHY: iOS WKWebView attaches to the
Appium/CDP bridge asynchronously. Intercepts registered before the context is fully attached are
silently ignored.

---

### Pattern 260 — WDIO v9.27.0: `multiRemoteBrowser` Rename (Breaking camelCase Fix)

WDIO v9.27.0 renamed the global `multiremotebrowser` (all-lowercase) to `multiRemoteBrowser`
(camelCase) to align with WDIO's standard naming conventions. Projects using multiremote for
cross-platform iOS + Android testing must update their TypeScript declarations and any
direct global references.

```typescript
// Before (v9.26.x and earlier):
// multiremotebrowser.iOS.browser.findElement(...)
// declare const multiremotebrowser: MultiRemoteBrowser<'async'>;

// After (v9.27.0+):
// multiRemoteBrowser.iOS.browser.findElement(...)

// wdio.conf.ts — multiremote capability config (unchanged)
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  capabilities: {
    iOS: {
      capabilities: {
        platformName: 'iOS',
        'appium:deviceName': 'iPhone 16',
        'appium:platformVersion': '18.3',
        'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
        'appium:app': process.env.IOS_APP_PATH!,
      },
    },
    Android: {
      capabilities: {
        platformName: 'Android',
        'appium:deviceName': 'emulator-5554',
        'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
        'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,
      },
    },
  },
});

// In your test file — use camelCase multiRemoteBrowser:
it('sends a push notification from Android, receives on iOS', async () => {
  // Android side: trigger a push notification
  await multiRemoteBrowser.Android.browser.$('~sendPushBtn').click();

  // iOS side: wait for and dismiss the notification
  const iOSAlert = multiRemoteBrowser.iOS.browser.$('-ios predicate string:type == "XCUIElementTypeAlert"');
  await iOSAlert.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
  await multiRemoteBrowser.iOS.browser.$('~Accept').click();
});
```

**[community] The `multiremotebrowser` → `multiRemoteBrowser` rename is a silent runtime
failure in JavaScript projects (no TypeScript error) — the all-lowercase `multiremotebrowser`
is now `undefined`, causing a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` that appears
only when the first multiremote method is called:** WHY: JavaScript doesn't enforce variable
names at compile time. Add `tsc --noEmit` to your CI pipeline or use `@wdio/globals/types`
strictly so TypeScript catches the missing global before runtime.

**[community] VS Code IntelliSense may still suggest the old `multiremotebrowser` spelling
even after upgrading to v9.27.0 if the `@wdio/globals/types` declarations in `node_modules`
are cached — run `npx tsc --build --force` and reload the VS Code TypeScript server to
flush the old types:** WHY: VS Code caches `.d.ts` files from `node_modules` for performance;
after a package upgrade the old declaration file may remain in the compilation cache until
explicitly invalidated.

---

### Pattern 261 — WDIO v9: `tsx` Auto-Compilation (ts-node No Longer Needed)

Starting with WDIO v9 (confirmed in the TypeScript documentation and v9.27.x release notes),
WebdriverIO automatically compiles TypeScript configuration and test files when `tsx` is
installed as a `devDependency`. The older `ts-node`/`@ts-node/esm` setup is no longer
required. This simplifies TypeScript project setup significantly.

```bash
# Install tsx instead of ts-node
npm install --save-dev tsx

# Remove ts-node (optional, but reduces dependency tree)
npm uninstall ts-node @types/ts-node
```

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — standard typed config, no ts-node setup needed
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  runner: 'local',
  framework: 'mocha',
  reporters: ['spec'],
  specs: ['./test/specs/**/*.ts'],
  // No need for require: ['ts-node/register'] or autoCompileOpts
});
```

```json
// tsconfig.json — required by tsx auto-detection
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "types": ["node", "@wdio/globals/types", "@wdio/mocha-framework"]
  },
  "include": ["test/**/*.ts", "wdio.conf.ts"]
}
```

**[community] If both `tsx` and `ts-node` are installed, WDIO v9 prefers `tsx` but may emit
a deprecation warning about the presence of `ts-node`. Remove `ts-node` to suppress the
warning and avoid potential module resolution conflicts:** WHY: Both `tsx` and `ts-node`
register `.ts` file transformers in Node's require/import hooks; having both registered can
cause double-transform warnings and subtle module identity mismatches (two instances of the
same module).

**[community] `tsx` does NOT perform type-checking — it transpiles only. Your CI pipeline
must run `npx tsc --noEmit` as a separate step, otherwise TypeScript type errors are
silently swallowed during test execution:** WHY: `tsx` uses `esbuild` internally for fast
transpilation and strips types without validating them. The WDIO docs explicitly note "run
`tsc` separately for type-checking."

**[community] The `tsconfig.json` file must be in the same directory as `wdio.conf.ts`
for `tsx` auto-detection to work. Monorepo setups with `tsconfig.json` at a parent directory
require either symlinking or explicitly setting `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH` env variable:** WHY:
`tsx` searches for `tsconfig.json` relative to the entry file's directory, not the Node
working directory.

### Pattern 262 — UIAutomator2 v7.2.3 + Server v10.0.1 Upgrade Path

UIAutomator2 driver v7.2.3 (May 11, 2026) upgrades the bundled server from v9.11.2 to
v10.0.1. The UIAutomator2 server v10.0.0 is an ESM-only migration (documented in Cycle 20,
Pattern 248). Key additional notes for v10.0.1:

- **Named imports only**: `import { AndroidDriver } from 'appium-uiautomator2-server'`
  (default import `import AndroidDriver from ...` no longer works)
- **Type exports added in v10.1.0**: The `@types/appium-uiautomator2-server` separate package
  is no longer needed; types ship with the package itself.
- **Promise handling**: Bluebird removed in UIAutomator2 driver v7.2.0; server v10.0+ uses
  native Promises throughout. Code that caught `.catch()` on Bluebird-specific rejection
  reasons must be updated to standard `Promise.reject` patterns.

```typescript
// ESM import pattern for UIAutomator2 server v10+ (in custom plugin/driver code)
// ✅ Named import (ESM)
import { UIAutomator2Server } from 'appium-uiautomator2-server';

// ❌ Default import — fails in v10+
// import UIAutomator2Server from 'appium-uiautomator2-server'; // TypeError

// In WDIO test configs: driver version pinning recommendation
// package.json
// "appium-uiautomator2-driver": ">=7.2.3"  // gets server v10.0.1+
// "appium-xcuitest-driver": ">=11.1.0"     // gets screen recording wrappers

// Runtime check for Bluebird removal (if you relied on .isCancelled(), etc.):
// Bluebird-specific: promise.isCancelled()  ← no longer exists
// Native equivalent: use AbortController for cancellable operations
const controller = new AbortController();
const { signal } = controller;

const result = await Promise.race([
  browser.waitUntil(() => $('~myElement').isDisplayed(), { timeout: 10_000 }),
  new Promise<never>((_, reject) =>
    signal.addEventListener('abort', () => reject(new Error('Aborted')))
  ),
]);
```

**[community] UIAutomator2 server v10.0.0 ESM migration broke the `appium-chromedriver`
package on older Node 18 setups that used `require()` to import UIAutomator2 server
internals — the fix is to upgrade to Node 20+ where `import()` dynamic async imports
work correctly in all contexts:** WHY: Node 18 supports ESM but has edge cases with dynamic
`import()` of packages that use top-level `await` — UIAutomator2 server v10 uses top-level
`await` in its module initializer.

**[community] Pinning `appium-uiautomator2-driver` to `"7.2.2"` to avoid the server v10
ESM migration will cause a Dependabot/Renovate auto-upgrade alert — add an explicit ignore
rule for this package or upgrade to Node 20+ to resolve the underlying compatibility
issue:** WHY: Security bots flag any package pinned below the latest version as potentially
vulnerable; the mismatch is a compatibility issue, not a security bug.

### Pattern 263 — UIAutomator2 v7.1.0: `mobile:setStylusHandwriting` (Security Flag Pattern)

UIAutomator2 v7.1.0 (March 24, 2026) added `mobile:setStylusHandwriting` to toggle Android's
stylus handwriting recognition on/off for test isolation. This command requires explicit
activation via the Appium security flag `--allow-insecure=stylusHandwritingControl` because
it modifies device input method settings that persist across sessions.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — enable the security flag in Appium service config
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export const config = defineConfig({
  services: [
    ['appium', {
      command: 'appium',
      args: {
        allowInsecure: ['stylusHandwritingControl'],
      },
    }],
  ],
  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'Android',
    'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
    'appium:deviceName': 'emulator-5554',
    'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,
  }],
});

// In a test that exercises a handwriting input field:
describe('Stylus handwriting input', () => {
  before(async () => {
    // Enable stylus handwriting for the test suite
    await browser.execute('mobile: setStylusHandwriting', { enable: true });
  });

  after(async () => {
    // Always restore: the setting persists on the emulator between sessions
    await browser.execute('mobile: setStylusHandwriting', { enable: false });
  });

  it('accepts handwritten text in the notes field', async () => {
    const notesField = await $('~notesInputField');
    await notesField.click();
    // Verify that the stylus handwriting IME is active
    const currentIme = await browser.getCurrentActivity();
    expect(currentIme).toContain('StylusHandwriting');
    // ... draw stylus strokes via W3C Actions API pointer events
  });
});
```

**[community] `mobile:setStylusHandwriting` has no effect on real Android devices that ship
without a stylus (non-Note/Tab S-series) — the IME is never installed on those devices, so
the command silently no-ops:** WHY: Android's stylus handwriting IME (`android.os.SystemService.STYLUS_HANDWRITING_SERVICE`) is only present on devices with `PackageManager.FEATURE_STYLUS_HANDWRITING`. Guard with `getDeviceInfo()` before enabling.

**[community] The `stylusHandwritingControl` security flag must be added to **both** the
Appium server `--allow-insecure` list **and** the session capability `appium:allowInsecure`
if you use Appium 3 in remote mode (e.g., BrowserStack / Sauce Labs) — cloud providers
whitelist these flags per-request, not at the server level:** WHY: Appium 3's security model
separates server-level permissions (configured by the server admin) from session-level
permissions (requested by the client). Cloud providers only honor session-level flags to
maintain multi-tenant security boundaries.

### Pattern 264 — XCUITest v11.2.0: Bluebird Removal (Native Promise Migration)

XCUITest v11.2.0 (May 4, 2026) removed the `bluebird` promise library, completing the
ecosystem-wide migration to native Promises that UIAutomator2 v7.2.0 started. If your
project uses XCUITest driver internals (custom plugins, direct imports) with Bluebird-specific
methods, they must be migrated to native Promise equivalents.

```typescript
// Common Bluebird patterns that need migration in custom Appium plugins:

// ❌ Bluebird-specific: Promise.any (Bluebird equivalent of Promise.any)
// import B from 'bluebird';
// await B.any([promise1, promise2]);

// ✅ Native ES2021 equivalent:
await Promise.any([promise1, promise2]);

// ❌ Bluebird .tap() for side effects without modifying the resolved value
// await getElement().tap(el => console.log('found:', el.id));

// ✅ Native equivalent using .then():
await getElement().then(el => { console.log('found:', el); return el; });

// ❌ Bluebird Promise.delay() in test timeouts
// await B.delay(500);

// ✅ Use WDIO's built-in waitUntil instead (never use arbitrary delays):
await browser.waitUntil(
  async () => (await $('~loadingSpinner').isDisplayed()) === false,
  { timeout: 5_000, interval: 100 }
);

// Timeout cancellation — Bluebird had .cancel(); native uses AbortController:
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 5_000);

const result = await Promise.race([
  fetchSomething(),
  new Promise<never>((_, reject) =>
    ac.signal.addEventListener('abort', () => reject(new Error('Timeout')))
  ),
]);
```

**[community] Custom Appium plugins that imported from `appium/support` indirectly received
Bluebird through the now-removed transitive dependency — after XCUITest v11.2.0, Appium's
own `@appium/support` package also removed Bluebird, so any custom plugin using
`support.util.cancellableDelay()` must be updated:** WHY: `@appium/support` was the last
internal Appium package shipping Bluebird; its removal is tracked in the Appium 3.4 milestone.

### Pattern 265 — XCUITest v11.3.0: `download-wda` CLI Command

XCUITest v11.3.0 (May 9, 2026) introduced the `download-wda` CLI command, enabling CI
pipelines to pre-download and cache a signed WebDriverAgent bundle independently of a running
Appium session. Previously, WDA was built or downloaded only when a session was initiated,
which slowed cold CI starts.

```bash
# Download WDA to a local cache directory (CI pre-setup step):
appium driver run xcuitest download-wda --output ./wda-cache/WebDriverAgentRunner.ipa

# In GitHub Actions — cache the downloaded WDA across runs:
# .github/workflows/ios-tests.yml
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ios-tests.yml
jobs:
  ios-test:
    runs-on: macos-15
    steps:
      - name: Cache WebDriverAgent
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        id: wda-cache
        with:
          path: ./wda-cache
          key: wda-${{ runner.os }}-xcuitest-v11.3.0

      - name: Download WDA (if not cached)
        if: steps.wda-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          npm install -g appium
          appium driver install xcuitest
          appium driver run xcuitest download-wda --output ./wda-cache/WebDriverAgentRunner.ipa

      - name: Run tests with pre-downloaded WDA
        run: npx wdio run wdio.conf.ts
        env:
          APPIUM_WDA_PATH: ./wda-cache/WebDriverAgentRunner.ipa
```

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — point XCUITest to the pre-downloaded WDA
export const config = {
  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'iOS',
    'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
    'appium:deviceName': 'iPhone 16 Simulator',
    // Use pre-built WDA from cache to skip rebuild:
    'appium:usePreinstalledWDA': true,
    'appium:webDriverAgentUrl': process.env.APPIUM_WDA_PATH ?? undefined,
  }],
};
```

**[community] `download-wda` only downloads the **simulator** WDA binary by default — for
real device testing you still need to sign the WDA using `sign-wda` (added in v11.4.0) with
your `.p12` certificate and provisioning profile:** WHY: Simulator WDA binaries are unsigned
(iOS simulators don't enforce code signing), but real devices require a valid Apple development
certificate. The two CLI commands are designed to be used together in a real-device CI pipeline.

**[community] The `APPIUM_WDA_PATH` environment variable is not an official Appium variable —
it's a convention shown in the community setup guides. The actual capability to configure a
pre-downloaded WDA path in XCUITest is `appium:bootstrapPath` (for the WDA project root)
or `appium:derivedDataPath` (for the Xcode derived data dir):** WHY: Naming confusion
between official capabilities and community conventions has caused teams to set the wrong
environment variable and wonder why WDA is still being rebuilt.

---

### Pattern 266 — XCUITest v11.4.0: `sign-wda` CLI for Real-Device WDA Re-Signing

XCUITest v11.4.0 (May 13, 2026) adds the `sign-wda` CLI command via `appium driver run
xcuitest sign-wda`. This enables signing or inspecting a downloaded WDA bundle with a team's
own Apple development certificate, completing the `download-wda` → `sign-wda` → deploy CI
workflow for real-device testing without requiring Xcode to rebuild WDA from source.

```bash
# Sign a downloaded WDA IPA with your P12 certificate:
appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda \
  --wda-path ./wda-cache/WebDriverAgentRunner.ipa \
  --signing-cert ./certs/team-dev.p12 \
  --provisioning-profile ./certs/wildcard-dev.mobileprovision \
  --output ./wda-signed/WebDriverAgentRunner.ipa

# Inspect existing signing info (no modification):
appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda \
  --wda-path ./wda-cache/WebDriverAgentRunner.ipa \
  --inspect
# Output shows: Bundle ID, Team Identifier, Certificate details
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: full download → sign → test workflow for real iOS devices
- name: Sign WDA for real device
  run: |
    # Write P12 from secret:
    echo "${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}" | base64 -d > ./certs/team-dev.p12
    echo "${{ secrets.MOBILEPROVISION_BASE64 }}" | base64 -d > ./certs/wildcard-dev.mobileprovision

    appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda \
      --wda-path ./wda-cache/WebDriverAgentRunner.ipa \
      --signing-cert ./certs/team-dev.p12 \
      --provisioning-profile ./certs/wildcard-dev.mobileprovision \
      --output ./wda-signed/WebDriverAgentRunner.ipa
  env:
    P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
```

**[community] `sign-wda` requires macOS — it shells out to `codesign` and `security` CLI
tools which are only available on macOS hosts. Running it on a Linux CI runner (e.g., to
pre-sign for a macOS test step) will fail with `command not found: codesign`:** WHY:
Apple's `codesign` binary is macOS-only. For fully Linux-based CI pipelines, use
`ios-deploy` or `ldid` alternatives, or use a macOS-hosted runner for the signing step.

**[community] The bundle ID embedded in the pre-downloaded WDA IPA must match the bundle ID
in your provisioning profile — if `download-wda` fetches a WDA built with a different bundle
ID, `sign-wda` will sign it successfully but Appium will fail to install it on the device
with `INSTALL_FAILED_INVALID_PROVISIONING_PROFILE`:** WHY: iOS device trust is anchored to
bundle ID + team ID in the provisioning profile; re-signing changes the certificate chain
but does not alter the embedded bundle ID.

**[community] After re-signing, the WDA bundle's `Info.plist` CFBundleVersion is unchanged —
if your device already has a WDA installed with the same bundle ID but a different team's
certificate, `usePreinstalledWDA: true` will fail because iOS rejects apps signed by different
teams even with identical bundle IDs:** WHY: iOS enforces certificate pinning at the team level
for installed apps; a different team's certificate causes `MismatchedApplicationIdentifierEntitlement`
on install, which Appium surfaces as a cryptic session creation error.

---

### Pattern 267 — `@wdio/mcp` Model Context Protocol Server (February 2026)

`@wdio/mcp` (released February 4, 2026) provides a Model Context Protocol server that
exposes WebdriverIO's automation capabilities to AI assistants (Claude Desktop, VS Code
Copilot, Cursor, etc.). It is the "one server for browsers and mobile apps" counterpart to
Playwright's MCP server, built on top of the WDIO session you already have running.

```bash
# Install as a dev dependency:
npm install --save-dev @wdio/mcp
```

```json
// Claude Desktop: ~/.config/claude/claude_desktop_config.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "webdriverio": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["wdio-mcp", "--port", "4321"],
      "env": {
        "WDIO_CONFIG": "./wdio.conf.ts"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```json
// VS Code Copilot: .vscode/settings.json
{
  "github.copilot.chat.experimental.mcpServers": {
    "webdriverio": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["wdio-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "WDIO_CONFIG": "./wdio.conf.ts"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```typescript
// What @wdio/mcp exposes to the AI assistant:
// - navigate(url): open a URL in the browser/app
// - click(selector): click an element by selector
// - type(selector, text): type text into an element
// - screenshot(): capture current screen state
// - getPageSource(): get full page/screen XML/HTML
// - findElement(selector): locate an element and describe it
// - scroll(direction, amount): scroll the screen
// - waitForElement(selector, timeout): wait for element to appear
//
// The AI assistant can use these tools to: generate test scripts,
// debug failing selectors, explore app structure, and write POM classes.

// Example: ask Claude "write a test for the login flow"
// Claude calls: navigate('/login') → screenshot() → type('#email', ...) → click('#submit')
// ...and generates the corresponding WDIO TypeScript test file
```

**[community] `@wdio/mcp` starts its own Appium/browser session when invoked via MCP — it
does NOT attach to an already-running WDIO test session. This means running `@wdio/mcp`
and your test suite simultaneously requires separate Appium port assignments to avoid port
conflicts (use `appium:systemPort` for Android, `appium:wdaLocalPort` for iOS):** WHY:
MCP servers are designed to be long-lived autonomous processes; WDIO's test runner creates
sessions per-spec. They are architecturally separate from each other.

**[community] The AI assistant's `@wdio/mcp` context does not persist between chat sessions
in Claude Desktop — each new chat opens a fresh MCP connection, which means the AI loses
knowledge of elements discovered in a previous exploration session. Use `getPageSource()` at
the start of each session to re-establish context:** WHY: Claude Desktop creates a new MCP
client connection per conversation thread; the WDIO driver session may still be running (if
not explicitly closed), but the AI's in-context knowledge of the app state is reset.

**[community] `@wdio/mcp` screenshot() returns a base64 PNG string — LLM token consumption
for a full-screen mobile screenshot (1080×2400) at full quality can exceed 8,000 tokens per
call, which quickly exhausts context windows in multi-step exploration sessions. Configure
`screenshotQuality: 'low'` in the MCP server options for exploration, and `'high'` only for
assertion generation:** WHY: Mobile screenshots are high-resolution; base64 encoding inflates
size by ~33%, and the vision model encoding further inflates token usage. At 8K tokens/screenshot,
a 10-step exploration uses 80K tokens — near GPT-4/Claude's context limits.

---

### Pattern 268 — WDIO v9: `expect.soft()` Built-In Soft Assertions

Since `expect-webdriverio` v5.2.0 (shipped with WDIO v9.16+), soft assertions are available
natively via `expect.soft()`. This allows a test to continue executing after an assertion
failure, collecting all failures and reporting them together at the end of the test, instead
of stopping at the first failure.

```typescript
// Soft assertions — collect all failures, report together at test end
describe('Product detail page validation', () => {
  it('validates all visible product fields in one pass', async () => {
    await browser.url('/products/widget-x');

    // Soft assertions: test continues even if these fail
    await expect.soft(await $('~productTitle').getText())
      .toEqual('Widget X Pro');

    await expect.soft(await $('~productPrice').getText())
      .toMatch(/\$\d+\.\d{2}/);

    await expect.soft(await $('~addToCartButton').isDisplayed())
      .toBe(true);

    await expect.soft(await $('~productRating').getAttribute('value'))
      .toBeGreaterThanOrEqual('4.0');

    // This hard assertion runs regardless and throws immediately if it fails:
    await expect(await $('~productImage').isDisplayed()).toBe(true);

    // At end of test, WDIO reports ALL soft assertion failures together
  });
});

// SoftAssertionService (auto-included since WDIO v9.16): ensures soft failures
// are surfaced as test failures even if the test function itself didn't throw.
// No manual configuration needed — works out of the box.

// Pattern: combine soft assertions for field validations with hard assertions
// for critical path (navigation, session state):
it('validates form submission result', async () => {
  await $('~submitButton').click();

  // Hard assertion: the page must navigate away (session-critical)
  await expect(browser).toHaveUrl('/confirmation');

  // Soft assertions: validate all confirmation fields
  await expect.soft(await $('~confirmationTitle').getText())
    .toContain('Order Confirmed');
  await expect.soft(await $('~orderNumber').isDisplayed())
    .toBe(true);
  await expect.soft(await $('~estimatedDelivery').isDisplayed())
    .toBe(true);
});
```

**[community] `expect.soft()` is **not** natively available in the older `@wdio/expect-webdriverio`
package pinned to v4.x — it requires `expect-webdriverio@5.2.0+`. After upgrading, run
`npx tsc --noEmit` to catch any type mismatches since the v5 type signatures changed for
chained matchers:** WHY: The v4→v5 upgrade is a peer-dependency bump when upgrading
`webdriverio` to v9.16+; teams that pinned `expect-webdriverio` separately may stay on v4.

**[community] Soft assertion failures in `beforeEach` hooks do NOT prevent the `it()` block
from running — this is by design (soft = keep going), but teams expect hook failures to skip
the test. Use hard `expect()` in `beforeEach` for preconditions; reserve `expect.soft()` for
validations inside test bodies:** WHY: Hook failures are typically precondition failures; soft
assertions in hooks produce confusing reports where the test "passed" its soft assertions but
a setup step quietly failed.

**[community] `getSoftFailures()` is available on the `expect` object to programmatically
inspect pending soft failures mid-test (before they are reported). This enables conditional
logic: if a soft assertion failed, skip dependent soft assertions to reduce noise in the report:**
WHY: Cascading soft failures (e.g., title wrong AND all sub-elements wrong due to wrong page)
are less useful than a single root-cause failure; checking `expect.getSoftFailures().length > 0`
lets you short-circuit.

---

### Pattern 269 — WDIO v9 Visual Service: Storybook Runner (Beta)

`@wdio/visual-service` includes a Storybook runner mode that automatically captures
screenshots of every Storybook story and compares them to baselines for visual regression
testing — without writing individual test specs.

```bash
# Run visual regression on all Storybook stories:
npx wdio tests/configs/wdio.local.desktop.storybook.conf.ts --storybook

# Run with parallel sharding for faster execution:
npx wdio tests/configs/wdio.local.desktop.storybook.conf.ts --storybook \
  --numShards 4

# Skip specific stories:
npx wdio tests/configs/wdio.local.desktop.storybook.conf.ts --storybook \
  --skipStories "Button--loading,Button--disabled"

# Capture only a specific component area (not full viewport):
npx wdio tests/configs/wdio.local.desktop.storybook.conf.ts --storybook \
  --clip --clipSelector ".storybook-button"
```

```typescript
// wdio.local.desktop.storybook.conf.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';
import type { VisualServiceOptions } from '@wdio/visual-service';

export const config = defineConfig({
  baseUrl: 'http://localhost:6006',   // Storybook dev server URL

  services: [
    ['visual', {
      baselineFolder: './visual-baselines/storybook',
      formatImageName: '{tag}-{width}x{height}',
      screenshotPath: '.tmp/screenshots',
      autoSaveBaseline: true,         // auto-create baselines on first run
      isHybridApp: false,
    } satisfies VisualServiceOptions],
  ],

  // Storybook runner uses its own spec discovery — no specs array needed
  // when running with --storybook flag.
});
```

```typescript
// Interaction testing: capture snapshots at specific component states
it('Button hover state visual check', async () => {
  // Wait for Storybook component to load:
  await browser.waitForStorybookComponentToBeLoaded({ id: 'button--hover' });

  // Simulate hover:
  const button = await $('button.storybook-button');
  await button.moveTo();

  // Take a named snapshot at the hovered state:
  await expect(browser).toMatchScreenSnapshot('button-hover-state');
});
```

**[community] The Storybook runner with `--numShards N` creates N WDIO worker instances
that each navigate the Storybook iframe independently — if your Storybook uses a shared
indexedDB-backed store (e.g., a Redux demo app), shards will overwrite each other's store
state. Disable story state persistence or use `--numShards 1` for stateful stories:** WHY:
Each shard runs in its own browser context but targets the same Storybook server; stories
that mutate shared IndexedDB state from within their decorators cause non-deterministic
baseline captures.

**[community] `autoSaveBaseline: true` silently passes ALL stories on first run (no baseline
exists → auto-created → comparison passes). This means the first CI run with Storybook
visual testing always green — only subsequent runs catch regressions. Commit baselines to
your repository before enabling visual checks in branch CI:** WHY: The visual service is
designed to require deliberate baseline approval; auto-saving is a convenience for local
setup, not a CI strategy.

---

### Pattern 270 — WDIO v9.27.1: Shadow Root Memory Leak Guard for SPA Navigation

WDIO v9.27.1 fixed a shadow root element handle memory leak that affected Single-Page
Applications using React Router or Angular Router. When a component with a shadow root was
rendered, then the route changed without a full page reload, WDIO retained stale shadow root
references in its internal element cache. The fix deregisters shadow roots on page navigation
events. This pattern documents the defensive coding style to adopt regardless of WDIO version.

```typescript
// Defensive shadow root access pattern: always re-query after navigation
// ❌ Fragile: cache shadow root reference across navigation
const shadowHost = await $('my-custom-element');
const shadowRoot = await shadowHost.shadow$('div.content');  // cached reference

await browser.url('/another-route');   // navigation → shadow root is now stale

await shadowRoot.isDisplayed();  // throws StaleElementReferenceError on WDIO < v9.27.1
                                 // (fixed in v9.27.1 but pattern is still best practice)

// ✅ Robust: re-query shadow DOM after any navigation
await browser.url('/another-route');

// Re-query from scratch after navigation
const freshShadowRoot = await $('my-custom-element').shadow$('div.content');
await freshShadowRoot.isDisplayed();  // always works

// ✅ Page Object pattern for SPA with shadow DOM
class MyComponentPage {
  // Never cache ChainablePromiseElement as a class instance property across navigations
  get contentPanel() {
    // Getter re-evaluates on every access → always fresh
    return $('my-custom-element').shadow$('div.content');
  }

  async isLoaded(): Promise<boolean> {
    return (await this.contentPanel).isDisplayed();
  }
}
```

**[community] The WDIO v9.27.1 shadow root fix prevents the **internal** reference leak but
does not prevent your test code from holding stale `ChainablePromiseElement` references in
local variables — if you `const el = await $$('...shadow...')` before navigation and use `el`
after, it still throws `StaleElementReferenceError`:** WHY: The fix deregisters internal
WDIO cache entries; it does not make externally-held references magically fresh. The user-facing
best practice of re-querying after navigation is still required.

**[community] In WDIO v9.27.x, shadow DOM traversal via `.shadow$()` requires the host
element to be in the DOM at the time of the call — unlike Playwright's `locator()` which
returns a lazy handle, WDIO's `shadow$()` resolves immediately. In SPA apps with
component lazy-loading, add a `waitForExist()` on the host element before calling
`.shadow$()` to avoid `NoSuchElementError`:** WHY: Playwright's locator API is lazy (evaluated
at interaction time); WDIO's `$()` resolves the element handle synchronously on the first
`await`. Lazy-loaded components that have not yet mounted return `null` element handles.

### Pattern 271 — UIAutomator2 v7.3.0: Strict TypeScript Mode — Impact on Test Code

UIAutomator2 v7.3.0 (released 2026-05-13) enables TypeScript strict mode in the driver
codebase itself. While this is an internal change, it has a practical downstream effect:
type definitions exported from `appium-uiautomator2-driver` are now stricter. Any TypeScript
test project that imports driver types (e.g., for capability declaration merging or custom
command typings) may encounter new compilation errors.

The most common impact is on capability declarations that previously accepted `string | undefined`
but now require explicit union types or `Required<>` wrappers.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — strict-mode-safe Android capability declaration
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

// Use the official AppiumCapabilities type with UIAutomator2-specific extensions
type AndroidCapabilities = WebdriverIO.Capabilities & {
  'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2';
  'appium:deviceName': string;
  'appium:platformVersion': string;
  'appium:app': string;
  'appium:avd'?: string;
  'appium:avdArgs'?: string[];
  'appium:systemPort'?: number;         // Required for parallel execution
  'appium:disableWindowAnimation'?: boolean;
};

// Fails strict mode if 'appium:app' is undefined:
// ❌ const caps: AndroidCapabilities = { 'appium:app': process.env.APP_PATH };
//    → Type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'

// ✅ Use non-null assertion or default:
const androidCaps: AndroidCapabilities = {
  platformName: 'Android',
  'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
  'appium:deviceName': 'emulator-5554',
  'appium:platformVersion': '15.0',
  'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,   // non-null assertion
  'appium:systemPort': Number(process.env.SYSTEM_PORT ?? '8200'),
  'appium:disableWindowAnimation': true,
};

export default defineConfig({
  capabilities: [androidCaps],
  // ...
});
```

**[community] The UIAutomator2 v7.3.0 strict TS mode change causes `tsc --noEmit` failures in
CI pipelines that import driver types transitively via `webdriverio` — even if you never import
`appium-uiautomator2-driver` directly, the stricter union types propagate through WDIO's
internal type declarations:** WHY: TypeScript resolves transitive type imports at compile time;
stricter union types in a dependency tighten the inferred types in your code. Pin
`appium-uiautomator2-driver` to `^7.2.3` until your capability declarations are updated.

**[community] `process.env.APP_PATH!` non-null assertion silences the TypeScript error but
still passes `undefined` to Appium at runtime if the env var is missing — add a startup guard
to catch this early in `onPrepare`:** WHY: TypeScript's `!` operator is a compile-time bypass;
it does not add a runtime check. A missing `APP_PATH` causes a cryptic Appium session creation
error rather than a clear "env var missing" message.

### Pattern 272 — XCUITest v11.3.1: `remotexpc` 1.1.8 Tunnel Cleanup and Connection Stability

XCUITest v11.3.1 (released 2026-05-12) bumped `remotexpc` to version 1.1.8. The `remotexpc`
library manages the secure XPC tunnel between the Appium host and real iOS devices via USB.
Version 1.1.8 addresses tunnel cleanup races — when a test session ended abruptly (e.g.,
process kill in CI), the previous version left orphaned tunnel processes that blocked new
sessions from connecting on the same device.

This pattern shows robust session teardown to complement the library fix:

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — session teardown guard for real iOS device CI
import { Options } from '@wdio/types';
import { exec } from 'child_process';
import { promisify } from 'util';

const execAsync = promisify(exec);

export const config: Options.Testrunner = {
  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'iOS',
    'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
    'appium:deviceName': process.env.IOS_DEVICE_UDID ?? 'iPhone 16',
    'appium:udid': process.env.IOS_DEVICE_UDID,
    'appium:xcodeOrgId': process.env.XCODE_ORG_ID,
    'appium:xcodeSigningId': 'iPhone Developer',
    // v11.3.1+: faster tunnel teardown
    'appium:newCommandTimeout': 120,
  }],

  // Hard-stop lingering tunnel processes after suite completes
  async onComplete(_exitCode, _config, _caps, results) {
    if (process.platform === 'darwin') {
      try {
        // Clean up any orphaned remotexpc processes from this CI agent
        await execAsync('pkill -f "remotexpc" || true');
        await execAsync('pkill -f "xpc_proxy" || true');
      } catch {
        // Ignore — pkill exits non-zero when nothing was found
      }
    }
  },

  // Fail fast on first test failure in CI to avoid tunnel leak accumulation
  bail: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0,
};
```

**[community] On macOS GitHub Actions runners (`macos-15`), remotexpc tunnel processes
orphaned by a SIGKILL sometimes hold the USB multiplexer port. A subsequent `appium driver
run xcuitest download-wda` call on the same runner fails with `EADDRINUSE` — running
`pkill -f remotexpc` before the download-wda step is a reliable mitigation:** WHY: macOS
USB multiplexer (`usbmuxd`) port 27015 is held by the orphaned process. The OS does not
auto-release it until the process exits; `pkill` forces the release.

**[community] `appium:newCommandTimeout: 0` (unlimited timeout) should never be used with
real iOS devices in CI — it causes tunnel connections to be kept alive indefinitely when
tests hang, eventually exhausting the macOS USB descriptor table and blocking all subsequent
device connections on the same machine:** WHY: Each active Appium session holds a remotexpc
tunnel file descriptor. With unlimited timeouts and a hung test, the descriptor is never
released until the Appium process itself is killed.

### Pattern 273 — WDIO `trackSelectorPerformance` Beta: Native Selector Performance Optimizer

The `@wdio/appium-service` ships a built-in **Native Mobile Selector Performance Optimizer**
(MSPO) that profiles XPath selector execution times during a real test run, suggests native
alternatives (`-ios predicate string`, accessibility ID, class chain), validates the
alternatives, and generates JSON / Markdown / CLI reports. iOS only; Android support is
planned for a future release.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — enable MSPO for a periodic optimisation run
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export default defineConfig({
  services: [
    ['appium', {
      command: 'appium',
      args: { address: '127.0.0.1', port: 4723, relaxedSecurity: true },

      // BETA: enable only for dedicated optimisation runs — NOT standard CI
      trackSelectorPerformance: {
        // Required: directories where page-object files live
        pageObjectPaths: ['./test/pageobjects', './test/screens'],
        // Print a summary table to the terminal
        enableCliReport: true,
        // Write a Markdown file alongside the JSON report
        enableMarkdownReport: true,
        // Where to save reports (defaults to wdio outputDir)
        reportPath: './reports/selector-optimizer',
        // Wrap terminal output at 120 chars
        maxLineLength: 120,
      },
    }],
  ],
  // Run only a representative subset of tests during optimisation
  specs: ['./test/pageobjects/**/*.spec.ts'],
});
```

```typescript
// scripts/apply-selector-optimisations.mjs — helper to review MSPO report output
import { readFileSync } from 'fs';

// Load the MSPO JSON report
const report = JSON.parse(
  readFileSync('./reports/selector-optimizer/selector-report.json', 'utf-8')
);

// Print top-10 most impactful optimisations
console.log('=== Top 10 optimisations ===');
report.topOptimisations.slice(0, 10).forEach((opt, i) => {
  console.log(`[${i + 1}] ${opt.file}:${opt.line}`);
  console.log(`  Original : ${opt.original}  (${opt.originalMs}ms avg)`);
  console.log(`  Suggested: ${opt.suggested}  (${opt.suggestedMs}ms avg, -${opt.improvementPct}%)`);
  console.log('');
});
```

**[community] Running `trackSelectorPerformance` alongside standard parallel workers inflates
test duration by 3–8x on large suites because each selector lookup now involves a round-trip
validation step — always gate it behind an env var or a separate npm script so it is never
accidentally enabled in main CI:** WHY: The optimizer validates every suggested alternative
selector during the same test run, doubling the Appium round trips per element lookup.

**[community] The MSPO suggestion engine only proposes native selectors that it can
_validate_ against the current app build — if an accessibility ID was never set in the app
code, the engine will not suggest it even though it would be faster. The report marks these
as "no-faster-alternative-found," which is a signal to add `accessibilityIdentifier` in the
native app code, not a WDIO limitation:** WHY: The optimizer measures what exists; it cannot
invent identifiers that the app does not expose.

**[community] MultiRemote sessions (iOS + Android simultaneous) automatically disable MSPO
even when configured — no warning is emitted at the `warn` log level, only at `debug`. If
you are running a MultiRemote setup and wonder why no report is generated, lower
`logLevel: 'debug'` to see the skip message:** WHY: MSPO requires per-worker selector timing
aggregation which is architecturally incompatible with the MultiRemote session model.

### Pattern 274 — WDIO `browser.emulate()` Full Guide: BiDi-Powered Test Condition Simulation

`browser.emulate()` uses the WebDriver BiDi protocol to patch browser built-ins (`Date`,
`navigator.geolocation`, `window.matchMedia`, `navigator.onLine`, `navigator.userAgent`)
without modifying network traffic. It requires `webSocketUrl: true` in capabilities. Each
call returns a reset function; call it in `afterEach` or use the `using` disposable pattern.

```typescript
// test/specs/dark-mode.spec.ts
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';
import { expect } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('Dark mode and offline simulation', () => {

  it('renders dark theme when prefers-color-scheme is dark', async () => {
    // Emulate dark mode — patches window.matchMedia on the page
    const resetColorScheme = await browser.emulate('colorScheme', 'dark');

    await browser.url('/settings');
    await expect($('[data-testid="theme-indicator"]')).toHaveText('Dark');

    // Always reset so subsequent tests are unaffected
    await resetColorScheme();
  });

  it('shows offline banner when navigator.onLine is false', async () => {
    const resetOnLine = await browser.emulate('onLine', false);

    await browser.url('/dashboard');
    await expect($('[data-testid="offline-banner"]')).toBeDisplayed();

    await resetOnLine();
  });

  it('shows geo-gated content for New York coordinates', async () => {
    const resetGeo = await browser.emulate('geolocation', {
      latitude: 40.7128,
      longitude: -74.0060,
    });

    await browser.url('/deals');
    await expect($('[data-testid="local-deals-title"]')).toHaveText('Deals near New York');

    await resetGeo();
  });

  it('shows subscription expired banner when 30-day trial has lapsed', async () => {
    // Freeze time at 31 days after the trial start date
    const trialStart = new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00Z').getTime();
    const afterTrialExpiry = trialStart + 31 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

    const resetClock = await browser.emulate('clock', {
      now: afterTrialExpiry,
      toFake: ['Date', 'setTimeout', 'setInterval'],
    });

    await browser.url('/subscription');
    await expect($('[data-testid="trial-expired-banner"]')).toBeDisplayed();

    await resetClock();
  });
});
```

**[community] `browser.emulate('colorScheme', ...)` patches `window.matchMedia` but NOT
CSS media queries evaluated server-side (SSR) or in static builds — apps that generate
HTML with embedded dark-mode styles at build time will not respond to the emulation because
those styles are baked in before the browser executes any JavaScript:** WHY: `emulate()` is
a client-side JavaScript monkey patch; it cannot retroactively alter server-generated HTML.
Use the real OS dark mode setting for SSR dark-mode tests.

**[community] `browser.emulate('onLine', false)` patches `navigator.onLine` but does NOT
block network traffic — `fetch()` and `XMLHttpRequest` calls still succeed. If your app
only reads `navigator.onLine` (not `offline` event + actual fetch failure), this emulation
is sufficient; otherwise use `browser.throttle` or a service worker offline handler:** WHY:
The BiDi emulation modifies a browser property; network traffic is handled at the OS level,
outside BiDi's scope.

**[community] The reset function returned by `browser.emulate()` is async and must be
`await`-ed — calling it without `await` in `afterEach` leaves the emulation active for the
next test, causing hard-to-diagnose cross-test contamination:** WHY: The reset function
sends a BiDi command to the browser to restore the original built-in; without awaiting, the
restore command races with the next test's page load.

### Pattern 275 — XCUITest `sign-wda`: Windows/Linux CI Signing Without Xcode

XCUITest v11.4.0 introduced the `sign-wda` CLI task that re-signs a pre-built
`WebDriverAgentRunner.app` bundle on any OS — including Windows and Linux CI agents.
Previously, WDA had to be signed on macOS with Xcode. Now a GitHub Actions runner with no
Xcode can sign WDA using a `.p12` certificate stored as a CI secret.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ios-real-device.yml
name: iOS Real Device Tests
on: [push]

jobs:
  ios-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest   # Non-macOS runner!
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Install Appium and XCUITest driver
        run: |
          npm install -g appium
          appium driver install xcuitest

      - name: Write signing certificate
        run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}" | base64 -d > /tmp/dev-cert.p12

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wda-bundle
          path: /tmp/wda

      - name: Sign WDA
        run: |
          appium driver run xcuitest sign-wda \
            --wda-path /tmp/wda/WebDriverAgentRunner-Runner.app \
            --p12-cert /tmp/dev-cert.p12 \
            --bundle-id "io.appium.WebDriverAgentRunner.${{ github.run_id }}"
        env:
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Run WDIO tests
        run: npx wdio run wdio.conf.ts
        env:
          IOS_WDA_PATH: /tmp/wda/WebDriverAgentRunner-Runner.app
```

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — point to the pre-signed WDA bundle
export const config = {
  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'iOS',
    'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
    'appium:deviceName': process.env.IOS_DEVICE_NAME!,
    'appium:udid': process.env.IOS_DEVICE_UDID!,
    // Use the pre-built and signed WDA instead of building from Xcode
    'appium:usePreinstalledWDA': true,
    'appium:prebuiltWDAPath': process.env.IOS_WDA_PATH,
  }],
};
```

**[community] `sign-wda` with `--p12-cert` and `--p12-key` (separate PEM files) does not
require `P12_PASSWORD` — the tool auto-generates a temporary PKCS12 password internally.
Using the combined `--p12-file` (.p12 format) DOES require either `P12_PASSWORD` env var
or interactive password entry — confusing because both flags look similar in `--help`
output:** WHY: The `--p12-cert/--p12-key` path generates a fresh `.p12` in memory; the
`--p12-file` path loads an existing `.p12` that already has a password embedded.

**[community] Re-signing WDA with a unique `--bundle-id` per CI run (appending `$GITHUB_RUN_ID`)
prevents bundle ID conflicts when multiple CI jobs install WDA on the same pool of shared
real devices simultaneously — without this, Job B's WDA installation silently overwrites
Job A's and can corrupt the in-progress session:** WHY: iOS real devices identify installed
apps by bundle ID; two apps with the same bundle ID are treated as the same app, and
installing the second one terminates the first.

### Pattern 276 — UIAutomator2 v7.2.0: Bluebird Removal — Native Promise Migration Patterns

UIAutomator2 v7.2.0 and XCUITest v11.2.0 both dropped the `bluebird` promise library
in favour of native ES2022 Promises. From a test code perspective this is invisible — WDIO
commands always returned native `Promise` objects even when Appium internally used Bluebird.
However, custom WebdriverIO services or plugins that imported `bluebird` via Appium's
dependency tree may break.

```typescript
// ❌ Bluebird-specific methods no longer available via Appium internals
// Promise.map with concurrency option (NOT in native Promise)
// await Promise.map(elements, async (el) => el.getText(), { concurrency: 3 });

// ❌ Bluebird's .tap() for side-effects (NOT on native Promise)
// await $('~loginButton').tap((el) => console.log('found:', el));

// ✅ Native async/await for sequential element interactions
import { $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const loginBtn = await $('~loginButton');
console.log('found:', await loginBtn.getAccessibilityLabel());
await loginBtn.click();

// ✅ pLimit: native replacement for Bluebird concurrency-limited Promise.map
// npm install p-limit
import pLimit from 'p-limit';

const limit = pLimit(3);   // max 3 concurrent Appium calls
const elements = await $$('~listItem');
const texts = await Promise.all(
  elements.map((el) => limit(() => el.getText()))
);
console.log('All texts:', texts);

// ✅ Native Promise.allSettled for resilient batch element checks
const results = await Promise.allSettled(
  elements.map((el) => el.isDisplayed())
);
const visibleCount = results.filter(
  (r) => r.status === 'fulfilled' && r.value
).length;
console.log(`${visibleCount}/${elements.length} elements visible`);
```

**[community] `pLimit` is a lightweight replacement for Bluebird's concurrency-limited
`Promise.map` — the `p-limit` package is ~0.5 KB, tree-shakeable, and ESM-native.
`bluebird` was 70 KB; removing it from Appium drivers reduces the driver install footprint
noticeably:** WHY: Bluebird was originally added for performance on Node.js < 12; modern
V8 promise internals are competitive with Bluebird for typical test automation workloads.

**[community] `@wdio/allure-reporter`'s `addStep()` implementation used a Bluebird-style
`.spread()` call internally in versions before `@wdio/allure-reporter` v8.40 — after
upgrading UIAutomator2 to v7.2.0+, if Allure steps silently stop attaching screenshots,
check whether your `@wdio/allure-reporter` version is at least 8.40:** WHY: `.spread()` was
a Bluebird prototype method; the reporter now uses `Promise.all()` with destructuring.

### Pattern 277 — WDIO v9.25.0: `waitForClickable()` in Native Context Fix

WDIO v9.25.0 (released 2026-03-10) fixed `waitForClickable()` when called on native
(non-WebView) elements. Prior to this fix, `waitForClickable()` always evaluated clickability
via a CDP/BiDi CSS visibility check, which is only meaningful in a browser context. On native
elements (Appium native context), the CSS check returned `false` for any element, causing
`waitForClickable()` to always time out regardless of the element's actual state.

```typescript
// WDIO v9.25.0+: waitForClickable() works correctly in native context

import { browser, $, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('Checkout flow', () => {

  it('waits for the confirm button to become tappable', async () => {
    await $('~cartTab').click();

    // ✅ v9.25.0+: works correctly in native context
    const confirmBtn = await $('~confirmOrderButton');
    await confirmBtn.waitForClickable({ timeout: 10_000 });
    await confirmBtn.click();

    await expect($('~orderConfirmationScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});

// Polyfill for WDIO < v9.25.0 — can be removed after upgrading
async function waitForNativeClickable(
  selector: string,
  timeoutMs = 10_000
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const el = await $(selector);
      const [enabled, displayed] = await Promise.all([
        el.isEnabled(),
        el.isDisplayed(),
      ]);
      return enabled && displayed;
    },
    {
      timeout: timeoutMs,
      interval: 500,
      timeoutMsg: `Element ${selector} not clickable after ${timeoutMs}ms`,
    }
  );
}
```

**[community] After upgrading to WDIO v9.25.0 to get the native `waitForClickable()` fix,
some teams observed new test failures for elements that were previously always detected as
"not clickable" — these tests were passing because the broken `waitForClickable()` was
silently timing out and the `timeout: 0` default was being treated as "skip wait."
Auditing for `waitForClickable({ timeout: 0 })` calls is recommended after the upgrade:**
WHY: The fixed implementation now actually evaluates native clickability, surfacing genuine
element-state bugs that the broken version was hiding.

**[community] `waitForClickable()` on Android native elements checks `isEnabled()` (the
W3C active/disabled state) but NOT `isDisplayed()` — a hidden-but-enabled element passes
`waitForClickable()`. For scroll-to-reveal patterns, always call `scrollIntoView()` before
`waitForClickable()`:** WHY: The W3C WebDriver spec defines "clickable" as "enabled and not
obscured by a modal." WDIO follows this spec; the displayed/visible check is separate.

---

### Pattern 278 — `@wdio/mcp` Deep-Dive: AI-Assisted Mobile Test Authoring Workflow

The `@wdio/mcp` package (released February 2026) exposes WebdriverIO's browser and Appium
driver state as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, allowing AI assistants (Claude,
Cursor, GitHub Copilot Chat) to inspect the running app, execute actions, and generate test
code in a live session. The key differentiator from Playwright MCP and Appium MCP is a
single unified server for both web and native mobile.

```typescript
// Install: npm install --save-dev @wdio/mcp

// wdio.mcp.conf.ts — config for MCP-assisted authoring sessions (NOT for CI)
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

export default defineConfig({
  runner: 'local',
  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'iOS',
    'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
    'appium:deviceName': 'iPhone 16 Pro',
    'appium:platformVersion': '18.3',
    'appium:app': process.env.IOS_APP_PATH!,
    // BiDi required for full emulate() support in MCP sessions
    webSocketUrl: true,
  }],

  services: [
    // @wdio/mcp listens on a local port and exposes WDIO commands as MCP tools
    ['mcp', {
      port: 3001,   // default 3000; use 3001 to avoid conflict with visual-service
      // Restrict to safe read/interact commands only
      allowedCommands: [
        'getPageSource', 'getContexts', 'switchContext',
        'findElement', 'click', 'setValue', 'getText',
        'takeScreenshot', 'scrollIntoView', 'getAccessibilityLabel',
      ],
    }],
    ['appium', { command: 'appium' }],
  ],

  // Keep the session open after tests complete for interactive MCP exploration
  after: async () => {
    if (process.env.MCP_INTERACTIVE) {
      console.log('MCP server at http://localhost:3001 — attach your AI assistant now');
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5 * 60 * 1000)); // 5 min interactive window
    }
  },
});
```

```json
// .vscode/settings.json — wire Claude Desktop or Cursor to the local MCP server
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wdio-mobile": {
      "url": "http://localhost:3001/sse"
    }
  }
}
```

**[community] `@wdio/mcp` exposes the full live browser/device state to the AI assistant
including element attribute values — do not start an MCP session against an app that
handles real user credentials or PII, as the AI assistant's conversation transcript may
log element text values (passwords, tokens):** WHY: MCP tools return element properties in
plain text to the LLM context window. Use a dedicated test environment with mock data.

**[community] The MCP server port conflicts with `@wdio/visual-service`'s internal diffing
server if both are used in the same WDIO process — visual service defaults to port 3000.
Set `mcp.port: 3001` or `visualService.port: 3001` to avoid the `EADDRINUSE` on startup:**
WHY: Both services bind to `localhost:3000` by default; running both in a single `wdio`
process causes the second service to fail silently.
