### Pattern 279 — `browser.emulate('clock')`: Subscription and Trial-Expiry Time Testing

Fake clock via `browser.emulate('clock', ...)` is the BiDi-native replacement for injecting
`Date` stubs via `browser.execute()`. It patches `Date`, `setTimeout`, and `setInterval`
at the browser level — covering React's `useEffect` timers, third-party analytics trackers,
and any JS that calls `new Date()`.

```typescript
// test/specs/subscription-lifecycle.spec.ts
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';
import { expect } from '@wdio/globals';

const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

// Helper: freeze browser clock at a specific ISO date
async function freezeClockAt(
  isoDate: string
): Promise<() => Promise<void>> {
  return browser.emulate('clock', {
    now: new Date(isoDate).getTime(),
    toFake: ['Date', 'setTimeout', 'setInterval', 'clearTimeout', 'clearInterval'],
  });
}

describe('Subscription lifecycle', () => {
  let resetClock: (() => Promise<void>) | undefined;

  afterEach(async () => {
    if (resetClock) {
      await resetClock();
      resetClock = undefined;
    }
  });

  it('shows trial-active state on day 1', async () => {
    resetClock = await freezeClockAt('2026-06-01T00:00:00Z');
    await browser.url('/account/subscription');
    await expect($('[data-testid="trial-days-remaining"]')).toHaveText('30 days remaining');
  });

  it('shows trial-expired CTA on day 31', async () => {
    resetClock = await freezeClockAt('2026-07-02T00:00:00Z');  // 31 days after June 1
    await browser.url('/account/subscription');
    await expect($('[data-testid="upgrade-cta"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('shows renewal notice 3 days before billing cycle', async () => {
    resetClock = await freezeClockAt('2026-06-28T08:00:00Z');
    await browser.url('/account/subscription');
    await expect($('[data-testid="renewal-notice"]')).toHaveText('Billing in 3 days');
  });
});
```

**[community] `browser.emulate('clock')` only fakes the browser's JS timer APIs — it does
NOT alter `Date` on the Node.js side where WDIO runs. If your test code reads `new Date()`
on the Node side (e.g., in a custom reporter or `browser.execute()` return value comparison),
it uses the real wall clock:** WHY: The BiDi clock patch is scoped to the browser context;
the WDIO test runner process has its own independent JS runtime.

**[community] `browser.emulate('clock')` does NOT advance time automatically after being
set — timers registered before the `emulate` call (e.g., a React `useEffect` with
`setInterval`) will fire only if you call `browser.execute(() => window.__clock.tick(ms))`
after setting the clock. Without a tick, interval-based UI updates (countdowns, progress
bars) appear frozen:** WHY: `emulate('clock')` is equivalent to sinon/FakeTimers `install()`
with the clock paused at the given epoch; manual `tick()` advances synthetic time.

### Pattern 280 — WDIO v9 `scrollIntoView()` Cross-Platform Native Options

WDIO v9 enhanced `element.scrollIntoView()` with native mobile options that abstract
platform-specific scroll implementations. Prior to v9, mobile scrollIntoView required calling
`browser.execute('mobile: scroll', ...)` or building W3C Actions sequences manually.

```typescript
// test/pageobjects/ProductListPage.ts
import { $ } from '@wdio/globals';

export class ProductListPage {

  // Scroll to any element with cross-platform options
  async scrollToProduct(productId: string): Promise<void> {
    const productEl = await $(`[data-testid="product-${productId}"]`);

    await productEl.scrollIntoView({
      // Maximum scroll steps before giving up (default: 10; use higher for long lists)
      maxScrolls: 15,
      // Scroll direction when element is off-screen
      // iOS: up/down/left/right; Android: vertical only (left/right → down)
      direction: 'down' as const,
      // iOS-only: percentage of screen height per scroll step (0.0–1.0)
      // Smaller = finer scroll, larger = faster but may overshoot
      percentage: 0.3,
    });
  }

  // Horizontal scroll (carousel / tab bar) — iOS only
  async scrollCarouselRight(): Promise<void> {
    const carousel = await $('~productCarousel');
    const lastItem = await carousel.$('~carouselItem:last-child');

    await lastItem.scrollIntoView({
      direction: 'right' as const,
      maxScrolls: 5,
      percentage: 0.5,
    });
  }

  // Tap after scrolling to ensure element is in view
  async tapProductById(productId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.scrollToProduct(productId);
    await $(`[data-testid="product-${productId}"]`).click();
  }
}
```

**[community] On Android, `scrollIntoView({ direction: 'right' })` is silently remapped
to `'down'` by the UIAutomator2 driver — horizontal scrolling via scrollIntoView is iOS
only. For Android horizontal RecyclerViews, use `browser.swipe()` with pixel-precise
`from`/`to` coordinates or `mobile: scrollGesture`:** WHY: UIAutomator2's `scrollTo`
implementation is vertical-only; the WDIO abstraction does not raise an error, it simply
ignores the unsupported direction.

**[community] `maxScrolls: 0` does not mean "no limit" — it means zero scroll attempts,
so the element is expected to already be in view. Use a large number like `100` for deeply
nested infinite-scroll lists. The default of `10` is too low for feeds that lazy-load items:**
WHY: The `maxScrolls` option is a hard cap on scroll iterations; setting it to `0` skips
all scrolling and will fail if the element is not already visible.

### Pattern 281 — Appium 3.4.x: `@appium/support` Uint8Array Plist Fix (iOS 18.4)

Appium 3.4.2 (released 2026-05-07) includes `@appium/support@7.2.2` which fixes parsing
of iOS plist files containing `Uint8Array` or `ArrayBuffer` data. Prior to this fix,
`plistlib.parse()` in the support module threw a `TypeError` when encountering binary plist
entries that used typed arrays rather than `Buffer` — common in newer iOS 18.4 device info
plists returned during session creation.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — onPrepare Appium version guard + capability workaround for < 3.4.2
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';
import { exec } from 'child_process';
import { promisify } from 'util';

const execAsync = promisify(exec);

export default defineConfig({
  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'iOS',
    'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
    'appium:platformVersion': '18.4',
    'appium:deviceName': process.env.IOS_DEVICE_NAME!,
    'appium:app': process.env.IOS_APP_PATH!,
  }],

  async onPrepare() {
    // Validate Appium version before running against iOS 18.4
    try {
      const { stdout } = await execAsync('appium --version');
      const version = stdout.trim();
      const [major, minor, patch] = version.split('.').map(Number);
      const hasPlixFix = major > 3
        || (major === 3 && minor > 4)
        || (major === 3 && minor === 4 && patch >= 2);

      if (!hasPlixFix) {
        console.warn(
          `[WARN] Appium ${version} contains a plist parse bug on iOS 18.4.` +
          ` Upgrade to appium >= 3.4.2 to fix "TypeError: Cannot read plist data".`
        );
      }
    } catch {
      // appium not in PATH — cloud provider manages version; skip check
    }
  },
});
```

**[community] The `@appium/support` plist bug (pre-7.2.2) only manifests on iOS 18.4+
physical devices — iOS Simulators use a different device info format that does not include
the binary plist entries with typed arrays. CI pipelines that test exclusively on Simulators
may miss this failure until a real-device smoke test is run:** WHY: Apple changed the device
info plist format in iOS 18.4 to use binary data for certain capability fields. Simulators
continue using the legacy XML plist format.

**[community] The `TypeError: Cannot read plist data` error from this bug is thrown during
Appium session creation — before the WDIO `before()` hook fires. The error appears in the
Appium server log but WDIO reports it as a generic "Session not created" error. Checking
the raw Appium server log (`--log appium.log`) is required to diagnose the root cause:**
WHY: WDIO catches the WebDriver error response from Appium and wraps it in a generic
message; the underlying cause is only visible in the Appium process stdout/stderr.

### Pattern 282 — `browser.emulate()` Reset Function Lifecycle: LIFO Array and `using` Keyword

`browser.emulate()` returns a reset function — a common pattern is to wire reset functions
into a WDIO `afterEach` scoped array. TypeScript 5.2+ supports the `using` keyword for
explicit resource management via `Symbol.asyncDispose`.

```typescript
// test/specs/theme-resilience.spec.ts
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';
import { expect } from '@wdio/globals';

// ─── Pattern A: explicit LIFO reset array (all TypeScript versions) ───
describe('Theme resilience — explicit reset', () => {
  const resets: Array<() => Promise<void>> = [];

  afterEach(async () => {
    // Drain all resets in reverse-application order (LIFO)
    for (const reset of resets.reverse()) {
      await reset();
    }
    resets.length = 0;
  });

  it('composes multiple emulations', async () => {
    resets.push(await browser.emulate('colorScheme', 'dark'));
    resets.push(await browser.emulate('onLine', false));
    resets.push(await browser.emulate('userAgent', 'TestAgent/1.0'));

    await browser.url('/home');
    await expect($('[data-testid="theme"]')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
    await expect($('[data-testid="offline-badge"]')).toBeDisplayed();
    // afterEach auto-restores all three in reverse order
  });
});

// ─── Pattern B: Symbol.asyncDispose wrapper (TypeScript 5.2+, target: ES2022) ───
async function emulateWith(
  scope: Parameters<typeof browser.emulate>[0],
  value: Parameters<typeof browser.emulate>[1]
): Promise<{ [Symbol.asyncDispose](): Promise<void> }> {
  const reset = await browser.emulate(scope, value as any);
  return {
    async [Symbol.asyncDispose]() {
      await reset();
    },
  };
}

describe('Theme resilience — using keyword', () => {
  it('auto-disposes emulations at block exit', async () => {
    await using _dark    = await emulateWith('colorScheme', 'dark');
    await using _offline = await emulateWith('onLine', false);

    await browser.url('/home');
    await expect($('[data-testid="theme"]')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
    // _dark and _offline are automatically reset when the test function exits
  });
});
```

**[community] Forgetting to `await` `browser.emulate()` resets in `afterEach` is the most
common cause of "flaky-looking" dark-mode or offline test failures in test suites that run
in a shared browser session (`reuseSession: true`) — the emulated state bleeds into the
next spec because the reset was fire-and-forget:** WHY: `emulate()` issues a BiDi command;
without `await`, the restore command races with the next test's page load.

**[community] The `using` keyword requires `"target": "ES2022"` (or higher) in `tsconfig.json`
AND `"lib": ["ES2022"]` or `"useDefineForClassFields": true` — setting only `target` without
updating `lib` causes `Symbol.asyncDispose is not a function` at runtime even though TypeScript
compiles without errors:** WHY: `Symbol.asyncDispose` is a runtime symbol defined in the ES2022
well-known symbols; the `lib` config controls which built-in globals TypeScript's type checker
knows about, but the actual runtime polyfill must be present.

### Pattern 283 — `expect.soft()` and `getSoftFailures()` CI Reporting Pipeline

`expect.soft()` (expect-webdriverio >= 5.2.0 / WDIO v9.16+) accumulates assertion failures
without stopping the test. After a test block, call `expect.getSoftFailures()` to retrieve
them for structured reporting in Allure or JUnit.

```typescript
// test/specs/product-detail.spec.ts
import { browser, $, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('Product detail page — soft assertions', () => {

  afterEach(() => {
    // Always reset the soft failure accumulator between tests to prevent bleed
    // (getSoftFailures() returns failures since last flush/reset)
    expect.flushSoftFailures?.();
  });

  it('validates all visible fields without early exit on first failure', async () => {
    await browser.url('/products/iphone-case-leather');

    // Collect all failures across the page without stopping on the first one
    expect.soft(await $('[data-testid="product-title"]')).toHaveText('Leather iPhone Case');
    expect.soft(await $('[data-testid="product-price"]')).toHaveText('$29.99');
    expect.soft(await $('[data-testid="product-rating"]'))
      .toHaveAttribute('aria-label', /4\.\d stars/);
    expect.soft(await $('[data-testid="add-to-cart"]')).toBeEnabled();
    expect.soft(await $('[data-testid="product-image"]'))
      .toHaveAttribute('alt', /leather.*case/i);

    // Retrieve failures and write to CI output for triage
    const softFailures = expect.getSoftFailures();

    if (softFailures.length > 0) {
      const summary = softFailures
        .map((f, i) => `[${i + 1}] ${f.message}`)
        .join('\n');
      process.stdout.write(`[soft-assert] ${softFailures.length} failure(s):\n${summary}\n`);
    }

    // This single call fails the test with ALL accumulated failures visible
    expect.flushSoftFailures();
  });
});
```

**[community] `expect.getSoftFailures()` returns failures accumulated since the last
`flushSoftFailures()` call — NOT only failures from the current `it()` block. In WDIO v9
parallel workers each worker has its own accumulator, so parallelism is safe; in a
shared-browser multi-spec run you MUST call `flushSoftFailures()` in `afterEach` to prevent
failures from bleeding between tests:** WHY: The soft assertion store is a module-level
variable per WDIO worker process, not scoped to a single test.

**[community] `expect.soft()` does NOT work with chained WDIO `waitUntil()` or
`waitForDisplayed()` — those throw immediately on timeout regardless of soft mode.
Use `expect.soft()` only for snapshot-style property assertions (`toHaveText`,
`toHaveAttribute`, `toBeEnabled`), not for wait-based readiness checks:** WHY:
`waitForDisplayed()` is a polling command implemented in WDIO core, not in the
`expect-webdriverio` assertion library; the soft-assertion wrapper only intercepts
`expect()` matcher failures.

### Pattern 284 — Hybrid App WebView Debugging: `getPageSource()` XML Parsing

On native context, `browser.getPageSource()` returns the full UIKit/AndroidView XML
hierarchy. On WebView context it returns HTML. Parsing the XML in native context is useful
for understanding element tree structure when Appium Inspector is unavailable (e.g., headless CI).

```typescript
// utils/pageSourceDebug.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import { parseStringPromise } from 'xml2js';   // npm install xml2js @types/xml2js

interface XmlElement {
  $: Record<string, string>;
  [tagName: string]: XmlElement[] | Record<string, string> | undefined;
}

// Dump all accessibility IDs from the current native view hierarchy
export async function dumpAccessibilityIds(): Promise<string[]> {
  const source = await browser.getPageSource();
  const parsed = await parseStringPromise(source, { explicitArray: true });

  const ids: string[] = [];

  function walk(node: XmlElement): void {
    if (node.$ && node.$['accessibility-id']) {
      ids.push(node.$['accessibility-id']);
    }
    for (const key of Object.keys(node)) {
      if (key !== '$' && Array.isArray(node[key])) {
        (node[key] as XmlElement[]).forEach(walk);
      }
    }
  }

  walk(parsed);
  return ids;
}

// In a test: call dumpAccessibilityIds() when a selector fails
it('taps the checkout button', async () => {
  const btn = await $('~checkoutButton');

  if (!(await btn.isDisplayed())) {
    const ids = await dumpAccessibilityIds();
    console.error('[DEBUG] Available accessibility IDs:', ids.join(', '));
    throw new Error(`checkoutButton not found. Available IDs: ${ids.join(', ')}`);
  }

  await btn.click();
  await expect($('~orderConfirmationScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**[community] `browser.getPageSource()` on Android returns a flat XML document where all
text content is in `text` attributes — not child text nodes. On iOS it uses `value` and
`label` attributes. Build platform-aware parsers using `(await driver.capabilities).platformName`
to select the right attribute name:** WHY: UIAutomator2 serialises the view hierarchy
differently from XCUITest — Android uses `text` for visible text, iOS uses `value`.

**[community] On iOS, `getPageSource()` XML includes the system-level accessibility tree
including the status bar and home indicator — these appear as top-level `XCUIElementTypeOther`
nodes and can confuse selectors if you are using `$('XCUIElementTypeOther')` to find app
content. Always qualify with `accessibility-id` or `name` attributes to exclude system UI:**
WHY: iOS accessibility APIs expose the full screen including system chrome, not just the app window.

### Pattern 285 — Android 15/16 Predictive Back Gesture: `pressBack()` Migration

Android 15 (API 35) and Android 16 (API 36) enforce predictive back gesture by default.
When a test calls `driver.navigate().back()` or Appium's `mobile: pressBack`, the system
shows a predictive back animation (~300 ms) before completing navigation. Tests that assert
the previous screen is displayed immediately after pressing back fail intermittently.

```typescript
// utils/androidBack.ts
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Predictive-back-safe navigation helper for Android 15+.
 * Always waits for the target screen selector to appear after pressing back.
 */
export async function pressBackAndWaitFor(
  nextScreenSelector: string,
  timeoutMs = 6_000
): Promise<void> {
  // KEYCODE_BACK = 4; use pressKeyCode for UIAutomator2 < v7 compatibility
  await browser.pressKeyCode(4);

  // Wait for the next screen to appear after the predictive animation
  await $(nextScreenSelector).waitForDisplayed({
    timeout: timeoutMs,
    timeoutMsg:
      `Screen '${nextScreenSelector}' not visible after back navigation ` +
      `(predictive back animation may have extended the delay)`,
  });
}

// Alternative using UIAutomator2 v7+ mobile:pressKey (triggers gesture pipeline)
export async function pressHardwareBackV7(): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: pressKey', {
    keycode: 4,   // KEYCODE_BACK
  });
}

// test usage
it('navigates back from product detail to product list', async () => {
  await $('~productItem').click();
  await $('~productDetailScreen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

  // ✅ Safe on Android 15+: waits for the animation + next screen
  await pressBackAndWaitFor('~productListScreen');

  await expect($('~productListScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**[community] Android 15 predictive back affects ALL `pressBack()` calls regardless of
whether `android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback` is set in the app manifest — the system-level
animation runs unconditionally on API 35+ devices. The only way to disable it for testing
is `adb shell settings put global transitional_back_gesture 0` (requires root or AVD with
writable system partition):** WHY: Predictive back is a system service animation, not an
app-level feature; it cannot be disabled via AndroidManifest.

**[community] `browser.pressKeyCode(4)` (legacy UIAutomator2 < v7) sends a raw input event
that bypasses the predictive back gesture system entirely — the navigation completes immediately
without the animation. After upgrading UIAutomator2 to v7+, `mobile: pressKey` was introduced
to route through the proper gesture pipeline. If existing tests break after upgrading, add a
small `waitForDisplayed` guard as shown above rather than downgrading the driver:** WHY:
The UIAutomator2 v7 `mobile: pressKey` command triggers the full gesture recogniser; older
`pressKeyCode` commands bypass it at the input dispatcher level.

### Pattern 286 — Appium 3.5 Plugin System Overhaul: `--source git` and Type Validation

Appium 3.5.0 (May 2026) refactored the plugin/driver installer to add strict type
validation and a `--source git` shorthand that accepts a full repo URL with optional
`#ref` fragment. The previous `npm:@appium/plugin-name` specifier still works but
the new `git:` scheme pins to a commit SHA for reproducible CI installs.

```typescript
// scripts/appium-setup.ts — CI bootstrap with pinned plugin versions
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

interface AppiumPlugin {
  name: string;
  source: 'npm' | 'git' | 'local';
  ref: string;   // npm semver, git repo URL with optional #SHA, or local path
}

const REQUIRED_PLUGINS: AppiumPlugin[] = [
  { name: 'images',       source: 'npm', ref: '@appium/plugin-images@3.0.2' },
  { name: 'relaxed-caps', source: 'npm', ref: 'appium-relaxed-caps-plugin@1.1.0' },
  // Git-pinned experimental plugin — reproducible across CI runs
  {
    name: 'gestures',
    source: 'git',
    ref: 'https://github.com/AppiumTestDistribution/appium-gestures-plugin#abc1234',
  },
];

function installPlugin(plugin: AppiumPlugin): void {
  const spec =
    plugin.source === 'git'
      ? `--source git --package ${plugin.ref}`
      : `--source npm --package ${plugin.ref}`;
  const cmd = `appium plugin install ${spec}`;
  console.log(`[appium-setup] ${cmd}`);
  execSync(cmd, { stdio: 'inherit' });
}

function ensurePlugins(): void {
  // List installed plugins as JSON — Appium 3.5+ supports --json flag
  const raw = execSync('appium plugin list --installed --json', { encoding: 'utf8' });
  const installed: Array<{ name: string }> = JSON.parse(raw);
  const installedNames = new Set(installed.map((p) => p.name));

  for (const plugin of REQUIRED_PLUGINS) {
    if (!installedNames.has(plugin.name)) {
      installPlugin(plugin);
    } else {
      console.log(`[appium-setup] Plugin '${plugin.name}' already installed — skipping`);
    }
  }
}

ensurePlugins();
```

**When to use:** Use `--source git` with a SHA ref in CI to guarantee bit-for-bit
reproducible plugin installs. npm semver ranges are convenient for local dev but can
pull a broken minor release between CI runs.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use `--source git` for plugins published on npm with
strong semantic versioning guarantees — npm's integrity hash checking already provides
tamper protection. Git SHAs in CI add noise to Dependabot/Renovate upgrade workflows.

**[official] Appium 3.5 added `appium plugin list --installed --json` output format;
earlier 3.x versions returned human-readable text only. If you parse the installed
plugin list in CI, gate behind a version check or use `--json` defensively with a
try/catch text fallback.**

**[community] The `--source git` flag in Appium 3.5 bypasses npm lifecycle scripts
(`postinstall`, etc.) — plugins that rely on postinstall to compile native addons
(e.g., sharp-based image comparison) will silently fail at runtime with
`MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Always run `npm rebuild` in the plugin directory after a git-source
install when native addons are involved:** WHY: npm lifecycle hooks run only during
`npm install`; Appium's git fetcher uses a stripped download path that skips them.

### Pattern 287 — WDIO v9.28+ BiDi Network Intercept on Android WebView Contexts

WebDriverIO v9.28 extended its BiDi network intercept API (`browser.network`) to
work inside Android WebView contexts (requires UIAutomator2 v7.4+ and
`appium:chromedriverForwardBiDi: true`). This allows mocking REST endpoints inside
hybrid apps without a proxy server.

```typescript
// test/specs/hybrid-network-intercept.spec.ts
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';
import { expect } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('Hybrid app — BiDi network intercept in WebView', () => {
  let interceptId: string | undefined;

  before(async () => {
    // Switch to WebView context first — BiDi intercept follows the active context
    const contexts = await browser.getContexts();
    const webView = contexts.find(
      (c) => typeof c === 'object' && 'webviewPageId' in c
    ) as { id: string } | undefined;
    if (!webView) throw new Error('No WebView context found');
    await browser.switchContext(webView.id);
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    if (interceptId) {
      await browser.network.removeIntercept(interceptId);
      interceptId = undefined;
    }
  });

  it('mocks /api/user/profile to return 403 and shows error banner', async () => {
    // Register a BiDi network intercept for the profile API endpoint
    const intercept = await browser.network.addIntercept({
      phases: ['beforeRequestSent'],
      urlPatterns: [{ type: 'string', pattern: '**/api/user/profile' }],
    });
    interceptId = intercept.interceptId;

    // Override response with 403 Forbidden
    browser.on('network.beforeRequestSent', async (event) => {
      await browser.network.continueResponse({
        requestId: event.requestId,
        statusCode: 403,
        reasonPhrase: 'Forbidden',
        body: {
          type: 'string',
          value: JSON.stringify({ error: 'unauthorized' }),
        },
      });
    });

    await browser.url('/dashboard');

    // The app should render an error banner when profile fetch returns 403
    await expect($('[data-testid="error-banner"]')).toBeDisplayed();
    await expect($('[data-testid="error-banner"]')).toHaveText(
      expect.stringContaining('session expired')
    );
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Use BiDi network intercept in WebView when your hybrid app makes
fetch/XHR calls that are hard to reproduce with real backend data: auth errors,
rate-limit responses, or flaky third-party APIs.

**When NOT to use:** BiDi network intercept only works in the WebView context. Native
Appium context interactions (tapping native UI, reading accessibility IDs) are outside
the BiDi WebSocket protocol — switch back to the native context before driving native UI.

**[community] `appium:chromedriverForwardBiDi: true` must be set in capabilities BEFORE
session creation — you cannot enable BiDi WebSocket forwarding mid-session. If the
capability is missing, `browser.network.addIntercept()` is a silent no-op: the intercept
is registered but never fires, and no error is thrown:** WHY: UIAutomator2 v7.4+ enables
the BiDi forwarding tunnel at session init time; there is no mid-session renegotiation
path in the ChromeDriver protocol.

**[community] Calling `browser.switchContext()` after registering a BiDi network
intercept clears all active intercepts — the intercept is scoped to the WebView page
session, not the WDIO `browser` object. Re-register intercepts after every
`switchContext()` call to WebView:** WHY: Each ChromeDriver session maintains its own
BiDi intercept registry; switching context creates a new ChromeDriver session handle.

### Pattern 288 — XCUITest v11.5.x: iPhone Mirroring Mode Detection and CI Avoidance

iPhone Mirroring (macOS Sequoia) exposes the phone as a virtual display on macOS.
When `xcrun xcdevice list` detects a mirrored iPhone, XCUITest v11.5+ may erroneously
attempt to use it instead of targeting the correct physical UDID, causing session
creation failures with `DeviceNotFound`.

```typescript
// scripts/validate-ios-devices.ts — run in CI onPrepare to avoid mirror confusion
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

interface XCDevice {
  identifier: string;
  modelName: string;
  platform: string;
  connectionProperties?: { transportType?: string };
}

function listRealDevices(): XCDevice[] {
  const raw = execSync('xcrun xcdevice list', { encoding: 'utf8' });
  let devices: XCDevice[] = [];
  try {
    devices = JSON.parse(raw);
  } catch {
    // xcdevice may print non-JSON on older Xcode versions — skip check
    return [];
  }
  // Exclude mirrored devices — transport type is 'Mirror' in macOS Sequoia
  return devices.filter(
    (d) =>
      d.platform === 'com.apple.platform.iphoneos' &&
      d.connectionProperties?.transportType !== 'Mirror'
  );
}

/** Assert that a target UDID resolves to a real (non-mirrored) physical device. */
export function assertDeviceAvailable(targetUdid: string): void {
  const available = listRealDevices();
  const found = available.find((d) => d.identifier === targetUdid);
  if (!found) {
    const ids = available
      .map((d) => `${d.identifier} (${d.modelName})`)
      .join(', ');
    throw new Error(
      `Device UDID '${targetUdid}' not found among real (non-mirrored) devices.\n` +
        `Available: ${ids || '(none)'}\n` +
        'Ensure iPhone Mirroring is disabled in macOS System Settings.'
    );
  }
  console.log(`[validate] Target device '${found.modelName}' (${targetUdid}) — OK`);
}

// wdio.conf.ts usage:
// import { assertDeviceAvailable } from './scripts/validate-ios-devices';
// onPrepare: async () => { assertDeviceAvailable(process.env.IOS_UDID!); }
```

**When to use:** Add this guard in `onPrepare` on macOS Sequoia self-hosted CI runners
where developers may have iPhone Mirroring active. The check adds <200 ms and prevents
cryptic `DeviceNotFound` errors.

**When NOT to use:** Skip on Linux CI (no macOS Sequoia), ephemeral containers, or
clean CI images where no user session is active — iPhone Mirroring requires an
interactive user session.

**[community] iPhone Mirroring sessions in macOS Sequoia persist across reboots if
the user has "Allow iPhone Mirroring" toggled on. On long-lived self-hosted macOS
runners, a single developer connecting a phone via mirroring can break every subsequent
CI run until the setting is manually disabled:** WHY: XCUITest's device discovery via
`xcrun xcdevice` lists all USB and mirror-attached devices with no Appium capability
to filter mirror connections.

### Pattern 289 — UIAutomator2 v7.4.x: `appium:remoteAdbHost` for Cloud Multi-Device Topology

In distributed test clouds (self-hosted device farms, OpenSTF, AWS Device Farm Private),
each physical Android device's ADB daemon may live on a different host IP.
UIAutomator2 v7.4.x formalises `appium:remoteAdbHost` and `appium:adbPort` as
per-session capabilities, enabling a single Appium node to route ADB traffic to
multiple remote hosts.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — multi-host device farm capability matrix
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

interface FarmDevice {
  adbHost: string;
  adbPort: number;
  deviceSerial: string;
  platformVersion: string;
  /** Unique system port to avoid UIAutomator2 server conflicts */
  systemPort: number;
}

function buildAndroidCaps(device: FarmDevice): WebdriverIO.Capabilities {
  return {
    platformName: 'Android',
    'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
    'appium:deviceName': device.deviceSerial,
    'appium:udid': device.deviceSerial,
    'appium:platformVersion': device.platformVersion,
    'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,
    // UIAutomator2 v7.4+ — route ADB traffic to a remote host
    'appium:remoteAdbHost': device.adbHost,
    'appium:adbPort': device.adbPort,
    // Deterministic system port prevents parallel session conflicts
    'appium:systemPort': device.systemPort,
    'appium:disableWindowAnimation': true,
  };
}

const FARM_DEVICES: FarmDevice[] = [
  { adbHost: '10.0.1.11', adbPort: 5037, deviceSerial: 'RF8M123456A',
    platformVersion: '14', systemPort: 8301 },
  { adbHost: '10.0.1.12', adbPort: 5037, deviceSerial: 'RF9X789012B',
    platformVersion: '15', systemPort: 8302 },
];

export default defineConfig({
  maxInstances: FARM_DEVICES.length,
  capabilities: FARM_DEVICES.map(buildAndroidCaps),
  logLevel: 'warn',
});
```

**When to use:** Use `appium:remoteAdbHost` when your Appium server is centralised but
devices are spread across multiple lab machines or VMs. This is the Appium-native
approach; the alternative (one Appium node per host) requires WDIO Multiremote or an
external load balancer.

**When NOT to use:** Do not set `appium:remoteAdbHost` for locally-connected devices —
the default `localhost:5037` ADB server is used implicitly and adding a remote host
adds latency without benefit.

**[community] `appium:remoteAdbHost` requires the remote ADB server to be already
running — Appium does NOT start the remote ADB daemon. On lab machines that hibernate
or restart, the ADB server exits and must be restarted (`adb -H <host> -P <port> start-server`).
Add an ADB heartbeat check to your CI warm-up pipeline:** WHY: UIAutomator2 v7.4's
remote ADB client assumes the server is ready; it has no server-start retry path like
the local ADB client.

**[community] `appium:systemPort` collisions are the #1 cause of parallel Android
session failures when multiple WDIO workers target the same `remoteAdbHost`. Use a
deterministic assignment (base port + fixed worker index from device config) rather
than `Math.random()` in production pipelines to make collisions immediately visible
in logs:** WHY: Random port assignment converts port-conflict failures from
consistently-failing to occasionally-failing, making them much harder to diagnose.

### Pattern 290 — `appium:androidBundleFile`: Android App Bundle (`.aab`) Direct Install

Appium 3.5+ (with UIAutomator2 v7.4+) supports `appium:androidBundleFile` to install
an Android App Bundle directly without requiring a pre-built APK. Appium uses
`bundletool` under the hood to generate a device-specific APK set and sideload it.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — .aab capability with bundletool path
import path from 'path';
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

const BUNDLETOOL_PATH =
  process.env.BUNDLETOOL_JAR ??
  path.resolve(process.env.HOME!, '.appium/bundletool/bundletool.jar');

export default defineConfig({
  capabilities: [
    {
      platformName: 'Android',
      'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
      'appium:deviceName': 'emulator-5554',
      'appium:platformVersion': '15',
      // Use .aab directly — no manual apks extraction step needed in CI
      'appium:androidBundleFile': path.resolve(__dirname, '../build/app-release.aab'),
      // Point to the bundletool jar (bundled with UIAutomator2 by default)
      'appium:bundletoolPath': BUNDLETOOL_PATH,
      // Keystore for signing device-specific APK sets extracted from the bundle
      'appium:keystorePath': path.resolve(__dirname, '../keys/release.keystore'),
      'appium:keystorePassword': process.env.KEYSTORE_PASSWORD!,
      'appium:keyAlias': process.env.KEY_ALIAS!,
      'appium:keyPassword': process.env.KEY_PASSWORD!,
      'appium:noReset': false,
    },
  ],
});
```

**When to use:** Use `appium:androidBundleFile` when your CI artifact is an `.aab`
(standard for Play Store uploads) and you want to avoid adding a `bundletool build-apks`
+ `install-apks` shell script around `wdio run`.

**When NOT to use:** The `.aab` install path is slower than `.apk` install — `bundletool`
must run locally and generate device-specific splits. For large bundles (>150 MB),
total install time can exceed 90 seconds on first run. If test startup time is critical,
pre-build the APK in the CI build stage and pass it as `appium:app`.

**[official] `appium:bundletoolPath` defaults to the bundletool jar bundled with
UIAutomator2 (`~/.appium/node_modules/appium-uiautomator2-driver/...`). If you rely
on the bundled version, pin UIAutomator2 to a tested version — bundletool minor
version changes affect the APK split algorithm.**

**[community] Keystore credentials passed as capabilities appear in the Appium session
creation request body, which is logged at `--log-level info`. Rotate keys after every
test run OR set `--log-level warn` in CI to prevent keystore passwords appearing in
log files accessible to all CI users:** WHY: Appium logs the full capabilities dict
at `info` level during session creation; there is no built-in secrets masking for
capability values.

---

### Pattern 291 — iOS 18 Privacy Manifest Validation in Appium `onPrepare`

iOS 18.x (and App Store submission rules effective Spring 2024) require apps to include
a `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` manifest declaring API usage. The Simulator ignores the
manifest — apps with missing or malformed manifests install and run normally on
Simulator but are rejected at App Store review. This pattern validates the manifest
in CI before running the test suite.

```typescript
// scripts/ios-privacy-manifest-check.ts
import path from 'path';
import fs from 'fs';
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

/**
 * Validates that a .app bundle contains a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest with
 * the required NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes key. Runs on macOS only (requires plutil).
 */
export function validatePrivacyManifest(appPath: string): void {
  if (process.platform !== 'darwin') {
    console.log('[privacy-manifest] Skipping — plutil only available on macOS');
    return;
  }

  const manifestPath = path.join(appPath, 'PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy');

  if (!fs.existsSync(manifestPath)) {
    console.warn(
      `[privacy-manifest] WARNING: PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy not found in:\n  ${appPath}\n` +
        '  App Store submission will be rejected for iOS 18+ apps using required APIs.\n' +
        '  Required APIs: NSUserDefaults, FileTimestamp, SystemBootTime, DiskSpace, ActiveKeyboards'
    );
    return;
  }

  // Convert binary plist to XML for inspection (plutil ships with Xcode CLT)
  let xmlOutput: string;
  try {
    xmlOutput = execSync(`plutil -convert xml1 -o - "${manifestPath}"`, {
      encoding: 'utf8',
      timeout: 5_000,
    });
  } catch {
    console.warn(`[privacy-manifest] Could not parse ${manifestPath} — skipping check`);
    return;
  }

  const hasApiTypes = xmlOutput.includes('NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes');
  const hasTracking  = xmlOutput.includes('NSPrivacyTracking');

  if (!hasApiTypes) {
    console.warn(
      '[privacy-manifest] NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes key missing — ' +
        'apps using required reason APIs must declare usage reasons.'
    );
  }
  if (!hasTracking) {
    console.warn(
      '[privacy-manifest] NSPrivacyTracking key missing — ' +
        'declare false if the app does not track users.'
    );
  }

  if (hasApiTypes && hasTracking) {
    console.log('[privacy-manifest] PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy found and structurally valid.');
  }
}

// wdio.conf.ts usage:
// import { validatePrivacyManifest } from './scripts/ios-privacy-manifest-check';
// onPrepare: async () => { validatePrivacyManifest(process.env.IOS_APP_PATH!); }
```

**When to use:** Add this to `onPrepare` for iOS app test suites that will be submitted
to TestFlight or the App Store. Catches manifest issues in CI before a human review
cycle.

**When NOT to use:** Skip for Simulator-only pipelines where App Store compliance is
irrelevant (unit-level UI tests). Also skip on Linux CI — `plutil` requires macOS.

**[community] The iOS Simulator ignores `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` entirely — an app
with a missing or malformed manifest installs and runs normally on Simulator but is
rejected during App Store review. Teams testing exclusively on Simulators regularly
discover this failure only at submission time:** WHY: Apple enforces the manifest at
the notarisation/review stage, not at install time; the Simulator bypasses notarisation.

**[community] Binary plist format used by newer Xcode versions makes the manifest
unreadable with a plain text search — always use `plutil -convert xml1` before parsing.
A `grep NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` may return false-negative
on binary plists, silently missing the validation:** WHY: Xcode 15.3+ writes
`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` as binary plist by default when built via `xcodebuild`; the
binary format is not human-readable and not parseable by standard XML tools.

---

### Pattern 292 — WDIO `browser.action()` Pointer API: Freehand Drawing and Precise Drag

`browser.action('pointer')` (W3C Actions API) lets you compose multi-step pointer
sequences with precise coordinates and timing. This is the correct API for gesture
inputs that `browser.swipe()` and `element.dragAndDrop()` cannot express: freehand
drawing, multi-finger pinch, or slow drags with intermediate waypoints.

```typescript
// test/specs/canvas-draw.spec.ts
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';
import { expect } from '@wdio/globals';

/** Draw a smooth diagonal line via W3C Actions pointer sequence. */
async function drawLineOnCanvas(
  startX: number,
  startY: number,
  endX: number,
  endY: number,
  steps = 20
): Promise<void> {
  const pointer = browser.action('pointer', {
    parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' },  // 'touch' | 'mouse' | 'pen'
  });

  // Move to start position, then press down
  pointer
    .move({ x: startX, y: startY, duration: 0, origin: 'viewport' })
    .down({ button: 0 });

  // Interpolate intermediate waypoints for a smooth path
  for (let i = 1; i <= steps; i++) {
    const progress = i / steps;
    pointer.move({
      x: Math.round(startX + (endX - startX) * progress),
      y: Math.round(startY + (endY - startY) * progress),
      duration: 50,
      origin: 'viewport',
    });
  }

  pointer.up({ button: 0 });

  // Dispatch the entire sequence in one W3C Actions call
  await browser.performActions([pointer]);
  // MUST call releaseActions() to clear the stateful input source
  await browser.releaseActions();
}

describe('Canvas drawing tool', () => {
  it('draws a diagonal line and verifies stroke count increments', async () => {
    await browser.url('/draw');
    await $('[data-testid="canvas"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    await drawLineOnCanvas(100, 200, 300, 400, 30);

    // The app exposes the stroke count via a data attribute for testing
    const strokeCount = await $('[data-testid="stroke-counter"]').getAttribute(
      'data-count'
    );
    expect(Number(strokeCount)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Use `browser.action('pointer')` for any gesture requiring >2
intermediate waypoints, multi-finger coordination, or `pen` pointer type.
Use `browser.swipe()` for simple single-direction swipes — it is more readable.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use `browser.action()` in the native Appium context for
native gestures — the W3C pointer coordinate system is the full-screen viewport, which
differs from element-relative coordinates. Use `mobile:` gesture commands for native
precision.

**[community] `browser.releaseActions()` MUST be called after `browser.performActions()`
— failing to release leaves a dangling pointer-down state in the WebDriver session.
On iOS, this manifests as a phantom touch that interferes with the next tap or scroll
in the same test:** WHY: W3C Actions API maintains a stateful input source registry
per session; `performActions` applies the sequence but does not automatically reset
the source state.

**[community] The `duration` parameter in pointer `move` actions is approximate —
actual gesture timing varies ±50 ms due to the OS gesture recogniser sampling rate
(typically 60 Hz). If your app differentiates "slow drag" from "fast drag" by timing,
add extra `pause()` steps between `move` calls instead of relying on a single
`duration` value:** WHY: W3C `duration` is a hint; actual event delivery timing is
controlled by the platform gesture pipeline, not the test framework.

---

### Pattern 293 — Appium Doctor v2: Health Checks in CI `onPrepare`

`@appium/doctor` v2 (bundled with Appium 3.3+) exposes a programmatic-style CLI
alongside the GUI. Running `appium driver doctor <name> --json` in `onPrepare` catches
environment misconfiguration (missing Xcode CLI tools, wrong Android SDK path, missing
`bundletool`) before the test suite starts — far earlier than a session-creation failure.

```typescript
// scripts/appium-health-check.ts
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

interface DoctorResult {
  ok: string[];
  notOk: string[];
  optional: string[];
}

/**
 * Runs `appium driver doctor <driverName> --json` and throws if any required
 * check fails. Only runs in the primary WDIO launcher process (not per-worker).
 */
export function runAppiumDoctor(
  driverName: 'xcuitest' | 'uiautomator2',
  opts: { failOnOptional?: boolean } = {}
): void {
  let raw = '{}';
  try {
    raw = execSync(`appium driver doctor ${driverName} --json`, {
      encoding: 'utf8',
      timeout: 30_000,
    });
  } catch (err) {
    // Non-zero exit: at least one required check failed; stdout has the JSON
    raw =
      (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException & { stdout?: string }).stdout ?? '{}';
  }

  let result: DoctorResult;
  try {
    result = JSON.parse(raw) as DoctorResult;
  } catch {
    console.warn('[appium-doctor] Could not parse doctor output as JSON — skipping check');
    return;
  }

  if (result.notOk.length > 0) {
    const lines = result.notOk.map((msg) => `  - ${msg}`).join('\n');
    throw new Error(
      `[appium-doctor] ${driverName} environment check failed:\n${lines}\n` +
        'Fix the issues above before running the test suite.'
    );
  }

  if (opts.failOnOptional && result.optional.length > 0) {
    const lines = result.optional.map((msg) => `  - ${msg}`).join('\n');
    throw new Error(`[appium-doctor] Optional checks not satisfied:\n${lines}`);
  }

  console.log(
    `[appium-doctor] ${driverName} — ${result.ok.length} checks passed` +
      (result.optional.length > 0
        ? `, ${result.optional.length} optional warnings`
        : '')
  );
}

// wdio.conf.ts usage:
// import { runAppiumDoctor } from './scripts/appium-health-check';
// onPrepare: async () => { runAppiumDoctor('uiautomator2'); }
```

**When to use:** Add the doctor check to `onPrepare` for self-hosted CI runners
(macOS/Linux bare metal or VMs) where the environment can drift between runs.

**When NOT to use:** Skip on ephemeral Docker-based CI where the image is rebuilt
from scratch each run — the Dockerfile guarantees a correct environment, and the
check adds 3–5 seconds without value.

**[official] `appium driver doctor <name> --json` is available from Appium 3.3+.
In Appium 3.5 the JSON output format was stabilised (keys: `ok`, `notOk`, `optional`).
In Appium 3.2 and earlier, doctor output was text-only.**

**[community] Placing `runAppiumDoctor()` in the WDIO `before` hook (per-worker) rather
than `onPrepare` (launcher, runs once) causes multiple concurrent doctor processes —
one per parallel worker — which can produce interleaved stdout and false-positive
`notOk` results when the SDK tool checks race for the same lock file:** WHY: `before`
runs inside each WDIO worker process; `onPrepare` runs once in the launcher before
workers spawn. Doctor checks are environment checks, not session checks — they belong
in `onPrepare`.

---

### Pattern 294 — WDIO TypeScript 5.5 Inferred Type Predicates in Page Object Guards

TypeScript 5.5 (June 2024) introduced inferred type predicates — when a function's
return type can be determined to narrow a type, TypeScript infers `x is T`
automatically without an explicit annotation. WDIO page objects benefit from this
for null-safe element access patterns.

```typescript
// pages/BasePage.ts
import { $, browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import type { ChainablePromiseElement } from 'webdriverio';

type MaybeElement = ChainablePromiseElement | null;

// TypeScript 5.5: return type is inferred as `elem is ChainablePromiseElement`
// No explicit `: elem is ChainablePromiseElement` annotation needed
async function isElementReady(elem: MaybeElement): Promise<boolean> {
  if (elem === null) return false;
  try {
    return await elem.isDisplayed();
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

export abstract class BasePage {
  protected abstract get pageName(): string;
  protected abstract primaryElement(): Promise<MaybeElement>;

  async waitForReady(timeoutMs = 8_000): Promise<void> {
    await browser.waitUntil(
      async () => isElementReady(await this.primaryElement()),
      {
        timeout: timeoutMs,
        timeoutMsg: `${this.pageName} did not become ready within ${timeoutMs} ms`,
        interval: 300,
      }
    );
  }
}

// pages/CheckoutPage.ts
export class CheckoutPage extends BasePage {
  protected get pageName(): string { return 'CheckoutPage'; }

  protected async primaryElement(): Promise<MaybeElement> {
    try {
      return $('[data-testid="checkout-form"]');
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  async fillShippingAddress(address: {
    line1: string;
    city: string;
    zip: string;
  }): Promise<void> {
    await this.waitForReady();
    await $('[name="address-line1"]').setValue(address.line1);
    await $('[name="city"]').setValue(address.city);
    await $('[name="postal-code"]').setValue(address.zip);
  }

  async submitOrder(): Promise<void> {
    await $('[data-testid="place-order-btn"]').click();
    await $('[data-testid="order-confirmation"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
  }
}
```

**When to use:** Use inferred type predicates for page object guards on conditionally
rendered elements (lazy-loaded views, role-gated UI, dynamic modals). TypeScript 5.5
removes the need for verbose `function x(y): y is T` annotations.

**When NOT to use:** Do not over-engineer null-safety for elements that are always
present — the added abstraction increases cognitive overhead. Reserve this pattern
for genuinely optional UI.

**[community] TypeScript 5.5 inferred type predicates only apply when the function
body has a single, statically-analysable narrowing path. If your guard has multiple
return paths or catches a non-null value and returns `await elem.isEnabled()` without
a prior null check, TypeScript falls back to `boolean` and the predicate is NOT
inferred. Verify with `tsc --noEmit --strict` and check the inferred return type in
your IDE:** WHY: TypeScript 5.5's predicate inference algorithm requires exactly one
narrowing per code path; mixed `null`-check and non-null return paths defeat inference.

### Pattern 295 — Android `UiScrollable` vs UIAutomator2 `mobile: scroll`: Choosing the Right Strategy

UIAutomator2 exposes two scrolling mechanisms: the classic `UiScrollable` (via
`android=` selector) and the modern `mobile: scroll` command. Choosing wrongly causes
missed elements or over-scrolling.

```typescript
// utils/androidScroll.ts
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Strategy A — UiScrollable: best for RecyclerView/ListView with known text content.
 * Scrolls the first scrollable container until the target text is visible.
 * Fastest approach — UIAutomator handles the loop natively on-device.
 */
export async function scrollToTextUiScrollable(text: string): Promise<void> {
  const selector =
    `new UiScrollable(new UiSelector().scrollable(true)).scrollIntoView(` +
    `new UiSelector().text("${text}"))`;
  const el = await $(`android=${selector}`);
  // UiScrollable may return a non-null element proxy even if scroll failed —
  // always verify with waitForDisplayed
  await el.waitForDisplayed({
    timeout: 10_000,
    timeoutMsg: `Text "${text}" not found via UiScrollable`,
  });
}

/**
 * Strategy B — mobile:scroll: best for custom scroll views, horizontal lists,
 * or when precise scroll-distance control is needed.
 */
export async function scrollToElementByA11yId(
  accessibilityId: string,
  direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right' = 'down',
  maxAttempts = 10
): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < maxAttempts; i++) {
    const el = await $(`~${accessibilityId}`);
    if (await el.isDisplayed()) return;

    await browser.execute('mobile: scroll', {
      direction,
      percent: 0.7,   // 70% of container height — safer than 100% on gesture nav bar
    });
  }
  throw new Error(
    `Element '~${accessibilityId}' not found after ${maxAttempts} scroll(s)`
  );
}

/**
 * Strategy C — WDIO v9 scrollIntoView: best for elements in the hierarchy
 * but clipped outside the visible area by a small amount.
 */
export async function scrollElementIntoView(
  selector: string,
  containerSelector = '[data-testid="scrollable-container"]'
): Promise<void> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  await el.scrollIntoView({
    maxScrolls: 8,
    scrollDirection: 'down',
    scrollableElement: await $(containerSelector),
  });
}
```

**When to use:**
- Strategy A (UiScrollable): RecyclerViews/ListViews with stable text labels.
  Fastest — the scroll loop runs natively on the device without round-trips.
- Strategy B (mobile:scroll): Custom scroll views, horizontal carousels, or when
  you need `percent` or `left/right` direction control.
- Strategy C (scrollIntoView): Elements that ARE in the accessibility hierarchy but
  clipped just off-screen — avoids over-scrolling past the target.

**When NOT to use UiScrollable:** Do not use it for WebView content, Flutter apps,
or views using `NestedScrollView` where the `scrollable=true` flag may not propagate
correctly to UIAutomator.

**[community] `UiScrollable` silently returns a non-null element proxy even when the
target is not found after exhausting its scroll budget — `isDisplayed()` on this proxy
returns `false`. Always add `waitForDisplayed()` after a UiScrollable scroll to confirm
the element actually appeared:** WHY: UIAutomator2 returns the UiScrollable proxy
element regardless of scroll success; the caller is responsible for confirming result.

**[community] `mobile: scroll` with `percent: 1.0` overshoots on Android phones with
gesture navigation bar (Android 10+) because the gesture inset reduces the scrollable
height. Use `percent: 0.7–0.8` for full-screen containers on modern Android:** WHY:
The gesture navigation bar inset is included in the container's reported height but
cannot be scrolled through; a 100% scroll attempts to drag through the system gesture
zone and is silently rejected.

### Pattern 296 — `returnDetailedContexts` Migration: XCUITest v11.5+ Context API

XCUITest v11.5 deprecated the `appium:fullContextList` capability in favour of passing
`returnDetailedContexts: true` as an argument to `getContexts()`. Teams relying on the
capability for `webviewBundleId` and `webviewPageId` fields must migrate.

```typescript
// utils/contextSwitch.ts — XCUITest v11.5+ compatible context helper
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

// Detailed context shape returned by XCUITest v11.5+ argument-based API
interface DetailedContext {
  id: string;               // e.g., 'WEBVIEW_com.example.app'
  title?: string;           // Page <title> if available
  url?: string;             // Current page URL
  bundleId?: string;        // iOS only
  webviewBundleId?: string; // XCUITest v11.5+: replaces appium:fullContextList field
  webviewPageId?: string;   // XCUITest v11.5+: disambiguates multiple WKWebViews
}

/** Returns detailed context list using the v11.5+ argument-based API.
 *  Falls back to string array for older XCUITest versions. */
async function getDetailedContexts(): Promise<DetailedContext[]> {
  try {
    return (await browser.getContexts({
      returnDetailedContexts: true,
    })) as DetailedContext[];
  } catch {
    // Fallback: XCUITest < v11.5 returns a plain string array
    const basic = await browser.getContexts();
    return (basic as string[]).map((id) => ({ id }));
  }
}

/** Switch to the first WebView context matching an optional URL pattern. */
export async function switchToWebView(urlPattern?: RegExp): Promise<void> {
  const contexts = await getDetailedContexts();
  const webViewContext = contexts.find((ctx) => {
    if (ctx.id === 'NATIVE_APP' || !ctx.id.startsWith('WEBVIEW_')) return false;
    if (urlPattern && ctx.url) return urlPattern.test(ctx.url);
    return true;
  });

  if (!webViewContext) {
    const ids = contexts.map((c) => c.id).join(', ');
    throw new Error(`No matching WebView context found. Available: ${ids}`);
  }

  await browser.switchContext(webViewContext.id);
  console.log(`[context] Switched to: ${webViewContext.url ?? webViewContext.id}`);
}
```

**When to use:** Use the argument-based `getContexts({ returnDetailedContexts: true })`
for all new code targeting XCUITest v11.5+. Use the try/catch fallback wrapper when
your test suite must support a range of XCUITest versions.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use `appium:fullContextList` for new code targeting
XCUITest v11.5+ — the capability is silently ignored and `getContexts()` returns a
basic string array instead of detailed objects.

**[community] The `appium:fullContextList` deprecation warning in XCUITest v11.5 is
emitted as an Appium server log warning only — WDIO does NOT surface it in the console
or test output. Teams suppressing Appium server logs (`--log-level error`) will not see
the deprecation until their tests break after the capability is removed in a future
version:** WHY: Appium deprecation notices go through the driver's internal logger, not
through the WebDriver response; client frameworks have no visibility into driver log lines.

**[community] When `returnDetailedContexts: true` is used and the app has multiple
WKWebView instances (e.g., an in-app browser + an embedded ad WKWebView), all contexts
share the same `WEBVIEW_com.example.app` prefix in their `id`. You MUST use
`webviewPageId` or `url` to distinguish them — the `id` prefix alone is not unique:**
WHY: XCUITest associates all WKWebViews for the same app process under the same
`bundleId`; page-level disambiguation requires the page ID.

### Pattern 297 — WDIO JUnit Reporter v9: Attachment API for Screenshots on Failure

WDIO v9's `@wdio/junit-reporter` added an `attachScreenshot` option that embeds
base64-encoded screenshots directly in the JUnit XML `<failure>` element. CI systems
like GitLab, Jenkins, and CircleCI can render these as inline images in test reports.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — JUnit reporter with screenshot attachment on failure
import type { Options } from '@wdio/types';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

export const config: Options.Testrunner = {
  reporters: [
    'spec',
    [
      'junit',
      {
        outputDir: './reports/junit',
        outputFileFormat: (options) =>
          `test-results-${options.cid}-${Date.now()}.xml`,
        // Enable base64 screenshot embedding in <failure> elements (WDIO v9.10+)
        attachScreenshot: true,
      },
    ],
  ],

  afterTest: async (test, _context, result) => {
    if (result.passed) return;

    const screenshotDir = path.resolve('./reports/screenshots');
    fs.mkdirSync(screenshotDir, { recursive: true });

    // Sanitise test title for use as filename
    const safeName = test.title.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_').toLowerCase();
    const screenshotPath = path.join(screenshotDir, `${safeName}_${Date.now()}.png`);

    try {
      await browser.saveScreenshot(screenshotPath);
      // When attachScreenshot: true, WDIO's saveScreenshot() automatically
      // attaches the PNG to the current reporter context.
      // For manual binary attachment (e.g., a video MP4), use:
      // await browser.addAttachment('recording', fs.readFileSync(videoPath), 'video/mp4');
      console.log(`[reporter] Screenshot saved and attached: ${screenshotPath}`);
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn(`[reporter] Could not save screenshot: ${err}`);
    }
  },
};
```

**When to use:** Use `attachScreenshot: true` when your CI system renders JUnit XML
attachment extensions (GitLab CI, Jenkins JUnit plugin, CircleCI test insights).

**When NOT to use:** Do not use `attachScreenshot: true` if your JUnit XML is parsed
by tools that reject non-standard `<attachments>` extension elements. In that case,
use the Allure reporter with its native attachment support instead.

**[community] Base64-encoded screenshots in JUnit XML significantly inflate file size —
a single 1080x2400 PNG adds ~3 MB to the XML. JUnit XML parsers in many CI systems have
an undocumented file size limit (typically 5–25 MB). A test suite with 5+ failures on
high-resolution Android devices can exceed this limit and cause the XML upload to fail
silently:** WHY: Base64 encoding expands binary data by ~33%; JUnit XML size limits are
not documented by most CI platforms.

### Pattern 298 — WDIO `specFileRetries` with `onTestRetry` Per-Attempt Hooks

WDIO v9 `specFileRetries` retries the entire spec file on failure. Combining it with
the `onTestRetry` hook enables per-attempt behaviour: clearing app state, logging which
attempt is running, or rotating proxy credentials between retries.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — spec-level retry with per-attempt app-reset hook
import type { Options } from '@wdio/types';

const APP_ID =
  process.env.IOS_BUNDLE_ID ?? process.env.ANDROID_APP_ID ?? 'com.example.app';

export const config: Options.Testrunner = {
  // Retry the entire spec file up to 2 times on failure
  specFileRetries: 2,
  // Wait 5 s between spec file retry attempts
  specFileRetriesDelay: 5,
  // Retry immediately after failure (set true to defer until all other specs run)
  specFileRetriesDeferred: false,

  onTestRetry: async (test, error, retryCount /* 0-based */) => {
    // Log human-friendly attempt number (retryCount + 1)
    console.log(
      `[retry] Attempt ${retryCount + 1} for: "${test.title}"\n` +
        `  Failed with: ${error.message}`
    );

    // Reset app state before the next attempt to avoid stale state bleed
    try {
      await browser.execute('mobile: terminateApp', { bundleId: APP_ID });
      await browser.pause(800);
      await browser.execute('mobile: activateApp', { bundleId: APP_ID });
      console.log(`[retry] App reset complete for attempt ${retryCount + 2}`);
    } catch (cleanupErr) {
      console.warn(`[retry] App reset failed: ${cleanupErr}`);
    }
  },

  afterTest: async (_test, _ctx, { error, retries }) => {
    if (error && typeof retries !== 'undefined' && retries.attempts < (retries.limit ?? 0)) {
      console.log(
        `[afterTest] Intermediate failure (attempt ${retries.attempts + 1}) — ` +
          'will retry per specFileRetries config'
      );
    }
  },
};
```

**When to use:** Use `specFileRetries` for tests that are genuinely flaky due to
external factors (device connectivity blips, network latency, third-party service
timeouts) that cannot be fixed in test code. Limit to 1–2 retries.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use spec retries to mask test instability. A retry budget
of 3+ on a large suite signals that the app or infrastructure is unreliable — fix
the root cause first.

**[community] `specFileRetriesDeferred: false` (default) retries the spec immediately
after failure. Setting it to `true` defers retries until after all other specs have
run — useful when failures are caused by a shared resource lock (e.g., a single
physical device) that will be free after other specs finish:** WHY: Immediate retry
competes for the same resource that just failed; deferred retry gives the resource
time to become available.

**[community] The `onTestRetry` hook receives `retryCount` starting from 0 (first retry
= 0). Teams that log `retryCount` directly in "Attempt X of Y" messages produce
off-by-one output ("Attempt 0 of 2") which is confusing in CI dashboards. Always log
`retryCount + 1`:** WHY: WDIO uses zero-based retry counters internally, matching
array indexing conventions but conflicting with natural language counting.

### Pattern 299 — Appium 3.x `--base-path` for Kubernetes Ingress Routing

Appium 3.x `--base-path` (default: `/`) moves all endpoints under a custom prefix,
enabling multiple Appium nodes to share a single Kubernetes Ingress via path-based
routing. Without this, each node needs its own LoadBalancer IP or port.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — WDIO targeting Appium behind a K8s Ingress with --base-path
// Appium launch: appium --port 4723 --base-path /appium/node1
// K8s Ingress:   /appium/node1/* → appium-node1:4723 (no path rewrite)
import { defineConfig } from '@wdio/config';

const APPIUM_NODE = process.env.APPIUM_NODE ?? 'node1';
const INGRESS_HOST = process.env.INGRESS_HOST ?? 'appium.internal.example.com';

async function waitForAppiumReady(baseUrl: string, retries = 5): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < retries; i++) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/status`);
      if (res.ok) {
        const body = (await res.json()) as { value: { ready: boolean } };
        if (body.value.ready) {
          console.log(`[onPrepare] Appium node '${APPIUM_NODE}' is ready`);
          return;
        }
      }
    } catch { /* not ready yet */ }
    console.log(`[onPrepare] Waiting for Appium node (attempt ${i + 1}/${retries})...`);
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 3_000));
  }
  throw new Error(`Appium node at ${baseUrl}/status not ready after ${retries} attempts`);
}

export default defineConfig({
  hostname: INGRESS_HOST,
  port: 443,
  protocol: 'https',
  // Must match --base-path on the Appium node — no trailing slash
  path: `/appium/${APPIUM_NODE}`,

  capabilities: [
    {
      platformName: 'Android',
      'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
      'appium:deviceName': 'emulator-5554',
      'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,
    },
  ],

  onPrepare: async () => {
    const baseUrl = `https://${INGRESS_HOST}/appium/${APPIUM_NODE}`;
    await waitForAppiumReady(baseUrl);
  },
});
```

**When to use:** Use `--base-path` when deploying multiple Appium nodes behind a
shared Kubernetes Ingress or Nginx reverse proxy. This avoids the need for one
LoadBalancer IP per Appium node.

**When NOT to use:** Do not add a custom `--base-path` for a single-node deployment —
the default `/` path works and a custom prefix complicates WDIO configuration without
benefit.

**[official] Appium 3.x validates that `--base-path` starts with `/` and does not end
with `/` (unless it is exactly `/`). The `path` in `wdio.conf.ts` must exactly match
the Appium `--base-path` — a trailing slash mismatch causes every request to return 404.**

**[community] Kubernetes Ingress controllers (nginx, Traefik) may strip or rewrite
the path prefix before forwarding to the Appium pod. Configure `rewrite-target: /$2`
on nginx or `stripPrefix` on Traefik to preserve the path that Appium expects.
Misconfigured rewrites produce `404 Not Found` for session creation with no Appium-side
log entry — the request never reaches Appium:** WHY: Ingress path rewriting happens at
the proxy layer before the packet reaches the Appium process; the 404 comes from
Appium's HTTP router not recognising the rewritten path.

**[community] Do NOT append `/wd/hub` to the WDIO `path` config when using Appium 3.x.
Appium 3 removed the Selenium-legacy `/wd/hub` prefix; combining both gives
`/appium/node1/wd/hub` which returns 404. This is the most common copy-paste mistake
when migrating a WDIO config written for Appium 1.x or 2.x:** WHY: Appium 2.x and 3.x
use the W3C WebDriver endpoint scheme directly at the configured base path; the
`/wd/hub` namespace was removed with Appium 2.0.

### Pattern 300 — Appium `appium:forceSimulatorSoftwareKeyboardPresence` for iOS CI Text Input

iOS Simulator suppresses the software keyboard by default when a hardware keyboard is
connected (common in CI Macs where the build agent uses a physical keyboard). Appium
3.x exposes `appium:forceSimulatorSoftwareKeyboardPresence` to always show the software
keyboard so `setValue()` and `addValue()` work correctly without relying on the
hardware keyboard path.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — iOS Simulator capability: always show software keyboard
import type { Options } from '@wdio/types';
import type { AppiumCapabilities } from '@wdio/types';

const iosSimulatorCaps: AppiumCapabilities = {
  platformName: 'iOS',
  'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
  'appium:deviceName': 'iPhone 16',
  'appium:platformVersion': '18.0',
  'appium:app': process.env.IOS_APP_PATH!,
  // Force software keyboard so setValue() triggers the correct input method
  // on CI Macs that also have a physical keyboard attached
  'appium:forceSimulatorSoftwareKeyboardPresence': true,
};

export const config: Options.Testrunner = {
  capabilities: [iosSimulatorCaps],

  beforeTest: async () => {
    // Dismiss any auto-complete popup that iOS may show on first text field focus
    const firstResponder = await $('**/XCUIElementTypeTextField');
    if (await firstResponder.isDisplayed()) {
      await firstResponder.click();
      // Wait for keyboard animation to complete before calling setValue
      await browser.pause(400);
    }
  },
};
```

**When to use:** Set `appium:forceSimulatorSoftwareKeyboardPresence: true` on every CI
agent that might have a physical keyboard. Without it, XCUITest may route text through
the hardware keyboard path, causing `setValue()` to silently fail (no characters typed,
no error thrown).

**When NOT to use:** Do not set it for performance benchmarks testing keyboard
presentation timing — the forced software keyboard always appears immediately and
eliminates the real-world delay.

**[community] CI Macs with a Bluetooth keyboard left paired to the system exhibit the
most frequent occurrence of this bug. The symptom is `setValue()` calling succeeds (no
exception) but the text field remains empty after the call. Adding the capability is
the fix; clearing the Bluetooth pairing state across CI agents is impractical:**
WHY: XCUITest detects any connected keyboard (Bluetooth included) and routes text
input through it, bypassing the software keyboard entirely.

**[official] `appium:forceSimulatorSoftwareKeyboardPresence` is an XCUITest driver
capability. It calls the Simulator `simctl` API to set `SoftwareKeyboardPresence = true`
in the device preferences before the session starts.**
