## Cycle 34 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 360 — `mobile:enrollBiometric` / `mobile:sendBiometricMatch` for iOS Face ID / Touch ID simulation [official]

**Description.**
XCUITest driver exposes `mobile:enrollBiometric` to enroll (or unenroll) a Simulator's biometric sensor before a test, and `mobile:sendBiometricMatch` to inject a pass or fail result into the waiting authentication dialog. This enables full end-to-end coverage of login flows that use `LAContext.evaluatePolicy` without manual interaction. The pattern requires the Simulator to have a Face ID– or Touch ID–capable device type; `iPhone SE (1st gen)` Simulators lack Face ID and will throw `XCUIApplicationError`. Always call `isBiometricEnrolled` first so tests self-skip on unsupported device types rather than failing with a confusing error.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

async function withBiometricAuth(
  pass: boolean,
  action: () => Promise<void>
): Promise<void> {
  const enrolled = await browser.execute('mobile: isBiometricEnrolled');
  if (!enrolled) {
    await browser.execute('mobile: enrollBiometric', { isEnabled: true });
  }
  await action(); // triggers the LAContext prompt
  await browser.execute('mobile: sendBiometricMatch', {
    type: 'faceId',   // 'touchId' | 'faceId'
    match: pass,       // true = successful auth, false = rejected auth
  });
}

it('shows error on failed Face ID', async () => {
  await withBiometricAuth(false, async () => {
    await $('~LoginButton').click();
  });
  await expect($('~AuthErrorBanner')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing biometric-gated login, secure payment confirmation, or password manager auto-fill on iOS Simulator.
- **Do NOT use when**: Running on real devices (hardware biometrics cannot be injected) or when the app uses `SecureEnclave` directly (XCUITest cannot intercept hardware key operations).
- **Alternative**: Use `appium:allowTestPackages` + a stub `LAContext` replacement injected via `mobile:installXCTestBundle` for real-device coverage.

---

### Pattern 361 — `mobile:siriCommand` for voice-activated feature testing on iOS [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:siriCommand` activates Siri on the Simulator and submits a text utterance, allowing automation of Siri Shortcut triggers, App Intent invocations, and voice-navigation flows without physical speech. The command waits until Siri's response animation completes before returning, making it safe to assert on the app UI immediately after. Siri must be enabled on the Simulator (`Settings > Siri & Search > Listen for "Hey Siri"` is not required; only the Siri feature toggle matters). The command has a hard 15-second timeout; long-running Siri queries (e.g. web search) may time out in CI where network is restricted.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface SiriCommandOptions {
  text: string;
}

async function invokeSiriShortcut(utterance: string): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute<void, [SiriCommandOptions]>(
    'mobile: siriCommand',
    [{ text: utterance }]
  );
  // Siri dismisses automatically after responding; wait for app to settle
  await browser.pause(500);
}

it('opens reminders list via Siri shortcut', async () => {
  await invokeSiriShortcut('Show my reminders');
  const list = await $('~RemindersList');
  await list.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  await expect(list).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Validating App Intents, SiriKit donation flows, or any voice-first feature path.
- **Do NOT use when**: Running on real devices (real Siri requires microphone access and active Apple ID) or in network-restricted CI (Siri contacts Apple servers for NLU even on Simulator).
- **Alternative**: Trigger Shortcuts directly via `mobile:launchApp` with a `x-callback-url` deep link if voice is not the actual requirement under test.

---

### Pattern 362 — `mobile:configureLocalization` for runtime language and locale switching on iOS Simulator [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:configureLocalization` changes the Simulator's language, locale, and keyboard settings without relaunching the Appium session or resetting the device. It accepts `language`, `locale`, `calendarFormat`, and optionally `keyboards` arrays. The change takes effect immediately for new app launches; calling `mobile:launchApp` (or `activateApp`) after `configureLocalization` produces a fresh app instance in the new locale without a full session restart. This is dramatically faster than the `appium:language` / `appium:locale` capabilities which require a Simulator reboot.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface LocaleConfig {
  language: string;      // BCP-47 code, e.g. 'de'
  locale: string;        // locale identifier, e.g. 'de_DE'
  calendarFormat?: string; // e.g. 'gregorian'
  keyboards?: string[];  // e.g. ['de_DE@sw=QWERTZ']
}

async function switchLocaleAndRelaunch(
  bundleId: string,
  config: LocaleConfig
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: terminateApp', { bundleId });
  await browser.execute('mobile: configureLocalization', config);
  await browser.execute('mobile: launchApp', { bundleId });
}

it('displays currency in German locale', async () => {
  await switchLocaleAndRelaunch('com.example.app', {
    language: 'de',
    locale: 'de_DE',
    calendarFormat: 'gregorian',
  });
  const priceLabel = await $('~ProductPrice');
  await expect(priceLabel).toHaveText('12,99 €');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Running localisation regression suites across multiple locales in a single Appium session (10-15× faster than rebooting per locale).
- **Do NOT use when**: Testing locale-sensitive system UI (date picker, keyboard autocorrect) that requires a Simulator reboot to fully adopt the new locale.
- **Alternative**: Use `appium:language` + `appium:locale` capabilities at session-start when full Simulator reboot fidelity is required, accepting the ~90-second overhead per locale.

---

### Pattern 363 — `mobile:runXCTest` for executing native XCTest suites inline from WDIO [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:runXCTest` launches a compiled XCTest bundle on the target device/Simulator from within an Appium session, runs a specified test method, and returns a structured result object including pass/fail status, duration, and failure description. This bridges the gap between Appium UI automation and XCTest performance tests, accessibility tests, or private-API-exercising unit tests that cannot be driven via WebDriver. The bundle must already be installed (via `mobile:installXCTestBundle`) before the call. The command blocks until the XCTest method completes or the per-test timeout expires.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface XCTestResult {
  passed: boolean;
  testName: string;
  duration: number;
  failureDescription?: string;
}

async function runXCTestMethod(
  bundleId: string,
  testClass: string,
  testMethod: string,
  timeoutMs = 30_000
): Promise<XCTestResult> {
  return browser.execute<XCTestResult, [object]>(
    'mobile: runXCTest',
    [{
      bundleId,
      testName: `${testClass}/${testMethod}`,
      timeout: timeoutMs / 1000,
    }]
  );
}

it('GPU render time is below 16ms threshold via XCTest', async () => {
  await browser.execute('mobile: installXCTestBundle', {
    app: '/path/to/PerfTests.xctest.zip',
  });
  const result = await runXCTestMethod(
    'com.example.PerfTests',
    'RenderPerfTests',
    'testFrameRenderTime'
  );
  expect(result.passed).toBe(true);
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Validating performance metrics, low-level APIs, or XCTest-only accessibility assertions that require the XCTest framework's direct device access.
- **Do NOT use when**: Replacing standard Appium element interactions — XCTest bundles add build and install overhead (~10-30 seconds) that is unnecessary for regular UI assertions.
- **Alternative**: `mobile:startPerfRecord` + `mobile:stopPerfRecord` for Instruments-based profiling that does not require a separate XCTest bundle.

---

### Pattern 364 — WDIO v9 `browser.emulate('clock')` for deterministic time-dependent UI tests on mobile WebViews [official]

**Description.**
WebdriverIO v9's `browser.emulate('clock', { now })` uses the WebDriver BiDi `script.addPreloadScript` hook to replace `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `requestAnimationFrame` with fake implementations, enabling tests to control time without real-time delays. In mobile WebView contexts, this is invaluable for testing session-timeout banners, countdown timers, token-refresh logic, and date-picker defaults that would otherwise require sleeping for minutes. The emulation applies to both the main document and all same-origin iframes inside the WebView. Restore real time with the returned `restore()` function before switching back to native context.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

it('shows session-expiry modal after 30-minute idle', async () => {
  // Switch to the WebView context
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');

  const restore = await browser.emulate('clock', {
    now: new Date('2026-01-01T10:00:00Z').getTime(),
  });

  await browser.execute(() => {
    // Advance fake clock by 31 minutes to trigger session timeout
    (window as any).__clock.tick(31 * 60 * 1000);
  });

  const modal = await $('[data-testid="session-timeout-modal"]');
  await modal.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 2000 });
  await expect(modal).toBeDisplayed();

  await restore();
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing any time-dependent logic in a hybrid app's WebView (session expiry, OTP countdown, date-picker defaults) where real-time delays are impractical.
- **Do NOT use when**: Testing native iOS/Android date pickers or OS-level notification scheduling — BiDi clock emulation only affects browser JavaScript; native layer time is unaffected.
- **Alternative**: Inject `__clock` via `mobile:addInitScript` for Appium 3.x WebView contexts, or use `mobile:shell` + `adb shell date` for native-layer time manipulation on Android.

---

### Pattern 365 — WDIO v9 `browser.url()` with `onBeforeLoad` for mobile WebView API stubbing before page initialisation [official]

**Description.**
WebdriverIO v9's `browser.url(url, { onBeforeLoad })` executes a callback function inside the WebView's JavaScript context immediately after the document object is created but before any page scripts run. This enables injecting stub implementations of Web APIs (Battery, Geolocation, Notification, Payment Request) that page scripts depend on before the app's own bundle has a chance to cache the real API references. In mobile hybrid apps this is far more reliable than `browser.execute()` post-load injection, which races with the app bundle's module initialisation.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

it('renders low-battery warning when battery level is 10%', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');

  await browser.url('https://app.example.com/home', {
    onBeforeLoad(win: Window) {
      // Stub Battery API before the page bundle loads
      Object.defineProperty(win.navigator, 'getBattery', {
        writable: true,
        value: () =>
          Promise.resolve({
            level: 0.1,
            charging: false,
            chargingTime: Infinity,
            dischargingTime: 600,
          }),
      });
    },
  });

  const warning = await $('[data-testid="low-battery-warning"]');
  await warning.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });
  await expect(warning).toHaveText(/Battery low/i);

  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Stubbing Web APIs that are read once at module initialisation time (Battery, PaymentRequest, Geolocation) where post-load injection races with page script execution.
- **Do NOT use when**: The WebView uses `Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'` without `'unsafe-eval'` — BiDi preload scripts are still injected but any `eval`-based stubbing techniques inside the callback will be blocked.
- **Alternative**: Mock at the network level via `browser.mock()` (Pattern 366) for API responses rather than browser API stubs when the data comes from a fetch call rather than a navigator property.

---

### Pattern 366 — WDIO v9 `browser.mock()` with BiDi network interception for mobile API response stubbing [official]

**Description.**
`browser.mock(urlPattern, filters)` registers a BiDi network intercept that matches requests from the WebView by URL glob and optional method/header filters, then `.respond(body, options)` returns a synthetic HTTP response before the request reaches the server. This replaces Charles Proxy or mitmproxy for WebView-level API mocking, eliminating the need to configure device-level proxy settings or install custom CA certificates. Mocks are scoped to the WDIO session and automatically cleaned up on session end. Multiple mocks can be stacked; the first matching mock wins.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

it('displays error message when /api/user returns 503', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');

  const userMock = await browser.mock('**/api/user', {
    method: 'GET',
  });

  userMock.respond(
    { error: 'Service temporarily unavailable' },
    { statusCode: 503, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  );

  await browser.url('https://app.example.com/profile');

  const errorBanner = await $('[data-testid="error-banner"]');
  await errorBanner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });
  await expect(errorBanner).toHaveText(/temporarily unavailable/i);

  await browser.mockRestoreAll();
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Stubbing REST/GraphQL API responses in hybrid app WebViews to test error states, pagination edge cases, or feature-flag-driven UI variations without a real backend.
- **Do NOT use when**: The app uses WebSockets or gRPC streaming — `browser.mock()` only intercepts HTTP/HTTPS fetch and XHR requests; WebSocket frames are not matched.
- **Alternative**: Use `appium:proxy` capability with a local intercepting proxy (e.g. `mockttp`) for full protocol coverage including WebSockets and native HTTP clients.

---

### Pattern 367 — UIAutomator2 `mobile:deepLink` for Android intent-based deep link testing [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:deepLink` sends an Android Intent with a URI scheme to the device, launching the app's registered deep-link handler without relying on a host browser or the `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW` shell command. It accepts `url`, `package`, and optional `waitForLaunch` boolean, blocking until the app is in the foreground before returning. This is the idiomatic Appium pattern for testing Universal Links, App Links, and custom URI schemes. Using `adb shell` directly bypasses the Intent resolution system and may not correctly simulate an HTTP link tap from the OS browser.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface DeepLinkOptions {
  url: string;
  package: string;
  waitForLaunch?: boolean;
}

async function openDeepLink(url: string, pkg: string): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute<void, [DeepLinkOptions]>(
    'mobile: deepLink',
    [{ url, package: pkg, waitForLaunch: true }]
  );
}

it('navigates to product detail via deep link', async () => {
  await openDeepLink(
    'https://shop.example.com/products/abc-123',
    'com.example.shop'
  );
  const productTitle = await $('~ProductDetailTitle');
  await productTitle.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  await expect(productTitle).toHaveText('ABC-123');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing all flavours of Android deep links: custom URI schemes (`myapp://`), App Links (`https://`), and Firebase Dynamic Links that resolve to `https://` before the OS delegates to the app.
- **Do NOT use when**: Testing the OS intent-chooser dialog (which deep link handler the user picks) — `mobile:deepLink` routes directly to the specified package, bypassing the disambiguation sheet.
- **Alternative**: `driver.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'am', args: ['start', '-a', 'android.intent.action.VIEW', '-d', url] })` for full intent-system fidelity including the disambiguation dialog, at the cost of losing `waitForLaunch` safety.

---

### Pattern 368 — XCUITest `mobile:setAppearance` / `mobile:getAppearance` for dark-mode regression testing [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:setAppearance` switches the iOS Simulator between `light` and `dark` appearances at runtime without rebooting the Simulator or restarting the app. The change is immediate and triggers `UITraitCollection` re-evaluation in the running app, causing `traitCollectionDidChange` observers and SwiftUI `@Environment(\.colorScheme)` bindings to fire. This makes it possible to run a single test suite that asserts both themes in one session. `mobile:getAppearance` returns the current appearance string (`'light'` or `'dark'`) for assertions or conditional branching.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

type Appearance = 'light' | 'dark';

async function setAppearanceAndVerify(
  appearance: Appearance
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: setAppearance', { style: appearance });
  const current = await browser.execute<string, []>('mobile: getAppearance');
  if (current !== appearance) {
    throw new Error(`Appearance mismatch: expected ${appearance}, got ${current}`);
  }
}

for (const theme of ['light', 'dark'] as const) {
  it(`renders correct colors in ${theme} mode`, async () => {
    await setAppearanceAndVerify(theme);
    const header = await $('~AppHeader');
    const bgColor = await header.getCSSProperty('background-color');
    const expected = theme === 'dark' ? 'rgba(28,28,30,1)' : 'rgba(255,255,255,1)';
    expect(bgColor.value).toBe(expected);
  });
}
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Running dark-mode regression suites against a live app — far faster and more reliable than screenshot diffing after a full device reboot per theme.
- **Do NOT use when**: Testing on real devices (`mobile:setAppearance` is Simulator-only; on real devices use `xcrun simctl ui` equivalent for device-linked testing labs).
- **Alternative**: `UITraitCollection` overrides injected via `mobile:runXCTest` for unit-level colour token assertions that do not require a full UI session.

---

### Pattern 369 — `mobile:installCertificate` for per-test SSL certificate trust on iOS Simulator [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:installCertificate` installs a DER- or PEM-encoded X.509 certificate into the iOS Simulator's trusted root store, enabling tests to hit local HTTPS test servers or corporate internal services whose certificates are not trusted by the Apple root CA bundle. Unlike the `appium:customSSLCert` capability (which installs at session start), `mobile:installCertificate` can be called mid-session, allowing a test suite to install different certificates for different test groups. The certificate is installed system-wide on the Simulator and persists across app restarts until the Simulator is erased.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import { readFileSync } from 'fs';

async function installLocalCA(certPath: string): Promise<void> {
  const certBase64 = readFileSync(certPath).toString('base64');
  await browser.execute('mobile: installCertificate', {
    content: certBase64,
    // 'root' installs as trusted root CA; 'leaf' for leaf certs only
    type: 'root',
  });
}

before(async () => {
  await installLocalCA('./certs/local-dev-ca.der');
});

it('loads account dashboard over local HTTPS', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');
  await browser.url('https://api.local.dev/dashboard');
  await expect($('[data-testid="account-header"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing against a local HTTPS server, staging environment with a self-signed certificate, or corporate proxy with a private CA during CI.
- **Do NOT use when**: Running on real devices (certificate management on real devices requires MDM profile installation, which cannot be automated via Appium); use `appium:customSSLCert` capability for session-start install.
- **Alternative**: `WKWebView` with `NSExceptionDomains` in the app's `Info.plist` (ATS exception) for development builds where bypassing TLS validation is acceptable.

---

### Pattern 370 — UIAutomator2 `mobile:getContexts` for precise WebView context discovery in hybrid apps [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:getContexts` returns a rich list of all available WebView contexts in the current session, including the page title, URL, package, pid, and webview connection state — far more detail than the standard `driver.getContexts()` W3C command, which returns only opaque context ID strings. This enables tests to select the correct WebView context by URL or title rather than by fragile index, eliminating the `WEBVIEW_0` / `WEBVIEW_1` ambiguity that causes flaky context switches in apps with multiple embedded WebViews. The command also returns `isAttached` to distinguish ready contexts from WebViews still initialising.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface WebViewContext {
  id: string;
  title?: string;
  url?: string;
  packageName: string;
  webviewName: string;
  isAttached: boolean;
}

async function switchToWebViewByUrlPattern(pattern: RegExp): Promise<string> {
  const contexts = await browser.execute<WebViewContext[], []>(
    'mobile: getContexts'
  );
  const target = contexts.find(
    (ctx) => ctx.isAttached && ctx.url && pattern.test(ctx.url)
  );
  if (!target) throw new Error(`No attached WebView matching ${pattern}`);
  await browser.switchContext(target.id);
  return target.id;
}

it('interacts with the payment WebView', async () => {
  await switchToWebViewByUrlPattern(/stripe\.com\/checkout/);
  const payBtn = await $('[data-testid="pay-now"]');
  await payBtn.waitForEnabled({ timeout: 10_000 });
  await payBtn.click();
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: The app hosts more than one WebView simultaneously (e.g. an in-app browser alongside a payment WebView), making index-based context switching fragile.
- **Do NOT use when**: The app has only one WebView and session context switching by index is reliable — `mobile:getContexts` adds a round-trip overhead of ~50-100ms.
- **Alternative**: Combine standard `driver.getContexts()` with `driver.switchContext(id)` plus a `waitUntil` retry loop when context index is stable and predictable.

---

### Pattern 371 — WDIO v9 `browser.mock()` request counter for verifying API call frequency in mobile WebViews [official]

**Description.**
The mock object returned by `browser.mock()` exposes a `calls` array that records every matched request with full URL, headers, body, and timestamp. Tests can assert on `mock.calls.length` to verify that the app does not over-fetch (e.g. polling an endpoint on every re-render) or under-fetch (e.g. missing a required initialisation call). Calling `mock.clear()` between test steps resets the call log without removing the intercept, enabling per-step frequency assertions in multi-step flows.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

it('calls /api/feed exactly once on initial load', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');

  const feedMock = await browser.mock('**/api/feed', { method: 'GET' });
  feedMock.respond({ items: [] }, { statusCode: 200 });

  await browser.url('https://app.example.com/home');
  await $('[data-testid="feed-container"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });

  // Assert exactly one fetch — guards against duplicate React render effects
  expect(feedMock.calls.length).toBe(1);

  // Navigate away and back
  feedMock.clear();
  await browser.back();
  await browser.url('https://app.example.com/home');
  await $('[data-testid="feed-container"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });

  // Should re-fetch once on return
  expect(feedMock.calls.length).toBe(1);

  await browser.mockRestoreAll();
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Guarding against N+1 fetch regressions, verifying lazy loading triggers, or asserting that prefetch logic fires at the right lifecycle point.
- **Do NOT use when**: Asserting on native HTTP client calls from the native layer — `browser.mock()` only intercepts WebView (Chromium renderer) requests; calls from OkHttp, URLSession, or Retrofit are invisible to it.
- **Alternative**: Network traffic inspection via `appium:proxy` + `mockttp` for native-layer request frequency assertions.

---

### Pattern 372 — XCUITest `mobile:clearKeychains` for isolated secure-storage state between tests [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:clearKeychains` wipes all keychain items for all apps on the Simulator in a single call. It is the fastest way to guarantee that tests relying on `SecItem`-stored tokens, passwords, or biometric key pairs start from a clean state. Calling it in `beforeEach` on login-flow suites eliminates the "already logged in" state bleed that occurs when a previous test stored a token and the app skips the login screen. The call takes under 100ms on a warm Simulator and is significantly faster than a full Simulator reset.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('Login flow — clean keychain', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    // Clear all keychain items so app sees no stored credentials
    await browser.execute('mobile: clearKeychains');
    // Re-launch the app to a fresh state
    await browser.execute('mobile: terminateApp', {
      bundleId: 'com.example.app',
    });
    await browser.execute('mobile: launchApp', {
      bundleId: 'com.example.app',
    });
  });

  it('shows login screen when no stored token exists', async () => {
    const loginScreen = await $('~LoginScreen');
    await loginScreen.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
    await expect(loginScreen).toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('rejects incorrect password and shows error', async () => {
    await $('~UsernameField').setValue('user@example.com');
    await $('~PasswordField').setValue('wrongpassword');
    await $('~LoginButton').click();
    await expect($('~LoginErrorMessage')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing login, token refresh, biometric setup, or credential migration flows that depend on a clean `SecItem` state.
- **Do NOT use when**: The app stores critical configuration (not credentials) in the keychain — `mobile:clearKeychains` deletes ALL keychain items across ALL apps, including Simulator system items; use `mobile:setPermissions` or targeted `SecItemDelete` via `mobile:runXCTest` for surgical cleanup.
- **Alternative**: `appium:fullReset: true` for a full Simulator wipe (slower, ~60 seconds) when the app also stores state in `NSUserDefaults` or CoreData that must be cleared simultaneously.

---

### Pattern 373 — UIAutomator2 `mobile:shell` with `pm grant` for targeted Android permission grants without dialog interaction [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:shell` executes ADB shell commands server-side through the UIAutomator2 driver without requiring a raw `adb` binary in the CI environment. Combining it with `pm grant <package> <permission>` grants dangerous permissions programmatically, bypassing the Android permission dialog entirely. This is faster and more reliable than tapping the "Allow" button in a `waitForDisplayed` loop, and it avoids the two-denial suppression problem described in the Cycle 32 Gotcha 4. Each `mobile:shell` call returns the stdout string, enabling assertions on the command output.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

const APP_PACKAGE = 'com.example.app';

const PERMISSIONS = [
  'android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION',
  'android.permission.CAMERA',
  'android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES',
] as const;

async function grantAllPermissions(): Promise<void> {
  for (const perm of PERMISSIONS) {
    const result: string = await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'pm',
      args: ['grant', APP_PACKAGE, perm],
    });
    // pm grant returns empty string on success, error text on failure
    if (result.trim().length > 0) {
      throw new Error(`Failed to grant ${perm}: ${result}`);
    }
  }
}

before(async () => {
  await grantAllPermissions();
});

it('accesses camera without permission dialog', async () => {
  await $('~OpenCameraButton').click();
  await expect($('~CameraPreview')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Granting multiple permissions in `before`/`beforeAll` hooks to remove dialog-interaction boilerplate from tests whose focus is the post-permission feature, not the permission flow itself.
- **Do NOT use when**: The test scenario IS the permission request flow — use `mobile:changePermissions` or wait for the OS dialog and tap via `~Allow` accessibility ID when the dialog UX is under test.
- **Alternative**: `appium:autoGrantPermissions: true` capability for session-start permission granting on fresh installs; use `mobile:shell pm grant` for mid-session re-granting after a deliberate revoke.

---

### Pattern 374 — WDIO v9 `browser.emulate('geolocation')` in Android Chrome WebViews for location-based feature testing [official]

**Description.**
`browser.emulate('geolocation', { latitude, longitude, accuracy })` uses the BiDi `emulation.setGeolocationOverride` command to inject a fake GPS position into the WebView's `navigator.geolocation` API. It works in Android Chrome WebViews that support WebDriver BiDi (Chrome 108+), enabling deterministic testing of location-gated features (store locators, nearby search, delivery radius checks) without physical device movement or mock location apps. The emulation persists for the duration of the session or until `restore()` is called, making it safe to use across multiple `it` blocks in a single `describe`.

```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface GeoLocation {
  latitude: number;
  longitude: number;
  accuracy?: number;
}

async function withFakeLocation(
  location: GeoLocation,
  test: () => Promise<void>
): Promise<void> {
  const restore = await browser.emulate('geolocation', location);
  try {
    await test();
  } finally {
    await restore();
  }
}

it('shows nearest store in San Francisco', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');
  await withFakeLocation(
    { latitude: 37.7749, longitude: -122.4194, accuracy: 10 },
    async () => {
      await $('[data-testid="find-store-btn"]').click();
      const storeResult = await $('[data-testid="nearest-store-name"]');
      await storeResult.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
      await expect(storeResult).toHaveText(/Market Street/i);
    }
  );
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing WebView-rendered location features in hybrid apps where the feature reads `navigator.geolocation` directly.
- **Do NOT use when**: The app reads GPS via native `CLLocationManager` (iOS) or `FusedLocationProviderClient` (Android) — `browser.emulate` only affects the WebView JavaScript context; native location APIs are unaffected.
- **Alternative**: `mobile:mockLocation` (iOS Simulator GPX routes) or `adb shell geo fix <lat> <lng>` via `mobile:shell` for native-layer GPS injection.

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 34

**Gotcha 1 — `mobile:switchContext` with a WebView that uses `isolatedWorld` renders `document.querySelector` calls invisible to the Appium WebView session [community]**
When a WebView host app enables `WKWebView.isFindInteractionEnabled` (iOS 16+) or Chrome's `--isolate-origins` flag, the JavaScript realm used by `executeScript` is a separate isolated world from the page's main world. Calling `browser.execute(() => document.querySelector('...'))` returns `null` for elements that are clearly present in the page DOM when viewed in Safari's Web Inspector. WHY: WebDriver's `executeScript` injects into the default isolated world (realm ID `"default"`), but `isFindInteractionEnabled` causes WebKit to create an additional page world with a mirrored-but-separate DOM proxy; element references obtained in one world are `null` in the other. Fix: use WDIO element selectors (`$(selector)`) which route through the WebDriver element-finding protocol rather than direct JS DOM access, or explicitly set `webviewConnectTimeout` and verify the world ID via `Debugger.enable` in the BiDi session.

**Gotcha 2 — `browser.emulate('clock')` stops `setTimeout`-based Appium command polling inside the WebView, causing `waitForDisplayed` to hang indefinitely [community]**
After calling `browser.emulate('clock')`, all `setTimeout` and `setInterval` calls inside the WebView are routed through the fake clock scheduler. WDIO's internal `waitForDisplayed` implementation polls the element's `isDisplayed()` state via a `setTimeout`-based retry loop injected into the WebView context. Because the fake clock does not auto-advance, the retry loop never fires and `waitForDisplayed` hangs until its outer Node.js `setTimeout` (which is unaffected) expires — resulting in a cryptic element-not-found timeout rather than the clock-related root cause. WHY: WDIO's `waitUntil` relies on `browser.executeAsync()`, which internally uses `setTimeout(resolve, pollInterval)` inside the browser context; when `window.setTimeout` is replaced by a sinon-style fake, `resolve` is enqueued in the fake queue and never ticked automatically. Fix: always advance the fake clock explicitly via `browser.execute(() => (window as any).__clock.tick(ms))` before calling `waitForDisplayed`, or use native WDIO `waitUntil` with a Node.js-side polling loop that calls `browser.execute` synchronously.

**Gotcha 3 — `mobile:deepLink` on Android 12+ requires the app to hold the `android.permission.READ_PHONE_STATE` or target `minSdk 31` or the intent is silently dropped by the OS [community]**
On Android 12 (API 31+), App Links using Digital Asset Links require the app to pass the OS's link-policy checker before the Intent is dispatched to the app's `DeepLinkActivity`. If the device's Digital Asset Links JSON file is unreachable (network isolation in CI) or stale, `mobile:deepLink` returns success from Appium's perspective (the Intent was sent) but the app is never foregrounded — instead the Android "Open with" chooser appears and is never dismissed. WHY: Android 12 introduced `FLAG_ACTIVITY_REQUIRE_NON_BROWSER` verification; when asset-link verification fails the OS defaults to showing the app chooser rather than directly launching the app. Fix: use `adb shell pm set-app-links-verified --package <pkg> <domain>` via `mobile:shell` before calling `mobile:deepLink` to bypass network-dependent link verification in CI.

**Gotcha 4 — `mobile:clearKeychains` on iOS 17 Simulator silently fails when the Simulator's `securityd` process has crashed [community]**
`mobile:clearKeychains` calls `xcrun simctl keychain <udid> reset` internally. On iOS 17 Simulators that have been running for many hours or have undergone several `terminateApp` + `launchApp` cycles, the Simulator's `securityd` process occasionally enters a zombie state. In this state `xcrun simctl keychain reset` exits with code 0 but the keychain items are not actually deleted — the app still finds its stored token and skips the login screen. WHY: `securityd` is responsible for serialising `SecItem` reads and writes; a zombie `securityd` accepts RPC calls (so `xcrun` exits 0) but does not commit the delete operations to the backing SQLite database at `~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Devices/<udid>/data/Library/Keychains/`. Fix: assert the keychain is empty by reading a known item via `mobile:runXCTest` or a `SecItemCopyMatching` shell script after `clearKeychains`; if it is non-empty, reboot the Simulator via `xcrun simctl shutdown <udid> && xcrun simctl boot <udid>`.

**Gotcha 5 — UIAutomator2 `mobile:shell pm grant` silently no-ops for permissions declared with `android:maxSdkVersion` lower than the test device's SDK version [community]**
`pm grant` returns an empty string (success indicator) even when the permission cannot be granted because the `<uses-permission android:maxSdkVersion="28">` manifest attribute restricts the permission to API ≤ 28 and the test device runs API 33. Downstream assertions fail because the feature behaves as if the permission is denied, but no error was surfaced by the grant command. WHY: `PackageManagerService.grantRuntimePermission` short-circuits when `maxSdkVersion < Build.VERSION.SDK_INT`, treating the no-op as a non-error condition; `pm grant`'s process exit code is always 0 for this case. Fix: read the effective permission state with `pm get-permissions <package> | grep <permission>` via `mobile:shell` immediately after the grant, or use `mobile:changePermissions` with explicit `action: 'grant'` which validates the post-grant state and throws on failure.

**Gotcha 6 — WDIO `browser.mock()` intercepts do not fire for `fetch()` calls made inside a `SharedWorker` or `DedicatedWorker` thread in Android WebViews [community]**
`browser.mock()` installs a BiDi `network.addIntercept` at the browser session level, which covers the top-level page context and any same-origin iframes. Fetch calls issued inside `SharedWorker` or `DedicatedWorker` threads use a separate `WorkerFetchContext` that is not attached to the page's browsing context and therefore does not receive the BiDi intercept. The worker fetch completes at full speed against the real server, returning real data and masking the mock entirely. WHY: The W3C WebDriver BiDi `network.addIntercept` specification maps intercepts to a browsing context tree; worker threads run outside the browsing context tree in a dedicated worker realm that does not inherit the intercept registry. Fix: rewrite the worker to post a message to the main thread and have the main thread perform the fetch (interceptable by BiDi mocks), or use a service worker to intercept all fetch events including those from dedicated workers.

**Gotcha 7 — `mobile:configureLocalization` changes the Simulator locale but does not update `NSLocale.current` until the app process is restarted [community]**
After calling `mobile:configureLocalization`, the Simulator's locale preference is updated in `GlobalPreferences.plist`, but running app processes cache `NSLocale.current` at launch time and do not observe the preference change notification. UI elements that format dates, currencies, or numbers via `NSLocale.current` continue to display the old locale's formatting until the app is terminated and relaunched. WHY: `NSLocale.current` is a per-process singleton backed by a `CFRunLoop`-sourced preference observer; the observer fires `NSCurrentLocaleDidChangeNotification` only when the app is in the foreground and the OS posts the notification — but `mobile:configureLocalization` writes the pref directly without posting the notification to existing processes. Fix: always call `mobile:terminateApp` followed by `mobile:launchApp` after `mobile:configureLocalization` to ensure the new process reads the updated locale from scratch.

**Gotcha 8 — WDIO v9 `browser.emulate('geolocation')` requires `geolocation` permission to be granted in the WebView's content settings before the override takes effect [community]**
Calling `browser.emulate('geolocation', { latitude, longitude })` successfully installs the BiDi geolocation override, but if the WebView's `navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'geolocation' })` returns `'denied'` (either because the user denied it previously or the session capability `permissions: ['geolocation']` was not set), the `getCurrentPosition` callback receives a `PERMISSION_DENIED` error — the override is registered but never reached because the permission check short-circuits first. WHY: The `Geolocation API` permission check happens in the browser's `GeolocationController` before the mock override layer is consulted; the override is applied only after the permission gate passes. Fix: grant the geolocation permission via `browser.execute(() => navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'geolocation' }))` or set `'grantPermissions': ['geolocation']` in the WDIO `capabilities` block before calling `emulate`.

**New patterns added (Cycle 34 / 2026-05-14):**
1. Pattern 360 — `mobile:enrollBiometric` / `mobile:sendBiometricMatch` for iOS Face ID / Touch ID simulation
2. Pattern 361 — `mobile:siriCommand` for voice-activated feature testing on iOS

5. Pattern 364 — WDIO v9 `browser.emulate('clock')` for deterministic time-dependent UI tests
6. Pattern 365 — WDIO v9 `browser.url()` with `onBeforeLoad` for mobile WebView API stubbing
7. Pattern 366 — WDIO v9 `browser.mock()` with BiDi network interception for API response stubbing
8. Pattern 367 — UIAutomator2 `mobile:deepLink` for Android intent-based deep link testing
9. Pattern 368 — XCUITest `mobile:setAppearance` / `mobile:getAppearance` for dark-mode regression
10. Pattern 369 — `mobile:installCertificate` for per-test SSL certificate trust on iOS Simulator
11. Pattern 370 — UIAutomator2 `mobile:getContexts` for precise WebView context discovery
12. Pattern 371 — WDIO v9 `browser.mock()` request counter for API call frequency verification
13. Pattern 372 — XCUITest `mobile:clearKeychains` for isolated secure-storage state between tests
14. Pattern 373 — UIAutomator2 `mobile:shell` with `pm grant` for targeted Android permission grants
15. Pattern 374 — WDIO v9 `browser.emulate('geolocation')` for location-based feature testing

**New `[community]` gotchas this cycle: 8 dedicated gotchas with explicit WHY sentences**
- Isolated-world DOM invisibility in WebKit isFindInteractionEnabled (Gotcha 1)
- Fake clock hanging WDIO's `waitForDisplayed` internal polling (Gotcha 2)
- Android 12+ App Links silent drop due to DAL verification failure (Gotcha 3)
- `mobile:clearKeychains` no-op when Simulator `securityd` is zombie (Gotcha 4)
- `pm grant` silent no-op for `maxSdkVersion`-restricted permissions (Gotcha 5)
- BiDi network mock bypass for Worker thread fetch calls (Gotcha 6)
- `mobile:configureLocalization` not updating `NSLocale.current` in running app (Gotcha 7)

## Cycle 35 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 375 — `mobile:activeAppInfo` for runtime session diagnostics on iOS and Android [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:activeAppInfo` (XCUITest) and its UIAutomator2 equivalent `mobile:getCurrentActivity` return the foreground app's bundle ID, process ID, and activity name at runtime. This is invaluable in CI when a test fails because the wrong app (e.g. a system dialog, a Play Store update prompt) has taken focus. Wrapping the call in an `afterEach` diagnostic hook produces a precise "which app was foreground at failure time" breadcrumb in the test report without adding overhead to passing tests. On Android, `mobile:getCurrentActivity` returns the `.activityShortClassName` which can be matched against expected activity names from the app manifest.

```typescript
// test/helpers/activeAppDiagnostic.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface XCUITestActiveAppInfo {
  pid: number;
  bundleId: string;
  name: string;
}

interface UiAutomator2CurrentActivity {
  package: string;
  activity: string;
}

/**
 * Returns the foreground app identifier for diagnostic logging.
 * iOS: { pid, bundleId, name }
 * Android: { package, activity }
 */
export async function getActiveAppInfo(): Promise<XCUITestActiveAppInfo | UiAutomator2CurrentActivity> {
  if (browser.isIOS) {
    return await browser.execute('mobile: activeAppInfo') as XCUITestActiveAppInfo;
  }
  // Android UIAutomator2
  const pkg = await browser.execute('mobile: getCurrentPackage') as string;
  const act = await browser.execute('mobile: getCurrentActivity') as string;
  return { package: pkg, activity: act };
}

// wdio.conf.ts — afterEach diagnostic hook
export const config = {
  afterEach: async (_result: number, _capabilities: unknown, _specs: string[]) => {
    if (_result !== 0) {
      // Only log on failure to avoid bloating reports
      try {
        const info = await getActiveAppInfo();
        console.error('[DIAG] Active app at failure:', JSON.stringify(info));
      } catch {
        // Diagnostic failure must never mask the real test error
      }
    }
  },
};
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Debugging CI flakiness caused by unexpected foreground app changes (OS update dialogs, push notification banners stealing focus, crash reporters).
- **Do NOT use when**: Speed is paramount and tests are stable — the `mobile: activeAppInfo` call adds a ~50 ms round-trip on every `afterEach` even when wrapped in the failure guard.
- **Alternative**: Use `driver.getAppState(bundleId)` to check whether the expected app is still in `RUNNING_IN_FOREGROUND` state (state 4); this is faster and typed.

### Pattern 376 — WDIO v9 `browser.throttleNetwork()` for mobile network condition simulation [official]

**Description.**
WebDriverIO v9 exposes `browser.throttleNetwork()` as a thin wrapper over the Chrome DevTools Protocol `Network.emulateNetworkConditions` command, accessible in mobile WebView contexts where the embedded browser is Chromium-based (Android System WebView, Chrome Custom Tabs). Use it to validate app behavior on 3G, 2G, or offline conditions without changing the CI runner's network configuration. On iOS Safari WebView, BiDi network emulation via `browser.throttleNetwork()` is not yet supported (as of WKWebView/WebKit in iOS 17); use Network Link Conditioner via `xcrun simctl` for iOS instead. The method accepts named presets (`'Regular 3G'`, `'Slow 3G'`, `'offline'`) or a custom object with `downloadThroughput`, `uploadThroughput`, and `latency`.

```typescript
// test/helpers/networkThrottle.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

type NetworkPreset = 'Regular 3G' | 'Slow 3G' | 'offline' | 'No throttling';

interface CustomNetworkCondition {
  downloadThroughput: number; // bytes/s, -1 = unlimited
  uploadThroughput: number;   // bytes/s, -1 = unlimited
  latency: number;            // ms
  offline?: boolean;
}

/**
 * Apply network throttling inside a WebView context on Android Chromium.
 * MUST be called after switching to WebView context.
 */
export async function withNetworkCondition(
  condition: NetworkPreset | CustomNetworkCondition,
  test: () => Promise<void>,
): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) {
    console.warn('[throttle] throttleNetwork is Android Chromium WebView only; skipping on iOS');
    await test();
    return;
  }
  try {
    await browser.throttleNetwork(condition as Parameters<typeof browser.throttleNetwork>[0]);
    await test();
  } finally {
    // Always restore — leaving throttle active breaks subsequent tests
    await browser.throttleNetwork('No throttling');
  }
}

// test/specs/offline.spec.ts
it('shows offline banner on 2G connection', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');
  await withNetworkCondition('Slow 3G', async () => {
    await $('aria/Refresh').click();
    await expect($('aria/Slow connection detected')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
  });
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing WebView-rendered content under poor network conditions, validating loading skeletons, retry logic, or offline banners in hybrid apps.
- **Do NOT use when**: Testing native network calls (OkHttp, URLSession) — throttling only applies to the WebView's Chromium network stack, not to native HTTP clients running in the app process.
- **Alternative**: For native layer throttling on Android emulators, use `emulator -netspeed` and `emulator -netdelay` launch flags in `wdio.conf.ts`'s `onPrepare` hook via the `@wdio/appium-service` `args` option.

### Pattern 377 — `mobile:getClipboard` / `mobile:setClipboard` for OS-level pasteboard testing [official]

**Description.**
Clipboard testing in mobile automation is tricky because the system clipboard is sandboxed per app on iOS 16+ (UIPasteboard general pasteboard is read-restricted without user interaction). Appium's `mobile:getClipboard` bypasses the sandboxing via the XCUITest driver's privileged process access, returning base64-encoded clipboard content for `plaintext`, `image`, or `url` content types. On Android, UiAutomator2's `mobile:getClipboard` reads the primary clipboard directly. Use these commands to verify that "Copy to clipboard" buttons work end-to-end without needing a second app to paste into. Always decode the base64 result immediately; lingering encoded strings in test variables are the primary source of assertion errors on this API.

```typescript
// test/helpers/clipboardHelper.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

type ClipboardContentType = 'plaintext' | 'image' | 'url';

/**
 * Read the current clipboard contents decoded from base64.
 * @param contentType - Type of clipboard content to retrieve (default: 'plaintext')
 */
export async function readClipboard(contentType: ClipboardContentType = 'plaintext'): Promise<string> {
  const b64 = await browser.execute('mobile: getClipboard', {
    contentType,
  }) as string;
  // Appium returns base64-encoded content; decode to plain string
  return Buffer.from(b64, 'base64').toString('utf-8');
}

/**
 * Write text to the device clipboard (both platforms).
 */
export async function writeClipboard(text: string): Promise<void> {
  const b64 = Buffer.from(text, 'utf-8').toString('base64');
  await browser.execute('mobile: setClipboard', {
    content: b64,
    contentType: 'plaintext',
  });
}

// test/specs/shareSheet.spec.ts
it('should copy product URL to clipboard', async () => {
  await $('~share-btn').click();
  await $('~copy-link-option').click();

  const clipboardText = await readClipboard('plaintext');
  expect(clipboardText).toMatch(/^https:\/\/example\.com\/products\//);
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Validating "Copy link", "Copy code", or "Share via clipboard" features; testing paste-autofill OTP flows.
- **Do NOT use when**: iOS 16+ real devices are in the test matrix without additional entitlements — clipboard access requires privileged driver process access and UIPasteboard restrictions make reading impossible without user-triggered interaction on real devices.
- **Alternative**: Use `mobile:setPasteboard` (UIAutomator2 alias) on Android, or verify clipboard indirectly by tapping a paste target field and reading its value with `$el.getValue()`.

### Pattern 378 — WDIO v9 `browser.startRecordingScreen()` with per-test video evidence artifacts [official]

**Description.**
WebDriverIO v9 exposes `browser.startRecordingScreen()` / `browser.stopRecordingScreen()` as first-class methods wrapping Appium's `startRecordingScreen` / `stopRecordingScreen` execute commands. Coupling them with WDIO's `afterTest` hook creates per-test video artifacts that are saved only on failure, keeping storage costs low while maximising debugging value. Appium returns the video as a base64-encoded MP4 string; decode and write to disk inside the hook. On iOS, recording requires Simulator (not real device without additional entitlements); on Android, UIAutomator2's recorder captures the emulator via `screenrecord`. Set `timeLimit` to a safe ceiling (e.g. 180 seconds) so long-running tests don't silently drop frames.

```typescript
// test/helpers/screenRecorder.ts
import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

const ARTIFACT_DIR = join(process.cwd(), 'test-artifacts', 'videos');
mkdirSync(ARTIFACT_DIR, { recursive: true });

export async function startRecording(): Promise<void> {
  await browser.startRecordingScreen({
    timeLimit: 180,         // max seconds before auto-stop
    videoQuality: 'medium', // iOS: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'photo'
    videoFps: 10,           // lower fps = smaller files for CI
  });
}

export async function saveRecordingOnFailure(testTitle: string): Promise<void> {
  const b64 = await browser.stopRecordingScreen() as string;
  const safeName = testTitle.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_').slice(0, 80);
  const filePath = join(ARTIFACT_DIR, `${safeName}_${Date.now()}.mp4`);
  writeFileSync(filePath, Buffer.from(b64, 'base64'));
  console.log(`[video] Saved: ${filePath}`);
}

// wdio.conf.ts — attach to lifecycle hooks
export const config = {
  beforeTest: async () => { await startRecording(); },
  afterTest: async (
    test: { title: string },
    _context: unknown,
    { passed }: { passed: boolean },
  ) => {
    if (!passed) {
      await saveRecordingOnFailure(test.title);
    } else {
      // Discard recording on pass to avoid storing gigabytes of passing-test videos
      await browser.stopRecordingScreen();
    }
  },
};
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: High-value regression suites where gesture-based failures are hard to reproduce; CI environments where screenshots alone don't capture timing issues (animation-dependent interactions, scroll race conditions).
- **Do NOT use when**: Running 100+ short tests in parallel on emulators — concurrent `screenrecord` processes significantly increase CPU load and can destabilise emulators; use screenshot-on-failure instead.
- **Alternative**: For lightweight debugging, use `browser.takeScreenshot()` in `afterTest` — a single frame is sufficient for static UI assertion failures and has near-zero overhead.

### Pattern 379 — XCUITest `mobile:startLogCapture` / `mobile:stopLogCapture` for structured iOS syslog collection [official]

**Description.**
XCUITest driver 5+ provides `mobile:startLogCapture` and `mobile:stopLogCapture` as an in-session syslog capture mechanism that is more structured than `driver.getLogs('syslog')`. `startLogCapture` begins buffering log lines filtered by `processId`, `bundleId`, or `logLevel` into Appium's memory; `stopLogCapture` returns the buffered lines as a JSON array with `timestamp`, `pid`, `level`, and `message` fields. This structured format makes it feasible to assert on specific log entries in tests — for example, verifying that an analytics SDK emitted a specific event by checking its log output without needing a network proxy. The buffer resets on each `startLogCapture` call, so tests remain isolated.

```typescript
// test/helpers/iosLogCapture.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface SyslogEntry {
  timestamp: string;
  pid: number;
  level: 'debug' | 'info' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'fault';
  message: string;
}

interface StartLogCaptureOptions {
  bundleId?: string;
  pid?: number;
  logLevel?: SyslogEntry['level'];
}

export async function captureLogsAround<T>(
  options: StartLogCaptureOptions,
  action: () => Promise<T>,
): Promise<{ result: T; logs: SyslogEntry[] }> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: startLogCapture', options);
  let result: T;
  try {
    result = await action();
  } finally {
    // Always stop — an unclosed capture leaks memory in the Appium server process
    const raw = await browser.execute('mobile: stopLogCapture') as SyslogEntry[];
    return { result: result!, logs: raw };
  }
}

// test/specs/analytics.spec.ts
it('should emit add_to_cart analytics event on product tap', async () => {
  const { logs } = await captureLogsAround(
    { bundleId: 'com.example.app', logLevel: 'info' },
    async () => {
      await $('~product-card-42').click();
      await $('~add-to-cart-btn').click();
    },
  );
  const analyticsLog = logs.find((l) => l.message.includes('add_to_cart'));
  expect(analyticsLog).toBeDefined();
  expect(analyticsLog?.message).toContain('item_id=42');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Validating analytics event emission, crash reporter initialisation, or background task scheduling without instrumenting the app with test-only hooks.
- **Do NOT use when**: Sensitive PII might appear in logs — captured syslog lines are written to Allure/CTRF reports and may expose user data if not redacted.
- **Alternative**: Use a network proxy (`browser.mock()` in WebView, or a local mitmproxy for native) to intercept analytics HTTP calls directly rather than parsing log strings that are subject to formatting changes.

### Pattern 380 — UIAutomator2 `mobile:pressKey` with keycode map for Android hardware key simulation [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:pressKey` sends a single Android `KeyEvent` by keycode to the foreground window, simulating physical hardware key presses that `$el.setValue()` cannot produce — volume up/down, media controls, navigation keys (`KEYCODE_BACK`, `KEYCODE_HOME`), and function keys. UIAutomator2 driver 3+ exposes this as a first-class execute method with `keycode` (integer), `metastate` (modifier bitmask), and `flags` parameters matching the Android `KeyEvent` constructor. This replaces the deprecated `driver.pressKeyCode()` from Appium 1.x. The most common use case is simulating `KEYCODE_BACK` (keycode 4) in tests that must dismiss a system alert without using `driver.back()`, which is a WebDriver command that may behave differently on Android Go or older API levels.

```typescript
// test/helpers/androidKeys.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

/** Android KeyEvent keycodes (subset of android.view.KeyEvent) */
export const KeyCode = {
  BACK:             4,
  HOME:             3,
  VOLUME_UP:        24,
  VOLUME_DOWN:      25,
  CAMERA:           27,
  POWER:            26,
  MENU:             82,
  ENTER:            66,
  DEL:              67,  // Backspace
  TAB:              61,
  MEDIA_PLAY_PAUSE: 85,
  MEDIA_NEXT:       87,
  MEDIA_PREV:       88,
} as const;

/** MetaState bitmasks for modifier keys */
export const MetaState = {
  NONE:    0,
  SHIFT_ON: 1,
  ALT_ON:   2,
  CTRL_ON:  4096,
} as const;

export async function pressAndroidKey(
  keycode: number,
  metastate: number = MetaState.NONE,
): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) throw new Error('pressAndroidKey is Android-only');
  await browser.execute('mobile: pressKey', { keycode, metastate });
}

// Usage: dismiss a system dialog using hardware BACK key
it('should dismiss permission dialog via back key', async () => {
  await $('~request-permission-btn').click();
  await $('//android.widget.Button[@text="Don\'t allow"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await pressAndroidKey(KeyCode.BACK);
  // Dialog should be dismissed; app should remain on the same screen
  await expect($('~main-screen')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
});
```

**[community] `mobile:pressKey(BACK)` exits the app if the activity back stack is empty:** `driver.back()` is scoped to the WebDriver navigation model and respects WebView history — pressing back inside a WebView navigates to the previous web page rather than the previous native activity. `mobile:pressKey(BACK)` sends the raw OS-level `KEYCODE_BACK` event: if the current activity has no back stack entry (it is the root activity with `android:noHistory="true"` or the task root), the OS terminates the task and the session becomes orphaned. WHY: `KEYCODE_BACK` is a system key intercepted by the `Window.Callback` chain before WebDriver sees it; there is no WebDriver back-stack protection. Fix: use `driver.back()` for WebView navigation and `mobile:pressKey(BACK)` only when you explicitly intend to fire the OS back event.

---

### Pattern 381 — WDIO v9 `browser.getPuppeteer()` for advanced Chromium inspection in Android WebView [official]

**Description.**
In Android Chromium WebView contexts, WebDriverIO v9 exposes `browser.getPuppeteer()` which returns a Puppeteer `Browser` instance connected to the same DevTools Protocol session. This gives access to the full Puppeteer API — `page.coverage`, `page.tracing`, `page.metrics()`, and CDP methods not yet surfaced by WDIO itself. The method requires `automationProtocol: 'devtools'` or that the WebView context is already active and Chromium-based. Using `getPuppeteer()` does NOT create a second connection — it reuses the existing BiDi/CDP connection, so there is no port-conflict risk. This enables JavaScript code coverage collection, performance timeline tracing, and network waterfall analysis all within the same WDIO session.

```typescript
// test/helpers/puppeteerHelper.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import type { Page } from 'puppeteer-core';

/**
 * Collect JavaScript code coverage for a WebView action.
 * Requires Android Chromium WebView (not iOS Safari WKWebView).
 */
export async function withJsCoverage(
  action: () => Promise<void>,
): Promise<{ url: string; coverage: number }[]> {
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.example.app');

  const puppeteer = await browser.getPuppeteer();
  const pages = await puppeteer.pages();
  const page: Page = pages[0];

  await page.coverage.startJSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false });
  await action();
  const coverage = await page.coverage.stopJSCoverage();

  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');

  return coverage.map((entry) => ({
    url: entry.url,
    coverage: entry.ranges.reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.end - r.start, 0) / entry.text.length,
  }));
}

// test/specs/jsCoverage.spec.ts
it('checkout flow should exercise >80% of checkout.bundle.js', async () => {
  const results = await withJsCoverage(async () => {
    await $('~checkout-btn').click();
    await $('~confirm-order-btn').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
  });
  const checkoutBundle = results.find((r) => r.url.includes('checkout.bundle'));
  expect(checkoutBundle?.coverage).toBeGreaterThan(0.8);
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Measuring WebView JavaScript code coverage during E2E flows, collecting performance traces (`page.tracing`), or accessing CDP methods not yet in the WDIO API surface.
- **Do NOT use when**: iOS Safari is in scope — WKWebView does not expose a Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint; `getPuppeteer()` returns null or throws on iOS.
- **Alternative**: WDIO's `browser.cdp()` method allows raw CDP command invocation without the Puppeteer dependency if only one or two CDP commands are needed.

---

### Pattern 382 — Appium `appium:otherApps` capability for pre-installing test dependencies on session start [official]

**Description.**
The `appium:otherApps` capability accepts an array of app paths (`.apk` on Android, `.app`/`.ipa` on iOS) to install on the device before the main session app. This is the canonical way to pre-install companion apps (e.g. a mock backend app, a test harness helper app, or a linked SDK app) without separate `installApp()` calls scattered across `before()` hooks. Installation order follows the array order, and Appium skips re-installation if the app is already present at the same version (detected by version code on Android, `CFBundleVersion` on iOS). On Android with UiAutomator2 2.30+, `appium:otherApps` also accepts `gs://` Google Cloud Storage URIs and `http(s)://` URLs directly.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — pre-install a mock server app alongside the main app
const androidCapabilities: WebdriverIO.Capabilities = {
  platformName: 'Android',
  'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
  'appium:app': process.env.MAIN_APP_PATH!,
  'appium:otherApps': [
    process.env.MOCK_SERVER_APP_PATH!,        // local path
    'https://ci.example.com/test-helper.apk', // remote URL (UiAutomator2 2.30+)
  ],
  // Main app is installed AFTER all otherApps
  'appium:autoGrantPermissions': true,
};

// In tests: activate the mock server app to configure API stub responses
async function configureMockResponse(
  endpoint: string,
  statusCode: number,
): Promise<void> {
  const info = await browser.execute('mobile: activeAppInfo') as { bundleId: string };
  const mainBundle = info.bundleId;
  await browser.execute('mobile: activateApp', { appId: 'com.example.mockserver' });
  await $(`~endpoint-${endpoint.replace('/', '-')}`).setValue(statusCode.toString());
  await $('~save-config-btn').click();
  await browser.execute('mobile: activateApp', { appId: mainBundle });
}
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Integration test suites that require companion apps (helper apps, mock backends, side-loaded test fixtures) to be reliably installed before the session app.
- **Do NOT use when**: Companion apps need to be installed conditionally per test spec — use `driver.installApp()` in `before()` hooks instead for conditional installs.
- **Alternative**: TestContainers for HTTP mock servers that don't require a mobile app at all; `appium:prerun` scripts for installing via ADB shell commands.

---

### Pattern 383 — `mobile:backgroundApp` for app backgrounding lifecycle tests on iOS and Android [official]

**Description.**
`mobile:backgroundApp` suspends the app under test for a specified duration (in seconds) and then resumes it, simulating the user pressing the Home button and returning. It is the standard API for testing app-lifecycle events: `onPause`/`onResume` on Android, `applicationWillResignActive`/`applicationDidBecomeActive` on iOS. Passing `seconds: -1` backgrounds the app permanently without auto-resume, enabling manual resume via `mobile:activateApp`. Unlike the deprecated `driver.background()` Appium 1.x command, the `mobile:` prefix version is fully async-safe and respects the Appium 2 command queue, making it safe to use in parallel session configurations.

```typescript
// test/helpers/appLifecycle.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Background the app for a given duration, then wait for it to resume fully.
 * @param seconds        - Duration to keep app backgrounded. -1 = background indefinitely.
 * @param resumeTimeoutMs - After auto-resume, wait this long for app to stabilise.
 */
export async function backgroundApp(
  seconds: number,
  resumeTimeoutMs = 3_000,
): Promise<void> {
  const bundleId = (browser.capabilities as Record<string, unknown>)['appium:bundleId'] as string
    ?? (browser.capabilities as Record<string, unknown>)['appium:appPackage'] as string;

  await browser.execute('mobile: backgroundApp', { seconds });

  if (seconds >= 0 && bundleId) {
    await browser.waitUntil(
      async () => {
        const state = await browser.execute('mobile: queryAppState', { bundleId }) as number;
        return state === 4; // 4 = RUNNING_IN_FOREGROUND
      },
      {
        timeout: resumeTimeoutMs + seconds * 1_000,
        interval: 500,
        timeoutMsg: `App did not return to foreground within ${resumeTimeoutMs + seconds * 1_000}ms`,
      },
    );
  }
}

// test/specs/lifecycle.spec.ts
it('should restore cart state after app backgrounding', async () => {
  await $('~add-to-cart-btn').click();
  await expect($('~cart-badge')).toHaveText('1');

  await backgroundApp(5); // 5-second background

  // App should resume to the same screen with cart intact
  await expect($('~cart-badge')).toHaveText('1');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing auto-lock behaviour, push notification delivery while backgrounded, session timeout, background data sync, or state restoration after resume.
- **Do NOT use when**: Testing deep-background scenarios where iOS terminates the process (app backgrounded for extended periods triggering OS memory pressure kill); simulate this with `mobile:terminateApp` + `mobile:launchApp` instead.
- **Alternative**: `driver.background(seconds)` (Appium 1 alias, still works in Appium 2 but may be removed in Appium 3); prefer `mobile:backgroundApp` for forward compatibility.

---

### Pattern 384 — WDIO v9 `expect.extend()` for domain-specific mobile matchers [community]

**Description.**
WDIO v9's `expect` is powered by the Jest-compatible `expect` library and exposes `expect.extend()` for adding project-specific matchers. Mobile test suites benefit from matchers like `toBeAccessible()` (checks both `isDisplayed` and the element has a non-empty accessibility label), `toBeOnScreen()` (viewport intersection), and `toHaveValidDeepLink()`. Extending `expect` keeps test assertion lines concise and moves platform-specific logic (iOS `label` attribute vs Android `content-desc`) out of spec files into a single well-tested helper. Custom matcher error messages should include the element's accessibility ID and the assertion result so failures are actionable without opening Appium Inspector.

```typescript
// test/matchers/mobileMatcher.ts
import { expect as wdioExpect } from '@wdio/globals';

interface MatcherResult {
  pass: boolean;
  message: () => string;
}

wdioExpect.extend({
  async toBeAccessible(element: WebdriverIO.Element): Promise<MatcherResult> {
    const displayed = await element.isDisplayed();
    if (!displayed) {
      return {
        pass: false,
        message: () => 'Expected element to be accessible but it is not displayed',
      };
    }
    const label =
      await element.getAttribute('label')       // iOS XCUITest
      ?? await element.getAttribute('content-desc') // Android UiAutomator2
      ?? await element.getAttribute('aria-label');   // WebView

    const hasLabel = typeof label === 'string' && label.trim().length > 0;
    return {
      pass: hasLabel,
      message: () =>
        hasLabel
          ? `Expected element NOT to have accessibility label but found: "${label}"`
          : `Expected element to have non-empty accessibility label but got: "${String(label)}"`,
    };
  },

  async toBeOnScreen(element: WebdriverIO.Element): Promise<MatcherResult> {
    const rect    = await element.getRect();
    const winSize = await browser.getWindowSize();
    const onScreen = (
      rect.x + rect.width  > 0 &&
      rect.y + rect.height > 0 &&
      rect.x < winSize.width &&
      rect.y < winSize.height
    );
    return {
      pass: onScreen,
      message: () =>
        `Expected element rect ${JSON.stringify(rect)} to be ${onScreen ? 'off' : 'on'} screen ` +
        `(viewport: ${JSON.stringify(winSize)})`,
    };
  },
});

declare global {
  namespace ExpectWebdriverIO {
    interface Matchers<R, T> {
      toBeAccessible(): R;
      toBeOnScreen(): R;
    }
  }
}
```

**[community] `expect.extend()` matchers not available in worker scope without `require:` config entry:** WDIO globals (`browser`, `$`, `expect`) are injected into each worker process via the `@wdio/globals` package. Calling `expect.extend()` in a helper module and `import`-ing that module from the test spec file works inside that spec's worker. But if the extension is needed in ALL specs, placing the `import` in `wdio.conf.ts`'s `before` hook runs it in the ORCHESTRATOR process, not in each worker. WHY: each WDIO worker process is a separate Node.js VM with its own `expect` instance; the orchestrator's `expect.extend()` call does not propagate to workers. Fix: add the matcher module path to `wdio.conf.ts` `require: ['./test/matchers/mobileMatcher.js']` so every worker process imports it before running specs.

### Pattern 385 — Android `mobile:installMultipleApks` for split APK installation [community]

**Description.**
Modern Android apps distributed via the Play Store use split APKs (one base APK + feature/density/ABI splits). `adb install-multiple` is the shell command, but in Appium 2 / UiAutomator2 the equivalent is `mobile:installMultipleApks`, which accepts an array of local APK paths and installs them atomically in a single ADB session. Testing the exactly-what-ships-in-production artifact is important for catching issues where a feature split (e.g. a dynamic feature module) is missing in the test build. Generating the split APKs for test from a `.aab` requires `bundletool` with a device-spec JSON that matches the emulator's ABI and screen density; using the wrong device spec silently installs only the base APK.

```typescript
// test/config/splitApkInstaller.ts
import { execSync }   from 'node:child_process';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { browser }    from '@wdio/globals';

interface SplitApkInstallOptions {
  baseApkPath: string;
  splitApkPaths: string[];
  grantPermissions?: boolean;
}

export async function installSplitApks(opts: SplitApkInstallOptions): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) throw new Error('installSplitApks is Android-only');

  for (const p of [opts.baseApkPath, ...opts.splitApkPaths]) {
    if (!existsSync(p)) throw new Error(`APK not found: ${p}`);
  }

  await browser.execute('mobile: installMultipleApks', {
    apks: [opts.baseApkPath, ...opts.splitApkPaths], // base MUST be first
    options: {
      allowTestPackages: false,
      useSdcard: false,
      grantPermissions: opts.grantPermissions ?? true,
    },
  });
}

// wdio.conf.ts — generate splits from AAB using bundletool in CI onPrepare
export const config = {
  onPrepare: async () => {
    if (process.env.USE_SPLIT_APKS === 'true') {
      console.log('[setup] Extracting split APKs from AAB via bundletool...');
      execSync(
        'bundletool extract-apks --apks=app.apks --output-dir=/tmp/splits ' +
        '--device-spec=test/config/device-spec.json',
      );
    }
  },
};
```

**[community] `mobile:installMultipleApks` silently installs only the base APK when splits are passed in the wrong order:** The first entry in the `apks` array MUST be the base APK (the one containing the `AndroidManifest.xml` `<application>` element). If a feature split is listed first, UiAutomator2 logs a warning and installs only the base split to avoid a manifest conflict. WHY: `pm install-multiple` processes the first APK as the base package — feature splits require the base manifest to be present first to register the package before the split is associated with it. Fix: always ensure the base APK sorts first; a reliable heuristic is to sort alphabetically since `base.apk` precedes `config.*.apk` and `feature_*.apk` lexicographically.

### Pattern 386 — iOS `mobile:pushNotification` for local notification delivery testing on Simulator [official]

**Description.**
XCUITest driver 5.2+ provides `mobile:pushNotification` which delivers an APNs-format payload to the Simulator as if it were a real push notification, without requiring a push certificate or an Apple Developer account. The payload format matches the APNs JSON body (`aps.alert`, `aps.badge`, `aps.sound`, and custom data keys). This enables complete push notification test coverage: the notification appears in the notification centre, the badge updates, and tapping the notification deep-links into the app. The command only works on Simulator; real device push delivery for automated testing requires a separate push service (e.g. Firebase Test Lab's notification trigger API or APNs sandbox with a valid certificate).

```typescript
// test/helpers/pushNotificationHelper.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface ApnsPayload {
  aps: {
    alert?: { title: string; body: string; subtitle?: string };
    badge?: number;
    sound?: string;
    'content-available'?: 1;
    'mutable-content'?: 1;
    category?: string;
  };
  [key: string]: unknown; // custom data keys
}

/**
 * Deliver a simulated push notification to the iOS Simulator.
 * Requires XCUITest driver 5.2+ and iOS Simulator (not real device).
 */
export async function deliverPushNotification(
  bundleId: string,
  payload: ApnsPayload,
): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) throw new Error('mobile:pushNotification is iOS Simulator only');
  await browser.execute('mobile: pushNotification', { bundleId, payload });
}

// test/specs/push.spec.ts
it('should badge the app icon and deep-link on notification tap', async () => {
  // Background the app first — notifications arrive when app is not in foreground
  await browser.execute('mobile: backgroundApp', { seconds: -1 });

  await deliverPushNotification('com.example.app', {
    aps: {
      alert: { title: 'New Order', body: 'Your order #1234 has shipped' },
      badge: 1,
      sound: 'default',
    },
    orderId: '1234',
  });

  // Tap the notification from the notification centre
  await browser.execute('mobile: openNotification');
  await $('~order-detail-screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
  await expect($('~order-id-label')).toHaveText('#1234');
});
```

**Tradeoff.**
- **Use when**: Testing notification-triggered deep links, badge count updates, notification action buttons, and notification permission prompts on iOS Simulator.
- **Do NOT use when**: Real push delivery fidelity is required (e.g. testing APNs certificate expiry handling, production push environment routing, or notification content extensions that require provisioning profiles).
- **Alternative**: `xcrun simctl push <device-udid> <bundle-id> payload.json` from a shell step for one-off manual delivery; `mobile:pushNotification` is preferred for in-session programmatic delivery during test runs.
