### Pattern 423 — Appium `mobile: getClipboard` / `mobile: setClipboard` Round-Trip Test for Copy-to-Clipboard UI [official]

Many mobile apps expose "copy to clipboard" buttons for share codes, OTP seeds, wallet addresses, and referral links. Verifying that the correct value was written to the clipboard requires `driver.getClipboard()` (Android) or `mobile: getClipboard` execute script (iOS) after triggering the UI action. On iOS Simulator `driver.getClipboard()` returns the value set by `driver.setClipboard()` or by the app directly; on real iOS devices clipboard access requires the app to have clipboard permission granted. On Android, UiAutomator2 v3+ supports clipboard read without special permissions in the test process. Always restore clipboard state in `afterEach` to avoid cross-test pollution where the next test's paste action inserts the previous test's data.

```typescript
// test/helpers/clipboardHelper.ts
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Read current clipboard text — cross-platform.
 * Returns empty string if clipboard is empty or inaccessible.
 */
export async function readClipboard(): Promise<string> {
  if (browser.isIOS) {
    const result = await driver.execute('mobile: getClipboard', { contentType: 'plaintext' }) as string;
    return result ?? '';
  }
  // Android — UiAutomator2 native clipboard read
  return await driver.getClipboard('plaintext') as string;
}

/**
 * Write text to clipboard — cross-platform.
 */
export async function writeClipboard(text: string): Promise<void> {
  if (browser.isIOS) {
    await driver.execute('mobile: setClipboard', { content: btoa(text), contentType: 'plaintext' });
  } else {
    await driver.setClipboard(Buffer.from(text).toString('base64'), 'plaintext');
  }
}

/**
 * Wraps a test action; restores clipboard to its original value after.
 */
export async function withRestoredClipboard<T>(action: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  const original = await readClipboard();
  try {
    return await action();
  } finally {
    if (original) await writeClipboard(original);
  }
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/share-code.spec.ts
import { readClipboard, withRestoredClipboard } from '../helpers/clipboardHelper.js';

it('should copy referral code to clipboard', async () => {
  await withRestoredClipboard(async () => {
    const referralCode = await $('[data-testid="referral-code-text"]').getText();
    await $('[data-testid="copy-referral-btn"]').click();
    const clipped = await readClipboard();
    expect(clipped).toBe(referralCode);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** On iOS real devices, clipboard reading via Appium triggers the system privacy banner ("App pasted from X") starting in iOS 16. This banner can obscure UI elements in subsequent screenshots and disrupt screenshot assertions. Suppress it in test builds by adding the `NSClipboardUsageDescription` key to Info.plist and requesting clipboard permission explicitly before your tests. The iOS 16+ clipboard banner cannot be suppressed via Appium capabilities. [official]

---

### Pattern 424 — WDIO v9 Visual Testing `checkScreen()` with Mobile Exclusion Zones for Dynamic Content [community]

`@wdio/visual-service` `checkScreen()` fails noisily on dynamic content — timestamps, user avatars, real-time counters, and map tiles change per run. Use the `blockOut` option to exclude rectangular regions from pixel comparison, and `ignoreColors` together with a custom `saveAboveTolerance` threshold to suppress antialiasing noise on retina displays. Pair each call with a unique `tag` that encodes the device model and OS version so baselines are segregated by device form factor. Without device-segregated baselines, an iPhone 15 Pro baseline will always fail on an iPhone SE run because font metrics and pixel density differ.

```typescript
// test/specs/visual/dashboard.visual.spec.ts
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const DEVICE_TAG = `${process.env.DEVICE_MODEL ?? 'unknown'}_${process.env.PLATFORM_VERSION ?? 'x'}`;

describe('Dashboard visual regression', () => {
  it('should match dashboard layout baseline', async () => {
    await browser.url('https://app.example.com/dashboard');
    // Wait for skeleton loaders to resolve before capture
    await $('[data-testid="dashboard-content"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });

    await browser.checkScreen(`dashboard_${DEVICE_TAG}`, {
      // Block out the real-time trade price ticker (top-right)
      blockOut: [{ x: 300, y: 60, width: 75, height: 24 }],
      // Allow 2% pixel deviation for antialiasing on retina screens
      saveAboveTolerance: 2,
      // Ignore the status bar (carrier name, battery, time)
      blockOutStatusBar: true,
      // Ignore the navigation bar (Android back/home/overview buttons)
      blockOutToolBar: true,
    });
  });

  it('should match product card element baseline', async () => {
    const card = $('[data-testid="product-card-0"]');
    await card.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    // Element snapshot — immune to page scroll position
    await browser.checkElement(card, `product_card_${DEVICE_TAG}`, {
      saveAboveTolerance: 3,
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `blockOut` coordinates are screen-pixel coordinates, not element-relative coordinates, so they shift when the layout changes or the device orientation changes. Prefer element-level `checkElement()` snapshots for components you care about instead of full-screen `checkScreen()` with large blockOut arrays. When `saveAboveTolerance` is set too high (>5%) genuine visual regressions can slip through. Use `0` tolerance on static brand assets (logos, icons) and higher tolerance only on text-heavy regions where font rendering varies across OS versions. [community]

---

### Pattern 425 — Appium `mobile: shell` with `input keyevent` for Android Hardware Key Simulation [official]

Android's `input keyevent` command (dispatched via `mobile: shell` in Appium) sends hardware key events that bypass the soft keyboard. This is the correct way to test Back button behaviour, volume keys, media controls, and camera shutter in automated tests. Soft keyboards rendered by the app or by the OS may not receive key events dispatched via `driver.keys()` if the UI element is not focused, but `input keyevent` dispatches at the Android InputManager level and works regardless of focus state. Key codes follow the `android.view.KeyEvent` integer constants.

```typescript
// test/helpers/androidKeyHelper.ts
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';

// Common Android KeyEvent constants
export const AndroidKey = {
  BACK:          4,
  HOME:          3,
  MENU:         82,
  VOLUME_UP:    24,
  VOLUME_DOWN:  25,
  CAMERA:       27,
  ENTER:        66,
  DELETE:       67,   // Backspace
  DPAD_UP:      19,
  DPAD_DOWN:    20,
  DPAD_LEFT:    21,
  DPAD_RIGHT:   22,
  DPAD_CENTER:  23,
} as const;

/**
 * Press an Android hardware key by KeyEvent code.
 * Works on both emulator and real device.
 */
export async function pressAndroidKey(keyCode: number): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) throw new Error('pressAndroidKey is Android-only');
  await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'input',
    args: ['keyevent', String(keyCode)],
  });
}

/**
 * Press Back and verify the expected screen is shown.
 */
export async function pressBackExpecting(expectedSelector: string): Promise<void> {
  await pressAndroidKey(AndroidKey.BACK);
  await $(expectedSelector).waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/back-navigation.spec.ts
import { pressAndroidKey, pressBackExpecting, AndroidKey } from '../helpers/androidKeyHelper.js';

it('should navigate back from product detail to product list', async () => {
  await $('~product-item-0').click();
  await $('~product-detail-screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

  await pressBackExpecting('~product-list-screen');
  await expect($('~product-list-screen')).toBeDisplayed();
});

it('should dismiss keyboard with Back key', async () => {
  await $('~search-input').click();
  await expect(driver).toHaveKeyboardShown();
  await pressAndroidKey(AndroidKey.BACK);
  await expect(driver).not.toHaveKeyboardShown();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `input keyevent` fires at the system level and cannot be intercepted by `onBackPressedDispatcher` overrides in fragment-based navigation in the same way as hardware button presses on physical devices. In some React Navigation and Jetpack Compose Navigation configurations, `input keyevent 4` (BACK) triggers the OS activity stack pop rather than the in-app back handler. Test both paths: verify that the in-app navigation state (NavController backstack) matches expectations and not just the displayed element. [official]

---

### Pattern 426 — XCUITest `mobile: swipe` with `velocity` Parameter for Momentum-Sensitive iOS Scroll Tests [official]

XCUITest driver exposes `mobile: swipe` with a `velocity` parameter (points/second) that controls how fast the swipe gesture registers in the iOS engine. Low-velocity swipes land on `UIScrollView` as slow drags (useful for date pickers and carousels where the cell should not overshoot the target), while high-velocity swipes trigger momentum scrolling (fling). Using WDIO's `browser.swipe()` default velocity triggers momentum on most scroll views, causing the list to coast past the target element. Setting `velocity: 200` (slow drag) is the correct value for date picker column scroll tests where you want to land on a specific value.

```typescript
// test/helpers/iosSwipeHelper.ts
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface SwipeOptions {
  direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right';
  /** Velocity in points/sec. Default iOS ~1000 (momentum). Use ~200 for slow drag. */
  velocity?: number;
  element?: WebdriverIO.Element;
}

/**
 * Perform an iOS swipe with explicit velocity control.
 * Use low velocity (100-300) for date pickers and precision carousels.
 * Use high velocity (800-1500) for full-screen list fling testing.
 */
export async function iosSwipe(opts: SwipeOptions): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) throw new Error('iosSwipe is iOS-only');
  await driver.execute('mobile: swipe', {
    direction: opts.direction,
    velocity: opts.velocity ?? 1000,
    ...(opts.element ? { elementId: await opts.element.elementId } : {}),
  });
}

/**
 * Scroll a date picker column to a target value using slow swipes.
 * Retries up to maxSwipes times checking the accessibility label after each swipe.
 */
export async function scrollDatePickerColumn(
  columnAccessibilityId: string,
  targetValue: string,
  direction: 'up' | 'down' = 'up',
  maxSwipes = 10,
): Promise<void> {
  const column = $(`~${columnAccessibilityId}`);
  for (let i = 0; i < maxSwipes; i++) {
    const current = await column.getAttribute('value');
    if (current === targetValue) return;
    await iosSwipe({ direction, velocity: 200, element: column });
    await browser.pause(150); // allow snap animation to settle
  }
  throw new Error(`Could not reach "${targetValue}" in column "${columnAccessibilityId}" after ${maxSwipes} swipes`);
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/date-picker.spec.ts
import { scrollDatePickerColumn } from '../helpers/iosSwipeHelper.js';

it('should select January 15, 2027 in the date picker', async () => {
  await $('~open-date-picker-btn').click();
  await $('~date-picker').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });

  await scrollDatePickerColumn('month-column', 'January', 'down');
  await scrollDatePickerColumn('day-column',   '15',      'up');
  await scrollDatePickerColumn('year-column',  '2027',    'up');

  await $('~confirm-date-btn').click();
  await expect($('~selected-date-label')).toHaveText('January 15, 2027');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `velocity` is XCUITest-specific and has no equivalent in UiAutomator2. On Android, scroll velocity is controlled indirectly via the `speed` parameter in `mobile: scrollGesture` (pixels/second). Date picker testing on Android is further complicated by Material date pickers rendering as calendar grids rather than scroll columns, requiring a completely different interaction strategy (tap on day cell). Abstract the date-picker interaction behind a platform-agnostic helper that delegates to the correct strategy per `browser.isIOS`. [official]

---

### Pattern 427 — WDIO v9 `browser.mock().respond()` for Deterministic API Fixtures in Hybrid App Tests [community]

`browser.mock()` with `.respond()` replaces a real HTTP response with a fixture payload, enabling deterministic test states without modifying the backend or injecting feature flags. In Capacitor/Ionic hybrid apps all API calls pass through the WebView's Fetch/XHR stack and are interceptable by the CDP mock layer. Use `respondOnce()` to inject an error state for the first request and then allow subsequent retries to succeed — testing the app's retry UX without a flaky network. The mock object accumulates all matched requests in `mock.calls`, which can be asserted post-action to verify the app issued the expected API shape (URL, method, body).

```typescript
// test/helpers/apiMockHelper.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

/** Inject a fixture response for every matching request until restore() is called. */
export async function mockApiEndpoint<T>(
  urlPattern: string,
  fixture: T,
  statusCode = 200,
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Mock> {
  const mock = await browser.mock(urlPattern, { method: 'GET' });
  mock.respond(fixture, { statusCode, fetchResponse: false });
  return mock;
}

/** Inject an error on the first request, then allow real responses through. */
export async function mockApiErrorOnce(urlPattern: string, statusCode: 500 | 429 | 503): Promise<WebdriverIO.Mock> {
  const mock = await browser.mock(urlPattern);
  mock.respondOnce({ error: 'simulated server error' }, { statusCode, fetchResponse: false });
  return mock;
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/product-list.spec.ts
import { mockApiEndpoint, mockApiErrorOnce } from '../helpers/apiMockHelper.js';

describe('Product list API states', () => {
  afterEach(async () => {
    // Restore all mocks to avoid cross-test pollution
    const mocks = await browser.getMocks();
    for (const m of mocks) await m.restore();
  });

  it('should show empty state when API returns empty products array', async () => {
    await mockApiEndpoint('**/api/products', { items: [], total: 0 });
    await browser.url('https://app.example.com/products');
    await expect($('[data-testid="empty-products-message"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('should show retry toast on 500 then succeed', async () => {
    const mock = await mockApiErrorOnce('**/api/products', 500);
    await browser.url('https://app.example.com/products');
    await expect($('[data-testid="retry-toast"]')).toBeDisplayed();
    // After one failure mock is exhausted — real request succeeds
    await $('[data-testid="retry-btn"]').click();
    await expect($('[data-testid="product-card"]')).toBeDisplayed();
    // Confirm the mock was hit exactly once
    expect(mock.calls).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.mock()` requires Chrome DevTools Protocol and therefore only works in local Chromium contexts and Selenium Grid v4+ with CDP support. It cannot be used with BrowserStack, Sauce Labs, or other cloud grids. For cloud environments, inject fixture state via app-level feature flags, a dedicated mock server (e.g. `msw` running inside the WebView), or Appium's `mobile: shell` to swap a bundled local JSON fixture. The `mock.calls` accumulation grows unboundedly during a session — call `mock.clear()` between test cases to keep assertion cardinality meaningful. [community]

---

### Pattern 428 — Appium `mobile: activateApp` + `xcrun simctl openurl` for iOS Universal Links Deep-Link Verification [community]

iOS Universal Links open the app via a native URL scheme dispatched by the iOS link-resolution system. Testing them from an Appium session requires navigating Safari to the Universal Link URL, which triggers the iOS system prompt "Open in App?", accepting it, and then verifying the app landed on the correct in-app screen. An alternative and more reliable technique for CI is to use `xcrun simctl openurl`, which iOS supports on Simulator and bypasses the OS confirmation dialog. Combining deep-link navigation with `driver.getClipboard()` lets you assert the share sheet URL that the app writes to the clipboard when the user taps "Share".

```typescript
// test/helpers/deepLinkHelper.ts
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

/**
 * Open a Universal Link on iOS Simulator by invoking xcrun simctl openurl.
 * More reliable than navigating Safari — bypasses the OS confirmation dialog.
 */
export async function openUniversalLink(url: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) throw new Error('openUniversalLink is iOS-only');
  // Obtain the booted simulator UDID
  const simctlOutput = execSync('xcrun simctl list devices booted --json').toString();
  const { devices } = JSON.parse(simctlOutput) as {
    devices: Record<string, Array<{ udid: string; state: string }>>;
  };
  let udid: string | undefined;
  for (const runtimeDevices of Object.values(devices)) {
    const booted = runtimeDevices.find(d => d.state === 'Booted');
    if (booted) { udid = booted.udid; break; }
  }
  if (!udid) throw new Error('No booted iOS Simulator found');
  // Shell-escape the URL to handle & in query strings
  const safeUrl = url.replace(/&/g, '\\&');
  execSync(`xcrun simctl openurl "${udid}" "${safeUrl}"`);
  // Allow the app to foreground and render the target screen
  await browser.pause(1500);
}

/**
 * Assert a Universal Link navigates to the expected in-app screen.
 */
export async function assertDeepLinkLandsOn(
  url: string,
  expectedScreenAccessibilityId: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await openUniversalLink(url);
  await $(`~${expectedScreenAccessibilityId}`).waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
  await expect($(`~${expectedScreenAccessibilityId}`)).toBeDisplayed();
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/deep-links.spec.ts
import { assertDeepLinkLandsOn } from '../helpers/deepLinkHelper.js';

it('should open product detail via universal link', async () => {
  await assertDeepLinkLandsOn(
    'https://shop.example.com/products/42',
    'product-detail-screen',
  );
  await expect($('~product-id-label')).toHaveText('42');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `xcrun simctl openurl` works exclusively on iOS Simulator (not real device) and requires macOS with Xcode installed. On real devices, use `driver.execute('mobile: deepLink', { url, bundleId })` instead — this uses the XCUITest driver's `open` command which bypasses the system browser prompt. On Android, `browser.deepLink(url, packageName)` (WDIO v9.10+) wraps `adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d <url> <package>`. [community]

---

### Pattern 429 — WDIO v9 `browser.scriptAddPreloadScript()` BiDi API for Injecting Test Utilities into Every WebView Page [official]

The WebDriver BiDi `scriptAddPreloadScript` command registers a JavaScript function that executes before any page script on every navigation within the current browsing context. This replaces fragile `driver.execute(injectScript)` calls that race with page load timing. In mobile WebView testing, preload scripts are useful for exposing a `window.__testBus` event bus that your tests can listen to via `browser.waitUntil()`, for stubbing `window.analytics` to prevent real tracking during tests, and for injecting a deterministic random seed for apps that use `Math.random()` in UI layout logic (e.g. shuffle order of product cards).

```typescript
// test/helpers/preloadScriptHelper.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Inject a preload script that stubs window.analytics to capture events.
 * Returns the script ID (use with removePreloadScript to clean up).
 */
export async function injectAnalyticsStub(): Promise<string> {
  const { script: scriptId } = await browser.scriptAddPreloadScript({
    functionDeclaration: `() => {
      window.__analyticsEvents = [];
      window.analytics = {
        track:    (event, props) => {
          window.__analyticsEvents.push({ event, props, ts: Date.now() });
        },
        identify: () => {},
        page:     () => {},
      };
    }`,
  });
  return scriptId;
}

/**
 * Read the analytics events captured since the last page load.
 */
export async function getTrackedEvents(): Promise<Array<{ event: string; props: unknown }>> {
  return await browser.execute(() => (window as Window & { __analyticsEvents?: Array<{ event: string; props: unknown }> }).__analyticsEvents ?? []);
}

/**
 * Remove the preload script to stop injection on subsequent navigations.
 */
export async function removePreloadScript(scriptId: string): Promise<void> {
  await browser.scriptRemovePreloadScript({ script: scriptId });
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/analytics.spec.ts
import { injectAnalyticsStub, getTrackedEvents, removePreloadScript } from '../helpers/preloadScriptHelper.js';

describe('Analytics event tracking', () => {
  let scriptId: string;

  before(async () => { scriptId = await injectAnalyticsStub(); });
  after(async ()  => { await removePreloadScript(scriptId); });

  it('should track add_to_cart event on product tap', async () => {
    await browser.url('https://app.example.com/products');
    await $('~add-to-cart-btn').click();
    const events = await getTrackedEvents();
    expect(events.some(e => e.event === 'add_to_cart')).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `scriptAddPreloadScript` requires WebDriver BiDi (`webSocketUrl: true`) and Chromium 115+ inside the WebView. The preload script is bound to the browsing context created at session start; if the app opens a new WebView window (e.g. via `window.open()`), the new context does not inherit the preload script unless you register it per-context. BiDi scripting commands are not supported in cloud grids that proxy CDP but do not forward BiDi websocket connections — check your grid provider's BiDi support matrix before relying on this pattern. [official]

---

### Pattern 430 — Appium UIAutomator2 `mobile: dragGesture` for Android Drag-and-Drop with Intermediate Points [official]

`mobile: dragGesture` in UIAutomator2 sends a drag gesture using Android's `UiDevice.drag()` under the hood, which accurately simulates a long-press-then-drag sequence. Unlike `W3C Actions` pointer chains, `mobile: dragGesture` accepts `startX/Y`, `endX/Y`, `speed` (pixels/second), and an optional `elementId` for element-relative coordinates. For list reordering, kanban board rearrangement, and resizable panel tests, provide an `elementId` so coordinates are relative to the element's bounding box rather than the screen — making the test resolution-independent. The `speed` parameter (default 2500 px/s) controls how the Android motion event timeline is constructed; slower speeds (800-1200 px/s) are more reliable on dense RecyclerViews where fast drags can over-scroll.

```typescript
// test/helpers/androidDragHelper.ts
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface DragOptions {
  startElement?: WebdriverIO.Element;
  endElement?: WebdriverIO.Element;
  startX: number;
  startY: number;
  endX: number;
  endY: number;
  /** Drag speed in pixels/second. Default: 2500. Use 1000 for dense lists. */
  speed?: number;
}

/**
 * Perform a drag gesture on Android using UIAutomator2's native drag.
 */
export async function androidDrag(opts: DragOptions): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) throw new Error('androidDrag is Android-only');

  const args: Record<string, unknown> = {
    startX: opts.startX,
    startY: opts.startY,
    endX:   opts.endX,
    endY:   opts.endY,
    speed:  opts.speed ?? 2500,
  };

  if (opts.startElement) {
    args.elementId = await opts.startElement.elementId;
  }

  await driver.execute('mobile: dragGesture', args);
}

/**
 * Reorder a list item by dragging it to the position of another item.
 * Grabs drag handles by accessibility ID.
 */
export async function reorderListItem(
  fromHandleId: string,
  toHandleId: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const fromHandle = $(`~${fromHandleId}`);
  const toHandle   = $(`~${toHandleId}`);

  const [fromLoc, toLoc] = await Promise.all([
    fromHandle.getLocation(),
    toHandle.getLocation(),
  ]);

  await androidDrag({
    startX: fromLoc.x + 20,
    startY: fromLoc.y + 20,
    endX:   toLoc.x + 20,
    endY:   toLoc.y + 20,
    speed:  1000,
  });
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/list-reorder.spec.ts
import { reorderListItem } from '../helpers/androidDragHelper.js';

it('should reorder tasks by dragging', async () => {
  const tasksBefore = await $$('~task-item').map(el => el.getText());
  await reorderListItem('task-drag-handle-0', 'task-drag-handle-2');
  const tasksAfter  = await $$('~task-item').map(el => el.getText());
  expect(tasksAfter[2]).toBe(tasksBefore[0]);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: dragGesture` works correctly only when the target view is not inside a `NestedScrollView` or has scroll interception disabled. WHY: Android dispatches drag motions through the view hierarchy's `onInterceptTouchEvent`; a parent scroll view can intercept the long-press and convert it to a scroll gesture, silently ignoring the drag. Fix: disable scroll interception on the parent (`canScrollVertically(1) = false`) in debug builds, or use `mobile: longClickGesture` followed by a separate `mobile: swipeGesture` to simulate the drag in two steps. [official]

---

### Pattern 431 — WDIO v9 `browser.isStable()` for Animation-Aware Element Readiness in Complex Transitions [official]

`browser.isStable(element)` (WDIO v9.18+) returns `true` only when the element has no ongoing CSS animations or layout reflows. Using `waitForDisplayed()` alone on an element that animates into view can produce click interactions that land before the animation completes — causing the element to receive a tap at its mid-animation position rather than its resting position. `isStable()` polls element bounding box and CSS `animationPlayState` until the element stops moving for two consecutive frames. Call it via `browser.waitUntil(() => browser.isStable(el))` after `waitForDisplayed()` for any element reachable via a transition animation.

```typescript
// test/helpers/animationHelper.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Wait until element is displayed AND has finished all CSS animations/transitions.
 * Prevents clicks on mid-animation elements (e.g. slide-in drawers, scale-in modals).
 */
export async function waitForStable(
  element: WebdriverIO.Element,
  timeout = 8_000,
): Promise<void> {
  await element.waitForDisplayed({ timeout });
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => browser.isStable(element),
    {
      timeout,
      interval: 100,
      timeoutMsg: `Element ${element.selector} did not stabilise within ${timeout}ms`,
    },
  );
}

/**
 * Wait for stable, then click.
 * Drops the race condition between animation completion and user interaction.
 */
export async function stableClick(element: WebdriverIO.Element): Promise<void> {
  await waitForStable(element);
  await element.click();
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/modal-flow.spec.ts
import { stableClick, waitForStable } from '../helpers/animationHelper.js';

it('should tap confirm button in slide-up modal', async () => {
  await $('~open-modal-btn').click();
  const confirmBtn = $('~modal-confirm-btn');
  // Modal slides up with a 300ms animation — stable click prevents mid-animation tap
  await stableClick(confirmBtn);
  await expect($('~modal-overlay')).not.toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.isStable()` polls via JavaScript `requestAnimationFrame` pairs, which requires a live rendering context. In headless WebView tests where the rendering thread may be throttled, `isStable()` can return `true` prematurely before the GPU commit finishes. On real devices this is rarely an issue; on CI emulators with GPU acceleration disabled (`-gpu swiftshader_indirect`), add a `browser.pause(50)` after `isStable()` returns `true` as a one-frame safety buffer. The API does not detect native layer animations (UIView animations, ObjectAnimator) — for native animations use `mobile: waitForAnimations` (XCUITest) or explicit `waitForExist` on the expected post-animation element state. [official]

---

### Pattern 432 — Appium `mobile: getNetworkSpeed` / `mobile: setNetworkSpeed` for Android Emulator Radio Type Simulation [official]

UIAutomator2 exposes `mobile: getNetworkSpeed` (read current network type: `none`, `gsm`, `edge`, `hscsd`, `gprs`, `umts`, `hsdpa`, `lte`, `full`) and `mobile: setNetworkSpeed` for Android emulators, controlling the emulator's radio emulation. Unlike `driver.setNetworkConnection()` (which toggles Wi-Fi/data/airplane bitmask), network speed simulation changes the actual radio type reported by `TelephonyManager.getNetworkType()`, enabling tests for apps that render different UI based on connection quality (e.g. a "You're on 2G — enable data saver?" banner). This command is supported only on Android Emulator AVDs — not on real physical devices.

```typescript
// test/helpers/androidEmulatorNetworkHelper.ts
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export type AndroidNetworkSpeed =
  | 'none' | 'gsm' | 'edge' | 'hscsd' | 'gprs'
  | 'umts' | 'hsdpa' | 'lte' | 'full';

/**
 * Set Android emulator radio type.
 * WARNING: Emulator only — throws on real device.
 */
export async function setEmulatorNetworkSpeed(speed: AndroidNetworkSpeed): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) throw new Error('Android-only');
  await driver.execute('mobile: setNetworkSpeed', { speed });
}

/**
 * Read the current Android emulator network speed label.
 */
export async function getEmulatorNetworkSpeed(): Promise<AndroidNetworkSpeed> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) throw new Error('Android-only');
  return await driver.execute('mobile: getNetworkSpeed') as AndroidNetworkSpeed;
}

/**
 * Wraps a test block with a specific network speed; always restores 'full' after.
 */
export async function withEmulatorNetworkSpeed<T>(
  speed: AndroidNetworkSpeed,
  action: () => Promise<T>,
): Promise<T> {
  const original = await getEmulatorNetworkSpeed();
  await setEmulatorNetworkSpeed(speed);
  try {
    return await action();
  } finally {
    await setEmulatorNetworkSpeed(original as AndroidNetworkSpeed);
  }
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/data-saver-banner.spec.ts
import { withEmulatorNetworkSpeed } from '../helpers/androidEmulatorNetworkHelper.js';

it('should show data-saver prompt on EDGE connection', async () => {
  await withEmulatorNetworkSpeed('edge', async () => {
    await driver.execute('mobile: activateApp', { appId: 'com.example.app' });
    await $('~data-saver-banner').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await expect($('~data-saver-banner')).toHaveText(/You.*2G.*data saver/i);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: setNetworkSpeed` changes the radio type enum but does not throttle actual TCP throughput or add latency to emulator traffic. For throughput throttling use `browser.throttleNetwork()` in a WebView context or Android's `tc` command via `mobile: shell`. WHY: The radio type enumeration is a metadata signal from `TelephonyManager`; the emulator kernel still routes packets at full loopback speed. Apps that read `NetworkCapabilities.getLinkDownstreamBandwidthKbps()` or do real-world performance profiling will not see a throttled connection — only apps that check the network type enum (NETWORK_TYPE_EDGE etc.) will behave differently. [official]

---

### Pattern 433 — WDIO v9 `@wdio/shared-store-service` for Cross-Worker Device Lease Management in Parallel iOS Simulator Tests [community]

When running `maxInstances > 1` with Appium on a Mac CI runner with multiple iOS Simulators, each WDIO worker must know which `UDID` to claim to avoid two workers targeting the same Simulator. `@wdio/shared-store-service` provides a key-value store accessible from all workers and from `onPrepare`/`onComplete` hooks in the config. Use it to implement a device-lease pattern: `onPrepare` writes the list of available UDIDs, each worker atomically claims a UDID on `beforeSession`, and releases it on `afterSession`. This avoids the session collision error `Session already exists on device`.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — shared-store device lease (relevant excerpts)
import type { Options } from '@wdio/types';
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

function getBootedSimulatorUdids(): string[] {
  const raw  = execSync('xcrun simctl list devices booted --json').toString();
  const data = JSON.parse(raw) as {
    devices: Record<string, Array<{ udid: string; state: string }>>;
  };
  return Object.values(data.devices).flat()
    .filter(d => d.state === 'Booted')
    .map(d => d.udid);
}

export const config: Options.Testrunner = {
  maxInstances: 3,
  services: [['shared-store', {}]],

  onPrepare: async (_config, _caps, store) => {
    const s = store as { setValue: (k: string, v: unknown) => Promise<void> };
    await s.setValue('available_udids', getBootedSimulatorUdids());
    await s.setValue('leased_udids', []);
  },

  beforeSession: async (_config, caps, _specs, _cid, store) => {
    const s = store as {
      getValue: (k: string) => Promise<unknown>;
      setValue: (k: string, v: unknown) => Promise<void>;
    };
    let claimed: string | undefined;
    await browser.waitUntil(async () => {
      const available = await s.getValue('available_udids') as string[];
      const leased    = await s.getValue('leased_udids')    as string[];
      const free      = available.filter(u => !leased.includes(u));
      if (free.length === 0) return false;
      claimed = free[0];
      await s.setValue('leased_udids', [...leased, claimed]);
      return true;
    }, { timeout: 60_000, interval: 500 });
    (caps as Record<string, unknown>)['appium:udid'] = claimed;
  },

  afterSession: async (_config, caps, _specs, _cid, store) => {
    const s     = store as { getValue: (k: string) => Promise<unknown>; setValue: (k: string, v: unknown) => Promise<void> };
    const udid  = (caps as Record<string, unknown>)['appium:udid'] as string;
    const leased = await s.getValue('leased_udids') as string[];
    await s.setValue('leased_udids', leased.filter(u => u !== udid));
  },
};
```

**Tradeoff:** The `waitUntil` spin-wait in `beforeSession` can stall indefinitely if the number of test workers exceeds the number of available UDIDs AND a worker crashes without releasing its lease in `afterSession`. Add a lease timeout: store a `{ udid, leasedAt }` object instead of a bare string, and in `beforeSession` reclaim UDIDs whose `leasedAt` is older than the test timeout threshold. WHY: WDIO's `afterSession` hook is only guaranteed to run on clean exit; an Appium driver crash can leave a worker terminated without running `afterSession`, permanently leaking the UDID lease. [community]

---

### Pattern 434 — Appium XCUITest `mobile: alert` Commands for Native iOS Alert Interaction Without `autoAcceptAlerts` [official]

XCUITest driver's `mobile: alert` family of execute commands (`getText`, `getButtons`, `accept`, `dismiss`, `sendKeys`) provides deterministic, non-polling native alert interaction that avoids the timing races of `autoAcceptAlerts`. Unlike the capability-level auto-accept which fires on a background polling thread (potentially consuming an alert meant for a different test phase), `mobile: alert` calls are synchronous from the test's perspective and return the alert button labels so you can assert the correct message before acting. Use it to verify that destructive action confirmation dialogs contain the expected warning text, and to selectively accept or dismiss based on button content.

```typescript
// test/helpers/iosAlertHelper.ts
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export interface IOSAlertInfo {
  text:    string;
  buttons: string[];
}

/** Check whether a native iOS alert is currently visible. */
export async function isAlertShown(): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    await driver.execute('mobile: alert', { action: 'getText' });
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/** Get native iOS alert text and available button labels. */
export async function getAlertInfo(): Promise<IOSAlertInfo> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) throw new Error('getAlertInfo is iOS-only');
  const text    = await driver.execute('mobile: alert', { action: 'getText' })    as string;
  const buttons = await driver.execute('mobile: alert', { action: 'getButtons' }) as string[];
  return { text, buttons };
}

/** Tap a specific button on the current native iOS alert by label. */
export async function tapAlertButton(buttonLabel: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) throw new Error('tapAlertButton is iOS-only');
  await driver.execute('mobile: alert', { action: 'accept', buttonLabel });
}

/** Assert alert text then accept with the specified button. */
export async function acceptAlertExpecting(
  expectedText: RegExp | string,
  buttonLabel: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const info = await getAlertInfo();
  if (expectedText instanceof RegExp) {
    expect(info.text).toMatch(expectedText);
  } else {
    expect(info.text).toContain(expectedText);
  }
  if (!info.buttons.includes(buttonLabel)) {
    throw new Error(`Button "${buttonLabel}" not found. Available: ${info.buttons.join(', ')}`);
  }
  await tapAlertButton(buttonLabel);
}
```

```typescript
// test/specs/delete-account.spec.ts
import { acceptAlertExpecting, isAlertShown } from '../helpers/iosAlertHelper.js';

it('should show confirmation alert before deleting account', async () => {
  await $('~delete-account-btn').click();
  await browser.waitUntil(() => isAlertShown(), { timeout: 3_000 });
  await acceptAlertExpecting(/permanently delete your account/i, 'Delete');
  await expect($('~login-screen')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: alert` commands work only for XCUITest-managed native alerts (`UIAlertController`). Custom in-app modal dialogs built with SwiftUI `Alert` or `sheet()` are rendered as UIKit views but may not be recognised as alerts by XCUITest's alert handler — test those with standard accessibility-ID selectors. On iOS 17+, system permission alerts (camera, location, notifications) are rendered in a separate process (`tccd`) and are accessible via `mobile: alert` only when `autoAcceptAlerts: false`; if `autoAcceptAlerts: true` the capability's background handler may dismiss the alert before your test code runs. [official]

## Cycle 38 Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C38-1 — `browser.emulate('clock')` epoch default silently breaks relative-time UI [community]**

WHY: `browser.emulate('clock')` without a `now` option defaults the clock to Unix epoch (January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC). Apps that render relative timestamps ("2 minutes ago", "just now") calculate offsets from `Date.now()`. With the clock frozen at 1970, `Date.now()` returns 0 and all timestamp math produces enormous negative relative times — UI shows "55 years ago" or renders the empty state instead of the date label. Always pass an explicit `now: new Date(...)` to `browser.emulate('clock')`.

**Gotcha C38-2 — `browser.mock()` URL glob `**` does not match protocol-relative URLs [community]**

WHY: `browser.mock('**/api/products')` matches `https://app.example.com/api/products` but silently fails to match `//cdn.example.com/api/products` (protocol-relative URL) because the glob engine prepends a protocol scheme before pattern matching. In React Native Web apps that use a CDN origin for API calls, the protocol-relative form is common and tests that expect `mock.calls.length > 0` see zero calls. Fix: add a second mock for the explicit protocol-relative pattern, or use a regex-based `filterOptions.url` matcher instead of a glob.

**Gotcha C38-3 — `mobile: dragGesture` on Android 13+ requires `INJECT_EVENTS` permission that debug builds may not have [community]**

WHY: Android 13 tightened the `INJECT_EVENTS` permission check for non-system processes. UIAutomator2's server APK requests this permission, but if it is not granted (rare in some enterprise MDM profiles), `mobile: dragGesture` silently sends the events without a visual effect — the element does not move. The Appium session does not throw an error. Diagnose by checking `adb shell dumpsys input | grep INJECT` and verifying the UiAutomator2 server APK has the permission. Fix: reinstall the Appium UIAutomator2 server APK (`appium driver run uiautomator2 install-server`) on the device.

**Gotcha C38-4 — `registerDialogRules` listener accumulates across tests without explicit cleanup [community]**

WHY: `browser.on('dialog', handler)` registers a persistent EventEmitter listener. If `cleanupDialogs()` is not called in `afterEach` (e.g. the test throws before `afterEach` executes), the handler remains registered. The next test that triggers a dialog fires multiple handlers, each calling `accept()` or `dismiss()`. Calling `accept()` twice on the same dialog throws `Protocol error (Target.activateTarget): Session closed`. Fix: store the handler reference and call `browser.off('dialog', handler)` in a `finally` block, or use WDIO's `after` hook (which runs even on test failure) instead of `afterEach`.

**Gotcha C38-5 — `xcrun simctl openurl` shell-escaping breaks URLs with query strings [community]**

WHY: `execSync(\`xcrun simctl openurl "${udid}" "${url}"\`)` fails when `url` contains `&` characters (e.g. `?utm_source=email&utm_medium=push`) because the shell interprets `&` as a background-job separator. The URL is truncated at the first `&` and the app receives an incomplete deep-link that lands on the wrong screen. Fix: always shell-escape the URL argument — replace `&` with `\&` before interpolating into the shell command, or use `encodeURIComponent` on the full URL before passing it.

**Gotcha C38-6 — `@wdio/shared-store-service` eventual consistency allows parallel workers to double-claim the same UDID [community]**

WHY: The shared store uses a central HTTP server with optimistic concurrent writes. Two workers checking `available_udids` and `leased_udids` within the same polling interval may both observe the same UDID as unclaimed before either write completes. This causes two sessions to start with the same `appium:udid` — Appium's XCUITest driver throws `Session already exists on device UDID`. Fix: implement an advisory lock key (e.g. `leasing_lock`) that workers atomically set before mutating the leased list, or introduce a random jitter delay (0–200ms) before the lease claim to reduce the contention window.

**Gotcha C38-7 — `mobile: alert getButtons` index ordering changed between iOS 15 and iOS 17 [community]**

WHY: `UIAlertController` button order is defined by insertion order in the app code, but iOS renders "Destructive" style buttons and "Cancel" buttons in platform-specific positions. On iOS 15 the Cancel button is always last in `getButtons`; on iOS 17+ it is first. Tests that hardcode `info.buttons[0]` to be the Cancel button fail on iOS 17+. WHY: Apple changed the internal `UIAlertController` accessibilityElement ordering in iOS 17 to match the visual layout change (Cancel moved to the top). Fix: always select buttons by label text (`tapAlertButton('Cancel')`) rather than by index.

## Cycle 39 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 435 — WDIO v9 `browser.getContexts({ returnDetailedContexts: true })` for Hybrid App WebView Identification [official]

WebdriverIO v9 extends the standard Appium context API with `getContexts({ returnDetailedContexts: true })`, which returns rich metadata for every context — on Android this includes `title`, `url`, `packageName`, `webviewPageId`, and layout bounds; on iOS it includes `bundleId`, `title`, and `url`. This solves a classic hybrid-app pain point: when an app embeds multiple WebViews (e.g. one for the main UI and another for an in-app browser or ads iframe), the default `driver.getContexts()` returns opaque strings like `WEBVIEW_com.example:1` that cannot reliably distinguish which WebView contains the page you want to automate. Enrich context selection with a helper that matches on `url` or `title` patterns, then call `browser.switchContext()` with the matching ID.

```typescript
// test/helpers/hybridContext.ts

interface DetailedContext {
  id: string;
  title?: string;
  url?: string;
  packageName?: string;   // Android
  bundleId?: string;      // iOS
  webviewPageId?: string; // Android
}

/**
 * Switch to the WebView context whose URL matches the given pattern.
 * Uses WDIO v9 `returnDetailedContexts` — requires Appium 2+ and
 * current appium-xcuitest-driver / appium-uiautomator2-driver.
 */
export async function switchToWebViewByUrl(urlPattern: RegExp): Promise<string> {
  const contexts = (await browser.getContexts({
    returnDetailedContexts: true,
  })) as DetailedContext[];

  const target = contexts.find(
    (ctx) => ctx.url && urlPattern.test(ctx.url)
  );
  if (!target) {
    const available = contexts.map((c) => c.url ?? c.id).join(', ');
    throw new Error(`No WebView context matched ${urlPattern}. Available: ${available}`);
  }
  await browser.switchContext(target.id);
  return target.id;
}

// test/specs/in-app-browser.spec.ts
import { switchToWebViewByUrl } from '../helpers/hybridContext.js';

it('should fill the checkout form inside the in-app WebView', async () => {
  await $('~open-checkout-btn').click();
  await switchToWebViewByUrl(/checkout\.example\.com\/cart/);
  await $('#email-field').setValue('user@example.com');
  await $('#place-order-btn').click();
  await expect($('.order-confirmation')).toBeDisplayed();
  // return to native layer
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `returnDetailedContexts: true` makes an additional introspection call under the hood, adding 100–300 ms per invocation — noticeable only if called in a tight polling loop. Avoid calling `getContexts` on every assertion; store the context ID after the first match and switch back to it directly. On Android, `webviewPageId` becomes stale if the WebView navigates to a new page while the native layer is active — re-fetch contexts after significant app-triggered navigations. [official]
