### Pattern 436 — WDIO v9 `browser.deepLink()` with `waitForLaunch: false` for Cold-Start Deep-Link Timing Tests [official]

WebdriverIO v9 wraps the Appium deep-link invocation in `browser.deepLink(link, appIdentifier, { waitForLaunch })`. Setting `waitForLaunch: false` decouples the link dispatch from the app-launch handshake, enabling you to measure the elapsed time from link delivery to the first visible screen — a pattern critical for cold-start instrumentation and onboarding funnel analytics. Pair it with a `performance.now()` timer and a `browser.waitUntil()` assertion on the landing screen to capture precise cold-start deep-link latency. This replaces the earlier pattern of shelling out to `xcrun simctl openurl` (which required shell-escaping hacks for URLs with query strings) with a safe, cross-platform API.

```typescript
// test/specs/cold-start-deeplink.spec.ts

const COLD_START_BUDGET_MS = 2_500;

it('should land on the product detail screen within cold-start budget', async () => {
  // Terminate the app first to force a cold start
  await browser.execute('mobile: terminateApp', {
    bundleId: 'com.example.shopapp',
  });

  const t0 = Date.now();

  // waitForLaunch: false => don't block on the OS launch animation
  await browser.deepLink(
    'shopapp://products/42?ref=email_promo',
    'com.example.shopapp',
    { waitForLaunch: false }
  );

  // Wait for the product title to be visible, measuring elapsed time
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => (await $('~product-title').isDisplayed()),
    { timeout: 5_000, interval: 100 }
  );

  const elapsed = Date.now() - t0;
  console.log(`Cold-start deep-link latency: ${elapsed} ms`);
  expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(COLD_START_BUDGET_MS);

  await expect($('~product-title')).toHaveText('Wireless Headphones Pro');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `waitForLaunch: false` means the test may query elements before the app process has fully initialised — the `waitUntil` call absorbs this race condition, but if the app takes longer than the `waitUntil` timeout the test fails rather than waiting indefinitely. Choose a `timeout` that is larger than the expected worst-case cold start on your slowest CI device. On Android emulators with Compose UI, activity transitions may fire the accessibility events that `waitForDisplayed` relies on up to 400 ms earlier than the frame is fully rendered; prefer `waitUntil` with a stable text assertion over `waitForDisplayed` alone. [official]

---

### Pattern 437 — WDIO v9 `element.longPress({ duration })` for Context Menu and Press-and-Hold UI Patterns [official]

WebdriverIO v9 exposes `longPress({ x, y, duration })` as a first-class element command, abstracting the W3C pointer-down/pause/pointer-up action chain that varied across Appium driver versions. The `duration` defaults to 1500 ms but can be lowered to 500 ms for apps that show context menus quickly, or raised to 3000 ms for press-to-record UIs (voice messaging, video capture). The `x` and `y` offsets allow triggering the long press at a specific sub-region of the element — useful for elements whose context menu depends on which text word is pressed. For iOS web contexts specifically, WDIO uses a JavaScript simulation fallback because XCUITest cannot inject a long press into a `WKWebView` DOM element directly.

```typescript
// test/helpers/contextMenuHelper.ts

export interface ContextMenuOption {
  label: string;
  accessibilityId: string;
}

/**
 * Long-press an element and wait for a context menu item to appear.
 * Returns the context menu item element for further interaction.
 */
export async function longPressForContextMenu(
  targetSelector: string,
  expectedMenuItemId: string,
  duration = 1_500
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  const target = await $(targetSelector);
  await target.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
  await target.longPress({ duration });

  const menuItem = await $(`~${expectedMenuItemId}`);
  await menuItem.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 2_000 });
  return menuItem;
}

// test/specs/message-context-menu.spec.ts
import { longPressForContextMenu } from '../helpers/contextMenuHelper.js';

it('should show copy option when long-pressing a chat message', async () => {
  const copyBtn = await longPressForContextMenu(
    '~msg-bubble-0',
    'copy-message',
    800  // this app shows menu at 800 ms
  );
  await copyBtn.click();
  const clipboard = await browser.getClipboard();
  expect(clipboard).toContain('Hello, this is a test message');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** The `duration` threshold for triggering a context menu is hard-coded in the app, not the OS. Different app versions may change this threshold during UI refactors, silently breaking the long-press test if `duration` is at the boundary. Build in a 200 ms buffer above the documented threshold (e.g. use 1000 ms for an app threshold of 800 ms). On iOS with `WKWebView`, the JavaScript simulation fallback does not fire `touchstart`/`touchend` DOM events; apps relying on `addEventListener('contextmenu', ...)` in the web layer will not see the event — use native accessibility-ID selectors and a native layer interaction instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 438 — WDIO v9 `browser.swipe()` with `scrollableElement` for Bounded In-Component Scrolling [official]

The WDIO v9 `browser.swipe({ direction, percent, duration, scrollableElement })` command restricts the swipe to the bounds of a specific scrollable container instead of the full device viewport. This matters whenever an app embeds multiple scrollable regions (e.g. a horizontal carousel inside a vertically scrolling feed): without `scrollableElement`, the swipe coordinates default to the viewport centre and may land on the wrong container, scrolling the parent list rather than the inner carousel. Pass the resolved element reference to `scrollableElement`. The `percent` parameter (0–1) avoids swiping from the absolute edges of the scrollable element, which on iOS triggers the system back gesture or rubber-band bounce rather than an in-app scroll.

```typescript
// test/helpers/carouselHelper.ts

/**
 * Swipe left through a horizontal carousel until the item with
 * the given accessibility ID is visible, up to maxSwipes attempts.
 */
export async function swipeCarouselToItem(
  carouselSelector: string,
  itemId: string,
  maxSwipes = 8
): Promise<void> {
  const carousel = await $(carouselSelector);
  await carousel.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });

  for (let i = 0; i < maxSwipes; i++) {
    if (await $(`~${itemId}`).isDisplayed()) return;
    await browser.swipe({
      direction: 'left',
      scrollableElement: carousel,
      percent: 0.75,
      duration: 600,
    });
    // Brief pause so the carousel snap animation settles
    await browser.pause(200);
  }
  throw new Error(`Item ~${itemId} not found after ${maxSwipes} swipes in carousel`);
}

// test/specs/product-carousel.spec.ts
import { swipeCarouselToItem } from '../helpers/carouselHelper.js';

it('should show the "New Arrivals" card in the hero carousel', async () => {
  await swipeCarouselToItem('~hero-carousel', 'new-arrivals-card');
  await expect($('~new-arrivals-card')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `scrollableElement` coordinates are resolved at invocation time. If the scrollable container changes size during animation (e.g. a collapsing toolbar), WDIO may compute wrong bounds. Call `browser.swipe()` only after animations complete. The default Android fallback selector (`//android.widget.ScrollView`) may match the wrong scrollable element in screens with multiple `ScrollView` nodes — always pass an explicit `scrollableElement` resolved from a unique accessibility ID. [official]

---

### Pattern 439 — Appium `browser.scrollIntoView()` with `maxScrolls` Guard for Deep-List Item Navigation [official]

`browser.scrollIntoView()` (WDIO v9 mobile command) replaces the brittle pattern of manually computing scroll coordinates to bring an element into view. The `maxScrolls` parameter (default 10) caps the number of swipe attempts so the test fails fast with a clear error rather than spinning indefinitely on a missing list item. Set `direction` to `down` for standard lists and `right` for horizontal carousels; set `scrollableElement` to target a nested scrollable container. The `percent` option (0–1, default 0.95) controls how much of the container is swept per swipe — lower values create more precise, slower scrolling for lists with large item heights.

```typescript
// test/helpers/listNavigationHelper.ts

interface ScrollOptions {
  direction?: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right';
  maxScrolls?: number;
  percent?: number;
  durationMs?: number;
}

/**
 * Scroll within a named container until the target element is visible.
 * Fails clearly if the element is not found within maxScrolls attempts.
 */
export async function scrollUntilVisible(
  containerSelector: string,
  targetSelector: string,
  opts: ScrollOptions = {}
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  const container = await $(containerSelector);
  const target = await $(targetSelector);

  await target.scrollIntoView({
    direction: opts.direction ?? 'down',
    maxScrolls: opts.maxScrolls ?? 10,
    percent: opts.percent ?? 0.85,
    duration: opts.durationMs ?? 1_200,
    scrollableElement: container,
  });

  await expect(target).toBeDisplayed();
  return target;
}

// test/specs/order-history.spec.ts
import { scrollUntilVisible } from '../helpers/listNavigationHelper.js';

it('should display order #1001 in the order history list', async () => {
  const orderRow = await scrollUntilVisible(
    '~order-history-list',
    '~order-row-1001',
    { maxScrolls: 15, percent: 0.9 }
  );
  await orderRow.click();
  await expect($('~order-detail-header')).toHaveText('Order #1001');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `scrollIntoView` works by sending swipe actions — it cannot jump directly to an element offset. For lists with 500+ items, 10–15 swipes may not be enough; increase `maxScrolls` or (better) use Appium's `mobile: scroll` execute command with the element's resource ID as an anchor, which on Android can leverage `UiScrollable.scrollIntoView()` in a single command. On iOS, XCUITest's own scroll-to-element mechanism is faster for native `UITableView` but is not exposed through this API; for very long lists consider `mobile: scroll` with `predicateString` targeting instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 440 — WDIO v9 `browser.getPerformanceData()` for Android Runtime Memory and CPU Regression Gates [official]

`browser.getPerformanceData(packageName, dataType, readTimeout)` queries the Android `UiAutomator2` performance subsystem for live metrics including `cpuinfo`, `memoryinfo`, `batteryinfo`, and `networkinfo`. Use it as an inline performance gate in feature tests: capture a baseline reading before a heavy operation (e.g. loading a 500-item feed), perform the operation, then re-sample and assert the delta is within budget. Pair with `getPerformanceDataTypes()` to discover which data types the current device/API level supports before querying them — this avoids silent empty-result failures on devices that do not expose certain metrics.

```typescript
// test/helpers/perfHelper.ts

export async function sampleMemory(packageName: string): Promise<number> {
  const types = await browser.getPerformanceDataTypes();
  if (!types.includes('memoryinfo')) {
    throw new Error('memoryinfo not supported on this device');
  }
  const rows = await browser.getPerformanceData(packageName, 'memoryinfo', 5);
  // rows[0] is the header row; rows[1] is the data row
  // Columns: totalPrivateDirty, nativePrivateDirty, dalvikPrivateDirty, ...
  const header = rows[0] as string[];
  const data   = rows[1] as string[];
  const idx = header.indexOf('totalPrivateDirty');
  return parseInt(data[idx], 10); // kB
}

// test/specs/feed-memory-gate.spec.ts
import { sampleMemory } from '../helpers/perfHelper.js';

const PKG = 'com.example.feedapp';
const MAX_MEMORY_DELTA_KB = 15_000; // 15 MB per feed-load operation

it('should not leak more than 15 MB loading the main feed', async () => {
  await browser.activateApp(PKG);
  const before = await sampleMemory(PKG);

  await $('~feed-refresh-btn').click();
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => (await $$('~feed-item').length) >= 20,
    { timeout: 10_000 }
  );

  const after = await sampleMemory(PKG);
  const delta = after - before;
  console.log(`Memory delta: ${delta} kB`);
  expect(delta).toBeLessThan(MAX_MEMORY_DELTA_KB);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `getPerformanceData` is Android-only and relies on `UiAutomator2`'s bridge to the `dumpsys` subsystem — it is not available in iOS test sessions. On Android emulators, `cpuinfo` values are unreliable because the host machine's CPU scheduler affects virtual CPU metrics; restrict CPU-based gates to real-device jobs in CI. The data freshness window is approximately 500 ms by default; if the operation under test completes faster, request a shorter `readTimeout` (minimum 1 s). [official]

---

### Pattern 441 — WDIO v9 `browser.toggleEnrollTouchId()` + `browser.touchId()` for Biometric Auth Flow Testing on iOS Simulator [official]

WDIO v9 wraps the XCUITest biometric APIs in two clean commands: `browser.toggleEnrollTouchId(true)` enrolls a biometric identity on the simulator, and `browser.touchId(true)` / `browser.touchId(false)` fires a matching or non-matching biometric event. This enables end-to-end testing of authentication flows that require Touch ID or Face ID — scenarios that were previously untestable in automated environments. Both commands require the `allowTouchIdEnroll: true` capability in `wdio.conf.ts`. To test Face ID, pass `'faceId'` as the second argument to `touchId()`. Enroll in `before()`, fire match/non-match events per test, and disenroll in `after()` to avoid state contamination across test suites.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts (relevant excerpt)
// capabilities: [{ 'appium:allowTouchIdEnroll': true, ... }]

// test/helpers/biometricHelper.ts

/**
 * Set up Touch ID enrollment for the simulator session.
 * Call in `before()` for any suite that tests biometric auth.
 */
export async function enrollBiometrics(type: 'touchId' | 'faceId' = 'touchId'): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) return; // no-op on Android
  await browser.toggleEnrollTouchId(true);
  console.log(`[biometric] Enrolled ${type} on simulator`);
}

export async function disenrollBiometrics(): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) return;
  await browser.toggleEnrollTouchId(false);
}

export async function simulateBiometricMatch(match: boolean, type: 'touchId' | 'faceId' = 'touchId'): Promise<void> {
  await browser.touchId(match, type);
}

// test/specs/biometric-login.spec.ts
import { enrollBiometrics, disenrollBiometrics, simulateBiometricMatch } from '../helpers/biometricHelper.js';

describe('Biometric login flow', () => {
  before(async () => {
    await enrollBiometrics('touchId');
  });

  after(async () => {
    await disenrollBiometrics();
  });

  it('should log in successfully on Touch ID match', async () => {
    await $('~use-touch-id-btn').click();
    await browser.pause(500); // wait for biometric prompt to appear
    await simulateBiometricMatch(true, 'touchId');
    await expect($('~home-screen')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  });

  it('should show error on Touch ID non-match', async () => {
    await $('~use-touch-id-btn').click();
    await browser.pause(500);
    await simulateBiometricMatch(false, 'touchId');
    await expect($('~biometric-error-msg')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `toggleEnrollTouchId` and `touchId` are iOS Simulator-only — they throw a `NotImplementedError` on real devices and on Android. On real iOS devices, biometric prompts live in a separate security enclave process (`SpringBoard`) that is not accessible to test automation. For real-device biometric testing, use a test-backdoor capability (e.g. a debug scheme that bypasses the biometric check) or accept the limitation and restrict biometric flow coverage to Simulator-based CI. The `allowTouchIdEnroll` capability must be set before session creation; setting it mid-session has no effect. [official]

---

### Pattern 442 — WDIO v9 `browser.gsmCall()` / `browser.gsmSignal()` for Android Emulator Telephony Simulation [official]

WDIO v9 exposes `browser.gsmCall(phoneNumber, action)` and `browser.gsmSignal(signalStrength)` for Android emulator telephony testing. `gsmCall` with action `'call'` simulates an incoming call notification — useful for testing apps that display a call overlay or pause audio playback during a call. `gsmSignal` accepts `'none'`, `'poor'`, `'moderate'`, `'good'`, or `'great'` to simulate varying cellular signal conditions without toggling airplane mode. Combine them to test UX degradation paths: assert that the app shows a "Weak Signal" banner when `gsmSignal('poor')` is set, or that an active voice call is properly interrupted and queued when `gsmCall` fires.

```typescript
// test/helpers/telephonyHelper.ts

type GsmSignalStrength = 'none' | 'poor' | 'moderate' | 'good' | 'great';
type GsmCallAction = 'call' | 'accept' | 'cancel' | 'hold';

export async function simulateIncomingCall(number: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) return;
  await browser.gsmCall(number, 'call');
}

export async function cancelSimulatedCall(number: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) return;
  await browser.gsmCall(number, 'cancel');
}

export async function setSignalStrength(strength: GsmSignalStrength): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) return;
  await browser.gsmSignal(strength);
}

// test/specs/call-interrupt.spec.ts
import {
  simulateIncomingCall,
  cancelSimulatedCall,
  setSignalStrength,
} from '../helpers/telephonyHelper.js';

it('should pause podcast playback on incoming call', async () => {
  await $('~play-btn').click();
  await expect($('~now-playing-bar')).toBeDisplayed();

  await simulateIncomingCall('+15550001234');
  await browser.pause(800); // allow app to react to the call event

  await expect($('~call-overlay')).toBeDisplayed();
  await expect($('~now-playing-bar')).not.toBeDisplayed();

  await cancelSimulatedCall('+15550001234');
  await expect($('~now-playing-bar')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
});

it('should display "Weak Signal" banner when GSM signal is poor', async () => {
  await setSignalStrength('poor');
  await expect($('~weak-signal-banner')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
  await setSignalStrength('great'); // restore
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `gsmCall` and `gsmSignal` only work on Android emulators — they are no-ops (or throw) on real devices and on iOS. The `gsmCall('call')` event triggers the system-level incoming call UI overlay in some AOSP emulator images, which steals focus and may cause subsequent element lookups to fail. If the app does not implement a call overlay, use `gsmCall('cancel')` immediately after `call` to dismiss the system UI. `gsmSignal` changes are asynchronous; allow 500–1000 ms after setting signal before asserting UI that reacts to connectivity events. [official]

---

### Pattern 443 — Appium UIAutomator2 `mobile: flingGesture` for Testing Infinite-Scroll Boundary Detection [official]

`mobile: flingGesture` sends a rapid momentum-based swipe that continues scrolling past the initial touch contact, unlike `mobile: swipeGesture` which stops where the finger lifts. Its return value (`{ result: true | false }`) indicates whether the gesture found the end of the scrollable container — `false` means there is more content, `true` means the list boundary was reached. This is the correct API for testing that infinite-scroll feeds actually load additional items: fling until `result === true`, then assert the "You've reached the end" footer is displayed rather than a loading spinner.

```typescript
// test/helpers/flingHelper.ts

interface FlingResult {
  result: boolean; // true = hit scroll boundary
}

interface FlingOptions {
  elementId?: string;
  left?: number; top?: number; width?: number; height?: number;
  direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right';
  speed?: number; // px/s, default 7500
}

/**
 * Fling a scrollable element until its scroll boundary is reached,
 * collecting intermediate item counts to verify incremental loading.
 */
export async function flingToEnd(
  containerSelector: string,
  opts: Omit<FlingOptions, 'elementId'> = { direction: 'down', speed: 9_000 }
): Promise<void> {
  const el = await $(containerSelector);
  await el.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  const { elementId } = el as unknown as { elementId: string };

  let hitBoundary = false;
  let attempts = 0;
  while (!hitBoundary && attempts < 20) {
    const res = (await browser.execute('mobile: flingGesture', {
      elementId,
      direction: opts.direction,
      speed: opts.speed ?? 7_500,
    })) as FlingResult;
    hitBoundary = res.result;
    attempts++;
    await browser.pause(300); // allow lazy-loading to complete
  }
}

// test/specs/infinite-scroll.spec.ts
import { flingToEnd } from '../helpers/flingHelper.js';

it('should load all items and show the end-of-feed footer', async () => {
  await flingToEnd('~activity-feed-list', { direction: 'down', speed: 8_000 });
  await expect($('~end-of-feed-label')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await expect($('~loading-spinner')).not.toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: flingGesture` is Android/UIAutomator2-only. The speed parameter controls pixel velocity per second — values above 15 000 px/s can skip items so fast that lazy-image loading is never triggered, causing test-environment image count discrepancies. On iOS, approximate fling behaviour via XCUITest `mobile: swipe` with `velocity: 2500` (see Pattern 426). The boundary detection (`result === true`) only applies to elements that implement `UiScrollable.isScrollable()` — custom `RecyclerView` adapters with `setScrollingCacheEnabled(false)` may never report `true`, causing an infinite loop; add the `attempts < 20` guard. [official]

---

### Pattern 444 — WDIO v9 `browser.pinch()` / `element.pinch()` for Zoom-Sensitive UI Testing [official]

WDIO v9 provides a high-level `element.pinch({ scale, duration })` command that abstracts the W3C multi-touch pointer action sequence for pinch-close (zoom-out) gestures. `scale` is a float between 0 and 1 where 1.0 represents 100% of the element's width; passing 0.5 closes the fingers to half-width. A companion `browser.zoom()` command performs the inverse (pinch-open). These commands are available on both iOS (XCUITest) and Android (UIAutomator2), making them the portable choice over raw `driver.execute('mobile: pinchCloseGesture', ...)` calls. Use them to verify that map tiles re-render at the correct zoom level and that PDF viewers scale content predictably.

```typescript
// test/helpers/mapGestureHelper.ts

/**
 * Pinch-close (zoom out) on a map element and verify scale label.
 * scale: 0.0-1.0 (1.0 = full element width, 0.2 = very tight pinch)
 */
export async function zoomOutMap(
  mapSelector: string,
  scale = 0.4,
  duration = 2_000
): Promise<void> {
  const mapEl = await $(mapSelector);
  await mapEl.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await mapEl.pinch({ scale, duration });
  // Allow tile re-render time
  await browser.pause(500);
}

/**
 * Pinch-open (zoom in) using WDIO zoom() - mirrors pinch but expands.
 */
export async function zoomInMap(
  mapSelector: string,
  scale = 0.8,
  duration = 2_000
): Promise<void> {
  const mapEl = await $(mapSelector);
  await mapEl.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await (mapEl as any).zoom({ scale, duration });
  await browser.pause(500);
}

// test/specs/map-zoom.spec.ts
import { zoomOutMap, zoomInMap } from '../helpers/mapGestureHelper.js';

it('should show city-level view after pinch-out from street level', async () => {
  // Start at street-level zoom
  await expect($('~map-zoom-label')).toHaveText('Street Level');
  await zoomOutMap('~map-container', 0.3, 2_500);
  await expect($('~map-zoom-label')).toHaveText('City Level');
});

it('should return to street level after pinch-in', async () => {
  await zoomInMap('~map-container', 0.9, 2_000);
  await expect($('~map-zoom-label')).toHaveText('Street Level');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** The `scale` values translate differently across devices because the gesture coordinates are proportional to the element size. A `scale: 0.3` on a 5-inch phone (physical element width ~300 px) moves the fingers 90 px apart — a modest zoom-out. On a 10-inch tablet with a 600 px element width, the same scale moves fingers 180 px apart — a much larger zoom-out, potentially crossing tile level boundaries the test doesn't anticipate. For zoom-level-specific assertions, calibrate `scale` per device family or use `mobile: pinchCloseGesture` with absolute coordinate distances instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 445 — WDIO v9 `browser.shake()` for iOS Accelerometer-Triggered Undo/Report-Abuse Flow Testing [official]

`browser.shake()` simulates a device shake gesture on iOS Simulator and real iOS devices. Apps that implement shake-to-undo (UIKit's `motionBegan/Ended`), shake-to-report (custom gesture recogniser), or accelerometer-driven easter eggs can be tested without physically shaking hardware. The command requires no parameters and works via the XCUITest driver's `mobile: shake` execute method. Call it after a text-editing operation to trigger the undo prompt, or in a game test to trigger the "Report Abuse" dialog. Pair with `browser.waitUntil()` to wait for the resulting UI to settle after the motion event.

```typescript
// test/helpers/shakeHelper.ts

/**
 * Shake the device and wait for the resulting dialog/UI to appear.
 * Accepts an optional selector for the expected post-shake element.
 */
export async function shakeAndWait(
  expectedSelector?: string,
  timeoutMs = 3_000
): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) {
    console.warn('[shake] shake() is iOS-only; skipping on Android');
    return;
  }
  await browser.shake();
  if (expectedSelector) {
    await browser.waitUntil(
      async () => $(expectedSelector).isDisplayed(),
      { timeout: timeoutMs, interval: 200 }
    );
  } else {
    await browser.pause(500); // brief settle time
  }
}

// test/specs/text-undo.spec.ts
import { shakeAndWait } from '../helpers/shakeHelper.js';

it('should show Undo Typing prompt after shake following text input', async () => {
  const field = await $('~notes-text-field');
  await field.click();
  await field.setValue('Draft text that will be undone');
  await expect(field).toHaveValue('Draft text that will be undone');

  await shakeAndWait('~undo-typing-alert');
  await $('~undo-typing-alert').click(); // tap "Undo"
  await expect(field).toHaveValue('');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.shake()` is iOS-only — on Android the command throws `NotImplementedError`. For Android apps that respond to `SensorManager.SENSOR_DELAY_UI` shake detection, inject a simulated motion event via `adb shell input motionEvent` or use `driver.execute('mobile: sensorSet', { sensorType: 'acceleration', value: '9.8:9.8:9.8' })` on supported emulators. iOS real devices support `shake()` but the motion is synthetic and may not reach the native `CMMotionManager` — test shake UX on Simulator where XCUITest has direct UIKit access. [official]

---

### Pattern 446 — Appium UIAutomator2 `mobile: listWindows` for Multi-Window Android Test Coordination [official]

Android 12+ introduced multi-window and multi-display support (split-screen, freeform windowing on tablets and foldables). UIAutomator2 exposes `mobile: listWindows` to enumerate all visible windows across displays, and `mobile: listDisplays` to describe each connected display. Use these commands to verify that your app's activity appears in the expected display/window slot, and to resolve the correct `displayId` for directing subsequent gestures to the right screen. This is especially relevant for foldable device testing where the app may be on the inner or outer display.

```typescript
// test/helpers/multiWindowHelper.ts

interface AppiumWindow {
  id: number;
  layer: number;
  displayId: number;
  type: string;
  bounds: { left: number; top: number; right: number; bottom: number };
  focused: boolean;
  packageName?: string;
}

interface AppiumDisplay {
  id: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  density: number;
  orientation: number;
}

export async function getWindowsForPackage(packageName: string): Promise<AppiumWindow[]> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) return [];
  const windows = (await browser.execute('mobile: listWindows', {})) as AppiumWindow[];
  return windows.filter((w) => w.packageName === packageName);
}

export async function listDisplays(): Promise<AppiumDisplay[]> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) return [];
  return (await browser.execute('mobile: listDisplays', {})) as AppiumDisplay[];
}

// test/specs/split-screen.spec.ts
import { getWindowsForPackage, listDisplays } from '../helpers/multiWindowHelper.js';

it('should run in split-screen with the app in the top half', async () => {
  const displays = await listDisplays();
  expect(displays.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);

  const appWindows = await getWindowsForPackage('com.example.myapp');
  expect(appWindows.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  const mainDisplay = displays.find((d) => d.id === 0)!;
  const appWindow = appWindows[0];

  // Verify the app window occupies the top half of the primary display
  const windowMidY = (appWindow.bounds.top + appWindow.bounds.bottom) / 2;
  expect(windowMidY).toBeLessThan(mainDisplay.height / 2);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: listWindows` returns all system windows including overlays, launchers, and status bars — not just app windows. Filter by `packageName` or by `type === 'TYPE_APPLICATION'` to isolate your app's windows. On Android 12+ emulators in multi-window mode, `focused: true` may be wrong immediately after `swipe` or `keyEvent` actions that shift focus; add a `browser.pause(300)` before calling `listWindows` if focus-based assertions are unreliable. This API is unavailable on iOS — use `XCUIElementType.Window` accessibility queries via XCUITest for multi-window iPad scenarios. [official]

---

### Pattern 447 — WDIO v9 `browser.openNotifications()` + `browser.sendSms()` for Push and SMS Notification E2E Verification on Android Emulator [official]

`browser.openNotifications()` programmatically pulls down the Android notification shade, and `browser.sendSms(phoneNumber, message)` delivers a simulated SMS to the emulator — no carrier or real SIM required. Combining them tests the full notification-to-app flow: send a simulated SMS, open the notification shade, tap the notification to launch the app, and verify the deep-link destination is correct. This pattern eliminates the need for real test phone numbers, SIM cards, or third-party SMS gateways in local and CI environments.

```typescript
// test/helpers/notificationHelper.ts

/**
 * Send a simulated SMS to the Android emulator, open the notification
 * shade, tap the SMS notification, and return to the app.
 *
 * Requires: Android emulator (not real device), Appium UIAutomator2.
 */
export async function tapSmsNotificationAndVerifyApp(
  fromNumber: string,
  messageText: string,
  expectedSelector: string
): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) return;

  // Deliver the simulated SMS
  await browser.sendSms(fromNumber, messageText);
  await browser.pause(1_000); // allow notification to post

  // Open the notification shade
  await browser.openNotifications();
  await browser.pause(500);

  // Find and tap the SMS notification
  const notification = await $(`**/android.widget.TextView[@text="${messageText}"]`);
  await notification.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await notification.click();

  // Verify the app reacted to the SMS notification
  await expect($(expectedSelector)).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
}

// test/specs/sms-otp-flow.spec.ts
import { tapSmsNotificationAndVerifyApp } from '../helpers/notificationHelper.js';

it('should open the OTP verification screen after tapping SMS notification', async () => {
  await tapSmsNotificationAndVerifyApp(
    '+15550001234',
    'Your verification code is 123456',
    '~otp-entry-screen'
  );
  const otpField = await $('~otp-input');
  await expect(otpField).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.sendSms()` is Android emulator-only — it does not work on real devices (no emulator console port) or on iOS. On some Android API 33+ emulators, the system Messages app must be the default SMS handler; if it has been replaced by the app under test as the default handler, `sendSms` may trigger the app directly without a notification appearing in the shade. Use `openNotifications()` with a `waitForDisplayed` timeout rather than an immediate check — notifications can be delayed by 800–1500 ms on emulators with constrained RAM. [official]

---

### Pattern 448 — Appium `mobile: activateApp` + `browser.queryAppState()` for Reliable App Foreground/Background State Assertions [official]

`browser.queryAppState(bundleIdOrPackageName)` returns a numeric state code (0 = not installed, 1 = not running, 2 = running in background and suspended, 3 = running in background, 4 = running in foreground) that gives precise visibility into an app's lifecycle beyond the binary "is it displayed?" check. Combine it with `browser.activateApp()` and `browser.background()` to write lifecycle-contract tests: assert the app transitions to state 3 within N ms after being backgrounded (iOS), or returns to state 4 within M ms after `activateApp`. This is the correct API for testing apps that restore state correctly on foreground restore.

```typescript
// test/helpers/appLifecycleHelper.ts

// Appium app state codes
export const AppState = {
  NOT_INSTALLED:        0,
  NOT_RUNNING:          1,
  BACKGROUND_SUSPENDED: 2,
  BACKGROUND:           3,
  FOREGROUND:           4,
} as const;

type AppStateValue = typeof AppState[keyof typeof AppState];

export async function waitForAppState(
  appId: string,
  expectedState: AppStateValue,
  timeoutMs = 5_000,
  intervalMs = 200
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const state = await browser.queryAppState(appId);
      return state === expectedState;
    },
    {
      timeout: timeoutMs,
      interval: intervalMs,
      timeoutMsg: `App ${appId} did not reach state ${expectedState} within ${timeoutMs} ms`,
    }
  );
}

// test/specs/background-restore.spec.ts
import { AppState, waitForAppState } from '../helpers/appLifecycleHelper.js';

const APP_ID = browser.isIOS ? 'com.example.myapp' : 'com.example.myapp';

it('should restore the cart contents after background/foreground cycle', async () => {
  await $('~add-to-cart-btn').click();
  await expect($('~cart-badge')).toHaveText('1');

  // Background the app for 3 seconds
  await browser.background(3);
  await waitForAppState(APP_ID, AppState.BACKGROUND, 5_000);

  // Re-activate
  await browser.activateApp(APP_ID);
  await waitForAppState(APP_ID, AppState.FOREGROUND, 5_000);

  // Cart badge should still show 1 (state was preserved)
  await expect($('~cart-badge')).toHaveText('1');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** State codes differ between iOS and Android: on iOS, the distinction between state 2 (suspended) and state 3 (background-running) reflects whether the background task completed; on Android both commonly return 3 for backgrounded apps. Do not assert `=== AppState.BACKGROUND_SUSPENDED` in cross-platform tests unless you are intentionally testing iOS-only background task behaviour. `background(-1)` sends the app to background indefinitely; always re-activate or the next test inherits a backgrounded app, silently failing session-dependent assertions. [official]

---

### Pattern 449 — WDIO v9 `browser.toggleAirplaneMode()` + `waitUntil` for Offline/Reconnect UX State Machine Testing [official]

`browser.toggleAirplaneMode()` flips the Android emulator's airplane mode on and off without requiring ADB shell access or a `mobile: setConnectivity` execute command. Use it to test offline error states, reconnection banners, retry queues, and "Saved offline" confirmation flows. The command is a toggle — call it once to go offline, call it again to reconnect. Pair with `browser.waitUntil()` polling to detect the exact moment the app's UI transitions between offline and online states, rather than using fixed `browser.pause()` delays that vary by device speed.

```typescript
// test/helpers/connectivityHelper.ts

/**
 * Toggle airplane mode and wait for the app to reflect the new
 * connectivity state via a UI indicator.
 *
 * @param offlineBannerSelector - accessibility ID of the offline/online banner
 * @param expectVisible - whether to expect the banner to appear (true) or disappear (false)
 */
export async function setAirplaneModeAndWait(
  offlineBannerSelector: string,
  expectVisible: boolean,
  timeoutMs = 10_000
): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid) return; // Android-only command

  await browser.toggleAirplaneMode();
  await browser.pause(500); // allow the radio stack to stabilise

  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const banner = await $(offlineBannerSelector);
      const visible = await banner.isDisplayed();
      return visible === expectVisible;
    },
    {
      timeout: timeoutMs,
      interval: 300,
      timeoutMsg: `Banner ${offlineBannerSelector} visibility (${expectVisible}) not reached within ${timeoutMs} ms`,
    }
  );
}

// test/specs/offline-mode.spec.ts
import { setAirplaneModeAndWait } from '../helpers/connectivityHelper.js';

it('should show "You are offline" banner and hide it on reconnect', async () => {
  // Go offline
  await setAirplaneModeAndWait('~offline-banner', true);
  await expect($('~offline-banner')).toBeDisplayed();
  await expect($('~offline-banner')).toHaveText('You are offline');

  // Reconnect
  await setAirplaneModeAndWait('~offline-banner', false);
  await expect($('~online-banner')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `toggleAirplaneMode()` is Android-only. On iOS, use `browser.execute('mobile: setConnectivity', { wifi: false, data: false })` (XCUITest driver, simulator only) or the Network Link Conditioner profile approach for real device testing. On Android emulators, toggling airplane mode takes 800–2000 ms to propagate to the app's `ConnectivityManager` listener — the `pause(500)` plus `waitUntil` pattern absorbs this; a bare `pause(2000)` works but makes the suite 1.5 s slower per offline/online cycle. Always end the test by toggling airplane mode back off, otherwise subsequent tests run with no connectivity. [official]

## Cycle 39 Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C39-1 — `browser.getContexts({ returnDetailedContexts: true })` returns stale `url` after in-WebView SPA navigation [community]**

WHY: `getContexts` with `returnDetailedContexts` calls Appium's context introspection at a point in time. When a React-based WebView performs an in-page navigation via `history.pushState()` (no full reload), the WebView context's `url` field in Appium's response lags by up to one full `getContexts` polling cycle — typically 1–2 seconds. Tests that call `getContexts` immediately after a WebView route change and assert on `ctx.url` see the previous URL. Fix: add a `browser.waitUntil()` loop that repeatedly calls `getContexts` until the observed `url` matches the expected pattern before asserting.

**Gotcha C39-2 — `browser.deepLink()` on Android silently succeeds even when the package is not installed [community]**

WHY: On Android, `browser.deepLink()` dispatches an `Intent` via the Appium UIAutomator2 driver. If no application handles the intent (package not installed, wrong URI scheme), Android silently drops the Intent without throwing an exception or returning an error — the `deepLink()` promise resolves successfully. Tests that assert on a subsequent screen element will time out rather than failing with a useful "package not installed" error. Fix: always call `browser.queryAppState(packageName)` before `deepLink()` and assert it is `>= 1` (installed), throwing a descriptive error if not.

**Gotcha C39-3 — `browser.toggleAirplaneMode()` called twice in quick succession enters a race with the radio stack and leaves airplane mode in an indeterminate state [community]**

WHY: `toggleAirplaneMode()` fires an `adb shell settings put global airplane_mode_on 1` followed by a broadcast intent. If two toggles arrive within ~300 ms, the second toggle races the broadcast and the radio stack may ignore the second state change — leaving the emulator in the first toggled state. Tests that call `toggleAirplaneMode()` in `afterEach` without verifying the resulting state silently pollute subsequent tests with missing connectivity. Fix: after each toggle, verify connectivity state via `adb shell settings get global airplane_mode_on` (returns `0` or `1`) before proceeding, or add a 600 ms minimum gap between consecutive toggles.

**Gotcha C39-4 — `browser.sendSms()` delivers to the emulator console but does not trigger the Appium-installed test helper's SMS broadcast receiver on Android 14+ [community]**

WHY: Android 14 tightened implicit broadcast receiver restrictions (`RECEIVER_EXPORTED` flag). The `sendSms` command routes through the emulator console to inject a fake SMS, which fires a `android.provider.Telephony.SMS_RECEIVED` broadcast. On Android 14+ emulators, if the system Messages app is not the default SMS handler and no exported receiver is registered, the broadcast is queued and eventually dropped — the notification never appears. Fix: ensure the test emulator has a default SMS handler app installed and set as default, or set `RECEIVER_EXPORTED` on any custom SMS broadcast receiver in the test APK's `AndroidManifest.xml`.

**Gotcha C39-5 — `browser.queryAppState()` returns `3` (background) on iOS for apps that have been force-quit by the OS due to memory pressure [community]**

WHY: Apple's XCUITest introspection of app state relies on SpringBoard's process list. When an app is force-terminated by the OS (OOM killer or thermal shutdown), SpringBoard briefly retains the app's entry in its registry before finalising the kill — during this window, `queryAppState()` reports state `3` (background) instead of state `1` (not running). Tests that assert `state === AppState.NOT_RUNNING` immediately after the OS terminates the app can intermittently receive `3` and pass the assertion, then fail the next step. Fix: add a 1.5 s pause after `terminateApp` on real iOS devices before calling `queryAppState`, or use a `waitUntil` loop polling for state `<= 1`.

**Gotcha C39-6 — `browser.gsmCall('cancel')` does not dismiss the system call overlay if the app has accepted the call via `CallKit` [community]**

WHY: `gsmCall('cancel')` sends an AT command to the emulator modem to end the simulated call. However, when an iOS or Android app integrates with `CallKit` (iOS) or `ConnectionService` (Android), the OS routes incoming call state through the respective framework's call manager. Once the app answers via `CallKit.CXAnswerCallAction`, the emulator modem command is no longer the authoritative source for call state — the app's call manager holds the active state. `gsmCall('cancel')` triggers the modem-level hangup but `CallKit` does not relay this to the app's active call UI. Fix: end the call via the in-app "End Call" button (`$('~end-call-btn').click()`) rather than `gsmCall('cancel')` in tests that exercise `CallKit`-integrated apps.

**Gotcha C39-7 — `browser.openNotifications()` fails on Android 13+ emulators when the notification permission has not been granted [community]**

WHY: Android 13 introduced the `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` runtime permission. On clean emulator images used in CI, this permission defaults to denied for test APKs. `browser.openNotifications()` can pull down the shade, but if no notifications are present (because the app could not post them without the permission), the test assertion that follows — looking for a specific notification — will time out. The failure message points to the missing notification element, not the missing permission. Fix: grant the notification permission explicitly via `adb shell pm grant <packageName> android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS` in the `before()` hook, or use Appium's `mobile: grantPermission` execute method.

## Cycle 40 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 450 — Appium `mobile: installCertificate` for HTTPS Traffic Interception on iOS Simulators [official]

Testing HTTPS-intercepting proxies (Charles, mitmproxy, Proxyman) on iOS Simulators requires the proxy's root certificate to be trusted by the system keychain. Appium's XCUITest driver exposes `mobile: installCertificate` to install a base64-encoded DER certificate into the simulator's keychain without leaving the test session. This replaces the manual drag-and-drop of a `.pem` file into the simulator window, which is not automatable. Pair the installation with a `mobile: terminateApp` + `mobile: launchApp` cycle to force the app to pick up the new trust root. Combine with the proxy capability `appium:webkitResponseTimeout` to absorb initial proxy handshake latency.

```typescript
// test/helpers/certHelper.ts
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

/**
 * Install a proxy root certificate into the iOS Simulator's keychain
 * so that HTTPS connections routed through the proxy are trusted.
 *
 * @param certPath - Absolute path to the proxy's .cer / .der file
 */
export async function installProxyCertificate(certPath: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) {
    throw new Error('installProxyCertificate is iOS Simulator only');
  }
  const certBytes = fs.readFileSync(certPath);
  const base64Cert = certBytes.toString('base64');

  await browser.execute('mobile: installCertificate', {
    content: base64Cert,
    commonName: 'Proxy Root CA', // display name in Settings > General > About > Certificate Trust
  });
}

// test/specs/https-proxy-spec.ts
import { installProxyCertificate } from '../helpers/certHelper.js';

before(async () => {
  await installProxyCertificate('/certs/mitmproxy-ca-cert.cer');
  // Re-launch app so it picks up the new trust root immediately
  await browser.execute('mobile: terminateApp', { bundleId: 'com.example.myapp' });
  await browser.execute('mobile: launchApp', { bundleId: 'com.example.myapp' });
});

it('should complete checkout over HTTPS via proxy', async () => {
  await $('~checkout-btn').click();
  await expect($('~order-confirm')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: installCertificate` only works on iOS Simulators — real devices require MDM enrollment or manual trust. The certificate is installed into the simulator's system store permanently for the lifetime of that simulator UDID; if you re-use simulator UDIDs across CI runs, previously installed certs persist, which may mask "clean install" regressions. For Android, use `adb shell security import-cacert` or a `mobile: shell` command in a `before` hook instead. XCUITest driver v5.14+ required. [official]
