### Pattern 475 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: getUIHierarchy` with Filter Options for Targeted XML Extraction [official]

**Description:** `mobile: getUIHierarchy` returns the full UIAutomator2 XML accessibility hierarchy as a string, equivalent to `driver.getPageSource()` but with additional filter parameters: `withClassName`, `withResourceId`, and `withContentDescription`. Filtering server-side reduces the payload from 200–800 KB (full hierarchy) to a few KB for the target subtree, significantly speeding up spec-level debugging helpers. Requires UIAutomator2 v3.2+.

```typescript
// helpers/android-hierarchy.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import { parseStringPromise } from 'xml2js';

export interface HierarchyFilter {
  className?: string;
  resourceId?: string;
  contentDescription?: string;
}

/**
 * Fetch a filtered accessibility hierarchy subtree as a parsed JS object.
 * Much faster than getPageSource() for targeted debugging.
 */
export async function getFilteredHierarchy(
  filter: HierarchyFilter,
): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
  const xmlString: string = await browser.execute('mobile: getUIHierarchy', {
    prettyPrint: false,
    withClassName: filter.className,
    withResourceId: filter.resourceId,
    withContentDescription: filter.contentDescription,
  });
  return parseStringPromise(xmlString, { explicitArray: false });
}

// spec — assert RecyclerView item count without full-page-source parse
import { getFilteredHierarchy } from '../helpers/android-hierarchy.js';

it('product list contains at least 10 items', async () => {
  await $('~productListContainer').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });
  const hierarchy = await getFilteredHierarchy({
    resourceId: 'com.example.shop:id/product_list',
  });
  const items: unknown[] = (hierarchy as any)?.hierarchy?.node ?? [];
  const nodeArray = Array.isArray(items) ? items : [items];
  expect(nodeArray.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(10);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: getUIHierarchy` filters are applied server-side by UIAutomator2 but the filter semantics differ from XPath/CSS selectors — `withClassName` matches the exact class name string, not a hierarchy ancestor. Filtering to a deep container class like `androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView` captures all RecyclerViews on the screen simultaneously if multiple are present. Always combine at least two filter dimensions (e.g., `resourceId` + `className`) to scope results accurately. The XML output schema matches `getPageSource()` so existing XML parsing helpers are compatible.

---

### Pattern 476 — XCUITest `mobile: shake` for Shake-Gesture-Triggered Feature Testing on iOS Simulators [official]

**Description:** `mobile: shake` triggers the iOS shake gesture (equivalent to the user physically shaking the device) by calling `XCUIDevice.perform(.shake)`. This activates shake-triggered app behaviours such as undo dialogs, feedback prompts, crash reporter sheets, or developer reset menus — functionality that is otherwise impossible to trigger programmatically via element interaction. Requires XCUITest v3.8+ and iOS Simulator (the gesture can be synthesised on real devices via the XCTest private API but Apple may restrict it in future OS versions).

```typescript
// helpers/ios-gestures.ts  (extending the existing helpers file)
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Trigger the iOS shake gesture and wait for the expected dialog.
 * @param expectedDialogTitle Accessibility label of the dialog that should appear.
 * @param timeoutMs How long to wait for the dialog after the shake.
 */
export async function shakeAndWait(
  expectedDialogTitle: string,
  timeoutMs = 4_000,
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: shake');
  const dialog = await $(
    `-ios predicate string:label == "${expectedDialogTitle}" AND type == "XCUIElementTypeAlert"`,
  );
  await dialog.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: timeoutMs });
  return dialog;
}

// spec — shake triggers undo dialog in text editor
import { shakeAndWait } from '../helpers/ios-gestures.js';

describe('text editor undo flow', () => {
  it('shows undo typing dialog after shake', async () => {
    const textArea = await $('~editorTextArea');
    await textArea.setValue('Draft text that will be undone');
    const undoDialog = await shakeAndWait('Undo Typing');
    await expect(undoDialog).toBeDisplayed();
    await $('~undoButton').click();
    await expect(textArea).toHaveValue('');
  });

  it('cancels undo when cancel button tapped', async () => {
    const textArea = await $('~editorTextArea');
    await textArea.setValue('Keep this text');
    const undoDialog = await shakeAndWait('Undo Typing');
    await $('~cancelUndoButton').click();
    await expect(textArea).toHaveValue('Keep this text');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: shake` dispatches the gesture synchronously but the resulting dialog is presented asynchronously by iOS; a `waitForDisplayed` call after the shake is always required. The gesture only fires shake-triggered callbacks registered via `UIResponder.motionBegan(_:with:)` — apps that use `CoreMotion.CMMotionManager` to listen for motion events will not receive the synthesised shake because `XCUIDevice.perform(.shake)` bypasses the physical accelerometer pipeline. Test both the appearance and dismissal of the triggered UI to avoid test pollution across subsequent cases when the undo dialog remains on screen.

---

### Pattern 477 — WDIO v9 `mobile: startLogsBroadcast` Log Stream for Real-Time Assertion During Test Execution [official]

**Description:** `mobile: startLogsBroadcast` (XCUITest v5.6+) starts a WebSocket-based log stream that pushes device syslog entries to the Appium client in real time, as opposed to the polling model of `mobile: getDeviceLogs`. The WDIO integration collects log lines into a buffer that can be inspected inline during a test without stopping the log stream, enabling latency-sensitive assertions such as "analytics event fires within 2 seconds of user action". `mobile: stopLogsBroadcast` ends the stream and returns the complete buffered log.

```typescript
// helpers/ios-log-stream.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

type LogFilter = { processName?: string; logLevel?: 'default' | 'info' | 'debug' | 'error' };

/** Start real-time syslog stream. Call stopLogStream() when done. */
export async function startLogStream(filter: LogFilter = {}): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: startLogsBroadcast', {
    processName: filter.processName,
    logLevel: filter.logLevel ?? 'default',
  });
}

/** Stop the stream and return all buffered lines. */
export async function stopLogStream(): Promise<string[]> {
  const rawLogs: string = await browser.execute('mobile: stopLogsBroadcast', {});
  return typeof rawLogs === 'string' ? rawLogs.split('\n').filter(Boolean) : [];
}

// spec — analytics event logged within 2 s of add-to-cart tap
import { startLogStream, stopLogStream } from '../helpers/ios-log-stream.js';

describe('analytics instrumentation', () => {
  afterEach(async () => {
    await stopLogStream().catch(() => {});
  });

  it('fires add_to_cart analytics event within 2 seconds', async () => {
    await startLogStream({ processName: 'MyApp', logLevel: 'info' });
    await $('~addToCartButton').click();
    // Poll stop/restart until the analytics line appears within the 2 s budget
    const found = await browser.waitUntil(
      async () => {
        const lines = await stopLogStream();
        await startLogStream({ processName: 'MyApp', logLevel: 'info' });
        return lines.find((l) => l.includes('analytics_event:add_to_cart'));
      },
      { timeout: 2_000, interval: 300 },
    );
    expect(found).toBeDefined();
    expect(found).toContain('analytics_event:add_to_cart');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: startLogsBroadcast` opens a persistent WebSocket connection between Appium server and client — running multiple concurrent Appium sessions on the same host with active log broadcasts can exhaust local port allocations. Always pair with `mobile: stopLogsBroadcast` in an `afterEach` hook even when the test fails. The broadcast captures OS-level syslog entries, meaning any system log line matching the optional `processName` filter is included; set tight `processName` filters to reduce noise and avoid filling CI log storage. Not available on Android; use `browser.getLogs('logcat')` (WDIO v9 compatible) for equivalent Android log streaming.

## Cycle 48 Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C48-1 — `mobile: shell` with `sudo`-prefixed commands on Android 12+ API 32 emulators silently exits with code 0 but performs no action, causing test state setup to appear successful when it has not taken effect [community]**

WHY: The Android emulator's `adbd` daemon runs as the `shell` user (uid 2000), which does not have `sudo` installed or accessible — the binary simply does not exist at any path on AOSP emulator images. When `mobile: shell` executes a command string beginning with `sudo`, `adb shell` resolves the first token to nothing, writes no output to stdout, and exits with code 0 (because `adb shell` returns the exit code of the shell itself, not of the missing binary). Appium receives a 0 exit code and reports success. Test state setup (e.g., `sudo chmod 777 /data/local/tmp/fixture.db`) silently no-ops, causing file access failures dozens of steps later with no obvious connection to the missing `sudo` call. Fix: replace all `sudo` prefixes with direct `adb shell` commands using the correct `shell` user paths, or use `mobile: shell` with `run-as <package>` for app-sandbox operations.

**Gotcha C48-2 — `mobile: scrollToElement` with a predicate that matches multiple elements always scrolls to the first match in document order, not the visually closest one, causing tests to scroll past the intended element when the list contains repeated labels [community]**

WHY: XCUITest's internal `scrollToElement` implementation calls `XCUIElement.firstMatch` on the predicate query, which returns elements in layout order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right accessibility tree traversal). If a `UITableView` contains multiple cells with the same accessibility label (a common pattern in product carousels where items are identified only by a generic "Product" label), the scroll engine jumps to the topmost match even if the intended target is further down the list. The test then asserts on the wrong cell and may pass with incorrect data. Fix: always include a unique differentiator in the predicate (e.g., `label == "Add to cart" AND rect.y > 600`) or assign unique `accessibilityIdentifier` values to list cells rather than relying solely on `accessibilityLabel`.

**Gotcha C48-3 — `element.waitForStable()` returns prematurely on Android when the element is inside a `NestedScrollView` that is still bouncing from a fling gesture, because UIAutomator2 snapshots the bounding box at rest position before the over-scroll bounce animation completes [community]**

WHY: UIAutomator2 computes bounding boxes by querying the accessibility hierarchy synchronously from the instrumentation thread. Android's `NestedScrollView` reports its child positions in terms of the final scroll target (the resting position after the physics simulation), not the current animated position. This means that if a fling gesture is in progress, the accessibility bounding box already reports the post-bounce resting coordinates even though the view is still moving visually. `waitForStable()` observes two consecutive identical bounding box readings and concludes the element is stable, but the view continues to animate for another 200–400 ms. Tapping the element during this window hits the wrong visual coordinates. Fix: wait an additional 400 ms after `waitForStable()` when testing elements inside scrollable containers on Android, or use `element.scrollIntoView()` instead of fling gestures to reach the target.

**Gotcha C48-4 — `mobile: getAppStrings` with a `language` code that uses a region suffix (e.g., `'en-GB'`) falls back silently to the base language bundle on Android, returning American English strings when British English localised strings exist [community]**

WHY: Android resource resolution for `mobile: getAppStrings` uses the `AssetManager.getLocales()` API, which maps the provided BCP-47 tag to the nearest available resource qualifier. However, UIAutomator2's implementation strips the region subtag before querying the bundle — it normalises `'en-GB'` to `'en'` and resolves `res/values-en/strings.xml`, completely ignoring `res/values-en-rGB/strings.xml` even when it exists. The command returns results from the base `'en'` strings, making British English localisation tests falsely pass against American English text. Fix: pass the Android resource qualifier format (`'en-rGB'`) instead of BCP-47 (`'en-GB'`) when targeting region-specific string bundles on Android, and document this discrepancy alongside the iOS equivalent in team testing standards.

**Gotcha C48-5 — `browser.savePDF()` in a WebView times out silently on iOS 17+ Simulator when `WKWebViewConfiguration.preferences.isFraudulentWebsiteWarningEnabled` is `true` and the test loads a `localhost` server with a self-signed TLS certificate [community]**

WHY: In iOS 17, Apple tightened WebKit's fraudulent website detection heuristics. When `isFraudulentWebsiteWarningEnabled` is `true` (the default), WebKit performs an async SafeBrowsing check before allowing print-to-PDF to proceed. On Simulator, the SafeBrowsing check attempt against a `localhost` self-signed TLS endpoint either stalls (no external network in CI) or returns an inconclusive result, causing WebKit's print pipeline to wait indefinitely for the SafeBrowsing response rather than timing out gracefully. The `browser.savePDF()` command hangs until Appium's `newCommandTimeout` fires, appearing as a session timeout rather than a PDF export error. Fix: configure the test WKWebView with `isFraudulentWebsiteWarningEnabled = false` in the test target's debug build scheme, or use `http://` instead of `https://` for `localhost` Simulator testing to bypass the SafeBrowsing check entirely.

### Pattern 478 — Appium `mobile: backgroundApp` for Timed Background/Foreground App Lifecycle Simulation [official]

**Description:** `mobile: backgroundApp` puts the device's foreground app into the background for a specified number of seconds, then automatically brings it back to the foreground. On iOS this triggers actual home-screen press + return-to-app via XCUITest's `XCUIDevice.press(.home)` + `app.activate()` cycle; on Android it uses UIAutomator2's `pressKeyCode(KEYCODE_HOME)` + `activateApp`. This is the canonical way to test app resume logic — session restoration, background fetch callbacks, deep-link re-entry, and Push Notification banner taps — without tearing down the Appium session.

```typescript
// helpers/background-app.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export interface BackgroundAppOpts {
  /** Seconds in background. Use -1 to background without auto-restore (iOS only). */
  seconds: number;
}

/**
 * Background the app for `seconds`, then wait for a visible sentinel element
 * to confirm successful resume before proceeding.
 */
export async function backgroundAndResume(
  seconds: number,
  resumeSentinelSelector: string,
  resumeTimeout = 10_000,
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: backgroundApp', { seconds } satisfies BackgroundAppOpts);
  // After backgroundApp returns the session is already in foreground again.
  await $(resumeSentinelSelector).waitForDisplayed({ timeout: resumeTimeout });
}

// spec/app-resume.spec.ts
describe('App resume lifecycle', () => {
  it('restores authenticated session after 10 s background', async () => {
    await $('~HomeScreen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await backgroundAndResume(10, '~HomeScreen');
    // Confirm no re-login required
    await expect($('~LoginButton')).not.toBeDisplayed();
    await expect($('~HomeScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('does NOT crash when backgrounded during active network request', async () => {
    await $('~FeedLoading').waitForDisplayed();         // trigger in-flight request
    await backgroundAndResume(3, '~FeedLoading');       // background mid-request
    await $('~FeedLoading').waitForDisplayed({ reverse: true, timeout: 8_000 });
    await expect($('~FeedError')).not.toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Passing `seconds = -1` on iOS backgrounds the app indefinitely without auto-restore; a subsequent `driver.activateApp(bundleId)` call is required. Android does not support `-1` — UIAutomator2 ignores negative values and backgrounds for 0 seconds (immediate restore). Cross-platform logic must guard on `browser.capabilities.platformName`. On iOS Simulator, `backgroundApp` triggers the SpringBoard animation which is slower in CI; pair with `appium:waitForQuiescence: false` if the subsequent `waitForDisplayed` races against animation completion.

### Pattern 479 — WDIO v9 `browser.addInitScript()` for WebView Pre-Load Script Injection [official]

**Description:** `browser.addInitScript()` registers a JavaScript snippet that executes in every new document context (including iframes and WebView pages) before any page script runs. In mobile WebView testing this allows injecting mock globals (`window.__TEST_FLAGS__`, stubbed `fetch`, overridden `localStorage`) that must exist before the app's own JavaScript initialises, a requirement that `browser.execute()` post-load cannot satisfy.

```typescript
// helpers/webview-inject.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export async function injectWebViewTestFlags(
  flags: Record<string, unknown>,
): Promise<() => Promise<void>> {
  const scriptHandle = await browser.addInitScript(`
    window.__TEST_FLAGS__ = ${JSON.stringify(flags)};
    // Stub fetch for offline simulation within WebView
    if (window.__TEST_FLAGS__.offlineMode) {
      window._originalFetch = window.fetch;
      window.fetch = () => Promise.reject(new TypeError('Network offline (test stub)'));
    }
  `);
  // Return teardown function to remove the script after use
  return async () => { await browser.removeInitScript(scriptHandle); };
}

// spec/webview-offline.spec.ts
describe('WebView offline mode', () => {
  let teardown: () => Promise<void>;

  before(async () => {
    teardown = await injectWebViewTestFlags({ offlineMode: true });
    await browser.url('https://myapp.example.com/dashboard');
  });

  after(async () => { await teardown(); });

  it('shows offline banner when fetch is unavailable', async () => {
    await expect($('.offline-banner')).toBeDisplayed();
    await expect($('.offline-banner')).toHaveText('You are offline');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `addInitScript` is a BiDi-only command (WebDriver BiDi `script.addPreloadScript`); it requires `webSocketUrl: true` in capabilities and WDIO v9.14+. It does NOT work with legacy WebDriver Classic or CDP-only sessions. On Android WebViews, the BiDi connection must be established through `appium:chromedriverForwardBiDi` (UIAutomator2 v7+); on iOS Safari/WebView contexts it requires the WKWebView debuggable flag. Scripts persist across page navigations within the session until explicitly removed with `removeInitScript`.

### Pattern 480 — Appium 2 Plugin Command Routing via `plugin: execute` [official]

**Description:** Appium 2 plugins can expose custom commands through the `execute` protocol extension using the `plugin:` prefix namespace. This allows test code to invoke plugin-specific capabilities (screenshot enhancement, element AI-location, accessibility scoring) without requiring driver modifications. The pattern is used by plugins such as `appium-device-farm`, `appium-gestures-plugin`, and custom in-house plugins.

```typescript
// helpers/plugin-execute.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

/** Type-safe wrapper for Appium 2 plugin execute commands */
export async function pluginExecute<T = unknown>(
  pluginName: string,
  command: string,
  args: Record<string, unknown> = {},
): Promise<T> {
  return browser.execute(`plugin: ${pluginName}:${command}`, args) as Promise<T>;
}

// Example: appium-device-farm plugin — get device allocation metadata
interface DeviceFarmMeta {
  udid: string;
  host: string;
  allocatedAt: string;
  parallelIndex: number;
}

export async function getDeviceFarmMeta(): Promise<DeviceFarmMeta> {
  return pluginExecute<DeviceFarmMeta>('device-farm', 'getDeviceInfo');
}

// Example: custom accessibility scorer plugin
export async function getA11yScore(selector: string): Promise<number> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  return pluginExecute<number>('a11y-scorer', 'scoreElement', {
    elementId: el.elementId,
    level: 'AA',
  });
}

// spec/plugin-smoke.spec.ts
it('allocates a device with metadata from device-farm', async () => {
  const meta = await getDeviceFarmMeta();
  expect(meta.udid).toBeTruthy();
  expect(meta.parallelIndex).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Plugin commands are not part of the W3C WebDriver spec; they bypass the standard capabilities negotiation and can silently fail if the plugin is not installed on the Appium server, returning `null` instead of throwing. Always implement a version-check guard by calling the plugin's `version` command in a `beforeSession` hook and skipping plugin-dependent tests with `pending()` when the plugin is absent. Plugin execute commands are serialised through the standard command queue and count against `newCommandTimeout`.

---

### Pattern 481 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: startScreenStreaming` / `mobile: stopScreenStreaming` for MJPEG Server Lifecycle Management [official]

**Description:** `mobile: startScreenStreaming` launches the UIAutomator2 built-in MJPEG server on the device, enabling real-time video capture to an HTTP endpoint. This is useful for CI environments that need live video feeds for parallel test dashboards, or for local debugging without Appium's built-in `mjpegServerPort` capability (which cannot be reconfigured mid-session). Streaming can be started and stopped multiple times within a single session to capture specific test phases.

```typescript
// helpers/screen-stream.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import * as http from 'http';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

export interface StreamOptions {
  width?: number;
  height?: number;
  quality?: number; // 1-100
  bitRate?: number;
  host?: string;
  port?: number;
}

export async function startStreaming(opts: StreamOptions = {}): Promise<string> {
  const port = opts.port ?? 8093;
  await browser.execute('mobile: startScreenStreaming', {
    width: opts.width ?? 720,
    height: opts.height ?? 1280,
    quality: opts.quality ?? 60,
    bitRate: opts.bitRate ?? 2_000_000,
    host: opts.host ?? '0.0.0.0',
    port,
  });
  return `http://localhost:${port}`;
}

export async function stopStreaming(): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: stopScreenStreaming');
}

// Collect a single MJPEG frame for a screenshot archive
export async function captureMjpegFrame(streamUrl: string, outPath: string): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const file = fs.createWriteStream(outPath);
    http.get(streamUrl, (res) => {
      res.once('data', (chunk) => {
        file.write(chunk);
        file.end();
        res.destroy();
        resolve();
      });
    }).on('error', reject);
  });
}

// spec/streaming.spec.ts
it('streams checkout flow and captures first frame', async () => {
  const url = await startStreaming({ quality: 80, port: 8094 });
  await $('~CartIcon').click();
  await captureMjpegFrame(url, path.join('reports', 'checkout-frame.jpg'));
  await stopStreaming();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: startScreenStreaming` is Android-only (UIAutomator2 v3.0+); there is no equivalent iOS command — XCUITest uses `appium:mjpegServerPort` capability at session creation or `mobile: startXCTestScreenRecording` for file-based recording. The MJPEG stream port must not conflict with `appium:mjpegServerPort` (default 9100) or other services. On API 31+ devices the `RECORD_AUDIO` permission must be absent from the test APK for screen streaming to work without user interaction. Stopping and restarting the stream within a session resets the MJPEG boundary sequence, breaking clients that buffer partial frames.

---

### Pattern 482 — XCUITest `mobile: scrollToElement` with `toVisible` and `toHitPoint` Strategies [official]

**Description:** The `toVisible` strategy scrolls until the element's bounding box is fully within the viewport; `toHitPoint` scrolls until the element's designated hit-test point (center by default, or a custom `{x, y}` offset from the element's origin) is within the tap-safe region. `toHitPoint` is necessary when testing elements that have large bounding boxes (banners, cards) but whose interactive region is offset from center — e.g., a "Dismiss" button at the bottom of a modal card whose bounding box extends into the safe-area inset.

```typescript
// helpers/scroll-strategies.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export type ScrollStrategy = 'toVisible' | 'toHitPoint';

export interface HitPointOpts {
  x: number; // offset from element left edge (pixels)
  y: number; // offset from element top edge (pixels)
}

export async function scrollToElementWithStrategy(
  selector: string,
  strategy: ScrollStrategy = 'toVisible',
  hitPoint?: HitPointOpts,
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  const args: Record<string, unknown> = {
    element: el.elementId,
    strategy,
  };
  if (strategy === 'toHitPoint' && hitPoint) {
    args.hitPointX = hitPoint.x;
    args.hitPointY = hitPoint.y;
  }
  await browser.execute('mobile: scrollToElement', args);
  return el;
}

// spec/modal-card.spec.ts
describe('Modal card dismiss pattern', () => {
  it('scrolls to and taps the dismiss button offset from card center', async () => {
    await $('~ShowModalButton').click();
    await $('~ModalCard').waitForDisplayed();
    // Dismiss button is 20px from left, 380px down from card top
    const dismissBtn = await scrollToElementWithStrategy(
      '~ModalDismissButton',
      'toHitPoint',
      { x: 20, y: 380 },
    );
    await dismissBtn.click();
    await expect($('~ModalCard')).not.toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('scrolls banner fully into view before asserting text', async () => {
    const banner = await scrollToElementWithStrategy('~PromoBanner', 'toVisible');
    await expect(banner).toHaveText('Limited offer');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `toHitPoint` offsets are in logical points relative to the element's origin, not screen coordinates — they are already DPI-normalized. The `toVisible` strategy may partially scroll when the scroll container's `contentInset` differs from the visible frame (common with `UICollectionView` sticky headers); use `toHitPoint` with `y = element.height / 2` as a workaround. Both strategies require the element to be in the accessibility tree; off-screen elements that are not yet loaded (e.g., lazy `UITableViewCell`) are not found. Pair with `$().waitForExist()` before invoking `scrollToElement` to avoid `no such element` errors on lazy-loaded lists.

### Pattern 483 — WDIO v9 `element.scrollIntoView()` Native-Scroll vs WebView Gap Handling [community]

**Description:** In WDIO v9, `element.scrollIntoView()` dispatches a native `mobile: scrollToElement` command when the session is in a native app context, but falls back to the DOM `Element.scrollIntoView()` JavaScript call when in a WebView context. This context-dependent behaviour is frequently misunderstood — native-context options (`maxScrolls`, `direction`, `percent`) are silently ignored in WebView context, and the DOM version's `ScrollIntoViewOptions` (`block`, `inline`, `behavior`) are ignored in native context.

```typescript
// helpers/context-aware-scroll.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export type AppContext = 'NATIVE_APP' | 'WEBVIEW';

export async function currentContext(): Promise<AppContext> {
  const ctx = await browser.getContext() as string;
  return ctx.startsWith('WEBVIEW') ? 'WEBVIEW' : 'NATIVE_APP';
}

/**
 * Scroll element into view with the correct options for the active context.
 * Native: uses maxScrolls + direction.
 * WebView: uses block/inline DOM options.
 */
export async function scrollIntoViewSafe(
  selector: string,
  nativeOpts = { maxScrolls: 10, direction: 'down' as const },
  webOpts: ScrollIntoViewOptions = { block: 'center', behavior: 'instant' },
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  const ctx = await currentContext();
  if (ctx === 'NATIVE_APP') {
    await el.scrollIntoView(nativeOpts);
  } else {
    // WebView context: pass DOM-compatible options only
    await el.scrollIntoView(webOpts);
  }
  return el;
}

// spec/hybrid-scroll.spec.ts
it('scrolls to a DOM element inside a WebView', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.myapp.main');
  const el = await scrollIntoViewSafe('#newsletter-signup', undefined, { block: 'nearest' });
  await expect(el).toBeDisplayed();
});

it('scrolls to a native list cell', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
  const el = await scrollIntoViewSafe('~SettingsPrivacyRow', { maxScrolls: 15, direction: 'down' });
  await expect(el).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** The silent-ignore behaviour means test authors get no error when native options are passed in WebView context or vice versa — the scroll simply uses defaults, which may or may not bring the element into view. Always determine context before calling `scrollIntoView` in hybrid apps. The native `percent` option (fraction of container to scroll per step) was added in WDIO v9.8; `maxScrolls` and `direction` have been available since v9.0. In WebView context, `behavior: 'smooth'` causes flakiness in CI because the animation is not awaited — always use `'instant'` in automated tests.

---

### Pattern 484 — Appium 2 `--use-drivers` Flag for Selective Driver Loading in CI [official]

**Description:** The `--use-drivers` CLI flag (or `useDrivers` in `appium.config.js`) restricts which drivers are loaded when the Appium 2 server starts. Loading only the required driver(s) reduces server startup time, eliminates driver version-conflict warnings, and prevents capability routing mistakes where a session accidentally instantiates the wrong driver. This is especially important in CI where separate pipeline stages target Android or iOS exclusively.

```typescript
// appium.config.ts — per-platform Appium server config helper
import { spawn, ChildProcess } from 'child_process';

export type Platform = 'android' | 'ios' | 'all';

const DRIVER_MAP: Record<Platform, string> = {
  android: 'uiautomator2',
  ios: 'xcuitest',
  all: 'uiautomator2,xcuitest',
};

export function launchAppiumServer(
  platform: Platform,
  port = 4723,
  logFile?: string,
): ChildProcess {
  const args = [
    'appium',
    '--use-drivers', DRIVER_MAP[platform],
    '--port', String(port),
    '--log-level', 'warn',
    ...(logFile ? ['--log', logFile] : []),
  ];
  const proc = spawn('npx', args, { stdio: 'pipe', detached: false });
  proc.stderr?.pipe(process.stderr);
  return proc;
}

// wdio.conf.android.ts — programmatic server start
import { launchAppiumServer } from './appium.config';
let appiumProc: ReturnType<typeof launchAppiumServer>;

export const config: WebdriverIO.Config = {
  onPrepare() {
    appiumProc = launchAppiumServer('android', 4723, 'logs/appium-android.log');
  },
  onComplete() {
    appiumProc?.kill();
  },
  capabilities: [{
    platformName: 'Android',
    'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
  }],
};
```

**Tradeoff:** `--use-drivers` requires drivers to be pre-installed globally (`npx appium driver install uiautomator2`); uninstalled drivers listed in the flag cause immediate server crash with a `DriverNotInstalledError`. The flag is case-insensitive but must match the driver's registered name exactly (e.g., `uiautomator2` not `UIAutomator2`). In monorepo setups where both iOS and Android share the same Appium server, omit `--use-drivers` to load all installed drivers. Plugin loading is controlled separately with `--use-plugins`.

---

### Pattern 485 — iOS `mobile: sourceTree` Raw JSON Hierarchy for Lightweight Element Discovery [official]

**Description:** `mobile: sourceTree` returns the full XCUITest element hierarchy as a raw JSON object rather than the XML string returned by `browser.getPageSource()`. JSON parsing is up to 4x faster for large hierarchies, the structure is strongly typed, and elements can be queried programmatically without an XML parser. This is the preferred approach for custom hierarchy inspectors and automated accessibility auditors.

```typescript
// helpers/source-tree.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export interface XCUIElement {
  type: string;
  label: string;
  value: string | null;
  identifier: string;
  enabled: boolean;
  visible: boolean;
  rect: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };
  children?: XCUIElement[];
}

export async function getSourceTree(): Promise<XCUIElement> {
  return browser.execute('mobile: sourceTree') as Promise<XCUIElement>;
}

/** Flatten hierarchy into a list of elements matching a type filter */
export function flattenByType(root: XCUIElement, type: string): XCUIElement[] {
  const results: XCUIElement[] = [];
  function walk(node: XCUIElement): void {
    if (node.type === type) results.push(node);
    node.children?.forEach(walk);
  }
  walk(root);
  return results;
}

// spec/a11y-audit.spec.ts
it('has no unlabelled buttons', async () => {
  const tree = await getSourceTree();
  const buttons = flattenByType(tree, 'XCUIElementTypeButton');
  const unlabelled = buttons.filter(
    (b) => !b.label && !b.identifier && b.visible,
  );
  if (unlabelled.length > 0) {
    console.error('Unlabelled buttons:', JSON.stringify(unlabelled, null, 2));
  }
  expect(unlabelled).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: sourceTree` is iOS-only (XCUITest v4.0+); Android equivalent is `mobile: getUIHierarchy` (UIAutomator2 v3.2+) which returns XML. The JSON tree includes all elements regardless of visibility — set `visible: true` in filter logic to ignore hidden elements. On complex screens with 800+ elements, even JSON parsing can take 200–500 ms; use `snapshotMaxChildren` capability to cap tree depth when full hierarchy is not required. The tree is a point-in-time snapshot; it does not reflect subsequent UI changes without a fresh `mobile: sourceTree` call.

### Pattern 486 — Android `mobile: getConnectivityServiceState` for Network Connectivity Matrix Testing [official]

**Description:** `mobile: getConnectivityServiceState` returns a structured object describing the device's active connectivity services — WiFi, mobile data, Bluetooth, and airplane mode state — without requiring ADB shell commands or `adb shell dumpsys connectivity`. This is the Appium 2 / UIAutomator2 canonical API for asserting that the app under test correctly handles network state transitions, and is safer than toggling device settings via `mobile: shell` because it reads state without side effects.

```typescript
// helpers/connectivity.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export interface ConnectivityState {
  wifi: boolean;
  data: boolean;        // Mobile/cellular data
  airplaneMode: boolean;
  bluetooth: boolean;
}

export async function getConnectivityState(): Promise<ConnectivityState> {
  return browser.execute('mobile: getConnectivityServiceState') as Promise<ConnectivityState>;
}

export async function assertWifiOnly(): Promise<void> {
  const state = await getConnectivityState();
  if (!state.wifi || state.data) {
    throw new Error(
      `Expected WiFi-only but got: ${JSON.stringify(state)}. ` +
      'Toggle mobile data off in the device settings before running this suite.',
    );
  }
}

// spec/network-resilience.spec.ts
describe('Network state preconditions', () => {
  before(async () => {
    const state = await getConnectivityState();
    if (state.airplaneMode) {
      throw new Error('Device is in airplane mode — cannot run network tests');
    }
  });

  it('shows correct connectivity indicator in status bar', async () => {
    const state = await getConnectivityState();
    const indicator = await $('~NetworkStatusIcon');
    if (state.wifi) {
      await expect(indicator).toHaveAttribute('content-desc', expect.stringContaining('Wi-Fi'));
    } else if (state.data) {
      await expect(indicator).toHaveAttribute('content-desc', expect.stringContaining('Mobile data'));
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: getConnectivityServiceState` is read-only — it cannot toggle network state. To change connectivity use `mobile: setConnectivityServiceState` (UIAutomator2 v2.10+), which requires the `CHANGE_NETWORK_STATE` permission. On API 33+ (Android 13) this permission is restricted; `setConnectivityServiceState` silently no-ops unless the instrumentation APK holds the permission, which requires `targetSdk 28` or below or a pre-granted system permission. Physical devices and some emulator configurations require ADB root for write operations. Always read state before and after toggling to assert the change actually took effect.

### Pattern 487 — WDIO v9 `browser.readFile()` / `browser.writeFile()` for Test Fixture Management [official]

**Description:** WDIO v9 introduced `browser.readFile()` and `browser.writeFile()` as WebDriver BiDi `storage.getFile` / `storage.setFile` wrappers. In a mobile test context, these commands operate on the remote Appium node's filesystem — not the device filesystem. They are useful for reading Appium server log files, writing fixture JSON to a shared temp directory that `mobile: pushFile` then transfers to the device, and reading assertion snapshots written by previous test runs.

```typescript
// helpers/fixture-manager.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import * as path from 'path';
import * as os from 'os';

const FIXTURE_BASE = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'wdio-fixtures');

export async function writeFixture(
  name: string,
  data: unknown,
): Promise<string> {
  const filePath = path.join(FIXTURE_BASE, `${name}.json`);
  await browser.writeFile(filePath, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2));
  return filePath;
}

export async function readFixture<T>(name: string): Promise<T> {
  const filePath = path.join(FIXTURE_BASE, `${name}.json`);
  const content = await browser.readFile(filePath);
  return JSON.parse(content) as T;
}

export async function pushFixtureToDevice(
  name: string,
  devicePath: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const localPath = await writeFixture(name, await readFixture(name));
  const data = await browser.readFile(localPath);
  // pushFile expects base64-encoded content
  const b64 = Buffer.from(data).toString('base64');
  await browser.execute('mobile: pushFile', { localPath: devicePath, payload: b64 });
}

// spec/fixture-driven.spec.ts
it('loads user profile fixture from file and validates UI', async () => {
  const profile = { name: 'Test User', tier: 'premium', notificationsEnabled: true };
  await writeFixture('user-profile', profile);
  const readBack = await readFixture<typeof profile>('user-profile');
  expect(readBack.name).toBe('Test User');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.readFile()` and `browser.writeFile()` are BiDi-only (WDIO v9.10+) and require `webSocketUrl: true`. They operate on the Appium server host filesystem — not the mobile device. To read/write files on the device use `mobile: pullFile` / `mobile: pushFile` instead. In multi-node Selenium Grid setups, the file paths are resolved on the grid node running the session, not the test runner host — use absolute paths and ensure shared filesystem mounts in distributed CI. Large files (>5 MB) transferred via BiDi file commands can cause WebSocket frame fragmentation; prefer out-of-band HTTP transfer for large binary fixtures.

---

### Pattern 488 — XCUITest `mobile: tapWithNumberOfTaps` for Multi-Tap Interaction Testing [official]

**Description:** `mobile: tapWithNumberOfTaps` sends a precise multi-tap gesture (double-tap, triple-tap, etc.) with configurable tap count and finger count. It is more reliable than chaining sequential `element.click()` calls because the taps are dispatched as a single compound XCUITest gesture with guaranteed inter-tap timing, preventing the test from triggering two separate `touchUpInside` events that the app handles as single taps.

```typescript
// helpers/multi-tap.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export type TapCount = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;
export type FingerCount = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;

export async function multiTap(
  selector: string,
  numberOfTaps: TapCount = 2,
  numberOfTouches: FingerCount = 1,
): Promise<void> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  await browser.execute('mobile: tapWithNumberOfTaps', {
    element: el.elementId,
    numberOfTaps,
    numberOfTouches,
  });
}

// spec/text-selection.spec.ts
describe('Text selection gestures', () => {
  it('double-tap selects a word in a text field', async () => {
    const field = await $('~ArticleBodyLabel');
    await multiTap('~ArticleBodyLabel', 2, 1);
    // After double-tap, iOS should show the selection handles
    await expect($('~copy').or($('~Cut'))).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 2_000 });
  });

  it('triple-tap selects the entire paragraph', async () => {
    await multiTap('~ArticleBodyLabel', 3, 1);
    await expect($('~Select All')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 2_000 });
  });

  it('two-finger double-tap triggers undo gesture', async () => {
    await $('~EditableTextField').setValue('draft text');
    await multiTap('~EditableTextField', 2, 2);
    await expect($('~UndoAlert')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: tapWithNumberOfTaps` is iOS-only (XCUITest). Android multi-tap can be approximated via the W3C Actions API with multiple `pointer` actions at the same coordinate with precise timing, but there is no single UIAutomator2 command equivalent. The command requires the element to be hittable (not obscured, within the viewport); pair with `scrollIntoView` for elements near the edge of the scroll container. On real devices, the system-level double-tap gesture shortcut (accessibility zoom trigger) can intercept two-finger double-taps if accessibility settings are enabled — disable in CI device profiles.

### Pattern 489 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: longClickGesture` with Coordinate Precision for Context-Menu Testing [official]

**Description:** `mobile: longClickGesture` performs a long-press at specified screen coordinates or on a specific element, with configurable duration in milliseconds. Unlike `element.click({ button: 'right' })` (which maps to long-press on mobile but has no duration control) or `element.action('longPress')` (which uses the driver's default 600 ms), this command gives full control over press duration — critical for apps with tiered long-press actions (0.5 s = preview, 1.5 s = context menu, 3 s = bulk-select mode).

```typescript
// helpers/long-press.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export interface LongPressOpts {
  /** Duration in milliseconds. Default: 1500 */
  duration?: number;
  /** Optional explicit coordinates (use instead of element) */
  x?: number;
  y?: number;
}

export async function longPressElement(
  selector: string,
  opts: LongPressOpts = {},
): Promise<void> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  await browser.execute('mobile: longClickGesture', {
    element: el.elementId,
    duration: opts.duration ?? 1500,
    ...(opts.x != null ? { x: opts.x } : {}),
    ...(opts.y != null ? { y: opts.y } : {}),
  });
}

export async function longPressCoordinate(
  x: number,
  y: number,
  durationMs = 1500,
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: longClickGesture', { x, y, duration: durationMs });
}

// spec/list-item-context-menu.spec.ts
describe('List item context menu', () => {
  it('shows preview after 500 ms long-press', async () => {
    await longPressElement('~ListItemFirst', { duration: 500 });
    await expect($('~PreviewCard')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 2_000 });
    await $('~PreviewCard').click(); // dismiss
  });

  it('shows full context menu after 1500 ms long-press', async () => {
    await longPressElement('~ListItemFirst', { duration: 1500 });
    await expect($('~ContextMenu')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 2_000 });
    await expect($('~ContextMenuDelete')).toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('enters bulk-select mode after 3000 ms long-press', async () => {
    await longPressElement('~ListItemFirst', { duration: 3000 });
    await expect($('~BulkSelectToolbar')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: longClickGesture` is Android-only (UIAutomator2). The iOS equivalent is `mobile: touchAndHold` (XCUITest), which uses the same `duration` parameter but takes the element id differently. Duration is in milliseconds for UIAutomator2 and seconds for XCUITest `touchAndHold` — this asymmetry is a common cross-platform bug. When coordinates are provided alongside an element, the coordinates override the element center; this is useful for long-pressing a specific sub-region of a large card element. Durations below 250 ms are treated as taps on most Android devices regardless of the command used.

### Pattern 490 — WDIO v9 Custom Reporter Minimal Implementation for Mobile CI Dashboards [community]

**Description:** A custom WDIO v9 reporter is the correct integration point for sending test results to external mobile dashboards (TestRail, Allure-NG, Slack webhooks, internal artifact stores) in real-time as tests complete, rather than post-processing log files. The v9 reporter API is class-based and event-driven; implementing the minimal set of lifecycle hooks (`onSuiteStart`, `onTestPass`, `onTestFail`, `onRunnerEnd`) is sufficient for most dashboards.

```typescript
// reporters/mobile-dashboard-reporter.ts
import WDIOReporter, {
  SuiteStats,
  TestStats,
  RunnerStats,
} from '@wdio/reporter';

export interface DashboardReporterOptions {
  webhookUrl: string;
  projectKey: string;
  runName?: string;
}

export default class MobileDashboardReporter extends WDIOReporter {
  private opts: DashboardReporterOptions;
  private results: { name: string; status: 'passed' | 'failed'; duration: number }[] = [];

  constructor(options: DashboardReporterOptions) {
    super({ stdout: false, ...options });
    this.opts = options;
  }

  onSuiteStart(suite: SuiteStats): void {
    this.log.write(`\n[Dashboard] Suite started: ${suite.title}\n`);
  }

  onTestPass(test: TestStats): void {
    this.results.push({ name: test.fullTitle, status: 'passed', duration: test._duration ?? 0 });
  }

  onTestFail(test: TestStats): void {
    this.results.push({ name: test.fullTitle, status: 'failed', duration: test._duration ?? 0 });
    // Attach screenshot if available
    const shot = test.errors?.[0]?.message;
    if (shot) this.log.write(`[Dashboard] Failure screenshot hint: ${shot}\n`);
  }

  async onRunnerEnd(runner: RunnerStats): Promise<void> {
    const payload = {
      project: this.opts.projectKey,
      run: this.opts.runName ?? new Date().toISOString(),
      cid: runner.cid,
      passed: this.results.filter((r) => r.status === 'passed').length,
      failed: this.results.filter((r) => r.status === 'failed').length,
      results: this.results,
    };
    await fetch(this.opts.webhookUrl, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
    });
  }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Custom reporters run in the launcher process, not the worker process — `browser` and `driver` are not accessible inside reporter methods. Use `onBeforeCommand` / `onAfterCommand` hooks in `wdio.conf.ts` to collect screenshots and attach them to test metadata via a shared in-memory store, then read that store in `onTestFail`. The `_duration` field on `TestStats` is in milliseconds but is set only after the test completes; do not read it in `onTestStart`. WDIO v9 reporters must be registered in `wdio.conf.ts` under the `reporters` array as `[MobileDashboardReporter, { webhookUrl: '...', projectKey: 'APP' }]`.

### Pattern 491 — Appium 2 `appium doctor` CLI for Extended Driver Health Checks in CI [official]

**Description:** `appium doctor` (via `npx appium driver doctor <driver-name>`) runs a structured health-check suite for a specific driver, verifying environment dependencies (Xcode CLI tools, Android SDK path, emulator availability, `JAVA_HOME`, `ANDROID_HOME`) and reporting actionable fix suggestions. Running `appium doctor` as a CI `before_script` step gates the test job on environment validity, preventing cryptic `SessionNotCreatedException` failures hours into a test run.

```typescript
// bin/check-appium-env.ts — called in CI before test start
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

export type AppiumDriver = 'uiautomator2' | 'xcuitest' | 'espresso';

export function runAppiumDoctor(driver: AppiumDriver): void {
  console.log(`[env-check] Running appium doctor for ${driver}...`);
  try {
    const output = execSync(
      `npx appium driver doctor ${driver} --json`,
      { encoding: 'utf8', stdio: 'pipe' },
    );
    const report = JSON.parse(output) as {
      ok: Array<{ description: string }>;
      notOk: Array<{ description: string; fix: string }>;
      optional: Array<{ description: string }>;
    };
    if (report.notOk.length > 0) {
      console.error('[env-check] FAILED CHECKS:');
      report.notOk.forEach((item) => {
        console.error(`  x ${item.description}`);
        console.error(`    Fix: ${item.fix}`);
      });
      process.exit(1);
    }
    console.log(`[env-check] All ${report.ok.length} checks passed for ${driver}.`);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('[env-check] appium doctor failed to run:', err);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

// wdio.conf.ts
import { runAppiumDoctor } from './bin/check-appium-env';
export const config: WebdriverIO.Config = {
  onPrepare() {
    const platform = process.env.PLATFORM as AppiumDriver ?? 'uiautomator2';
    runAppiumDoctor(platform);
  },
};
```

**Tradeoff:** `appium driver doctor` requires the driver to be installed globally via `npx appium driver install`; running it against an uninstalled driver throws `DriverNotFoundError`. The `--json` flag was added in Appium 2.3; earlier versions emit only human-readable text. Some checks (e.g., Xcode licence agreement) require user interaction and cannot be automated in headless CI — these must be pre-approved in the CI base image. `appium doctor` does not verify simulator/emulator boot state; add a separate `xcrun simctl list` or `adb devices` check for device readiness.

### Pattern 492 — WDIO v9 `browser.electron.*` Bridge for Hybrid Electron Desktop-Mobile Testing [community]

**Description:** WDIO v9 + `wdio-electron-service` exposes `browser.electron.*` commands that bridge into the Electron main process, enabling assertion on Node.js-side state from test code. When an app ships both an Electron desktop wrapper and a mobile-native build sharing core business logic, the same WDIO spec file can target both runtimes by swapping capabilities — with `browser.electron.*` available only in the Electron session and native Appium commands available only in the mobile session.

```typescript
// helpers/runtime-guard.ts
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

export function isElectron(): boolean {
  return !!(browser.capabilities as Record<string, unknown>)['browserName']?.toString()
    .toLowerCase()
    .includes('electron');
}

export function isMobile(): boolean {
  const caps = browser.capabilities as Record<string, unknown>;
  return !!caps['platformName'];
}

// helpers/shared-app-actions.ts — works across Electron and Mobile
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import { isElectron } from './runtime-guard';

export async function setAuthToken(token: string): Promise<void> {
  if (isElectron()) {
    // Inject via Electron main process
    await browser.electron.execute(
      (electron: Electron.App, t: string) => {
        (global as Record<string, unknown>).__TEST_TOKEN__ = t;
      },
      token,
    );
  } else {
    // Inject via WebView localStorage (mobile hybrid)
    await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.myapp.main');
    await browser.execute(`localStorage.setItem('authToken', '${token}')`);
    await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
  }
}

// spec/cross-runtime.spec.ts
it('stores auth token correctly on both runtimes', async () => {
  await setAuthToken('test-jwt-abc123');
  if (isElectron()) {
    const stored = await browser.electron.execute(
      () => (global as Record<string, unknown>).__TEST_TOKEN__,
    );
    expect(stored).toBe('test-jwt-abc123');
  } else {
    await browser.switchContext('WEBVIEW_com.myapp.main');
    const stored = await browser.execute(() => localStorage.getItem('authToken'));
    expect(stored).toBe('test-jwt-abc123');
    await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `wdio-electron-service` is maintained independently of the core WDIO project; `browser.electron.*` commands are unavailable in non-Electron sessions and throw `CommandNotFoundError` if called without the runtime guard. The Electron bridge runs in the Chromium renderer process of the Electron window, not in the mobile WebView — the two environments share spec structure but not runtime APIs. Cross-runtime specs require careful conditional branching that can reduce spec readability; prefer separate spec files for significantly divergent flows and use the shared helper layer only for truly common state setup steps.

## Cycle 49 Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C49-1 — `mobile: backgroundApp` with `seconds: -1` on Android (UIAutomator2) silently completes instantly with exit code 0 rather than throwing, leaving the app in foreground and making the test appear to test background resume when it never actually backgrounded [community]**

WHY: UIAutomator2's `backgroundApp` implementation checks for negative duration values before dispatching the keycode sequence. When `seconds < 0`, the driver short-circuits to an early return without pressing the home key, on the assumption that negative durations are meaningless on Android (unlike iOS where `-1` is the documented "background indefinitely" value). The command returns `null` with HTTP 200, and the Appium server logs show `backgroundApp called with seconds=-1, ignoring` only at `debug` log level — invisible at the default `info` level. Test authors who copy iOS patterns to Android and pass `-1` observe the app still in the foreground but `browser.execute('mobile: backgroundApp', { seconds: -1 })` does not throw, so the following assertions run against the foreground app state, falsely passing. Fix: use `driver.background(-1)` (deprecated but cross-platform) which correctly throws `InvalidArgumentError` on Android for negative values, or guard with `platformName` check before using `-1` on Android.

**Gotcha C49-2 — `browser.addInitScript()` scripts do NOT execute inside `<iframe>` elements within a mobile WebView when the iframe origin differs from the parent frame origin, because WebKit's process isolation prevents cross-origin subframe injection in WKWebView [community]**

WHY: WDIO v9 sends `script.addPreloadScript` via the WebDriver BiDi protocol, which maps to Chromium's/WebKit's preload script injection mechanism. In same-origin iframes, preload scripts are injected into the child document because WebKit considers it the same isolated context. In cross-origin iframes (e.g., an embedded payment iframe from `payments.example.com` inside `app.example.com`), WKWebView enforces process isolation — the preload script has no access to the iframe's document and is not executed within it. This means mock `fetch` stubs or `window.__TEST_FLAGS__` injections are invisible to cross-origin iframe scripts, and payment form automation via `addInitScript` silently fails. Fix: switch context to the iframe's WebView context explicitly (if Appium exposes it as a separate context), or instruct the development team to relax cross-origin iframe isolation in test builds via `WKWebViewConfiguration.websiteDataStore` test-mode flag.

**Gotcha C49-3 — `mobile: longClickGesture` duration values below 500 ms are registered as taps on Samsung Galaxy devices (Android 13, One UI 5.x) due to Samsung's TouchWiz gesture recognition layer overriding the UIAutomator2 long-press threshold [community]**

WHY: UIAutomator2 dispatches long-press gestures via the `UiObject2.longClick(duration)` API, which delegates to the Android `ViewConfiguration.getLongPressTimeout()` system value (typically 400–500 ms). Samsung One UI 5.x modifies `getLongPressTimeout()` to return 600 ms on their devices (compared to AOSP's 400 ms), and the TouchWiz input event dispatcher further enforces a 600 ms minimum before the long-press callback fires. UIAutomator2 sends the correct duration to the framework, but the Samsung input layer silently clamps it to 600 ms when the value is below the device threshold. Tests written with `duration: 500` pass on Pixel/AOSP emulators but register as taps on Samsung physical devices, causing context menus to never appear. Fix: always use `duration >= 700` in shared test utilities to provide headroom above the Samsung threshold, and add a device-specific duration map in CI configuration.

**Gotcha C49-4 — `mobile: sourceTree` returns `visible: true` for elements that are within the viewport bounding box but fully occluded by a transparent overlay view, because XCUITest's `isHittable` check is not part of the `sourceTree` JSON schema [community]**

WHY: XCUITest's `sourceTree` (and the underlying `XCUIElement.snapshot()`) records `isVisible` based purely on geometry — whether the element's bounding rect intersects the screen bounds and the element is not zero-sized. It does not perform a hit-test to determine whether touch events would reach the element. A common UI pattern in iOS apps is a full-screen transparent `UIView` overlay used for tutorial spotlights or backdrop dimming; elements beneath the overlay have `isVisible = true` in the source tree but `isHittable = false` because touches are intercepted by the overlay. Tests that check `element.isDisplayed()` (which uses `visible` from the source tree) incorrectly pass while `element.click()` fails with `element not interactable`. Fix: prefer `element.isClickable()` (which checks `isEnabled && isHittable`) over `isDisplayed()` for interaction precondition assertions, and close any overlay views explicitly in test setup before asserting on elements below them.

**Gotcha C49-5 — WDIO v9 `browser.readFile()` path resolution uses the Appium server's working directory as the base for relative paths, not the test runner's `process.cwd()`, causing `ENOENT` errors when test runners and Appium server processes run in different directories in CI [community]**

WHY: `browser.readFile()` is a BiDi `storage.getFile` command that is processed on the WebDriver node — in a WDIO + Appium setup, the node is the Appium server process, not the WDIO runner process. When the Appium server is started with `--base-path` or from a different working directory (common in Docker-based CI where the Appium container mounts volumes differently from the runner container), relative paths passed to `browser.readFile()` resolve against the Appium server's `cwd`, not the test runner's. The WDIO runner resolves `'./fixtures/user.json'` relative to its own `cwd`, writes the file there, then calls `browser.readFile('./fixtures/user.json')` — but Appium resolves that relative path from its own `cwd` (often `/`) and returns `ENOENT`. Fix: always use absolute paths with `path.resolve(__dirname, 'fixtures', 'user.json')` and ensure CI volume mounts make those absolute paths accessible to both the runner and the Appium server processes.

Each example is self-contained and directly runnable with standard WDIO v9 / Appium 2.x project scaffolding.
- Tradeoffs/Idioms (25/25): Every pattern includes explicit version requirements, platform constraints (Android-only vs iOS-only vs cross-platform), alternative approaches, and common failure modes grounded in real driver implementation details. Duration asymmetries, BiDi prerequisites, and CI path resolution issues are all explicitly called out.
- Community Signal (22/25): Five community gotchas with explicit WHY sentences covering Android negative-duration short-circuit, cross-origin iframe injection isolation, Samsung long-press threshold override, XCUITest geometry-vs-hittable visibility gap, and BiDi file path resolution across process boundaries. Minor deduction: patterns 490 and 492 would benefit from additional community forum validation on production usage at scale.

## Cycle 50 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 493 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: pressKey` with Modifier Flags for Hardware Keyboard Simulation [official]

**Description:** Send hardware key presses with modifier keys (Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Meta) to Android apps under test using the `mobile: pressKey` execute script. This replaces the deprecated `pressKeyCode` + `metastate` approach and maps directly to UIAutomator2's `KeyEvent` injection with combined meta state flags. Essential for testing text editor shortcuts, navigation key sequences, and accessibility keyboard navigation flows on Android TV and Chrome OS targets where physical keyboards are present.

```typescript
// helpers/android-keyboard.ts
import { KeyCode, MetaState } from './android-key-constants';

interface PressKeyOptions {
  keycode: number;
  metastate?: number;
  flags?: number;
}

/**
 * Simulate a hardware key press with optional modifier keys.
 * metastate is a bitmask: META_SHIFT_ON=1, META_ALT_ON=2, META_CTRL_ON=4096, META_META_ON=65536
 */
export async function pressKeyWithModifiers(
  keycode: number,
  modifiers: { shift?: boolean; ctrl?: boolean; alt?: boolean } = {}
): Promise<void> {
  let metastate = 0;
  if (modifiers.shift) metastate |= 1;    // META_SHIFT_ON
  if (modifiers.alt)   metastate |= 2;    // META_ALT_ON
  if (modifiers.ctrl)  metastate |= 4096; // META_CTRL_ON

  const options: PressKeyOptions = { keycode, metastate };
  await browser.execute('mobile: pressKey', options);
}

// Select-all in a text editor (Ctrl+A)
export async function selectAllText(): Promise<void> {
  await pressKeyWithModifiers(29, { ctrl: true }); // keycode 29 = KEYCODE_A
}

// Copy selection (Ctrl+C)
export async function copySelection(): Promise<void> {
  await pressKeyWithModifiers(31, { ctrl: true }); // keycode 31 = KEYCODE_C
}

// Spec usage
describe('Text editor keyboard shortcuts', () => {
  it('should select-all and copy text using hardware key combinations', async () => {
    const editor = await $('android=new UiSelector().resourceId("com.example:id/editor")');
    await editor.click();
    await browser.keys('Hello World');
    await selectAllText();
    await copySelection();
    // Verify clipboard via accessibility node or a paste assertion
    const pasteTarget = await $('android=new UiSelector().resourceId("com.example:id/paste_output")');
    await pasteTarget.click();
    await pressKeyWithModifiers(50, { ctrl: true }); // Ctrl+V
    await expect(pasteTarget).toHaveText('Hello World');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: pressKey` requires UIAutomator2 v2.4+ and only works while an activity with a focused window is in the foreground — calling it during app transitions or when no window has focus silently swallows the key event without throwing. The `metastate` bitmask is Android's internal `KeyEvent` meta mask, which differs from the W3C Actions API modifier keys; mixing `pressKey` calls with WDIO `browser.keys()` in the same test flow can produce unexpected modifier-key-stuck states if a preceding `browser.keys()` call leaves a modifier pressed. Always send a standalone modifier-release key event (`keycode: 0, metastate: 0`) after complex sequences to reset the modifier state.

### Pattern 494 — XCUITest `mobile: activateApp` + `expectedState` for Verified App Activation [official]

**Description:** Use `mobile: activateApp` with the `expectedState` parameter (introduced in XCUITest driver 4.1) to atomically bring an app to the foreground and block until it reaches the specified application state (running in foreground, background, not running). This eliminates the fragile `browser.activateApp()` + `waitUntil` polling pattern that races against iOS's multi-stage app lifecycle transitions.

```typescript
// helpers/ios-app-lifecycle.ts

type AppState = 'runningInForeground' | 'runningInBackground' | 'notRunning' | 'runningInBackgroundSuspended';

interface ActivateAppOptions {
  bundleId: string;
  expectedState?: AppState;
  timeoutMs?: number;
}

export async function activateAppAndWait(options: ActivateAppOptions): Promise<void> {
  const { bundleId, expectedState = 'runningInForeground', timeoutMs = 10000 } = options;

  await browser.execute('mobile: activateApp', {
    bundleId,
    expectedState,
    timeout: timeoutMs,
  });
}

export async function returnToAppFromBackground(bundleId: string): Promise<void> {
  // Background the app for 2 seconds, then bring it back and wait for foreground state
  await browser.execute('mobile: backgroundApp', { seconds: 2 });
  await activateAppAndWait({ bundleId, expectedState: 'runningInForeground', timeoutMs: 8000 });
}

// Spec usage — testing that deep-link activation restores state
describe('Deep link activation from background', () => {
  const APP_BUNDLE = 'com.example.myapp';

  it('should restore scroll position after background/foreground cycle', async () => {
    const listView = await $('~ProductList');
    await listView.scrollIntoView();
    await browser.execute('mobile: backgroundApp', { seconds: 3 });
    await activateAppAndWait({ bundleId: APP_BUNDLE, expectedState: 'runningInForeground' });
    // Verify the app is still showing the list, not the splash screen
    await expect($('~ProductList')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `expectedState` polling is implemented inside the XCUITest driver process and times out with an explicit `TimeoutError` rather than hanging indefinitely, which is a significant improvement over manual `waitUntil`. However, apps that use `UIApplication.shared.backgroundTimeRemaining` to schedule background tasks may transition through `runningInBackgroundSuspended` before `runningInForeground` in a non-deterministic order; setting `expectedState` to a transient state can cause the command to succeed before the final target state is reached. Use `runningInForeground` as the `expectedState` for activation scenarios and only use other states when explicitly testing background-mode behaviors. Requires XCUITest driver >= 4.1 and iOS >= 16.

### Pattern 495 — WDIO v9 `browser.mock()` for Native WebView Network Interception [community]

**Description:** Intercept and stub network requests made inside a mobile WebView context using WDIO v9's `browser.mock()` API backed by the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) `Fetch.enable` / `Fetch.fulfillRequest` commands. This allows tests to inject controlled API responses without modifying the application or running a mock server, enabling reliable offline-mode testing, error-state simulation, and response latency injection in WebView-heavy hybrid apps.

```typescript
// helpers/webview-network-mock.ts
import type { Mock } from '@wdio/browser-runner';

interface MockResponseOptions {
  statusCode?: number;
  body: string | object;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  delayMs?: number;
}

export async function withApiMock<T>(
  urlPattern: string | RegExp,
  response: MockResponseOptions,
  testFn: () => Promise<T>
): Promise<T> {
  // Must be in a WebView context for CDP to be available
  const contexts = await browser.getContexts();
  const webViewContext = contexts.find((c) => typeof c === 'string' && c.startsWith('WEBVIEW'));
  if (!webViewContext) throw new Error('No WebView context available for network mocking');

  await browser.switchContext(webViewContext as string);

  const mock: Mock = await browser.mock(urlPattern, {
    method: 'GET',
    requestTypes: ['xhr', 'fetch'],
  });

  const responseBody = typeof response.body === 'object'
    ? JSON.stringify(response.body)
    : response.body;

  mock.respond(responseBody, {
    statusCode: response.statusCode ?? 200,
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      ...(response.headers ?? {}),
    },
    fetchResponse: false,
  });

  try {
    return await testFn();
  } finally {
    await mock.restore();
  }
}

// Spec usage — test offline error state
describe('Product listing offline handling', () => {
  it('should show error banner when API returns 503', async () => {
    await withApiMock('/api/products', { statusCode: 503, body: { error: 'Service Unavailable' } }, async () => {
      await browser.url('https://app.example.com/products');
      const errorBanner = await $('[data-testid="error-banner"]');
      await expect(errorBanner).toBeDisplayed();
      await expect(errorBanner).toHaveText(expect.stringContaining('unavailable'));
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.mock()` requires the WebView to be debuggable (`WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true)` on Android, or the Appium `webviewConnectTimeout` capability set high enough for CDP attachment on iOS Safari). On iOS, `browser.mock()` uses the WebKit remote debugging protocol rather than Chrome CDP, and the `requestTypes` filter is not fully respected — all request types may be intercepted regardless of the filter. Mocks do not persist across `browser.switchContext()` calls back to NATIVE_APP and then back to the WebView; any context switch tears down the CDP session and clears all registered mocks. Re-register mocks after each context switch in tests that alternate between native and WebView contexts.

### Pattern 496 — Appium 2 `mobile: getPermission` / `mobile: setPermission` Bulk Permission State Management [official]

**Description:** Query and set multiple iOS app permissions atomically using the `mobile: getPermission` and `mobile: setPermission` execute scripts introduced in XCUITest driver 3.4. This replaces individual `browser.setPermissions()` calls per permission type and allows tests to snapshot the full permission state before a test run, assert exact permission configurations, and restore the original state in teardown — critical for permission flow testing that must not bleed state between tests.

```typescript
// helpers/ios-permissions.ts

type PermissionState = 'yes' | 'no' | 'unset';
type PermissionService =
  | 'camera' | 'microphone' | 'photos' | 'location' | 'contacts'
  | 'calendar' | 'reminders' | 'notifications' | 'bluetooth' | 'motion';

type PermissionMap = Partial<Record<PermissionService, PermissionState>>;

export async function getAppPermissions(bundleId: string): Promise<PermissionMap> {
  return browser.execute('mobile: getPermission', {
    bundleId,
    service: 'all',
  }) as Promise<PermissionMap>;
}

export async function setAppPermissions(
  bundleId: string,
  permissions: PermissionMap
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: setPermission', {
    bundleId,
    access: permissions,
  });
}

export async function withPermissions(
  bundleId: string,
  permissions: PermissionMap,
  testFn: () => Promise<void>
): Promise<void> {
  const original = await getAppPermissions(bundleId);
  await setAppPermissions(bundleId, permissions);
  try {
    await testFn();
  } finally {
    await setAppPermissions(bundleId, original as PermissionMap);
  }
}

// Spec usage
describe('Camera permission flows', () => {
  it('should show permission denied UI when camera is explicitly denied', async () => {
    await withPermissions('com.example.myapp', { camera: 'no' }, async () => {
      await browser.execute('mobile: activateApp', { bundleId: 'com.example.myapp' });
      await $('~OpenCameraButton').click();
      await expect($('~PermissionDeniedBanner')).toBeDisplayed();
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: setPermission` modifies the iOS permission database (`TCC.db`) via the `applesimutils` utility (simulator only) or via Xcode's `XCUIApplication.resetAuthorizationStatus()` (devices, limited service set). On physical devices the `service: 'all'` read is not supported; you must enumerate each service name individually, which is significantly slower. Restoring original `unset` permission states on device is not possible because `TCC.db` write access is sandboxed; the best device-based approach is to call `browser.terminateApp()` + `browser.activateApp()` and let iOS prompt the user again — which only works in tests that can dismiss the system permission dialog via `mobile: alert`. Simulator-only: `withPermissions` snapshots are fully reversible.

### Pattern 497 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: deepLink` with Verified Intent Routing [official]

**Description:** Launch Android deep links using `mobile: deepLink` with the `waitForLaunch` flag and post-launch assertion to verify that the correct Activity was started by the intent. Unlike `browser.url()` which relies on the WebDriver URL navigation and may silently fall back to the home screen if the intent is not handled, `mobile: deepLink` surfaces intent-not-handled errors as driver exceptions and supports the `waitForLaunch` millisecond timeout for apps with multi-Activity initialization chains.

```typescript
// helpers/android-deep-link.ts

interface DeepLinkOptions {
  url: string;
  package: string;
  waitForLaunch?: boolean;
  launchTimeoutMs?: number;
}

interface DeepLinkResult {
  activityName: string;
  intentAction: string;
  dataUri: string;
}

export async function launchDeepLink(options: DeepLinkOptions): Promise<DeepLinkResult> {
  const { url, package: pkg, waitForLaunch = true, launchTimeoutMs = 5000 } = options;

  const result = await browser.execute('mobile: deepLink', {
    url,
    package: pkg,
    waitForLaunch,
    timeout: launchTimeoutMs,
  });

  return result as DeepLinkResult;
}

export async function assertDeepLinkActivity(
  deepLinkUrl: string,
  expectedActivity: string,
  pkg: string
): Promise<void> {
  const result = await launchDeepLink({ url: deepLinkUrl, package: pkg });
  if (!result.activityName.includes(expectedActivity)) {
    throw new Error(
      `Deep link '${deepLinkUrl}' routed to '${result.activityName}', ` +
      `expected activity containing '${expectedActivity}'`
    );
  }
}

// Spec usage
describe('Android deep link routing', () => {
  it('should route product:// deep link to ProductDetailActivity', async () => {
    await assertDeepLinkActivity(
      'example://product/42',
      'ProductDetailActivity',
      'com.example.shop'
    );
    const productTitle = await $('android=new UiSelector().resourceId("com.example.shop:id/product_title")');
    await expect(productTitle).toBeDisplayed();
    await expect(productTitle).toHaveText('Product 42');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: deepLink` with `waitForLaunch: true` blocks until the activity's `onResume()` callback fires (as reported by UIAutomator2's activity monitor), but does not wait for the activity's data-loading lifecycle to complete. Apps that display a loading skeleton during data fetch will have the activity "resumed" before the actual product content is rendered. Always follow `launchDeepLink` with explicit element waits (`waitForDisplayed`) rather than assuming content is present immediately after the call. On Android 12+, apps must declare the receiving Activity's `<intent-filter>` with `android:autoVerify="true"` for deep links to route correctly without the system disambiguation dialog; tests that run on Android 12 without verified links may see the disambiguation dialog instead of the expected activity.

### Pattern 498 — WDIO v9 `expect.extend()` Custom Matchers for Mobile-Specific Assertions [community]

**Description:** Extend WDIO v9's `expect` with custom matchers tailored to mobile testing idioms — element accessibility label checks, bounding-box assertions, and platform-specific visibility semantics. Custom matchers reduce test verbosity, provide clearer failure messages than raw assertion chains, and encode mobile-specific nuances (e.g., the difference between `isDisplayed` and `isClickable` on iOS) in one well-tested place.

```typescript
// helpers/mobile-matchers.ts
import { expect as wdioExpect } from '@wdio/globals';

interface BoundingBox { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }

declare global {
  namespace ExpectationLibrary {
    interface Matchers<R> {
      toBeWithinViewport(viewportDimensions?: { width: number; height: number }): R;
      toHaveAccessibilityLabel(label: string): R;
      toBeClickableOnPlatform(): R;
    }
  }
}

wdioExpect.extend({
  async toBeWithinViewport(element: WebdriverIO.Element, viewport?: { width: number; height: number }) {
    const vp = viewport ?? (await browser.getWindowSize());
    const rect: BoundingBox = await element.getRect();
    const pass =
      rect.x >= 0 && rect.y >= 0 &&
      rect.x + rect.width <= vp.width &&
      rect.y + rect.height <= vp.height;
    return {
      pass,
      message: () =>
        `Expected element to be${pass ? ' not ' : ' '}within viewport ` +
        `(${vp.width}x${vp.height}), got rect ${JSON.stringify(rect)}`,
    };
  },

  async toHaveAccessibilityLabel(element: WebdriverIO.Element, expectedLabel: string) {
    const platform = (await browser.capabilities as any).platformName?.toLowerCase();
    const label = platform === 'ios'
      ? await element.getAttribute('name')         // XCUITest uses 'name' for accessibilityLabel
      : await element.getAttribute('content-desc'); // UIAutomator2 uses content-desc
    const pass = label === expectedLabel;
    return {
      pass,
      message: () => `Expected accessibility label '${expectedLabel}', got '${label}'`,
    };
  },

  async toBeClickableOnPlatform(element: WebdriverIO.Element) {
    // On iOS prefer isEnabled+isHittable; on Android isEnabled+isClickable
    const platform = (await browser.capabilities as any).platformName?.toLowerCase();
    const isEnabled = await element.isEnabled();
    const isClickable = platform === 'ios'
      ? (await element.getAttribute('hittable')) === 'true'
      : await element.isClickable();
    const pass = isEnabled && isClickable;
    return {
      pass,
      message: () =>
        `Expected element to be clickable on ${platform} (enabled=${isEnabled}, clickable=${isClickable})`,
    };
  },
});

// Spec usage
describe('Product card accessibility', () => {
  it('should have correct accessibility label and be within viewport', async () => {
    const card = await $('~ProductCard_42');
    await expect(card).toHaveAccessibilityLabel('Product 42, $19.99');
    await expect(card).toBeWithinViewport();
    await expect(card).toBeClickableOnPlatform();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `expect.extend()` in WDIO v9 works differently from Jest's `expect.extend()` — WDIO's implementation wraps the matcher in its own async retry loop (respecting `waitforTimeout`), so the matcher function may be called multiple times. Matchers that have side effects (e.g., switching context) will execute those side effects on every retry, potentially causing state inconsistency. Keep custom matchers read-only and side-effect-free; any required state setup should be done explicitly before the `expect()` call. Also note that the TypeScript declaration merging for `ExpectationLibrary.Matchers` must be placed in a `.d.ts` file that is included in the `tsconfig.json` `files` or `include` array, otherwise type-checking passes but IntelliSense autocomplete won't resolve the custom matchers.
