### Pattern 519 — Appium 2 `mobile: startLogsBroadcast` / `stopLogsBroadcast` for Real-Time Device Log Streaming [official]

**Description:** Use Appium 2's `mobile: startLogsBroadcast` and `mobile: stopLogsBroadcast` to stream device log output (iOS syslog, Android Logcat) to a WebSocket endpoint during test execution, enabling real-time log analysis, crash detection, and late-arriving error attribution without polling `driver.getLogs('syslog')` after test completion (which truncates to the last N entries).

```typescript
// helpers/log-broadcast.ts
import WebSocket from 'ws';

interface LogBroadcastOptions {
  port?: number;           // WebSocket port, default 8081
  includeSyslog?: boolean; // iOS: include OS syslog (not just AUT logs)
}

interface LogLine {
  timestamp: string;
  level: string;
  tag?: string;           // Android only
  message: string;
}

const logBuffer: LogLine[] = [];
let wsClient: WebSocket | undefined;

export async function startLogStreaming(options: LogBroadcastOptions = {}): Promise<void> {
  const port = options.port ?? 8081;
  await browser.execute('mobile: startLogsBroadcast', {
    port,
    includeSyslog: options.includeSyslog ?? false,
  });

  await browser.pause(500); // allow WebSocket server to start
  wsClient = new WebSocket(`ws://localhost:${port}`);
  logBuffer.length = 0;

  wsClient.on('message', (data: Buffer) => {
    try {
      const lines: LogLine[] = JSON.parse(data.toString());
      logBuffer.push(...lines);
    } catch {
      // non-JSON partial frame — ignore
    }
  });

  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    wsClient!.once('open', resolve);
    wsClient!.once('error', reject);
  });
}

export async function stopLogStreaming(): Promise<LogLine[]> {
  wsClient?.close();
  wsClient = undefined;
  await browser.execute('mobile: stopLogsBroadcast', {});
  return [...logBuffer];
}

export function getLogLinesMatching(pattern: RegExp): LogLine[] {
  return logBuffer.filter(l => pattern.test(l.message));
}

// Spec usage
it('should not log any ERROR lines during successful login', async () => {
  await startLogStreaming({ includeSyslog: false });
  try {
    await $('~EmailInput').setValue('user@example.com');
    await $('~PasswordInput').setValue('correct-password');
    await $('~LoginButton').click();
    await $('~HomeScreen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
  } finally {
    const logs = await stopLogStreaming();
    const errors = logs.filter(l => l.level === 'ERROR' || l.level === 'FATAL');
    expect(errors).toHaveLength(0);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: startLogsBroadcast` opens a WebSocket server on the Appium host machine (not the device), and the port must be externally reachable from the test runner process. In Docker-based CI, the Appium server and test runner may be in separate containers — in that case, use `appium:webDriverAgentPort` forwarding to expose the WebSocket port via the same proxy used for the WDA/UIAutomator2 server. The broadcast buffer on the Appium server side is bounded (typically 4096 log lines for iOS syslog); if the AUT is extremely verbose (debug-level logging enabled), older log lines are evicted from the buffer before they reach the WebSocket client. For crash-critical log capture, always set `appium:eventTimings: true` in capabilities alongside log broadcasting, which adds XCUITest lifecycle markers that help correlate log timestamps with driver command execution timestamps.

---

### Pattern 520 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: performEditorAction` for Keyboard IME Action Handling [official]

**Description:** Trigger IME action buttons (Done, Go, Search, Next, Send) on the Android software keyboard using `mobile: performEditorAction` instead of sending a `\n` keystroke or tapping the keyboard action button by coordinate. This is the canonical approach for submitting forms and navigating between fields via the keyboard action, working reliably across all OEM keyboard implementations (Gboard, Samsung Keyboard, AOSP Keyboard) where keyboard layout and action button positions differ.

```typescript
// helpers/ime-actions.ts

type ImeActionCode =
  | 'normal'    // 0
  | 'unspecified' // 0
  | 'none'      // 1
  | 'go'        // 2
  | 'search'    // 3
  | 'send'      // 4
  | 'next'      // 5
  | 'done'      // 6
  | 'previous'  // 7
  ;

interface PerformEditorActionOptions {
  action: ImeActionCode | number;
}

export async function performImeAction(
  action: ImeActionCode
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: performEditorAction', {
    action,
  } as PerformEditorActionOptions);
}

export async function fillFieldAndMoveNext(
  fieldSelector: string,
  value: string
): Promise<void> {
  const field = await $(fieldSelector);
  await field.click();
  await field.clearValue();
  await field.setValue(value);
  await performImeAction('next');
}

export async function fillFieldAndSubmit(
  fieldSelector: string,
  value: string
): Promise<void> {
  const field = await $(fieldSelector);
  await field.click();
  await field.clearValue();
  await field.setValue(value);
  await performImeAction('done');
}

// Spec usage — multi-field form with IME navigation
it('should submit login form via keyboard IME actions', async () => {
  await fillFieldAndMoveNext('~EmailInput', 'user@example.com');
  // Focus automatically moves to password field via IME 'next'
  const passwordField = await $('~PasswordInput');
  await expect(passwordField).toBeFocused();
  await fillFieldAndSubmit('~PasswordInput', 'S3cure!Pass');
  // Form submitted via 'done' — verify navigation to home
  await expect($('~HomeScreen')).toBeDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: performEditorAction` sends the IME action directly to the currently focused input field's `InputConnection` via UIAutomator2's accessibility service. It does not visually press the keyboard action button — the keyboard UI is not involved at all. This means the action code sent must match the `android:imeOptions` attribute declared on the EditText in the AUT's XML layout; sending `'search'` to a field configured with `imeOptions="actionDone"` will silently fire the wrong action (the actual registered action) because Android resolves IME actions at the `InputConnection` level, not the code level. For apps using Jetpack Compose `TextField`, the IME action is configured via `KeyboardOptions.imeAction`; the `mobile: performEditorAction` command works correctly with Compose TextFields as of Compose 1.6+ (prior versions had an `InputConnection` implementation bug that caused Compose TextFields to ignore injected IME actions from UIAutomator2). Always verify the `android:imeOptions` value in the AUT's source or via `adb shell uiautomator dump` to confirm the expected action code before writing the test.

---

### Pattern 521 — WDIO v9 `@wdio/allure-reporter` `step()` API for Mobile Test Reporting with Screenshots [community]

**Description:** Structure mobile test reports with embedded screenshots at each logical step using WDIO v9's `@wdio/allure-reporter` `addStep()` / `step()` API combined with `browser.saveScreenshot()`. This provides navigable, timestamped visual evidence in Allure reports — essential for diagnosing flaky mobile tests where the failure screenshot alone does not reveal the pre-condition state that caused the failure.

```typescript
// helpers/allure-steps.ts
import AllureReporter from '@wdio/allure-reporter';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import * as os from 'os';

export async function mobileStep(
  name: string,
  action: () => Promise<void>,
  captureScreenshot = true
): Promise<void> {
  AllureReporter.startStep(name);
  try {
    await action();
    if (captureScreenshot) {
      const tmpPath = path.join(os.tmpdir(), `step-${Date.now()}.png`);
      await browser.saveScreenshot(tmpPath);
      AllureReporter.addAttachment(
        `${name} — screenshot`,
        fs.readFileSync(tmpPath),
        'image/png'
      );
      fs.unlinkSync(tmpPath);
    }
    AllureReporter.endStep('passed');
  } catch (err) {
    if (captureScreenshot) {
      const tmpPath = path.join(os.tmpdir(), `step-fail-${Date.now()}.png`);
      try {
        await browser.saveScreenshot(tmpPath);
        AllureReporter.addAttachment(
          `${name} — FAILED screenshot`,
          fs.readFileSync(tmpPath),
          'image/png'
        );
        fs.unlinkSync(tmpPath);
      } catch { /* screenshot capture itself failed */ }
    }
    AllureReporter.endStep('failed');
    throw err;
  }
}

export function mobileTestInfo(
  deviceName: string,
  platformVersion: string,
  testEnvironment: string
): void {
  AllureReporter.addDescription(
    `Device: ${deviceName} | Platform: ${platformVersion} | Env: ${testEnvironment}`,
    'text'
  );
}

// Spec usage
it('should complete product purchase flow', async () => {
  mobileTestInfo('iPhone 15 Pro', 'iOS 17.4', 'staging');

  await mobileStep('Open product detail', async () => {
    await $('~ProductCard_1').click();
    await $('~ProductDetailTitle').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  });

  await mobileStep('Add to cart', async () => {
    await $('~AddToCartButton').click();
    await $('~CartBadge').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
  });

  await mobileStep('Checkout and pay', async () => {
    await $('~CartIcon').click();
    await $('~CheckoutButton').click();
    await $('~OrderConfirmation').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 15_000 });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `AllureReporter.addAttachment()` with screenshot bytes adds the image inline to the Allure JSON report as a base64-encoded attachment, which increases the per-test report size significantly (a typical 1080×2340 PNG is 200–500 KB). For suites with 100+ test cases, this can produce Allure result directories exceeding 500 MB, which strains CI artifact storage and Allure report generation time. Mitigate by using device screenshot compression: call `browser.saveScreenshot()` and then use the `sharp` library to scale down to 50% resolution before attaching (`sharp(path).resize({ width: 540 }).toBuffer()`). Alternatively, limit `captureScreenshot = true` only for the final step of each test, not every intermediate step. The `mobileStep` wrapper adds approximately 200–400 ms per step due to the screenshot capture round-trip to the Appium server; factor this into test timeout budgets for suites with many steps.

---

### Pattern 522 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: getAppStrings` for Localization Test Coverage [official]

**Description:** Retrieve the full Android app string resources for a specific locale directly from the installed APK using `mobile: getAppStrings`, enabling tests to assert that UI labels and translated strings match the expected localization bundle without hardcoding expected strings in test code. This makes localization tests self-maintaining: adding a new language to the app automatically makes the test coverage extend to that language without test code changes.

```typescript
// helpers/app-strings.ts

interface GetAppStringsOptions {
  language?: string;   // BCP 47 language tag, e.g. 'de', 'fr', 'ja', 'zh-Hant'
  stringFile?: string; // defaults to 'strings.xml'
}

type AppStringsMap = Record<string, string>;

const stringsCache = new Map<string, AppStringsMap>();

export async function getAppStrings(
  language?: string
): Promise<AppStringsMap> {
  const cacheKey = language ?? 'default';
  if (stringsCache.has(cacheKey)) return stringsCache.get(cacheKey)!;

  const opts: GetAppStringsOptions = {};
  if (language) opts.language = language;

  const strings = await browser.execute(
    'mobile: getAppStrings', opts
  ) as AppStringsMap;

  stringsCache.set(cacheKey, strings);
  return strings;
}

export async function assertUiStringMatchesResource(
  elementSelector: string,
  resourceKey: string,
  language?: string
): Promise<void> {
  const [strings, actualText] = await Promise.all([
    getAppStrings(language),
    $(elementSelector).getText(),
  ]);

  const expectedText = strings[resourceKey];
  if (expectedText === undefined) {
    throw new Error(`String resource key '${resourceKey}' not found in app strings (language: ${language ?? 'default'})`);
  }

  expect(actualText.trim()).toBe(expectedText.trim());
}

// Spec usage
describe('German localization', () => {
  before(async () => {
    // Set device locale to German before suite
    await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'am',
      args: ['broadcast', '-a', 'com.android.intent.action.SET_LOCALE', '-e', 'locale', 'de-DE'],
    });
    await browser.pause(2_000); // allow locale to propagate
    await browser.execute('mobile: activateApp', { appId: 'com.example.app' });
  });

  it('should display German string for login button', async () => {
    await assertUiStringMatchesResource('~LoginButton', 'btn_login', 'de');
  });

  it('should display German string for email placeholder', async () => {
    const strings = await getAppStrings('de');
    const field = await $('~EmailInput');
    const placeholder = await field.getAttribute('content-desc');
    expect(placeholder).toContain(strings['hint_email'] ?? '');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: getAppStrings` extracts strings from the APK's compiled `resources.arsc` binary, which contains the current active locale's resolved strings. If the device locale is not set to the language you request via `language`, Android's resource resolver may fall back to the default locale's strings rather than returning the requested language's strings — the `language` parameter filters the resource table but relies on the APK having the requested language compiled into `resources.arsc`. Apps that load translations from remote servers (i18n backends, Firebase Remote Config string tables) instead of the APK resource bundle will return the APK-bundled fallback strings, not the remote translations; test those via UI assertion after locale switch instead. Cache invalidation is per-session — the `stringsCache` Map is module-scoped and is cleared on worker restart; in `--maxInstances > 1` WDIO runs each worker maintains its own cache, which is the desired behavior.

---

## Cycle 51 Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C51-1 — `mobile: startMediaProjectionRecording` on Android 14+ real devices silently produces a zero-length MP4 when the AUT's `targetSdkVersion` is 34 and the test does not explicitly grant `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION` before starting the recording [community]**

WHY: Android 14 (API 34) introduced a mandatory `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION` permission that must be declared in the AUT's `AndroidManifest.xml` and granted at runtime before a `MediaProjection` session can be started via the foreground service pathway. UIAutomator2's `mobile: startMediaProjectionRecording` implementation launches an internal foreground service to hold the MediaProjection grant, and this service requires the new permission on apps with `targetSdkVersion >= 34`. When the permission is absent from the AUT's manifest, Android silently allows `startMediaProjectionRecording` to return without error but the MediaProjection session is never established, causing the stop command to return a payload encoding a zero-length video file. The test sees a successful command completion, the MP4 file is created with valid container headers, but its duration is 0 seconds and the video track has no frames. Fix: add `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION"/>` to the AUT's test manifest overlay (in `src/androidTest/AndroidManifest.xml`), or switch to `browser.startRecordingScreen()` which uses a non-foreground-service recording pathway that does not require this permission on Android 14.

**Gotcha C51-2 — `mobile: updateSafariPreferences` called after `browser.url()` has been executed does not update the preferences for the current page because Safari has already started the page load using the old preference values — the new preferences only take effect on the next page navigation [community]**

WHY: `mobile: updateSafariPreferences` writes to the Safari plist using `NSUserDefaults` synchronization, which updates the on-disk preference file immediately. However, Safari's WebKit process reads preferences into an in-memory cache at page-load time, not at preference-write time. When `mobile: updateSafariPreferences` is called after Safari has already loaded a page, the WebKit renderer's in-memory preference cache for the current page still reflects the old values. The plist update will be read on the *next* `browser.url()` navigation because a new WebKit page load triggers a preference cache refresh from disk. Tests that call `configureSafariForTesting()` after the initial `browser.url('about:blank')` "warmup" pattern and then navigate to the test URL will see the correct preferences. Tests that call `browser.url()` directly without a prior `configureSafariForTesting()` call and then try to update preferences mid-test to disable JavaScript will find that `JavaScriptEnabled: false` has no effect until the next navigation. Fix: always call `mobile: updateSafariPreferences` before any `browser.url()` call, ideally in a `before` or `beforeEach` hook that runs before the test's first navigation.

**Gotcha C51-3 — `browser.addInitScript()` callbacks registered inside a `before()` hook run after the *first* WebView page load in the spec file because WDIO's `before()` hook resolves after the driver session is created but before the first `browser.url()` call, meaning the init script is not yet installed when the first navigation fires if `browser.url()` is called from within the same `before()` hook after `addInitScript()` [community]**

WHY: WDIO v9's `browser.addInitScript()` sends a `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` CDP command to the attached page session. The command is registered on the *current* page session handle. When called from within a `before()` hook that also calls `browser.url()`, the sequence is: (1) `addInitScript()` registers the script on the current blank-page session, (2) `browser.url()` navigates to the target URL, which creates a *new* page session, (3) the new page session does not have the `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` binding because it was registered on the *previous* session. The CDP binding is only inherited by the new session if the navigation is a same-origin navigation within the existing page session. Navigating from `about:blank` to an `https://` origin is treated as a cross-origin navigation and creates a new page session, dropping the init script registration. Fix: split the `before()` hook — call `addInitScript()` in `before()`, call `browser.url()` in `beforeEach()`, so the init script is registered on the page session that will receive the navigation.

**Gotcha C51-4 — `mobile: listSMS` returns messages out of chronological order on devices with Qualcomm RIL (Radio Interface Layer) when the SMS database contains more than 500 messages, because the UIAutomator2 cursor query to the `content://sms/inbox` provider uses a default ORDER BY that is overridden by the Qualcomm SMS provider's custom cursor implementation [community]**

WHY: The standard Android SMS content provider at `content://sms/inbox` supports `ORDER BY date DESC` via the ContentResolver query API. UIAutomator2's `mobile: listSMS` implementation queries the provider with `sortOrder = "date DESC"` in the cursor query. On devices with Qualcomm-derived RIL/SMS provider implementations (common on Snapdragon SoC devices including many Samsung Galaxy and OnePlus models), the Qualcomm SMS provider overrides the default cursor sort with an internal index-based ordering when the SMS database contains more than ~500 messages. The result is that messages are returned in insertion-index order rather than date order for large databases, causing the `sort((a, b) => b.date - a.date)` call in the test helper to re-sort correctly but only after the fact — tests that assume the first returned message is the most recent will fail non-deterministically on high-message-count devices. Fix: always explicitly re-sort the returned messages array by `date` descending in the test helper before accessing `messages[0]`, regardless of what order the provider returns them in. Reset the SMS database to a known small state (< 100 messages) in `beforeEach` using `mobile: deleteSMS` for bulk cleanup or `mobile: shell` + `adb shell content delete --uri content://sms` for a full wipe.

**Gotcha C51-5 — WDIO v9 `browser.call()` wrapping an `axios` HTTP call that takes longer than the WDIO `connectionRetryTimeout` (default 120 seconds) will cause the WDIO command queue to throw a timeout error that orphans the axios promise, leaving an unresolved promise in the Node.js event loop that prevents the test runner process from exiting cleanly after the test suite completes [community]**

WHY: WDIO v9's `browser.call()` implementation wraps the provided async function in a WDIO command with a timeout governed by `connectionRetryTimeout` (default 120 s). If the wrapped async function takes longer than `connectionRetryTimeout`, WDIO resolves the command slot with a timeout error and moves the queue to the next command. However, the original `axios` promise is not cancelled — JavaScript promises are not cancellable, and `axios` does not have a `CancelToken` equivalent that WDIO knows to invoke. The `axios` request continues running in the background after WDIO has already moved on. When the `axios` request eventually resolves (or rejects), it logs an unhandled rejection warning and may trigger WDIO's `unhandledRejection` handler, which in some WDIO v9 configurations calls `process.exit(1)` — causing CI to report a false failure after the test suite has already completed. Fix: always pass an explicit `timeout` in the `axios` config that is shorter than `connectionRetryTimeout` (e.g., `timeout: 30_000` for a 30-second HTTP deadline), and use `axios.CancelToken` or `AbortController` signal to cancel the in-flight request in the `browser.call()` error handler if the WDIO command times out.

### Pattern 523 — WDIO v9 `browser.url()` with `onBeforeLoad` Callback for Pre-Navigation Environment Injection

The WDIO v9 enhanced `url()` command accepts an `onBeforeLoad` callback that fires synchronously before the page's JavaScript begins executing, giving tests a chance to override `window` APIs, install fakes, or set flags that the application reads on startup. This is the idiomatic replacement for the pattern of navigating then immediately calling `browser.execute()` to patch globals, because by the time `browser.execute()` runs the app may have already read the original API values during its module-initialization phase. The callback receives the `window` object of the newly created browsing context and can mutate it freely.

```typescript
// helpers/navigate.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

interface NavigateOptions {
  stubGeolocation?: { latitude: number; longitude: number; accuracy: number };
  stubOnLine?: boolean;
  extraHeaders?: Record<string, string>;
}

export async function navigateWithStubs(
  driver: Browser,
  url: string,
  opts: NavigateOptions = {}
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.url(url, {
    auth: opts.extraHeaders
      ? undefined
      : undefined,
    onBeforeLoad(win: Window) {
      if (opts.stubGeolocation !== undefined) {
        const { latitude, longitude, accuracy } = opts.stubGeolocation;
        (win.navigator as any).geolocation = {
          getCurrentPosition: (success: PositionCallback) =>
            success({ coords: { latitude, longitude, accuracy } } as GeolocationPosition),
          watchPosition: () => 0,
          clearWatch: () => undefined,
        };
      }
      if (opts.stubOnLine !== undefined) {
        Object.defineProperty(win.navigator, 'onLine', {
          get: () => opts.stubOnLine,
          configurable: true,
        });
      }
    },
  });
}

// spec usage:
// await navigateWithStubs(browser, 'https://app.example.com/maps',
//   { stubGeolocation: { latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522, accuracy: 10 } });
// const locationText = await $('[data-testid="current-city"]').getText();
// expect(locationText).toContain('Paris');
```

**Tradeoff:** The `onBeforeLoad` callback only fires in WebView/browser contexts accessed via WDIO's BiDi channel; it is not available in native Appium contexts and has no effect when the session is in `NATIVE_APP` context. The callback cannot perform async operations — any `await` inside it will not be awaited and the promise will be silently ignored. Global mutations made via `onBeforeLoad` persist only for the lifetime of the current page session; a `browser.url()` call to a different origin resets the browsing context and the stubs must be re-applied via a new `onBeforeLoad`. On Safari/WKWebView, BiDi `onBeforeLoad` support requires iOS 17.4+ and Appium XCUITest v8.0+.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 524 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: setStylusHandwriting` for Android Stylus Handwriting API Testing

The `mobile: setStylusHandwriting` command (UIAutomator2 v7.1+) enables or disables the Android Stylus Handwriting API at runtime during a test session, allowing tests to verify that text fields accept stylus handwriting input and that the handwriting overlay UI appears and dismisses correctly. The command is gated behind the `--allow-insecure=set_stylus_handwriting` Appium server flag because it modifies a device-wide system setting that persists across apps. This command is the only programmatic way to toggle stylus handwriting state without using Settings UI automation, which is substantially slower and unreliable across Android OEM skins.

```typescript
// helpers/stylus.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

export async function enableStylusHandwriting(driver: Browser): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: setStylusHandwriting', { enable: true });
}

export async function disableStylusHandwriting(driver: Browser): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: setStylusHandwriting', { enable: false });
}

// spec usage — verify that handwriting overlay appears on long-press with stylus pointer type:
describe('Stylus Handwriting', () => {
  before(async () => { await enableStylusHandwriting(browser); });
  after(async () => { await disableStylusHandwriting(browser); });

  it('shows handwriting overlay when stylus touches a text field', async () => {
    const field = await $('~noteInputField');
    await field.waitForDisplayed();
    // Simulate stylus pointer type via W3C Actions API
    await browser.action('pointer', { parameters: { pointerType: 'pen' } })
      .move({ origin: field })
      .down()
      .pause(1200) // hold to trigger handwriting IME
      .up()
      .perform();
    const overlay = await $('android=new UiSelector().descriptionContains("Handwriting")');
    await expect(overlay).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: setStylusHandwriting` is gated behind `--allow-insecure=set_stylus_handwriting` and will throw `UnsupportedOperationError` if the server is not started with this flag, failing the test with an opaque error rather than a skip. The API only affects the system-level `STYLUS_HANDWRITING_ENABLED` secure setting; apps that manage their own stylus input handling via `MotionEvent.TOOL_TYPE_STYLUS` filtering will not be affected by this toggle. On emulators without a stylus device profile (the default AVD config), the W3C pen pointer type is accepted by UIAutomator2 but Android treats it as a `TOOL_TYPE_FINGER` touch, so the handwriting IME may not activate; use a real device or an AVD with a `StylusPointerType` hardware config for accurate behavior.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 525 — WDIO v9 `browser.setViewport()` + `browser.emulate('device')` for Responsive WebView Layout Verification

WDIO v9 provides two complementary APIs for simulating mobile device rendering in WebView contexts: `setViewport()` changes only the viewport dimensions (leaving the window size unchanged) and `emulate('device', ...)` sets the user agent, screen metrics, and device pixel ratio together to match a specific named device. Using them in combination allows tests to verify both the responsive CSS breakpoints and the device-detection logic in JavaScript (which often reads `window.navigator.userAgent` or `window.devicePixelRatio` to branch behavior). The `emulate()` return value is a reset function that restores the original values, making teardown explicit and safe.

```typescript
// helpers/responsive.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

const MOBILE_DEVICES = {
  'iPhone 15 Pro': {
    userAgent:
      'Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 17_0 like Mac OS X) ' +
      'AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/17.0 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1',
    viewport: { width: 393, height: 852, devicePixelRatio: 3 },
  },
  'Pixel 8': {
    userAgent:
      'Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 14; Pixel 8) ' +
      'AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Mobile Safari/537.36',
    viewport: { width: 412, height: 915, devicePixelRatio: 2.625 },
  },
} as const;

type DeviceName = keyof typeof MOBILE_DEVICES;

export async function emulateDevice(
  driver: Browser,
  device: DeviceName
): Promise<() => Promise<void>> {
  const config = MOBILE_DEVICES[device];
  const resetUa = await driver.emulate('userAgent', config.userAgent);
  await driver.setViewport(config.viewport);
  return async () => {
    await resetUa();
    // Reset to default viewport — arbitrary large desktop value
    await driver.setViewport({ width: 1280, height: 800, devicePixelRatio: 1 });
  };
}

// spec usage:
it('renders mobile nav bar on iPhone 15 Pro viewport', async () => {
  const reset = await emulateDevice(browser, 'iPhone 15 Pro');
  try {
    await browser.url('/home');
    const mobileNav = await $('[data-testid="mobile-nav"]');
    await expect(mobileNav).toBeDisplayed();
    const desktopNav = await $('[data-testid="desktop-nav"]');
    await expect(desktopNav).not.toBeDisplayed();
  } finally {
    await reset();
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.setViewport()` and `browser.emulate()` require WebDriver BiDi support and are only valid in WebView/browser contexts, not in `NATIVE_APP` context. The `emulate('device', ...)` form (using a named device profile) depends on the driver's internal device catalog; for custom device dimensions, use `emulate('userAgent', ...)` plus `setViewport()` separately as shown above. Changes to `devicePixelRatio` via `setViewport()` affect CSS media queries (`@media (-webkit-device-pixel-ratio: 3)`) but not `window.screen.width`/`window.screen.height` which are read-only DOM properties — apps relying on `screen.width` for layout decisions will not reflect the emulated viewport. On Safari/WKWebView the `emulate()` command requires iOS 17.4+ and is not available on iOS 16.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 526 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: listWindows` for Multi-Window and Split-Screen Context Enumeration

The `mobile: listWindows` command (UIAutomator2 v6.5+) returns a list of all currently visible Android window layers including their package names, bounds, z-order, focused state, and window type. This is the correct way to detect that a split-screen or picture-in-picture layout is active before attempting to interact with a specific window, rather than relying on element-level accessibility tree inspection which cannot distinguish between overlapping windows from different apps. The command output can also be used to verify that a dialog or overlay window has appeared and is positioned over the expected underlying window.

```typescript
// helpers/windows.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

interface AndroidWindowInfo {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  packageName: string;
  bounds: { left: number; top: number; right: number; bottom: number };
  type: string;
  focused: boolean;
  layer: number;
}

export async function listAndroidWindows(driver: Browser): Promise<AndroidWindowInfo[]> {
  return driver.execute('mobile: listWindows', {}) as Promise<AndroidWindowInfo[]>;
}

export async function getFocusedWindow(driver: Browser): Promise<AndroidWindowInfo | undefined> {
  const windows = await listAndroidWindows(driver);
  return windows.find((w) => w.focused);
}

export async function assertSplitScreenActive(
  driver: Browser,
  app1Package: string,
  app2Package: string
): Promise<void> {
  const windows = await listAndroidWindows(driver);
  const packages = windows.map((w) => w.packageName);
  if (!packages.includes(app1Package) || !packages.includes(app2Package)) {
    throw new Error(
      `Expected split-screen with ${app1Package} and ${app2Package}; ` +
      `found windows: ${packages.join(', ')}`
    );
  }
}

// spec usage — verify PiP overlay appears after video minimize:
it('shows PiP window after minimize', async () => {
  await $('[data-testid="minimize-video"]').click();
  await browser.waitUntil(async () => {
    const windows = await listAndroidWindows(browser);
    return windows.some((w) => w.type === 'TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY' && w.packageName === 'com.example.app');
  }, { timeout: 5000, timeoutMsg: 'PiP window did not appear within 5 s' });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: listWindows` queries the Android `WindowManagerService` via accessibility APIs and returns all windows visible to the UIAutomator2 service account; on API 31+ devices with strict accessibility sandboxing enabled by the OEM, windows from apps that declare `allowBackup="false"` and `usesCleartextTraffic="false"` in a security-hardened manifest may not appear in the list even if they are visually on screen. The `type` field uses the `WindowManager.LayoutParams` type integer codes (e.g., `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY = 2038`) not human-readable string names in raw UIAutomator2 responses; use a lookup table in your helper to map them to readable names. The command returns a snapshot at the moment of the call and is not reactive — rapidly appearing/disappearing windows (e.g., a toast) may not be captured if the call executes after the window is already dismissed.

**Tag: [official]**

---

### Pattern 527 — WDIO v9 `browser.switchFrame()` Function-Predicate Pattern for WebView Iframe Targeting

The WDIO v9 `browser.switchFrame()` command accepts a predicate function that iterates over all available frames, passing each frame's `window` object to the callback, and switches to the first frame for which the callback returns `true`. This function-based form is the most robust way to target iframes in mobile WebView contexts because frame indices change when dynamic content loads/unloads iframes, URL-based matching breaks when the iframe loads a redirect, and element-based matching requires the iframe element itself to be visible in the parent frame's DOM.

```typescript
// helpers/frame.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

/**
 * Switch to the iframe that contains a DOM element matching the given selector.
 * Falls back to NATIVE_APP context switch if no matching frame is found.
 */
export async function switchToFrameContaining(
  driver: Browser,
  selector: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  let found = false;
  try {
    await driver.switchFrame(async () => {
      // This callback runs inside the frame's window context
      return Boolean(document.querySelector(selector));
    });
    found = true;
  } catch {
    // No matching frame found — remain in current context
  }
  return found;
}

/**
 * Switch to the frame whose URL includes the given path segment.
 */
export async function switchToFrameByUrlPath(
  driver: Browser,
  urlSegment: string
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.switchFrame(() => {
    return window.location.href.includes(urlSegment);
  });
}

// spec usage — target embedded payment iframe by its checkout selector:
it('fills in payment form inside iframe', async () => {
  await browser.url('https://shop.example.com/checkout');
  const switched = await switchToFrameContaining(browser, '#card-number-input');
  expect(switched).toBe(true);
  await $('#card-number-input').setValue('4111111111111111');
  await $('#card-expiry-input').setValue('12/28');
  await browser.switchFrame(null); // return to top-level frame
  await $('[data-testid="place-order-btn"]').click();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** The predicate function passed to `browser.switchFrame()` executes inside each candidate frame's JavaScript context via a BiDi `script.callFunction` call, meaning it has no access to Node.js variables or the outer test scope — all data it needs must be serializable and passed as arguments. Functions returning `Promise<boolean>` are supported since WDIO v9.2.0; earlier v9.x releases require synchronous callbacks only. On Android WebViews, the BiDi frame-switching predicate requires the WebView to have remote debugging enabled (`WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true)`) and the `appium:chromedriverAutodownload: true` capability; without remote debugging, `switchFrame()` falls back to the legacy CDP frame-ID switching which does not support predicate functions.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 528 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: listDisplays` for Multi-Display / Foldable Secondary-Screen Testing

The `mobile: listDisplays` command (UIAutomator2 v6.6+) returns metadata about all currently active Android display surfaces including their IDs, sizes, densities, and state (on/off/doze). On foldable devices and Android desktop-mode environments, this command is used to discover the secondary display ID before passing it to `currentDisplayId` (UIAutomator2 v7+ capability) or to `mobile: screenshots` with a `displayId` argument to capture the secondary screen's state. This is the prerequisite step for any test that needs to target or verify content on a non-primary display.

```typescript
// helpers/displays.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

interface AndroidDisplayInfo {
  id: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  density: number;
  state: 'ON' | 'OFF' | 'DOZE' | 'DOZE_SUSPEND' | 'ON_SUSPEND';
  name: string;
  flags: number;
}

export async function listDisplays(driver: Browser): Promise<AndroidDisplayInfo[]> {
  return driver.execute('mobile: listDisplays', {}) as Promise<AndroidDisplayInfo[]>;
}

export async function getSecondaryDisplayId(driver: Browser): Promise<number | null> {
  const displays = await listDisplays(driver);
  const secondary = displays.find((d) => d.id !== 0 && d.state === 'ON');
  return secondary ? secondary.id : null;
}

export async function captureSecondaryDisplay(
  driver: Browser,
  outputPath: string
): Promise<void> {
  const displayId = await getSecondaryDisplayId(driver);
  if (displayId === null) throw new Error('No active secondary display found');
  const b64Screenshot: string = await driver.execute('mobile: screenshots', {
    displayId,
    format: 'png',
  });
  const fs = await import('fs/promises');
  await fs.writeFile(outputPath, Buffer.from(b64Screenshot, 'base64'));
}

// spec usage — verify content on foldable outer display:
it('shows notification on outer display when folded', async () => {
  // Assume device is folded — outer display is display ID 2
  const displays = await listDisplays(browser);
  const outerDisplay = displays.find((d) => d.id === 2);
  expect(outerDisplay?.state).toBe('ON');
  // Send notification and check outer display screenshot via visual diff
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'am',
    args: ['broadcast', '-a', 'com.example.TRIGGER_NOTIFICATION'],
  });
  await browser.pause(500); // allow notification to render
  await captureSecondaryDisplay(browser, './test-output/outer-display.png');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: listDisplays` reflects the displays registered with Android's `DisplayManager` at the time of the call; virtual displays created by apps using `MediaProjection` or `VirtualDisplay` APIs also appear in the list and must be filtered by `flags` if you only want physical displays (`DisplayManager.DISPLAY_FLAG_TRUSTED` bit mask). Display IDs are not stable across reboots or across session restarts on some OEM foldable implementations — always use `listDisplays` to discover the current display ID dynamically rather than hardcoding `displayId: 1` or `displayId: 2`. The `state` field reports the display power state, not whether content is being rendered; a display with `state: 'ON'` may still be showing a screensaver or lock screen rather than the AUT's content.

**Tag: [official]**

---

### Pattern 529 — WDIO v9 `browser.mock()` URLPattern with `requestOverride` for Dynamic API Response Shaping in WebView Tests

WDIO v9's `browser.mock()` accepts URLPattern strings and an optional `requestOverride` function that receives the intercepted request and can return a modified response body, status code, and headers. The `requestOverride` form is more powerful than the static `mock.respond()` form because it can inspect the outgoing request body (for POST requests) and return different fixtures based on what the app is requesting — enabling stateful API mocking without a proxy server. This pattern is essential for testing error states, pagination edge cases, and race conditions in WebView-heavy mobile apps.

```typescript
// helpers/mocks.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

interface MockOptions {
  method?: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE' | 'PATCH';
  matchBodyKey?: string;
  matchBodyValue?: string;
}

export async function mockApiEndpoint(
  driver: Browser,
  urlPattern: string,
  opts: MockOptions,
  responseFn: (requestBody: unknown) => { status: number; body: unknown }
): Promise<ReturnType<Browser['mock']>> {
  const m = await driver.mock(urlPattern, { method: opts.method ?? 'GET' });
  m.respond(async (req) => {
    let parsedBody: unknown = null;
    try {
      parsedBody = req.postData ? JSON.parse(req.postData) : null;
    } catch { /* ignore non-JSON bodies */ }
    const { status, body } = responseFn(parsedBody);
    return {
      statusCode: status,
      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(body),
    };
  });
  return m;
}

// spec usage — simulate a 429 rate-limit response for search requests:
it('shows rate limit error UI when API returns 429', async () => {
  const mock = await mockApiEndpoint(
    browser,
    '**/api/v2/search**',
    { method: 'POST' },
    (body: any) => {
      if (body?.query?.length > 50) {
        return { status: 429, body: { error: 'rate_limit_exceeded', retryAfter: 60 } };
      }
      return { status: 200, body: { results: [] } };
    }
  );
  try {
    await browser.url('https://app.example.com/search');
    await $('[data-testid="search-input"]').setValue('a'.repeat(51));
    await $('[data-testid="search-btn"]').click();
    await expect($('[data-testid="rate-limit-error"]')).toBeDisplayed();
    await expect($('[data-testid="retry-message"]')).toHaveText('Please wait 60 seconds');
  } finally {
    await mock.restore();
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.mock()` with `requestOverride` functions requires WebDriver BiDi support and is unavailable in Safari/WKWebView sessions on iOS because WKWebView does not expose a CDP network interception layer to third-party drivers. The `postData` field on the intercepted request is only populated for requests with a body (POST, PUT, PATCH); GET requests always have `postData: null`. URLPattern matching in WDIO v9 follows the WHATWG URL Pattern spec which requires a Node.js polyfill (automatically applied by WDIO v9.1+); patterns with query string wildcards must use `**/endpoint?**` not `**/endpoint*` to correctly match query parameters because `*` does not match `?` in the WHATWG URL Pattern path segment syntax.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 530 — UIAutomator2 `mobile: pressKey` with `source` Parameter for Hardware vs Software Input Disambiguation

The `mobile: pressKey` command (UIAutomator2 v6.8+) accepts a `source` parameter that specifies the input device source class for the injected `KeyEvent`, allowing tests to simulate keys from hardware keyboard sources (`keyboard`, `gamepad`, `dpad`) separately from the software keyboard (the default). Specifying `source: 'keyboard'` is required when testing apps that branch behavior based on `InputDevice.SOURCE_KEYBOARD` meta-detection, such as productivity apps that show keyboard shortcuts only when a physical keyboard is connected, or games that require D-pad source events to navigate menus rather than accepting touch-simulated key injection.

```typescript
// helpers/keys.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

type KeySource = 'keyboard' | 'gamepad' | 'dpad' | 'touchscreen';

interface PressKeyOptions {
  keycode: number;
  metastate?: number;
  source?: KeySource;
  flags?: number;
  isLongPress?: boolean;
}

const KEYCODES = {
  ENTER: 66,
  BACK: 4,
  DPAD_UP: 19,
  DPAD_DOWN: 20,
  DPAD_LEFT: 21,
  DPAD_RIGHT: 22,
  DPAD_CENTER: 23,
  PAGE_UP: 92,
  PAGE_DOWN: 93,
  TAB: 61,
  ESCAPE: 111,
} as const;

export async function pressHardwareKey(
  driver: Browser,
  key: keyof typeof KEYCODES,
  source: KeySource = 'keyboard'
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: pressKey', {
    keycode: KEYCODES[key],
    source,
    flags: 0,
    isLongPress: false,
  } satisfies PressKeyOptions);
}

export async function navigateDpadMenu(
  driver: Browser,
  steps: Array<'UP' | 'DOWN' | 'LEFT' | 'RIGHT' | 'CENTER'>
): Promise<void> {
  for (const step of steps) {
    const key = `DPAD_${step}` as keyof typeof KEYCODES;
    await pressHardwareKey(driver, key, 'dpad');
    await driver.pause(150); // allow focus animation to settle
  }
}

// spec usage — verify keyboard shortcut overlay appears with hardware keyboard:
it('shows keyboard shortcuts help when ? pressed from hardware keyboard', async () => {
  await pressHardwareKey(browser, 'ESCAPE', 'keyboard'); // ensure focus is in app
  // keycode 56 = '/' ; for '?' we need shift + /
  await driver.execute('mobile: pressKey', {
    keycode: 56, // '/' key
    metastate: 64, // META_SHIFT_ON
    source: 'keyboard',
  });
  await expect($('[data-testid="keyboard-shortcuts-overlay"]')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** The `source` parameter in `mobile: pressKey` maps to Android's `InputDevice.SOURCE_*` constants and is passed directly to `UiDevice.pressKeyCode(keycode, metastate)` with a synthetic `InputEvent` source override; on Android 13+ with strict `InputManager` validation, injected events with source classes that don't match any registered `InputDevice` on the device may be filtered out by the system `InputFilter` pipeline. On emulators without a hardware keyboard device registered, `source: 'keyboard'` events arrive at the app but `KeyEvent.getDevice()` returns `-1` (no device), which means apps checking `device.getSources() & InputDevice.SOURCE_KEYBOARD != 0` will not detect the event as from a hardware keyboard; only real devices with a paired Bluetooth keyboard or physical USB keyboard pass this check.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 531 — WDIO v9 `browser.emulate('onLine', false)` for Offline Mode and Network Resilience Testing in WebViews

WDIO v9's `browser.emulate('onLine', false)` simulates the `navigator.onLine === false` state and fires the `offline` event on the window, allowing tests to verify that web apps in mobile WebViews correctly display offline banners, cache stale content, queue mutations for sync, and re-sync when connectivity is restored. Unlike `browser.throttleNetwork()` (which intercepts actual network requests), `emulate('onLine')` only changes the `navigator.onLine` flag and fires `window` events — it does not block real HTTP traffic, making it ideal for testing the app's UI-layer offline-detection logic without needing to actually disconnect the device from the network.

```typescript
// helpers/offline.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

export async function simulateOffline(driver: Browser): Promise<() => Promise<void>> {
  const reset = await driver.emulate('onLine', false);
  // Also fire the event manually for apps that only listen to the event
  await driver.execute(() => {
    window.dispatchEvent(new Event('offline'));
  });
  return async () => {
    await reset();
    await driver.execute(() => {
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event('online'));
    });
  };
}

// spec usage:
describe('Offline resilience', () => {
  it('shows offline banner when network is lost', async () => {
    await browser.url('https://app.example.com/feed');
    await $('[data-testid="feed-content"]').waitForDisplayed();
    const goOnline = await simulateOffline(browser);
    try {
      const offlineBanner = $('[data-testid="offline-banner"]');
      await offlineBanner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });
      await expect(offlineBanner).toHaveText('You are offline');
    } finally {
      await goOnline();
    }
  });

  it('queues POST request while offline and syncs on reconnect', async () => {
    await browser.url('https://app.example.com/notes');
    const goOnline = await simulateOffline(browser);
    try {
      await $('[data-testid="new-note-input"]').setValue('Offline note content');
      await $('[data-testid="save-note-btn"]').click();
      await expect($('[data-testid="pending-sync-badge"]')).toBeDisplayed();
    } finally {
      await goOnline();
      await $('[data-testid="pending-sync-badge"]').waitForDisplayed({
        timeout: 5000,
        reverse: true,
      });
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `browser.emulate('onLine', false)` is a DOM-layer simulation only — real HTTP requests made by the WebView's JavaScript (XHR, `fetch`, WebSocket) will still succeed because the network interface is not actually blocked. Apps that determine "offline" status by attempting a probe HTTP request (rather than reading `navigator.onLine`) will not detect the offline state via this emulation. To block actual HTTP traffic, combine with `browser.throttleNetwork({ offline: true })` for the request layer and `browser.emulate('onLine', false)` for the DOM event layer; note that `throttleNetwork` is reset on each WKWebView page navigation (Gotcha C50-1). The reset function returned by `browser.emulate()` does not automatically fire the `online` event — you must dispatch it manually as shown in the helper above if your app listens for `window.online`.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 532 — WDIO v9 `@wdio/visual-service` `createJsonReportFiles` for CI-Integrated Visual Regression Baseline Diff Reports

The `@wdio/visual-service` v5 `createJsonReportFiles` option (enabled via `createJsonReportFiles: true` in the service config) writes a structured JSON file alongside each actual screenshot containing the comparison metadata: device name, browser, platform, mismatch percentage, bounding box coordinates of differing regions, and pass/fail status. These JSON files can be consumed by CI pipelines to generate trend reports, set percentage-based failure thresholds per test rather than using the global `compareOptions.misMatchPercentage`, and feed visual diff data into PR comment bots without parsing image diff overlays.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts (relevant excerpt)
import VisualService from '@wdio/visual-service';

export const config: WebdriverIO.Config = {
  services: [
    [
      VisualService,
      {
        baselineFolder: './visual-baselines',
        screenshotPath: './visual-actual',
        autoSaveBaseline: process.env.CI !== 'true', // only auto-save locally
        createJsonReportFiles: true,  // NEW in v5 — write JSON diff reports
        formatImageName: '{tag}_{deviceName}_{orientation}',
        disableCSSAnimation: true,
        addIOSBezelCorners: false,    // keep clean for CI diffs
        compareOptions: {
          // Global fallback threshold — per-test override preferred
          misMatchPercentage: 2.5,
        },
      },
    ],
  ],
};

// helpers/visual.ts
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

interface VisualDiffReport {
  tag: string;
  deviceName: string;
  misMatchPercentage: number;
  isWithinMisMatchTolerance: boolean;
  passedSaveBaseline: boolean;
}

export function loadVisualReport(tag: string, screenshotPath = './visual-actual'): VisualDiffReport | null {
  const reportFile = path.join(screenshotPath, 'actual', `${tag}.json`);
  if (!fs.existsSync(reportFile)) return null;
  return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(reportFile, 'utf-8')) as VisualDiffReport;
}

// spec usage:
it('product page matches visual baseline', async () => {
  await browser.url('/products/widget-pro');
  await $('[data-testid="product-hero"]').waitForDisplayed();
  await browser.checkFullPageScreen('product-page-widget-pro', {
    hideElements: [$('[data-testid="dynamic-price"]')], // hide volatile price
  });
  // Post-check: verify per-test mismatch doesn't exceed 1% threshold
  const report = loadVisualReport('product-page-widget-pro');
  if (report && report.misMatchPercentage > 1.0) {
    throw new Error(
      `Visual mismatch ${report.misMatchPercentage.toFixed(2)}% exceeds 1% threshold`
    );
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `createJsonReportFiles: true` writes one JSON file per visual comparison call; in a test suite with 200+ `checkScreen` calls, this produces 200+ JSON files in the `actual/` directory which can accumulate across CI runs if the artifact directory is not cleaned. The JSON report is written synchronously after the comparison and before the WDIO test result is finalized, meaning a CI artifact upload step can safely read it immediately after the test completes. The `isWithinMisMatchTolerance` field in the JSON reflects the global `misMatchPercentage` threshold, not any per-comparison threshold passed inline — if you pass `{ misMatchPercentage: 0.5 }` to `checkScreen()`, the JSON report's `isWithinMisMatchTolerance` will still use the service-level config value, making the JSON report unreliable for per-test threshold enforcement without the post-check pattern shown above.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 533 — WDIO v9 Element `waitForStable()` Guard for Animated Mobile UI Components

WDIO v9's `element.waitForStable()` polls the element via `isStable()` (which uses `getComputedStyle` animation checks) and waits until the element's CSS animations have fully stopped before proceeding. This is the recommended guard pattern for mobile WebView tests where bottom sheets, modals, carousels, and transition animations cause `element.click()` to land on the wrong coordinates because the element was mid-animation when the tap was dispatched. The method accepts `timeout` and `interval` options matching the `waitForDisplayed` API contract.

```typescript
// helpers/stable-interactions.ts
import type { ChainablePromiseElement } from 'webdriverio';

/**
 * Wait for an element to stop animating, then interact with it.
 * Falls back gracefully if the element is a native view (isStable not supported).
 */
export async function stableClick(
  el: ChainablePromiseElement,
  opts: { timeout?: number; interval?: number } = {}
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await el.waitForStable({
      timeout: opts.timeout ?? 3000,
      interval: opts.interval ?? 100,
    });
  } catch (err: unknown) {
    // isStable() returns false in native context — log and proceed
    if (!(err instanceof Error) || !err.message.includes('isStable is not supported')) {
      throw err;
    }
  }
  await el.click();
}

export async function stableScreenshot(
  selector: string,
  tag: string
): Promise<void> {
  const el = $(selector);
  await el.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  await el.waitForStable({ timeout: 3000 });
  await browser.saveScreenshot(`./screenshots/${tag}.png`);
}

// spec usage — bottom sheet animation guard:
it('taps "Confirm" button after bottom sheet finishes sliding up', async () => {
  await $('[data-testid="show-confirmation-sheet"]').click();
  const confirmBtn = $('[data-testid="confirm-action-btn"]');
  await confirmBtn.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });
  await stableClick(confirmBtn, { timeout: 2000 });
  await expect($('[data-testid="success-toast"]')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `element.isStable()` uses `getComputedStyle` to detect running CSS animations and transitions — it detects only CSS-driven animations, not JavaScript-driven animations (e.g., `requestAnimationFrame` loops, GSAP, Framer Motion imperative animations). Elements animated entirely via JS that do not set CSS `animation` or `transition` properties will always report `isStable() === true` even while visually moving. The method is unavailable in native Appium contexts (`UnsupportedOperationError` is thrown), and the `waitForStable` guard must be wrapped in a try/catch when used in specs that switch between `NATIVE_APP` and `WEBVIEW` contexts as shown. Disabling animations globally in the test environment (`browser.execute(() => document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--transition-duration', '0ms'))`) is preferred when feasible and eliminates the need for this guard entirely.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 534 — `mobile: resetAccessibilityCache` for Stale Accessibility Tree Recovery in Long-Running Android Test Sessions

The `mobile: resetAccessibilityCache` command (UIAutomator2 v6.4+) instructs the UIAutomator2 server to discard its cached accessibility node tree and force a full re-query from the Android `AccessibilityNodeInfo` API on the next element-finding operation. This command resolves the class of `StaleElementReferenceError`-equivalent failures in UIAutomator2 where the cached node tree drifts out of sync with the live view hierarchy after dynamic view recycling (e.g., `RecyclerView` with `DiffUtil`, view pagers with fragment transactions, or React Native's bridge-driven re-renders that batch multiple `addView`/`removeView` calls outside the UIAutomator2 polling window).

```typescript
// helpers/accessibility.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

/**
 * Reset the UIAutomator2 accessibility cache and wait for the new tree
 * to stabilize before returning. Use when element finders return stale
 * references after complex view transitions.
 */
export async function resetA11yCache(
  driver: Browser,
  settleMs = 300
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: resetAccessibilityCache', {});
  if (settleMs > 0) {
    await driver.pause(settleMs);
  }
}

/**
 * Retry an element-finding operation up to maxAttempts times,
 * resetting the accessibility cache between retries.
 */
export async function findWithCacheReset<T>(
  driver: Browser,
  finder: () => Promise<T>,
  maxAttempts = 3
): Promise<T> {
  let lastError: unknown;
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await finder();
    } catch (err) {
      lastError = err;
      if (attempt < maxAttempts) {
        await resetA11yCache(driver, 500);
      }
    }
  }
  throw lastError;
}

// spec usage — find element after complex React Native screen transition:
it('shows updated cart count after adding item', async () => {
  await $('~add-to-cart-button').click();
  // Complex bridge re-render may lag UIAutomator2 cache
  await resetA11yCache(browser, 400);
  const cartBadge = await findWithCacheReset(
    browser,
    () => $('~cart-item-count').getText(),
  );
  expect(Number(cartBadge)).toBe(1);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mobile: resetAccessibilityCache` triggers a full accessibility tree traversal on the next element query, which on complex screens with deep view hierarchies (100+ nodes) can add 200–800 ms latency to the subsequent `findElement` call compared to using the cached tree. The command should be used sparingly — only after known complex view transitions — rather than as a blanket "fix flakiness" measure at the start of every test step. On Android 12+ with `WindowInsetsController` animations enabled, the accessibility tree is frozen during window inset animations and `resetAccessibilityCache` called during an active animation will result in an empty tree being cached; add a `browser.pause(animationDurationMs)` before calling `resetAccessibilityCache` if the screen has just transitioned.

**Tag: [official]**

### Pattern 535 — WDIO v9 `browser.url()` `waitUntil: 'networkIdle'` for Ensuring WebView API Requests Complete Before Assertions

The WDIO v9 `url()` command's `waitUntil: 'networkIdle'` option (combined with a `timeout` parameter) instructs the navigation to wait until there are no in-flight network requests before resolving, rather than waiting only for the DOM `DOMContentLoaded` or `load` events. This is the correct pattern for SPAs loaded in mobile WebViews that fire multiple sequential API calls (auth → user profile → feed data) during startup: without `networkIdle`, assertions run during the API loading phase and either see loading spinners or partially populated data.

```typescript
// helpers/spa-navigation.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

/**
 * Navigate to a SPA route and wait for network to settle before returning.
 * Uses networkIdle to ensure all startup API calls have completed.
 */
export async function navigateToSPARoute(
  driver: Browser,
  route: string,
  networkIdleTimeoutMs = 8000
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.url(route, {
    waitUntil: 'networkIdle',
    timeout: networkIdleTimeoutMs,
  });
}

/**
 * Navigate and assert a key data-loaded indicator is present,
 * combining networkIdle wait with an explicit sentinel element check.
 */
export async function navigateAndAwaitContent(
  driver: Browser,
  route: string,
  sentinelSelector: string,
  opts: { networkTimeout?: number; sentinelTimeout?: number } = {}
): Promise<void> {
  await navigateToSPARoute(driver, route, opts.networkTimeout ?? 8000);
  await driver.$(sentinelSelector).waitForDisplayed({
    timeout: opts.sentinelTimeout ?? 5000,
    timeoutMsg: `Data sentinel ${sentinelSelector} not visible after networkIdle on ${route}`,
  });
}

// spec usage:
it('shows populated dashboard after login', async () => {
  await navigateAndAwaitContent(
    browser,
    'https://app.example.com/dashboard',
    '[data-testid="dashboard-widget-revenue"]',
    { networkTimeout: 10000, sentinelTimeout: 6000 }
  );
  const revenueValue = await $('[data-testid="dashboard-widget-revenue"]').getText();
  expect(revenueValue).toMatch(/\$[\d,]+/);
});

// Combined with per-test WebView context switching:
it('SPA dashboard loads correctly in hybrid app WebView', async () => {
  const contexts = await browser.getContexts({ returnDetailedContexts: true });
  const webviewCtx = contexts.find((c: any) => c.url?.includes('dashboard'));
  if (webviewCtx) await browser.switchContext(webviewCtx.id);
  await navigateAndAwaitContent(
    browser,
    '/dashboard',
    '[data-testid="dashboard-widget-revenue"]'
  );
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `waitUntil: 'networkIdle'` uses BiDi network event monitoring and considers the network "idle" when there have been no in-flight requests for 500 ms (the BiDi spec default, not configurable in WDIO v9.x). Apps that use long-polling, Server-Sent Events, or WebSocket connections will never reach networkIdle because those connections keep the request count above zero indefinitely; for such apps, use `waitUntil: 'load'` and guard with a sentinel-element `waitForDisplayed` instead. The `timeout` parameter applies to the entire `networkIdle` wait, not to individual requests; a slow CDN asset that takes 7 s to resolve will cause a `timeout: 8000` navigation to succeed only if no other requests fire during those final 500 ms after the CDN response arrives.

**Tag: [official]**

---

### Pattern 536 — WDIO v9 `browser.action('pointer', { pointerType: 'touch' })` Multi-Touch Sequence for Pinch-to-Zoom Verification in Native Contexts

WDIO v9's W3C Actions API with `pointerType: 'touch'` supports multi-touch sequences via `browser.actions([touch1, touch2])` for simulating two-finger gestures like pinch and spread on native mobile views. While `browser.pinch()` and `browser.zoom()` provide higher-level abstractions, the raw Actions API is necessary when the element-relative coordinate math in the high-level helpers doesn't account for scroll offset or when you need to control the gesture velocity (via the `duration` parameter on `move` actions) precisely to reproduce a specific user interaction speed that triggers physics-based animations.

```typescript
// helpers/multi-touch.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

interface Point { x: number; y: number }

/**
 * Two-finger pinch gesture using W3C Actions API.
 * @param center - Center point of the pinch in absolute screen coordinates
 * @param startSpread - Initial distance between fingers (px)
 * @param endSpread - Final distance between fingers (px) — smaller = pinch in
 * @param durationMs - Gesture duration in milliseconds
 */
export async function pinchAtPoint(
  driver: Browser,
  center: Point,
  startSpread: number,
  endSpread: number,
  durationMs = 600
): Promise<void> {
  const finger1 = driver.action('pointer', {
    parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' },
  });
  const finger2 = driver.action('pointer', {
    parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' },
  });

  const halfStart = startSpread / 2;
  const halfEnd = endSpread / 2;

  await driver.actions([
    finger1
      .move({ x: center.x - halfStart, y: center.y, duration: 0 })
      .down({ button: 0 })
      .pause(50)
      .move({ x: center.x - halfEnd, y: center.y, duration: durationMs })
      .up({ button: 0 }),
    finger2
      .move({ x: center.x + halfStart, y: center.y, duration: 0 })
      .down({ button: 0 })
      .pause(50)
      .move({ x: center.x + halfEnd, y: center.y, duration: durationMs })
      .up({ button: 0 }),
  ]);
}

// spec usage — verify map zoom level changes after pinch:
it('zooms out map with two-finger pinch', async () => {
  await $('~mapView').waitForDisplayed();
  const location = await $('~mapView').getLocation();
  const size = await $('~mapView').getSize();
  const center: Point = {
    x: location.x + size.width / 2,
    y: location.y + size.height / 2,
  };
  const zoomLevelBefore = await $('~zoomLevelLabel').getText();
  // Pinch in (spread from 200px to 50px) = zoom out
  await pinchAtPoint(browser, center, 200, 50, 800);
  await browser.pause(500); // wait for zoom animation
  const zoomLevelAfter = await $('~zoomLevelLabel').getText();
  expect(Number(zoomLevelAfter)).toBeLessThan(Number(zoomLevelBefore));
});
```

**Tradeoff:** The W3C Actions API multi-touch sequence dispatches two concurrent `MotionEvent` streams; on Android, these are received correctly by `ScaleGestureDetector` and `GestureDetector` when both pointers are dispatched within the same `InputEvent` batch. However, UIAutomator2 sends each `MotionEvent` from the two Action sources in the `actions` array sequentially within the same batch — the batch dispatch happens correctly but there is a known edge case on Android 12+ where `MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN` for the second touch arrives with a timestamp delta that exceeds the system's multi-touch confirmation window (~50 ms) if the UIAutomator2 server is under CPU load, causing the gesture detector to not recognize it as a multi-touch sequence. Add `pause(50)` between `down()` calls on both fingers to ensure they arrive in the same batch as shown. The high-level `browser.pinch()` helper has its own coordinate calculation that does not take scroll offset into account; for elements in a scrollable list, the raw Actions API approach with explicit screen coordinates is more reliable.

**Tag: [official]**

---

### Pattern 537 — Community Pattern: Defensive `getContexts()` Retry Loop for Flaky WebView Attachment on Android Real Devices

On Android real devices (especially budget and mid-range devices with limited RAM), the Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint that UIAutomator2 uses to attach to WebView instances is not immediately available when the WebView finishes loading its initial URL — the WebView's renderer process registers its CDP endpoint with `LocalSocket` asynchronously and may take 1–3 seconds after the WebView's `onPageFinished` callback fires. A single `getContexts()` call immediately after navigating to a page in the hybrid app will return only `['NATIVE_APP']`, causing the test to fail when it tries to `switchContext()` to a WebView that does not yet appear in the list.

```typescript
// helpers/webview.ts
import type { Browser } from 'webdriverio';

interface DetailedContext {
  id: string;
  title?: string;
  url?: string;
  bundleId?: string;
  packageName?: string;
}

/**
 * Wait for a WebView context matching the given URL pattern to become available.
 * Retries getContexts() up to maxAttempts times before throwing.
 *
 * Community pattern — addresses ChromeDriver CDP attachment latency on real devices.
 */
export async function waitForWebViewContext(
  driver: Browser,
  urlPattern: RegExp | string,
  opts: { maxAttempts?: number; pollIntervalMs?: number; timeoutMs?: number } = {}
): Promise<string> {
  const maxAttempts = opts.maxAttempts ?? 15;
  const pollIntervalMs = opts.pollIntervalMs ?? 500;

  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const contexts: DetailedContext[] = await driver.getContexts({
      returnDetailedContexts: true,
      androidWebviewConnectionRetryTime: 200,
      androidWebviewConnectTimeout: 4000,
    }) as DetailedContext[];

    const target = contexts.find((c) => {
      if (!c.url) return false;
      return typeof urlPattern === 'string'
        ? c.url.includes(urlPattern)
        : urlPattern.test(c.url);
    });

    if (target) return target.id;

    if (attempt < maxAttempts) {
      await driver.pause(pollIntervalMs);
    }
  }

  const elapsed = maxAttempts * pollIntervalMs;
  throw new Error(
    `WebView context matching ${urlPattern} not found after ${maxAttempts} attempts (${elapsed} ms). ` +
    'Ensure WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true) is called before the WebView loads.'
  );
}

// spec usage:
it('loads checkout page inside hybrid WebView', async () => {
  await $('~checkout-btn').click();
  const webviewCtxId = await waitForWebViewContext(browser, /checkout\.example\.com/);
  await browser.switchContext(webviewCtxId);
  await expect($('[data-testid="checkout-header"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** This retry loop is a community-developed workaround for real-device CDP attachment latency and is not needed on emulators where the CDP endpoint registers synchronously. Setting `androidWebviewConnectionRetryTime` and `androidWebviewConnectTimeout` in the `getContexts()` call passes these options to Appium's internal ChromeDriver attachment logic, which already does its own internal retries — the outer loop in `waitForWebViewContext` adds a second layer of retries at the test level for cases where Appium's internal retry exhausts without finding the context. On devices with less than 3 GB RAM, the WebView renderer process may be killed by the Android Low Memory Killer between `getContexts()` calls if another app is in the foreground; `switchContext()` to a previously found context ID may fail with `CannotAttachToChromeError` — always call `getContexts()` fresh rather than caching the context ID across test steps.

**Tag: [community]**

---

## Cycle 52 Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C52-1 — `browser.emulate('onLine', false)` does not block actual HTTP requests made by `fetch()` or `XMLHttpRequest` inside the WebView — apps that detect offline state by making a probe request to a known endpoint (rather than reading `navigator.onLine`) will not observe the offline state because the request succeeds normally, causing offline-mode UI branches to never be exercised [community]**

WHY: The `browser.emulate('onLine', false)` command uses the WebDriver BiDi `browsingContext.setOnLine` API (where supported) or a CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions` equivalent that only updates the `navigator.onLine` property and dispatches the `offline` window event. It does not configure the OS-level network interface or the browser's network stack to actually drop packets or refuse connections — the underlying TCP/IP stack remains fully connected. Apps that implement offline detection via a "connectivity check" (e.g., `fetch('/api/ping').catch(() => setOffline(true))`) will receive a successful HTTP 200 response from the ping endpoint and conclude that the device is online, never setting the offline state flag. The correct test approach for these apps is `browser.throttleNetwork({ offline: true })` (which blocks real requests via CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions`) combined with `browser.emulate('onLine', false)` for the DOM event — but note that `throttleNetwork` is reset on each WKWebView navigation on iOS (Gotcha C50-1), so the offline block must be re-applied after every `browser.url()` call in the same test.

**Gotcha C52-2 — `mobile: setStylusHandwriting` requires the `--allow-insecure=set_stylus_handwriting` Appium server flag at server startup time; passing it via `appium:allowInsecure` capability in the session definition does NOT enable the command, because UIAutomator2 evaluates the `allowInsecure` list from the server's launch flags only, not from per-session capability overrides [community]**

WHY: Appium 2's security architecture distinguishes between server-level `--allow-insecure` flags (applied at server startup and governing all sessions) and per-session `appium:allowInsecure` capability values (allowed by the server only if the server was started with `--relaxed-security` or the specific flag is already in the server-level allow list). For `set_stylus_handwriting`, UIAutomator2 checks the server-level allow list at the time `mobile: setStylusHandwriting` is invoked, not at session creation time. If the server was started without `--allow-insecure=set_stylus_handwriting`, sending `{ allowInsecure: ['set_stylus_handwriting'] }` in the session capabilities is silently accepted (the capability is stored) but the UIAutomator2 server-side handler still reads from the startup-time allow list and finds the flag absent, throwing `SecurityError: set_stylus_handwriting is not in the server allow list`. This is a common trap in cloud device farm setups where testers can add capabilities but cannot control Appium server startup flags; the command is simply not usable on farms that have not explicitly opted in at the infrastructure level.

**Gotcha C52-3 — WDIO v9 `browser.switchFrame()` with a function predicate throws `Error: Frame not found` when called while the page is in the middle of a navigation (e.g., immediately after `browser.url()` before `DOMContentLoaded`), because the BiDi frame enumeration snapshot taken at the time of the `switchFrame()` call captures the blank interim document's frame list, which contains only the root frame with no child iframes, even though the target iframes will exist moments later [community]**

WHY: The WDIO v9 `browser.switchFrame()` implementation with a predicate function sends a BiDi `browsingContext.getTree` call to enumerate all available frames, then iterates the returned frame tree calling the predicate function in each frame's context via `script.callFunction`. The `getTree` snapshot is taken synchronously at the time of the `switchFrame()` call. If `switchFrame()` is called immediately after `browser.url()` resolves (which resolves when the HTTP response is received, before `DOMContentLoaded`), the page's frame tree at that moment contains only the root browsing context with an empty children array because the HTML parser has not yet processed the `<iframe>` tags in the document body. The predicate therefore never matches, and `switchFrame()` throws `Frame not found`. The fix is to wait for `DOMContentLoaded` (or a specific sentinel element in the parent frame) before calling `switchFrame()` — use `$('iframe[src*="payment"]').waitForExist({ timeout: 5000 })` in the parent frame first to confirm the iframe element exists in the DOM before invoking the frame switch.

**Gotcha C52-4 — `mobile: listWindows` on Android 12+ devices running OneUI (Samsung) returns window entries with `packageName: 'com.android.systemui'` for ALL windows when the device is running a Samsung Android 12 system image, because Samsung's OneUI overrides `WindowManager` reporting to attribute all window ownership to SystemUI in the accessibility API responses for security hardening, making it impossible to distinguish windows from different apps by package name using this command on Samsung real devices [community]**

WHY: Samsung's OneUI Android 12 security hardening introduced a `WindowManagerService` policy change that strips per-app window ownership metadata from `AccessibilityWindowInfo` responses when apps query window metadata via the `AccessibilityService` API. UIAutomator2's `mobile: listWindows` implementation reads window metadata via `UiAutomation.getWindows()` which calls into `AccessibilityService`. On OneUI 4.x (Android 12) Samsung devices, `AccessibilityWindowInfo.getRoot().getPackageName()` returns `com.android.systemui` for all application windows, not the actual app's package name. This means the `assertSplitScreenActive()` helper pattern (Pattern 526 above) will always fail on Samsung Android 12 real devices when checking by package name — use window `bounds` dimensions to distinguish between split-screen halves instead (each window in split-screen occupies approximately half the screen height), as the bounds data is not stripped by the Samsung policy.

**Gotcha C52-5 — WDIO v9 `browser.url()` with `waitUntil: 'networkIdle'` hangs indefinitely (until the `timeout` is reached) on pages that use `EventSource` (Server-Sent Events) or long-polling `fetch()` requests with `keepalive: true`, because these request types keep the browser's active request count above zero for the lifetime of the page, preventing the networkIdle condition from ever being satisfied [community]**

WHY: WebDriver BiDi's networkIdle detection tracks active network requests by monitoring `network.beforeRequestSent` and `network.responseCompleted` (and `network.fetchError`) events. A "network idle" condition is declared when no `beforeRequestSent` event has fired for 500 ms without a corresponding completion event. `EventSource` connections send a `GET` request that the server keeps open by never sending a response termination, so `network.responseCompleted` never fires for the SSE connection — the request stays permanently "in flight" in BiDi's accounting. Similarly, long-polling `fetch()` with `keepalive: true` opens a connection that outlives normal request lifecycle tracking. The `timeout` parameter in `browser.url({ waitUntil: 'networkIdle', timeout: N })` will eventually reject after `N` ms, throwing a timeout error that fails the test. The fix is to use `waitUntil: 'load'` or `waitUntil: 'interactive'` for pages known to use SSE or long-polling, and guard readiness with an explicit sentinel element `waitForDisplayed()` call after navigation instead of relying on networkIdle.
