**Pattern 588: WDIO v9 `element.tap()` with `direction` and `maxScrolls` for Auto-Scroll-and-Tap on Deep List Items** [official]
WDIO v9's `element.tap()` on native app elements automatically scrolls the element into view before tapping, unlike `element.click()` which throws `ElementNotInteractableException` if the element is outside the viewport. The `direction` and `maxScrolls` parameters control how the auto-scroll behaves: `direction: 'down'` searches downward (suitable for standard top-to-bottom lists), and `maxScrolls` caps the search to prevent infinite scrolling on dynamically-loading feeds.
```typescript
import { $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface TapScrollOptions {
  direction?: 'down' | 'up' | 'left' | 'right';
  maxScrolls?: number;
  scrollableElement?: WebdriverIO.Element;
}

async function tapListItemByLabel(
  label: string,
  opts: TapScrollOptions = {}
): Promise<void> {
  const el = await $(`~${label}`);
  await el.tap({
    direction: opts.direction ?? 'down',
    maxScrolls: opts.maxScrolls ?? 8,
    scrollableElement: opts.scrollableElement,
  });
}

it('taps 15th item in long product list from top', async () => {
  await $('~productList').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  const list = await $('~productList');

  // Tap item that requires 3-4 scrolls to reach
  await tapListItemByLabel('product-item-15', {
    direction: 'down',
    maxScrolls: 10,
    scrollableElement: list,
  });

  await $('~productDetailScreen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });
  await expect($('~productTitle')).toBeDisplayed();
});

it('taps item in horizontally-scrolling category strip', async () => {
  const strip = await $('~categoryStrip');
  await strip.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });

  await tapListItemByLabel('category-electronics', {
    direction: 'right',
    maxScrolls: 5,
    scrollableElement: strip,
  });

  await expect($('~electronicsCategoryScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `element.tap()` auto-scroll on iOS uses XCUITest's `scroll(to:)` which works relative to the closest enclosing `UIScrollView`. If the element is inside a nested scroll view but the outer `UITableView` is detected first, the scroll may stop at the wrong container. Providing an explicit `scrollableElement` pointing to the innermost scroll container prevents this. On Android, `maxScrolls` uses UIAutomator2's `UiScrollable.scrollIntoView()` which always scrolls to the top of the list first if the element is not found — this resets scroll position for any previously-visible items. Use `direction: 'up'` for items above the current viewport to avoid the full-reset behavior.

---

**Pattern 589: Appium 2 `mobile: getPerformanceData` with `cpuinfo`/`memoryinfo` for Automated Memory Leak Detection in Soak Tests** [official]
Long-running soak tests that exercise a navigation flow repeatedly can silently accumulate memory leaks. `mobile: getPerformanceData` with `dataType: 'memoryinfo'` returns `totalPrivateDirty`, `nativePrivateDirty`, and `dalvikPrivateDirty` fields from Android's `ActivityManager.MemoryInfo`, enabling per-iteration memory delta tracking. A regression is flagged when private dirty memory grows monotonically across 20+ iterations without stabilizing, indicating a leak rather than normal GC fluctuation.
```typescript
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface MemorySnapshot {
  totalPrivateDirty: number;
  nativePrivateDirty: number;
  dalvikPrivateDirty: number;
  iteration: number;
  timestamp: number;
}

async function captureMemorySnapshot(iteration: number): Promise<MemorySnapshot> {
  const packageName = 'com.example.myapp';
  const raw = await driver.execute('mobile: getPerformanceData', {
    packageName,
    dataType: 'memoryinfo',
    dataReadTimeout: 5,
  }) as string[][];

  // raw is [headers, values] — map to object
  const headers = raw[0];
  const values = raw[1];
  const mem: Record<string, number> = {};
  headers.forEach((h, i) => { mem[h] = parseInt(values[i], 10); });

  return {
    totalPrivateDirty: mem['totalPrivateDirty'] ?? 0,
    nativePrivateDirty: mem['nativePrivateDirty'] ?? 0,
    dalvikPrivateDirty: mem['dalvikPrivateDirty'] ?? 0,
    iteration,
    timestamp: Date.now(),
  };
}

function detectMonotonicGrowth(snapshots: MemorySnapshot[]): boolean {
  if (snapshots.length < 5) return false;
  const last5 = snapshots.slice(-5);
  return last5.every((s, i) =>
    i === 0 || s.totalPrivateDirty > last5[i - 1].totalPrivateDirty
  );
}

it('navigation soak test: memory does not grow monotonically over 20 iterations', async () => {
  const snapshots: MemorySnapshot[] = [];
  const ITERATIONS = 20;

  for (let i = 0; i < ITERATIONS; i++) {
    await $('~homeTab').click();
    await $('~productList').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4000 });
    await $('~productCard').click();
    await $('~productDetailScreen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4000 });
    await browser.back();

    if (i % 4 === 0) {
      const snap = await captureMemorySnapshot(i);
      snapshots.push(snap);
    }
  }

  const growthDetected = detectMonotonicGrowth(snapshots);
  const finalMem = snapshots[snapshots.length - 1];
  const initialMem = snapshots[0];
  const growthKB = finalMem.totalPrivateDirty - initialMem.totalPrivateDirty;

  expect(growthDetected).toBe(false);
  expect(growthKB).toBeLessThan(5000); // < 5 MB total growth over 20 iterations
}, 180_000);
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: getPerformanceData` is Android-only — there is no direct iOS equivalent (use Instruments `XCTest` metrics API via `XCTMetric` in XCTest framework, which is not exposed through Appium). The data returned by `memoryinfo` on Android varies by device manufacturer: Xiaomi and Samsung MIUI/OneUI devices report inflated `nativePrivateDirty` due to vendor services running inside the app process. Establish a baseline on each target device family before setting absolute thresholds. Also, calling `getPerformanceData` during animation frames causes a 200–400 ms UI jank due to the `am meminfo` shell invocation — call it only between navigation steps, never during scroll or animation.

---

**Pattern 590: WDIO v9 `browser.toggleAirplaneMode()` with `queryAppState()` for Offline-Mode Graceful Degradation Testing** [official]
Testing offline error handling requires reliably toggling network connectivity and verifying the app transitions through correct states (`loading → offline_error → cached_content`). WDIO v9's `browser.toggleAirplaneMode()` (Android) combined with `browser.queryAppState(bundleId)` for iOS's equivalent state check provides a cross-platform offline simulation wrapper that includes retry verification the mode actually changed before proceeding with assertions.
```typescript
import { browser, driver } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (browser.capabilities as { platformName: string }).platformName.toLowerCase();
const APP_BUNDLE = 'com.example.myapp';
const APP_PACKAGE = 'com.example.myapp';

async function setNetworkOffline(offline: boolean): Promise<void> {
  if (PLATFORM === 'android') {
    await browser.toggleAirplaneMode();
    // Verify airplane mode state via shell
    await browser.waitUntil(async () => {
      const state = await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
        command: 'settings',
        args: ['get', 'global', 'airplane_mode_on'],
      }) as string;
      return offline ? state.trim() === '1' : state.trim() === '0';
    }, { timeout: 5000, interval: 500 });
  } else if (PLATFORM === 'ios') {
    // iOS: use mobile: toggleAirplaneMode (XCUITest driver >= 4.17)
    await driver.execute('mobile: toggleAirplaneMode');
    await browser.pause(2000); // iOS network state change propagates slowly
  }
}

it('app shows cached content and offline banner when network is unavailable', async () => {
  // Load content while online
  await $('~homeScreen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8000 });
  await $('~articleList').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  const onlineArticleCount = await $$('~articleCard').length;

  // Go offline
  await setNetworkOffline(true);
  try {
    await browser.refresh().catch(() => {}); // trigger re-fetch
    await browser.pause(2000);

    const offlineBanner = await $('~offlineBanner');
    await offlineBanner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });
    await expect(offlineBanner).toHaveText('You are offline');

    const cachedArticles = await $$('~articleCard');
    expect(cachedArticles.length).toBe(onlineArticleCount); // cached content preserved
  } finally {
    // Always restore network regardless of test outcome
    await setNetworkOffline(false);
    await browser.pause(1000);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.toggleAirplaneMode()` is a toggle, not a set — calling it when airplane mode is already on will turn it off. Always query current state before toggling to avoid double-toggling. On Android 13+ work profile devices, airplane mode requires device owner permissions and may silently fail without error — use `mobile: shell` with `settings get global airplane_mode_on` to confirm the actual state. On iOS, `mobile: toggleAirplaneMode` requires simulator or a jailbroken device; on physical iOS devices under test, use `browser.toggleWiFi()` and `browser.toggleData()` separately as a substitute that covers most offline scenarios without requiring airplane mode.

---

**Pattern 591: XCUITest `mobile: scroll` with `predicateString` for Predicate-Based Element Scroll on iOS Without Accessibility IDs** [official]
Many production iOS apps contain `UITableViewCell` and `UICollectionViewCell` subviews that lack `accessibilityIdentifier` values but have predictable `label`, `value`, or `type` attributes accessible via NSPredicate. `mobile: scroll` with `predicateString` (a UIAutomation predicate expression) scrolls the nearest enclosing `UIScrollView` until the first matching element is accessible, without requiring accessibility IDs on every cell.
```typescript
import { driver, browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function scrollToPredicateElement(
  predicateString: string,
  containerSelector: string,
  direction: 'up' | 'down' = 'down'
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: scroll', {
    predicateString,
    direction,
    element: await $(containerSelector).getElement(),
  });

  // Now find the element that was scrolled into view
  const el = await $(`-ios predicate string:${predicateString}`);
  await el.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });
  return el;
}

it('scrolls to and taps "Confirm" cell in settings list without accessibility ID', async () => {
  const tableView = await $('~settingsTableView');
  await tableView.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });

  const confirmCell = await scrollToPredicateElement(
    'label == "Confirm" AND type == "XCUIElementTypeCell"',
    '~settingsTableView',
    'down'
  );

  await confirmCell.tap();
  await $('~confirmationAlert').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4000 });
  await expect($('~confirmationAlert')).toBeDisplayed();
});

it('scrolls to cell with specific value attribute for localization-agnostic matching', async () => {
  // Match by value (subtitle text) rather than label (title text) for locale-independence
  const priceCell = await scrollToPredicateElement(
    'value CONTAINS "$" AND type == "XCUIElementTypeCell"',
    '~productList',
    'down'
  );

  await expect(priceCell).toBeDisplayed();
  const priceText = await priceCell.$('*[type="XCUIElementTypeStaticText"]').getText();
  expect(priceText).toMatch(/\$\d+\.\d{2}/);
});
```
Tradeoff: `predicateString` in `mobile: scroll` uses XCUITest's `XCUIElementQuery.matching(_:)` which evaluates the predicate against the **currently visible** accessibility tree snapshot. If the matching element is deeply nested (e.g., inside a `UIStackView` inside a `UITableViewCell`), the predicate must match the cell-level element, not the inner label — matching `type == "XCUIElementTypeStaticText"` with `predicateString` will not cause `mobile: scroll` to scroll to it unless that text element is itself a scroll-visible accessibility node. Use `classChain` with `mobile: scroll`'s `toElement` parameter for nested element targeting. Also, iOS 17.2+ changed predicate evaluation order for `UICollectionView` cells with `compositionalLayout`, making `value CONTAINS "x"` queries 2–3x slower than `label ==` exact matches.

---

**Pattern 592: WDIO v9 `browser.fingerPrint()` / `browser.touchId()` for Biometric Authentication Flow Testing** [official]
Biometric authentication gates (FaceID, TouchID on iOS; Fingerprint on Android) block test flows when the biometric prompt appears. `browser.touchId(true)` on iOS simulators sends a successful biometric match signal to the Simulator's enrolled fingerprint sensor, while `browser.fingerPrint(1)` on Android emulators injects a fingerprint sensor event with the enrolled finger ID. Combining these with `browser.toggleEnrollTouchId()` enables testing both enrolled and non-enrolled states.
```typescript
import { browser, driver, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (browser.capabilities as { platformName: string }).platformName.toLowerCase();

async function authenticateWithBiometrics(succeed: boolean): Promise<void> {
  if (PLATFORM === 'ios') {
    // Ensure TouchID is enrolled before attempting
    await browser.toggleEnrollTouchId(true);
    await browser.pause(500);
    await browser.touchId(succeed);
  } else if (PLATFORM === 'android') {
    // fingerPrint(fingerprintId) — use enrolled ID (default: 1)
    await browser.fingerPrint(succeed ? 1 : 99); // ID 99 = not enrolled = failure
  }
}

it('biometric auth success unlocks vault screen', async () => {
  await $('~vaultButton').click();
  const biometricPrompt = await $('~biometricPrompt');
  await biometricPrompt.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });

  await authenticateWithBiometrics(true);

  const vaultScreen = await $('~vaultContentsScreen');
  await vaultScreen.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });
  await expect(vaultScreen).toBeDisplayed();
});

it('biometric auth failure shows fallback PIN prompt', async () => {
  await $('~vaultButton').click();
  await $('~biometricPrompt').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });

  await authenticateWithBiometrics(false);

  const fallbackPin = await $('~fallbackPinScreen');
  await fallbackPin.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4000 });
  await expect(fallbackPin).toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.touchId()` only works on iOS Simulator — physical device biometric testing requires `XCTest`'s `performInteractionWithKey()` API, which is not exposed by Appium. For physical iOS devices, use `mobile: alert` to intercept the `LAContext` biometric prompt's cancel button and test the fallback path instead. On Android, `browser.fingerPrint()` requires emulator with a fingerprint-enrolled `AVD`; hardware device fingerprint injection via Appium requires a rooted device. Always wrap biometric commands in a try/catch with platform version guards: `browser.touchId()` throws on iOS 17.4+ when the simulator's FaceID hardware simulation is not enabled in Xcode's I/O menu.

---

**Pattern 593: Appium 2 `mobile: getDeviceInfo` Combined with `browser.getWindowSize()` for Notch/DynamicIsland-Safe Tap Coordinate Calculation** [official]
On iPhone 14 Pro+ and iPhone 15 series, the Dynamic Island occupies the top-center area (≈37×126 pts). Tapping coordinates in the safe area without accounting for the Dynamic Island causes taps to be swallowed by the system UI. `mobile: getDeviceInfo` returns `statusBarHeight` and `navigationBarHeight` (for Android) and the raw screen dimensions, while `browser.getWindowSize()` returns the logical viewport — the ratio between these two reveals the pixel density and safe area insets, enabling Dynamic Island-safe coordinate calculation.
```typescript
import { driver, browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface SafeArea {
  topInset: number;
  bottomInset: number;
  leftInset: number;
  rightInset: number;
}

async function getIOSSafeAreaInsets(): Promise<SafeArea> {
  const deviceInfo = await driver.execute('mobile: getDeviceInfo') as {
    statusBarSize: { width: number; height: number };
    isSimulator: boolean;
    name: string;
  };

  const statusBarHeight = deviceInfo.statusBarSize?.height ?? 44;
  const windowSize = await browser.getWindowSize();

  // Dynamic Island detection: status bar > 50pt signals notch/DI device
  const hasDynamicIsland = statusBarHeight > 50;

  return {
    topInset: hasDynamicIsland ? statusBarHeight + 6 : statusBarHeight,
    bottomInset: 34, // Standard home indicator height for Face ID devices
    leftInset: 0,
    rightInset: 0,
  };
}

async function tapSafe(
  xPercent: number,
  yPercent: number
): Promise<void> {
  const size = await browser.getWindowSize();
  const insets = await getIOSSafeAreaInsets();

  const safeWidth = size.width - insets.leftInset - insets.rightInset;
  const safeHeight = size.height - insets.topInset - insets.bottomInset;

  const x = Math.round(insets.leftInset + safeWidth * xPercent);
  const y = Math.round(insets.topInset + safeHeight * yPercent);

  await driver.execute('mobile: tap', { x, y });
}

it('taps top navigation bar item without hitting Dynamic Island', async () => {
  // 50% from left, 3% from top of safe area (just below status bar)
  await tapSafe(0.5, 0.03);

  const navTitle = await $('~navigationBarTitle');
  await navTitle.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });
  await expect(navTitle).toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: getDeviceInfo`'s `statusBarSize.height` returns logical points (not pixels) on iOS, which matches `getWindowSize()` values directly — no pixel-ratio conversion needed. However, on iPad models with Stage Manager enabled (iPadOS 16+), `statusBarSize` reflects the floating window's status bar, not the device bezel status bar. Stage Manager tests should use `$('XCUIApplication').frame` via XCUITest's `mobile: source` to determine actual window bounds rather than relying on `getWindowSize()`.

---

**Pattern 594: WDIO v9 `browser.background()` for App Suspension Testing and iOS `applicationWillResignActive` Hook Verification** [official]
`browser.background(seconds)` sends the app to the background for a specified duration, then restores it — this is distinct from `terminateApp()` in that the process remains alive. It exercises the `UIApplicationDelegate` lifecycle hooks (`applicationWillResignActive`, `applicationDidEnterBackground`, `applicationWillEnterForeground`, `applicationDidBecomeActive`) and Android equivalents (`onPause`, `onStop`, `onRestart`, `onResume`). Testing these transitions catches state-saving bugs and notification-handling regressions that only surface on a full lifecycle round-trip.
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function backgroundAndRestore(durationSeconds: number): Promise<void> {
  await browser.background(durationSeconds);
  // After background() returns, app is restored — wait for active state
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const el = await $('~appMainContent');
      return el.isDisplayed();
    },
    { timeout: 10000, interval: 500, timeoutMsg: 'App did not restore within 10s after backgrounding' }
  );
}

it('form data is preserved after 5-second background suspension', async () => {
  await $('~firstNameField').setValue('Alice');
  await $('~lastNameField').setValue('Smith');
  await $('~emailField').setValue('alice@example.com');

  await backgroundAndRestore(5);

  // Verify form state was preserved across suspension
  await expect($('~firstNameField')).toHaveValue('Alice');
  await expect($('~lastNameField')).toHaveValue('Smith');
  await expect($('~emailField')).toHaveValue('alice@example.com');
});

it('push notification received while backgrounded triggers badge update on restore', async () => {
  // Pre-condition: trigger a server-side notification
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'am',
    args: ['broadcast', '-a', 'com.example.TEST_NOTIFICATION', '--es', 'title', 'Test'],
  });

  await backgroundAndRestore(3);

  const tabBadge = await $('~notificationTabBadge');
  await tabBadge.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4000 });
  await expect(tabBadge).toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.background(-1)` on Android sends the app to the background indefinitely — only use a positive duration for reliable test flow; `-1` requires a manual `activateApp()` call to restore, which is not automatically called after the `background()` command returns on all Appium driver versions. On iOS, `browser.background(0)` is interpreted as "send to background and return immediately" by XCUITest driver < 4.15, but as "send to background for 0 seconds then restore" (effectively a no-op) on 4.15+. Always use `duration >= 2` for meaningful lifecycle testing. Note that XCTest's process does not receive actual `applicationWillResignActive` during `background()` on iOS Simulator — this event only fires on physical devices.

---

**Pattern 595: Appium 2 `mobile: startActivity` with `optionalIntentArguments` for Android Deep Link Intent Testing Without URL Schemes** [official]
Some Android apps implement deep navigation via explicit `Intent` with `putExtra()` payloads rather than (or in addition to) URL scheme deep links. Testing these entry points with `mobile: startActivity` and `optionalIntentArguments` bypasses the Launcher/disambiguation dialog and directly invokes the target `Activity` with arbitrary `Intent` extras, enabling parameterized deep-navigation test cases without publishing a URL scheme handler.
```typescript
import { driver, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface ActivityLaunchParams {
  appPackage: string;
  appActivity: string;
  intentAction?: string;
  intentCategory?: string;
  intentFlags?: string;
  optionalIntentArguments?: string;
  stopApp?: boolean;
}

async function startActivityWithExtras(
  params: ActivityLaunchParams
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: startActivity', {
    appPackage: params.appPackage,
    appActivity: params.appActivity,
    intentAction: params.intentAction ?? 'android.intent.action.VIEW',
    intentCategory: params.intentCategory ?? 'android.intent.category.DEFAULT',
    intentFlags: params.intentFlags ?? '0x10200000',
    optionalIntentArguments: params.optionalIntentArguments ?? '',
    stopApp: params.stopApp ?? false,
  });
}

it('launches product detail activity directly via Intent extra', async () => {
  await startActivityWithExtras({
    appPackage: 'com.example.shop',
    appActivity: 'com.example.shop.ProductDetailActivity',
    optionalIntentArguments:
      '--es product_id "SKU-12345" --es source "push_notification"',
  });

  const productTitle = await $('~productDetailTitle');
  await productTitle.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8000 });
  await expect(productTitle).toBeDisplayed();

  const skuBadge = await $('~productSkuBadge');
  await expect(skuBadge).toHaveText('SKU-12345');
});

it('launches checkout activity with pre-filled cart Intent extras', async () => {
  await startActivityWithExtras({
    appPackage: 'com.example.shop',
    appActivity: 'com.example.shop.CheckoutActivity',
    optionalIntentArguments:
      '--eia cart_item_ids 101,102,103 --es coupon_code "SAVE20"',
    stopApp: true, // Restart app fresh to avoid state bleed
  });

  const couponField = await $('~couponCodeField');
  await couponField.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });
  await expect(couponField).toHaveValue('SAVE20');
});
```
Tradeoff: `optionalIntentArguments` is a raw shell-escaped string passed directly to `am start`. String values with spaces must be double-quoted within the argument string (e.g., `--es key "value with spaces"`). Integer arrays use `--eia` (not `--ei`) for arrays — using the wrong flag type causes a silent `Intent` parsing failure where the extra is omitted without error. UIAutomator2 driver versions < 2.29 do not support `optionalIntentArguments` for `mobile: startActivity` — they silently ignore the extra arguments and launch the activity without them. Verify extra delivery with `await driver.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'dumpsys', args: ['activity', 'top'] })` and parse the `Intent` section of the output in CI.

**Pattern 596: WDIO v9 `browser.getClipboard()` / `browser.setClipboard()` for Copy-to-Clipboard UX Flow Verification** [official]
Testing "Copy to clipboard" buttons in mobile apps (share codes, wallet addresses, invite links) requires verifying the clipboard was actually populated with the correct string after the button tap. `browser.getClipboard()` returns the current clipboard content as a base64-encoded string, enabling post-tap assertion without relying on visual toast notifications (which are timing-dependent) or accessibility announcements.
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function getClipboardText(): Promise<string> {
  const base64 = await browser.getClipboard();
  return Buffer.from(base64, 'base64').toString('utf-8');
}

async function clearClipboard(): Promise<void> {
  // Set clipboard to empty string to isolate each test
  await browser.setClipboard(
    Buffer.from('').toString('base64'),
    'plaintext'
  );
}

it('copy referral code button populates clipboard with correct code', async () => {
  await clearClipboard();

  const referralScreen = await $('~referralCodeScreen');
  await referralScreen.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });

  const displayedCode = await $('~referralCodeText').getText();
  await $('~copyReferralCodeButton').click();

  // Allow clipboard async write to settle
  await browser.pause(500);

  const clipboardContent = await getClipboardText();
  expect(clipboardContent).toBe(displayedCode);
  expect(clipboardContent).toMatch(/^[A-Z0-9]{8}$/); // Format: 8 uppercase alphanumeric chars
});

it('copy wallet address button populates clipboard and shows confirmation toast', async () => {
  await clearClipboard();
  await $('~walletAddressSection').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4000 });

  const walletAddress = await $('~walletAddressText').getText();
  await $('~copyAddressButton').click();

  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const text = await getClipboardText();
      return text === walletAddress;
    },
    { timeout: 3000, interval: 200, timeoutMsg: `Clipboard not populated within 3s` }
  );

  // Verify toast is shown (secondary check)
  const toast = await $('~copiedToast');
  await toast.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 2000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.getClipboard()` on iOS requires the app to have `NSPasteboardUsageDescription` in its `Info.plist` and the user (or automation) to have granted clipboard access. On iOS 16+, reading the clipboard triggers a system banner notification "App is pasting from another app" — this banner can briefly obscure the top of the screen and interfere with subsequent `element.tap()` calls if the test does not wait for it to dismiss (approximately 2 seconds). On Android 13+, `getClipboard()` returns an empty string when called from a background context — always ensure the app is in the foreground before reading the clipboard. Use `browser.waitUntil()` with clipboard polling rather than a fixed `pause()` since clipboard write latency varies by app implementation.

**Pattern 597: Appium 2 Espresso Driver `mobile: idlingResources` Wait for Synchronization with OkHttp/Room Database Operations** [community]
When testing apps built with the Espresso driver (instead of UIAutomator2), Espresso's `IdlingResource` mechanism can synchronize test execution with ongoing OkHttp network calls and Room database transactions. Registering custom `CountingIdlingResource` instances and waiting for them to idle before assertion eliminates the fixed `browser.pause()` anti-pattern for data-loading screens.
```typescript
import { driver, browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

// Note: Requires Appium Espresso driver, not UIAutomator2
// Set capability: 'appium:automationName': 'Espresso'

async function waitForIdlingResources(timeoutMs = 10000): Promise<void> {
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const resources = await driver.execute('mobile: idlingResources') as {
        name: string;
        isIdleNow: boolean;
      }[];
      return resources.every(r => r.isIdleNow);
    },
    {
      timeout: timeoutMs,
      interval: 250,
      timeoutMsg: `IdlingResources did not become idle within ${timeoutMs}ms`,
    }
  );
}

async function registerIdlingResource(resourceName: string): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: registerIdlingResource', {
    resourceName,
    resourceClass: 'androidx.test.espresso.idling.CountingIdlingResource',
  });
}

it('product list loads completely before assertion (Espresso-synchronized)', async () => {
  // Register app's OkHttp idling resource (must be registered in app test build)
  await registerIdlingResource('OkHttpIdlingResource');

  await $('~productsTabBarItem').click();

  // Espresso will not proceed until all registered IdlingResources are idle
  await waitForIdlingResources(15000);

  const productCards = await $$('~productCard');
  expect(productCards.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Verify no loading spinners remain
  const spinner = await $('~loadingSpinner');
  await expect(spinner).not.toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: idlingResources` is only available with the Espresso driver (`appium:automationName: 'Espresso'`) — it throws `UnknownCommandError` when used with UIAutomator2. The Espresso driver requires the app to include `espresso-idling-resource` in its test dependencies and the app's debug build to expose its `IdlingResource` instances to the test process. This creates a coupling between the test suite and the app's build configuration that UIAutomator2 does not require. For teams that cannot modify the app build, use `mobile: getPerformanceData` CPU polling as a proxy for "app is processing" (CPU > 15% = likely loading, CPU < 5% = idle) rather than idling resources.

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C56-1: WDIO v9 `element.tap()` auto-scroll on Android overshoots and loses focus on `NestedScrollView` inside `CoordinatorLayout` when `AppBarLayout` uses `SCROLL_FLAG_EXIT_UNTIL_COLLAPSED`**
When a `CoordinatorLayout` contains an `AppBarLayout` with `app:layout_scrollFlags="scroll|exitUntilCollapsed"` and a `NestedScrollView` as the sibling, WDIO v9's `element.tap()` auto-scroll calls `UiScrollable.scrollIntoView()` which dispatches `MotionEvent.ACTION_SCROLL` to the root `ViewGroup`. The `CoordinatorLayout.onNestedScroll()` method intercepts the scroll event and first collapses the `AppBarLayout` (consuming the scroll offset to collapse the toolbar), then forwards the remaining scroll delta to the `NestedScrollView`. When the toolbar collapse distance equals the element's out-of-viewport distance, UIAutomator2 considers the element visible after the toolbar collapses — but the element's accessibility node bounds are not recalculated until the next `View.onLayout()` pass (triggered by `requestLayout()`), causing the tap to land on stale bounds that now point to the wrong element.

WHY: UIAutomator2's `UiObject2.click()` captures the element's bounding box immediately after `scrollIntoView()` returns, before the `CoordinatorLayout` triggers a second layout pass to redistribute the `AppBarLayout` collapse offset. `View.getGlobalVisibleRect()` returns the pre-layout-pass rect, which is offset by the toolbar height that was just collapsed. The tap event is sent to coordinates that now correspond to a different view (the element one visual row above the intended target). Fix: after `element.tap()` or before tapping elements in `CoordinatorLayout` pages, call `await browser.pause(300)` to allow the layout pass to complete, then use `await element.getLocation()` to verify the element's Y coordinate matches the expected screen region before proceeding.

---

**Gotcha C56-2: Appium 2 `mobile: getContexts` returns stale WebView context IDs after `WKWebView.reload()` on iOS 17.2+ because the CDP target ID is regenerated but Appium's session context registry is not invalidated**
After programmatically calling `WKWebView.reload()` inside a hybrid iOS app, the page's CDP target receives a new `Target.targetId` from WebKit's internal target management system. The old context ID (e.g., `WEBVIEW_12345.1`) remains in Appium's session context registry (cached from the previous `getContexts` call), but attempting to `switchContext()` to it throws `SessionNotCreatedException: Could not connect to CDP target`. Re-calling `getContexts()` returns the old cached entries unless the Appium session detects a WebSocket disconnection from the stale target.

WHY: Appium's XCUITest driver caches context IDs in `RemoteDebugger.connectedContextIds` — a `Set<string>` that is populated when `getContexts` polls for available WebKit remote debug targets. When `WKWebView.reload()` triggers an internal navigation (classified as `Target.Type.page`), WebKit's `WKRemoteInspectorConnection` closes the existing CDP WebSocket and reopens a new one with a freshly generated `targetId`. Appium's `RemoteDebugger` detects the WebSocket close event but does NOT automatically evict the stale context ID from `connectedContextIds` — it only updates on the next explicit `getContexts` call. Fix: after any `WKWebView.reload()` or programmatic navigation in a hybrid app, call `await browser.getContexts({ returnDetailedContexts: true })` with a `browser.waitUntil()` loop that polls until the context list's `url` field for the WebView context matches the expected post-reload URL, then call `switchContext()` with the newly returned ID.

---

**Gotcha C56-3: UIAutomator2 `mobile: swipe` on `RecyclerView` with `GridLayoutManager` using `spanCount > 2` scrolls to the wrong row when `getItemCount()` is not a multiple of `spanCount`, causing the last row to be partially filled**
`RecyclerView` with `GridLayoutManager(context, 3)` (3-column grid) and, say, 10 items creates a grid of 4 rows: rows 0–2 are full (3 items each) and row 3 has 1 item. UIAutomator2's `mobile: swipe` with `strategy: 'accessibility id'` and a selector targeting the last item calls `UiScrollable.getChildByDescription()`, which iterates through accessibility nodes in adapter order. For the partially-filled last row, `GridLayoutManager`'s `AccessibilityNodeProvider` reports the single item's `accessibilityPaneTitle` at the span-start position (column 0), but its actual rendered X-coordinate is column 0 of the last row. When UIAutomator2 calculates the scroll endpoint as "center of the item's bounds", it uses the node's reported bounds which include the span's full column-0 to column-2 width — tapping the center of this inflated bounds rectangle lands in column 1 (between the item and empty space), hitting an empty `RecyclerView` placeholder cell.

WHY: `GridLayoutManager.LayoutParams.spanSize` defaults to 1 for all items (each spans 1 column), but `GridLayoutManager.SpanSizeLookup.getSpanSize()` returns 1 while `LayoutManager.getSpanGroupIndex()` calculates the item's accessibility node bounding rect as occupying the full row width when it is the sole item in a row (due to the default `ACCESS_FULL_ROW` accessibility mode added in `RecyclerView` 1.3.0). UIAutomator2 reads these inflated bounds and the tap center is offset from the actual item. Fix: override `GridLayoutManager.setSpanSizeLookup()` in your test build to return a fixed span size of 1 for all items (disabling the `ACCESS_FULL_ROW` behavior), or scroll using UIAutomator2's `mobile: scroll` with `strategy: 'uiautomator'` and the selector `new UiSelector().text("item label")` which uses text matching against the rendered view's `contentDescription` rather than the inflated accessibility bounds.

---

**Gotcha C56-4: WDIO v9 `browser.toggleWiFi()` on Android 14 does not restore previous WiFi state when called twice in rapid succession because `WifiManager.setWifiEnabled()` is asynchronous and the second call races with the first call's state propagation**
Calling `browser.toggleWiFi()` disables WiFi. Immediately calling it again (within 800 ms) to "restore" WiFi state will sometimes call `WifiManager.setWifiEnabled(true)` while the system's `WifiStateMachine` is still processing the `CMD_DISABLE_WIFI` transition. The `WifiStateMachine` drops the `setWifiEnabled(true)` call because it is in the `DisablingWifiState` (a transient state that rejects enable requests until the current disable completes). The second toggle call returns success without error, but WiFi remains disabled, leaving the device in an offline state that persists for all subsequent tests in the suite.

WHY: Android's `WifiManager.setWifiEnabled()` is a one-way IPC call to `WifiService.setWifiEnabled()` in the system server. `WifiService` dispatches the enable/disable command to the `WifiStateMachine` via a `Message` on its `Handler`. The `DisablingWifiState` (active during a disable operation) has an explicit `deferMessage(CMD_SET_WIFI_ENABLED)` call — meaning it defers all enable/disable commands received while transitioning, processes them after the transition completes, but the deferred `true` message from the second toggle arrives after the machine has already settled in `WifiDisabledState`. At that point, `WifiDisabledState` processes the deferred `CMD_SET_WIFI_ENABLED(true)` — BUT on Android 14, `WifiDisabledState.processMessage()` checks a `mUserWifiEnabled` flag that was set to `false` by the first toggle, and the deferred `true` call was issued by UIAutomator2's shell command (not by a user gesture), so the flag is not updated by the deferred message on API 34. Fix: after each `toggleWiFi()` call, poll `settings get global wifi_on` via `mobile: shell` until it returns the expected state (`0` for off, `1` for on) with a `browser.waitUntil()` loop and a 3-second timeout before issuing the next toggle call.

---

**Gotcha C56-5: XCUITest `element.setValue()` on a `WKWebView` `<input type="number">` field inserts a comma separator on iOS locales where the decimal separator is a comma (e.g., de_DE, fr_FR), causing `parseFloat()` on the server side to return `NaN`**
On iOS devices with a locale set to German (`de_DE`) or French (`fr_FR`), `WKWebView`'s `<input type="number">` fields display the numeric keyboard with a comma as the decimal separator (matching the locale's `NSLocale.decimalSeparator`). When XCUITest's `element.setValue('3.14')` is called from a test, XCUITest translates the period character (`.`) to the locale's decimal separator (`,`) because `XCUIElement.typeText()` goes through the software keyboard's key mapping layer. The field receives `3,14` as its `value`, which the browser renders as `3.14` visually (normalizing the locale separator for display), but the underlying `HTMLInputElement.value` is `3,14` — which `parseFloat()` returns as `3` (truncated at the comma) and `Number()` returns as `NaN`.

WHY: XCUITest's `typeText()` implementation calls `XCUIElementQuery.perform(XCUIElementType.key, ".")` which maps to the current keyboard's comma/period key based on `UIKeyboardInputLocaleName`. `WKWebView`'s `<input type="number">` uses the `UIKeyboardTypeDecimalPad` which, in `de_DE` locale, replaces the `.` key with a `,` key — so `typeText(".")` sends a `,` character. The `HTMLInputElement` sanitization step in WebKit's DOM implementation accepts `,` as a valid decimal separator for numeric input when the page's `lang` attribute is absent (inheriting the system locale), but JavaScript's `parseFloat()` always uses `.` as the decimal separator regardless of locale. Fix: in your test helper, replace `.` with the locale-appropriate decimal character via `await browser.execute(() => navigator.language)` to detect the effective locale, then substitute accordingly. Alternatively, use `element.clearValue()` followed by `browser.execute("arguments[0].value = arguments[1]", el, '3.14')` to bypass the keyboard layer entirely and set the value programmatically as the canonical `.` decimal form.

**Pattern 598** — WDIO v9 `browser.longPress()` with `duration` for Context-Menu Invocation and Long-Press-Dependent State Verification
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'android') as 'android' | 'ios';

/**
 * Invokes a long-press on a list item to reveal a context menu,
 * then verifies the expected menu options appear.
 */
async function longPressAndVerifyContextMenu(
  itemSelector: string,
  expectedMenuOptions: string[],
  durationMs = 1500
): Promise<void> {
  const item = await $(itemSelector);
  await item.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });

  // WDIO v9 longPress() wraps mobile: longClickGesture (Android)
  // and mobile: touchAndHold (iOS), passing duration in ms
  await item.longPress({ duration: durationMs });

  for (const option of expectedMenuOptions) {
    const menuItem = await $(`~${option}`);
    await expect(menuItem).toBeDisplayed();
  }
}

it('long-press on message bubble reveals Copy, Reply, Forward options', async () => {
  await longPressAndVerifyContextMenu(
    '~messageBubble_0',
    ['Copy', 'Reply', 'Forward'],
    1200
  );

  // Dismiss context menu
  await browser.pressKeyCode(PLATFORM === 'android' ? 4 : 0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `duration` below 800 ms on Android (UIAutomator2 `mobile: longClickGesture`) is unreliable because the system's `ViewConfiguration.getLongPressTimeout()` defaults to 400 ms but many apps use `OnLongClickListener` with a custom GestureDetector that requires the pointer to remain down for the full `ViewConfiguration` timeout plus a 200 ms debounce. On iOS, `mobile: touchAndHold` with `duration < 1.0` (seconds, not ms — note WDIO converts ms to seconds for XCUITest) may not trigger Haptic Touch on devices with `UILongPressGestureRecognizer.minimumPressDuration` overridden to 0.8 s. Use 1200 ms as a cross-platform safe default; if testing long-press timing sensitivity specifically (e.g., force touch), use `browser.action()` W3C API directly with explicit `pause()` durations for sub-millisecond precision.

**Pattern 599** — Appium 2 `mobile: getStrings` for Localization Resource Validation Against App Bundle String Tables
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface AppStrings {
  [key: string]: string;
}

/**
 * Fetches the app's localized string resources and validates
 * visible UI strings match the expected locale's string table.
 */
async function getLocalizedStrings(
  language?: string,
  stringFile?: string
): Promise<AppStrings> {
  const result = await browser.execute('mobile: getStrings', {
    ...(language && { language }),
    ...(stringFile && { stringFile }),
  }) as AppStrings;
  return result;
}

it('all home screen labels match German (de) localization strings', async () => {
  // Fetch the German string table from the app bundle
  const deStrings = await getLocalizedStrings('de', 'Localizable');
  expect(typeof deStrings).toBe('object');
  expect(Object.keys(deStrings).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Verify specific UI element text matches the string table
  const greetingLabel = await $('~homeGreetingLabel');
  const greetingText = await greetingLabel.getText();
  expect(greetingText).toBe(deStrings['home_greeting'] ?? '');

  // Verify no raw key placeholders are visible (sign of missing translations)
  const allLabels = await $$('//XCUIElementTypeStaticText');
  for (const label of allLabels) {
    const text = await label.getText();
    expect(text).not.toMatch(/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$/); // raw key pattern
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: getStrings` is supported by XCUITest (reads `Localizable.strings` from the app bundle's `.lproj` directories) and UIAutomator2 (reads `strings.xml` from the APK's `res/values-<locale>/` directories), but the `stringFile` parameter behaves differently: on iOS it accepts the filename without extension (e.g., `'Localizable'`), while on Android it is ignored — UIAutomator2 always reads `strings.xml` from the current active locale's resource directory. For multi-module Android apps using `strings.xml` in feature modules (AAR), `mobile: getStrings` only returns strings from the main app's merged `R.string` resource table, not from dynamically loaded feature modules. Validate feature module strings by reading them via `mobile: shell` with `dumpsys resources` or by querying the app's resource resolver at runtime via `browser.execute()` in a WebView context.

**Pattern 600** — WDIO v9 `browser.zoom()` and `browser.pinch()` for Map Scale Level Assertion in Native Map Views
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'android') as 'android' | 'ios';

/**
 * Performs a pinch-to-zoom gesture on a native map view and reads
 * back the resulting zoom level via accessibility value.
 */
async function getMapZoomLevel(): Promise<number> {
  if (PLATFORM === 'ios') {
    // iOS MapKit exposes zoom via accessibility value on MKMapView
    const mapView = await $('//XCUIElementTypeMap');
    const value = await mapView.getAttribute('value') ?? '';
    const match = value.match(/zoom level: ([\d.]+)/i);
    return match ? parseFloat(match[1]) : -1;
  }
  // Android: read zoom from Google Maps content description
  const mapView = await $('//android.view.View[@content-desc="Map"]');
  const desc = await mapView.getAttribute('content-desc') ?? '';
  const match = desc.match(/Zoom level ([\d.]+)/i);
  return match ? parseFloat(match[1]) : -1;
}

it('pinch-in reduces map zoom level and zoom-out restores it', async () => {
  const mapView = await $('~mapContainer');
  await mapView.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });

  const zoomBefore = await getMapZoomLevel();

  // Pinch in (zoom out) — scale < 1 means fingers moving together
  await browser.pinch(mapView, 0.5, 500);
  await browser.pause(600); // wait for map animation to settle

  const zoomAfterPinch = await getMapZoomLevel();
  expect(zoomAfterPinch).toBeLessThan(zoomBefore);

  // Zoom back in — scale > 1 means fingers moving apart
  await browser.zoom(mapView, 2.0, 500);
  await browser.pause(600);

  const zoomAfterZoom = await getMapZoomLevel();
  expect(zoomAfterZoom).toBeGreaterThan(zoomAfterPinch);
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.pinch()` and `browser.zoom()` are WDIO v9 wrapper commands around `mobile: pinchGesture` (UIAutomator2) and multi-touch W3C Actions (XCUITest). The `scale` parameter meaning differs: UIAutomator2 `mobile: pinchGesture` uses `scale` as the ratio of final finger distance to initial distance (< 1 = pinch in), while WDIO's `browser.pinch()` normalizes this to a 0–1 percentage. On iOS Simulator, multi-touch gestures require holding the Option key (⌥) to simulate two fingers, which Appium handles via `XCUICoordinate.press(forDuration:thenDragTo:)` — but this does not trigger `UIPinchGestureRecognizer` on all iOS versions (known to fail on Simulator pre-iOS 16). Always test pinch/zoom on physical devices or Xcode 15+ Simulator for reliable gesture recognition.

**Pattern 601** — Appium 2 `mobile: scroll` with `toVisible: true` for Reliable Navigation to Off-Screen Elements Without Hardcoded Scroll Counts
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'android') as 'android' | 'ios';

/**
 * Cross-platform helper that scrolls an element into view using
 * the platform's native scroll-to-element API.
 */
async function scrollToElement(
  elementAccessibilityId: string,
  containerAccessibilityId?: string
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  if (PLATFORM === 'ios') {
    // XCUITest: scroll the containing scrollview to make element visible
    await browser.execute('mobile: scroll', {
      predicateString: `label == "${elementAccessibilityId}"`,
      toVisible: true,
      ...(containerAccessibilityId && {
        element: await $(containerAccessibilityId).getElement(),
      }),
    });
  } else {
    // UIAutomator2: use UiScrollable to find and scroll to element
    await browser.execute('mobile: scroll', {
      strategy: 'accessibility id',
      selector: elementAccessibilityId,
      ...(containerAccessibilityId && {
        element: await $(containerAccessibilityId).getElement(),
      }),
    });
  }

  const el = await $(`~${elementAccessibilityId}`);
  await el.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  return el;
}

it('settings page terms-of-service link is reachable via scroll', async () => {
  const tosLink = await scrollToElement('termsOfServiceLink', '~settingsScrollView');
  await expect(tosLink).toBeDisplayed();
  await tosLink.click();
  const tosTitle = await $('~tosPageTitle');
  await expect(tosTitle).toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: scroll` with `toVisible: true` on iOS uses `XCUIElement.scroll(byDeltaX:deltaY:)` internally which performs a geometric scroll — it may overshoot on `UITableView` with variable-height cells because `XCUITest` estimates the scroll distance based on the element's reported position in the accessibility tree, not the actual rendered frame. On Android, UIAutomator2 `mobile: scroll` with `strategy: 'accessibility id'` calls `UiScrollable.scrollIntoView()` which uses `UiSelector` — if the element does not appear within `UiScrollable.maxSearchSwipes()` (default 30), the command throws `UiObjectNotFoundException`. For long lists (> 100 items), increase `maxScrolls` via `mobile: scroll` options or use `mobile: scrollGesture` with explicit `direction` and `percent` parameters to scroll page-by-page with manual `waitForDisplayed` polling.

**Pattern 602** — WDIO v9 `browser.getStrings()` Integration with i18n Test Fixtures for Parameterized Locale Coverage
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const SUPPORTED_LOCALES = ['en', 'de', 'fr', 'ja', 'ar'] as const;
type SupportedLocale = typeof SUPPORTED_LOCALES[number];

interface LocaleTestCase {
  locale: SupportedLocale;
  expectedKeys: string[];
  rtl: boolean;
}

const LOCALE_CASES: LocaleTestCase[] = [
  { locale: 'en', expectedKeys: ['app_name', 'login_button', 'logout_button'], rtl: false },
  { locale: 'ar', expectedKeys: ['app_name', 'login_button', 'logout_button'], rtl: true },
  { locale: 'ja', expectedKeys: ['app_name', 'login_button', 'logout_button'], rtl: false },
];

for (const { locale, expectedKeys, rtl } of LOCALE_CASES) {
  it(`[${locale}] all required string keys are present and non-empty`, async () => {
    const strings = await browser.execute('mobile: getStrings', {
      language: locale,
    }) as Record<string, string>;

    for (const key of expectedKeys) {
      expect(strings[key]).toBeDefined();
      expect(strings[key].trim()).not.toBe('');
      // Verify no untranslated English fallback for non-English locales
      if (locale !== 'en') {
        const enStrings = await browser.execute('mobile: getStrings', {
          language: 'en',
        }) as Record<string, string>;
        // Only fail if the value is identical AND the English string is non-trivial
        if (enStrings[key]?.length > 3) {
          // Allow fallback only for locale-neutral strings (URLs, codes)
          if (!strings[key].match(/^https?:|^[A-Z]{2,4}$|^\d+$/)) {
            expect(strings[key]).not.toBe(enStrings[key]);
          }
        }
      }
    }

    // Verify RTL layout direction for Arabic
    if (rtl) {
      const body = await $('//android.widget.FrameLayout[@resource-id="android:id/content"]');
      const layoutDir = await body.getAttribute('layoutDirection');
      expect(layoutDir).toBe('rtl');
    }
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Calling `mobile: getStrings` once per locale per test wastes significant test time (each call takes 150–400 ms on a physical device due to ADB round-trip or XPC call overhead). Cache the string tables in a `beforeAll` suite hook, keyed by locale, and share them across test cases via a module-level `Map<string, Record<string, string>>`. The RTL layout direction check via `layoutDirection` attribute is Android-only; on iOS, check `UIApplication.shared.userInterfaceLayoutDirection` via `mobile: execScript` or verify `semanticContentAttribute` on the root view. RTL layout attribute polling is only reliable after the app restarts with the new locale set in Appium capabilities (`appium:language`, `appium:locale`) — dynamically switching locales at runtime without restarting the app session does not update layout direction in most apps.

---

**Pattern 603** — Appium 2 `mobile: dragGesture` for Reorder-by-Drag Validation in `UITableView` and `RecyclerView` Edit Mode
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'android') as 'android' | 'ios';

/**
 * Drags a list item from one position to another in an editable list.
 * Assumes the list is already in edit/reorder mode.
 */
async function dragListItemToPosition(
  fromIndex: number,
  toIndex: number,
  listSelector: string
): Promise<void> {
  const listItems = await $$(listSelector + ' > *');
  const fromItem = listItems[fromIndex];
  const toItem   = listItems[toIndex];

  const fromLoc  = await fromItem.getLocation();
  const fromSize = await fromItem.getSize();
  const toLoc    = await toItem.getLocation();

  const startX = fromLoc.x + fromSize.width * 0.5;
  const startY = fromLoc.y + fromSize.height * 0.5;
  const endY   = toLoc.y + (await toItem.getSize()).height * 0.5;

  if (PLATFORM === 'android') {
    await browser.execute('mobile: dragGesture', {
      startX, startY,
      endX: startX,
      endY,
      speed: 600, // px/s — slow enough for RecyclerView ItemTouchHelper threshold
    });
  } else {
    // iOS: use W3C Actions for UITableView drag-reorder handle
    await browser.action('pointer', { parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' } })
      .move({ x: startX, y: startY })
      .down()
      .pause(800)   // hold until drag handle activates
      .move({ x: startX, y: endY, duration: 800 })
      .pause(200)
      .up()
      .perform();
  }
}

it('user can reorder playlist items by drag in edit mode', async () => {
  await $('~editPlaylistButton').click();
  await browser.pause(500); // wait for edit mode animation

  const listItems = await $$('~playlistItem');
  const firstItemTextBefore = await listItems[0].getText();

  await dragListItemToPosition(0, 2, '~playlistList');
  await browser.pause(400); // settle animation

  const updatedItems = await $$('~playlistItem');
  expect(await updatedItems[2].getText()).toBe(firstItemTextBefore);
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: dragGesture` (UIAutomator2 2.3+) accepts a `speed` parameter in pixels/second. Values above 1200 px/s may not trigger `ItemTouchHelper.Callback.onMove()` on `RecyclerView` because the `ItemTouchHelper`'s drag threshold requires the pointer to dwell at the drag handle for at least one `onInterceptTouchEvent()` cycle before the swipe velocity trips the "drag started" condition. On iOS, the 800 ms `pause()` before move is required for `UITableView` edit-mode drag handles — the `UITableViewCell` reorder control only activates after `UILongPressGestureRecognizer.minimumPressDuration` (default 0.5 s) plus an additional 200 ms internal debounce. Using `mobile: dragGesture` on iOS is not supported by XCUITest driver; always use W3C Actions for iOS drag interactions.

---

**Pattern 604** — WDIO v9 `browser.scrollIntoView()` with `{ block: 'nearest' }` for WebView Scroll Precision in Hybrid Apps
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Switches to a WebView context and scrolls a DOM element into view
 * using the scroll-into-view options API for precise positioning.
 */
async function scrollWebViewElementIntoView(
  contextUrl: string,
  cssSelector: string,
  block: ScrollLogicalPosition = 'nearest'
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  // Switch to the matching WebView context
  const contexts = await browser.getContexts({
    returnDetailedContexts: true,
  }) as Array<{ id: string; url?: string }>;

  const targetCtx = contexts.find(c => c.url?.includes(contextUrl));
  if (!targetCtx) throw new Error(`WebView context matching ${contextUrl} not found`);
  await browser.switchContext(targetCtx.id);

  const el = await $(cssSelector);
  await el.waitForExist({ timeout: 5000 });

  // Use WebdriverIO's scrollIntoView with W3C scroll options
  await el.scrollIntoView({ block, inline: 'nearest' });
  await browser.pause(200); // allow scroll animation to complete

  await expect(el).toBeDisplayed();
  return el;
}

it('terms acceptance checkbox is scrollable into view in hybrid onboarding WebView', async () => {
  const checkbox = await scrollWebViewElementIntoView(
    'onboarding/terms',
    'input[name="acceptTerms"]',
    'center'
  );
  await checkbox.click();
  expect(await checkbox.isSelected()).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: `element.scrollIntoView()` in a WebView context executes `element.scrollIntoView(options)` as a JavaScript call via the WebDriver `executeScript` command — it uses the browser's native scroll behavior, which respects `scroll-behavior: smooth` CSS on the container element. In apps that set `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `body` or the scroll container, the scroll animation may take 300–600 ms; callers should increase the `pause()` duration or use `browser.waitUntil()` polling on `element.isInViewport()`. In WebView contexts on Android using `WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(false)` (production builds), `getContexts()` returns the WebView context ID but Appium cannot attach the Chrome DevTools Protocol session, causing all WebView interactions to fail with `SessionNotCreatedException`. Always enable `WebContentsDebuggingEnabled` in your test build variant.

---

**Pattern 605** — Appium 2 `mobile: pressButton` for Hardware Button Testing on iOS (Home, Volume, Lock) Without Simulator Shortcuts
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

type iOSButton = 'home' | 'volumeup' | 'volumedown' | 'lock' | 'siri';

/**
 * Presses a hardware button on an iOS device via XCUITest mobile: pressButton.
 * Works on both physical devices and Simulator (Xcode 14+).
 */
async function pressHardwareButton(button: iOSButton): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: button });
}

it('pressing volume-up twice from home screen activates shortcut if configured', async () => {
  // Return to home screen first
  await pressHardwareButton('home');
  await browser.pause(800);

  // First volume press — may show volume HUD
  await pressHardwareButton('volumeup');
  await browser.pause(300);
  await pressHardwareButton('volumeup');
  await browser.pause(300);

  // Verify app is still in foreground (volume HUD auto-dismisses)
  const appState = await browser.queryAppState('com.example.testapp');
  expect([3, 4]).toContain(appState); // 3 = foreground inactive, 4 = foreground active
});

it('lock button puts device into screen-locked state', async () => {
  await pressHardwareButton('lock');
  await browser.pause(1500);

  // Verify screen is locked via XCUITest isLocked capability
  const isLocked = await browser.execute('mobile: isLocked');
  expect(isLocked).toBe(true);

  // Unlock for remaining tests
  await browser.execute('mobile: unlock');
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: pressButton` is XCUITest-only — UIAutomator2 uses `driver.pressKeyCode()` with Android keycode constants (`KEYCODE_HOME = 3`, `KEYCODE_VOLUME_UP = 24`). On iOS Simulator, `mobile: pressButton` with `name: 'home'` triggers the simulated home button press, but on iPhone X+ form factor Simulators (which have no home button), the command maps to the Simulator's "Home" menu action, which may not replicate the full swipe-up-from-bottom gesture. For iOS 17+ app testing, `mobile: pressButton` with `name: 'siri'` activates Siri via the side button long-press — but Siri activation in test environments requires disabling Siri's "Hey Siri" consent screen via `appium:settings.acceptAlertTimeout` and accepting the Siri consent alert within the Appium session timeout window.

**Pattern 606** — WDIO v9 W3C Pointer Actions for Draw-on-Canvas Gesture Sequences in Creative Apps
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface Point { x: number; y: number; }

/**
 * Draws a sequence of connected line segments on a canvas element
 * using W3C Pointer Actions touch API for high-fidelity gesture replay.
 */
async function drawPathOnCanvas(
  canvasSelector: string,
  path: Point[],
  durationPerSegmentMs = 100
): Promise<void> {
  if (path.length < 2) throw new Error('Path must have at least 2 points');

  const actions = browser.action('pointer', { parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' } });

  // Start: move to first point and press
  actions.move({ x: path[0].x, y: path[0].y });
  actions.down();
  actions.pause(50);

  // Draw each segment
  for (let i = 1; i < path.length; i++) {
    actions.move({
      x: path[i].x,
      y: path[i].y,
      duration: durationPerSegmentMs,
    });
  }

  actions.up();
  await actions.perform();
}

it('user can draw a signature on the signature canvas', async () => {
  const canvas = await $('~signatureCanvas');
  await canvas.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  const loc  = await canvas.getLocation();
  const size = await canvas.getSize();

  // Draw a simple S-curve signature path
  const path: Point[] = [
    { x: loc.x + size.width * 0.2, y: loc.y + size.height * 0.3 },
    { x: loc.x + size.width * 0.5, y: loc.y + size.height * 0.2 },
    { x: loc.x + size.width * 0.8, y: loc.y + size.height * 0.4 },
    { x: loc.x + size.width * 0.5, y: loc.y + size.height * 0.6 },
    { x: loc.x + size.width * 0.2, y: loc.y + size.height * 0.8 },
  ];

  await drawPathOnCanvas('~signatureCanvas', path, 120);

  const confirmButton = await $('~confirmSignatureButton');
  await expect(confirmButton).toBeEnabled();
});
```
Tradeoff: W3C Pointer Actions `move({ x, y, duration })` generates a series of intermediate `MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE` events sampled at the Appium server's tick rate (default 60 Hz for UIAutomator2, ~30 Hz for XCUITest). For canvas drawing tests, the intermediate point density affects the rendered stroke smoothness — if `duration` is too short (< 50 ms per segment), UIAutomator2 may interpolate too few intermediate events, resulting in jagged strokes that fail pixel-comparison baselines. For smooth stroke simulation, use segments no shorter than 80 ms at 20 px intervals. On iOS, `XCUICoordinate.press(forDuration:thenDragTo:)` used by XCUITest does not fire `UITouch.force` values — apps that require 3D Touch / Apple Pencil pressure data cannot be tested via standard W3C Actions; use Appium's `mobile: action` with `pressure` parameter (XCUITest driver 5.0+) for pressure-sensitive canvas inputs.

---

**Pattern 607** — Appium 2 `mobile: setPermission` for Runtime Permission State Management Without Permission Dialog Interaction
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'android') as 'android' | 'ios';

type AndroidPermission =
  | 'android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION'
  | 'android.permission.CAMERA'
  | 'android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES'
  | 'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS';

type iOSPermission = 'location' | 'camera' | 'photos' | 'notifications';
type PermissionState = 'granted' | 'denied' | 'provisional';

/**
 * Sets a runtime permission without triggering the system permission dialog.
 * Requires: UIAutomator2 >= 2.30 | XCUITest >= 4.16
 */
async function setAppPermission(
  bundleIdOrPackage: string,
  permission: AndroidPermission | iOSPermission,
  state: PermissionState
): Promise<void> {
  if (PLATFORM === 'android') {
    await browser.execute('mobile: changePermissions', {
      appPackage: bundleIdOrPackage,
      permissions: [permission as AndroidPermission],
      action: state === 'granted' ? 'grant' : 'revoke',
    });
  } else {
    await browser.execute('mobile: setPermission', {
      bundleId: bundleIdOrPackage,
      access: permission as iOSPermission,
      ...(state === 'granted' && { value: 'yes' }),
      ...(state === 'denied'  && { value: 'no' }),
    });
  }
}

beforeEach(async () => {
  // Start each test with camera permission in a known state
  await setAppPermission(
    'com.example.testapp',
    PLATFORM === 'android' ? 'android.permission.CAMERA' : 'camera',
    'granted'
  );
});

it('camera scan screen activates immediately when permission is pre-granted', async () => {
  await $('~scanButton').click();
  const cameraPreview = await $('~cameraPreviewView');
  await expect(cameraPreview).toBeDisplayed();
  // No permission dialog should appear
  const alert = await $('~permissionDialog');
  await expect(alert).not.toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: setPermission` (XCUITest) and `mobile: changePermissions` (UIAutomator2) bypass the system permission dialog entirely, which is ideal for test isolation but means the test never exercises the app's permission-request UI flow. Maintain a separate test suite that exercises the permission dialog by NOT pre-setting permissions and instead using `driver.acceptAlert()` / `driver.dismissAlert()` to handle system dialogs. On Android 13+, `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` and `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` are runtime permissions that require the `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` or `REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES` permission to be granted at install time before `mobile: changePermissions` can modify them programmatically — verify the app is installed with the correct permission metadata in the manifest's `uses-permission` before calling this command.

---

**Pattern 608** — WDIO v9 `browser.mock()` and `browser.mockRestoreAll()` for Network Response Interception in Android WebView Tests
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

/**
 * Intercepts a specific API endpoint in a WebView context and returns
 * a mock response, allowing UI state testing without a live backend.
 */
async function mockWebViewEndpoint(
  urlPattern: string,
  mockResponse: object,
  statusCode = 200
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Mock> {
  const mock = await browser.mock(urlPattern, {
    method: 'GET',
  });

  mock.respond(JSON.stringify(mockResponse), {
    statusCode,
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    fetchResponse: false,
  });

  return mock;
}

it('empty state is shown when API returns an empty product list', async () => {
  // Intercept the product list API before navigating
  const productMock = await mockWebViewEndpoint(
    '**/api/v1/products**',
    { items: [], totalCount: 0 }
  );

  await $('~catalogTab').click();
  await browser.pause(1000); // let the WebView load and request fire

  // Verify empty state UI is shown
  const emptyState = await $('~emptyStateContainer');
  await expect(emptyState).toBeDisplayed();

  // Verify the mock was actually called
  expect(productMock.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  await browser.mockRestoreAll();
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.mock()` is implemented via Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) Fetch domain interception and only works in WebView contexts where Appium has an active CDP session (Android `WebContentsDebuggingEnabled = true`; iOS in Simulator using `safariAllowPopups` capability). `browser.mock()` is NOT supported for native app network traffic — native requests bypass the WebView CDT session entirely. For native network interception on Android, use `mobile: shell` to configure `iptables` rules or a local proxy (e.g., `mitmproxy`) started before the test session. Mock patterns with glob strings (`**/api/**`) use Minimatch path matching, not RegExp — patterns with query strings require URL encoding the `?` as `%3F` or using a RegExp pattern object instead of a string.

---

**Pattern 609** — Appium 2 `mobile: activateApp` with `mobile: terminateApp` for Clean App State Reset Between Tests Without Full Session Restart
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'android') as 'android' | 'ios';
const APP_ID = PLATFORM === 'android' ? 'com.example.testapp' : 'com.example.TestApp';

/**
 * Terminates and re-activates the app to reset UI state without
 * creating a new Appium session (preserves device state).
 */
async function resetAppState(clearData = false): Promise<void> {
  // Terminate running instance
  await browser.execute('mobile: terminateApp', { appId: APP_ID });
  await browser.pause(500); // allow process to fully terminate

  if (clearData && PLATFORM === 'android') {
    // Clear app data for a true cold-start equivalent on Android
    await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'pm',
      args: ['clear', APP_ID],
    });
  }

  // Re-launch the app
  await browser.execute('mobile: activateApp', { appId: APP_ID });
  await browser.pause(1000); // wait for app initialization
}

afterEach(async () => {
  await resetAppState(false); // soft reset: restart but keep data
});

it('app shows onboarding after data clear on first launch', async () => {
  await resetAppState(true); // hard reset: clear all app data
  const onboarding = await $('~onboardingWelcomeScreen');
  await expect(onboarding).toBeDisplayed();
});

it('app restores last session state on soft restart', async () => {
  await $('~loginButton').click();
  await $('~usernameField').setValue('testuser@example.com');
  await resetAppState(false);
  // After soft restart, the app should remember the session
  const dashboard = await $('~dashboardScreen');
  await expect(dashboard).toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: terminateApp` followed by `mobile: activateApp` is significantly faster than `driver.reloadSession()` (which tears down and rebuilds the WebDriver session, taking 15–30 s per cycle). The tradeoff is that `terminateApp` + `activateApp` does NOT reset WebDriver session state — any `browser.mock()` intercepts, context switches, or implicit wait overrides applied in the previous test remain active. Always call `browser.mockRestoreAll()` and `browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP')` in `afterEach` hooks before using the terminate/activate pattern. On iOS, `mobile: terminateApp` calls `XCUIApplication.terminate()` which sends `SIGKILL` to the process — if the app has unsaved CoreData changes or pending background URLSession tasks, these will be lost without the normal `applicationWillTerminate` lifecycle callback (which is only called for graceful termination, not `SIGKILL`).

---

**Pattern 610** — Appium 2 `mobile: getDeviceTime` for Timestamp-Sensitive Notification and Scheduling Test Verification
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'android') as 'android' | 'ios';

interface DeviceTime {
  epochSeconds: number;
  iso8601: string;
  timezone: string;
}

/**
 * Gets the current device time in ISO 8601 format.
 * Used to anchor relative time calculations for scheduling tests.
 */
async function getDeviceTime(): Promise<DeviceTime> {
  const raw = await browser.execute('mobile: getDeviceTime', {
    format: 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ',
  }) as string;

  return {
    iso8601: raw,
    epochSeconds: Math.floor(new Date(raw).getTime() / 1000),
    timezone: raw.slice(-6), // e.g. "+05:30"
  };
}

it('scheduled notification fires within 5 seconds of the configured delay', async () => {
  const { epochSeconds: scheduledAt } = await getDeviceTime();

  // Schedule a notification for 3 seconds from now
  await $('~scheduleNotificationButton').click();
  await $('~delaySecondsField').setValue('3');
  await $('~confirmScheduleButton').click();

  // Wait for notification to appear
  await browser.pause(4500);

  if (PLATFORM === 'android') {
    await browser.openNotifications();
    const notif = await $('~scheduledTestNotification');
    await expect(notif).toBeDisplayed();
    const { epochSeconds: firedAt } = await getDeviceTime();
    expect(firedAt - scheduledAt).toBeLessThanOrEqual(5);
  } else {
    // iOS: check notification via accessibility identifier on banner
    const banner = await $('-ios predicate string:label CONTAINS "Test Notification"');
    await expect(banner).toBeDisplayed();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: getDeviceTime` (UIAutomator2 2.x / XCUITest 4.x) returns the device's wall-clock time, which may differ from the test runner's host clock by ±2 s on emulators/simulators due to clock sync drift. For scheduling tests requiring precise sub-second timing, use `mobile: shell` with `date +%s%N` on Android to get nanosecond-precision epoch time, or `mobile: execScript` on iOS to call `Date.now()` in a WKWebView JavaScript context. On CI devices shared across test runs, the device timezone may differ from the expected timezone if the device was provisioned in a different region — always set `appium:locale` and verify device timezone matches test expectations by comparing `getDeviceTime()` timezone suffix against your test's `process.env.TZ`.

**Pattern 611** — WDIO v9 `browser.startRecordingScreen()` / `browser.stopRecordingScreen()` for Video Evidence Capture on Test Failure
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'android') as 'android' | 'ios';
const EVIDENCE_DIR = path.join(process.cwd(), 'test-evidence', 'videos');

/**
 * Starts screen recording at the beginning of each test.
 * Saves video to disk on failure; discards on pass.
 */
async function startTestRecording(): Promise<void> {
  fs.mkdirSync(EVIDENCE_DIR, { recursive: true });
  await browser.startRecordingScreen({
    videoType: 'mp4',
    videoQuality: 'low',      // reduce file size for CI artifacts
    videoFps: 15,             // 15 fps sufficient for debugging
    timeLimit: 180,           // max 3 minutes per test
    ...(PLATFORM === 'ios' && { videoScale: '320:568:-2' }), // scale down on iOS
  });
}

async function stopAndSaveRecordingOnFailure(
  testName: string,
  passed: boolean
): Promise<void> {
  const video = await browser.stopRecordingScreen();
  if (!passed) {
    const sanitizedName = testName.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9-_]/g, '_');
    const filePath = path.join(EVIDENCE_DIR, `${sanitizedName}_${Date.now()}.mp4`);
    fs.writeFileSync(filePath, Buffer.from(video, 'base64'));
    console.log(`[EVIDENCE] Video saved: ${filePath}`);
  }
}

// In wdio.conf.ts afterTest hook:
// afterTest: async (test, _ctx, { passed }) => {
//   await stopAndSaveRecordingOnFailure(test.fullTitle, passed);
// }
beforeEach(async () => { await startTestRecording(); });
```
Tradeoff: Screen recording via `mobile: startRecordingScreen` (UIAutomator2 uses `screenrecord` shell command; XCUITest uses `XCUIScreen.recordVideo()`) adds 8–15% CPU overhead on the device under test, which can affect performance-sensitive tests (animation frame rate assertions, scroll performance benchmarks). For performance tests, disable recording in the `beforeEach` hook by checking a `PERF_TEST=1` environment variable flag. The `timeLimit` parameter caps recording at a maximum duration (default 180 s for UIAutomator2, 600 s for XCUITest) — tests exceeding this limit will have their recording silently truncated. On Android, `screenrecord` requires API level 19+ and generates H.264 `.mp4` files capped at 3 minutes even when `timeLimit: 600` is specified; for longer recordings, stop and restart recording in 3-minute segments via `stopRecordingScreen()` + `startRecordingScreen()` within the test.

**Pattern 612** — Appium 2 `mobile: shell` with `wm size` and `wm density` for Viewport-Responsive Layout Testing on Android Without Multiple Devices
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface DisplayConfig {
  widthPx: number;
  heightPx: number;
  density: number;
  label: string;
}

const DISPLAY_CONFIGS: DisplayConfig[] = [
  { widthPx: 1080, heightPx: 2400, density: 420, label: 'FHD_Phone' },
  { widthPx: 1600, heightPx: 2560, density: 320, label: 'QHD_Tablet_10' },
  { widthPx: 800,  heightPx: 1280, density: 240, label: 'WXGA_Tablet_7' },
];

async function setDisplayConfig(config: DisplayConfig): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'wm',
    args: ['size', `${config.widthPx}x${config.heightPx}`],
  });
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'wm',
    args: ['density', `${config.density}`],
  });
  await browser.pause(1200); // allow system to reconfigure layouts
}

async function resetDisplayConfig(): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'wm', args: ['size', 'reset'] });
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'wm', args: ['density', 'reset'] });
  await browser.pause(800);
}

for (const config of DISPLAY_CONFIGS) {
  it(`[${config.label}] navigation drawer is accessible and correctly sized`, async () => {
    await setDisplayConfig(config);
    await $('~hamburgerMenuButton').click();
    const drawer = await $('~navigationDrawer');
    await expect(drawer).toBeDisplayed();
    const drawerSize = await drawer.getSize();
    // Drawer should be at most 85% of screen width per Material Design spec
    expect(drawerSize.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(config.widthPx * 0.85);
    await resetDisplayConfig();
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: `wm size` and `wm density` overrides are ADB shell commands that work on rooted devices, Android emulators, and physical devices where the test runner has `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` permission or root access. On non-rooted physical devices without this permission, `wm size reset` may silently succeed but not actually change the display configuration. These overrides persist across app restarts within the same ADB connection session — always call `resetDisplayConfig()` in `afterEach` to prevent display config leakage between tests. On foldable devices (e.g., Samsung Galaxy Z Fold series), `wm size` overrides conflict with the device's native foldable display management via `DisplayAreaManager`; the override may be ignored or cause the device to enter an undefined display state. Use `browser.getWindowSize()` after the command to verify the override took effect before asserting layout.
