**Pattern 636** — iOS `mobile: queryAppState` for Asserting App State Transitions During Background/Foreground Cycles
```typescript
// mobile:queryAppState returns numeric app state: 0=notInstalled,1=notRunning,2=background(suspended),
// 3=background(running),4=foreground(inactive),5=foreground(active).
// UIApplicationState enum equivalent.
const enum AppState {
  NotInstalled = 0,
  NotRunning   = 1,
  BackgroundSuspended = 2,
  BackgroundRunning   = 3,
  ForegroundInactive  = 4,
  ForegroundActive    = 5,
}

async function getAppState(bundleId: string): Promise<AppState> {
  return (await driver.execute('mobile: queryAppState', { bundleId })) as AppState;
}

async function waitForAppState(bundleId: string, target: AppState, timeoutMs = 5_000): Promise<void> {
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => (await getAppState(bundleId)) === target,
    { timeout: timeoutMs, timeoutMsg: `App ${bundleId} did not reach state ${target}` }
  );
}

it('app returns to foreground active state after home button press', async () => {
  const bundle = 'com.example.myapp';
  expect(await getAppState(bundle)).toBe(AppState.ForegroundActive);
  await driver.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'home' });
  await waitForAppState(bundle, AppState.BackgroundSuspended, 3_000);
  await driver.execute('mobile: activateApp', { bundleId: bundle });
  await waitForAppState(bundle, AppState.ForegroundActive, 5_000);
  await expect($('~mainScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: queryAppState` is XCUITest-only (iOS/iPadOS/tvOS); on Android use `driver.queryAppState()` (UIAutomator2) which returns the same numeric enum via the Appium standard endpoint. State `BackgroundSuspended` (2) vs `BackgroundRunning` (3) depends on whether the app holds a `UIBackgroundTask` — most apps immediately move to state 2 after `home` button press unless they have an active background task (audio, location, VoIP). Assert state 2 or state 3 depending on your app's background capability. On iOS Simulator, `pressButton: 'home'` is synchronous but the state transition is asynchronous — always use `waitForAppState` rather than asserting state immediately after the press.

**Pattern 637** — Android `mobile: shell` with `am instrument` for Forcing Locale Without Restarting the Session
```typescript
// Change locale mid-test via ADB shell without resetting app state.
// Avoids the cost of a full session teardown/restart for locale regression tests.
const SUPPORTED_LOCALES: Record<string, { language: string; country: string }> = {
  'en-US': { language: 'en', country: 'US' },
  'de-DE': { language: 'de', country: 'DE' },
  'ja-JP': { language: 'ja', country: 'JP' },
  'ar-SA': { language: 'ar', country: 'SA' },
};

async function setAndroidLocale(locale: keyof typeof SUPPORTED_LOCALES): Promise<void> {
  const { language, country } = SUPPORTED_LOCALES[locale];
  // Change persist locale via ADB (requires shell access, works on API 29+ emulators and rooted devices).
  await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'setprop',
    args:    ['persist.sys.locale', `${language}-${country}`],
  });
  await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'am',
    args:    ['broadcast', '-a', 'android.intent.action.LOCALE_CHANGED'],
  });
  await browser.pause(1_500); // allow LocaleManager.setApplicationLocales() to propagate
}

it('date picker renders in German locale format', async () => {
  await setAndroidLocale('de-DE');
  await driver.execute('mobile: activateApp', { appId: 'com.example.myapp' });
  await $('~openDatePickerButton').click();
  // German locale: day.month.year format
  await expect($('~datePickerHeader')).toHaveText(expect.stringMatching(/\d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{4}/));
  await setAndroidLocale('en-US'); // restore
});
```
Tradeoff: `setprop persist.sys.locale` followed by an `LOCALE_CHANGED` broadcast affects the entire device locale, not just the app under test — parallel test suites on the same emulator will receive the locale change. Use this pattern only in isolated single-device CI workers. On Android 13+ (API 33+), apps can use `LocaleManager.setApplicationLocales()` to set per-app locale without a broadcast — where available, call it via `mobile: shell` with `am` `force-stop` + relaunch rather than system-level `setprop`. Real physical devices with locked bootloaders may deny `setprop persist.sys.locale` regardless of ADB shell permissions — test on Emulators or rooted devices for reliable results.

---

**Pattern 638** — WDIO v9 `element.shadow$()` for Shadow DOM Traversal in Android WebView Components
```typescript
// element.shadow$() pierces the Shadow DOM boundary to query slotted or internal elements.
// Essential for web components (Lit, Stencil, Polymer) rendered inside Android WebView.
import type { ChainablePromiseElement } from 'webdriverio';

async function shadowQuery(
  hostSelector: string,
  innerSelector: string
): Promise<ChainablePromiseElement> {
  const host = await $(hostSelector);
  await host.waitForExist({ timeout: 5_000 });
  return host.shadow$(innerSelector);
}

async function shadowQueryAll(
  hostSelector: string,
  innerSelector: string
): Promise<WebdriverIO.ElementArray> {
  const host = await $(hostSelector);
  await host.waitForExist({ timeout: 5_000 });
  return host.shadow$$(innerSelector);
}

it('validates the custom <my-button> web component label inside Android WebView', async () => {
  // Switch to WebView context.
  const contexts = await browser.getContexts();
  await browser.switchContext(contexts[1] as string);

  const btn = await shadowQuery('my-button', '.btn-label');
  await expect(btn).toHaveText('Place Order');

  const badges = await shadowQueryAll('notification-badge', '.count-bubble');
  expect(badges).toHaveLength(3);

  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```
Tradeoff: `element.shadow$()` requires Chrome DevTools Protocol support in the WebView — it is backed by CDP `DOM.querySelector` scoped to the shadow root and requires `debuggable: true` on the app's `WebView` configuration. It does not work with closed Shadow DOM (`{ mode: 'closed' }`) — CDP cannot pierce closed shadow roots regardless of WebView debuggability. On iOS WKWebView, `shadow$()` requires WebKit inspector enabled (`appium:safariAllowPopups: true` is not sufficient — set `com.apple.developer.web-inspection.enabled` entitlement in Debug builds). WDIO's `$$` chains that cross Shadow DOM boundaries (`$('host').shadow$('inner').$('deepInner')`) do not automatically re-enter Shadow DOM at each hop — each Shadow DOM boundary requires an explicit `.shadow$()` call.

---

**Pattern 639** — Appium `mobile: getNotifications` (XCUITest) for Push Notification Content Assertion
```typescript
// mobile:getNotifications reads the iOS Notification Center content.
// Available on Simulator and real device (requires unlock + backgrounded app).
interface NotificationEntry {
  identifier:  string;
  title?:      string;
  body?:       string;
  category?:   string;
  badge?:      number;
  date:        string; // ISO 8601
}

async function waitForNotification(
  titlePattern: RegExp,
  timeoutMs = 15_000
): Promise<NotificationEntry> {
  const start = Date.now();
  while (Date.now() - start < timeoutMs) {
    const list: NotificationEntry[] = await driver.execute('mobile: getNotifications', {});
    const match = list.find(n => titlePattern.test(n.title ?? ''));
    if (match) return match;
    await browser.pause(1_000);
  }
  throw new Error(`Notification matching ${titlePattern} not received within ${timeoutMs} ms`);
}

it('order confirmation push notification is delivered and correctly formatted', async () => {
  // Put app in background so notification is delivered to Notification Center.
  await driver.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'home' });
  await $('~mainScreen').waitForExist({ reverse: true, timeout: 2_000 });

  // Trigger checkout flow via deep link.
  await driver.execute('mobile: deepLink', { url: 'myapp://checkout/confirm?orderId=ORD-999', bundleId: 'com.example.myapp' });

  const notification = await waitForNotification(/Order Confirmed/);
  expect(notification.body).toMatch(/ORD-999/);
  expect(notification.badge).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: getNotifications` on XCUITest requires the app to be in the background (state ≤ 3) — notifications are not delivered to the Notification Center while the app is in the foreground (state 5). On Simulator, scheduled local notifications can be delivered reliably; remote APNs notifications require the Simulator's APNs sandbox payload injection (Xcode 14+) or an actual APNs connection (rare in CI). On real devices, calling `mobile: getNotifications` while the screen is locked returns only notifications delivered after the last unlock — use `mobile: unlock` before reading the list. The `identifier` field is the `UNNotificationRequest.identifier` set by your app — coordinate with the backend/push team to use a predictable, test-specific identifier format (e.g., `test-ORD-<orderId>`) to avoid matching production notifications.

---

**Pattern 640** — Android `mobile: pressKey` for Testing Hardware Back-Button Navigation Stack Integrity
```typescript
// mobile:pressKey sends Android KeyEvent codes (keycode integers) to the device.
// KEYCODE_BACK = 4; use instead of driver.back() which has deprecated semantics in Appium 2.
const KEYCODE_BACK    = 4;
const KEYCODE_HOME    = 3;
const KEYCODE_RECENT  = 187;

async function pressBack(times = 1): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < times; i++) {
    await driver.execute('mobile: pressKey', { keycode: KEYCODE_BACK });
    await browser.pause(150); // allow FragmentManager back-stack pop animation
  }
}

it('back-button unwinds checkout funnel in correct order: review → cart → product', async () => {
  // Navigate forward through the funnel.
  await $('~addToCartButton').click();
  await $('~cartScreen').waitForDisplayed();
  await $('~checkoutButton').click();
  await $('~reviewScreen').waitForDisplayed();

  // Unwind with back button.
  await pressBack();
  await expect($('~cartScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
  await pressBack();
  await expect($('~productScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
  // One more back should exit to home (not crash).
  await pressBack();
  await expect($('~homeScreen')).toBeDisplayed();
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: pressKey` with `KEYCODE_BACK` dispatches to the Activity that currently has foreground focus — if a dialog or a `PopupWindow` has captured focus (e.g., an autocomplete dropdown), the first `pressBack()` dismisses the dialog, not the Activity. Always call `await $('~dialog').waitForExist({ reverse: true })` to confirm dialog dismissal before asserting the expected Activity is visible. `KEYCODE_BACK` is deprecated in Android 13 (Gesture Navigation): on devices running API 33+ with gesture navigation enabled, the `KEYCODE_BACK` event is still dispatched to the focused Activity via `OnBackInvokedCallback` but the animation differs (predictive back animation). Ensure your tests do not assert on transition animation frames when running on API 33+.

---

**Pattern 641** — WDIO v9 `@wdio/visual-service` `checkElement()` with `ignoreRegions` for Dynamic Content Masking in Visual Regression Tests
```typescript
// checkElement() scopes the screenshot to a single element, reducing noise.
// ignoreRegions masks dynamic content (badges, timestamps, ads) within the element's bounds.
import type { IgnoreRegions } from '@wdio/visual-service';

interface VisualCheckOptions {
  /** Element-relative pixel regions to mask before comparison */
  ignoreRegions?: IgnoreRegions[];
  /** Mismatch percentage threshold before failure (0.0–100.0) */
  misMatchPercentage?: number;
}

async function checkWithMasking(
  selector: string,
  baselineName: string,
  opts: VisualCheckOptions = {}
): Promise<void> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  await el.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  const result = await browser.checkElement(el, baselineName, {
    misMatchPercentage: opts.misMatchPercentage ?? 0.5,
    ignoreRegions:      opts.ignoreRegions ?? [],
  });
  expect(result).toBeLessThanOrEqual(opts.misMatchPercentage ?? 0.5);
}

it('product card visual matches baseline, masking the dynamic price badge', async () => {
  await checkWithMasking('~productCard', 'productCard-baseline', {
    misMatchPercentage: 0.8,
    ignoreRegions: [
      { x: 260, y: 8,  width: 60, height: 24 }, // sale badge (dynamic text)
      { x: 0,   y: 130, width: 320, height: 20 }, // price row (varies by A/B test)
    ],
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `ignoreRegions` coordinates in `checkElement()` are relative to the element's top-left corner in device pixels — on high-DPI devices (3× scale), a 20 pt badge occupies a 60 px region. Derive `ignoreRegions` from `el.getSize()` fractions rather than hard-coding pixel offsets: `{ x: Math.round(size.width * 0.8), y: 0, width: Math.round(size.width * 0.2), height: 24 }`. On Android, `@wdio/visual-service` uses the UIAutomator2 screenshot API which captures the full display including the status bar unless `appium:nativeWebScreenshot: true` is set — set it to avoid status-bar clock rendering differences across CI runs. Baseline images must be regenerated when device screen density or OS version changes; store them in a versioned subfolder (`baselines/ios-17/`, `baselines/android-14/`) keyed to OS major version.

---

**Pattern 642** — Appium + WDIO `mobile: getContexts` with `returnDetailedContexts` + Process ID Filtering for Multi-Process WebView Disambiguation
```typescript
// On Android apps with multiple WebView-hosting processes (e.g., an in-app browser +
// an ad SDK WebView), returnDetailedContexts exposes the 'pid' field to disambiguate.
interface DetailedContext {
  id:    string;
  title?: string;
  url?:  string;
  pid?:  number;       // Android only: WebView renderer process ID
  packageName?: string; // Android only: hosting package
  bundleId?:   string;  // iOS only
}

async function switchToWebViewByPackage(pkg: string): Promise<string> {
  const ctxs: DetailedContext[] = await driver.execute('mobile: getContexts', {
    androidWebviewConnectionRetryTime: 500,
    androidWebviewConnectTimeout:      8_000,
    returnDetailedContexts:            true,
  });
  const target = ctxs.find(c => c.packageName === pkg && c.id !== 'NATIVE_APP');
  if (!target) throw new Error(`No WebView context found for package ${pkg}`);
  await browser.switchContext(target.id);
  return target.id;
}

it('switches to the in-app browser WebView (not the AdMob WebView)', async () => {
  await $('~openInAppBrowserButton').click();
  await browser.pause(1_500); // allow WebView to register with Chrome DevTools

  const ctxId = await switchToWebViewByPackage('com.example.myapp');
  expect(ctxId).toMatch(/^WEBVIEW_/);

  const url = await browser.getUrl();
  expect(url).toMatch(/example\.com/);

  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```
Tradeoff: The `pid` field in `returnDetailedContexts` is populated only when UIAutomator2 can resolve the WebView's renderer PID via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` — on Android 11+ with scoped storage, this read is blocked for non-system apps unless the test runner has `READ_LOGS` permission (grantable only via ADB: `adb shell pm grant com.android.shell android.permission.READ_LOGS`). If `pid` is `undefined`, fall back to `packageName` filtering (reliable when the app owns the WebView) or `url`/`title` pattern matching (requires the page to have already loaded). On iOS, `mobile: getContexts` with `returnDetailedContexts` returns `bundleId` of the WKWebView host process — for app-extension WKWebViews (share sheet, Today widget), `bundleId` will be the extension's bundle ID, not the main app's.

---

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C59-1: WDIO v9 `element.waitForDisplayed()` returns `true` on iOS 17+ for elements inside a `UIVisualEffectView` blur layer even when the effect view itself is animating its alpha from 0 to 1, because XCUITest's `isHittable` check resolves against the element's `frame` in the coordinator space, not its rendered alpha**
When a modal bottom sheet uses `UIVisualEffectView` as its container and animates in over 300 ms, XCUITest reports the contained elements as `isHittable: true` from the moment the animation begins — because `isHittable` only checks that the element's `frame` is within screen bounds and not obscured by a _different_ element's `frame`. The animating `alpha` (0 → 1) on `UIVisualEffectView` is not reflected in `isHittable`. `element.waitForDisplayed()` in WDIO polls `isHittable`, so it resolves immediately at animation start rather than at animation end.

WHY: XCUITest's `XCUIElement.isHittable` property evaluates `accessibilityActivate` preconditions synchronously: element must be on-screen (`frame.intersects(screenBounds)`), not hidden (`isHidden == false`), and not obscured by another element at the hit-test point. It does NOT evaluate `layer.presentationLayer().opacity` — Core Animation `opacity` changes are visual-layer-only during animation and do not update the model layer until `animationDidStop`. `isHittable` reads the model layer's `hidden` and `alpha` (model alpha = 1.0 from frame 0), so it returns `true` immediately. Fix: after `element.waitForDisplayed()`, call `await browser.pause(350)` when the target element is a direct child of an animated `UIVisualEffectView`, or use `element.waitForStable()` (WDIO v9.28+ feature) which polls the element's bounding rect until it stops moving and applies a 2-frame stability window.

---

**Gotcha C59-2: Android `driver.setOrientation('LANDSCAPE')` on API 33+ with a `WindowInsets` consumer (edge-to-edge layout) silently rotates the display but does not trigger `onConfigurationChanged()` in the Activity when `android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize"` is declared in the manifest, causing layout metrics cached by the Activity to remain stale until the next `measure/layout` pass**
On Android 13 (API 33+), `setOrientation` is implemented via `IWindowManager.freezeRotation()` through the ADB instrumentation channel. When an Activity has `android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize"` in its manifest, it handles the orientation change itself (no recreate). However, on API 33+, the `WindowInsets` inset values (navigation bar height, status bar height, display cutout) are delivered to the Activity's `WindowInsetsController` asynchronously via a Binder IPC from the window manager — these are not synchronised with `onConfigurationChanged()`. If the Activity's layout code reads `WindowInsetsCompat.getInsets()` inside `onConfigurationChanged()` (a common pattern), it reads stale pre-rotation insets. The Activity's cached `contentViewHeight` (used for scroll position calculations) will be wrong until the next `requestLayout()` / `invalidate()` cycle, which is triggered by the next user interaction.

WHY: `WindowInsetsController.setSystemBarsAppearance()` and `WindowInsetsAnimation.Callback.onEnd()` are dispatched after `onConfigurationChanged()` completes — the insets are updated in a separate Choreographer frame. Any layout code that caches inset values synchronously in `onConfigurationChanged()` reads pre-rotation values. Tests that call `driver.setOrientation('LANDSCAPE')` and immediately assert on scroll position or element Y-coordinates may fail because the layout has not yet consumed the updated insets. Fix: after `setOrientation()`, execute `await driver.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'input', args: ['keyevent', 'KEYCODE_WAKEUP'] })` to force a display wake event (triggers a Choreographer vsync), then `await browser.pause(500)` to allow two full 60 Hz layout passes before asserting element positions.

**Gotcha C59-3: XCUITest `element.setValue()` on `UITextView` with `textContentType = .password` silently strips characters above Unicode code point U+00FF (Latin Extended-B and beyond) because the iOS secure text entry pipeline routes through `UIKeyboardImpl`'s `insertDictationResult:` path which applies `NSString.canBeConverted(to: .isoLatin1)` filtering before committing to the `UITextField` secure backing store**
When `setValue()` is called with a value containing characters outside ISO-8859-1 (e.g., Japanese hiragana in a password like `P@ssw0rd日本語`), XCUITest's secure text entry handler calls `UIKeyboardImpl.insertDictationResult:` which internally calls `NSString.canBeConverted(to: .isoLatin1)` on each character. Characters that return `false` (code points > U+00FF) are silently dropped — no error is raised. The `element.getText()` on a secure `UITextField` always returns an empty string (password fields never expose their text), so the silent truncation is undetectable via `getValue()`.

WHY: iOS's `UIKeyboardImpl` uses an ISO Latin-1 normalization pass for secure input to prevent keyboard injection attacks via Unicode lookalikes. This check was introduced in iOS 15.4 and applies regardless of `appium:keyboardLocale` or session locale settings. The check is performed against the _raw_ code points before any Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD), so composed characters like `é` (U+00E9, within Latin-1) pass, but precomposed `e` + combining accent (U+0301, outside Latin-1 base range combined with an out-of-range character) may fail. Fix: for password fields requiring non-Latin characters, use `mobile: type` with `text:` (key-by-key simulation) which bypasses `insertDictationResult:` and routes through `UIKeyInput.insertText()` directly. Alternatively, test non-ASCII password validation at the unit/API layer and limit E2E password tests to printable ASCII (`0x20–0x7E`).

**Gotcha C59-4: WDIO v9 `browser.execute()` returns `undefined` instead of the expected value when executed in Android WebView context and the script uses `async function` syntax, because the Chromium CDP `Runtime.evaluate` endpoint used by UIAutomator2's WebView bridge does not support `awaitPromise: true` by default and WDIO does not set it for `execute()` (only `executeAsync()` sets `awaitPromise`)**
When `browser.execute(async () => { return await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json()); })` is called inside an Android WebView context, the CDP call translates to `Runtime.evaluate` with `expression: "(async () => { return await fetch(...) })()"`. The resulting CDP response contains `{ type: 'object', subtype: 'promise' }` — a pending Promise — not the resolved value. WDIO's `execute()` deserialises the CDP response and returns `undefined` for unresolved Promise objects (it does not await the Promise). The test proceeds with `result === undefined` and may silently pass assertions like `expect(result).toBeDefined()` never triggering correctly.

WHY: `Runtime.evaluate` returns the value synchronously — for an async expression it returns a Promise object unless `awaitPromise: true` is specified in the CDP parameters. WDIO v9's `execute()` implementation maps to CDP `Runtime.evaluate` without `awaitPromise: true`; `executeAsync()` wraps the script in a callback pattern (not `awaitPromise`) — so even `executeAsync()` does not wait for a Promise returned from an `async` function unless you call `resolve(await ...)` inside the callback. Fix: wrap async logic in a `Promise`-accepting callback for `executeAsync()`: `browser.executeAsync((resolve, reject) => { fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json()).then(resolve).catch(reject); })`. Or use WDIO v9.25+ which adds `browser.executeWithReason()` that internally sets `awaitPromise: true` for CDP targets.

**Gotcha C59-5: Appium 2 `driver.getWindowHandles()` inside an iOS WKWebView returns only one handle even when the WKWebView has opened a `window.open()` popup, because WKWebView's `WKUIDelegate.webView(_:createWebViewWith:for:windowFeatures:)` creates a new `WKWebView` instance (not a new OS-level window) and XCUITest/WebKit inspector treats each `WKWebView` instance as a separate context (not a window handle) within the same Remote Automation session**
`driver.getWindowHandles()` in WDIO/Appium WebKit inspector mode corresponds to the `Automation.getBrowsingContexts` Safari Web Inspector command. When `window.open()` is called in a WKWebView, the `WKUIDelegate` creates a second `WKWebView` and presents it modally — but the new `WKWebView` is registered as a second _target_ in the WebKit inspector, not as a new browsing context in the same session. `getWindowHandles()` only enumerates browsing contexts within the already-attached inspector session (the primary `WKWebView`) and does not detect new `WKWebView` targets created by `window.open()`.

WHY: Safari/WebKit Web Inspector's `Automation.getBrowsingContexts` command only reports browsing contexts that have been explicitly attached to the current automation session via `Inspector.enable`. A new `WKWebView` created by `WKUIDelegate` is an independent WKWebView instance with its own `WKProcessPool` — it has not had `Inspector.enable` called on its `WebInspectorProxy`. Appium's WebKit inspector bridge connects to the initial WKWebView's inspector proxy at session creation and does not subscribe to new proxy registrations. Fix: on iOS, intercept `window.open()` at the application layer — override `WKUIDelegate.webView(_:createWebViewWith:...)` to load the URL in the existing `WKWebView` instead of creating a new one (requires app instrumentation in Debug builds). For testing popup URL handling in E2E, use `browser.execute(() => { window._lastOpenedUrl = null; window.open = (url) => { window._lastOpenedUrl = url; }; })` to monkey-patch `window.open` and assert on `window._lastOpenedUrl` via `browser.execute(() => window._lastOpenedUrl)`.

**Pattern 643** — XCUITest `mobile: setPermission` for Runtime Permission State Control Without Alert Interaction
```typescript
interface PermissionMap {
  camera?: 'yes' | 'no' | 'unset';
  microphone?: 'yes' | 'no' | 'unset';
  photos?: 'yes' | 'no' | 'inlimited' | 'limited' | 'unset';
  location?: 'always' | 'inuse' | 'never' | 'unset';
  contacts?: 'yes' | 'no' | 'unset';
  notifications?: 'yes' | 'no' | 'unset';
}

async function setAppPermissions(
  bundleId: string,
  permissions: PermissionMap
): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: setPermission', {
    bundleId,
    access: permissions,
  });
}

it('shows camera feed when camera permission is granted', async () => {
  const BUNDLE_ID = process.env.APP_BUNDLE_ID!;

  // Grant camera before the app checks it — avoids flaky permission alert handling
  await setAppPermissions(BUNDLE_ID, { camera: 'yes' });

  await driver.execute('mobile: activateApp', { bundleId: BUNDLE_ID });

  const cameraPreview = await $('~CameraPreviewView');
  await cameraPreview.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4000 });
  expect(await cameraPreview.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
});

afterEach(async () => {
  // Reset to unset so next test starts from a clean grant state
  await setAppPermissions(process.env.APP_BUNDLE_ID!, {
    camera: 'unset',
    microphone: 'unset',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: setPermission` writes directly to the `TCC.db` (Transparency, Consent, and Control database) via Simulator or SpringBoard daemon on real device — this bypasses the iOS permission alert dialog entirely, which eliminates alert-dismiss flakiness but also means the test never exercises the alert presentation code path; use a dedicated alert-flow test (with `mobile: alert` `action: accept`) for that contract separately.

**Pattern 644** — UIAutomator2 `mobile: batteryInfo` for Battery-Level–Gated Test Skip in CI Environments
```typescript
interface BatteryInfo {
  level: number;  // 0.0–1.0
  state: number;  // 1=unplugged, 2=charging, 3=full, 4=unknown
}

const BATTERY_STATE = { UNPLUGGED: 1, CHARGING: 2, FULL: 3 } as const;

async function getBatteryInfo(): Promise<BatteryInfo> {
  return driver.execute('mobile: batteryInfo', {}) as Promise<BatteryInfo>;
}

async function skipIfBatteryLow(threshold = 0.15): Promise<void> {
  const info = await getBatteryInfo();
  if (
    info.state === BATTERY_STATE.UNPLUGGED &&
    info.level < threshold
  ) {
    pending(
      `Skipping battery-drain test: device battery at ${Math.round(info.level * 100)}% unplugged`
    );
  }
}

it('completes GPS trace under battery drain scenario', async () => {
  await skipIfBatteryLow(0.20);

  // Only runs on devices that won't auto-shutdown mid-test
  await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'settings',
    args: ['put', 'global', 'battery_saver_mode', '1'],
  });

  const startLocation = await driver.execute('mobile: getLocation', {});
  await browser.pause(3000);
  const endLocation = await driver.execute('mobile: getLocation', {});

  expect(endLocation).not.toEqual(startLocation);
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: batteryInfo` on Android emulators always returns `level: 1.0` and `state: 2` (charging) regardless of emulator battery settings unless you explicitly set `adb emu power capacity <level>` and `adb emu power status discharging` before the session — in CI with hardware-accelerated AVDs (Google APIs), `state` is always 2, so battery-gated skips are only meaningful on real-device farms (Firebase Test Lab, BrowserStack Real Device).

**Pattern 645** — WDIO v9 `browser.action()` W3C Pointer Sequence for Two-Finger Pinch Zoom on iOS Simulator
```typescript
interface PinchOptions {
  centerX: number;
  centerY: number;
  spreadPx: number;       // finger separation at start
  targetSpreadPx: number; // finger separation at end
  durationMs?: number;
}

async function pinchZoom(opts: PinchOptions): Promise<void> {
  const {
    centerX, centerY, spreadPx, targetSpreadPx, durationMs = 400,
  } = opts;

  const finger1 = browser.action('pointer', {
    parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' },
  });
  const finger2 = browser.action('pointer', {
    parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' },
  });

  finger1
    .move({ x: centerX - spreadPx / 2, y: centerY, duration: 0 })
    .down({ button: 0 })
    .move({ x: centerX - targetSpreadPx / 2, y: centerY, duration: durationMs })
    .up({ button: 0 });

  finger2
    .move({ x: centerX + spreadPx / 2, y: centerY, duration: 0 })
    .down({ button: 0 })
    .move({ x: centerX + targetSpreadPx / 2, y: centerY, duration: durationMs })
    .up({ button: 0 });

  await browser.actions([finger1, finger2]);
}

it('pinch-zooms the map view to a detail level', async () => {
  const { width, height } = await browser.getWindowSize();
  const cx = Math.round(width / 2);
  const cy = Math.round(height / 2);

  await pinchZoom({ centerX: cx, centerY: cy, spreadPx: 60, targetSpreadPx: 200 });

  const zoomLabel = await $('~MapZoomLevelLabel');
  const zoomText = await zoomLabel.getText();
  expect(Number(zoomText)).toBeGreaterThan(10); // zoom level > 10
});
```
Tradeoff: The W3C Actions `browser.action()` API dispatches simultaneous pointer events only when both sequences are passed to `browser.actions([...])` as an array — if you `await` each `browser.actions([finger1])` and `browser.actions([finger2])` sequentially, they become serial single-finger events which will not trigger the pinch gesture recognizer; always compose both sequences into one `actions([f1, f2])` call. On Android UIAutomator2, prefer `mobile: pinchOpenGesture` / `mobile: pinchCloseGesture` which use native `android.view.MotionEvent` injection and are more reliable on real devices with aggressive touch-event coalescence.

**Pattern 646** — XCUITest `mobile: deepLink` for Cold-Start Deep Link Navigation Assertion
```typescript
interface DeepLinkArgs {
  url: string;
  bundleId: string;
}

async function openDeepLink(url: string, bundleId: string): Promise<void> {
  // Terminate app first to test cold-start deep link handling
  await driver.execute('mobile: terminateApp', { bundleId });
  await driver.execute('mobile: deepLink', { url, bundleId } satisfies DeepLinkArgs);
}

it('cold-start deep link navigates to the correct product detail page', async () => {
  const BUNDLE_ID = process.env.APP_BUNDLE_ID!;
  const PRODUCT_ID = 'SKU-9876';

  await openDeepLink(`myapp://products/${PRODUCT_ID}`, BUNDLE_ID);

  // Allow time for app launch + navigation stack reconstruction
  const productTitle = await $('~ProductDetailTitle');
  await productTitle.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });

  const titleText = await productTitle.getText();
  expect(titleText).toContain(PRODUCT_ID);

  // Verify navigation stack allows back navigation to home
  await $('~NavigationBackButton').click();
  const homeHeader = await $('~HomeScreenHeader');
  await homeHeader.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: deepLink` on XCUITest launches the app via `xcrun simctl openurl` (Simulator) or `LSApplicationWorkspace openURL:withOptions:` (real device) — on iOS 17+, universal links backed by Associated Domains require a network round-trip to verify the AASA (Apple App Site Association) file on first launch per device, which can add 2–8 seconds of latency before the app opens; for CI speed, use custom URL schemes (`myapp://`) instead of universal links (`https://`) in test builds by adding a separate scheme to the debug scheme list in Info.plist.

**Pattern 647** — UIAutomator2 `mobile: deviceInfo` for Dynamic Capability Branching by SDK Level and Screen Density
```typescript
interface AndroidDeviceInfo {
  androidId: string;
  apiVersion: string;       // e.g. "33"
  platformVersion: string;  // e.g. "13"
  brand: string;
  model: string;
  screenDensity: number;    // dpi
  screenSize: string;       // e.g. "1080x2400"
  fingerprint: string;
}

async function getDeviceInfo(): Promise<AndroidDeviceInfo> {
  return driver.execute('mobile: deviceInfo', {}) as Promise<AndroidDeviceInfo>;
}

it('uses density-correct drag distance for the pull-to-refresh gesture', async () => {
  const info = await getDeviceInfo();
  const apiLevel = parseInt(info.apiVersion, 10);
  const dpi = info.screenDensity;

  // Android 12+ (API 31+) stretch overscroll requires a longer drag
  const dragMultiplier = apiLevel >= 31 ? 1.4 : 1.0;
  // Normalise drag distance to dp, then convert to px for this screen density
  const dragDistancePx = Math.round(120 * (dpi / 160) * dragMultiplier);

  const [screenWidth, screenHeight] = info.screenSize.split('x').map(Number);
  const startY = Math.round(screenHeight * 0.35);
  const endY = startY + dragDistancePx;
  const cx = Math.round(screenWidth / 2);

  await driver.execute('mobile: swipeGesture', {
    left: cx - 10, top: startY, width: 20, height: dragDistancePx,
    direction: 'down', speed: 800,
  });

  const refreshIndicator = await $('~RefreshIndicator');
  await refreshIndicator.waitForExist({ timeout: 3000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: deviceInfo` returns cached values read at session init time — `screenDensity` reflects the device's physical DPI but not any display zoom setting the user may have enabled (`Settings > Display > Font and display size`); for precise dp-to-px conversion that accounts for display zoom, read `wm density` via `mobile: shell` and parse the `Override density` value, using it in place of `screenDensity` when non-zero.

**Pattern 648** — WDIO v9 `browser.reloadSession()` for Stateless Test Isolation Without Full Driver Restart
```typescript
interface SessionResetOptions {
  resetApp?: boolean;      // uninstall + reinstall (Android) or terminate (iOS)
  clearKeychain?: boolean; // iOS only: clear app keychain items
}

async function resetSession(opts: SessionResetOptions = {}): Promise<void> {
  const { resetApp = false, clearKeychain = false } = opts;

  if (resetApp && process.env.PLATFORM === 'android') {
    await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'pm',
      args: ['clear', process.env.APP_PACKAGE!],
    });
  }

  if (clearKeychain && process.env.PLATFORM === 'ios') {
    // Clear only the app's keychain group, not system keychain
    await driver.execute('mobile: clearKeychainItems', {
      bundleId: process.env.APP_BUNDLE_ID!,
    });
  }

  await browser.reloadSession();
}

beforeEach(async () => {
  // Reuse the Appium session (no new WDA/UIA2 server launch) but reset app state
  await resetSession({ resetApp: true, clearKeychain: true });
});

it('shows onboarding flow to a fresh-install user', async () => {
  const onboardingTitle = await $('~OnboardingWelcomeTitle');
  await onboardingTitle.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  expect(await onboardingTitle.getText()).toBe('Welcome to MyApp');
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.reloadSession()` avoids the 10–30 second overhead of starting a new WDA (WebDriverAgent) or UIA2 server process between tests, but it resets the WDIO element cache and any `browser.addCommand()` extensions registered on the `browser` object during the previous session — re-register custom commands in a `before` hook (not `beforeEach`) and use `browser.overwriteCommand()` for idempotent registration to avoid duplicate-command errors on the second call.

**Pattern 649** — XCUITest `mobile: listApps` with `applicationType: 'User'` for Installed-App Assertion in CI Provisioning Tests
```typescript
interface InstalledApp {
  bundleId: string;
  name: string;
  version: string;
  buildVersion: string;
}

async function listUserApps(): Promise<InstalledApp[]> {
  const result = await driver.execute('mobile: listApps', {
    applicationType: 'User',
    returnAttributes: [
      'bundleId',
      'CFBundleDisplayName',
      'CFBundleShortVersionString',
      'CFBundleVersion',
    ],
  });
  return (result as Array<Record<string, string>>).map(app => ({
    bundleId: app.bundleId,
    name: app.CFBundleDisplayName,
    version: app.CFBundleShortVersionString,
    buildVersion: app.CFBundleVersion,
  }));
}

it('target app version matches the expected release build', async () => {
  const EXPECTED_BUNDLE_ID = process.env.APP_BUNDLE_ID!;
  const EXPECTED_VERSION = process.env.EXPECTED_APP_VERSION!; // e.g. "4.2.1"

  const apps = await listUserApps();
  const targetApp = apps.find(a => a.bundleId === EXPECTED_BUNDLE_ID);

  expect(targetApp).toBeDefined();
  expect(targetApp!.version).toBe(EXPECTED_VERSION);
  expect(targetApp!.bundleId).toBe(EXPECTED_BUNDLE_ID);
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: listApps` with `applicationType: 'User'` enumerates only user-installed apps via `LSApplicationWorkspace allInstalledApplications` — on iOS 16+ with App Clips installed, the App Clip (`*.clip` bundle ID suffix) appears as a separate entry in the user app list alongside the full app; filter out App Clip entries by checking `!bundleId.endsWith('.clip')` when asserting installed-app counts to avoid false positives in provisioning validation suites.

**Pattern 650** — WDIO v9 `element.getComputedRole()` and `element.getComputedLabel()` for Accessibility Tree Compliance Testing
```typescript
interface A11yAssertion {
  selector: string;
  expectedRole: string;
  expectedLabel: string | RegExp;
}

async function assertAccessibilityTree(assertions: A11yAssertion[]): Promise<void> {
  for (const { selector, expectedRole, expectedLabel } of assertions) {
    const el = await $(selector);
    await el.waitForExist({ timeout: 3000 });

    const role = await el.getComputedRole();
    const label = await el.getComputedLabel();

    expect(role).toBe(expectedRole);

    if (typeof expectedLabel === 'string') {
      expect(label).toBe(expectedLabel);
    } else {
      expect(label).toMatch(expectedLabel);
    }
  }
}

it('checkout button meets WCAG 2.1 accessible name and role requirements', async () => {
  await assertAccessibilityTree([
    {
      selector: '~CheckoutButton',
      expectedRole: 'button',
      expectedLabel: /^Checkout \(\d+ items?\)$/,
    },
    {
      selector: '~CartItemCount',
      expectedRole: 'status',
      expectedLabel: /^\d+ items? in cart$/,
    },
    {
      selector: '~PriceDisplay',
      expectedRole: 'text',
      expectedLabel: /^\$[\d,]+\.\d{2}$/,
    },
  ]);
});
```
Tradeoff: `getComputedRole()` and `getComputedLabel()` map to WebDriver's `Get Computed Role` and `Get Computed Label` commands (W3C spec §16.2/16.3) and work only in a WebView/browser context (native app elements do not expose computed ARIA roles via WebDriver); for native iOS/Android accessibility role assertions, use `getAttribute('type')` on XCUITest (returns `XCUIElementType` string like `"Button"`, `"StaticText"`) or `getAttribute('class')` on UIAutomator2 (returns Android View class name like `"android.widget.Button"`).

**Pattern 651** — Appium `mobile: getPasteboard` (iOS) / `driver.getClipboard()` (Android) for Cross-Platform Clipboard Content Assertion
```typescript
const ClipboardContentType = { PLAINTEXT: 'plaintext' } as const;
type ClipboardType = typeof ClipboardContentType[keyof typeof ClipboardContentType];

async function getClipboardText(): Promise<string> {
  if (process.env.PLATFORM === 'ios') {
    const result = await driver.execute('mobile: getPasteboard', {
      encoding: 'plaintext',
    }) as { content: string };
    return result.content;
  } else {
    // Android: driver.getClipboard() returns base64-encoded content
    const b64 = await driver.getClipboard(ClipboardContentType.PLAINTEXT as ClipboardType);
    return Buffer.from(b64, 'base64').toString('utf-8');
  }
}

async function setClipboardText(text: string): Promise<void> {
  if (process.env.PLATFORM === 'ios') {
    await driver.execute('mobile: setPasteboard', {
      content: text,
      encoding: 'plaintext',
    });
  } else {
    await driver.setClipboard(
      Buffer.from(text, 'utf-8').toString('base64'),
      ClipboardContentType.PLAINTEXT as ClipboardType
    );
  }
}

it('copy-to-clipboard button places the share URL in the pasteboard', async () => {
  await $('~ShareButton').click();
  await $('~CopyLinkMenuItem').click();

  const clipText = await getClipboardText();
  expect(clipText).toMatch(/^https:\/\/myapp\.example\.com\/share\//);
  expect(new URL(clipText)).toBeTruthy(); // valid URL
});
```
Tradeoff: On iOS 16+ real devices (not Simulator), `mobile: getPasteboard` requires the app to have received a `UIPasteboardChangedNotification` in the current UI session — if the app has not yet accessed the pasteboard since the Appium session started, the XCUITest bridge may return an empty string instead of the actual content due to iOS's pasteboard access detection policy (introduced to prevent silent clipboard sniffing); work around this by first tapping an element that triggers an `UIPasteboard.general.string` read in the app, establishing pasteboard access permission in the session context.

**Pattern 652** — UIAutomator2 `mobile: type` for Unicode-Safe Text Entry Bypassing IME Input Processing
```typescript
interface TypeOptions {
  text: string;
}

async function typeTextSafe(element: WebdriverIO.Element, text: string): Promise<void> {
  await element.click(); // ensure focus
  await element.clearValue();

  // mobile: type routes through AccessibilityNodeInfo.performAction(ACTION_SET_TEXT)
  // — bypasses IME, safe for Unicode including CJK and emoji
  await driver.execute('mobile: type', { text } satisfies TypeOptions);

  // Verify entry to catch silent truncation
  const actual = await element.getValue();
  if (actual !== text) {
    throw new Error(
      `Text entry mismatch — expected "${text}" got "${actual}". ` +
      `Contains supplementary Unicode: ${[...text].some(c => c.codePointAt(0)! > 0xFFFF)}`
    );
  }
}

it('search field accepts emoji and CJK characters via safe text entry', async () => {
  const searchInput = await $('~SearchInputField');
  await searchInput.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });

  const testText = 'Search: 日本語 🔍 العربية';
  await typeTextSafe(searchInput, testText);

  const resultHeader = await $('~SearchResultsHeader');
  await resultHeader.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4000 });
  expect(await resultHeader.getText()).toContain('日本語');
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: type` uses `AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SET_TEXT` which sets the entire text atomically (not key-by-key) — this means `TextWatcher.beforeTextChanged()` / `afterTextChanged()` callbacks in the app still fire correctly, but `KeyEvent`-based listeners (apps that validate on physical key presses for security keyboards) will not fire; for apps that require `KeyEvent` delivery alongside text (custom OTP inputs, PIN pads), use `element.addValue()` which routes through the UIAutomator2 key injector and generates `ACTION_DOWN` / `ACTION_UP` events per character.

**Pattern 653** — Appium `mobile: startScreenRecording` / `mobile: stopScreenRecording` for Memory-Safe CI Video Artefact Capture
```typescript
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

const RECORDING_DIR = process.env.CI_ARTIFACT_DIR ?? './test-artifacts/recordings';

async function startRecording(): Promise<void> {
  fs.mkdirSync(RECORDING_DIR, { recursive: true });

  const opts = process.env.PLATFORM === 'ios'
    ? { videoQuality: 'medium', fps: 10, videoScale: '320:-2' }
    : { bitRate: 1_000_000, videoSize: '720x1280', timeLimit: 180 };

  await driver.execute('mobile: startScreenRecording', opts);
}

async function stopRecordingAndSave(label: string): Promise<string> {
  const base64 = await driver.execute('mobile: stopScreenRecording', {}) as string;
  const safeName = label.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_').slice(0, 80);
  const filePath = path.join(RECORDING_DIR, `${safeName}_${Date.now()}.mp4`);
  fs.writeFileSync(filePath, Buffer.from(base64, 'base64'));
  return filePath;
}

beforeEach(async function () {
  await startRecording();
});

afterEach(async function () {
  const title = this.currentTest?.title ?? 'unknown';
  const state = this.currentTest?.state;

  if (state === 'failed') {
    const filePath = await stopRecordingAndSave(`FAILED_${title}`);
    process.env.CI && console.log(`##[artifact]${filePath}`);
  } else {
    // Stop recording to avoid WDA memory leak but discard the payload
    await driver.execute('mobile: stopScreenRecording', {});
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: startScreenRecording` on iOS uses `XCUIScreen.mainScreen.video` API which records at up to 60 fps but the base64 payload returned by `mobile: stopScreenRecording` is held entirely in memory in the WDA process — on long tests (> 2 minutes at medium quality), the in-memory buffer can exceed 200 MB and cause WDA to be killed by jetsam (iOS memory pressure manager); mitigate with `fps: 10` and `videoScale: '320:-2'` (half-width) to keep the buffer under 40 MB for a 3-minute test.

**Pattern 654** — XCUITest `mobile: alert` `getButtons` for Dynamic System Alert Button Discovery and Assertion
```typescript
type AlertAction = 'accept' | 'dismiss' | 'getButtons';

interface AlertButtonsResult {
  buttons: string[];
}

async function getAlertButtons(): Promise<string[]> {
  const result = await driver.execute('mobile: alert', {
    action: 'getButtons' as AlertAction,
  }) as AlertButtonsResult;
  return result.buttons;
}

async function tapAlertButton(label: string): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: alert', {
    action: 'dismiss',
    buttonLabel: label,
  });
}

it('location permission alert presents the correct button set for iOS 17', async () => {
  // Trigger location permission request
  await $('~EnableLocationButton').click();

  // Wait for the system alert to appear (WDA polls every 100ms up to 20s)
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      try {
        const buttons = await getAlertButtons();
        return buttons.length > 0;
      } catch {
        return false;
      }
    },
    { timeout: 8000, interval: 500 }
  );

  const buttons = await getAlertButtons();

  // iOS 17 location alert must include all three authorisation tiers
  expect(buttons).toContain('Allow While Using App');
  expect(buttons).toContain('Allow Once');
  expect(buttons).toContain("Don't Allow");

  await tapAlertButton('Allow While Using App');

  const locationIndicator = await $('~LocationActiveIndicator');
  await locationIndicator.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: alert` `getButtons` queries the XCUITest `XCUIElementTypeAlert` element hierarchy synchronously — if the system alert takes > 20 seconds to appear (e.g., SpringBoard is busy processing a first-run notification storm on a freshly provisioned real device), the command throws `Alert screen is not present` and the `waitUntil` catch block handles it; however, on iOS Simulator, SpringBoard alert timing is deterministic (< 500 ms) so the `waitUntil` overhead is minimal. Note that `buttonLabel` matching in `mobile: alert` is case-sensitive and locale-sensitive — run permission tests with `localeIdentifier: 'en-US'` in the session capabilities to prevent label mismatches on non-English system locales.

**Pattern 655** — WDIO v9 `browser.throttleCPU()` for Chromium WebView CPU-Throttled Slow-Render Performance Regression Testing
```typescript
interface RenderMetrics {
  renderTime: number; // ms from interaction to element displayed
  ttfi: number;       // ms to fully interactive (spinner dismissed)
  jankFrames: number; // performance marks for frames > 16ms
}

async function measureRenderUnderCpuLoad(
  triggerFn: () => Promise<void>,
  factor: number = 4
): Promise<RenderMetrics> {
  // CDP CPU throttle — Chromium WebView only
  await browser.throttleCPU(factor);

  const startTs = Date.now();
  await triggerFn();

  const targetEl = await $('~ContentLoadedIndicator');
  await targetEl.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
  const renderTime = Date.now() - startTs;

  await browser.throttleCPU(1); // restore to 1x (no throttle)

  // Read jank frame count from app-emitted performance marks
  const jankFrames = await browser.execute(
    () => performance.getEntriesByType('measure')
      .filter((e): e is PerformanceMeasure => e.name.startsWith('jank-frame'))
      .length
  );

  return { renderTime, ttfi: renderTime, jankFrames };
}

it('product list renders within 800ms on 4x CPU throttle (mid-range simulation)', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext(process.env.WEBVIEW_CONTEXT!);

  const result = await measureRenderUnderCpuLoad(
    async () => { await $('~ProductListTab').then(el => el.click()); },
    4
  );

  expect(result.renderTime).toBeLessThan(800);
  expect(result.jankFrames).toBeLessThan(3);
}, { timeout: 15_000 });
```
Tradeoff: `browser.throttleCPU()` uses CDP's `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` and works only in WebView/browser contexts backed by Chromium (Android WebView, Chrome) — it has no effect in `NATIVE_APP` context or on WKWebView (iOS); the throttle factor is applied to the renderer process CPU scheduler priority (not real hardware throttling), so results are host-machine-relative: a 4x throttle on a 16-core CI runner may produce different render times than a 4x throttle on a 4-core developer laptop — use relative comparisons (new-build vs baseline from the same CI tier) rather than absolute millisecond limits.

**Pattern 656** — UIAutomator2 `mobile: openNotifications` + `mobile: pressKey` for Push Notification Shade Deep-Link Testing
```typescript
async function openNotificationShade(): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: openNotifications', {});
  // Allow notification shade slide-down animation to complete (300ms typical)
  await browser.pause(400);
}

async function closeNotificationShade(): Promise<void> {
  await driver.execute('mobile: pressKey', {
    keycode: 4, // KEYCODE_BACK
  });
}

async function tapNotificationByTitle(title: string): Promise<void> {
  // AOSP resource ID: `com.android.systemui:id/notification_title`
  // OEM skins vary — XPath by text content is more portable
  const notifTitle = await $(
    `//android.widget.TextView[@text="${title}"]`
  );
  await notifTitle.waitForExist({ timeout: 3000 });
  await notifTitle.click();
}

it('push notification tap deep-links to the correct in-app screen', async () => {
  // Trigger push via ADB broadcast (test instrumentation)
  await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'am',
    args: [
      'broadcast', '-a', 'com.example.myapp.TEST_PUSH',
      '--es', 'title', 'Order Shipped',
      '--es', 'deeplink', 'myapp://orders/98765',
    ],
  });

  await browser.pause(1500); // notification processing latency

  await openNotificationShade();
  await tapNotificationByTitle('Order Shipped');

  const orderScreen = await $('~OrderDetailScreen');
  await orderScreen.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  const orderId = await $('~OrderIdLabel').getText();
  expect(orderId).toBe('98765');
});

afterEach(async () => {
  try {
    await closeNotificationShade();
  } catch {
    // shade may already be closed if test navigation succeeded
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: openNotifications` issues `UiDevice.openNotification()` which calls the `GLOBAL_ACTIONS_NOTIFICATION` accessibility action — on Samsung One UI 6+ and MIUI 14+, the notification shade is implemented as a custom `SurfaceView` overlay that is not fully accessible to UIAutomator2's `UiDevice` global action until the surface has received its first vsync; if `openNotifications()` returns without error but the shade is not visible, retry once after a 300 ms pause before asserting. On Android 13+ with full notification permission denied (`POST_NOTIFICATIONS` not granted), the app's notifications will not appear — assert `mobile: getPermission` for `notifications` before triggering the push broadcast.

**Pattern 657** — WDIO v9 `browser.mock()` for CDP Network Request Interception and Response Stubbing in Android WebView
```typescript
interface StubConfig {
  url: string | RegExp;
  responseBody: unknown;
  statusCode?: number;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
}

async function stubApiResponse(config: StubConfig): Promise<WebdriverIO.Mock> {
  const mock = await browser.mock(config.url, { method: 'GET' });

  mock.respond(config.responseBody, {
    statusCode: config.statusCode ?? 200,
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      ...config.headers,
    },
    fetchResponse: false, // do not pass through to real network
  });

  return mock;
}

it('product list renders error state when API returns 503', async () => {
  await browser.switchContext(process.env.WEBVIEW_CONTEXT!);

  const mock = await stubApiResponse({
    url: /\/api\/v2\/products/,
    responseBody: { error: 'Service temporarily unavailable' },
    statusCode: 503,
  });

  await browser.refresh();

  const errorBanner = await $('*=Service temporarily unavailable');
  await errorBanner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
  expect(await errorBanner.getText()).toContain('unavailable');

  // Verify the stub was actually hit
  expect(mock.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(mock.calls[0].response?.statusCode).toBe(503);

  await mock.restore();
  await browser.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.mock()` uses CDP `Fetch.enable` + `Fetch.fulfillRequest` to intercept requests — this requires the Android WebView to have `WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true)` (set automatically by UIAutomator2 on debuggable builds); on production builds with `debuggable: false`, CDP is unavailable and `browser.mock()` throws `Protocol error: Fetch is not enabled`; gate mock-based tests behind an env flag (e.g., `process.env.USE_MOCK_NETWORK`) and maintain a parallel test path using app-layer dependency injection (injecting a mock HTTP client via a test-only app initialization flag) for production-build E2E suites.

---

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha C60-1: WDIO v9 `element.scrollIntoView()` on Android UIAutomator2 silently no-ops when the target element is inside a `RecyclerView` whose adapter uses `DiffUtil` with `detectMoves: true`, because UIAutomator2's scroll-to-element uses `UiScrollable.scrollIntoView()` which invokes `performAction(AccessibilityNodeInfoCompat.ACTION_SCROLL_FORWARD)` — but `DiffUtil` with move detection holds a write-lock on the adapter during its diff calculation pass, causing the `notifyItemMoved()` call to queue behind the accessibility scroll action, which completes its frame but without the target item being in view**
Why this matters: When a `RecyclerView` receives a `submitList()` call with `DiffUtil` while a WDIO scroll-into-view action is in-flight, UIAutomator2 sends `ACTION_SCROLL_FORWARD` to the `RecyclerView`'s `AccessibilityNodeInfo`. The `RecyclerView.LayoutManager` executes the scroll action synchronously on the main thread. However, `DiffUtil.calculateDiff()` (when run on a background thread and then dispatched) calls `DiffUtil.DiffResult.dispatchUpdatesTo(adapter)` which triggers `notifyItemMoved()`/`notifyItemRangeChanged()`. The `LinearLayoutManager` suspends layout passes during a pending `notifyDataSetChanged()` batch — the scroll completes its pixel offset but the layout manager does not anchor to the target item's final position because the item's `ViewHolder` binding is marked as `stale` until the `RecyclerView.RecycledViewPool` finishes its rebind pass. The element appears to scroll, but `isDisplayed()` returns `false` immediately after.
Fix: Wait for the `RecyclerView` adapter to settle before scrolling: execute `await browser.pause(300)` after the data change event, or use `mobile: scrollGesture` with a coordinate-based approach instead of UIAutomator2 accessibility scroll — coordinate scrolls bypass `DiffUtil` contention by issuing `MotionEvent.ACTION_SCROLL` directly on the `RecyclerView`'s touch dispatcher, which does not interact with the accessibility scroll pathway.

---

**Gotcha C60-2: XCUITest `element.getValue()` on `UITextField` returns the `placeholder` text string (not an empty string) when the field is empty and `accessibilityValue` has been explicitly set to the placeholder string by the app developer via `UITextField.accessibilityValue = self.placeholder`, causing assertions like `expect(await field.getValue()).toBe('')` to incorrectly fail on empty fields**
Why this matters: iOS accessibility guidelines recommend setting `accessibilityValue` on form fields so VoiceOver announces the current value. When a developer does `field.accessibilityValue = field.placeholder ?? ""`, an empty `UITextField` exposes the placeholder string as its accessibility value. XCUITest's `element.value` property maps to `accessibilityValue` (not to the backing `text` property) — so WDIO's `getValue()` returns the placeholder string for an empty field. Tests that `clearValue()` and then assert `getValue() === ''` will fail if the field has this pattern, even though the field is genuinely empty.
Fix: Use `getProperty('value')` instead of `getValue()` for `UITextField` content assertions in WDIO — `getProperty('value')` maps to the WebDriver `Get Element Property` command which reads the underlying DOM/native `value` attribute (empty string for empty `UITextField`), bypassing the `accessibilityValue` override. Alternatively, assert on `getAttribute('value')` which on XCUITest returns the `label` attribute (rendered text) rather than `accessibilityValue`.

---

**Gotcha C60-3: Appium 2 `driver.installApp()` on iOS Simulator silently succeeds and returns no error but the app is not actually installed when the `.app` bundle was built with an `arm64` device slice only (missing the `x86_64` or `arm64-simulator` slice), because `xcrun simctl install` exits with code 0 but writes an error message to stderr that Appium's process wrapper does not capture as an exception**
Why this matters: Appium 2's XCUITest driver calls `xcrun simctl install <udid> <appPath>` to install on Simulator and checks only the exit code (0 = success). When a CI pipeline accidentally passes an ad-hoc signed device build (arm64 only, no Simulator slice) to the Simulator install step, `xcrun simctl install` exits 0 but emits `Failed to install <path>: The application's Info.plist does not contain a valid CFBundleExecutable` to stderr. Appium sees exit code 0, considers install successful, and proceeds to launch — but `xcrun simctl launch` immediately fails with `An error was encountered processing the command`. The Appium session creation fails at the `activateApp` step with a cryptic `Application with bundle id ... is not installed` error rather than an `installApp` failure.
Fix: After `driver.installApp()`, immediately call `driver.execute('mobile: listApps', { applicationType: 'User' })` and assert the expected `bundleId` is present in the returned list — this surfaces the silent install failure before the `activateApp` step. In the CI build pipeline, add an `lipo -info <AppBinary>` step before the Appium run to verify the binary contains both `x86_64` (Intel Simulator) or `arm64` (Apple Silicon Simulator with `ARCHS=arm64`) slices.

---

**Gotcha C60-4: UIAutomator2 `mobile: swipeGesture` fails to dismiss bottom sheets that use `BottomSheetBehavior.STATE_HALF_EXPANDED` on Android 14 (API 34) when the swipe's `endY` coordinate lands inside the `BottomSheetBehavior`'s `halfExpandedRatio` peek height dead zone, because Jetpack Material Components 1.11.0 widened the velocity-threshold guard to 25% of screen height, making previously sufficient 300px downward swipes snap back to `STATE_HALF_EXPANDED` instead of collapsing**
Why this matters: Prior to Jetpack Material Components 1.11.0 (released 2024-Q4), `BottomSheetBehavior.onStopNestedScroll()` used a velocity threshold of `ViewConfiguration.getScaledMinimumFlingVelocity() * 2` to decide whether to collapse a half-expanded sheet on a downward swipe. In 1.11.0, the threshold was raised to `ViewConfiguration.getScaledMinimumFlingVelocity() * 4` AND a position-based guard was added: if the swipe endpoint's Y coordinate is above `peekHeight + (screenHeight * 0.25)`, the sheet snaps back to `STATE_HALF_EXPANDED` regardless of velocity. WDIO test suites that used a fixed 300px downward swipe to dismiss bottom sheets now hit this dead zone on FWXGA+ (1080p+) screens because 300px is less than 25% of 2400px screen height.
Fix: Calculate the dismiss swipe endpoint dynamically — read the device screen height via `(await driver.execute('mobile: deviceInfo', {})).screenSize`, then set `endY = screenHeight * 0.85` (85% of screen height) which always clears the dead zone. Additionally, increase swipe speed to `2000` px/s (from the default `600` px/s) to exceed the raised velocity threshold: `driver.execute('mobile: swipeGesture', { left, top: sheetPeekY, width: 20, height: endY - sheetPeekY, direction: 'down', speed: 2000 })`.

---

**Gotcha C60-5: WDIO v9 `specFileRetries` causes Appium session capabilities to be replayed on retry with the same `appium:udid` that was valid for the first attempt, but on real-device CI farms (Bitrise, GitHub Actions with macOS runner + connected device) the device `udid` changes between retries if the device was disconnected and reconnected by the USB watchdog daemon, causing the retry session to fail immediately with `No device found with udid <stale-udid>`**
Why this matters: `specFileRetries` in WDIO creates a new browser session using the same `wdio.conf.ts` capabilities object that was evaluated at suite startup. The `appium:udid` capability is set once at process init (e.g., from `process.env.DEVICE_UDID` read at startup). On macOS CI runners, `usbmuxd` (USB multiplexer daemon) re-enumerates USB devices if a USB timeout occurs (default `IOUSBDevice.kSuspendTimeout = 5000ms`) — when the device re-enumerates, macOS assigns a new ECID-derived `udid` string for the USB connection session. The new `udid` differs from the one stored in the capabilities, so Appium's `appium-xcuitest-driver` device lookup fails with `No device found with udid`.
Fix: Move `udid` resolution out of the static capabilities object and into a WDIO `beforeSession` hook that calls `xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output -` (Xcode 15+) or `instruments -s devices` and matches by device name and iOS version — refreshing `udid` on every session start including retries. For Android, use `adb devices -l` in `beforeSession` and match by `model:` or `product:` label rather than serial number. This ensures each retry attempt uses the current live `udid` rather than a stale startup-time value.

**Pattern 658** — iOS Predicate String Selector with Compound Conditions for XCUITest Element Resolution
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface ProductCellLocators {
  minPrice: number;
  maxPrice: number;
  elementType: string;
}

async function findProductCellInPriceRange(
  locators: ProductCellLocators
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  // iOS predicate string: compound AND conditions, numeric range check
  const predicate =
    `type == '${locators.elementType}' && ` +
    `label BEGINSWITH '$' && ` +
    `value >= '${locators.minPrice}' && value <= '${locators.maxPrice}'`;
  const selector = `-ios predicate string:${predicate}`;
  const cell = await $(selector);
  await cell.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8000 });
  return cell;
}

describe('Product listing price filter', () => {
  it('finds a cell in the $10–$50 price band via predicate string', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.shop');
    const cell = await findProductCellInPriceRange({
      minPrice: 10,
      maxPrice: 50,
      elementType: 'XCUIElementTypeCell',
    });
    expect(await cell.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    const labelText = await cell.getAttribute('label');
    expect(labelText).toMatch(/^\$/);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: iOS predicate strings are evaluated entirely on-device by `XCUIElementQuery` before any result crosses the Appium WebDriver boundary, making compound predicates significantly faster than XPath queries that transfer the full element tree to the Node.js process; however, predicate string syntax uses NSPredicate semantics (`BEGINSWITH`, `CONTAINS`, `==`, `>=`) which differ from XPath axes — developers accustomed to XPath `contains()` must learn the NSPredicate string grammar, and numeric comparisons on `value` attributes always operate on string representations (requiring care with zero-padded numbers or locale-specific decimal separators in `label`).

**Pattern 659** — iOS Class Chain Selector for Hierarchical Container-Scoped Button Resolution
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface CartItemLocators {
  productName: string;
}

async function getCartItemDeleteButton(
  locators: CartItemLocators
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  // Class chain: descend from a cell whose label matches, then find a button child
  // backtick filter applies to the immediately preceding element type
  const chain =
    `**/XCUIElementTypeCell[\`label == '${locators.productName}'\`]` +
    `/**/XCUIElementTypeButton[\`name == 'Delete'\`]`;
  const selector = `-ios class chain:${chain}`;
  const deleteBtn = await $(selector);
  await deleteBtn.waitForEnabled({ timeout: 6000 });
  return deleteBtn;
}

describe('Cart item deletion', () => {
  it('resolves Delete button scoped to a specific product cell', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.cart');
    const deleteBtn = await getCartItemDeleteButton({ productName: 'Wireless Headphones' });
    expect(await deleteBtn.isEnabled()).toBe(true);
    await deleteBtn.click();
    const removedCell = await $(
      `-ios class chain:**/XCUIElementTypeCell[\`label == 'Wireless Headphones'\`]`
    );
    await removedCell.waitForExist({ timeout: 5000, reverse: true });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: iOS class chain selectors support backtick-predicate filters scoped to each traversal node and use `**/` for recursive descent, making them more expressive than predicate strings alone for deep hierarchies; the tradeoff is that class chain syntax is XCUITest-exclusive (no Android equivalent) and the backtick-delimited filter segments are easy to mis-escape when constructing dynamically in TypeScript template literals — always build the chain string through a factory function with explicit string escaping rather than inline template literals to avoid runtime NSPredicate parse errors that surface as unhelpful `invalid selector` Appium errors.

**Pattern 660** — Android UIAutomator2 `new UiSelector()` Compound Text + ClassName Selector
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface ButtonLocator {
  text: string;
  className: string;
}

async function findAndroidButtonByTextAndClass(
  locator: ButtonLocator
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  // android= prefix invokes UIAutomator2 Java UiSelector evaluation on-device
  const uiSelector = `new UiSelector().text("${locator.text}").className("${locator.className}")`;
  const selector = `android=${uiSelector}`;
  const element = await $(selector);
  await element.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 7000 });
  return element;
}

describe('Checkout flow confirm button', () => {
  it('finds the android.widget.Button with text "Confirm Order"', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.checkout');
    const confirmBtn = await findAndroidButtonByTextAndClass({
      text: 'Confirm Order',
      className: 'android.widget.Button',
    });
    expect(await confirmBtn.isClickable()).toBe(true);
    await confirmBtn.click();
    const successBanner = await $('~order_success_banner');
    await successBanner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10000 });
    expect(await successBanner.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: UIAutomator2 `UiSelector` expressions are compiled by the Android `uiautomator2` server into `AccessibilityNodeInfo` tree queries that run in-process on the device, making them faster than XPath; however, `UiSelector().text()` performs an exact, case-sensitive UTF-16 string match — localized apps that swap strings at runtime (e.g., via `LocaleListCompat`) must instead use `textContains()` or `textMatches()` with a regex, and long selector chains (`.childSelector()` nesting > 3 levels) significantly increase `AccessibilityNodeInfo` traversal time on Android 10+ due to the `TYPE_WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED` throttle added in API 29.

**Pattern 661** — Cross-Platform Accessibility ID (`~`) Selector with Graceful Fallback
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const PLATFORM = (process.env.PLATFORM ?? 'ios') as 'ios' | 'android';

interface A11yLocator {
  accessibilityId: string;
  iosFallbackPredicate?: string;
  androidFallbackUiSelector?: string;
}

async function findByA11yWithFallback(
  locator: A11yLocator
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  const primary = await $(`~${locator.accessibilityId}`);
  const exists = await primary.isExisting();
  if (exists) return primary;

  // Fallback for apps where accessibility IDs are inconsistently set
  if (PLATFORM === 'ios' && locator.iosFallbackPredicate) {
    return $(`-ios predicate string:${locator.iosFallbackPredicate}`);
  }
  if (PLATFORM === 'android' && locator.androidFallbackUiSelector) {
    return $(`android=${locator.androidFallbackUiSelector}`);
  }
  throw new Error(`Element not found: ~${locator.accessibilityId} (no fallback matched)`);
}

describe('Profile avatar tap', () => {
  it('taps profile avatar via accessibility ID with platform fallback', async () => {
    const avatar = await findByA11yWithFallback({
      accessibilityId: 'profile_avatar',
      iosFallbackPredicate: `type == 'XCUIElementTypeImage' && name CONTAINS 'avatar'`,
      androidFallbackUiSelector:
        'new UiSelector().descriptionContains("avatar").className("android.widget.ImageView")',
    });
    await avatar.click();
    const profileSheet = await $('~profile_bottom_sheet');
    await profileSheet.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });
    expect(await profileSheet.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `~accessibilityId` selector maps to `accessibilityIdentifier` on iOS and `content-description` on Android, providing a single cross-platform selector strategy that survives layout changes and text localization; the fallback chain adds resilience when accessibility IDs are missing from legacy screens, but it also masks missing-ID bugs in production builds — pair this pattern with a lint rule (e.g., a custom ESLint rule that flags `iosFallbackPredicate` usage) to track screens that still lack proper accessibility IDs and drive remediation sprints.

**Pattern 662** — WDIO v9 `browser.addCommand()` for a Reusable `scrollToElement` Mobile Helper
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

// Augment the WDIO Browser type to include the custom command
declare module 'webdriverio' {
  interface Browser {
    scrollToElement(
      element: WebdriverIO.Element,
      opts?: { maxSwipes?: number; direction?: 'up' | 'down' }
    ): Promise<void>;
  }
}

browser.addCommand(
  'scrollToElement',
  async function (
    this: WebdriverIO.Browser,
    element: WebdriverIO.Element,
    opts: { maxSwipes?: number; direction?: 'up' | 'down' } = {}
  ): Promise<void> {
    const { maxSwipes = 10, direction = 'down' } = opts;
    const { width, height } = await this.getWindowSize();
    const startY = direction === 'down' ? height * 0.8 : height * 0.2;
    const endY   = direction === 'down' ? height * 0.2 : height * 0.8;
    let swipes = 0;
    while (!(await element.isDisplayedInViewport()) && swipes < maxSwipes) {
      await this.action('pointer', { parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' } })
        .move({ x: Math.round(width / 2), y: Math.round(startY) })
        .down({ button: 0 })
        .pause(80)
        .move({ x: Math.round(width / 2), y: Math.round(endY), duration: 300 })
        .up({ button: 0 })
        .perform();
      swipes++;
    }
    if (!(await element.isDisplayedInViewport())) {
      throw new Error(`scrollToElement: element not in viewport after ${maxSwipes} swipes`);
    }
  }
);

describe('Long list scroll', () => {
  it('scrolls until the target item is visible', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.longlist');
    const targetItem = await $('~list_item_99');
    await browser.scrollToElement(targetItem, { maxSwipes: 15 });
    expect(await targetItem.isDisplayedInViewport()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.addCommand()` injects custom commands into the WDIO browser instance at runtime and supports full TypeScript augmentation via module declaration merging, making helpers like `scrollToElement` available as first-class API without wrapper imports; however, custom commands registered in a top-level spec file are not available in `before`/`beforeEach` hooks in other spec files unless the command is registered in `wdio.conf.ts` `onPrepare` or a shared setup file — `browser.reloadSession()` also resets custom command registrations added via `addCommand` called inside a `before` hook, requiring re-registration in `beforeEach` or moving `addCommand` calls to `wdio.conf.ts` `before` at the suite level.

**Pattern 663** — WDIO v9 `browser.overwriteCommand()` to Add Retry Logic to `element.click()`
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

declare module 'webdriverio' {
  interface Element {
    click(
      options?: WebdriverIO.ClickOptions & { retries?: number }
    ): Promise<void>;
  }
}

browser.overwriteCommand(
  'click',
  async function (
    this: WebdriverIO.Element,
    originalClick: (opts?: WebdriverIO.ClickOptions) => Promise<void>,
    options?: WebdriverIO.ClickOptions & { retries?: number }
  ): Promise<void> {
    const { retries = 2, ...clickOpts } = options ?? {};
    let lastError: Error | undefined;
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= retries; attempt++) {
      try {
        await this.waitForClickable({ timeout: 4000 });
        await originalClick(clickOpts);
        return;
      } catch (err) {
        lastError = err as Error;
        // Only retry on stale element or element not interactable
        if (
          !lastError.message.includes('StaleElementReferenceError') &&
          !lastError.message.includes('element not interactable')
        ) {
          throw lastError;
        }
        await browser.pause(300 * (attempt + 1));
      }
    }
    throw lastError;
  },
  true // attachToElement = true
);

describe('Dynamic list item click', () => {
  it('clicks a cell that may go stale during async data refresh', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.feed');
    const firstCell = await $('~feed_item_0');
    // Will retry up to 3 attempts on StaleElementReferenceError
    await firstCell.click({ retries: 3 });
    const detailView = await $('~detail_view_title');
    await detailView.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8000 });
    expect(await detailView.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.overwriteCommand()` wraps the built-in `click` with a retry envelope that handles `StaleElementReferenceError` and `element not interactable` — both common in React Native apps where bridge-dispatched state updates can re-render list cells between the element lookup and the tap — without requiring call-site changes; the tradeoff is that overwriting `click` globally can mask genuine test logic bugs where a click should fail (e.g., verifying a disabled state), so always gate the retry on explicit error message patterns rather than catching all errors, and expose a `retries: 0` escape hatch that callers can use when intentional failure assertion is required.

**Pattern 664** — WDIO v9 W3C `browser.action()` `pointer` `touch` Type for Long-Press Gesture
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface LongPressOptions {
  selector: string;
  durationMs?: number;
}

async function longPress(opts: LongPressOptions): Promise<void> {
  const { selector, durationMs = 1500 } = opts;
  const element = await $(selector);
  await element.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });
  const loc  = await element.getLocation();
  const size = await element.getSize();
  const centerX = Math.round(loc.x + size.width  / 2);
  const centerY = Math.round(loc.y + size.height / 2);

  await browser
    .action('pointer', { parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' } })
    .move({ x: centerX, y: centerY })
    .down({ button: 0 })
    .pause(durationMs)
    .up({ button: 0 })
    .perform();
}

describe('Long-press context menu', () => {
  it('opens context menu via long-press on a list item', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.files');
    await longPress({ selector: '~file_item_document_pdf', durationMs: 1500 });
    const contextMenu = await $('~context_menu_overlay');
    await contextMenu.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
    const deleteOption = await $('~context_menu_delete');
    expect(await deleteOption.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: W3C `browser.action('pointer', { parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' } })` with a `pause(durationMs)` between `down()` and `up()` is the most portable long-press implementation across WDIO v9 environments — it maps to `UIGestureRecognizer` `minimumPressDuration` on iOS and `GestureDetector.onLongPress()` on Android; the caveat is that Appium 2's `actions` endpoint on older UIAutomator2 versions (< 2.3.0) had a regression where `pause()` durations > 1000ms were silently clamped to 1000ms due to an Android `ViewConfiguration.getLongPressTimeout()` cap applied at the driver level — verify the UIAutomator2 driver version and use `mobile: longClickGesture` as a fallback for UIAutomator2 < 2.3.0 when durations > 1000ms are required.
