**Pattern 694** — `browser.appiumGetSystemBars()` — asserting status-bar and navigation-bar visibility for immersive mode and full-screen layout tests
```typescript
interface SystemBarInfo {
  visible: boolean;
  x: number;
  y: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}
interface SystemBars {
  statusBar: SystemBarInfo;
  navigationBar: SystemBarInfo;
}

async function assertImmersiveMode(): Promise<void> {
  const bars = await browser.appiumGetSystemBars() as SystemBars;
  expect(bars.statusBar.visible).toBe(false);
  expect(bars.navigationBar.visible).toBe(false);
}

async function assertNormalMode(): Promise<void> {
  const bars = await browser.appiumGetSystemBars() as SystemBars;
  expect(bars.statusBar.visible).toBe(true);
  expect(bars.statusBar.height).toBeGreaterThan(0);
}

describe('Full-screen video player', () => {
  it('hides system bars when video starts', async () => {
    await $('~play_button').click();
    await browser.pause(1_500); // allow window flag propagation
    await assertImmersiveMode();
  });

  it('restores system bars when video pauses', async () => {
    await $('~pause_button').click();
    await browser.pause(500);
    await assertNormalMode();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumGetSystemBars()` is Android-only and returns bar visibility based on `WindowInsets` reported by the `UiAutomation` accessibility service — on devices with display cutouts (notches, punch-hole cameras), the `y` coordinate of the status bar may be non-zero even when `visible: true`, and on Android 15+ with edge-to-edge enforcement the navigation bar reports `visible: false` by default for all apps regardless of the app's `SYSTEM_UI_FLAG` settings, so asserting `navigationBar.visible === true` will fail on API 35+ devices even when the bar is visually rendered as a translucent overlay.

**Pattern 695** — `browser.execute('mobile: scroll', ...)` — precise element-targeted scrolling without coordinate dependency
```typescript
async function scrollToElement(
  selector: string,
  direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right' = 'down',
  maxScrolls = 10
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  for (let i = 0; i < maxScrolls; i++) {
    const el = await $(selector);
    if (await el.isDisplayed()) return el;
    await browser.execute('mobile: scroll', {
      direction,
      // iOS: predicate-based scroll target; Android: use element strategy instead
      ...(driver.isIOS
        ? { predicateString: selector.startsWith('~') ? `name == "${selector.slice(1)}"` : undefined }
        : {}),
    });
    await browser.pause(300);
  }
  throw new Error(`Element ${selector} not found after ${maxScrolls} scrolls`);
}

describe('Long settings list', () => {
  it('reaches "About" section at bottom of settings', async () => {
    await $('~settings_nav_item').click();
    const aboutSection = await scrollToElement('~about_section', 'down');
    await aboutSection.click();
    await expect($('~app_version_label')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: scroll` with `predicateString` on iOS performs an XCUITest-native predicate scroll that targets the element directly — it is faster and more stable than coordinate-based swipe loops, but the `predicateString` syntax is iOS-only NSPredicate syntax; on Android the equivalent is `mobile: scrollGesture` with `elementId` or percentage-based bounds, so platform-branching is unavoidable; avoid `mobile: scroll` with no target predicate (i.e., direction-only scroll) on iOS Simulator because it maps to a fixed-distance scroll that ignores list boundary and can scroll past the target element on fast hardware.

---

**Pattern 696** — `browser.execute('mobile: swipe', ...)` — W3C Actions-free swipe for React Native ScrollView and FlatList
```typescript
interface SwipeParams {
  direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right';
  velocity?: number;   // iOS: points/s; Android: pixels/s
  percent?: number;    // fraction of scrollable area to traverse (0.0–1.0)
  elementId?: string;  // scope swipe to element rather than full screen
}

async function swipeOnElement(
  containerSelector: string,
  direction: SwipeParams['direction'],
  velocity = 800
): Promise<void> {
  const container = await $(containerSelector);
  await container.waitForDisplayed();
  const elementId = await container.elementId;
  await browser.execute('mobile: swipe', {
    direction,
    velocity,
    elementId,
  } as SwipeParams);
  await browser.pause(400); // settle after momentum
}

describe('Horizontal image carousel', () => {
  it('navigates to second image on swipe left', async () => {
    await $('~carousel_screen_nav').click();
    await swipeOnElement('~image_carousel', 'left', 1200);
    await expect($('~image_page_indicator_2')).toBeSelected();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: swipe` with `velocity` produces a momentum-based fling that closely matches user behaviour on iOS (XCUITest maps it to `XCUIGestureVelocity`) — however, on Android UIAutomator2, `velocity` is capped at a driver-internal maximum (~3000 pixels/s) and values above the cap are silently clamped, not errored; additionally, setting `velocity` too high on a React Native `FlatList` causes the virtualization buffer to under-render, resulting in items that are technically "scrolled to" but whose native view nodes have not yet been mounted, causing subsequent `isDisplayed()` checks to return `false` for 200–500 ms.

**Pattern 697** — `browser.execute('mobile: pinch', ...)` — map zoom and image scale gesture tests
```typescript
interface PinchParams {
  scale: number;    // > 1 = zoom in (spread), < 1 = zoom out (pinch), iOS only
  velocity: number; // rate of scale change per second
  elementId?: string;
}

async function pinchToZoom(
  selector: string,
  scale: number,
  velocity = 1.5
): Promise<void> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  await el.waitForDisplayed();
  const elementId = await el.elementId;
  // iOS XCUITest native pinch — no coordinate math needed
  await browser.execute('mobile: pinch', { scale, velocity, elementId } as PinchParams);
  await browser.pause(500);
}

describe('Map zoom controls', () => {
  it('zooms into city level on spread gesture', async () => {
    await $('~map_view').waitForDisplayed();
    const zoomBefore = await $('~zoom_level_label').getText();
    await pinchToZoom('~map_view', 2.5, 2.0);
    const zoomAfter = await $('~zoom_level_label').getText();
    expect(parseFloat(zoomAfter)).toBeGreaterThan(parseFloat(zoomBefore));
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: pinch` is iOS XCUITest only and maps directly to `XCUIElement.pinch(withScale:velocity:)` — on Android, pinch zoom must be simulated with the W3C Multi-Pointer Actions API using two simultaneous touch pointers, which requires calculating start/end coordinates from the element's bounding rect via `getLocation()` and `getSize()`, adding significant test boilerplate; also, on iOS 17+ apps using `UIScrollView` with `UIPinchGestureRecognizer` may require `velocity >= 1.0` or the gesture recogniser's minimum velocity threshold will reject the synthetic pinch.

---

**Pattern 698** — `browser.execute('mobile: dragFromToForDuration', ...)` — iOS drag-and-drop and reorder tests
```typescript
interface DragParams {
  duration: number;     // seconds to hold before drag initiates (typically 1.0–2.0)
  fromX: number; fromY: number;
  toX: number;   toY: number;
  pressDuration?: number;
}

async function dragElementToTarget(
  sourceSelector: string,
  targetSelector: string,
  holdDuration = 1.5
): Promise<void> {
  const [src, tgt] = await Promise.all([$(sourceSelector), $(targetSelector)]);
  const [srcLoc, tgtLoc, srcSize] = await Promise.all([
    src.getLocation(), tgt.getLocation(), src.getSize(),
  ]);
  const fromX = srcLoc.x + srcSize.width / 2;
  const fromY = srcLoc.y + srcSize.height / 2;
  const tgtSize = await tgt.getSize();
  const toX = tgtLoc.x + tgtSize.width / 2;
  const toY = tgtLoc.y + tgtSize.height / 2;
  await browser.execute('mobile: dragFromToForDuration', {
    duration: holdDuration,
    fromX, fromY, toX, toY,
  } as DragParams);
  await browser.pause(600);
}

describe('Kanban card reorder', () => {
  it('moves card from "To Do" to "In Progress" column', async () => {
    await dragElementToTarget('~todo_card_task_1', '~inprogress_column_dropzone');
    await expect($('~inprogress_column')).toHaveText(expect.stringContaining('Task 1'));
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: dragFromToForDuration` is iOS-only and requires `duration >= 1.0` for the long-press gesture recogniser to fire before the drag sequence begins — values below 1.0 result in a tap-and-swipe rather than a drag, silently depositing the element at the wrong position; on Android use `browser.action('pointer').move().down().move().up()` W3C pointer actions for drag, ensuring `duration` in the move step is >= 500 ms to trigger Android's `DragShadowBuilder` long-press threshold.

**Pattern 699** — `browser.installApp()` — dynamic APK/IPA sideloading within test sessions for multi-app integration tests
```typescript
interface InstallOptions {
  app: string;           // local path or URL
  checkVersion?: boolean; // skip reinstall if same version (Android only)
  grantPermissions?: boolean; // auto-grant all permissions at install (Android)
  replace?: boolean;     // force reinstall even if present
}

async function sideloadCompanionApp(
  appPath: string,
  bundleOrPackageId: string
): Promise<void> {
  const isInstalled = await browser.isAppInstalled(bundleOrPackageId);
  if (!isInstalled) {
    await browser.installApp(appPath);
    // Android: verify install by querying app state
    const state = await browser.queryAppState(bundleOrPackageId);
    // 1 = not running (installed), 0 = not installed
    if (state === 0) throw new Error(`Companion app failed to install: ${bundleOrPackageId}`);
  }
}

describe('Deep link from companion app', () => {
  before(async () => {
    await sideloadCompanionApp('./fixtures/companion.apk', 'com.example.companion');
  });

  it('opens main app via companion deep link', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.companion');
    await $('~trigger_deep_link_button').click();
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.app');
    await expect($('~deep_link_landing_screen')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.installApp()` wraps the Appium `install` driver command which uses `adb install` on Android and `ideviceinstaller` / `ios-deploy` on iOS — on Android, the install is blocking and returns after the package manager signals completion, but the app's `Application.onCreate()` is not called until first launch; on iOS real devices, `ideviceinstaller` can take 30–90 seconds for large IPAs and may silently fail with exit code 0 if the signing identity on the IPA does not match the device's provisioning profile, leaving the app absent from `isAppInstalled()` with no error raised by Appium.

**Pattern 700** — `browser.execute('mobile: deviceInfo', ...)` — reading device metadata for dynamic test branching and CI artefact tagging
```typescript
interface DeviceInfo {
  platformVersion: string;
  deviceName: string;
  deviceManufacturer: string;  // Android only
  deviceModel: string;
  deviceApiLevel?: number;     // Android only
  deviceScreenSize: string;    // e.g. "1080x1920"
  deviceScreenDensity?: number;
  deviceScreenDpi?: string;    // e.g. "xhdpi"
  realDevice: boolean;
}

async function getDeviceMetadata(): Promise<DeviceInfo> {
  return browser.execute('mobile: deviceInfo') as Promise<DeviceInfo>;
}

async function tagBuildWithDeviceInfo(): Promise<void> {
  const info = await getDeviceMetadata();
  // Inject metadata as custom capability for reporting plugins (Allure, ReportPortal)
  await browser.execute('lambdatest_executor: updateJob', {
    status: 'passed',
    reason: `${info.deviceName} — ${info.platformVersion} — ${info.deviceScreenSize}`,
  }).catch(() => { /* skip if not on LambdaTest */ });
  console.log(`[DEVICE] ${JSON.stringify(info)}`);
}

describe('Layout on high-density screen', () => {
  before(async () => { await tagBuildWithDeviceInfo(); });

  it('renders correctly at xhdpi density', async () => {
    const info = await getDeviceMetadata();
    if (info.deviceScreenDpi && !['xhdpi', 'xxhdpi', 'xxxhdpi'].includes(info.deviceScreenDpi)) {
      pending('Test targets high-density screens only');
    }
    await expect($('~icon_asset')).toHaveAttr('contentDesc', expect.stringContaining('@2x'));
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: deviceInfo` is supported on both iOS and Android in Appium 2.x but the returned fields differ by platform — `deviceApiLevel`, `deviceManufacturer`, `deviceScreenDensity`, and `deviceScreenDpi` are Android-only; iOS returns `deviceName`, `deviceModel`, `platformVersion`, and `realDevice`, but omits display density because UIKit uses logical points not physical pixels; always guard per-field access with optional chaining (`info.deviceApiLevel?.toString()`) to avoid `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` when the same helper is shared across platforms in a cross-platform test suite.

**Pattern 701** — `browser.execute('mobile: deepLink', ...)` with intent flag control for Android Universal Links and intent-based navigation
```typescript
interface DeepLinkOptions {
  url: string;
  package?: string;          // Android: explicit target package
  waitForLaunch?: boolean;   // Android: block until app foreground confirmed
  intentFlags?: number;      // Android: raw Intent flag bits (e.g. 0x10000000 = FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
}

async function navigateViaDeepLink(
  deepLinkUrl: string,
  opts: Partial<DeepLinkOptions> = {}
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: deepLink', {
    url: deepLinkUrl,
    package: opts.package,
    waitForLaunch: opts.waitForLaunch ?? true,
    intentFlags: opts.intentFlags,
  });
  // Settle: deep-link handler may push a navigation stack frame
  await browser.pause(800);
}

describe('Share extension deep link', () => {
  it('opens product page from share-sheet URL', async () => {
    const productUrl = 'myapp://products/detail?id=42';
    await navigateViaDeepLink(productUrl, { package: 'com.example.app' });
    await expect($('~product_title_label')).toBeDisplayed();
    await expect($('~product_id_label')).toHaveText('42');
  });

  it('returns to home when passed malformed URL', async () => {
    await navigateViaDeepLink('myapp://???', { package: 'com.example.app' });
    await expect($('~home_screen')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: On Android, `mobile: deepLink` fires an `am start` intent — if `waitForLaunch` is `true`, the driver polls `queryAppState` until the app is in foreground (state 4), which adds latency on slow emulators but prevents race conditions; on iOS, `mobile: deepLink` uses `XCUIApplication().open(URL)` which is synchronous but does not support Universal Link disambiguation when multiple apps claim the same URL domain — in that case the system sheet appears and the test must tap the correct app from the disambiguation sheet before proceeding, requiring an additional `$('~app_choice').click()` step that is not needed on Android.

**Pattern 702** — `browser.execute('mobile: type', ...)` — direct text injection bypassing XCUITest keyboard for fast and IME-independent input
```typescript
async function typeTextDirect(
  element: WebdriverIO.Element,
  text: string
): Promise<void> {
  await element.waitForEnabled();
  await element.click(); // ensure element has first-responder focus
  await browser.execute('mobile: type', { text });
  // Verify value was accepted — some fields have max-length or input filters
  const actual = await element.getValue();
  if (!actual.includes(text.slice(0, 10))) {
    throw new Error(`mobile: type did not commit text. Got: "${actual}"`);
  }
}

describe('Search with special characters', () => {
  it('searches using emoji and unicode in search field', async () => {
    await $('~search_bar').click();
    await typeTextDirect(await $('~search_input'), 'café ☕ test@example.com');
    await $('~search_submit').click();
    await expect($('~search_results_header')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: type` on iOS XCUITest injects text directly into the first-responder field without activating the software keyboard, making it 5–10x faster than `setValue()` for long strings and reliable for emoji and Unicode that the simulated keyboard mishandles — but it only sets the value when the element has first-responder focus (meaning `.click()` must precede `mobile: type`); on Android the equivalent is `element.setValue()` with `appium:unicodeKeyboard: true` and `appium:resetKeyboard: true` capabilities, because `mobile: type` does not exist in UIAutomator2.

### Community Gotchas

**C63-1** — `browser.appiumGetPerformanceData()` returns stale zeroes when called within 500 ms of app foreground — first poll is always zero
Why this matters: UIAutomator2's `getPerformanceData` command reads `/proc/<pid>/status` and Android's battery/network stats collector, which update on a 500 ms kernel tick. When a test calls `activateApp()` and immediately calls `appiumGetPerformanceData()`, the PID may not yet be registered in the stats collector and the returned `totalPss` is `0` for memory and `0` for CPU across all columns. Tests then assert `pss < threshold`, pass trivially against the zero value, and provide a false performance green signal. The zero result is not an error — Appium returns valid-shaped data with zero values.
Fix: Insert `await browser.pause(800)` after `activateApp()` and before the first `appiumGetPerformanceData()` call to allow the kernel stats collector to register the process; additionally, assert that the returned numeric values are `> 0` before comparing against a threshold, and log a warning (rather than failing the test) if the first read returns all zeros, then retry once after a further 500 ms pause.

---

**C63-2** — `browser.execute('mobile: swipe', { direction: 'up', elementId })` on Android UIAutomator2 swipes the screen, not the targeted element, when the element has `scrollable: false` in the view hierarchy
Why this matters: UIAutomator2's `mobile: swipe` gesture resolves the `elementId` to its bounding rectangle and performs a touch sequence within that rect — however, if the view's `AccessibilityNodeInfo.isScrollable()` returns `false` (because the container is a plain `LinearLayout` wrapped in a `NestedScrollView` that the accessibility service does not mark scrollable), UIAutomator2 falls back to a screen-level swipe originating from the element's centre point. The gesture visually appears correct in a recording but it scrolls the system-level scroll container (e.g., the WebView or the Activity's root scroll) rather than the intended `RecyclerView` nested inside, causing the target element to remain off-screen even after multiple swipes.
Fix: Verify the element's scrollable attribute with `const scrollable = await element.getAttribute('scrollable')` before calling `mobile: swipe` — if it returns `'false'`, use the W3C Actions API with explicit pointer coordinates calculated from `element.getLocation()` and `element.getSize()` instead: `await browser.action('pointer').move({x: cx, y: startY}).down().move({x: cx, y: endY, duration: 300}).up().perform()`.

---

**C63-3** — `browser.installApp()` on iOS real devices leaves the session in a broken state if called while the app under test is in the foreground — Appium returns success but the running process is killed mid-session
Why this matters: On iOS real devices, `installApp()` calls `ios-deploy --bundle <path>` which, when a process with the same bundle ID is already running, sends `SIGKILL` to the running process before installing the new version. Since the Appium XCUITest session's `XCUIApplication` object holds a reference to the killed process, all subsequent `element.click()` and `browser.execute()` calls throw `XCUITest runner process terminated unexpectedly` with exit code 137. Appium reports the install as successful (exit 0 from `ios-deploy`) and does not automatically restart the XCUITest runner, leaving the session irrecoverably broken.
Fix: Always call `browser.terminateApp(bundleId)` before `browser.installApp()` on iOS, and after installation call `browser.activateApp(bundleId)` to re-launch and re-attach the XCUITest runner to the new process; wrap the three calls in a `reinstallApp(bundleId, appPath)` helper that always terminates before installing, and verify the install succeeded by asserting `await browser.isAppInstalled(bundleId) === true` after the call.

---

**C63-4** — `browser.execute('mobile: type', { text })` silently drops characters when the text contains a null byte or a lone surrogate — the injection succeeds with no error but the field value is truncated at the invalid codepoint
Why this matters: `mobile: type` serialises the text parameter as a JSON string in the WebDriver protocol body; the Appium XCUITest driver then passes the string to `XCUIElement.typeText()`. `NSString` on iOS uses UTF-16 encoding and silently terminates string operations at NUL characters — the text is injected up to but not including the null byte, and no error is thrown. Similarly, lone UTF-16 surrogates (`\uD800`–`\uDFFF` without a pair) cause `NSString` to stop processing the remainder of the string. Test fixtures that contain NUL characters (e.g., binary content pasted from clipboard test data, or strings built with `\0` terminator guards) will silently produce truncated field values, causing assertion failures with confusing diffs showing the field contains only a prefix of the expected string.
Fix: Sanitise input text before passing to `mobile: type` by stripping NUL bytes and replacing lone surrogates: `text.replace(/\0/g, '').replace(/[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/g, '')`. Add a post-type assertion that `(await element.getValue()).length === sanitisedText.length` to surface silent truncation in CI before it masquerades as a UI bug.

---

**C63-5** — `browser.getAppiumContexts()` hangs indefinitely on Android when `chromedriver` is not found in `$PATH` and no `chromedriverExecutable` capability is set — the Appium server waits for a CDP response that never arrives instead of returning an error
Why this matters: UIAutomator2's context-list command attempts to enumerate Chrome DevTools Protocol targets by spawning a `chromedriver` process for each `WEBVIEW_*` context it detects in the accessibility tree. If `chromedriver` is absent from `$PATH` and `appium:chromedriverExecutable` is not set in capabilities, the driver spawns nothing but still sends a CDP `/json/list` request to a port that no process is listening on. The underlying `http.get()` call in the Appium server has no default timeout, so `getAppiumContexts()` waits indefinitely — the WDIO session-level `connectionRetryTimeout` (default 90 s) eventually fires and kills the WebDriver session rather than returning an empty contexts array.
Fix: Always set `appium:chromedriverExecutable` in capabilities pointing to the correct `chromedriver` binary matching the app's WebView Chrome version, or set `appium:chromedriverAutodownload: true` (available in UIAutomator2 >= 2.20) to auto-download the matching version; additionally set `appium:chromedriverConnectTimeout: 5000` (ms) to cap the CDP discovery phase — this ensures `getAppiumContexts()` returns `['NATIVE_APP']` promptly rather than hanging when no WebView is actually present.

## Cycle 64 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 703** — `appiumQueryAppState()` — lifecycle-state assertions for multi-app flows
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

// App state constants matching XCUITest / UIAutomator2 numeric codes
const APP_STATE = {
  NOT_INSTALLED: 0,
  NOT_RUNNING:   1,
  BACKGROUND_SUSPENDED: 2,
  BACKGROUND: 3,
  FOREGROUND: 4,
} as const;
type AppState = typeof APP_STATE[keyof typeof APP_STATE];

async function assertAppState(
  bundleIdOrPkg: string,
  expected: AppState,
  isAndroid: boolean,
  retries = 5,
  intervalMs = 400
): Promise<void> {
  // appiumQueryAppState accepts bundleId on iOS, appId on Android
  const args = isAndroid
    ? { appId: bundleIdOrPkg, bundleId: undefined }
    : { appId: undefined, bundleId: bundleIdOrPkg };

  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < retries; attempt++) {
    const state: number = await browser.appiumQueryAppState(args.appId as string, args.bundleId as string);
    if (state === expected) return;
    if (attempt < retries - 1) await browser.pause(intervalMs);
  }
  const final: number = await browser.appiumQueryAppState(args.appId as string, args.bundleId as string);
  throw new Error(
    `Expected app state ${expected} for ${bundleIdOrPkg}, got ${final} after ${retries} attempts`
  );
}

describe('Multi-app handoff flow', () => {
  const mainBundle  = 'com.example.main';
  const shareBundle = 'com.example.shareext';
  const isAndroid   = browser.isAndroid;

  it('transitions share-extension to background after main app is activated', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp(isAndroid ? shareBundle : undefined, !isAndroid ? shareBundle : undefined);
    await assertAppState(shareBundle, APP_STATE.FOREGROUND, isAndroid);

    await browser.activateApp(isAndroid ? mainBundle : undefined, !isAndroid ? mainBundle : undefined);
    await assertAppState(mainBundle,  APP_STATE.FOREGROUND,  isAndroid);
    await assertAppState(shareBundle, APP_STATE.BACKGROUND,  isAndroid);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumQueryAppState()` reads the OS process table synchronously on iOS and the activity stack on Android, making it the most reliable way to assert multi-app lifecycle transitions without polling the UI — but state `2` (BACKGROUND_SUSPENDED) is iOS-only and Android always returns `3` (BACKGROUND) for backgrounded apps regardless of suspension, so cross-platform test logic must treat states 2 and 3 as equivalent on Android or false-positive assertions will appear when running the same suite on both platforms.

---

**Pattern 704** — `browser.background(-1)` combined with `activateApp()` for background-notification testing
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface PushPayload {
  title: string;
  body:  string;
}

async function simulatePushWhileBackgrounded(
  bundleId: string,
  payload: PushPayload,
  backgroundMs: number = 3000
): Promise<void> {
  // -1 means "background without timeout" — app stays backgrounded until explicit activateApp
  await browser.background(-1 as unknown as number);

  // Deliver push notification via Appium's execute command while app is backgrounded
  await browser.execute('mobile: sendPushNotification', {
    bundleId,
    payload: { aps: { alert: { title: payload.title, body: payload.body }, badge: 1 } },
  });
  await browser.pause(backgroundMs);

  // Re-foreground — activateApp on iOS triggers the notification tap handler if banner is tapped
  await browser.activateApp(undefined, bundleId);
}

describe('Push notification while backgrounded', () => {
  it('shows notification banner and deep-links on tap', async () => {
    const bundleId = 'com.example.app';
    await simulatePushWhileBackgrounded(bundleId, { title: 'New message', body: 'Hello!' }, 2000);

    // Assert app opened to the deep-link target (notifications route)
    const header = await $('~notifications_screen_header');
    await header.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
    await expect(header).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.background(-1)` is the only way to keep an iOS app suspended in background without an automatic foreground timeout, which is required for accurate push-notification delivery timing tests — but passing `-1` requires a type cast because the WDIO type definition only accepts `number`, and on Android `background(-1)` behaves inconsistently across UIAutomator2 versions (some resume immediately, some never resume), so the pattern should be gated behind `if (browser.isIOS)` for production suites.

---

**Pattern 705** — `browser.switchAppiumContext()` with poll-until-ready for hybrid-app WebView stabilisation
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function switchToWebView(
  partialTitle: string,
  timeoutMs: number = 15000,
  pollMs: number    = 800
): Promise<string> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  let lastContexts: string[] = [];

  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    const contexts: string[] = await browser.getAppiumContexts();
    lastContexts = contexts;

    // WebView context names: WEBVIEW_<pid> on Android, WEBVIEW_<bundleId> on iOS
    const target = contexts.find(
      (c) => c.startsWith('WEBVIEW') && c !== 'WEBVIEW_undefined'
    );
    if (target) {
      await browser.switchAppiumContext(target);
      // Confirm the WebView has loaded a matching document title
      const title: string = await browser.getTitle();
      if (!partialTitle || title.toLowerCase().includes(partialTitle.toLowerCase())) {
        return target;
      }
      // Wrong WebView loaded — switch back to native and keep polling
      await browser.switchAppiumContext('NATIVE_APP');
    }
    await browser.pause(pollMs);
  }
  throw new Error(
    `WebView matching "${partialTitle}" not found within ${timeoutMs}ms. Contexts: ${lastContexts.join(', ')}`
  );
}

describe('Hybrid checkout WebView', () => {
  it('fills card form inside embedded WebView', async () => {
    await $('~checkout_button').click();
    const ctx = await switchToWebView('payment', 15000);
    console.log(`Switched to context: ${ctx}`);

    const cardField = await $('input[name="cardNumber"]');
    await cardField.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8000 });
    await cardField.setValue('4111111111111111');
    await $('button[type="submit"]').click();

    await browser.switchAppiumContext('NATIVE_APP');
    await expect($('~payment_success_banner')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Polling `getAppiumContexts()` until a WEBVIEW context appears is the only reliable way to handle WebView load latency in hybrid apps because the context is only registered by Chromedriver after the renderer process fully initialises — but each `getAppiumContexts()` call costs 200–400 ms on a physical Android device because UIAutomator2 enumerates all Chrome DevTools Protocol targets via HTTP, so tight poll intervals on a slow device will dominate test runtime; use `pollMs >= 800` and log the final context list on failure to aid debugging.

---

**Pattern 706** — `browser.startActivity()` with explicit intent flags for deep-link and back-stack testing
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface AndroidIntentOptions {
  appPackage:   string;
  appActivity:  string;
  intentAction?: string;
  intentFlags?:  string;
  intentCategory?: string;
  optionalIntentArguments?: string;
}

async function launchWithDeepLinkIntent(
  opts: AndroidIntentOptions,
  deepLinkUri: string
): Promise<void> {
  // FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK | FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP = 0x14000000
  // Required to ensure a fresh back stack when deep-linking into a running app
  await browser.appiumStartActivity(
    opts.appPackage,
    opts.appActivity,
    opts.appPackage,    // appWaitPackage
    opts.appActivity,  // appWaitActivity
    opts.intentAction  ?? 'android.intent.action.VIEW',
    opts.intentCategory ?? 'android.intent.category.DEFAULT',
    opts.intentFlags    ?? '0x14000000',
    `--es "uri" "${deepLinkUri}"`,
    'false'
  );
}

describe('Android deep-link back-stack', () => {
  it('clears the back stack and opens product detail via intent', async () => {
    await launchWithDeepLinkIntent(
      {
        appPackage:  'com.example.shop',
        appActivity: '.ui.ProductDetailActivity',
      },
      'https://example.com/products/42'
    );

    const title = await $('~product_detail_title');
    await title.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });
    await expect(title).toHaveText('Product 42');

    // Verify back press exits to home (empty back stack) rather than returning to previous screen
    await browser.back();
    const pkg = await browser.appiumGetCurrentPackage();
    expect(pkg).not.toBe('com.example.shop'); // returned to launcher
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumStartActivity()` with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP | FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK` is the most precise way to assert that a deep-link intent clears the Activity back stack on Android — but `appiumStartActivity` is deprecated in favour of `mobile: startActivity` in UIAutomator2 >= 2.22, and the `intentFlags` hex string is passed as-is to `am start`, so an incorrectly formatted flag silently launches the default Activity without applying the flag, giving false-positive back-stack tests; always assert `getCurrentActivity()` equals the expected activity immediately after the call to confirm the intent was honoured.

---

**Pattern 707** — `browser.appiumGetCurrentActivity()` / `appiumGetCurrentPackage()` for Activity-level navigation assertions
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface ActivityExpectation {
  pkg:      string;
  activity: string; // short form e.g. '.ui.LoginActivity' or fully qualified
}

async function assertCurrentActivity(
  expected: ActivityExpectation,
  timeoutMs: number = 5000,
  pollMs: number    = 300
): Promise<void> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  let lastPkg = '';
  let lastActivity = '';

  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    lastPkg      = await browser.appiumGetCurrentPackage();
    lastActivity = await browser.appiumGetCurrentActivity();

    const activityMatch =
      lastActivity === expected.activity ||
      lastActivity.endsWith(expected.activity);    // handle short-form

    if (lastPkg === expected.pkg && activityMatch) return;
    await browser.pause(pollMs);
  }
  throw new Error(
    `Expected ${expected.pkg}/${expected.activity}, ` +
    `got ${lastPkg}/${lastActivity} after ${timeoutMs}ms`
  );
}

describe('Login → Home navigation', () => {
  it('navigates to HomeActivity after successful login', async () => {
    await $('~username_input').setValue('user@example.com');
    await $('~password_input').setValue('secret');
    await $('~login_button').click();

    await assertCurrentActivity(
      { pkg: 'com.example.app', activity: '.ui.HomeActivity' },
      8000
    );
  });

  it('returns to LoginActivity after logout', async () => {
    await $('~menu_button').click();
    await $('~logout_item').click();
    await assertCurrentActivity(
      { pkg: 'com.example.app', activity: '.ui.LoginActivity' },
      5000
    );
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumGetCurrentActivity()` returns the Activity class name reported by `ActivityManager` and is the authoritative Android-side check for navigation correctness — it works even when the transition animation is running and the target Activity is not yet fully visible, unlike waiting for an element — but the method is deprecated in Appium 3 in favour of `mobile: getCurrentActivity`, and on Android 14+ activities with `android:exported="false"` may not appear in `ActivityManager` output, returning an empty string that breaks the assertion; always add a non-empty string guard before comparing.

---

**Pattern 708** — `browser.execute('mobile: getClipboard', { contentType: 'plaintext' })` for clipboard-copy flow verification
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

type ClipboardContentType = 'plaintext' | 'image' | 'url';

async function getClipboardText(): Promise<string> {
  // iOS XCUITest: contentType 'plaintext' returns base64-encoded string
  // Android UIAutomator2: returns plain UTF-8 string directly (no base64)
  const raw: string = await browser.execute('mobile: getClipboard', {
    contentType: 'plaintext' as ClipboardContentType,
  });
  if (browser.isIOS) {
    return Buffer.from(raw, 'base64').toString('utf8');
  }
  return raw;
}

async function setClipboardText(text: string): Promise<void> {
  const encoded = browser.isIOS ? Buffer.from(text).toString('base64') : text;
  await browser.execute('mobile: setClipboard', {
    content:     encoded,
    contentType: 'plaintext',
    label:       'test-clipboard', // Android label (shown in clipboard history)
  });
}

describe('Share link — copy to clipboard', () => {
  it('copies the product URL to the clipboard when the share button is tapped', async () => {
    await $('~share_button').click();
    await $('~copy_link_option').click();

    const clipboardText = await getClipboardText();
    expect(clipboardText).toMatch(/^https:\/\/example\.com\/products\/\d+$/);
  });

  it('pastes a pre-set coupon code into the coupon field via clipboard', async () => {
    await setClipboardText('SAVE20');
    await $('~coupon_field').click();
    if (browser.isIOS) {
      await browser.execute('mobile: type', { text: '' }); // trigger paste gesture placeholder
    } else {
      await $('~coupon_field').longClick();
      await $('~paste_menu_item').click();
    }
    await expect($('~coupon_field')).toHaveValue('SAVE20');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: getClipboard` is the only Appium method that reads clipboard content without triggering the iOS 14+ privacy prompt (which requires tapping "Allow Paste" in a system dialog) — but on iOS the returned string is always base64-encoded regardless of content type, whereas on Android UIAutomator2 returns a plain string, so a cross-platform helper that unconditionally base64-decodes will produce garbled text on Android; always branch on `browser.isIOS` before decoding.

---

**Pattern 709** — `browser.execute('mobile: biometricMatch', { match: true })` for Face ID / Touch ID simulator bypass
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

type BiometricResult = 'success' | 'failure';

async function triggerBiometric(result: BiometricResult): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isIOS) {
    // Android: use fingerprint simulation via ADB instead
    const fingerprintId = result === 'success' ? '1' : '99'; // 99 = unregistered finger
    await browser.execute('mobile: fingerprint', { fingerprintId: parseInt(fingerprintId) });
    return;
  }
  // iOS Simulator only — real devices require actual biometric input
  await browser.execute('mobile: biometricMatch', {
    match: result === 'success',
  });
}

describe('Biometric authentication', () => {
  it('unlocks the app on successful Face ID match', async () => {
    await $('~biometric_prompt').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8000 });
    await triggerBiometric('success');
    await expect($('~home_screen')).toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('shows retry prompt on failed Face ID match', async () => {
    await $('~biometric_prompt').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8000 });
    await triggerBiometric('failure');
    await expect($('~biometric_retry_button')).toBeDisplayed();
    const errorMsg = await $('~biometric_error_text');
    await expect(errorMsg).toHaveTextContaining('Face ID not recognized');
  });

  it('falls back to passcode after three failed attempts', async () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
      await $('~biometric_prompt').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5000 });
      await triggerBiometric('failure');
    }
    await expect($('~passcode_entry_screen')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: biometricMatch` provides deterministic control over biometric success/failure states on iOS Simulator without requiring a physical finger or face, enabling negative-path testing (lockout after N failures, fallback to passcode) that is impossible on real devices in CI — but the command is strictly Simulator-only: calling it on a real device throws `XCUITest: biometricMatch is not supported on real devices`, so capability-based gating with `appium:isSimulator` or `driver.isSimulator` is mandatory; Android requires a completely different approach via `mobile: fingerprint` with a registered fingerprintId.

---

**Pattern 710** — `browser.execute('mobile: alert', { action: 'accept' | 'dismiss' | 'getText' })` for system-dialog automation
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

type AlertAction = 'accept' | 'dismiss' | 'getText' | 'getButtons' | 'replaceValue';

interface AlertOptions {
  action:       AlertAction;
  buttonLabel?: string;  // tap a specific button by label (iOS only)
  value?:       string;  // for replaceValue (iOS prompt dialogs)
}

async function handleSystemAlert(opts: AlertOptions): Promise<string | string[] | void> {
  return browser.execute('mobile: alert', opts);
}

async function waitForAlertAndHandle(
  action: AlertAction,
  buttonLabel?: string,
  timeoutMs: number = 8000
): Promise<void> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    try {
      const buttons = await handleSystemAlert({ action: 'getButtons' }) as string[];
      if (buttons && buttons.length > 0) {
        await handleSystemAlert({ action, buttonLabel });
        return;
      }
    } catch {
      // Alert not yet present — keep polling
    }
    await browser.pause(300);
  }
  throw new Error(`System alert with action "${action}" not dismissed within ${timeoutMs}ms`);
}

describe('Permission request alerts', () => {
  it('grants camera permission and proceeds to QR scanner', async () => {
    await $('~open_scanner_button').click();
    await waitForAlertAndHandle('accept', 'Allow'); // iOS permission dialog
    await expect($('~qr_scanner_preview')).toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('dismisses location permission and shows degraded-mode banner', async () => {
    await $('~find_nearby_button').click();
    await waitForAlertAndHandle('dismiss');
    await expect($('~location_disabled_banner')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: alert` with `getButtons` is the only way to interact with iOS system permission dialogs whose button labels change between OS versions (e.g., "Allow Once" added in iOS 14, "Ask App Not to Track" added in iOS 14.5) — using `driver.acceptAlert()` / `dismissAlert()` always clicks the default first/last button without label awareness, causing tests to click the wrong permission tier; the tradeoff is that `mobile: alert` is XCUITest-only and Android permission dialogs must be handled via element accessors (`$('id=com.android.permissioncontroller:id/permission_allow_button')`).

---

**Pattern 711** — `browser.execute('mobile: siriCommand', { text })` for iOS voice-assistant integration testing
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function invokeSiri(command: string, waitForDismissMs = 4000): Promise<void> {
  // mobile: siriCommand sends the text directly to Siri without activating the mic
  // This bypasses microphone permission requirements in CI environments
  await browser.execute('mobile: siriCommand', { text: command });
  // Siri UI animates in and out — wait for it to complete the action before asserting
  await browser.pause(waitForDismissMs);
  // Dismiss Siri overlay if still present (e.g., Siri waiting for confirmation)
  const siriDismissButton = await $('-ios predicate string:name == "Home" AND type == "XCUIElementTypeButton"');
  if (await siriDismissButton.isDisplayed()) {
    await siriDismissButton.click();
    await browser.pause(500);
  }
}

describe('Siri shortcut — "Start my workout"', () => {
  before(async () => {
    // Siri must be enabled on simulator: Settings > Siri & Search > Listen for "Hey Siri"
    const isSimulator: boolean = (await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities())['appium:isSimulator'] as boolean ?? false;
    if (!isSimulator) {
      console.warn('Siri command tests require Simulator — skipping on real device');
      return;
    }
  });

  it('opens workout screen via donated Siri shortcut', async () => {
    await invokeSiri('Start my workout', 5000);
    await expect($('~workout_active_screen')).toBeDisplayed();
    const timerLabel = await $('~workout_timer');
    await expect(timerLabel).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: siriCommand` injects text directly into Siri's NLP pipeline on iOS Simulator without requiring microphone input, enabling CI-safe testing of app-donated Siri shortcuts and intents — but the command only works on Simulator (Appium throws `SiriCommand is not supported on real devices`) and requires that the Siri service is pre-enabled in Simulator settings before the session starts (it cannot be enabled via capability), so CI images must be pre-configured with Siri on; also, Siri response timing is non-deterministic and the required `pause` must be set conservatively (>= 4 s) or subsequent element lookups will race with the Siri animation.

---

**Pattern 712** — `browser.execute('mobile: batteryInfo')` for battery state assertions in power-management tests
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface BatteryInfo {
  level: number; // 0.0–1.0 (iOS) or 0–100 (Android percentage after normalisation)
  state: number; // iOS: 1=unplugged, 2=charging, 3=full | Android: 2=charging, 3=discharging, 4=full, 5=not charging
}

const IOS_BATTERY_STATE = { UNPLUGGED: 1, CHARGING: 2, FULL: 3 } as const;
const ANDROID_BATTERY_STATE = { CHARGING: 2, DISCHARGING: 3, FULL: 4, NOT_CHARGING: 5 } as const;

async function getBatteryInfo(): Promise<{ levelPct: number; isCharging: boolean }> {
  const raw = await browser.execute('mobile: batteryInfo') as BatteryInfo;
  const levelPct = browser.isIOS
    ? Math.round(raw.level * 100)
    : raw.level; // UIAutomator2 already returns integer percentage

  const isCharging = browser.isIOS
    ? raw.state === IOS_BATTERY_STATE.CHARGING || raw.state === IOS_BATTERY_STATE.FULL
    : raw.state === ANDROID_BATTERY_STATE.CHARGING || raw.state === ANDROID_BATTERY_STATE.FULL;

  return { levelPct, isCharging };
}

describe('Low-battery warning banner', () => {
  it('shows low-battery warning when device reports <= 20% (Simulator)', async () => {
    // On Simulator, battery level is pre-set via capability or xcrun simctl before session start
    // and cannot be changed at runtime — assert against whatever level the Sim reports
    const { levelPct, isCharging } = await getBatteryInfo();
    console.log(`Battery: ${levelPct}% | Charging: ${isCharging}`);

    if (levelPct <= 20 && !isCharging) {
      await expect($('~low_battery_banner')).toBeDisplayed();
    } else {
      console.warn(`Battery at ${levelPct}% — low-battery banner test skipped (need <= 20% and unplugged)`);
    }
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: batteryInfo` gives direct read access to the OS-reported battery level and charging state without any UI interaction, which is valuable for asserting that the app correctly reacts to low-battery conditions — but the level and state encoding differ between iOS and Android (iOS returns a 0.0–1.0 float and state integers 1/2/3, Android returns an integer percentage and different state constants), and on iOS Simulator the battery level is fixed at the value set before session start via `xcrun simctl` and cannot be changed at runtime, limiting low-battery path tests to pre-configured simulator states.

---

**Pattern 713** — `browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name })` for hardware-button simulation on iOS
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

type IOSButton = 'home' | 'volumeUp' | 'volumeDown' | 'sideButton' | 'camera';

async function pressHardwareButton(button: IOSButton, times: number = 1): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < times; i++) {
    await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: button });
    if (times > 1) await browser.pause(200); // inter-press gap for multi-press detection
  }
}

describe('Volume and hardware button interactions', () => {
  it('decreases media volume on single volumeDown press', async () => {
    await $('~media_player_screen').waitForDisplayed();
    // Capture initial volume level indicator
    const initialLabel = await $('~volume_indicator').getText();

    await pressHardwareButton('volumeDown', 3);

    const finalLabel = await $('~volume_indicator').getText();
    const initial = parseInt(initialLabel, 10);
    const final   = parseInt(finalLabel,   10);
    expect(final).toBeLessThan(initial);
  });

  it('triggers screenshot mode on side-button + volumeDown simultaneous press', async () => {
    // iOS screenshot: simultaneous sideButton + volumeDown — simulate as sequential with minimal gap
    await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'sideButton' });
    await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'volumeDown' });
    // Verify screenshot-taken animation overlay appears
    await expect($('-ios predicate string:name == "Screenshot" AND visible == true')).toBeDisplayed();
  });

  it('dismisses app via Home button and returns to Springboard', async () => {
    await pressHardwareButton('home');
    await browser.pause(800);
    // After home press, active app should be backgrounded
    const caps = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
    const bId  = caps['appium:bundleId'] as string;
    const state = await browser.appiumQueryAppState(undefined, bId);
    expect(state).toBe(3); // BACKGROUND
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: pressButton` is the only Appium method that simulates hardware button presses on iOS without using XCUITest UI automation (which cannot target hardware buttons), enabling tests for volume changes, screenshot gestures, and home-button navigation — but it is XCUITest-only (Android uses `pressKeyCode` via UIAutomator2), and the `camera` button value triggers the Camera app rather than any in-app camera button, so `name: 'camera'` is only useful for testing the system camera launch flow, not in-app camera permission flows which require tapping UIKit elements.

---

**Pattern 714** — `browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()` for runtime capability branching in multi-device CI
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface RuntimeCaps {
  platformName:    string;
  platformVersion: string;
  deviceName:      string;
  udid?:           string;
  isSimulator?:    boolean;
  automationName:  string;
  bundleId?:       string;
  appPackage?:     string;
}

let _cachedCaps: RuntimeCaps | null = null;

async function getRuntimeCaps(): Promise<RuntimeCaps> {
  if (_cachedCaps) return _cachedCaps;
  const raw = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
  _cachedCaps = {
    platformName:    (raw['platformName']           as string) ?? '',
    platformVersion: (raw['appium:platformVersion'] as string ?? raw['platformVersion'] as string) ?? '',
    deviceName:      (raw['appium:deviceName']      as string ?? raw['deviceName']      as string) ?? '',
    udid:            raw['appium:udid']             as string | undefined,
    isSimulator:     raw['appium:isSimulator']      as boolean | undefined,
    automationName:  (raw['appium:automationName']  as string) ?? '',
    bundleId:        raw['appium:bundleId']         as string | undefined,
    appPackage:      raw['appium:appPackage']       as string | undefined,
  };
  return _cachedCaps;
}

describe('Device-adaptive keyboard dismissal', () => {
  it('dismisses keyboard using the correct method for the current OS version', async () => {
    const caps = await getRuntimeCaps();
    const majorVersion = parseInt(caps.platformVersion.split('.')[0], 10);

    await $('~search_input').click();
    await $('~search_input').setValue('query');

    if (caps.platformName.toLowerCase() === 'ios' && majorVersion >= 16) {
      // iOS 16+ supports swipe-down keyboard dismissal
      await browser.execute('mobile: swipe', { direction: 'down', elementId: (await $('~keyboard_container')).elementId });
    } else if (caps.platformName.toLowerCase() === 'ios') {
      await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'home' });
      await browser.activateApp(undefined, caps.bundleId);
    } else {
      await browser.hideKeyboard();
    }
    await expect($('~keyboard_container')).not.toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `getAppiumSessionCapabilities()` returns the full resolved capability set (including server-side defaults and driver-injected values like `appium:isSimulator`) which is more reliable than reading from the WDIO config object — but the capability key naming is inconsistent: some drivers return keys without the `appium:` prefix, others with it, and the presence of a key does not guarantee a non-null value, so defensive access with nullish coalescing is required for every field; cache the result in a module-level variable to avoid one RTT per test.

---

**Pattern 715** — `browser.execute('mobile: getContexts', { waitForWebviewMs })` for precise WEBVIEW enumeration with load-wait
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface WebviewContext {
  id:    string;
  title: string;
  url:   string;
  bundleId?: string;
  packageName?: string;
}

async function getWebviewContextsWithMetadata(
  waitForWebviewMs: number = 10000
): Promise<WebviewContext[]> {
  // mobile: getContexts (note: NOT getAppiumContexts) returns rich objects on newer Appium
  // waitForWebviewMs waits up to N ms for at least one WEBVIEW context to appear before returning
  const contexts = await browser.execute('mobile: getContexts', {
    waitForWebviewMs,
  }) as Array<{ id: string; title?: string; url?: string; bundleId?: string; packageName?: string }>;

  return contexts
    .filter((c) => c.id !== 'NATIVE_APP')
    .map((c) => ({
      id:          c.id,
      title:       c.title ?? '',
      url:         c.url   ?? '',
      bundleId:    c.bundleId,
      packageName: c.packageName,
    }));
}

describe('Multi-WebView disambiguation', () => {
  it('switches to the payment WebView (not the ad-slot WebView)', async () => {
    await $('~checkout_cta').click();
    const webviews = await getWebviewContextsWithMetadata(12000);

    // Multiple WebViews may exist (main content + ad iframe rendered in separate WebView)
    const paymentCtx = webviews.find((c) => c.url.includes('payments.example.com'));
    if (!paymentCtx) {
      throw new Error(
        `Payment WebView not found. Available: ${webviews.map((c) => c.url).join(' | ')}`
      );
    }

    await browser.switchAppiumContext(paymentCtx.id);
    const cardInput = await $('input[autocomplete="cc-number"]');
    await cardInput.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6000 });
    await cardInput.setValue('4111111111111111');

    await browser.switchAppiumContext('NATIVE_APP');
    await expect($('~payment_processing_spinner')).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: getContexts` (the execute-method variant) returns rich metadata — including the page URL and document title for each WebView — which allows switching to the correct WebView by URL when multiple WEBVIEW contexts exist simultaneously (e.g., main content + in-app ad WebViews), unlike `getAppiumContexts()` which returns opaque `WEBVIEW_<pid>` strings that require switching to each one and calling `getTitle()` to identify — but `mobile: getContexts` is only available in XCUITest >= 4.16 and UIAutomator2 >= 2.27, so capability-gated version detection is needed for older driver versions, and the `waitForWebviewMs` parameter is iOS-only (Android returns immediately regardless of the value).

---

**Pattern 716** — `browser.execute('mobile: setPermission', { access, bundleId, ... })` for iOS simulator permission pre-seeding
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

type PermissionAccess  = 'YES' | 'NO' | 'unset' | 'limited';
type PermissionService =
  | 'camera'
  | 'microphone'
  | 'photos'
  | 'location'
  | 'contacts'
  | 'calendar'
  | 'reminders'
  | 'notifications'
  | 'motion'
  | 'health';

interface PermissionSpec {
  service: PermissionService;
  access:  PermissionAccess;
}

async function preGrantPermissions(
  bundleId: string,
  permissions: PermissionSpec[]
): Promise<void> {
  // mobile: setPermission modifies the iOS Simulator's TCC (Transparency, Consent, Control) database
  // This avoids system permission prompts during the test run itself
  for (const { service, access } of permissions) {
    await browser.execute('mobile: setPermission', {
      bundleId,
      service,
      access,
    });
  }
  // Re-launch app so that the permission changes take effect (TCC is read at launch)
  const caps  = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
  const bId   = (caps['appium:bundleId'] as string) ?? bundleId;
  await browser.terminateApp(undefined, bId);
  await browser.activateApp(undefined, bId);
}

describe('Onboarding — pre-granted permissions', () => {
  before(async () => {
    if (!browser.isIOS) return; // Android uses appium:autoGrantPermissions capability
    await preGrantPermissions('com.example.app', [
      { service: 'camera',        access: 'YES'  },
      { service: 'microphone',    access: 'YES'  },
      { service: 'photos',        access: 'limited' }, // test "limited" photo library access
      { service: 'notifications', access: 'YES'  },
      { service: 'location',      access: 'unset' }, // force the prompt on first use
    ]);
  });

  it('skips camera permission dialog because permission was pre-granted', async () => {
    await $('~scan_document_button').click();
    // Camera opens directly — no permission dialog should appear
    await expect($('~camera_viewfinder')).toBeDisplayed();
    await expect($('~camera_permission_alert')).not.toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: setPermission` pre-seeds the iOS Simulator's TCC database before a test scenario runs, eliminating non-deterministic permission dialogs from the test flow and enabling deterministic testing of the `limited` photo access path (which cannot be triggered by `acceptAlert()`) — but the command only works on iOS Simulator (real devices require `xcrun simctl privacy` or manual interaction), and the app must be restarted after calling `setPermission` for TCC changes to take effect, adding 3–5 seconds of startup overhead per `before()` block; for Android, the equivalent is `appium:autoGrantPermissions: true` in capabilities or `mobile: changePermissions` in UIAutomator2.

**Pattern 717** — `browser.execute('mobile: deviceInfo')` with capability-driven screen density branching for pixel-level assertions
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface DeviceInfo {
  timeZone:            string;
  currentLocale:       string;
  model:               string;
  uuid:                string;
  userInterfaceIdiom:  string;   // 'phone' | 'pad' (iOS)
  isSimulator?:        boolean;
  // Android-only fields
  displayDensity?:     number;   // dpi — e.g., 440, 560
  displaySize?:        { width: number; height: number };
  apiVersion?:         string;
}

type ScreenTier = 'ldpi' | 'mdpi' | 'hdpi' | 'xhdpi' | 'xxhdpi' | 'xxxhdpi';

function getDpiTier(dpi: number): ScreenTier {
  if (dpi <= 120) return 'ldpi';
  if (dpi <= 160) return 'mdpi';
  if (dpi <= 240) return 'hdpi';
  if (dpi <= 320) return 'xhdpi';
  if (dpi <= 480) return 'xxhdpi';
  return 'xxxhdpi';
}

async function getDeviceInfoCached(): Promise<DeviceInfo> {
  return browser.execute('mobile: deviceInfo') as Promise<DeviceInfo>;
}

describe('Pixel-level layout assertions', () => {
  it('applies the correct icon size for the device DPI tier', async () => {
    const info    = await getDeviceInfoCached();
    const density = info.displayDensity ?? 160;
    const tier    = getDpiTier(density);

    const icon = await $('~app_logo_icon');
    const size  = await icon.getSize();

    // Design spec: icon is 48dp — multiply by density bucket to get expected px
    const dpFactor: Record<ScreenTier, number> = {
      ldpi: 0.75, mdpi: 1.0, hdpi: 1.5, xhdpi: 2.0, xxhdpi: 3.0, xxxhdpi: 4.0,
    };
    const expectedPx = Math.round(48 * dpFactor[tier]);
    const tolerance  = 4; // +/- 4 px for sub-pixel rounding

    expect(Math.abs(size.width - expectedPx)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(tolerance);
    console.log(`DPI: ${density} (${tier}), expected icon: ${expectedPx}px, actual: ${size.width}px`);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: deviceInfo` returns the display density, model, locale, and timezone in a single round trip, enabling test logic to branch on DPI tier for pixel-level layout assertions without requiring a separate ADB shell call or hardcoded per-device lookup table — but the `displayDensity` and `displaySize` fields are Android-only (iOS returns `userInterfaceIdiom` instead), and `mobile: deviceInfo` is not available in all Appium driver versions (XCUITest added it in v4.8, UIAutomator2 in v2.15), so a version guard or a try/catch fallback to `capabilities['deviceDisplayDensity']` is needed for older CI environments.

### Community Gotchas

**C64-1** — `browser.switchAppiumContext()` to a WEBVIEW context silently fails when the matching Chromedriver version is not available — no error is thrown and subsequent `$('css-selector')` calls still target the native layer
Why this matters: When switching to a `WEBVIEW_<pid>` context on Android, UIAutomator2 must attach Chromedriver to the Chrome renderer process via CDP. If the installed Chromedriver version does not match the WebView's Chrome version (checked via `navigator.userAgent`), the attach step fails internally — but UIAutomator2 catches the error and returns a `200 OK` response to the WebDriver `POST /context` command anyway, leaving the session internally pointing at `NATIVE_APP`. All subsequent CSS selectors and `$('input')` calls will fail with `no such element` rather than a context-switch error, making the root cause (version mismatch) invisible in test logs. The only observable symptom is that element lookups behave as though the app is in `NATIVE_APP` context immediately after a `switchAppiumContext` call.
Fix: After calling `browser.switchAppiumContext(webviewCtx)`, immediately verify the switch succeeded by calling `const confirmed = await browser.getAppiumContext(); if (confirmed !== webviewCtx) throw new Error(...)`. Additionally, set `appium:chromedriverExecutableDir` to a directory containing multiple Chromedriver binaries and enable `appium:chromedriverAutodownload: true` to let UIAutomator2 select the correct version automatically; check the Appium server log for `ChromeDriver selection` lines to diagnose version mismatches.

---

**C64-2** — `browser.background(-1)` on Android with UIAutomator2 >= 2.30 returns immediately instead of keeping the app backgrounded — the breaking change removed indefinite background support
Why this matters: UIAutomator2 v2.30 changed the implementation of `appiumBackground(-1)` to cap the background duration at 30 seconds, treating `-1` as `30` to align with the W3C WebDriver extension spec which does not define indefinite background. Tests written against earlier UIAutomator2 versions that used `background(-1)` to hold the app backgrounded while a timer or notification fires will now resume the app after 30 seconds regardless, causing timing-sensitive tests (e.g., session expiry after 45 s, push delivery after 40 s) to see the app foreground prematurely and fail with `element not found` on the notification overlay.
Fix: Replace `background(-1)` with a helper that runs `adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_HOME` via `browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'input', args: ['keyevent', 'KEYCODE_HOME'] })` for Android, followed by `activateApp()` when the test needs to re-foreground; this approach is not affected by UIAutomator2 version changes and gives deterministic background duration by timing the pause between the two calls.

---

**C64-3** — `browser.appiumQueryAppState()` returns `1` (NOT_RUNNING) for a process that is actually running on Android 12+ due to process death detection changes — causes multi-app lifecycle assertions to fail spuriously
Why this matters: Android 12 introduced `AppHistory` restrictions that prevent third-party processes from reading the foreground/background state of apps they did not launch. UIAutomator2 calls `ActivityManager.getRunningAppProcesses()` to determine app state, but on Android 12+ this API returns only the calling process and processes that the caller has spawned — not arbitrary third-party processes. As a result, `appiumQueryAppState('com.other.app')` always returns `1` (NOT_RUNNING) on Android 12+ even when the target app is actively in the foreground, because `getRunningAppProcesses()` no longer includes it. Tests that assert a companion app is running (e.g., to verify a handoff flow) will see false `1` values and fail with misleading "app is not running" errors.
Fix: On Android 12+, replace `appiumQueryAppState()` cross-app checks with `getCurrentPackage()` / `getCurrentActivity()` assertions which still work correctly (they query `ActivityTaskManager` which is not subject to the same restriction), or use `mobile: shell` to run `adb shell dumpsys activity activities | grep mResumedActivity` and parse the output; gate the fix with a platform-version check via `getAppiumSessionCapabilities()`.

---

**C64-4** — `mobile: setPermission` does not take effect when called after the app has already launched — the TCC database is read once at app launch and in-session permission changes are ignored until the next cold start
Why this matters: Developers often call `mobile: setPermission` inside a `beforeEach()` to reset permission state between test cases, expecting that changing the TCC entry mid-session will affect the running app's `[CLLocationManager authorizationStatus]` or `[AVCaptureDevice authorizationStatus]`. In practice, iOS caches the permission status in the process's memory at launch and does not re-read TCC during the process lifetime. Calling `mobile: setPermission` while the app is in foreground updates the on-disk database but the in-process cached value remains stale, so `AVAuthorizationStatusDenied` or `CLAuthorizationStatusDenied` continues to be returned until the process is restarted. Tests that call `setPermission` in `beforeEach()` without a terminate/relaunch cycle will therefore see the old permission state and fail non-deterministically depending on the order test cases run.
Fix: Always follow `mobile: setPermission` with `browser.terminateApp(undefined, bundleId)` and `browser.activateApp(undefined, bundleId)` to force a cold start that re-reads TCC; wrap these three calls in a `resetPermission(service, access)` helper and use it only in `before()` (not `beforeEach()`) to amortise the 3–5 s restart cost across the suite rather than per-test.

---

**C64-5** — `browser.execute('mobile: getContexts', { waitForWebviewMs })` on Android returns stale WEBVIEW entries from a previously destroyed renderer process — the context list includes a PID that no longer exists and `switchAppiumContext` to it hangs
Why this matters: UIAutomator2's `mobile: getContexts` implementation enumerates Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) targets by connecting to each `WEBVIEW_<pid>` over a Unix abstract socket. When a WebView renderer is destroyed (e.g., the user navigated away and the OS reclaimed memory), the abstract socket may remain registered in the Linux namespace for up to 2 seconds after process death. `mobile: getContexts` will list the stale `WEBVIEW_<pid>` as available because the socket is still addressable, but when `switchAppiumContext` tries to attach Chromedriver to it, the CDP `/json/version` request times out (30 s default) because no process is listening on the socket. The test hangs for 30 seconds and then throws `ChromeDriver session creation failed`, with no indication that the context was stale.
Fix: After calling `mobile: getContexts`, filter out contexts whose PID does not appear in `mobile: shell` output of `ps -A | grep chrome` before attempting to switch; alternatively, wrap `switchAppiumContext` in a 5 s timeout using `Promise.race` with a `setTimeout` rejection and treat a timeout as a stale-context signal, then re-call `mobile: getContexts` to refresh the list and retry with the next available WEBVIEW context.

**Pattern 733** — `browser.appiumToggleNetworkSpeed()` — emulator-level network throttling for low-bandwidth UX tests
```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts capability: appium:avd must target an Android emulator, not a real device
// appiumToggleNetworkSpeed() maps to: adb emu network speed <netspeed>
// Valid netspeed values: 'gsm'|'hscsd'|'gprs'|'edge'|'umts'|'hsdpa'|'lte'|'evdo'|'full'

type NetSpeed = 'gsm' | 'gprs' | 'edge' | 'umts' | 'hsdpa' | 'lte' | 'full';

async function withNetworkThrottle(
  speed: NetSpeed,
  testFn: () => Promise<void>,
): Promise<void> {
  await browser.appiumToggleNetworkSpeed(speed);
  try {
    await testFn();
  } finally {
    // Always restore to full speed to avoid polluting subsequent tests
    await browser.appiumToggleNetworkSpeed('full');
  }
}

describe('Image loading under throttled network', () => {
  it('shows a skeleton loader within 500ms on EDGE speeds', async () => {
    await withNetworkThrottle('edge', async () => {
      await browser.url('https://app.example.com/feed');
      // Skeleton placeholder must appear quickly even when images are loading slowly
      const skeleton = await $('~skeleton_loader');
      await skeleton.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 500 });
      // Full image should eventually load (generous timeout for EDGE ~236 kbps)
      const heroImage = await $('~feed_hero_image');
      await heroImage.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 15_000 });
    });
  });

  it('shows a network-error state for GSM speeds on video content', async () => {
    await withNetworkThrottle('gsm', async () => {
      await browser.url('https://app.example.com/video/1');
      const errorBanner = await $('~network_error_banner');
      await errorBanner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
      expect(await errorBanner.getText()).toContain('poor connection');
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumToggleNetworkSpeed()` uses the Android emulator's built-in network speed emulation (`adb emu network speed`), which throttles the emulator's virtual NIC at the TCP/IP level and therefore affects all network activity in the app — including background services and analytics — making it a true end-to-end bandwidth test, but it is only available on emulators (not real devices), requires the `avd` capability to be set, and does not allow per-host throttling, so CI pipelines that test both real-device farms and emulators must guard the call with a `capabilities['avd'] !== undefined` check to avoid an `unknown method` error on physical device sessions.

**Pattern 734** — `browser.execute('mobile: getContexts', { waitForWebviewMs, androidWebviewConnectionRetryTime })` — filtering WEBVIEW contexts by URL pattern before switching
```typescript
// Requires UIAutomator2 >= 2.9.0 for the 'url' field in the returned context objects
// On iOS (XCUITest), the equivalent is: mobile: getContexts with 'bundleId' field

interface WebviewContextInfo {
  id: string;          // e.g. "WEBVIEW_1234"
  title?: string;
  url?: string;        // populated only when waitForWebviewMs > 0
  bundleId?: string;   // iOS only
  pid?: number;
  packageName?: string; // Android only
}

/**
 * Switch to the WEBVIEW context that matches the given URL substring.
 * Retries up to maxAttempts times with a short delay to handle WebView load race.
 */
async function switchToWebviewByUrl(
  urlSubstring: string,
  maxAttempts = 5,
): Promise<void> {
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const contexts = (await browser.execute('mobile: getContexts', {
      waitForWebviewMs: 4_000,                // wait up to 4 s for the WebView to attach
      androidWebviewConnectionRetryTime: 500, // retry CDP attach every 500 ms
    })) as WebviewContextInfo[];

    const target = contexts.find(
      (ctx) => ctx.id !== 'NATIVE_APP' && ctx.url?.includes(urlSubstring),
    );

    if (target) {
      await browser.switchAppiumContext(target.id);
      // Confirm switch succeeded
      const active = await browser.getAppiumContext();
      if (active === target.id) return;
    }

    if (attempt < maxAttempts) await browser.pause(1_000);
  }
  throw new Error(`No WEBVIEW context found matching URL: ${urlSubstring}`);
}

it('switches to the payment WebView and asserts the checkout URL', async () => {
  await $('~pay_now_button').click();
  await switchToWebviewByUrl('checkout.payments.example.com');
  const url = await browser.getUrl();
  expect(url).toContain('checkout.payments.example.com');
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing `waitForWebviewMs` to `mobile: getContexts` causes UIAutomator2 to block for up to the specified duration while polling for Chrome DevTools Protocol socket availability, returning context `url` and `title` fields populated from a live CDP `/json/list` query — which eliminates the need for a separate `getUrl()` call — but this blocking poll adds latency to every `getContexts` call even when the WebView is already attached, and the `url` field is absent on Android API < 23 (where CDPv1 is not supported) and on iOS simulator contexts where `bundleId` is returned instead, so the URL-matching logic must fall back to `title` for those environments.

**Pattern 735** — `browser.appiumToggleAirplaneMode()` / `browser.appiumToggleWiFi()` / `browser.appiumToggleData()` — offline-mode and connectivity-change UX tests
```typescript
// All three toggle methods are Android-only (UIAutomator2 driver)
// iOS equivalent: use 'mobile: setSimulatorNetworkConditions' (XCUITest) or Xcode Network Link Conditioner

import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

type ConnectivityState = 'airplane' | 'wifi-off' | 'data-off' | 'online';

async function getAirplaneModeState(): Promise<boolean> {
  const result = await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'settings',
    args: ['get', 'global', 'airplane_mode_on'],
  }) as string;
  return result.trim() === '1';
}

async function setConnectivity(state: ConnectivityState): Promise<void> {
  const airplaneOn = await getAirplaneModeState();
  if (state === 'airplane' && !airplaneOn)  await browser.appiumToggleAirplaneMode();
  if (state !== 'airplane' && airplaneOn)   await browser.appiumToggleAirplaneMode();
  if (state === 'wifi-off')                 await browser.appiumToggleWiFi();
  if (state === 'data-off')                 await browser.appiumToggleData();
}

describe('Offline mode behaviour', () => {
  afterEach(async () => {
    // Always restore connectivity after each test
    const airplaneOn = await getAirplaneModeState();
    if (airplaneOn) await browser.appiumToggleAirplaneMode();
  });

  it('shows an offline banner when airplane mode is enabled', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp(undefined, 'com.example.app');
    await setConnectivity('airplane');
    // App should detect connectivity loss within 3 s via Reachability/ConnectivityManager
    const banner = await $('~offline_banner');
    await banner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
    expect(await banner.getText()).toContain('No internet connection');
  });

  it('syncs queued actions when connectivity is restored', async () => {
    await setConnectivity('airplane');
    await $('~compose_post_button').click();
    await $('~post_body_input').setValue('Queued post content');
    await $('~submit_post_button').click();
    await expect($('~queued_indicator')).toBeDisplayed();
    // Restore connectivity
    await browser.appiumToggleAirplaneMode();
    // App should detect network recovery and sync within 10 s
    await expect($('~queued_indicator')).not.toBeDisplayed({ wait: 10_000 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumToggleAirplaneMode()`, `appiumToggleWiFi()`, and `appiumToggleData()` all modify actual device-level OS settings via UIAutomator2 system service calls — making them suitable for testing real `ConnectivityManager` callbacks in the app — but all three are stateful toggles that flip the current state rather than setting an absolute on/off value, so they require a pre-flight state check (via `mobile: shell settings get global airplane_mode_on`) before each call to avoid double-toggling; additionally, on Android 10+ these calls require the `ACCESS_WIFI_STATE` and `CHANGE_NETWORK_STATE` system permissions on the UIAutomator2 server APK, which is pre-granted on emulators but may be restricted on some OEM real-device configurations.

**Pattern 736** — `browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command, args })` — ADB shell passthrough for device-state inspection not exposed by WebDriver protocol
```typescript
// 'mobile: shell' is Android-only (UIAutomator2 driver)
// Requires appium:allowDelayAdb: true capability and UIAutomator2 >= 1.22
// iOS equivalent: 'mobile: execUIScript' or xcrun simctl commands via Node child_process

interface ShellResult {
  stdout: string;
  stderr: string;
  exitCode: number;
}

async function adbShell(command: string, ...args: string[]): Promise<ShellResult> {
  const result = await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command,
    args,
    includeStderr: true,
  }) as ShellResult;
  if (result.exitCode !== 0 && result.stderr) {
    console.warn(`ADB shell warning [${command} ${args.join(' ')}]: ${result.stderr}`);
  }
  return result;
}

describe('Deep link routing via ADB shell intent', () => {
  it('navigates to the product detail page via explicit intent', async () => {
    // Launch a deep link without using mobile: deepLink (works on non-browser apps too)
    await adbShell('am', 'start', '-a', 'android.intent.action.VIEW',
      '-d', 'https://app.example.com/product/42',
      'com.example.app/.MainActivity');

    const productTitle = await $('~product_title_label');
    await productTitle.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await productTitle.getText()).toBe('Product 42');
  });

  it('reads SharedPreferences value written by the app during onboarding', async () => {
    await $('~onboarding_complete_button').click();
    // Read the flag directly from SharedPreferences XML on /data/data/
    const { stdout } = await adbShell(
      'cat',
      '/data/data/com.example.app/shared_prefs/AppPreferences.xml',
    );
    expect(stdout).toContain('<boolean name="onboardingComplete" value="true"');
  });

  it('triggers a battery-low broadcast to test low-battery UI', async () => {
    await adbShell('am', 'broadcast', '-a', 'android.intent.action.BATTERY_LOW');
    const lowBatteryBanner = await $('~battery_low_banner');
    await lowBatteryBanner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: shell` gives direct access to ADB shell commands from within a WebDriver session — enabling SharedPreferences reads, intent broadcasts, and system service queries that are impossible via the standard WebDriver protocol — but it is limited to the security context of the `shell` user (UID 2000), which cannot read files under `/data/data/` on non-rooted, non-debuggable production builds and cannot write to `/system`; additionally, UIAutomator2 passes the command through ADB over TCP (not a local socket), adding ~20–60 ms per call overhead, so tight loops using `mobile: shell` for polling (instead of `driver.waitUntil`) will produce noticeably slower tests on remote device farms.
