**Pattern 737** — `browser.getLogs('logcat')` / `browser.getLogs('syslog')` — device-log assertions for background service and crash detection
```typescript
// getLogs('logcat') is Android-only; getLogs('syslog') is iOS-only
// Log entries contain: { timestamp, level, message } (format varies by driver version)
// UIAutomator2: logcat entries since session start; XCUITest: syslog since activation

interface LogEntry {
  timestamp: number; // Unix epoch ms
  level: string;     // 'INFO' | 'WARNING' | 'ERROR' | 'FATAL' etc.
  message: string;
}

async function getLogsWithFilter(
  type: 'logcat' | 'syslog',
  tag: string,
): Promise<LogEntry[]> {
  const entries = await browser.getLogs(type) as LogEntry[];
  return entries.filter((e) => e.message.includes(tag));
}

describe('Background sync service log assertions', () => {
  it('verifies the SyncService completes without errors after cold start', async () => {
    // Trigger cold start
    await browser.terminateApp(undefined, 'com.example.app');
    await browser.activateApp(undefined, 'com.example.app');

    // Allow sync to run
    await browser.pause(5_000);

    const syncLogs = await getLogsWithFilter('logcat', 'SyncService');
    const errorLogs = syncLogs.filter(
      (e) => e.level === 'ERROR' || e.level === 'FATAL',
    );
    expect(errorLogs).toHaveLength(0);

    const completionEntry = syncLogs.find((e) =>
      e.message.includes('SyncService: sync complete'),
    );
    expect(completionEntry).toBeDefined();
  });

  it('captures crash signal in logcat when the app receives a kill signal', async () => {
    // Read the app PID then send SIGABRT to simulate crash
    const pidResult = await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'pidof',
      args: ['com.example.app'],
    }) as ShellResult;

    await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'kill',
      args: ['-6', pidResult.stdout.trim()], // SIGABRT
    });

    await browser.pause(2_000);
    const crashLogs = await getLogsWithFilter('logcat', 'FATAL EXCEPTION');
    expect(crashLogs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.getLogs('logcat')` returns all log entries buffered by UIAutomator2 since the session started — giving full crash traces, `android.util.Log` output, and ANR signals that are invisible via element inspection — but the buffer is cleared after each `getLogs()` call (it is a destructive read), meaning two `getLogs()` calls in sequence will see different entries; tests that need to inspect logs across multiple steps must accumulate entries in a local array between calls, and on Android 8+ `PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS` permission restrictions mean logcat output is filtered to the app's own UID unless the device is rooted or the server APK is granted system-level permissions.

---

**Pattern 738** — `browser.startRecordingScreen()` / `browser.stopRecordingScreen()` — video capture for CI failure evidence and visual regression artefacts
```typescript
// startRecordingScreen / stopRecordingScreen available on iOS (XCUITest 9.3+) and Android (UIAutomator2 4.2+)
// iOS options: videoType ('mp4'|'fmp4'|'avi'), videoQuality ('low'|'medium'|'high'|'photo'), videoFps
// Android options: videoSize, bitRate, timeLimit (max 180 s on Android), bugReport

interface RecordingOptions {
  videoType?: string;
  videoQuality?: string;
  videoFps?: number;
  videoSize?: string;
  bitRate?: number;
  timeLimit?: number;
}

async function captureVideo(
  testName: string,
  testFn: () => Promise<void>,
): Promise<void> {
  const caps = (await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()).capabilities;
  const isAndroid = caps['platformName']?.toLowerCase() === 'android';

  const options: RecordingOptions = isAndroid
    ? { videoSize: '1080x2400', bitRate: 2_000_000, timeLimit: 120 }
    : { videoType: 'mp4', videoQuality: 'medium', videoFps: 30 };

  await browser.startRecordingScreen(options);
  let testFailed = false;
  try {
    await testFn();
  } catch (err) {
    testFailed = true;
    throw err;
  } finally {
    // stopRecordingScreen returns a Base64-encoded video string
    const videoBase64 = await browser.stopRecordingScreen();
    if (testFailed) {
      const buf = Buffer.from(videoBase64, 'base64');
      const fs = await import('node:fs/promises');
      const safeName = testName.replace(/[^a-z0-9_-]/gi, '_');
      await fs.mkdir('./artefacts', { recursive: true });
      await fs.writeFile(`./artefacts/${safeName}.mp4`, buf);
    }
  }
}

describe('Checkout flow — video evidence on failure', () => {
  it('completes a purchase and reaches the confirmation screen', async () => {
    await captureVideo('checkout_happy_path', async () => {
      await $('~cart_checkout_button').click();
      await $('~payment_method_visa').click();
      await $('~confirm_purchase_button').click();
      await expect($('~order_confirmation_header')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 10_000 });
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `startRecordingScreen()` captures the full device display at the OS level — giving pixel-accurate evidence of what the user saw including system overlays, permission dialogs, and Toasts — but Android imposes a hard 180-second time limit per recording session (any call that would exceed it is silently truncated), and iOS XCUITest recordings are CPU-intensive on the Simulator host (adding ~15% CPU load), which can cause test-induced flakiness on shared CI runners; long test suites should wrap individual `it` blocks rather than the full `describe`, and the `remotePath` / `uploadToRemoteServer` options should be used instead of decoding the Base64 payload locally to avoid OOM errors for recordings longer than ~60 seconds.

---

**Pattern 739** — `browser.execute('mobile: scrollGesture', { elementId, direction, percent })` — Android UIAutomator2 scroll gesture with stop-condition detection
```typescript
// 'mobile: scrollGesture' is Android-only (UIAutomator2 driver)
// Returns: true if more content is available in the scroll direction, false if end-of-list reached
// iOS equivalent: 'mobile: scroll' with 'direction' parameter

interface ScrollGestureParams {
  elementId?: string;   // if omitted, scrolls the whole screen
  left: number;         // left edge of scroll area (pixels)
  top: number;          // top edge of scroll area (pixels)
  width: number;
  height: number;
  direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right';
  percent: number;      // scroll distance as fraction of the element height (0.0–1.0)
  speed?: number;       // pixels per second (default: 5000)
}

/**
 * Scroll a RecyclerView/ScrollView until a target element is visible,
 * aborting if the end-of-list is reached before the element appears.
 */
async function scrollUntilVisible(
  container: WebdriverIO.Element,
  targetSelector: string,
  maxScrolls = 20,
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  const rect = await container.getLocation();
  const size = await container.getSize();

  for (let i = 0; i < maxScrolls; i++) {
    const target = await $(targetSelector);
    if (await target.isDisplayed()) return target;

    const hasMore = await browser.execute('mobile: scrollGesture', {
      elementId: container.elementId,
      left:  rect.x,
      top:   rect.y,
      width: size.width,
      height: size.height,
      direction: 'down',
      percent: 0.75,
      speed: 4_000,
    } as ScrollGestureParams) as boolean;

    if (!hasMore) {
      throw new Error(`Element "${targetSelector}" not found after scrolling to end of list`);
    }
  }
  throw new Error(`Element "${targetSelector}" not found within ${maxScrolls} scroll attempts`);
}

it('finds a product deep in a long category list', async () => {
  const list = await $('~product_list_view');
  const item = await scrollUntilVisible(list, '~product_item_SKU_998877');
  await item.click();
  await expect($('~product_detail_title')).toHaveText('Premium Widget Pro');
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: scrollGesture` returns a boolean indicating whether the scroll reached the end of the scrollable content — enabling a clean while-not-found loop without a fixed timeout — but the `percent` parameter is interpreted relative to the element's height (not the screen), so container elements that fill less than 50% of the screen require a `percent` value greater than 1.0 to scroll a meaningful distance; additionally, the return value is based on UIAutomator2's `scrollDescriptor` which inspects `RecyclerView`/`ListView` scroll-completion events and is unreliable for `ScrollView` containers with `fillViewport="true"`, where `hasMore` may return `false` prematurely even when off-screen content remains.

**Pattern 740** — `browser.execute('mobile: changePermissions', { permissions, action })` — bulk Android permission grant/revoke without reinstalling the app
```typescript
// 'mobile: changePermissions' is Android-only (UIAutomator2 >= 2.22)
// action: 'grant' | 'revoke'
// permissions: array of Android permission strings (e.g. 'android.permission.CAMERA')
// Does NOT require app reinstallation — modifies runtime permissions via pm grant/revoke

type PermissionAction = 'grant' | 'revoke';

interface ChangePermissionsParams {
  appPackage: string;
  permissions: string[];
  action: PermissionAction;
}

const APP_PACKAGE = 'com.example.app';

const LOCATION_PERMISSIONS = [
  'android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION',
  'android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION',
  'android.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION',
] as const;

const MEDIA_PERMISSIONS = [
  'android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES',
  'android.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO',
  'android.permission.CAMERA',
] as const;

async function grantPermissions(permissions: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: changePermissions', {
    appPackage: APP_PACKAGE,
    permissions: [...permissions],
    action: 'grant',
  } as ChangePermissionsParams);
}

async function revokePermissions(permissions: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: changePermissions', {
    appPackage: APP_PACKAGE,
    permissions: [...permissions],
    action: 'revoke',
  } as ChangePermissionsParams);
}

describe('Location permission scenarios', () => {
  afterEach(async () => {
    await revokePermissions(LOCATION_PERMISSIONS);
  });

  it('shows the map view when fine location is granted', async () => {
    await grantPermissions(LOCATION_PERMISSIONS);
    await browser.terminateApp(undefined, APP_PACKAGE);
    await browser.activateApp(undefined, APP_PACKAGE);
    await expect($('~map_container')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 5_000 });
  });

  it('shows the manual location input when location is revoked', async () => {
    await revokePermissions(LOCATION_PERMISSIONS);
    await browser.terminateApp(undefined, APP_PACKAGE);
    await browser.activateApp(undefined, APP_PACKAGE);
    await expect($('~manual_location_input')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 5_000 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: changePermissions` uses `pm grant` / `pm revoke` under the hood — which is instant (no reinstall needed) and works without a system-level APK — but permission changes only take effect after the app process is restarted, so `terminateApp` + `activateApp` is always required after the call; additionally, `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` cannot be granted via `pm grant` on Android 11+ without `REVOKE_RUNTIME_PERMISSIONS` system permission (which UIAutomator2 does not hold), so background location tests on API 30+ must instead use `mobile: setPermission` (XCUITest) or pre-seed the permission via `appium:permissions` capability at session creation.

**Pattern 741** — `browser.execute('mobile: setLocation', { latitude, longitude, altitude })` — GPS location spoofing for location-gated feature tests
```typescript
// 'mobile: setLocation' is available on iOS (XCUITest Simulator) and Android (UIAutomator2 emulator + real device)
// Android: requires 'ALLOW_MOCK_LOCATION' setting enabled in Developer Options or appium:locationServicesEnabled: true
// iOS: works only on Simulator; real iOS device requires a GPX file injected via Xcode scheme

interface GeoLocation {
  latitude: number;
  longitude: number;
  altitude?: number;
  horizontalAccuracy?: number; // iOS Simulator only (metres)
  verticalAccuracy?: number;   // iOS Simulator only (metres)
  speed?: number;              // iOS Simulator only (m/s)
  course?: number;             // iOS Simulator only (degrees, 0=North)
}

const LOCATIONS = {
  sanFrancisco:     { latitude: 37.7749,  longitude: -122.4194, altitude: 16 },
  newYork:          { latitude: 40.7128,  longitude: -74.0060,  altitude: 10 },
  london:           { latitude: 51.5074,  longitude: -0.1278,   altitude: 11 },
  outOfServiceZone: { latitude: 0.0,      longitude: 0.0,       altitude: 0  },
} satisfies Record<string, GeoLocation>;

async function setLocation(loc: GeoLocation): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: setLocation', loc);
  // Brief pause for CLLocationManager / FusedLocationProviderClient to deliver the mock fix
  await browser.pause(500);
}

describe('Location-gated feature tests', () => {
  it('shows local restaurant recommendations for San Francisco', async () => {
    await setLocation(LOCATIONS.sanFrancisco);
    await $('~home_tab').click();
    const heading = await $('~restaurants_nearby_heading');
    await heading.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await heading.getText()).toContain('San Francisco');
  });

  it('shows an unavailable banner for unsupported regions', async () => {
    await setLocation(LOCATIONS.outOfServiceZone);
    await $('~home_tab').click();
    await expect($('~service_unavailable_banner')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 5_000 });
  });

  it('delivers geofence entry notification when entering the delivery zone', async () => {
    // Start outside the zone, then move inside
    await setLocation(LOCATIONS.outOfServiceZone);
    await browser.pause(1_000);
    await setLocation(LOCATIONS.sanFrancisco);
    const notification = await $('~geofence_entry_notification');
    await notification.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: setLocation` injects a mock GPS fix directly into `CLLocationManager` (iOS) or Android's `FusedLocationProviderClient` (via Appium's mock location provider) — giving deterministic geofence and region-detection tests without physical movement — but on iOS it only works on the Simulator (real devices ignore the mock unless a GPX file is injected at Xcode scheme launch), and on Android the mock fix precision degrades when the app uses `PRIORITY_HIGH_ACCURACY` mode (which fuses GPS, WiFi, and cell signals), causing the app to receive the mocked latitude/longitude but with accuracy radius derived from actual WiFi/cell triangulation rather than the provided `horizontalAccuracy`, which can cause geofence boundary tests to be flaky on real-device farms near zone edges.

---

**Pattern 742** — `browser.execute('mobile: sendSms', { phoneNumber, message })` — SMS reception simulation on Android emulators for OTP and notification tests
```typescript
// 'mobile: sendSms' is Android emulator-only (UIAutomator2 via adb emu sms send)
// The SMS appears in the system SMS inbox and triggers the app's BroadcastReceiver for SMS_RECEIVED
// Requires: Android emulator (AVD), not available on real devices

interface SmsParams {
  phoneNumber: string; // sender phone number (arbitrary string, e.g. '+15551234567')
  message: string;     // SMS body text
}

const OTP_SENDER = '+15550000001';

async function waitForSmsOtp(
  otpInputSelector: string,
  timeoutMs = 10_000,
): Promise<string> {
  // Most apps using SMS Retriever API or READ_SMS permission auto-fill the OTP field
  const otpInput = await $(otpInputSelector);
  await otpInput.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const val = await otpInput.getValue();
      return val.length >= 4; // OTPs are typically 4–8 digits
    },
    { timeout: timeoutMs, interval: 500, timeoutMsg: 'OTP was not auto-filled' },
  );
  return otpInput.getValue();
}

describe('OTP login flow — emulator SMS injection', () => {
  it('auto-fills the OTP from an injected SMS and completes login', async () => {
    await $('~phone_number_input').setValue('+15559876543');
    await $('~send_otp_button').click();

    // Wait for the OTP request screen to appear
    await $('~otp_input_field').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    // Inject the OTP SMS into the emulator
    await browser.execute('mobile: sendSms', {
      phoneNumber: OTP_SENDER,
      message: 'Your verification code is 482719. Do not share this code.',
    } as SmsParams);

    // App should auto-fill via SMS User Consent API or READ_SMS
    const filledOtp = await waitForSmsOtp('~otp_input_field');
    expect(filledOtp).toBe('482719');

    await $('~verify_otp_button').click();
    await expect($('~home_dashboard')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 8_000 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: sendSms` uses the Android emulator's `adb emu sms send` console command — which triggers the full system SMS broadcast pipeline including `SMS_RECEIVED` intents, `SmsManager` delivery notifications, and notification-bar alerts — making it a true end-to-end OTP flow test, but it is restricted to emulators (the `adb emu` console is not available on real devices) and cannot simulate RCS messages or SMS from specific carrier short codes (which may bypass `SMS_RECEIVED` on some OEM builds); real-device OTP tests require a physical SIM card or a Twilio sandbox number injected by a separate API call outside the Appium session.

---

**Pattern 743** — `browser.execute('mobile: openUrl', { url })` — opening URLs in Safari/Chrome from within an app session without losing Appium context
```typescript
// 'mobile: openUrl' (iOS XCUITest) opens the URL in Safari without losing the session
// Android equivalent: 'mobile: deepLink' with browser package, or appiumStartActivity with VIEW intent
// Useful for: OAuth redirect testing, universal-link handling, inter-app browser handoffs

async function openUrlInBrowser(url: string): Promise<void> {
  const caps = (await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()).capabilities;
  const isIOS = caps['platformName']?.toLowerCase() === 'ios';

  if (isIOS) {
    // XCUITest 'mobile: openUrl' opens Safari and keeps the session alive
    await browser.execute('mobile: openUrl', { url });
  } else {
    // Android: launch Chrome via explicit intent
    await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'am',
      args: [
        'start', '-a', 'android.intent.action.VIEW',
        '-d', url,
        '-n', 'com.android.chrome/com.google.android.apps.chrome.Main',
      ],
    });
  }
  // Wait for browser to become active context
  await browser.pause(2_000);
}

describe('OAuth redirect flow — in-app browser handoff', () => {
  it('handles the OAuth callback and returns the app to an authenticated state', async () => {
    await $('~sign_in_with_google_button').click();

    // App opens an SFSafariViewController/Chrome Custom Tab — switch to WEBVIEW
    await browser.waitUntil(async () => {
      const contexts = await browser.getAppiumContexts();
      return contexts.some((c) => c !== 'NATIVE_APP');
    }, { timeout: 10_000, interval: 500 });

    const contexts = await browser.getAppiumContexts();
    const webCtx = contexts.find((c) => c !== 'NATIVE_APP');
    if (!webCtx) throw new Error('No WEBVIEW context found for OAuth flow');

    await browser.switchAppiumContext(webCtx);
    // Fill Google sign-in form in the browser WebView
    await $('input[type="email"]').setValue('testuser@example.com');
    await $('input[id="identifierNext"]').click();
    await $('input[type="password"]').setValue('TestP@ss!');
    await $('input[id="passwordNext"]').click();

    // Return to native app context after redirect
    await browser.switchAppiumContext('NATIVE_APP');
    await expect($('~user_avatar')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 15_000 });
  });

  it('opens an external URL from a notification and verifies deep-link return', async () => {
    await openUrlInBrowser('https://app.example.com/promo/summer2026');
    // App intercepts the Universal Link and navigates internally
    await browser.switchAppiumContext('NATIVE_APP');
    await expect($('~promo_banner_summer2026')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 8_000 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: openUrl` on iOS switches the device to Safari, which causes the Appium session's active context to remain in `NATIVE_APP` but the visible screen to show Safari — tests that call `switchAppiumContext('WEBVIEW_<pid>')` after `openUrl` are interacting with the Safari renderer, not with an in-app `WKWebView`, and `browser.getUrl()` will return the Safari address bar URL rather than a WebView URL; this distinction matters for Universal Link tests where the app is expected to intercept the URL and navigate internally, in which case `openUrl` will result in Safari opening rather than the app handling it unless the test device's Safari has "Open Links" set to "In App" in iOS Settings > Safari.

---

**Pattern 744** — `browser.appiumToggleLocationServices()` — location-services on/off toggle for privacy and permission-reset scenarios
```typescript
// appiumToggleLocationServices() is Android-only (UIAutomator2)
// iOS equivalent: use 'mobile: setPermission' with service: 'location' and access: 'always'|'never'
// Toggles the device-level Location Services master switch (Settings > Location)

async function getLocationMode(): Promise<number> {
  const result = await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'settings',
    args: ['get', 'secure', 'location_mode'],
  }) as string;
  return parseInt(result.trim(), 10);
}

async function assertLocationServicesEnabled(expectedEnabled: boolean): Promise<void> {
  // location_mode: 0 = off, 1 = sensors_only, 2 = battery_saving, 3 = high_accuracy
  const mode = await getLocationMode();
  expect(mode > 0).toBe(expectedEnabled);
}

describe('Location services master toggle', () => {
  let initialLocationMode: number;

  before(async () => {
    initialLocationMode = await getLocationMode();
  });

  after(async () => {
    // Restore original state to avoid cross-test pollution
    const currentMode = await getLocationMode();
    const currentlyEnabled = currentMode > 0;
    const wasEnabled = initialLocationMode > 0;
    if (currentlyEnabled !== wasEnabled) {
      await browser.appiumToggleLocationServices();
    }
  });

  it('shows a location-disabled prompt when location services are turned off', async () => {
    const mode = await getLocationMode();
    if (mode === 0) await browser.appiumToggleLocationServices(); // ensure it's on first
    await browser.appiumToggleLocationServices(); // now turn off

    await browser.terminateApp(undefined, 'com.example.app');
    await browser.activateApp(undefined, 'com.example.app');
    await expect($('~enable_location_prompt')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 5_000 });
    await assertLocationServicesEnabled(false);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumToggleLocationServices()` flips the device-level location master switch — which affects all apps and services on the device — making it appropriate for testing the app's initial-launch "please enable location" prompt, but because it is a device-wide change it can interfere with background location services used by other test apps running concurrently on the same device, and the toggle is stateful (it flips the current state) requiring a pre-flight `settings get secure location_mode` ADB query to determine whether the current state is on or off before each call; on Android 10+ the toggle also triggers a system permission review notification that can obscure test UI elements unless dismissed via `$('~allow_all_the_time_button')`.

---

**Pattern 745** — `browser.execute('mobile: flingGesture', { elementId, direction, speed })` — high-velocity fling for end-of-list detection and inertia-scroll tests on Android
```typescript
// 'mobile: flingGesture' is Android-only (UIAutomator2 driver)
// Returns: true if the gesture caused more scrolling (content remains), false if end-of-list reached
// Difference from scrollGesture: flingGesture uses velocity (speed) not distance (percent)
// speed range: 500–40000 pixels/second (default: 7500)

interface FlingGestureParams {
  elementId?: string;
  left?: number;
  top?: number;
  width?: number;
  height?: number;
  direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right';
  speed?: number; // px/s
}

/**
 * Fling a list to the bottom and collect all item labels seen during the fling.
 */
async function flingToBottom(
  listSelector: string,
  maxFlings = 10,
): Promise<string[]> {
  const list = await $(listSelector);
  const collectedLabels = new Set<string>();

  for (let i = 0; i < maxFlings; i++) {
    // Collect currently visible items
    const items = await list.$$('~list_item_label');
    for (const item of items) {
      collectedLabels.add(await item.getText());
    }

    const hasMore = await browser.execute('mobile: flingGesture', {
      elementId: list.elementId,
      direction: 'down',
      speed: 15_000, // fast fling to skip large chunks of the list
    } as FlingGestureParams) as boolean;

    if (!hasMore) break;
    await browser.pause(800); // wait for inertia scroll to settle
  }

  return [...collectedLabels];
}

it('loads all 200 items in the product catalogue via fling-to-bottom', async () => {
  await $('~products_tab').click();
  const allLabels = await flingToBottom('~product_list_container');
  expect(allLabels.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(200);
});

it('triggers the load-more sentinel at the bottom of an infinite scroll list', async () => {
  const list = await $('~infinite_scroll_list');
  let hasMore = true;
  while (hasMore) {
    hasMore = await browser.execute('mobile: flingGesture', {
      elementId: list.elementId,
      direction: 'down',
      speed: 20_000,
    } as FlingGestureParams) as boolean;
    await browser.pause(600);
  }
  await expect($('~end_of_feed_label')).toBeDisplayed({ wait: 5_000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: flingGesture` replicates a user's fast swipe-and-release motion including UIAutomator2's physics-based inertia continuation — making it suitable for testing infinite-scroll pagination triggers that only fire when the scroll velocity exceeds a threshold — but the `speed` parameter maps to UIAutomator2's `ViewConfiguration.getScaledMinimumFlingVelocity()` baseline, and on devices with high-density displays (xxxhdpi, 640 dpi) the effective scroll distance for a given speed value is roughly 4× that of an mdpi device; tests using fixed `speed` values calibrated on one DPI tier will overshoot or undershoot on other tiers, so production CI pipelines should divide the target speed by the DPI scale factor retrieved from `mobile: deviceInfo`.

---

**Pattern 746** — `browser.execute('mobile: doubleClickGesture', { elementId })` — double-tap interaction for zoom, like, and edit-mode activation
```typescript
// 'mobile: doubleClickGesture' is Android-only (UIAutomator2 driver, added Appium v1.21)
// iOS equivalent: use W3C Actions with two pointer-down/pointer-up sequences within 300ms
// or 'mobile: doubleTap' (XCUITest mobile execute)

interface DoubleClickGestureParams {
  elementId?: string;
  x?: number; // absolute screen x coordinate (if no elementId)
  y?: number; // absolute screen y coordinate (if no elementId)
}

// Cross-platform double-tap helper
async function doubleTap(element: WebdriverIO.Element): Promise<void> {
  const caps = (await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()).capabilities;
  const isAndroid = caps['platformName']?.toLowerCase() === 'android';

  if (isAndroid) {
    await browser.execute('mobile: doubleClickGesture', {
      elementId: element.elementId,
    } as DoubleClickGestureParams);
  } else {
    // iOS: W3C Actions — two tap events within 300ms
    await browser.action('pointer', {
      parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' },
    })
      .move({ origin: element })
      .down()
      .pause(50)
      .up()
      .pause(100)
      .down()
      .pause(50)
      .up()
      .perform();
  }
}

describe('Double-tap interaction patterns', () => {
  it('likes a photo when double-tapped', async () => {
    await $('~feed_tab').click();
    const firstPhoto = await $('~feed_photo_item');
    await firstPhoto.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    await doubleTap(firstPhoto);

    const likeHeart = await $('~like_heart_animation');
    await likeHeart.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 2_000 });
    const likeCount = await $('~like_count_label');
    expect(parseInt(await likeCount.getText(), 10)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  it('enters edit mode on a text cell when double-tapped', async () => {
    const textCell = await $('~editable_note_cell');
    await doubleTap(textCell);
    const editField = await $('~note_edit_text_field');
    await editField.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
    expect(await editField.isFocused()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: doubleClickGesture` on Android uses UIAutomator2's `UiObject2.doubleClick()` which fires two pointer events separated by UIAutomator2's internal double-click interval (~100ms) — ensuring the OS gesture recogniser always classifies the action as a double-tap — while the iOS W3C Actions approach requires manually calibrating the inter-tap pause (50–300ms window is device-dependent), making the Android implementation more reliable for apps using `GestureDetector.SimpleOnGestureListener.onDoubleTap()` but leaving the iOS path prone to single-tap misclassification if the Simulator host CPU is under load and the actual pointer event delivery is slower than the 300ms window.

---

**Pattern 747** — `browser.pullFile(remotePath)` / `browser.pushFile(remotePath, base64Content)` — device file system read/write for document upload, download, and media-library tests
```typescript
// pullFile / pushFile available on iOS (XCUITest) and Android (UIAutomator2)
// iOS: paths under @<bundleId>/ access the app's sandbox container
// Android: paths like /sdcard/Download/ access shared external storage
// remotePath format: iOS '@com.example.app/Documents/invoice.pdf', Android '/sdcard/Download/photo.jpg'

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';

const TEST_FIXTURES = join(process.cwd(), 'test', 'fixtures');

async function pushTestFile(
  devicePath: string,
  localFixtureName: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const fileContent = readFileSync(join(TEST_FIXTURES, localFixtureName));
  await browser.pushFile(devicePath, fileContent.toString('base64'));
}

async function pullAndVerify(
  devicePath: string,
  outputName: string,
): Promise<Buffer> {
  const base64Content = await browser.pullFile(devicePath);
  const buf = Buffer.from(base64Content, 'base64');
  writeFileSync(join(TEST_FIXTURES, 'output', outputName), buf);
  return buf;
}

describe('Document upload and export flow', () => {
  it('uploads a PDF to the app document picker on Android', async () => {
    // Pre-stage the PDF in external storage so the document picker can find it
    await pushTestFile('/sdcard/Download/test_invoice.pdf', 'invoice_sample.pdf');

    await $('~upload_document_button').click();
    await $('~document_picker_download_folder').click();
    await $('~file_test_invoice_pdf').click();

    const uploadSuccess = await $('~upload_success_indicator');
    await uploadSuccess.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
  });

  it('exports a generated PDF to the iOS app sandbox and verifies content', async () => {
    await $('~generate_invoice_button').click();
    await $('~export_to_files_button').click();

    await browser.pause(2_000); // Wait for file write to complete

    // Pull the exported file from the iOS app Documents sandbox
    const pdfBytes = await pullAndVerify(
      '@com.example.app/Documents/exported_invoice.pdf',
      'exported_invoice.pdf',
    );

    // Basic PDF header validation
    expect(pdfBytes.slice(0, 4).toString('ascii')).toBe('%PDF');
    expect(pdfBytes.length).toBeGreaterThan(1_024);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `pushFile` / `pullFile` transfer files directly via the Appium server's file system bridge — bypassing UI interaction for test data setup and artefact collection — but on iOS real devices (not Simulator) `pushFile` requires the app to have the `UIFileSharingEnabled` or `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace` Info.plist key set to `YES`; without this entitlement, `pushFile` silently returns success but the file is not created in the app sandbox, causing downstream test steps that depend on the file to fail with confusing `element not found` errors rather than a clear Appium error; always follow `pushFile` with a `pullFile` round-trip check on the same path to verify the file was actually written before proceeding.

**Pattern 748** — `browser.execute('mobile: longClickGesture', { elementId, duration })` — long-press for context menu, drag-initiation, and haptic feedback tests on Android
```typescript
// 'mobile: longClickGesture' is Android-only (UIAutomator2 driver)
// duration: milliseconds to hold the press (default: 500ms)
// iOS equivalent: 'mobile: touchAndHold' (XCUITest) or W3C Actions pointer down + pause + up

interface LongClickGestureParams {
  elementId?: string;
  x?: number;
  y?: number;
  duration?: number; // ms; default 500
}

// Cross-platform long-press helper
async function longPress(
  element: WebdriverIO.Element,
  durationMs = 800,
): Promise<void> {
  const caps = (await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()).capabilities;
  const isAndroid = caps['platformName']?.toLowerCase() === 'android';

  if (isAndroid) {
    await browser.execute('mobile: longClickGesture', {
      elementId: element.elementId,
      duration: durationMs,
    } as LongClickGestureParams);
  } else {
    // iOS: W3C touch action with explicit duration
    await browser.action('pointer', {
      parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' },
    })
      .move({ origin: element })
      .down()
      .pause(durationMs)
      .up()
      .perform();
  }
}

describe('Long-press context-menu interactions', () => {
  it('shows the copy/paste context menu on long-press of a message bubble', async () => {
    const bubble = await $('~message_bubble_text');
    await bubble.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await longPress(bubble, 800);

    const contextMenu = await $('~context_menu_popup');
    await contextMenu.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 2_000 });

    const menuItems = await contextMenu.$$('~context_menu_item');
    const labels = await Promise.all(menuItems.map((m) => m.getText()));
    expect(labels).toContain('Copy');
    expect(labels).toContain('Reply');
  });

  it('initiates drag-and-drop reorder on long-press of a list item', async () => {
    const firstItem  = await $('~reorder_list_item_0');
    const secondItem = await $('~reorder_list_item_1');
    const firstItemText  = await firstItem.getText();
    const secondItemText = await secondItem.getText();

    // Long-press to enter drag mode, then immediately perform drag gesture
    await longPress(firstItem, 700);
    const firstLoc  = await firstItem.getLocation();
    const firstSize = await firstItem.getSize();
    const secondLoc = await secondItem.getLocation();
    const secondSize = await secondItem.getSize();

    await browser.execute('mobile: dragGesture', {
      startX: firstLoc.x  + firstSize.width  / 2,
      startY: firstLoc.y,
      endX:   secondLoc.x + secondSize.width  / 2,
      endY:   secondLoc.y + secondSize.height,
      speed:  2_000,
    });

    // Verify items swapped positions
    expect(await $('~reorder_list_item_0').getText()).toBe(secondItemText);
    expect(await $('~reorder_list_item_1').getText()).toBe(firstItemText);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: longClickGesture` uses UIAutomator2's `UiObject2.longClick()` — which internally fires a `MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN` held for the specified `duration` — giving exact millisecond control over press duration and making it suitable for apps that use `View.setOnLongClickListener()` with a threshold greater than the 500ms Android default, but the gesture terminates immediately after `duration` without maintaining pointer contact, which means it cannot be chained directly into a drag gesture via the same pointer stream; drag-after-long-press sequences must use `mobile: dragGesture` as a separate call immediately after `longClickGesture` returns, and the tiny pause between the two calls can cause the drag to fail on apps that require uninterrupted pointer contact from the long-press trigger through the drag motion.

### Community Gotchas

**C66-1** — `browser.startRecordingScreen()` on Android silently truncates recordings longer than 180 seconds without throwing an error — causing CI failure evidence videos to be cut off mid-test
Why this matters: UIAutomator2 delegates Android screen recording to `adb shell screenrecord`, which has a hard OS-level 180-second limit imposed by MediaRecorder. When a test (or `beforeAll` + test combination) runs longer than 3 minutes, `startRecordingScreen()` continues returning success, but the underlying `screenrecord` process stops writing frames at the 180 s boundary and closes the file. `stopRecordingScreen()` then returns the truncated Base64 content without any error or indication that the recording was cut short. CI pipelines that use screen recordings as failure evidence will silently produce incomplete MP4 artefacts for slow tests, making crash investigations misleading. The only symptom is that the returned video ends abruptly at 3 minutes rather than at the actual test end.
Fix: Pass `timeLimit: 170` in the `startRecordingScreen()` options to allow a safety buffer before the OS limit, and for tests expected to run longer, implement a recording rotation pattern: call `stopRecordingScreen()` every 2 minutes (saving the chunk), then immediately call `startRecordingScreen()` again to begin the next chunk, accumulating segments that can be concatenated post-run with `ffmpeg -f concat`.

---

**C66-2** — `browser.pushFile()` to iOS real-device app sandbox silently succeeds but does not create the file when the app lacks the `UIFileSharingEnabled` or `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace` Info.plist keys
Why this matters: `pushFile('@com.example.app/Documents/test.pdf')` on iOS uses the WDA file-proxy endpoint, which requires either `UIFileSharingEnabled = YES` or `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace = YES` in the app's `Info.plist`. When neither key is present, the XCUITest driver returns HTTP 200 — indistinguishable from a successful write — but the file is never created on the device's file system. Test steps that depend on the file (e.g., a document picker that should show `test.pdf`) will fail with `element not found` rather than an Appium-level error, and the root cause is invisible in WDA or Appium server logs. This is particularly common in apps built from CI pipelines where the file-sharing entitlement is intentionally disabled in the Release build configuration used for testing.
Fix: Immediately after `pushFile()`, call `pullFile()` on the same path and assert the returned Base64 length is greater than 4 bytes to confirm the write succeeded before proceeding; if the round-trip check fails, enable `UIFileSharingEnabled` in the app's Debug/QA build Info.plist, or use `mobile: shell` on Android where the path is in external storage and no special entitlement is needed.

---

**C66-3** — `browser.execute('mobile: flingGesture', ...)` returns `false` (end-of-list) prematurely on `RecyclerView` with `StaggeredGridLayoutManager` — UIAutomator2's scroll-completion detection does not support staggered grid layouts
Why this matters: UIAutomator2's `mobile: flingGesture` end-of-list detection relies on `AccessibilityNodeInfo.getScrollableNodeInfos()` and `AccessibilityRecord.isToEnd()` to determine whether the `RecyclerView` has reached its scroll boundary. `RecyclerView` with `LinearLayoutManager` and `GridLayoutManager` update these accessibility signals correctly after each fling, but `StaggeredGridLayoutManager` has a known Android framework bug where `isToEnd()` returns `true` after the first fling that brings any item's bottom edge below the viewport — even when the majority of items are still off-screen. Tests that use `mobile: flingGesture` to scroll through a staggered grid (e.g., a Pinterest-style feed) will terminate the scroll loop on the first fling and miss all content beyond the first screenful.
Fix: Replace `mobile: flingGesture`'s boolean return with a content-length check: after each fling, count visible items with `$$('~staggered_item')` and compare to the previous count; if the count increased, continue fling regardless of the `false` return value; stop only when the count stabilises across two consecutive flings, indicating genuine end-of-content.

---

**C66-4** — `browser.execute('mobile: setLocation', ...)` on Android emulator does not update the location received by apps using `LocationManager.GPS_PROVIDER` directly — it only updates `FusedLocationProviderClient` (Google Play Services)
Why this matters: `mobile: setLocation` on Android works by injecting a mock fix via the Appium Mock Location Provider, which is registered as a test provider and delivered through `FusedLocationProviderClient` (FLPC). Apps that use FLPC (`LocationServices.getFusedLocationProviderClient()`) receive the mock coordinates correctly, but apps that use the raw Android `LocationManager` with `GPS_PROVIDER` — common in navigation, fitness, and outdoor apps — bypass FLPC entirely and continue receiving the emulator's default `0.0, 0.0` GPS fix. The distinction is invisible until the test runs: `mobile: setLocation` returns success in both cases, but location-dependent UI in GPS_PROVIDER apps will not react to the injected coordinates, causing geofence and route-calculation tests to fail silently with the app showing "GPS signal lost" or defaulting to the null-island location.
Fix: For apps using `GPS_PROVIDER`, inject the mock fix via `adb emu geo fix <lon> <lat>` using `mobile: shell` with `command: 'geo'` on Android emulators — this updates the emulator's GPS hardware stub which feeds `GPS_PROVIDER` directly — and guard the approach with a check for the `avd` capability (emulator-only); for real devices with GPS_PROVIDER, use NMEA sentence injection via `adb emu geo nmea` or switch the app's location provider strategy to FLPC in the test build configuration.

---

**C66-5** — `browser.getLogs('logcat')` returns an empty array when called too quickly after `activateApp()` — the UIAutomator2 log buffer requires ~500ms to hydrate after app activation
Why this matters: UIAutomator2's `getLogs('logcat')` reads from an internal ring buffer that UIAutomator2 populates by tailing the device's logcat stream via `adb logcat -d` at the point in time the call is made. When `getLogs()` is called within ~500ms of `activateApp()`, the logcat buffer hasn't yet captured the app's startup log output — including crash signals (`FATAL EXCEPTION`), service bindings, and analytics init entries — because the `adb logcat` read happens before the app process has written to the system log. Tests that call `activateApp()` immediately followed by `getLogs()` to assert on startup events will consistently see an empty array and false-pass the assertion, masking startup crashes that occur on cold launch. This is the inverse of the destructive-read issue: here the buffer is simply not yet populated.
Fix: Insert `await browser.pause(800)` or a `browser.waitUntil(async () => (await browser.getLogs('logcat') as LogEntry[]).length > 0)` after `activateApp()` before calling `getLogs()`; prefer the `waitUntil` approach with a 5-second timeout to adapt to device speed differences rather than a fixed sleep, and always accumulate log entries in a local array between `getLogs()` calls since each call destructively drains the buffer.

## Cycle 65 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 718** — `appiumGetPerformanceDataTypes()` + `appiumGetPerformanceData()` — CPU/memory regression guard
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

interface PerfMatrix { [key: string]: number }

async function getPerfSnapshot(pkg: string, type: 'cpuinfo' | 'memoryinfo'): Promise<PerfMatrix> {
  // appiumGetPerformanceData returns string[][]  — row 0 = headers, row 1 = values
  const raw = await browser.appiumGetPerformanceData(pkg, type, 3) as string[][];
  if (!raw || raw.length < 2 || raw[1].length === 0) {
    throw new Error(`perf data not ready for type=${type} — retry after warm-up`);
  }
  const [headers, values] = raw;
  return Object.fromEntries(headers.map((h, i) => [h, parseFloat(values[i] ?? '0')]));
}

describe('performance regression guard', () => {
  const PACKAGE = 'com.example.app';

  it('reports available perf types and guards missing ones', async () => {
    const types = await browser.appiumGetPerformanceDataTypes();
    expect(types).toContain('cpuinfo');
    expect(types).toContain('memoryinfo');
  });

  it('CPU stays under 30% during idle (user+kernel combined)', async () => {
    await browser.pause(2000); // allow one background poll cycle to populate buffer
    const cpu = await getPerfSnapshot(PACKAGE, 'cpuinfo');
    const total = (cpu['user'] ?? 0) + (cpu['kernel'] ?? 0);
    expect(total).toBeLessThan(30);
  });

  it('memory does not grow beyond 150 MB after 5 back-and-forth navigations', async () => {
    const baseline = await getPerfSnapshot(PACKAGE, 'memoryinfo');
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      await $('~nav_next').click();
      await browser.pause(500);
      await $('~nav_back').click();
      await browser.pause(500);
    }
    const after = await getPerfSnapshot(PACKAGE, 'memoryinfo');
    const growthKb = (after['totalPrivateDirty'] ?? 0) - (baseline['totalPrivateDirty'] ?? 0);
    expect(growthKb).toBeLessThan(150 * 1024);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumGetPerformanceData` is Android-only (UIAutomator2 driver) and returns a `string[][]` matrix whose column set differs between UIAutomator2 v2.x and v3.x — v3 drops `totalSharedDirty` and adds `gpuMemory` — so any assertion must use `?? 0` fallbacks and confirm column availability via `appiumGetPerformanceDataTypes()` first; on the first call after app launch the buffer is empty and `raw.length < 2`, requiring a 500 ms retry loop before usable data is returned, and iOS has no equivalent API (use `mobile: startPerfRecord` via XCUITest instead).

**Pattern 719** — `startRecordingScreen()` / `stopRecordingScreen()` — per-test video evidence on failure
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

const VIDEO_DIR = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../artifacts/videos');

async function startVideo(): Promise<void> {
  fs.mkdirSync(VIDEO_DIR, { recursive: true });
  // Stop any in-progress recording first — calling start twice silently discards the first buffer
  await browser.stopRecordingScreen().catch(() => { /* no-op if nothing was recording */ });
  await browser.startRecordingScreen({
    videoType: 'h264',        // iOS: h264 | mp4; Android: default mpeg4
    videoQuality: 'medium',   // iOS only: low | medium | high | photo
    videoFps: 10,             // lower fps = smaller file; 10 fps sufficient for failure diagnosis
    timeLimit: '180',         // cap at 3 minutes to prevent oversized CI artifacts
  });
}

async function stopVideo(testTitle: string, passed: boolean): Promise<string | null> {
  const base64 = await browser.stopRecordingScreen();
  if (!base64) return null;
  if (passed) return null; // discard passing-test recordings immediately
  const safeName = testTitle.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_').substring(0, 80);
  const outPath = path.join(VIDEO_DIR, `${safeName}_${Date.now()}.mp4`);
  fs.writeFileSync(outPath, Buffer.from(base64, 'base64'));
  return outPath;
}

// In wdio.conf.ts:
export const wdioHooks = {
  beforeTest: async () => startVideo(),
  afterTest: async (test: { title: string }, _ctx: unknown, result: { passed: boolean }) => {
    const videoPath = await stopVideo(test.title, result.passed);
    if (videoPath) console.log(`[FAILURE VIDEO] ${videoPath}`);
  },
};
```
Tradeoff: `stopRecordingScreen` encodes the full video in memory and returns it as a single Base64 string — on shared CI runners a 3-minute 1080p recording can take 8–12 seconds to encode after `stop` is called, blocking the `afterTest` hook and inflating total suite time by 15–20%; setting `videoFps: 10` and `videoSize: '720x1280'` reduces encoding time to under 2 seconds per test, and deleting passing-test recordings immediately avoids accumulating gigabytes of video artifacts that exceed CI artifact retention limits.

**Pattern 720** — `getLogs('logcat')` — Android logcat assertion for silent native crashes
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

interface LogEntry { timestamp: number; level: string; message: string }

async function drainLogcat(): Promise<LogEntry[]> {
  // getLogs clears the Appium ring buffer on each call — returns only new entries since last drain
  return (await browser.getLogs('logcat')) as LogEntry[];
}

function findFatalEntries(logs: LogEntry[]): LogEntry[] {
  return logs.filter(e =>
    e.level === 'FATAL' ||
    e.message.includes('AndroidRuntime') ||
    e.message.includes('FATAL EXCEPTION') ||
    e.message.includes('Application Not Responding')
  );
}

describe('crash-free navigation', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await drainLogcat(); // clear stale entries so each test starts with a clean buffer
  });

  it('checkout flow produces no FATAL or ANR log entries', async () => {
    await $('~cart_icon').click();
    await $('~checkout_btn').click();
    await $('~confirm_purchase_btn').click();
    await $('~order_success_banner').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });

    const logs = await drainLogcat();
    const fatals = findFatalEntries(logs);
    if (fatals.length > 0) {
      throw new Error(
        `Logcat: ${fatals.length} fatal entries during checkout:\n` +
        fatals.map(e => `  [${e.level}] ${e.message}`).join('\n')
      );
    }
    expect(fatals).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `getLogs('logcat')` returns only entries that accumulated since the last call (Appium server maintains a ring buffer capped at 10,000 entries by default) — if a test generates high log volume from a chatty library, earlier FATAL entries can be evicted before `getLogs` is called, producing false-clean results; mitigate by setting `appium:logcatFilterSpecs: ['*:W']` in capabilities to suppress DEBUG/INFO noise and keep only WARN/ERROR/FATAL entries, reducing buffer pressure by 80–90% in typical apps, and call `drainLogcat()` at a 1-second polling interval in `before()` for suites where log volume is high.

**Pattern 721** — `pushFile()` / `pullFile()` — deterministic fixture injection and result extraction
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

const FIXTURE = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../fixtures/mock-config.json');
// Android: bare /data/data/<pkg>/files/ path; iOS: must use @bundleId/ prefix
const ANDROID_DEVICE_PATH = '/data/data/com.example.app/files/config.json';
const IOS_DEVICE_PATH     = '@com.example.app/Documents/config.json';

async function devicePath(): Promise<string> {
  const caps = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as Record<string, unknown>;
  const platform = (caps['platformName'] as string ?? '').toLowerCase();
  return platform === 'ios' ? IOS_DEVICE_PATH : ANDROID_DEVICE_PATH;
}

async function pushFixture(localPath: string): Promise<void> {
  const content = fs.readFileSync(localPath);
  await browser.pushFile(await devicePath(), content.toString('base64'));
}

async function pullResult(relPath: string, localOut: string): Promise<string> {
  const caps = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as Record<string, unknown>;
  const platform = (caps['platformName'] as string ?? '').toLowerCase();
  const dp = platform === 'ios'
    ? `@com.example.app/${relPath}`
    : `/data/data/com.example.app/files/${relPath}`;
  const base64 = await browser.pullFile(dp);
  const decoded = Buffer.from(base64, 'base64').toString('utf8');
  fs.writeFileSync(localOut, decoded);
  return decoded;
}

it('app reads injected config and writes expected output file', async () => {
  await pushFixture(FIXTURE);
  await browser.terminateApp(undefined, 'com.example.app');
  await browser.activateApp(undefined, 'com.example.app');
  await $('~dashboard_header').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
  const result = await pullResult('result.json', '/tmp/result.json');
  const parsed = JSON.parse(result);
  expect(parsed.status).toBe('ok');
  expect(parsed.configVersion).toBe('2.0');
});
```
Tradeoff: `pushFile` and `pullFile` transfer data as Base64-encoded strings in the WebDriver JSON body — a 1 MB binary fixture becomes a ~1.33 MB string processed synchronously on the Appium server's main session thread, causing noticeable latency on real devices over USB for files over 5 MB; for large fixtures prefer pre-baking the file into the app bundle toggled via a launch argument, and on iOS the path **must** use the `@<bundleId>/` container-scoped prefix (bare paths silently write to the Appium server's local filesystem instead of the device, with no error returned).

**Pattern 722** — `appiumToggleNetworkSpeed()` — emulator network throttling for slow-network tests
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

type NetSpeed = 'full' | 'lte' | 'edge' | 'gprs' | 'none';

async function withNetworkSpeed<T>(speed: NetSpeed, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  await browser.appiumToggleNetworkSpeed(speed);
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    // Always restore full speed so subsequent tests are unaffected
    await browser.appiumToggleNetworkSpeed('full');
  }
}

async function isAndroidEmulator(): Promise<boolean> {
  const caps = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as Record<string, unknown>;
  const model = (caps['deviceModel'] as string ?? '').toLowerCase();
  return model.includes('emulator') || model.includes('sdk_gphone');
}

describe('slow-network resilience', () => {
  it('feed loads within 15 s on EDGE speed (emulator only)', async () => {
    if (!(await isAndroidEmulator())) {
      console.warn('appiumToggleNetworkSpeed only works on emulators — skipping on real device');
      return;
    }
    await withNetworkSpeed('edge', async () => {
      await $('~feed_refresh_btn').click();
      // EDGE ~236 kbps: 200 KB payload ≈ 7 s — use generous timeout
      const item = await $('~feed_item_0');
      await item.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 15_000 });
      expect(await item.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumToggleNetworkSpeed` maps to the Android emulator's `emulator -netspeed` console command and works only on Android emulators — it has no effect on physical Android devices or any iOS target; for real-device network simulation use a proxy tool (Proxyman, Charles) configured via `appium:proxyPort` in capabilities, and for iOS use the Network Link Conditioner profile activated at the OS level, which requires device-level setup outside the Appium session and must be documented as a manual precondition in the test suite.

**Pattern 723** — `appiumOpenNotifications()` + poll loop — push notification tap flow
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

async function waitForNotification(titleSubstring: string, timeoutMs = 15_000): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    await browser.appiumOpenNotifications();
    // UIAutomator2 exposes notification titles via android:id/title resource-id
    const titles = await $$('android=new UiSelector().resourceId("android:id/title")');
    for (const t of titles) {
      const text = await t.getText().catch(() => '');
      if (text.includes(titleSubstring)) return t;
    }
    // Dismiss drawer and pause before retrying
    await browser.back();
    await browser.pause(1500);
  }
  throw new Error(`Notification "${titleSubstring}" not received within ${timeoutMs} ms`);
}

it('tapping order-ready notification navigates to order detail screen', async () => {
  // Trigger a server-side push via test API / Firebase test console before this point
  const notif = await waitForNotification('Your order');
  await notif.click();
  const header = await $('~order_detail_header');
  await header.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
  expect(await header.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumOpenNotifications()` is Android-only and pulls down the system notification shade — on Samsung One UI and Xiaomi MIUI, the shade uses non-standard `resource-id` values that differ from AOSP's `android:id/title`, making selector-based notification lookup unreliable on OEM builds; always provide a fallback selector `new UiSelector().className("android.widget.TextView").textContains(...)` and on iOS simulate the notification tap via `activateApp` with a deep-link URI passed as a launch argument, since there is no programmatic way to access the iOS notification centre from an Appium session.

**Pattern 724** — `appiumGetSystemBars()` — status-bar and navigation-bar overlap guard
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

interface BarInfo { visible: boolean; x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }
interface SystemBars { statusBar: BarInfo; navigationBar: BarInfo }

async function assertElementClearOfSystemBars(selector: string): Promise<void> {
  const bars  = await browser.appiumGetSystemBars() as SystemBars;
  const el    = await $(selector);
  const loc   = await el.getLocation();
  const sz    = await el.getSize();
  const elTop    = loc.y;
  const elBottom = loc.y + sz.height;

  if (bars.statusBar.visible && bars.statusBar.height > 0) {
    const statusBottom = bars.statusBar.y + bars.statusBar.height;
    expect(elTop).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(statusBottom, {
      message: `${selector} overlaps status bar (statusBottom=${statusBottom}, elTop=${elTop})`,
    } as never);
  }
  // In gesture-navigation mode, navigationBar.height may be 0 — skip assertion when 0
  if (bars.navigationBar.visible && bars.navigationBar.height > 0) {
    expect(elBottom).toBeLessThanOrEqual(bars.navigationBar.y, {
      message: `${selector} overlaps nav bar (navTop=${bars.navigationBar.y}, elBottom=${elBottom})`,
    } as never);
  }
}

it('primary CTA is not obscured by any system bar', async () => {
  await $('~checkout_btn').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await assertElementClearOfSystemBars('~checkout_btn');
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumGetSystemBars()` is Android-only (UIAutomator2) and returns status-bar and navigation-bar dimensions in display pixels at the current orientation — on Android 10+ with gesture-navigation mode enabled, `navigationBar.height` is 0 px even though `visible: true` is returned, because gesture insets are enforced as OS-level padding and do not physically occlude elements; always skip the navigation-bar overlap assertion when `height === 0`, and for iOS use `safeAreaInsets` retrieved via `mobile: deviceInfo` to perform equivalent overlap checks.

**Pattern 725** — `getDeviceTime()` — time-sensitive assertions without device clock desync
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

async function getDeviceNow(): Promise<Date> {
  // Pass explicit format string to avoid locale-dependent output variations
  // UIAutomator2 returns RFC 3339 with offset; XCUITest returns space-separated UTC string
  const raw = await browser.getDeviceTime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S');
  const parsed = new Date(raw);
  if (isNaN(parsed.getTime())) {
    console.warn(`getDeviceTime() returned unparseable string "${raw}" — falling back to host clock`);
    return new Date();
  }
  return parsed;
}

it('session token expires at device time + 60 minutes (±30 s tolerance)', async () => {
  const before = await getDeviceNow();
  await $('~login_btn').click();
  await $('~home_screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });

  // Dev-only debug overlay showing token expiry ISO string
  const tokenEl  = await $('~debug_token_expiry');
  const tokenExpiry = new Date(await tokenEl.getText());

  const expectedExpiry = new Date(before.getTime() + 60 * 60 * 1000);
  const diffMs = Math.abs(tokenExpiry.getTime() - expectedExpiry.getTime());
  // Allow 30 s of slack for network latency during token issuance
  expect(diffMs).toBeLessThan(30_000);
});
```
Tradeoff: `getDeviceTime()` returns a string whose format varies by platform and locale — UIAutomator2 returns RFC 3339 with a timezone offset, XCUITest returns a space-separated UTC string, and some Android builds return locale-formatted strings like `14/05/2026, 14:32`; always pass an explicit `'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'` format string and wrap in a try/catch that falls back to `Date.now()` from the test runner host if parsing fails; for Android emulators started from a snapshot, the device clock may be hours behind until NTP syncs, so add a clock-sync health check via `adb shell su 0 date` in the global `before()` hook.

**Pattern 726** — `appiumLock()` / `appiumUnlock()` / `appiumIsLocked()` — screen-lock lifecycle tests
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

async function lockAndAssert(durationSeconds: number): Promise<void> {
  await browser.appiumLock(durationSeconds);
  // Immediately verify the lock engaged — on misconfigured simulators it silently no-ops
  const locked = await browser.appiumIsLocked();
  if (!locked) {
    throw new Error(
      'appiumLock() returned success but appiumIsLocked() returned false — ' +
      'check that the iOS Simulator has a passcode configured via: xcrun simctl keychain booted set-passcode 0000'
    );
  }
}

async function unlockAndAssert(): Promise<void> {
  await browser.appiumUnlock();
  await browser.pause(1000); // wait for unlock animation
  expect(await browser.appiumIsLocked()).toBe(false);
}

describe('lock-screen behaviour', () => {
  it('app session survives a 5-second device lock', async () => {
    await $('~home_screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await lockAndAssert(5);
    await browser.pause(5500); // wait for auto-unlock timer to fire
    await unlockAndAssert();
    const state = await browser.appiumQueryAppState(undefined, 'com.example.app');
    expect(state).toBe(4); // FOREGROUND_RUNNING
  });

  it('sensitive field is masked after lock (screenshot size heuristic)', async () => {
    await $('~credit_card_field').setValue('4111111111111111');
    await lockAndAssert(2);
    const screenshot = Buffer.from(await browser.takeScreenshot(), 'base64');
    // Lock screen screenshot should be < 50 KB; app content screenshot is typically > 200 KB
    expect(screenshot.length).toBeLessThan(50_000);
    await unlockAndAssert();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumLock(seconds)` accepts a duration after which the device auto-unlocks — on iOS Simulator the lock/unlock cycle works only when a passcode is configured via `xcrun simctl keychain booted set-passcode 0000`; without a passcode `appiumLock` silently succeeds but `appiumIsLocked()` returns `false` immediately, making lock-dependent tests pass vacuously; always assert `appiumIsLocked() === true` immediately after calling `appiumLock` and throw a descriptive error so the missing-passcode misconfiguration surfaces on the first run rather than masking flaky failures.

**Pattern 727** — `appiumPressKeyCode()` — Android hardware key simulation for navigation tests
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

const KEYCODE = {
  BACK:         4,
  HOME:         3,
  RECENT:     187,
  ENTER:       66,
  DEL:         67,  // backspace
  VOLUME_UP:   24,
  VOLUME_DOWN: 25,
} as const;

const META = { NONE: 0x0, SHIFT: 0x1, ALT: 0x2, CTRL: 0x1000 } as const;

async function pressKey(code: number, meta = META.NONE): Promise<void> {
  // appiumPressKeyCode fires key-down + key-up pair via UIAutomator2 injectInputEvent
  await browser.appiumPressKeyCode(code, meta, 0);
}

it('BACK from checkout returns to cart with address field cleared', async () => {
  await $('~checkout_address_field').setValue('123 Main St');
  await pressKey(KEYCODE.BACK);
  // Should be on cart screen
  await $('~cart_total').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  // Re-enter checkout — address must be cleared (fresh form)
  await $('~checkout_btn').click();
  const addr = await $('~checkout_address_field');
  expect(await addr.getValue()).toBe('');
});

it('volume-down key decreases in-app player volume', async () => {
  await $('~player_screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  const before = parseInt(await $('~volume_indicator').getText(), 10);
  await pressKey(KEYCODE.VOLUME_DOWN);
  await browser.pause(300);
  const after = parseInt(await $('~volume_indicator').getText(), 10);
  expect(after).toBeLessThan(before);
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumPressKeyCode` maps to the Android `KeyEvent` API and fires a real key-down + key-up pair via UIAutomator2's `injectInputEvent` — hardware navigation keys (BACK=4, HOME=3) and text-input keys (ENTER=66, DEL=67) work correctly on both emulators and physical devices, but `KEYCODE_MENU` (82) does not trigger the three-dot ActionBar overflow menu on apps targeting API 28+ because hardware menu-key dispatch was removed in modern `ActionBar`; for overflow menus always use `$('~overflow_menu_btn').click()` via accessibility ID, reserving `appiumPressKeyCode` exclusively for navigation and input keys.

**Pattern 728** — `rotateDevice()` — orientation change and layout reflow assertions
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

type OrientationTarget = 'PORTRAIT' | 'LANDSCAPE';

async function setOrientation(target: OrientationTarget): Promise<void> {
  // Euler z-angle: 0 = portrait, 90 = landscape-right (UIAutomator2); 270 = landscape-left
  const z = target === 'LANDSCAPE' ? 90 : 0;
  await browser.rotateDevice(0, 0, z);
  await browser.pause(800); // allow rotation animation and layout reflow
  // Verify the rotation took effect — on some XCUITest builds 90° produces landscape-left
  const orientation = await browser.getOrientation();
  if (target === 'LANDSCAPE' && !orientation.includes('LANDSCAPE')) {
    await browser.rotateDevice(0, 0, 270); // retry with opposite landscape angle
    await browser.pause(800);
  }
}

it('video player fills viewport width in landscape without letterboxing', async () => {
  await $('~video_player').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await setOrientation('LANDSCAPE');

  const player    = await $('~video_player');
  const playerSz  = await player.getSize();
  const caps      = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as Record<string, unknown>;
  const screenStr = (caps['deviceScreenSize'] as string ?? '').split('x').map(Number);
  const longerDim = Math.max(screenStr[0] ?? 0, screenStr[1] ?? 0);

  expect(Math.abs(playerSz.width - longerDim)).toBeLessThan(8); // ±8 px tolerance
  await setOrientation('PORTRAIT'); // always restore before next test
});
```
Tradeoff: `rotateDevice(x, y, z)` accepts Euler angles in degrees and maps to `SET_ROTATION` on iOS and `setOrientation` on Android — a z-axis rotation of 90 produces landscape-right on UIAutomator2 but may produce landscape-left on certain XCUITest device models, so always verify with `browser.getOrientation()` after the call and retry with z=270 if needed; additionally, `rotateDevice` fails on physical Android devices unless `appium:autoGrantPermissions` is true or the `android.permission.SET_ROTATION` runtime permission has been manually granted, which does not apply to emulators.

**Pattern 729** — `appiumToggleAirplaneMode()` — offline error-state validation with safe teardown
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';

async function withAirplaneMode<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  await browser.appiumToggleAirplaneMode();
  await browser.pause(2000); // wait for OS to report connectivity loss
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    await browser.appiumToggleAirplaneMode(); // always restore
    await browser.pause(2000);               // wait for connectivity to restore
  }
}

async function isIos(): Promise<boolean> {
  const caps = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as Record<string, unknown>;
  return ((caps['platformName'] as string) ?? '').toLowerCase() === 'ios';
}

describe('offline error handling', () => {
  it('account sync failure shows retry dialog, not a crash (Android only)', async () => {
    if (await isIos()) {
      console.warn('appiumToggleAirplaneMode is Android-only — skipping on iOS');
      return;
    }
    await $('~home_screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await withAirplaneMode(async () => {
      await $('~sync_now_btn').click();
      const dialog = await $('~sync_error_dialog');
      await dialog.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
      expect(await dialog.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
      expect(await $('~sync_retry_btn').isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    });
    // After airplane mode lifted, retry should succeed
    await $('~sync_retry_btn').click();
    await $('~sync_success_toast').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 15_000 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appiumToggleAirplaneMode()` is Android-only — on iOS there is no programmatic way to toggle airplane mode from an Appium session because the `toggleAirplaneMode` shell command is unavailable on real iOS devices and the Simulator does not expose an airplane-mode toggle via any public API; for iOS offline tests use a conditional skip based on `platformName === 'iOS'` with an explanatory message, and cover the iOS offline scenario by configuring a Network Link Conditioner profile at the machine level or using a Charles Proxy upstream rule to block all traffic, both of which must be set up as pre-test infrastructure outside the Appium session.

**Pattern 730** — `pullFolder()` — bulk device artifact retrieval for screenshot baseline comparison
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import AdmZip from 'adm-zip';

const DEVICE_SCREENSHOT_DIR = '/sdcard/Pictures/Screenshots';
const LOCAL_OUT = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../artifacts/device-screenshots');

async function pullDeviceScreenshots(): Promise<string[]> {
  // pullFolder returns a Base64-encoded ZIP of the entire directory tree
  const base64Zip = await browser.pullFolder(DEVICE_SCREENSHOT_DIR);
  const zipBuf = Buffer.from(base64Zip, 'base64');
  const zip = new AdmZip(zipBuf);
  fs.mkdirSync(LOCAL_OUT, { recursive: true });

  const pulled: string[] = [];
  for (const entry of zip.getEntries()) {
    if (entry.isDirectory) continue;
    const outPath = path.join(LOCAL_OUT, entry.entryName);
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(outPath), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(outPath, entry.getData());
    pulled.push(outPath);
  }
  return pulled;
}

it('device screenshot directory is populated after onboarding saves a screenshot', async () => {
  await $('~onboarding_start').click();
  await $('~onboarding_finish').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 20_000 });
  await browser.pause(1000); // allow the system screenshot to flush to disk

  const files = await pullDeviceScreenshots();
  expect(files.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
  expect(files.some(f => f.endsWith('.png'))).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: `pullFolder` returns the entire directory tree as a single Base64-encoded ZIP in one HTTP response — for directories containing large files (e.g., video recordings in `/sdcard/Movies`) the Base64 payload can exceed 50 MB, exhausting Node.js's default heap on CI runners with 512 MB memory; always scope `pullFolder` to a known small directory or enumerate file sizes first via `browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'ls', args: ['-la', DEVICE_SCREENSHOT_DIR] })` and fall back to individual `pullFile` calls for any file over 5 MB to avoid OOM conditions in the Appium HTTP client.
