**Pattern 731** — `getAppiumCommands()` + `getAppiumExtensions()` — runtime driver feature guard
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

interface ExtInfo { name: string; version: string }

// Cache results to avoid repeated ~150 ms round-trips per test
let _commandsCache: string[] | null = null;
let _extensionsCache: ExtInfo[] | null = null;

async function supportsCommand(cmd: string): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!_commandsCache) {
    _commandsCache = (await browser.getAppiumCommands()) as string[];
  }
  return _commandsCache.includes(cmd);
}

async function hasExtension(name: string): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!_extensionsCache) {
    _extensionsCache = (await browser.getAppiumExtensions()) as ExtInfo[];
  }
  return _extensionsCache.some(e => e.name === name);
}

describe('feature-guarded advanced capabilities', () => {
  it('runs screen recording only when the driver supports it', async () => {
    if (!(await supportsCommand('startRecordingScreen'))) {
      console.warn('startRecordingScreen not in driver command registry — skipping');
      return;
    }
    await browser.startRecordingScreen();
    await $('~nav_products').click();
    await browser.pause(2000);
    const base64 = await browser.stopRecordingScreen();
    expect(base64.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  it('runs biometric test only when appium-biometrics-plugin is installed', async () => {
    if (!(await hasExtension('appium-biometrics-plugin'))) {
      console.warn('appium-biometrics-plugin not installed — skipping biometric test');
      return;
    }
    await browser.execute('biometric: enroll', { enrolled: true });
    await $('~login_with_biometrics_btn').click();
    await browser.appiumTouchId(true);
    await $('~home_screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `getAppiumCommands()` returns the driver's static command registry, not a runtime device-capability check — a command may appear in the list even when the underlying hardware capability is absent (e.g., `startRecordingScreen` appears for UIAutomator2 on physical devices that lack the `MediaProjection` permission, throwing only at call time); always combine `getAppiumCommands()` guards with a try/catch on the first actual invocation, and cache the result (the call takes ~150 ms on remote Appium servers) so it does not become a 150 ms overhead per test case across a large suite.

---

**Pattern 732** — `installApp()` + `isAppInstalled()` + `removeApp()` — fresh-install lifecycle harness
```typescript
import { browser, expect } from '@wdio/globals';
import * as path from 'path';

const APK_PATH  = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../apps/example-app-debug.apk');
const APP_ID    = 'com.example.app';
const BUNDLE_ID = 'com.example.app';

async function safeRemoveApp(): Promise<void> {
  if (!(await browser.isAppInstalled(APP_ID))) return;
  // Force-stop first to terminate any foreground service — removeApp throws
  // INSTALL_FAILED_INTERNAL_ERROR if a foreground service is still running on Android
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'am', args: ['force-stop', APP_ID] });
  await browser.pause(1000);
  await browser.removeApp(APP_ID);
  await browser.pause(1500); // allow package manager to complete uninstall
  expect(await browser.isAppInstalled(APP_ID)).toBe(false);
}

async function installFresh(): Promise<void> {
  await browser.installApp(APK_PATH, { replace: true, grantPermissions: true });
  expect(await browser.isAppInstalled(APP_ID)).toBe(true);
  await browser.activateApp(undefined, BUNDLE_ID);
  await browser.pause(2000); // allow app to reach initial launch state
}

describe('fresh-install onboarding flow', () => {
  before(async () => {
    await safeRemoveApp();
    await installFresh();
  });

  it('first launch shows onboarding screen, not the home screen', async () => {
    const onboarding = await $('~onboarding_welcome');
    await onboarding.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    expect(await onboarding.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    expect(await $('~home_screen').isExisting()).toBe(false);
  });

  after(async () => {
    await safeRemoveApp(); // clean up — don't leave test APK on shared CI device
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `installApp` with `{ replace: true, grantPermissions: true }` installs the APK and auto-grants all `<uses-permission>` entries at install time — this is convenient for CI but completely bypasses the in-app runtime permission request dialogs (CAMERA, LOCATION, CONTACTS), meaning permission-request UX is never exercised by suites that use this flag; maintain a separate suite that omits `grantPermissions` and interacts with the system permission dialog via `mobile: alert` or `UiAutomator2` selector on `com.android.permissioncontroller`, and always call `am force-stop` before `removeApp` to prevent the `INSTALL_FAILED_INTERNAL_ERROR` thrown when a foreground service is still running at uninstall time.

---

### Community Gotchas

**C65-1** — `appiumGetPerformanceData()` returns an empty array on the very first call after app launch — the performance buffer needs one polling cycle to initialise
Why this matters: UIAutomator2's performance-data subsystem initialises lazily: `appiumGetPerformanceData(pkg, 'cpuinfo', 3)` internally polls `ActivityManager.getProcessMemoryInfo()` and `/proc/stat` on a background thread that starts only when the first API call is received. On that first call the thread has not yet produced a sample, so UIAutomator2 returns `[[]]` — a matrix with a single empty row — rather than a `[headers, values]` pair. Tests that immediately destructure `raw[0]` as headers and `raw[1]` as values throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')` on `raw[1]` because the array has only one element. The error appears intermittently: subsequent calls in the same session return populated data once the background thread has completed its first poll cycle, so the failure rate is highest at the start of a test run and decreases as the session warms up.
Fix: Wrap `appiumGetPerformanceData` in a retry helper that checks `raw.length >= 2 && raw[1].length > 0` before accepting the result, retrying up to 3 times with a 500 ms pause between attempts; treat the first call as a warm-up and always use the second call's data as the baseline measurement, matching the pattern used by Android's own `dumpsys meminfo` tooling which also requires one initialisation cycle before reporting stable values.

---

**C65-2** — `startRecordingScreen()` called twice without an intervening `stopRecordingScreen()` silently discards the first recording — no error is thrown and the first video is permanently lost
Why this matters: Appium's `startRecordingScreen` implementation does not check whether a recording is already in progress — if called a second time it silently starts a new session and the first recording's buffer is discarded without returning the Base64 data or writing any file. In test configurations where `startRecordingScreen` appears in both a `beforeAll` hook and a `beforeEach` hook (a common copy-paste error, or when a shared helper is called at multiple levels), the `beforeEach` invocation silently discards the `beforeAll` recording every time a test begins. The developer discovers this only when `stopRecordingScreen` returns a video clip that begins mid-suite rather than from the session start, and the recording covering the first failing test is permanently gone with no log message indicating the loss.
Fix: Before every `startRecordingScreen` call, always issue a guarded `stopRecordingScreen` first — `void browser.stopRecordingScreen().catch(() => {})` — to flush any in-progress session; additionally maintain an `isRecording` boolean flag in test scope, set it to `true` after start and `false` after stop, and throw if `startRecordingScreen` is called while `isRecording === true`; consider adding an ESLint custom rule that flags two `startRecordingScreen` calls in the same `describe` block without an intervening `stopRecordingScreen`.

---

**C65-3** — `pushFile` on iOS silently writes to the Appium server's local filesystem when a bare path is used — the device never receives the file and no error is thrown
Why this matters: On iOS, `pushFile` uses the XCUITest driver's app-container file system API, which requires a path prefixed with `@<bundleId>/` (e.g., `@com.example.app/Documents/config.json`) to target the app sandbox. If a bare path like `/Documents/config.json` or `./config.json` is passed instead, XCUITest silently interprets it as a relative path on the Appium server's local filesystem and writes the file there, returning a `200 OK` with no error. Subsequent `pullFile` calls from the same bare path return the server-side file, so tests pass in CI (where the server and device share the same machine) but fail on remote Appium grids (where the server and the device are on different hosts) with a `file not found` error that appears to be unrelated to the `pushFile` path issue.
Fix: Always use the `@<bundleId>/<relative-path>` container-scoped syntax for iOS `pushFile` and `pullFile` calls; encapsulate the platform difference in a `deviceFilePath(platform, bundleId, relPath)` helper that prepends `@${bundleId}/` on iOS and `/data/data/${bundleId}/files/` on Android; add this helper to the shared test utilities module and enforce its use in code review, since the iOS requirement is not surfaced in the WDIO documentation and is a frequent source of cross-environment test failures.

---

**C65-4** — `appiumToggleNetworkSpeed()` called on a physical Android device returns success but has no effect — the method silently no-ops and subsequent network calls run at full speed
Why this matters: `appiumToggleNetworkSpeed` maps to the Android emulator's `-netspeed` console command, which is only available when the device is an Android emulator with an open emulator console socket. On physical Android devices, UIAutomator2 sends the command internally, the emulator console socket is not present, and the call returns `200 OK` without throwing — the network speed is unchanged. Tests that use `appiumToggleNetworkSpeed('edge')` to simulate slow-network conditions will run at full device speed on physical devices and CI farms that use real phones, producing false-passing results where timeouts that should trigger under EDGE conditions are never hit. The silent success makes the failure mode entirely invisible unless test authors know to check the driver type before calling the method.
Fix: Always gate `appiumToggleNetworkSpeed` calls with `await isAndroidEmulator()` — check `caps['deviceModel']` for `'emulator'` or `'sdk_gphone'` before invoking; log a clear `console.warn` when the skip fires so it is visible in CI logs; for physical-device slow-network testing, configure a network throttling proxy (Charles, mitmproxy) upstream of the device and toggle rules via the proxy's REST API as a pre-test step.

---

**C65-5** — `removeApp()` throws `INSTALL_FAILED_INTERNAL_ERROR` on Android when the app has an active foreground service — the package manager refuses to uninstall a live service process
Why this matters: Android's package manager requires all processes associated with a package to be stopped before uninstall can proceed. If the app under test starts a foreground service (e.g., music playback, location tracking, or a sync service that persists beyond `terminateApp`) and `removeApp` is called while the service is still running, the package manager returns `INSTALL_FAILED_INTERNAL_ERROR`, which UIAutomator2 surfaces as `Error: Cannot uninstall com.example.app`. The error message does not mention the foreground service, so the root cause is invisible in test logs. Tests that call `removeApp` in an `after()` cleanup hook experience order-dependent failures depending on whether the previous test triggered the service — the first test in the suite passes cleanup, subsequent tests fail, and the pattern looks like an intermittent infrastructure issue rather than a deterministic foreground-service conflict.
Fix: Before every `removeApp` call, force-stop the app via `browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'am', args: ['force-stop', packageName] })`, which terminates all processes including foreground services unconditionally; follow with a 1-second `pause` to allow the OS to complete process teardown, then call `removeApp`; encapsulate all three steps in a `safeRemoveApp(pkg)` helper and use it exclusively in cleanup hooks — never call bare `removeApp` in test code.

**Pattern 749** — `browser.deepLink(link, appIdentifier, waitForLaunch)` — deep-link cold-start and warm-start routing with intent-filter verification
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const APP_PKG   = driver.isIOS ? 'org.example.myapp' : 'com.example.myapp';
const APP_BUNDLE = 'org.example.myapp';

async function openDeepLink(url: string): Promise<void> {
  // waitForLaunch (Android-only) blocks until a foreground activity appears
  await browser.deepLink(url, driver.isIOS ? APP_BUNDLE : APP_PKG, true);
}

async function assertCurrentApp(expectedPkg: string): Promise<void> {
  if (driver.isAndroid) {
    const activity = await browser.execute('mobile: currentActivity') as string;
    if (!activity.startsWith(expectedPkg)) {
      throw new Error(
        `deepLink did not land in ${expectedPkg} — landed in ${activity}. ` +
        'Check intent-filter registration in AndroidManifest.xml.'
      );
    }
  }
}

describe('deep-link routing', () => {
  it('cold-start deep link opens the product detail screen', async () => {
    await browser.terminateApp(driver.isIOS ? undefined : APP_PKG,
                                driver.isIOS ? APP_BUNDLE : undefined);
    await openDeepLink('myapp://products/42');
    await assertCurrentApp(APP_PKG);
    const heading = await $('~product_detail_heading');
    await heading.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });
    expect(await heading.getText()).toContain('Product 42');
  });

  it('warm-start deep link navigates without showing the splash screen', async () => {
    await openDeepLink('myapp://settings/notifications');
    await assertCurrentApp(APP_PKG);
    const title = await $('~notifications_settings_title');
    await title.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4_000 });
    expect(await $('~splash_screen').isExisting()).toBe(false);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.deepLink` on iOS passes the URL to `XCUIApplication.open()` which ignores the `waitForLaunch` boolean entirely — the parameter is silently dropped by the XCUITest driver, so on iOS you must follow every `deepLink` call with an explicit `waitForDisplayed` on the first expected in-app element rather than relying on the flag; on Android `waitForLaunch: true` polls `getCurrentActivity()` in a tight loop and will throw `Error: Activity did not start` if the intent is unhandled within the driver's 20-second window, but if the app's manifest registers the scheme only in a non-default build variant (e.g., `staging` flavour) the intent silently falls through to the launcher and no error is thrown — always call `assertCurrentApp` immediately after `deepLink` to convert silent misfires into actionable failures.

**Pattern 750** — `$(element).scrollIntoView({ direction, maxScrolls, duration, scrollableElement })` — native-list element discovery without coordinate arithmetic
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface NativeScrollOpts {
  direction?: 'down' | 'up' | 'left' | 'right';
  maxScrolls?: number;
  duration?: number;
  percent?: number;
  scrollableElement?: WebdriverIO.Element;
}

async function nativeScrollTo(
  selector: string,
  opts: NativeScrollOpts = {}
): Promise<WebdriverIO.Element> {
  const el = await $(selector);
  await el.scrollIntoView({
    direction:         opts.direction         ?? 'down',
    maxScrolls:        opts.maxScrolls        ?? 20,
    duration:          opts.duration          ?? 800,
    percent:           opts.percent           ?? 0.85,
    ...(opts.scrollableElement ? { scrollableElement: opts.scrollableElement } : {}),
  });
  const found = await el.isDisplayed();
  if (!found) {
    throw new Error(
      `scrollIntoView exhausted ${opts.maxScrolls ?? 20} scrolls ` +
      `without finding "${selector}" — increase maxScrolls or add content-desc to the element.`
    );
  }
  return el;
}

describe('transaction history infinite scroll', () => {
  it('scrolls to entry #50 and asserts its amount label', async () => {
    const list = await $('~transaction_list');
    await list.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });

    const item = await nativeScrollTo('~transaction_item_50', {
      scrollableElement: list,
      direction: 'down',
      maxScrolls: 25,
    });
    expect(await item.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    await item.click();
    expect(await $('~transaction_detail_amount').isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `scrollIntoView` on Android delegates to `UiScrollable.scrollIntoView()` which matches by `content-desc` or `resource-id` — plain `TextView` elements with only `text` set are not found by this mechanism and the scroll silently exhausts its budget without throwing; the subsequent `isDisplayed()` check in the helper then surfaces the failure as "element not displayed" rather than "element not found by scroll", misleading diagnosis; always ensure scrollable-list items carry `android:contentDescription` or a unique `android:id`, and reduce the default `percent: 0.85` to `0.60` for variable-height chat-style lists because a long message item scrolled at 85% of the container height can overshoot the target.

**Pattern 751** — `browser.swipe({ direction, duration, percent, scrollableElement })` — horizontal carousel and tab-strip swipe with snap-animation settlement
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function swipeCarousel(
  carouselSelector: string,
  direction: 'left' | 'right',
  times = 1
): Promise<void> {
  const carousel = await $(carouselSelector);
  await carousel.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

  for (let i = 0; i < times; i++) {
    await browser.swipe({
      direction,
      duration:          700,  // stay under fling threshold on Android
      percent:           0.75,
      scrollableElement: carousel,
    });
    // Allow the snap animation to settle before the next assertion
    await browser.pause(350);
  }
}

describe('product image carousel', () => {
  const titles = ['Hero Image', 'Detail View', 'Lifestyle Shot', 'Packaging', 'Size Guide'];

  it('swiping left through all 5 slides shows each title in order', async () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < titles.length - 1; i++) {
      const current = await $(`~carousel_title_${i + 1}`);
      expect(await current.getText()).toBe(titles[i]);
      await swipeCarousel('~product_carousel', 'left');
    }
    const last = await $(`~carousel_title_5`);
    await last.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
    expect(await last.getText()).toBe(titles[4]);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.swipe` with `scrollableElement` on iOS executes `XCUIElement.swipeLeft()` internally, ignoring the `duration` and `percent` parameters entirely — it always performs a fixed-speed full-width swipe regardless of what you pass; on Android `duration` is forwarded as the `MotionEvent` timestamp delta, so `duration: 200` is treated as a fling by `ViewPager2` and can skip multiple pages in one gesture, while `duration: 700` stays safely below the fling-velocity threshold; always add a `pause(300–400)` after each swipe to let the snap animation settle because `waitForDisplayed` can match the incoming slide's title element before the scroll-position transition completes.

**Pattern 752** — `$(element).longPress({ duration })` — context-menu and action-sheet activation with platform-aware hold duration
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

// UIAutomator2 clamps long-press duration to a minimum of 500ms;
// XCUITest honours durations down to 50ms.
const LONG_PRESS_MS = driver.isAndroid ? 650 : 350;

describe('message bubble long-press reaction picker', () => {
  it('long-pressing a message bubble opens the emoji reaction sheet', async () => {
    const bubble = await $('~message_bubble_0');
    await bubble.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    await bubble.longPress({ duration: LONG_PRESS_MS });

    const picker = await $('~reaction_picker_sheet');
    await picker.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4_000 });
    expect(await picker.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);

    await $('~reaction_thumbs_up').click();

    const badge = await $('~reaction_badge_0');
    await badge.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
    expect(await badge.getText()).toBe('👍 1');
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    const sheet = await $('~reaction_picker_sheet');
    if (await sheet.isExisting() && await sheet.isDisplayed()) {
      if (driver.isAndroid) {
        await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'back' });
      } else {
        await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'home' });
      }
    }
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `longPress({ duration })` on Android maps to a W3C `PointerDown` + `pause(duration)` + `PointerUp` action sequence via UIAutomator2 — durations below 500ms are silently clamped to 500ms by UIAutomator2's gesture engine, so context menus requiring a 300ms hold (common in iOS-ported apps) will never fire on Android below the 500ms threshold even though the call returns without error; on iOS XCUITest honours the `duration` down to 50ms via `pressForDuration`, so the same `{ duration: 300 }` call fires on iOS but is silently extended to 500ms on Android — always use a platform-conditional value and document the divergence with an inline comment to prevent future developers from "fixing" a correct implementation.

**Pattern 753** — `$(mapElement).pinch({ scale, duration })` — map zoom-out regression guard with cluster-count assertion
```typescript
import { browser, $, $$ } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('map pinch-to-zoom cluster regression', () => {
  it('pinch to country-level scale groups individual pins into clusters', async () => {
    const mapFrame = await $('~map_frame');
    await mapFrame.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });

    // scale: 0.3 → spread the two touch points to 30% of the element width apart
    // On Android this maps to a multi-touch MotionEvent; on iOS to XCUIElement.pinch(withScale:)
    await mapFrame.pinch({ scale: 0.3, duration: 1_500 });
    await browser.pause(1_200); // allow tile-fetch + cluster recomputation

    const clusters = await $$('~map_cluster_marker');
    const pins     = await $$('~map_pin');

    // At country level, individual markers must be grouped; at most 4 singleton pins
    expect(clusters.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(pins.length).toBeLessThan(5);

    // Verify the cluster badge shows aggregated count
    const firstBadge = await clusters[0].$('~cluster_count_badge');
    const count = parseInt(await firstBadge.getText(), 10);
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(1);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `pinch({ scale })` on Android uses UIAutomator2's two-pointer `PointerDown` + scaled `PointerMove` + `PointerUp` sequence where `scale` controls the ratio of the final touch-point spread to the element bounding-box width — identical `scale` values produce different absolute pixel deltas on small phones (360 dp) versus large tablets (1280 dp), causing the resulting map zoom level to differ by device form factor; on iOS `XCUIElement.pinch(withScale:velocity:)` interprets `scale < 1.0` as zoom-out while Android interprets `scale: 0.3` (a small spread) as zoom-out, which is the opposite convention from `zoom()`; always assert the map's visible tile-label text or zoom-level indicator element rather than a fixed cluster count, because the cluster outcome is DPI-dependent and a `scale: 0.3` that reaches continent level on a phone may only reach country level on a 12-inch tablet.

**Pattern 754** — `$(element).zoom({ scale, duration })` — photo-viewer zoom-in with accessibility-label and control-toolbar assertion
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('photo viewer zoom gesture', () => {
  it('zooming in past 1.5× reveals the zoom-controls toolbar', async () => {
    const photo = await $('~photo_viewer_image');
    await photo.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });

    const labelBefore = await photo.getAttribute('value');
    expect(labelBefore).toContain('1x');

    // zoom({ scale: 0.8 }) = spread to 80% of element width = zoom in on Android;
    // XCUITest interprets this differently (scale > 1 = zoom in on iOS).
    // Use a known-safe value that expands the image on both platforms.
    await photo.zoom({ scale: 0.8, duration: 1_200 });
    await browser.pause(500); // settle animation

    const labelAfter = await photo.getAttribute('value');
    expect(parseFloat(labelAfter ?? '0')).toBeGreaterThan(1.0);

    const toolbar = await $('~zoom_controls_toolbar');
    await toolbar.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
    expect(await toolbar.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    const photo = await $('~photo_viewer_image');
    if (await photo.isExisting()) {
      await photo.doubleClick(); // double-tap resets to 1×
      await browser.pause(400);
    }
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `zoom({ scale })` uses `XCUIElement.pinch(withScale:velocity:)` on iOS where `scale > 1.0` = zoom in and `scale < 1.0` = zoom out — the inverse of WebdriverIO's Android convention where `scale: 0.8` (a larger spread than 0.3 but less than full) means zoom in; this cross-platform inversion is undocumented in the WDIO API reference and causes zoom-in tests to silently zoom out on Android when `scale > 1.0` is used; always verify the outcome via the element's `value` accessibility attribute or a visible zoom-indicator label immediately after the gesture, and add a comment in the test code explicitly noting the `scale` direction inversion so contributors do not "fix" a working implementation.

**Pattern 755** — `$(source).dragAndDrop(target, { duration })` — kanban card reorder with column-membership assertion
```typescript
import { browser, $, $$ } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('kanban drag-and-drop', () => {
  it('dragging a card from "To Do" to "In Progress" updates its column', async () => {
    const card            = await $('~kanban_card_task_5');
    const inProgressCol   = await $('~kanban_column_in_progress');

    await card.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await inProgressCol.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    // duration >= 1000ms keeps motion below Android autoscroll velocity threshold
    await card.dragAndDrop(inProgressCol, { duration: 1_200 });
    await browser.pause(700); // wait for drop animation + list re-layout

    // Verify card is now in the In Progress column
    const ipCards = await inProgressCol.$$('~kanban_card');
    const ipIds   = await Promise.all(ipCards.map(c => c.getAttribute('content-desc')));
    expect(ipIds).toContain('kanban_card_task_5');

    // Verify card is no longer in the To Do column
    const todoCol   = await $('~kanban_column_todo');
    const todoCards = await todoCol.$$('~kanban_card');
    const todoIds   = await Promise.all(todoCards.map(c => c.getAttribute('content-desc')));
    expect(todoIds).not.toContain('kanban_card_task_5');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `dragAndDrop(target, { duration })` resolves the drop target to a single coordinate at the centre of the target element's bounding box at gesture-start time — if the target column is a vertically scrollable container, the centre coordinate is the midpoint of whatever is currently visible, and if the column autoscrolls during the drag (triggered when the pointer enters the autoscroll hot zone near the container edge), the card may be dropped on top of an existing card rather than appended at the bottom; scroll the target column to a stable position before initiating the drag, and use `duration >= 1000` ms because UIAutomator2 begins autoscrolling the nearest scrollable ancestor when pointer velocity exceeds approximately 2000 px/s — a `duration: 400` drag consistently triggers autoscroll on RecyclerViews while `duration: 1200` stays safely below it.

**Pattern 756** — `browser.activateApp()` + `browser.terminateApp()` — share-sheet handoff with return-state preservation
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

const PKG    = 'com.example.myapp';
const BUNDLE = 'com.example.myapp';

describe('share-sheet handoff with return-state preservation', () => {
  it('returning from the native share sheet restores the article scroll position', async () => {
    await browser.deepLink('myapp://articles/7', driver.isIOS ? BUNDLE : PKG);
    const para = await $('~article_paragraph_4');
    await para.scrollIntoView({ direction: 'down', maxScrolls: 12 });

    await $('~share_button').click();
    const sheet = await $('~share_sheet_container');
    await sheet.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    // Dismiss the native share sheet
    if (driver.isAndroid) {
      await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'back' });
    } else {
      await $('~share_sheet_cancel_button').click();
    }

    // Re-activate the app and assert scroll position was preserved
    if (driver.isAndroid) {
      await browser.activateApp(PKG);
    } else {
      await browser.activateApp(undefined, BUNDLE);
    }

    await para.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await para.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    expect(await $('~splash_screen').isExisting()).toBe(false);
  });

  after(async () => {
    await (driver.isAndroid
      ? browser.terminateApp(PKG)
      : browser.terminateApp(undefined, BUNDLE)
    ).catch(() => {});
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `activateApp` on Android dispatches an `am start` intent with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_REORDER_TO_FRONT` — apps with `android:launchMode="singleTop"` will create a new Activity instance if the back-stack top is not the target Activity, silently destroying the preserved scroll state you were testing; always verify `browser.execute('mobile: currentActivity')` returns the expected Activity class immediately after `activateApp`, and instrument the app's `onResume()` / `onNewIntent()` to emit a logcat marker (`D/TEST: resumed`) that you can assert via `getLogs('logcat')` to distinguish a true resume from a silent re-launch.

**Pattern 757** — `browser.execute('mobile: touchId', { match })` + `browser.execute('mobile: toggleEnrollTouchId', { enabled })` — iOS Simulator biometric authentication gate
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function getSimulatorFlag(): Promise<boolean> {
  const caps = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as Record<string, string>;
  const name  = (caps['deviceName']  ?? '').toLowerCase();
  const model = (caps['appium:deviceModel'] ?? '').toLowerCase();
  return name.includes('simulator') || model.includes('simulator');
}

describe('biometric authentication', () => {
  let onSimulator = false;

  before(async function () {
    onSimulator = await getSimulatorFlag();
    if (!onSimulator) return this.skip();
    await browser.execute('mobile: toggleEnrollTouchId', { enabled: true });
  });

  it('successful Touch ID match navigates to the dashboard', async () => {
    await $('~biometrics_login_button').click();
    await $('~biometric_prompt').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    await browser.execute('mobile: touchId', { match: true });

    const dashboard = await $('~dashboard_screen');
    await dashboard.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });
    expect(await dashboard.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('failed Touch ID match surfaces the fallback password entry', async () => {
    await $('~biometrics_login_button').click();
    await $('~biometric_prompt').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

    await browser.execute('mobile: touchId', { match: false });

    const pwField = await $('~fallback_password_field');
    await pwField.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4_000 });
    expect(await pwField.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  after(async () => {
    await browser.execute('mobile: toggleEnrollTouchId', { enabled: false }).catch(() => {});
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: touchId` requires the Appium server process to have macOS Accessibility permission in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility — if the permission is absent, the command returns `200 OK` without throwing and the biometric prompt waits indefinitely, timing out with a misleading `element not displayed` error on the dashboard element rather than a biometric API error; additionally `toggleEnrollTouchId` must be called before the UI action that triggers the biometric prompt because XCUITest reads the enrollment state once at prompt display time — calling it after the prompt appears has no effect; the `after` cleanup unenrolment must also complete before any subsequent test that asserts biometric prompts are not shown, otherwise the enrolled state bleeds into the next suite.

**Pattern 758** — `browser.execute('mobile: shake')` — shake-triggered undo and debug-menu activation with platform-aware fallback
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

describe('shake-to-undo text input (iOS)', () => {
  it('shaking after typing surfaces the Undo Typing alert', async function () {
    if (!driver.isIOS) return this.skip(); // shake works on iOS only in Appium
    const field = await $('~notes_input_field');
    await field.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await field.setValue('Disposable draft content');

    await browser.execute('mobile: shake');

    const undoAlert = await $('~Undo Typing');
    await undoAlert.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
    await undoAlert.click();

    await browser.pause(300);
    expect(await field.getValue()).toBe('');
  });
});

describe('debug menu — Android (KEYCODE_MENU fallback)', () => {
  it('sends KEYCODE_MENU to open the React Native developer menu', async function () {
    if (!driver.isAndroid) return this.skip();
    // On Android, shake is emulator-only and silently no-ops on real devices.
    // Use KEYCODE_MENU as the universal debug-menu trigger instead.
    await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'input',
      args: ['keyevent', 'KEYCODE_MENU'],
    });
    const devMenu = await $('~dev_menu_root');
    await devMenu.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await devMenu.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    // Dismiss menu before next test
    await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'back' });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: shake` maps to `XCUIDevice.shared.performAction(.shake)` on iOS — it works on iOS Simulator and real iOS devices when the Appium server process has macOS Accessibility entitlement; on Android `appiumShake()` injects an X-axis `SensorManager` event via the emulator sensor bridge, which only works inside Android Emulator and has no effect on physical Android devices (the call returns `200 OK` silently), meaning shake-triggered features like React Native's developer menu or undo prompts can never be exercised on physical Android devices via Appium's shake API; always substitute `KEYCODE_MENU` via `mobile: shell input keyevent` for Android developer-menu activation and document the limitation with an inline comment.

**Pattern 759** — `browser.execute('mobile: toggleWiFi')` + `browser.execute('mobile: toggleData')` — offline error-state and reconnect-banner validation on Android emulator
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function setWiFiEnabled(enabled: boolean): Promise<void> {
  // Read current state before toggling to avoid accidentally enabling WiFi
  const result = await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'dumpsys',
    args: ['wifi'],
  }) as string;
  const currently = result.includes('Wi-Fi is enabled');
  if (currently !== enabled) {
    await browser.execute('mobile: toggleWiFi');
    await browser.pause(2_000); // WiFi state machine is asynchronous
  }
}

describe('offline error handling', () => {
  before(async function () {
    if (!driver.isAndroid) this.skip(); // toggleWiFi is Android-UIAutomator2-only
  });

  it('turning off WiFi and data shows the offline retry banner', async () => {
    await $('~home_feed').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    await setWiFiEnabled(false);
    await browser.execute('mobile: toggleData');
    await browser.pause(2_000);

    const banner = await $('~offline_retry_banner');
    await banner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    expect(await banner.getText()).toContain('No internet connection');
  });

  it('re-enabling WiFi auto-dismisses the banner and refreshes the feed', async () => {
    await setWiFiEnabled(true);
    await browser.waitUntil(
      async () => !(await $('~offline_retry_banner').isDisplayed()),
      { timeout: 12_000, timeoutMsg: 'Offline banner did not dismiss after reconnect' }
    );
    expect(await $('~home_feed_item_0').isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  after(async () => {
    await setWiFiEnabled(true).catch(() => {});
    // Restore data — toggle again only if it was disabled
    await browser.execute('mobile: toggleData').catch(() => {});
    await browser.pause(1_500);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: toggleWiFi` and `mobile: toggleData` are parameterless state-flippers — calling them when the emulator is already in the desired state inadvertently reverses connectivity, which is why this pattern reads `dumpsys wifi` before every toggle; both commands are Android-only UIAutomator2 features and silently no-op on iOS (Apple intentionally blocks programmatic WiFi/data toggling from test code), so iOS offline testing must be routed through a network-condition proxy (Charles, mitmproxy) or iOS Simulator's built-in network link conditioner rather than through Appium; the `dumpsys wifi` shell check also fails on Android >= 12 in some security configurations where shell output is restricted — fall back to `netstat -rn` to detect connectivity when `dumpsys wifi` returns empty output.

---

**Pattern 760** — `browser.execute('mobile: startActivity', { appPackage, appActivity, appWaitActivity })` — direct Android Activity launch for screen-specific test isolation
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

interface ActivityOpts {
  appPackage: string;
  appActivity: string;
  appWaitActivity?: string;
  appWaitDuration?: number;
  intentFlags?: string;
}

async function launchActivity(opts: ActivityOpts): Promise<void> {
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'am',
    args: ['force-stop', opts.appPackage],
  });
  await browser.pause(600);
  await browser.execute('mobile: startActivity', {
    appPackage:       opts.appPackage,
    appActivity:      opts.appActivity,
    appWaitActivity:  opts.appWaitActivity ?? opts.appActivity,
    appWaitDuration:  opts.appWaitDuration ?? 12_000,
    intentFlags:      opts.intentFlags     ?? '0x10200000',
  });
}

describe('payment screen — direct activity launch', () => {
  const PKG = 'com.example.myapp';

  beforeEach(async function () {
    if (!driver.isAndroid) return this.skip();
    await launchActivity({
      appPackage:  PKG,
      appActivity: '.ui.payment.PaymentActivity',
    });
  });

  it('payment screen renders the card field without navigating through checkout flow', async () => {
    const cardField = await $('~payment_card_number_input');
    await cardField.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    expect(await cardField.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    // Verify we did NOT land on the login screen (regression guard for auth interceptors)
    expect(await $('~login_email_field').isExisting()).toBe(false);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: startActivity` bypasses the application's normal navigation stack — if the target `Activity` has `android:exported="false"` in the manifest, the `am start` command throws `SecurityException: Permission Denial` which UIAutomator2 surfaces as a generic `Error: Cannot launch activity` with no mention of the export restriction; always set `android:exported="true"` on Activities that need direct test launches (adding a test-flavour `<intent-filter>` with a custom action is the recommended approach), and inject any required auth tokens into SharedPreferences via `mobile: shell` before calling `startActivity` rather than attempting to bypass authentication guards, because Activities protected by a custom `authenticatedCheck()` in `onResume()` will immediately redirect to the login screen when launched without a valid session.

---

**Pattern 761** — `browser.updateSettings(overrides)` + `browser.getSettings()` — per-test implicit-wait and snapshot-depth tuning with guaranteed restoration
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

type DriverSettings = Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>;

async function withSettings(
  overrides: DriverSettings,
  fn: () => Promise<void>
): Promise<void> {
  const original = await browser.getSettings() as DriverSettings;
  await browser.updateSettings(overrides);
  try {
    await fn();
  } finally {
    // Always restore — even if the test throws — to prevent bleed-through
    await browser.updateSettings(original).catch(() => {});
  }
}

describe('heavy 1000-item list — relaxed timeout CI variant', () => {
  it('loads the full list within extended timeout on a slow emulator', async () => {
    await withSettings({
      waitForIdleTimeout:         8_000,
      waitForSelectorTimeout:     20_000,
      actionAcknowledgmentTimeout: 40_000,
      snapshotMaxDepth:           30, // reduce from 70 to speed up element lookup
    }, async () => {
      await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
        command: 'am',
        args: ['start', '-n', 'com.example.myapp/.HeavyListActivity'],
      });
      const list = await $('~heavy_list_root');
      await list.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 15_000 });
      const items = await $$('~heavy_list_item');
      expect(items.length).toBeGreaterThan(50);
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `updateSettings` mutates the Appium server-side session state for every subsequent command — unlike WDIO's `browser.setTimeout`, it affects server-level values like `snapshotMaxDepth` and `waitForIdleTimeout` that persist for the entire remaining session unless explicitly reverted; reducing `snapshotMaxDepth` below the actual depth of your app's view hierarchy causes `$('selector')` to silently return `null` for elements deeper than the cutoff without throwing any error, which causes test failures that appear unrelated to the settings change; always wrap settings changes in a `withSettings(overrides, fn)` higher-order function using a `finally` block to guarantee restoration even on test failure, because a test that calls `updateSettings` in `before` and fails before the `after` cleanup runs will leave every subsequent test in the session running under incorrect timeouts.

---

**Pattern 762** — `browser.execute('mobile: background', { seconds })` — foreground/background lifecycle and state-persistence testing with UIAutomator2 version guard
```typescript
import { browser, $ } from '@wdio/globals';

async function backgroundAppFor(seconds: number): Promise<void> {
  const caps = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as Record<string, string>;
  const driverVersion = caps['appium:driverVersion'] ?? '0.0.0';
  const [major, minor] = driverVersion.split('.').map(Number);

  if (driver.isAndroid && (major > 2 || (major === 2 && minor >= 30))) {
    // UIAutomator2 >= 2.30 removed timed background support; use explicit lifecycle instead
    await browser.terminateApp('com.example.myapp');
    await browser.pause(seconds * 1_000);
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.myapp');
  } else {
    await browser.execute('mobile: background', { seconds });
  }
}

describe('background/foreground state preservation', () => {
  it('form draft persists after the app is backgrounded for 5 seconds', async () => {
    const field = await $('~profile_name_input');
    await field.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await field.setValue('Preserved Name');
    await browser.pause(350); // allow autosave debounce to fire

    await backgroundAppFor(5);

    const restored = await $('~profile_name_input');
    await restored.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    expect(await restored.getValue()).toBe('Preserved Name');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `mobile: background` with `seconds: N > 0` on UIAutomator2 >= 2.30 returns immediately after backgrounding the app, ignoring the `seconds` value entirely due to a breaking change that removed indefinite and timed background-hold support — tests that relied on a 5-second background period to simulate auth-token expiry, push-notification delivery, or session-timeout logic now run with zero background time, silently producing false passes; always check the UIAutomator2 driver version via `getAppiumSessionCapabilities()['appium:driverVersion']` and apply the `terminateApp` + `pause` + `activateApp` workaround when the version is >= `2.30.0`, and pin your `appium-uiautomator2-driver` version in `package.json` resolutions to `< 2.30` on CI to stabilise existing test suites until they can be migrated to the explicit lifecycle pattern.

---

**Pattern 763** — `browser.getSettings()` + `browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()` — runtime capability introspection for graceful test-skip guards
```typescript
import { browser } from '@wdio/globals';

type DriverSettings = Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>;

async function isPhysicalDevice(): Promise<boolean> {
  // Device identity lives in caps, NOT in getSettings()
  const caps  = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as DriverSettings;
  const model = ((caps['deviceModel'] ?? caps['appium:deviceModel'] ?? '') as string).toLowerCase();
  const name  = ((caps['deviceName']  ?? caps['appium:deviceName']  ?? '') as string).toLowerCase();
  return !model.includes('emulator') && !model.includes('sdk_gphone') &&
         !name.includes('simulator') && !name.includes('emulator');
}

async function isBiometricEnrolled(): Promise<boolean> {
  // Enrollment flag lives in getSettings(), NOT in caps
  const settings = await browser.getSettings() as DriverSettings;
  return (settings['touchIdEnrollment'] as boolean | null) ?? false;
}

describe('capability-gated feature tests', () => {
  it('skips biometric tests when Touch ID is not enrolled', async function () {
    if (driver.isAndroid) return this.skip();
    if (!await isBiometricEnrolled()) return this.skip();
    await browser.execute('mobile: touchId', { match: true });
    expect(await $('~dashboard_screen').isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('skips WiFi-toggle tests on physical devices where they silently no-op', async function () {
    if (!driver.isAndroid) return this.skip();
    if (await isPhysicalDevice()) return this.skip();
    await browser.execute('mobile: toggleWiFi');
    await browser.pause(2_000);
    expect(await $('~offline_retry_banner').isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    await browser.execute('mobile: toggleWiFi'); // restore
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.getSettings()` returns the UIAutomator2 or XCUITest driver's session-level settings object (keys like `touchIdEnrollment`, `snapshotMaxDepth`, `waitForIdleTimeout`) while device-identity information (`deviceModel`, `deviceName`, `driverVersion`) lives in `getAppiumSessionCapabilities()` under Appium-prefixed keys (`appium:deviceModel`) — the two APIs are non-interchangeable and calling `getSettings()` to look up `deviceModel` always returns `undefined`, causing the physical-device guard to silently fail and run network-toggle tests on real devices; never mix the two APIs in a single guard expression without knowing which namespace each key belongs to, and always try both the prefixed (`appium:key`) and unprefixed (`key`) forms of capabilities because some Appium drivers omit the prefix while others require it.

### Community Gotchas

**C69-1** — `browser.deepLink()` on Android silently routes to the system browser when no app has registered the URL scheme — `waitForLaunch: true` returns success because a foreground activity (Chrome) appeared, not the target app
Why this matters: `browser.deepLink(url, appPkg, true)` on Android sends an `am start` intent for the given URL and polls until any foreground Activity appears — if the app's `AndroidManifest.xml` does not declare an `<intent-filter>` matching the scheme, the Android intent router falls through to the system browser or the "Open with" disambiguation dialog, both of which satisfy the `waitForLaunch: true` poll because a foreground Activity (Chrome, or `IntentResolverActivity`) appeared. UIAutomator2 returns `200 OK` and the test continues; the first assertion on an in-app element then fails with `element not found`, which appears to be a selector or navigation bug rather than a missing intent-filter registration. The failure is configuration-dependent: dev builds that register every scheme pass while release builds that strip unused schemes fail, creating a false sense of confidence in the deep-link routing.
Fix: Always assert the current app package immediately after `deepLink` returns using `await browser.execute('mobile: currentActivity')` and compare the package prefix to the expected value before querying any in-app element; wrap this check in a `assertDeepLinkLandedIn(expectedPkg)` helper that throws `'deepLink routed to ${actual} instead of ${expectedPkg} — check <intent-filter> in AndroidManifest.xml'`; add the helper as the first line of every deep-link test so silent browser-fallback misfires surface as immediately actionable failures rather than cryptic element-not-found errors.

---

**C69-2** — `$(element).scrollIntoView()` on iOS silently stops after `maxScrolls` iterations without throwing — the subsequent `waitForDisplayed` produces a misleading "element not visible" error that obscures the real cause
Why this matters: WebdriverIO's `scrollIntoView` on iOS executes repeated `XCUIElement.swipeUp()` calls up to `maxScrolls` times and then returns without throwing an error if the element was not found within the scroll budget. The subsequent `waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 })` call starts its own 3-second timer from zero and then expires with `Error: element not visible after 3000ms` — which points at a visibility or rendering problem rather than an exhausted scroll budget. On chat-style lists with variable-height messages, 10 scroll attempts may reach the target on a short message run but not on a long message run, producing intermittent failures whose error messages give no indication of the scroll budget constraint. The problem is compounded by the fact that `scrollIntoView` returns a resolved promise (not rejected), so `catch` handlers and `try/finally` blocks never fire.
Fix: After every `scrollIntoView` call, immediately assert `await el.isDisplayed()` (synchronously, not via `waitForDisplayed`) and throw a descriptive error if it returns `false` — `'scrollIntoView exhausted ${maxScrolls} scrolls without finding "${selector}" — increase maxScrolls, add content-desc to the element, or reduce list item height'`; for variable-height lists, set `maxScrolls: 30` and `percent: 0.60` (shorter swipes per step) to avoid overshooting the target on runs with unusually long items.

---

**C69-3** — `$(element).longPress({ duration: 300 })` on Android UIAutomator2 is silently clamped to 500ms — short-duration context menus from iOS-ported apps never trigger on Android even though the call returns without error
Why this matters: UIAutomator2 enforces a minimum long-press duration of 500ms at the driver layer before forwarding the `MotionEvent` to the Android view hierarchy — if `longPress({ duration: 300 })` is called, the driver silently upgrades the hold to 500ms and returns without logging the adjustment. Context menus in iOS-ported apps that display at the iOS-native 300ms threshold fire correctly on iOS (where XCUITest honours durations down to 50ms via `pressForDuration`) but never fire on Android under 500ms, producing a test failure that looks like a selector problem because the context-menu element never appears. The 500ms minimum is mentioned only in the UIAutomator2 driver changelog for version 2.9.0 and is absent from the WebdriverIO `longPress` API reference.
Fix: Use a platform-conditional duration `{ duration: driver.isAndroid ? 650 : 300 }` — 650ms is safely above the 500ms Android clamp and well below the typical 1500ms tap-cancel threshold; document the platform divergence with an inline comment so future contributors do not reduce the Android duration in a "performance optimisation"; add a `before` hook that logs the UIAutomator2 driver version from `getAppiumSessionCapabilities()` so CI logs surface the version context when investigating long-press failures.

---

**C69-4** — `mobile: toggleWiFi` returns immediately on Android while the OS WiFi state change completes asynchronously — asserting the offline UI within 500ms produces intermittent false failures
Why this matters: `mobile: toggleWiFi` dispatches an `am broadcast` to the Android WiFi state machine and returns as soon as the broadcast is sent — the actual WiFi disconnect, IP address release, DNS cache invalidation, and app-layer socket teardown complete 1–3 seconds later on emulators and 2–5 seconds later on physical devices. Tests that assert the offline retry banner within 500ms after `toggleWiFi` fail intermittently because the app's `ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback.onLost()` has not fired yet. The failure rate increases on CI emulators running on CPU-constrained hosts because the WiFi state machine is slower when the host is under load. Adding a fixed `browser.pause(500)` does not reliably fix the issue because emulator WiFi teardown time is non-deterministic.
Fix: After every `mobile: toggleWiFi` call, poll `browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'dumpsys', args: ['wifi'] })` for the string `'Wi-Fi is disabled'` (or `'enabled'`) in a `waitUntil` loop with a 6-second budget before proceeding to app-layer assertions; alternatively, use `browser.waitUntil(() => $('~offline_banner').isDisplayed(), { timeout: 12_000 })` which tolerates the async state transition; never use a fixed `pause` value because the emulator WiFi teardown time varies from 200ms to 4000ms depending on host CPU load.

---

**C69-5** — `browser.execute('mobile: background', { seconds })` with UIAutomator2 >= 2.30 returns immediately for all positive `seconds` values — time-dependent background behaviours are never exercised
Why this matters: UIAutomator2 2.30 (released October 2024) rewrote the `background` command to send the app to background and return immediately, ignoring the `seconds` parameter for both positive and `-1` values. The driver changelog describes this as "fix for indefinite blocking" but the change affects all timed background scenarios. Tests that relied on `background({ seconds: 5 })` to simulate auth-token expiry, push-notification delivery timing, or session-timeout logic now run with zero background time — the app is backgrounded and immediately re-foregrounded, meaning time-dependent background behaviours are never triggered. The call still returns `200 OK` with no error, making the regression invisible unless you specifically observe that background-dependent features never fire. The failure manifests as tests that always pass (because the timeout never triggers) rather than tests that fail.
Fix: Read the UIAutomator2 driver version via `(await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities() as Record<string, string>)['appium:driverVersion']` in a `before` hook, and if the semver is >= `2.30.0` replace every `mobile: background` call with an explicit `terminateApp(pkg)` + `browser.pause(seconds * 1000)` + `activateApp(pkg)` sequence; add a semver comparison utility to your test helpers so the workaround applies automatically based on the runtime version, and add a JIRA/GitHub issue reference comment so CI maintainers know when to remove the workaround once UIAutomator2 restores timed background support.

## Cycle 68 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 764** — `browser.getClipboard()` / `browser.setClipboard()` — clipboard copy-paste round-trip validation
```typescript
// Verify that tapping "Share Link" copies the correct URL,
// and that pre-seeding the clipboard enables the paste-import flow without user interaction.

const EXPECTED_SHARE_URL = 'https://example.com/product/42';

describe('clipboard copy-paste round trip', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    // Pre-clear clipboard to a deterministic empty state
    await browser.setClipboard(Buffer.from('').toString('base64'), 'plaintext');
  });

  it('tapping "Share Link" copies the product URL to the clipboard', async () => {
    await $('~product_card_42').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });
    await $('~share_link_button').click();
    await browser.pause(800); // allow native clipboard write to complete

    const raw     = await browser.getClipboard('plaintext');
    const decoded = Buffer.from(raw, 'base64').toString('utf8');
    expect(decoded).toBe(EXPECTED_SHARE_URL);
  });

  it('pre-seeded clipboard value drives the paste-import flow without user interaction', async () => {
    const importUrl = 'https://example.com/import-42';
    await browser.setClipboard(Buffer.from(importUrl).toString('base64'), 'plaintext');

    await $('~import_from_clipboard_button').click();
    const preview = await $('~import_url_preview');
    await preview.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await preview.getText()).toBe(importUrl);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.setClipboard()` writes reliably on both platforms, but `browser.getClipboard()` is silently blocked on Android 10+ (API 29+) — `ClipboardManager.getPrimaryClip()` returns `null` when called from the UIAutomator2 server process (not the foreground app), and the driver encodes `null` as the empty-string base64 with HTTP 200 and no warning; to validate clipboard reads on Android 10+, trigger the app's own paste UI (long-press field → Paste → read `getValue()`) instead of calling `getClipboard()` directly, and limit `setClipboard()` to write/pre-seed scenarios only.

---

**Pattern 765** — `browser.gsmCall()` — incoming call interrupt, accept, and cancel lifecycle
```typescript
// Verify the app handles an incoming GSM call correctly on Android emulator.
// gsmCall() maps to the emulator telnet console 'gsm call|accept|cancel|hold' commands.

const CALLER = '+1-555-0199';

async function isAndroidEmulator(): Promise<boolean> {
  const caps  = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
  const model = ((caps['deviceModel'] as string) ?? '').toLowerCase();
  return model.includes('emulator') || model.includes('sdk_gphone');
}

describe('incoming call interrupt', () => {
  before(async function () {
    if (!driver.isAndroid || !(await isAndroidEmulator())) this.skip();
  });

  it('app pauses audio on CALL_STATE_RINGING and resumes after call ends', async () => {
    await $('~play_button').click();
    expect(await $('~audio_status').getText()).toBe('Playing');

    await browser.gsmCall(CALLER, 'call');
    await browser.pause(1_500); // allow PHONE_STATE broadcast to propagate
    expect(await $('~audio_status').getText()).toBe('Paused');

    await browser.gsmCall(CALLER, 'accept');
    await browser.pause(800);
    await browser.gsmCall(CALLER, 'cancel');
    await browser.pause(1_500);

    const resumeBtn = await $('~resume_button');
    await resumeBtn.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4_000 });
    await resumeBtn.click();
    expect(await $('~audio_status').getText()).toBe('Playing');
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    // Flush any dangling call state to prevent CALL_STATE_OFFHOOK bleeding into the next test
    await browser.gsmCall(CALLER, 'cancel').catch(() => {});
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.gsmCall()` triggers a real `TelephonyManager.CALL_STATE_RINGING` broadcast via the emulator telnet console — but the `com.android.phone` call-notification overlay intercepts all touch events while the incoming-call UI is on screen, so any `$(...).click()` fired while the notification is visible throws `ElementClickInterceptedException`; always issue `gsmCall(number, 'cancel')` in `afterEach` even when prior steps accepted the call, because a dropped test leaves the emulator in `CALL_STATE_OFFHOOK` and every subsequent touch interaction in the session fails with the intercept error until the session is restarted.

---

**Pattern 766** — `browser.sendSms()` + `browser.gsmSignal()` — OTP SMS delivery and weak-signal UI test
```typescript
// Inject an OTP SMS and verify the notification, then degrade signal
// and confirm the app's weak-signal banner responds correctly.
// Both commands are Android emulator only (telnet console).

async function requireEmulator(ctx: Mocha.Context): Promise<void> {
  const caps  = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
  const model = ((caps['deviceModel'] as string) ?? '').toLowerCase();
  if (!driver.isAndroid || (!model.includes('emulator') && !model.includes('sdk_gphone'))) {
    ctx.skip();
  }
}

describe('SMS delivery + signal simulation', () => {
  before(async function () { await requireEmulator(this); });

  it('injected SMS shows OTP code in the notification shade', async () => {
    await browser.sendSms('+1-555-9876', 'Your OTP is 482910');
    await browser.pause(2_000); // allow SMS_RECEIVED broadcast to deliver

    await browser.appiumOpenNotifications();
    const notif = await $(`android=new UiSelector().textContains("482910")`);
    await notif.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await notif.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
    await browser.pressKeyCode(4); // KEYCODE_BACK — collapse notification shade
  });

  it('weak-signal banner shows at gsmSignal(0) and hides at gsmSignal(4)', async () => {
    await browser.gsmSignal(0); // no signal
    await browser.pause(1_000);
    const banner = await $('~weak_signal_banner');
    await banner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await banner.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);

    await browser.gsmSignal(4); // great signal
    await banner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000, reverse: true });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.sendSms()` delivers via the Android emulator telnet `sms send` command, firing a real `android.provider.Telephony.SMS_RECEIVED` broadcast that apps using a `BroadcastReceiver` receive correctly — but apps that use the Google Play Services `SmsRetriever` API depend on a GCM-backed delivery channel that the emulator console cannot simulate, so OTP auto-fill tests relying on `SmsRetriever.CONSENT_ACTION` will never be triggered by `sendSms()` on stock AOSP emulators and must use a physical device with a real SMS gateway or an instrumented mock.

**Pattern 767** — `browser.powerCapacity()` / `browser.powerAC()` — battery level and charging-state UI
```typescript
// Verify low-battery warning and charging indicator on Android emulator.
// powerCapacity and powerAC target the emulator's software battery profile.

async function requireAndroidEmulator(ctx: Mocha.Context): Promise<void> {
  const caps  = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
  const model = ((caps['deviceModel'] as string) ?? '').toLowerCase();
  if (!driver.isAndroid || (!model.includes('emulator') && !model.includes('sdk_gphone'))) {
    ctx.skip();
  }
}

describe('battery-aware UI', () => {
  before(async function () { await requireAndroidEmulator(this); });

  it('low-battery banner appears at 10% while discharging', async () => {
    await browser.powerCapacity(10);
    await browser.powerAC('off');
    await browser.pause(1_500); // wait for ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED broadcast

    const banner = await $('~low_battery_warning');
    await banner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await banner.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('charging icon shows and banner hides when AC is reconnected', async () => {
    await browser.powerAC('on');
    await browser.pause(1_500);

    await $('~low_battery_warning').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000, reverse: true });
    const chargingIcon = await $('~charging_indicator');
    await chargingIcon.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4_000 });
    expect(await chargingIcon.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  after(async () => {
    await browser.powerCapacity(100);
    await browser.powerAC('on');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.powerCapacity()` sets `BatteryManager.EXTRA_LEVEL` / `EXTRA_SCALE` and `browser.powerAC('off')` sets `BATTERY_STATUS_DISCHARGING` only when the Android Virtual Device uses a software battery profile (the default for AOSP AVDs) — on physical devices or AVDs created with a hardware battery profile, both commands silently return HTTP 200 but the `ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED` broadcast is never fired, making the app's `BroadcastReceiver` unreachable and the test a permanent false positive; always verify the emulator accepted the value with a pre-assertion `adb shell dumpsys battery | grep level` check in the `before` hook before trusting battery-state assertions in the test body.

**Pattern 768** — `browser.getDisplayDensity()` — DPI-aware minimum touch-target size assertion
```typescript
// Verify navigation bar buttons meet Android's 48dp minimum touch-target requirement.
// getDisplayDensity() is Android-only; iOS uses logical points natively.

const MINIMUM_DP = 48;

interface DpSize { width: number; height: number; }

async function getElementSizeInDp(selector: string): Promise<DpSize> {
  if (!driver.isAndroid) {
    const size = await (await $(selector)).getSize();
    return { width: size.width, height: size.height }; // iOS pts ≈ dp
  }
  const density  = await browser.getDisplayDensity(); // e.g. 420 DPI
  const dpFactor = density / 160;
  const el   = await $(selector);
  const size = await el.getSize();
  return {
    width:  Math.round(size.width  / dpFactor),
    height: Math.round(size.height / dpFactor),
  };
}

describe('touch-target accessibility — 48dp minimum', () => {
  const targets = [
    '~nav_home_button',
    '~nav_search_button',
    '~nav_profile_button',
    '~fab_create_action',
  ];

  for (const selector of targets) {
    it(`${selector} meets the 48dp accessibility minimum`, async () => {
      const dp = await getElementSizeInDp(selector);
      expect(dp.width).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(MINIMUM_DP);
      expect(dp.height).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(MINIMUM_DP);
    });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.getDisplayDensity()` returns the hardware DPI (e.g., 420 for `xxhdpi` Pixels), and dividing pixel sizes by `density / 160` converts to dp values — but on Samsung devices with user-adjusted Screen Zoom (Settings → Display → Screen Zoom), the rendered pixel count per dp changes while `getDisplayDensity()` still returns the hardware density, producing dp calculations that can be up to 30% too small; for authoritative cross-device dp validation, compare `getDisplayDensity()` against `adb shell wm density` in the `before` hook and log a warning if they diverge by more than 5%, then use the `wm density` value for the conversion factor rather than the hardware density from the capability.

**Pattern 769** — `browser.fingerPrint()` — Android emulator biometric auth success and lockout flow
```typescript
// fingerPrint(id) simulates a fingerprint sensor event on Android emulator.
// IDs 1-10 map to sensor slots configured in the AVD hardware profile.
// Success/failure depends on which IDs were enrolled at AVD creation time.

async function requireAndroidEmulator(ctx: Mocha.Context): Promise<void> {
  const caps  = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
  const model = ((caps['deviceModel'] as string) ?? '').toLowerCase();
  if (!driver.isAndroid || (!model.includes('emulator') && !model.includes('sdk_gphone'))) {
    ctx.skip();
  }
}

describe('fingerprint biometric authentication', () => {
  before(async function () { await requireAndroidEmulator(this); });

  it('enrolled fingerprint (sensor ID 1) grants access', async () => {
    await $('~biometric_prompt_title').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    await browser.fingerPrint(1);
    const home = await $('~authenticated_home');
    await home.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await home.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('three consecutive unregistered fingerprints (ID 9) trigger lockout', async () => {
    await $('~biometric_prompt_title').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
      await browser.fingerPrint(9); // unregistered sensor ID
      await browser.pause(500);
    }
    const lockout = await $('~biometric_lockout_message');
    await lockout.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await lockout.getText()).toContain('Too many attempts');
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await browser.activateApp(undefined, undefined);
    await browser.pause(400);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.fingerPrint(id)` is exclusively emulator-specific — on physical Android devices UIAutomator2 throws `UnsupportedOperationException` because real Secure Enclave hardware cannot be driven via ADB — and the authentication outcome depends on which sensor IDs were enrolled at AVD creation time (not the ID value itself), so a test relying on ID 1 succeeding must declare that dependency in the AVD configuration documentation and fail fast with a descriptive error when `getAppiumSessionCapabilities()['deviceModel']` indicates a real device, preventing silently skipped biometric coverage on physical CI farms.

**Pattern 770** — `browser.appiumTouchId()` / `browser.appiumToggleEnrollTouchId()` — iOS Simulator biometric gate
```typescript
// appiumTouchId(true)  → AUTH_SUCCESS (matching fingerprint/face)
// appiumTouchId(false) → AUTH_FAILED  (non-matching)
// appiumToggleEnrollTouchId(bool) → enroll or unenroll biometrics on the Simulator

describe('iOS Simulator biometric authentication', () => {
  before(async function () {
    if (!driver.isIOS) this.skip(); // iOS Simulator only — throws on real device
    await browser.appiumToggleEnrollTouchId(true);
    await browser.pause(400);
  });

  it('matching biometric grants access to the dashboard', async () => {
    await $('~sign_in_with_biometrics').click();
    await browser.pause(2_000); // wait for LAContext prompt to appear
    await browser.appiumTouchId(true);
    const dash = await $('~dashboard_root');
    await dash.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });
    expect(await dash.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('non-matching biometric shows "Authentication failed"', async () => {
    await $('~sign_in_with_biometrics').click();
    await browser.pause(2_000);
    await browser.appiumTouchId(false);
    const err = await $('~biometric_error_label');
    await err.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await err.getText()).toContain('Authentication failed');
  });

  it('unenrolling disables the biometric sign-in button', async () => {
    await browser.appiumToggleEnrollTouchId(false);
    await browser.pause(400);
    expect(await $('~sign_in_with_biometrics').getAttribute('enabled')).toBe('false');
    await browser.appiumToggleEnrollTouchId(true); // restore for subsequent tests
  });

  after(async () => { await browser.appiumToggleEnrollTouchId(false); });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.appiumTouchId(match)` fails on real iOS devices with `XCUITestError: Can't run 'fingerTouch' command on real device` because Secure Enclave biometric signals cannot be injected via XCUITest; `appiumToggleEnrollTouchId(true)` must be called before the biometric prompt appears — calling it while `LAContext.evaluatePolicy` is already in flight leaves the Simulator's `LocalAuthentication` framework permanently hung (the prompt stays on screen, `appiumTouchId` is accepted silently but the reply callback never fires, and the app UI freezes for the rest of the session requiring a full session restart).

**Pattern 771** — `browser.appiumQueryAppState()` + `browser.activateApp()` — multi-step lifecycle state assertion
```typescript
// Assert exact state transitions: activated → backgrounded → terminated → re-activated
// State codes: 0=not installed, 1=not running, 2=bg suspended, 3=bg active, 4=foreground

const APP_STATE = { NOT_INSTALLED: 0, NOT_RUNNING: 1, BG_SUSPENDED: 2, BG_ACTIVE: 3, FOREGROUND: 4 } as const;
const PKG    = driver.isAndroid ? 'com.example.app' : undefined;
const BUNDLE = driver.isIOS     ? 'com.example.app' : undefined;

async function queryState(): Promise<number> {
  return browser.appiumQueryAppState(PKG, BUNDLE) as Promise<number>;
}

describe('app lifecycle state machine', () => {
  it('state is FOREGROUND (4) after activateApp()', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp(PKG, BUNDLE);
    await browser.pause(1_000);
    expect(await queryState()).toBe(APP_STATE.FOREGROUND);
  });

  it('state is a background value (2 or 3) after pressing Home', async () => {
    if (driver.isAndroid) await browser.pressKeyCode(3); // KEYCODE_HOME
    else                  await browser.execute('mobile: pressButton', { name: 'home' });
    await browser.pause(1_500);
    const state = await queryState();
    expect([APP_STATE.BG_SUSPENDED, APP_STATE.BG_ACTIVE]).toContain(state);
  });

  it('state is NOT_RUNNING (1) after terminateApp()', async () => {
    await browser.terminateApp(PKG, BUNDLE);
    await browser.pause(1_000);
    expect(await queryState()).toBe(APP_STATE.NOT_RUNNING);
  });

  it('state is FOREGROUND (4) after re-activating from terminated state', async () => {
    await browser.activateApp(PKG, BUNDLE);
    await browser.pause(2_000);
    expect(await queryState()).toBe(APP_STATE.FOREGROUND);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.appiumQueryAppState()` returns state `2` (background-suspended) or `3` (background-active) depending on whether the app holds an active background task — iOS distinguishes these based on `URLSession`, `BGProcessingTask`, or background-fetch registration, while UIAutomator2 on Android conflates both into state `2`; tests that assert the exact background state will fail intermittently on iOS when background refresh is enabled (the app oscillates between 2 and 3), so always assert `state >= BG_SUSPENDED && state <= BG_ACTIVE` for background-state steps and reserve strict equality checks for `NOT_RUNNING` and `FOREGROUND` states only.

**Pattern 772** — `browser.execute('mobile: getContexts', { waitForWebviewMs })` — targeted webview context switching in hybrid apps
```typescript
// Use the enhanced mobile: getContexts command for per-page URL metadata
// to reliably switch into the correct webview in a multi-webview hybrid app

interface WebviewCtx {
  id: string;
  title?: string;
  url?: string;
}

async function switchToWebviewByUrl(fragment: string, timeoutMs = 15_000): Promise<void> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    const ctxs = await browser.execute('mobile: getContexts', {
      waitForWebviewMs: 3_000,
    }) as WebviewCtx[];

    const target = ctxs.find((c) => c.url?.includes(fragment) && c.id !== 'NATIVE_APP');
    if (target) {
      await browser.switchAppiumContext(target.id);
      return;
    }
    await browser.pause(1_000);
  }
  throw new Error(`Webview with URL fragment "${fragment}" not found after ${timeoutMs}ms`);
}

describe('hybrid app — payment webview', () => {
  it('fills the card form inside the payment webview and confirms in native layer', async () => {
    await $('~proceed_to_payment').click();
    await switchToWebviewByUrl('/payment/card-entry');

    const cardNum = await $('input[data-testid="card-number"]');
    await cardNum.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    await cardNum.setValue('4111 1111 1111 1111');
    await $('input[data-testid="card-expiry"]').setValue('12/28');
    await $('input[data-testid="card-cvv"]').setValue('123');
    await $('button[type="submit"]').click();

    await browser.switchAppiumContext('NATIVE_APP');
    await $('~payment_confirmation').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000 });
    expect(await $('~payment_confirmation').isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `mobile: getContexts` command with per-page `url` and `title` metadata requires `appium-uiautomator2-driver` >= 2.29.0 and `appium-xcuitest-driver` >= 4.16.0 — older drivers return a plain string array (`['NATIVE_APP', 'WEBVIEW_pkg']`) where all webview pages share one opaque context ID, forcing a blind switch followed by DOM-readiness polling; check `browser.getAppiumCommands()` for `mobile: getContexts` at session bootstrap and fall back to the legacy `getAppiumContexts()` + retry pattern when absent, otherwise tests fail with `UnknownCommandError` on older CI Appium installations with no indication in the error that the driver version is the root cause.

**Pattern 773** — `browser.swipe()` — element-scoped carousel swipe with snap-animation settlement
```typescript
// Swipe through an onboarding carousel and verify the correct card appears after each step.
// Setting percent=0.80 keeps the gesture within the element bounds on both platforms.

describe('onboarding carousel swipe navigation', () => {
  it('left-swipes through all three carousel cards in sequence', async () => {
    const carousel  = await $('~onboarding_carousel');
    await carousel.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });

    const cards = ['Welcome', 'Track Goals', 'Connect'];

    for (const [idx, title] of cards.entries()) {
      const cardTitle = await $('~carousel_card_title');
      await cardTitle.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4_000 });
      expect(await cardTitle.getText()).toBe(title);

      if (idx < cards.length - 1) {
        await browser.swipe({
          direction: 'left',
          duration: 800,
          percent: 0.80,
          scrollableElement: carousel,
        });
        await browser.pause(500); // wait for snap animation to settle
      }
    }
  });

  it('swipe-down on the feed triggers pull-to-refresh and reloads items', async () => {
    const feed       = await $('~feed_scroll_view');
    await feed.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });
    const beforeText = await $('~feed_item_0').getText();

    await browser.swipe({ direction: 'down', duration: 1_200, percent: 0.6, scrollableElement: feed });

    await $('~refresh_spinner').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await $('~refresh_spinner').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 10_000, reverse: true });
    expect(await $('~feed_item_0').getText()).not.toBe(beforeText);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.swipe({ scrollableElement })` computes the gesture vector from the element's bounding-box centre using the `percent` parameter (default 0.95) — `percent > 0.90` on iOS causes the gesture endpoint to overshoot the element boundary and trigger the parent `UIScrollView`'s gesture recogniser instead of the target carousel's, producing an unintended vertical scroll with no error thrown; set `percent` to 0.75–0.85 for iOS carousel elements, add a `pause` matching the carousel's snap-animation duration after each swipe to prevent consecutive swipes from compounding into a two-slide skip, and on Android with `RecyclerView` carousels use `duration >= 800ms` so UIAutomator2's velocity-based completion detection does not abort the gesture prematurely.
