**Pattern 774** — `browser.appiumGetStrings()` — localisation string map validation across locales
```typescript
// Retrieve the app's string resource map and verify required keys are present and non-empty.
// appiumGetStrings() reads strings.xml (Android) or Localizable.strings (iOS).

describe('localisation string resource coverage', () => {
  const locales = ['en', 'de', 'ja'] as const;

  for (const locale of locales) {
    it(`all critical string keys are present and non-empty for locale "${locale}"`, async () => {
      const strings = await browser.appiumGetStrings(locale) as Record<string, string>;

      const required = [
        'app_name',
        'login_button_label',
        'error_network_unavailable',
        'settings_title',
        'onboarding_skip_button',
      ];

      for (const key of required) {
        expect(strings).toHaveProperty(key);
        expect(strings[key].trim().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      }
    });
  }

  it('displayed login button text matches the bundled resource for the device locale', async () => {
    const strings = await browser.appiumGetStrings('en') as Record<string, string>;
    const btn     = await $('~login_button');
    await btn.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await btn.getText()).toBe(strings['login_button_label']);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.appiumGetStrings(language)` returns the app's singular string resources from `strings.xml` (Android) or `Localizable.strings` (iOS) but excludes plural-form resources (`<plurals>` on Android, `Localizable.stringsdict` on iOS) — tests that use `appiumGetStrings` to assert plural-form strings like "1 item" vs. "3 items" will silently receive `undefined` for the plural key and pass on the wrong singular form; use `appiumGetStrings` exclusively for singular string key validation and test plural forms by navigating the app to each quantity state and asserting the displayed text via element selectors.

**Pattern 775** — `browser.appiumShake()` — shake-gesture feedback dialog trigger and suppression test
```typescript
// Verify that the shake-to-report gesture works on screens that handle it
// and is correctly suppressed on screens where shake is disabled.
// appiumShake() delivers UIEventSubtypeMotionShake via XCUITest (iOS Simulator only).

describe('shake gesture — feedback dialog', () => {
  before(async function () {
    if (!driver.isIOS) this.skip(); // iOS Simulator only
  });

  it('shake opens the Report-an-Issue dialog on the main screen', async () => {
    await $('~main_content_area').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });
    await browser.appiumShake();
    await browser.pause(1_500);

    const dialog = await $('~feedback_dialog_title');
    await dialog.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await dialog.getText()).toContain('Report an Issue');
  });

  it('cancelling the dialog restores focus to the main content', async () => {
    await browser.appiumShake();
    await browser.pause(1_500);

    const cancelBtn = await $('~feedback_dialog_cancel');
    await cancelBtn.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await cancelBtn.click();

    await $('~feedback_dialog_title').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 4_000, reverse: true });
    expect(await $('~main_content_area').isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('shake does NOT trigger the dialog during fullscreen video playback', async () => {
    await $('~open_video_player').click();
    await $('~video_player_view').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });

    await browser.appiumShake();
    await browser.pause(1_500);
    expect(await $('~feedback_dialog_title').isExisting()).toBe(false);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.appiumShake()` delivers `UIEventSubtypeMotionShake` via the UIKit responder chain to the first `UIResponder` that overrides `motionEnded(_:with:)` — React Native and Flutter apps that detect shake via `DeviceEventEmitter` or third-party accelerometer libraries do not receive `UIEventSubtypeMotionShake` at all (they bypass the UIKit responder chain), making `appiumShake()` ineffective for those apps; verify the app's shake-detection mechanism before using this API, and for cross-framework apps consider a debug backdoor endpoint or `CoreMotion` injection rather than relying on the UIKit path.

**Pattern 776** — `browser.gsmVoice()` + `browser.gsmSignal()` — telephony codec degradation and dialer UI test
```typescript
// Simulate GSM voice codec quality degradation and verify the app's dialer UI response.
// Both commands map to the Android emulator telnet console (emulator-only).

async function requireAndroidEmulator(ctx: Mocha.Context): Promise<void> {
  const caps  = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
  const model = ((caps['deviceModel'] as string) ?? '').toLowerCase();
  if (!driver.isAndroid || (!model.includes('emulator') && !model.includes('sdk_gphone'))) {
    ctx.skip();
  }
}

describe('telephony degradation UI', () => {
  before(async function () { await requireAndroidEmulator(this); });

  it('voice-quality warning appears with EDGE codec + poor signal', async () => {
    await browser.gsmVoice('edge');
    await browser.gsmSignal(1); // poor
    await browser.pause(1_500);

    const warning = await $('~voice_quality_warning');
    await warning.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await warning.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('voice-quality warning clears when full voice and signal are restored', async () => {
    await browser.gsmVoice('on');
    await browser.gsmSignal(4); // great
    await browser.pause(1_500);
    await $('~voice_quality_warning').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000, reverse: true });
  });

  it('dialer shows "No Audio" banner when voice is muted', async () => {
    await $('~open_dialer').click();
    await $('~dialer_screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await browser.gsmVoice('muted');
    await browser.pause(1_000);
    const banner = await $('~dialer_no_audio_banner');
    await banner.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await banner.getText()).toContain('No Audio');
  });

  after(async () => {
    await browser.gsmVoice('on');
    await browser.gsmSignal(4);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.gsmVoice(quality)` sets the emulator telnet `gsm voice` codec state, affecting `TelephonyManager.getVoiceNetworkType()` — apps that check signal strength via `getNetworkType()` respond to `gsmSignal` but may not respond to `gsmVoice` if they do not distinguish codec type from signal level; the WebdriverIO-documented values (`'on'`, `'muted'`, `'gprs'`, `'edge'`, `'gsm'`, `'scch'`) and raw telnet values (`'home'`, `'roaming'`, `'searching'`) are both accepted by the emulator, but mixing them across calls within the same session can desynchronise the emulator's telephony state machine and produce `CallFailedException` on subsequent `gsmCall` commands — use only the documented WebdriverIO string constants throughout a session.

**Pattern 777** — `browser.getSettings()` / `browser.setSettings()` — scoped UIAutomator2 idle-timeout tuning
```typescript
// Scope UIAutomator2 performance settings to specific test blocks
// and guarantee restoration even on test failure using a try/finally wrapper.

interface AppiumSettings {
  ignoreUnimportantViews?: boolean;
  waitForIdleTimeout?: number;
  animationCoolOffTimeout?: number;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

async function withSettings<T>(
  overrides: Partial<AppiumSettings>,
  fn: () => Promise<T>
): Promise<T> {
  const original = (await browser.getSettings()) as AppiumSettings;
  await browser.setSettings(overrides as Record<string, unknown>);
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    await browser.setSettings(original as Record<string, unknown>);
  }
}

describe('UIAutomator2 settings-guarded performance tests', () => {
  it('reduced waitForIdleTimeout speeds up animation-free list scrolling', async () => {
    await withSettings({ waitForIdleTimeout: 100, animationCoolOffTimeout: 0 }, async () => {
      for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
        await browser.swipe({ direction: 'up', duration: 600 });
        const item = await $(`~list_item_${i + 5}`);
        await item.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
        expect(await item.isDisplayed()).toBe(true);
      }
    });
  });

  it('ignoreUnimportantViews cuts selector query time on dense RecyclerView layouts', async () => {
    await withSettings({ ignoreUnimportantViews: true }, async () => {
      const t0    = Date.now();
      const items = await $$('~product_card');
      expect(Date.now() - t0).toBeLessThan(1_000); // < 1s for 50-item list
      expect(items.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    });
  });

  it('withSettings() restores original values after the callback exits', async () => {
    const before = (await browser.getSettings()) as AppiumSettings;
    await withSettings({ waitForIdleTimeout: 500 }, async () => {
      expect(((await browser.getSettings()) as AppiumSettings).waitForIdleTimeout).toBe(500);
    });
    const after = (await browser.getSettings()) as AppiumSettings;
    expect(after.waitForIdleTimeout).toBe(before.waitForIdleTimeout);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.setSettings({ ignoreUnimportantViews: true })` enables UIAutomator2's compressed UI tree mode, reducing `$('~selector')` resolution time by 30–70% on dense layouts by pruning leaf nodes marked `importantForAccessibility="no"` — but elements with a `contentDescription` that are also marked `importantForAccessibility="no"` (common in complex `RecyclerView` items) disappear from the accessibility selector namespace after compression, causing `$('~label')` to throw `no such element` for elements that remain visually present; always run the suite once with compression disabled to baseline which selectors remain reachable, then enable `ignoreUnimportantViews` only in test blocks where every targeted selector has been verified reachable under compression.

**Pattern 778** — `browser.appiumGetStrings()` + `browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()` — locale-matched string assertion with cap-derived language
```typescript
// Derive the device locale from session capabilities and use it to
// fetch + assert the app's string resources without hardcoding a language code.

describe('capability-driven locale string assertion', () => {
  let deviceLocale: string;
  let strings: Record<string, string>;

  before(async () => {
    const caps = await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities();
    // 'language' cap is set via wdio.conf.ts capabilities block, e.g. { language: 'de' }
    deviceLocale = (caps['language'] as string | undefined) ?? 'en';
    strings = await browser.appiumGetStrings(deviceLocale) as Record<string, string>;
  });

  it('app name in About screen matches the bundled app_name string for device locale', async () => {
    await $('~nav_about').click();
    const appNameEl = await $('~about_app_name');
    await appNameEl.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    expect(await appNameEl.getText()).toBe(strings['app_name']);
  });

  it('error modal copy matches the bundled error_network_unavailable string', async () => {
    await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'svc', args: ['wifi', 'disable'],
    });
    await browser.pause(1_500);

    await $('~retry_network_button').click();
    const errorModal = await $('~error_modal_message');
    await errorModal.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });
    expect(await errorModal.getText()).toBe(strings['error_network_unavailable']);

    await browser.execute('mobile: shell', { command: 'svc', args: ['wifi', 'enable'] });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()` returns the `language` and `locale` values that were passed in `wdio.conf.ts` capabilities, making it possible to write locale-agnostic tests that self-configure from the session — however, the `language` cap controls the Appium server's language preference, not the device's system locale; if the device was provisioned with a different locale than the test session's `language` cap (a common CI misconfiguration), `appiumGetStrings(deviceLocale)` returns strings for the test's requested locale while the app renders strings from the device's OS locale, causing every `getText()` assertion to fail with a locale mismatch that appears to be a translation bug rather than a capability/device configuration mismatch; always cross-check `caps['language']` against `adb shell getprop persist.sys.locale` in the `before` hook and fail fast with a descriptive configuration error if they differ.

---

### Community Gotchas

**C68-1** — `browser.gsmCall()` leaves the Android emulator in `CALL_STATE_OFFHOOK` when the test is interrupted mid-call, causing every subsequent `$('~element').click()` to throw `ElementClickInterceptedException` for the rest of the session
Why this matters: When a test that calls `gsmCall(number, 'call')` or `gsmCall(number, 'accept')` is interrupted — by an assertion failure, a timeout, or a `before()` hook crash — the emulator's telephony subsystem remains in `CALL_STATE_OFFHOOK`. The `com.android.phone` call UI overlay persists on screen and intercepts all touch events. Every subsequent `$('~selector').click()` in the same session throws `ElementClickInterceptedException: android.view.View is not clickable at location (x, y). The element com.android.phone:id/incall_screen is covering it.` The error message names `com.android.phone` as the intercept element, but developers unfamiliar with this pattern misread it as a z-index UI bug in the app rather than a dangling emulator call state. Retrying the test without a fresh session makes the failure worse: the `com.android.phone` overlay accumulates with each new `gsmCall` invocation and never clears.
Fix: Add `afterEach(async () => { await browser.gsmCall(phoneNumber, 'cancel').catch(() => {}); })` to every `describe` block that uses `gsmCall`, wrapping the cancel in `.catch(() => {})` so it does not throw when no call is in progress; also add a `before()` hook that checks `getAppiumSessionCapabilities()` for a device guard and issues a `cancel` before the first test to flush any call state left by a previous interrupted run — both hooks together ensure the emulator is always in `CALL_STATE_IDLE` at every test boundary.

---

**C68-2** — `browser.powerCapacity()` and `browser.powerAC()` silently succeed on physical Android devices but never fire the `ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED` broadcast, causing battery-state UI tests to be permanent false positives on CI physical-device farms
Why this matters: `browser.powerCapacity(10)` and `browser.powerAC('off')` map to Android emulator telnet console commands (`power capacity 10`, `power ac off`) that directly manipulate the AVD's software battery profile. On physical Android devices, UIAutomator2 sends these commands, the emulator console socket is not present, and the commands silently return HTTP 200 with no error. The device's `BatteryManager` reports remain unchanged, the `ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED` broadcast is never fired, and the app's `BroadcastReceiver` is never invoked. The low-battery banner never appears, the test's `expect(await banner.isDisplayed()).toBe(true)` assertion fails with a generic `element not found` error, and CI logs show what appears to be an app rendering bug. The root cause — silently no-op commands on a physical device — is completely invisible without reading the UIAutomator2 source code to understand the telnet-console dependency.
Fix: Gate every `powerCapacity`/`powerAC` call with the emulator check (`isAndroidEmulator()`) and call `ctx.skip()` on physical devices; add a `before()` assertion that runs `adb shell dumpsys battery | grep level` and confirms the reported level matches the `powerCapacity` value before relying on battery-state assertions in the test body — if the values differ, the AVD is using a hardware battery profile and the suite must skip with a descriptive message.

---

**C68-3** — `browser.appiumGetStrings()` returns `undefined` for all plural-form resource keys, causing tests that assert plural UI strings to silently pass on the singular fallback form
Why this matters: `browser.appiumGetStrings(language)` reads `strings.xml` on Android and `Localizable.strings` on iOS. Neither file contains plural-form entries: on Android plurals live in `<plurals>` XML elements (resolved at runtime by `Resources.getQuantityString()`), and on iOS plural forms live in `Localizable.stringsdict` files (resolved at runtime by `NSLocalizedString` with a `%d` format argument). The `appiumGetStrings` API does not fetch these plural resources — it only returns the flat key-value string map from the base `strings.xml` / `Localizable.strings` file. A test that does `expect(strings['items_count']).toBe('3 items')` finds `strings['items_count']` is `undefined` (the key is a `<plurals>` element), so the assertion becomes `expect(undefined).toBe('3 items')`, which fails with `expected undefined to equal '3 items'` — but a test that does `expect(strings['items_count']).toBeDefined()` silently passes because `'items_count'` was added as a singular key in `strings.xml` for unrelated reasons, creating false coverage.
Fix: Use `appiumGetStrings` only for singular string key validation; for plural-form assertions, navigate the app to the state that produces each plural (0 items, 1 item, 3 items), read the displayed element text via `await element.getText()`, and assert that value directly — this exercises the app's runtime plural-resolution path rather than the static resource file.

---

**C68-4** — `browser.swipe({ scrollableElement })` on iOS silently scrolls the outer `UIScrollView` instead of the inner nested carousel, producing no error but leaving the carousel on slide 1
Why this matters: The XCUITest driver's `swipe` implementation computes the gesture start coordinate from the `scrollableElement` element's bounding-box centre, then performs a hit-test at that coordinate to identify which `UIScrollView` to scroll. In nested scroll views (e.g., a horizontal `UICollectionView` carousel inside a vertical `UITableView`), XCUITest's hit-test resolves to the outermost `UITableView` at that coordinate because the outer scroll view's gesture recogniser has higher priority in the UIKit responder chain. The outer table scrolls vertically, the inner carousel stays on slide 1, and `browser.swipe()` returns success with no error. The test fails only at the post-swipe assertion `expect(await $('~carousel_card_title').getText()).toBe('Track Goals')` — which reports `'Welcome'` — with no indication that the wrong scroll view was targeted. Developers typically rewrite the selector and retry, never discovering the gesture-resolution root cause.
Fix: Use `browser.execute('mobile: swipe', { direction: 'left', element: (await $('~inner_carousel')).elementId })` for nested scroll views — this XCUITest mobile execute command directly addresses the target element without coordinate hit-testing; alternatively, give the inner carousel a unique accessibility identifier that is not shared with any ancestor element so the hit-test resolves to the correct target.

---

**C68-5** — `browser.appiumQueryAppState()` returns state `1` (NOT_RUNNING) on Android 12+ for a process that is actually alive — Android's process-death-detection changes cause UIAutomator2 to misreport the running state
Why this matters: Android 12 (API 31) introduced changes to `ActivityManager.getRunningAppProcesses()` that restrict which processes are visible to other apps. UIAutomator2 implements `queryAppState` by calling `ActivityManager.getRunningAppProcesses()` and checking whether the target package appears in the list. On Android 12+, `getRunningAppProcesses()` returns only processes associated with the caller (`io.appium.uiautomator2.server`) — not third-party app processes — unless the caller holds `GET_TASKS` permission (removed in API 21). UIAutomator2 therefore never finds the target package in the process list and returns state `1` (NOT_RUNNING) even when the app is running in the background with active background tasks. Tests that assert `state === BG_SUSPENDED` or `state === BG_ACTIVE` after pressing Home on Android 12+ devices always fail with state `1`, appearing to indicate the app was killed by the OS when it was merely backgrounded.
Fix: On Android 12+ emulators and devices, replace `appiumQueryAppState` background-state assertions with a `pressKeyCode(3)` (Home) followed by a `terminateApp` call and a `queryAppState` assertion for state `1` (which reliably returns `NOT_RUNNING` after terminate) — this avoids the broken background-state reporting; alternatively, confirm the app is running in the background via `adb shell ps | grep <packageName>` in an `execute('mobile: shell', ...)` call rather than relying on `queryAppState` for background states on Android 12+.

**Pattern 779** — `ChainablePromiseArray.entries()` — indexed element-pair iteration without re-querying `$$`
```typescript
// ChainablePromiseArray.entries() was added in WDIO v9.7.2.
// It returns an AsyncIterableIterator of [index, ChainablePromiseElement] pairs,
// allowing you to iterate over $$ results with a numeric index *without*
// re-issuing the DOM query in a second $$ call or maintaining a manual counter.

describe('list item index validation', () => {
  it('every odd-positioned cart item has the discount badge visible', async () => {
    // $$ returns a ChainablePromiseArray — .entries() iterates it with indices
    const items = await $$('[data-testid="cart-item"]');

    for await (const [index, item] of items.entries()) {
      if (index % 2 !== 0) {
        // odd indices (1, 3, 5 …) must carry a discount badge
        const badge = await item.$('[data-testid="discount-badge"]');
        await expect(badge).toBeDisplayed({
          message: `cart item at index ${index} is missing its discount badge`,
        });
      }
    }
  });

  it('tracks the first error element by index for a precise failure message', async () => {
    const fields = await $$('[data-testid="form-field"]');
    const errors: Array<{ index: number; label: string }> = [];

    for await (const [index, field] of fields.entries()) {
      const hasError = await field.$('.field-error').isExisting();
      if (hasError) {
        const label = await field.$('label').getText();
        errors.push({ index, label });
      }
    }

    expect(errors).toHaveLength(0);  // fails with indices + labels if any field has an error
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `ChainablePromiseArray.entries()` produces an `AsyncIterableIterator`, so it requires `for await...of` — it cannot be used inside `Array.prototype.forEach` or `Promise.all` directly, and attempting to call `entries()` inside a synchronous `it()` without `async` causes a `TypeError: items.entries is not a function` runtime error at the iteration step (not at the call site) because the method is resolved lazily when iteration begins; always declare the surrounding `it` block and any helper function that uses `for await...of entries()` with `async`, and if you need parallel iteration across all elements, collect the `[index, element]` pairs into an array first with `const pairs = []; for await (const pair of items.entries()) pairs.push(pair);` before fanning out with `Promise.all`.

**Pattern 780** — `terminateApp()` options parameter — platform-specific terminate flags (v9.12.5+)
```typescript
// WDIO v9.12.5 added an `options` parameter to terminateApp() that is forwarded
// directly to the underlying Appium protocol command, enabling per-platform
// terminate flags without switching to raw execute() calls.
//
// On XCUITest (iOS) the option object is passed as the second argument to the
// XCUITest terminateApp() endpoint.  No XCUITest-specific flags exist today,
// but the parameter is reserved for future driver additions.
//
// On UIAutomator2 (Android) the key option is `timeout` — the milliseconds
// UIAutomator2 will wait for the process to exit before issuing a SIGKILL.

import type { AppiumCapabilities } from '@wdio/types';

async function safeTerminate(appPackage: string, timeoutMs = 5_000): Promise<void> {
  const caps = (await browser.getAppiumSessionCapabilities()) as AppiumCapabilities;
  const isAndroid = (caps.platformName ?? '').toLowerCase() === 'android';

  if (isAndroid) {
    // Pass the UIAutomator2 `timeout` option so the driver does not issue
    // SIGKILL prematurely on apps with long onDestroy() handlers (e.g. apps
    // that flush SQLite WAL to disk before exiting).
    await browser.terminateApp(appPackage, { timeout: timeoutMs } as Record<string, unknown>);
  } else {
    // iOS: no extra options currently; call without the second argument.
    await browser.terminateApp(appPackage);
  }

  // Confirm the app is no longer running before the next test step.
  await browser.waitUntil(
    async () => {
      const state = await browser.appiumQueryAppState(appPackage);
      return state === 1; // AppState.NOT_RUNNING
    },
    { timeout: timeoutMs + 2_000, interval: 300,
      timeoutMsg: `App ${appPackage} did not reach NOT_RUNNING within ${timeoutMs + 2_000} ms` },
  );
}

describe('app lifecycle — cold-start perf baseline', () => {
  it('terminates and cold-starts the app within 4 s on Android', async () => {
    await safeTerminate('com.example.myapp', 6_000);
    const t0 = Date.now();
    await browser.activateApp('com.example.myapp');
    await $('[data-testid="home-screen"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 8_000 });
    const launchMs = Date.now() - t0;
    expect(launchMs).toBeLessThan(4_000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `options` second argument to `terminateApp()` is typed as `Record<string, unknown>` in the Appium protocol layer, so TypeScript will not warn you if you pass an unsupported key — an unrecognised option silently falls through to the driver and is ignored rather than producing an error; always consult the release notes for `appium-uiautomator2-driver` and `appium-xcuitest-driver` to determine which option keys are valid for your installed driver version before relying on option-driven behaviour in CI, and pin the driver version in `package.json` so that a driver upgrade does not silently change which options are honoured.

**Pattern 781** — `expect.soft()` + `SoftAssertionService` + `autoAssertOnTestEnd` — deferred multi-assertion reporting in mobile tests
```typescript
// WDIO v9.16.0 automatically includes SoftAssertionService in the runner,
// making expect.soft() available without manual service registration.
// `autoAssertOnTestEnd: true` (default) causes all accumulated soft failures
// to be thrown at the end of each `it()` block automatically.
// Set `autoAssertOnTestEnd: false` in wdio.conf.ts to take manual control.

// wdio.conf.ts — opt-out of auto-throw to control assertion point manually
export const config = {
  autoAssertOnTestEnd: false,     // default: true
  // ... rest of config
};

// ── Pattern A: default mode (autoAssertOnTestEnd: true) ──────────────────────
// All soft assertions are checked automatically at the end of each it() block.
it('home screen critical fields all display correctly', async () => {
  await browser.activateApp('com.example.myapp');
  await $('[data-testid="home-screen"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 });

  // None of these throw immediately — test continues even if one fails
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="hero-title"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="cta-button"]')).toBeEnabled();
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="nav-bar"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="user-avatar"]')).toHaveAttribute('src');

  // SoftAssertionService throws here automatically with ALL failures aggregated,
  // giving one test failure that enumerates every broken element at once.
});

// ── Pattern B: manual mode (autoAssertOnTestEnd: false) ──────────────────────
// Use when you need to assert at a checkpoint mid-test and then continue.
it('onboarding form validates all fields before submission', async () => {
  await $('[data-testid="onboarding-form"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });

  // Validate page 1 fields — soft, so we see all errors before proceeding
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="first-name"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="last-name"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="email"]')).toBeEnabled();

  // Checkpoint: throw if any page-1 soft failure occurred before navigating
  // to page 2 (pointless to check page 2 if page 1 is broken)
  await expect.assertSoftFailures();  // throws if soft failures exist, clears them

  await $('[data-testid="next-btn"]').click();

  // Page 2 fields
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="phone"]')).toBeDisplayed();
  await expect.soft($('[data-testid="dob"]')).toBeEnabled();

  // Final manual checkpoint — equivalent to what autoAssertOnTestEnd does automatically
  await expect.assertSoftFailures();
});

// ── Soft failures don't prevent afterEach cleanup ─────────────────────────────
afterEach(async () => {
  // afterEach still runs even when soft assertions fail at test end.
  // Use this to guarantee teardown (e.g., log out, reset app state).
  await browser.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'am', args: ['force-stop', 'com.example.myapp'],
  }).catch(() => {});
});
```
Tradeoff: `expect.soft()` accumulates failures in a thread-local (per-worker) store managed by `SoftAssertionService`; when `maxInstances > 1` in the runner config, each worker maintains its own soft-failure list and `expect.clearSoftFailures()` only clears the calling worker's list — this is the intended design, but developers debugging failures in parallel runs often try to inspect soft failures from a shared structure (e.g., writing to a file and reading it in another worker) and find the list empty because the clearing already happened in the worker that ran the test; always inspect soft assertion output from the reporter output (Allure, spec reporter) rather than attempting cross-worker failure aggregation.

---

**Pattern 782** — `expect(browser).toHaveClipboardText()` — clipboard content assertion in WebView hybrid flows (expect-webdriverio v5+)
```typescript
// expect(browser).toHaveClipboardText() asserts the value of the system
// clipboard.  It retries with waitFor semantics (default 2 000 ms, 100 ms
// interval) so no manual pause() is needed after triggering a "copy" action.
//
// Mobile requirements:
//  - Android: UIAutomator2 v3+; clipboard read/write via ContentProvider proxy.
//  - iOS: requires foreground session; background clipboard reads silently return ''.
//  - Real iOS devices: paste permission dialog may intercept the read;
//    use appium:autoAcceptAlerts to dismiss it automatically.

describe('share sheet — copy-link flow', () => {
  it('tapping "Copy Link" places the canonical article URL on the clipboard', async () => {
    const articleUrl = 'https://example.com/articles/q3-review';

    // Navigate to the article and trigger the share sheet
    await browser.deepLink(articleUrl);
    await $('[data-testid="share-btn"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await $('[data-testid="share-btn"]').click();

    const copyBtn = await $('[data-testid="copy-link-btn"]');
    await copyBtn.waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
    await copyBtn.click();

    // Assert clipboard without pause() — retries until clipboard equals the URL
    await expect(browser).toHaveClipboardText(articleUrl);
  });

  it('clipboard text contains the short-link domain after deep-link share', async () => {
    await $('[data-testid="share-btn"]').click();
    await $('[data-testid="copy-short-link-btn"]').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 3_000 });
    await $('[data-testid="copy-short-link-btn"]').click();

    // Partial match: the short link domain must be present somewhere in clipboard
    await expect(browser).toHaveClipboardText(
      expect.stringContaining('sho.rt/'),
    );
  });

  it('clipboard is cleared between tests by setClipboard guard', async () => {
    // Seed with a known value before the test so we don't inherit a previous run's clipboard
    await browser.setClipboard('', 'plaintext');
    await $('[data-testid="copy-link-btn"]').click();
    await expect(browser).not.toHaveClipboardText('');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `expect(browser).toHaveClipboardText()` reads the clipboard via `getClipboard()` internally, which on iOS requires the test runner to be the foreground process — switching the app to the background (e.g., opening the system share sheet and tapping "Copy") temporarily suspends the WDA proxy connection on some iOS 17+ devices, causing the `getClipboard()` call inside the retry loop to throw `Error: The WDA connection was lost` rather than returning the clipboard value; the assertion then fails with a connection error rather than a clipboard mismatch, masking the true state of the test; work around this by calling `browser.pause(800)` after the copy action to let the WDA connection re-establish before the `toHaveClipboardText()` retry loop begins, and configure `appium:webviewConnectRetries: 3` to give WDA time to recover.

---

**Pattern 783** — `wdio/eslint-plugin-wdio` `no-floating-promise` rule — zero-config `await` enforcement for mobile test files (v9.25+)
```typescript
// WDIO v9.25.0 added the `wdio/no-floating-promise` ESLint rule to
// eslint-plugin-wdio.  It catches missing `await` on WebdriverIO command
// calls — a common source of silent test-pass-but-nothing-ran bugs in mobile
// suites where every browser/element command returns a Promise.
//
// .eslintrc.cjs (or eslint.config.mjs for flat config)
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// module.exports = {
//   plugins: ['wdio'],
//   extends: ['plugin:wdio/all'],   // enables ALL wdio rules incl. no-floating-promise
//   rules: {
//     'wdio/no-floating-promise': 'error',  // also available standalone
//   },
// };

// eslint.config.mjs (flat config — WDIO v9 recommended approach)
import wdioPlugin from 'eslint-plugin-wdio';

export default [
  {
    plugins: { wdio: wdioPlugin },
    rules: {
      ...wdioPlugin.configs['flat/recommended'].rules,
      'wdio/no-floating-promise': 'error',
    },
    files: ['test/**/*.ts', 'src/**/*.ts'],
  },
];

// ── Examples the rule catches ────────────────────────────────────────────────
// ❌ ESLint error: floating promise — click() returns Promise<void>, discarded
it('clicks the login button', async () => {
  $('[data-testid="login-btn"]').click();   // missing await — test passes silently
});

// ✅ Correct
it('clicks the login button', async () => {
  await $('[data-testid="login-btn"]').click();
});

// ❌ Inside loops — forEach does not await async callbacks
it('dismisses all toasts', async () => {
  const toasts = await $$('[data-testid="toast"]');
  toasts.forEach((t) => t.click());   // rule flags this as floating within forEach
});

// ✅ Use for...of instead
it('dismisses all toasts', async () => {
  const toasts = await $$('[data-testid="toast"]');
  for (const t of toasts) {
    await t.click();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `wdio/no-floating-promise` analyses static call sites and flags any WebdriverIO command call that is not wrapped in `await` or assigned to a variable — but it cannot track whether you later `await` a stored reference (e.g., `const p = element.click(); /* ... */ await p;`), so storing a promise and awaiting it later to batch parallel operations (a valid performance pattern for independent side-effect-free operations like `Promise.all([a.getText(), b.getText()])`) may trigger false-positive ESLint errors; configure `/* eslint-disable-next-line wdio/no-floating-promise */` on the individual variable assignment lines, or destructure into `await Promise.all([...])` directly, which the rule correctly recognises as an awaited expression.

---

**Pattern 784** — `multiRemoteBrowser` camelCase rename + parallel iOS/Android session coordination (v9.23.0 breaking change)
```typescript
// WDIO v9.23.0 renamed `multiremotebrowser` to `multiRemoteBrowser` for
// camelCase compliance.  Any code that imported or referenced the old name
// now receives `undefined` at runtime with no compile-time error in JS
// projects (TypeScript projects catch it via the updated @wdio/types).
//
// multiRemoteBrowser gives you named access to each capability's driver
// instance within the same test worker — essential for iOS/Android
// cross-platform smoke suites that share a single wdio.conf.ts.

// wdio.conf.ts — multiremote capability declaration
export const config = {
  capabilities: {
    // Named capabilities: keys become the handles for multiRemoteBrowser
    iOSPhone: {
      capabilities: {
        platformName: 'iOS',
        'appium:deviceName': 'iPhone 15 Pro',
        'appium:platformVersion': '17.5',
        'appium:app': './app/MyApp.ipa',
        'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
      },
    },
    androidPhone: {
      capabilities: {
        platformName: 'Android',
        'appium:deviceName': 'Pixel_8_API_34',
        'appium:platformVersion': '14',
        'appium:app': './app/MyApp.apk',
        'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
      },
    },
  },
};

// spec file — multiRemoteBrowser (v9.23+ camelCase)
import { multiRemoteBrowser } from '@wdio/globals';  // ← new camelCase name

describe('cross-platform home screen smoke', () => {
  it('both platforms display the home screen hero title within 6 s', async () => {
    // Run both assertions in parallel — each instance drives its own device
    const [iosTitle, androidTitle] = await Promise.all([
      multiRemoteBrowser.iOSPhone.$('[data-testid="hero-title"]')
        .waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 })
        .then(() => multiRemoteBrowser.iOSPhone.$('[data-testid="hero-title"]').getText()),
      multiRemoteBrowser.androidPhone.$('[data-testid="hero-title"]')
        .waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 6_000 })
        .then(() => multiRemoteBrowser.androidPhone.$('[data-testid="hero-title"]').getText()),
    ]);

    expect(iosTitle).toBe('Welcome to MyApp');
    expect(androidTitle).toBe('Welcome to MyApp');
  });

  it('iOS taps CTA and Android verifies the same deeplink opens', async () => {
    await multiRemoteBrowser.iOSPhone.$('[data-testid="cta-share-btn"]').click();
    const link = await multiRemoteBrowser.iOSPhone.$('[data-testid="share-url"]').getText();

    await multiRemoteBrowser.androidPhone.deepLink(link);
    await expect(
      multiRemoteBrowser.androidPhone.$('[data-testid="landing-heading"]'),
    ).toBeDisplayed();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `multiRemoteBrowser.<name>` gives synchronous access to each named browser instance, but each instance maintains an independent WebDriver session — calling `browser.pause()` in a multiremote spec pauses ALL instances simultaneously (it broadcasts to every session), not just the one you intended to delay; to pause only one platform, call `await multiRemoteBrowser.iOSPhone.pause(1000)` on the named instance directly, and be aware that any call on the bare `browser` global in a multiremote spec is also broadcast to all instances, so `await browser.activateApp('com.example.myapp')` will attempt to activate the app on both the iOS and Android sessions in parallel — if the package name differs between platforms (bundle ID vs. package name), one session will throw a `driver not started` or `invalid arguments` error that surfaces as a flaky cross-platform test failure rather than a configuration bug.

### Community Gotchas (iter 40)

**C69-1** — Shadow root element references leak memory across SPA navigations in WDIO v9.27.0 and earlier, causing worker heap to grow unboundedly during long test suites
Why this matters: WebdriverIO stores `shadowRoot` WeakMap entries for every element returned from `$()` or `$$()` calls that pierce the shadow DOM (v9 auto-pierce-shadow feature). Before v9.27.1, these entries were keyed on the element's `ElementId` string, which the WebDriver session recycles when the page navigates. On SPA-style hybrid apps that never trigger a hard page reload (e.g., React Native WebView apps using `react-navigation`), the `ElementId` values from the previous route remain in the WeakMap alongside the new route's elements, because the WeakMap key is a string (not an object), and strings are not garbage-collected by the WeakMap GC semantics. Over a 200-test suite with 50 navigations per test, this grows the worker heap by ~40–80 MB per worker, eventually causing `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed — JavaScript heap out of memory`. The error appears as a random mid-suite crash rather than a memory message, because the GC pause occurs during a `waitForDisplayed()` call and the stack trace points to the assertion rather than the memory accumulation.
Fix: Upgrade to WDIO v9.27.1 where the shadow root store was refactored to use `WeakRef`-keyed entries that are eligible for GC when the element reference is released; if you cannot upgrade immediately, add `--max-old-space-size=4096` to `execArgv` in `wdio.conf.ts` and increase `maxInstances` monitoring — this defers the OOM crash but does not fix the leak.

---

**C69-2** — `browser.waitForClickable()` on a native-context element silently resolves `true` in older sessions even when the element is obscured — v9.23.3 added native-context support but requires the capability flag
Why this matters: `waitForClickable()` calls the WebDriver `checkClickable` algorithm, which before v9.23.3 only operated in browser contexts (using `checkVisibility()`) — in a native mobile context (NATIVE_APP), it fell back to checking `isDisplayed() && isEnabled()`, which returns `true` for any non-hidden, non-disabled element even if it is visually obscured by an overlay. On iOS, a system permission dialog or `UIVisualEffectView` blur overlay leaves the element `isEnabled() === true` while making it untappable; `waitForClickable()` resolved immediately and the subsequent `click()` threw `ElementClickInterceptedException`. The v9.23.3 fix added proper native-context clickability detection, but it is gated behind the `appium:nativeWebScreenshot: true` capability (iOS) or the UIAutomator2 `waitForClickable` setting flag (Android) — without those, the old fallback behaviour is still used.
Fix: Add `'appium:nativeWebScreenshot': true` to your XCUITest capabilities to enable the v9.23.3 native-context `waitForClickable()` path; for UIAutomator2, set `{ waitForClickable: true }` via `browser.setSettings()` in a global `beforeEach` hook; in both cases, add a `waitForDisplayed()` call on any expected overlay element before `waitForClickable()` to confirm the overlay has dismissed before asserting clickability.

---

**C69-3** — `browser.addInitScript()` scripts containing `</script>` string literals are not escaped before injection in WDIO v9.19.1 and earlier, causing the WebView to silently truncate the script at the unescaped closing tag
Why this matters: `browser.addInitScript()` injects a JavaScript snippet into every new document before any page scripts run, making it useful for injecting mock globals or feature flags into a WebView under test. In v9.19.1 and earlier, the script string was wrapped in a `<script>` tag and injected via `innerHTML` assignment rather than a `document.createElement('script')` + `textContent` approach; the innerHTML path causes the HTML parser to treat the literal sequence `</script>` inside the script body as the closing tag, silently truncating the injected script at that point. Tests that inject mock objects containing `</script>` as a string value (e.g., `window.__mocks__ = { html: '</script>' }`) produce a corrupted global where only the first part of the object is defined, causing downstream `ReferenceError: window.__mocks__ is undefined` on the first line that reads the mock. The error is caught in the WebView JS context and silently swallowed by the driver; the test fails at the assertion with a `TypeError` that looks like a test-data bug.
Fix: Upgrade to WDIO v9.19.2 where `addInitScript` was patched to escape `</script>` sequences in the injected body; if pinned to v9.19.1 or earlier, replace `</script>` in your script strings with `<\/script>` (backslash-escaped forward slash) — this is valid JavaScript and is parsed identically by V8 while preventing HTML parser truncation.

## `appium:mjpegScalingFactor` and `appium:mjpegServerFramerate` — MJPEG Stream Quality Tuning  [community]

Appium's MJPEG server (used for screen recording and live view in Appium Inspector) can be tuned for CI environments where network bandwidth or CPU is constrained. `appium:mjpegScalingFactor` reduces the image size before compression; `appium:mjpegServerFramerate` caps the frames per second.

These capabilities apply to both UiAutomator2 and XCUITest drivers and take effect at session creation.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — MJPEG tuning for CI (reduces CPU and network load)
const iosCaps: WebdriverIO.Capabilities = {
  platformName: 'iOS',
  'appium:automationName': 'XCUITest',
  'appium:deviceName': 'iPhone 15',
  'appium:platformVersion': '17.0',
  'appium:app': process.env.IOS_APP_PATH!,
  // MJPEG tuning — reduce CI image payload by 50%, cap at 4 fps
  'appium:mjpegScalingFactor': 50,           // integer: 1–100 (percent of original resolution); default 100
  'appium:mjpegServerFramerate': 4,          // integer: frames per second; default 10
  'appium:mjpegServerPort': 9100,            // unique port per session for parallel runs
};

const androidCaps: WebdriverIO.Capabilities = {
  platformName: 'Android',
  'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
  'appium:deviceName': 'Pixel 7',
  'appium:platformVersion': '13',
  'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,
  'appium:mjpegScalingFactor': 50,
  'appium:mjpegServerFramerate': 4,
  'appium:mjpegServerPort': 9200,
};
```

**When to tune MJPEG:**

| Environment | `mjpegScalingFactor` | `mjpegServerFramerate` | Rationale |
|-------------|---------------------|----------------------|-----------|
| Local development | 100 (default) | 10 (default) | Full quality for Inspector and manual debugging |
| CI (no video) | 25–50 | 2–4 | Minimum overhead — video not needed |
| CI (failure videos) | 50–75 | 5–8 | Readable video at lower bandwidth cost |
| Device farm (metered) | 25 | 3 | Minimise egress cost |

```typescript
// test/helpers/mjpegHelper.ts — read MJPEG stream for live frame capture during test

/**
 * Capture a single MJPEG frame from the Appium MJPEG server.
 * Useful when driver.saveScreenshot() is too slow for rapid state checks.
 * Requires appium:mjpegServerPort to be set in capabilities.
 */
export async function captureMjpegFrame(port: number, timeoutMs = 3_000): Promise<Buffer> {
  const http = await import('http');
  return new Promise<Buffer>((resolve, reject) => {
    const req = http.get(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}`, (res) => {
      const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
      // MJPEG streams boundary markers: --BoundaryString\r\n
      let buffer = Buffer.alloc(0);
      res.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {
        buffer = Buffer.concat([buffer, chunk]);
        // Find JPEG start (FFD8) and end (FFD9) markers
        const start = buffer.indexOf(Buffer.from([0xFF, 0xD8]));
        const end   = buffer.indexOf(Buffer.from([0xFF, 0xD9]));
        if (start !== -1 && end !== -1 && end > start) {
          resolve(buffer.slice(start, end + 2));
          req.destroy();
        }
      });
      res.on('error', reject);
    });
    req.setTimeout(timeoutMs, () => {
      req.destroy();
      reject(new Error(`MJPEG frame capture timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`));
    });
    req.on('error', reject);
  });
}
```

**`appium:mjpegScalingFactor` / `appium:mjpegServerFramerate` gotchas [community]:**

1. **[community] `mjpegScalingFactor` below 25 makes Appium Inspector element selection unreliable:** WHY: At very low resolution, the coordinate mapping between Inspector's click position and the actual device pixel is approximated by Appium using the scale factor. Below 25% scale, rounding errors in the coordinate translation accumulate to more than one element width on dense screens (e.g. iPhone 15 Pro at 460 ppi). Fix: keep `mjpegScalingFactor` at 50 or above when using Inspector for element discovery; use lower values (25–33) only for CI recording where coordinate precision is not needed.

2. **[community] `mjpegServerPort` conflicts cause session creation failure with an undescriptive error:** WHY: If two parallel sessions use the same `mjpegServerPort`, the second session fails to bind the port and Appium throws `SessionNotCreatedException: Failed to start Appium session: Could not start MJPEG server`. The error message does not mention the port conflict. Fix: stagger `mjpegServerPort` values by session index: `9100 + index * 10` in a loop over capability array; ensure no other process (e.g. a zombie Appium from a previous run) holds the port before starting CI.

3. **[community] Setting `mjpegServerFramerate: 0` disables the MJPEG server entirely — `driver.startRecordingScreen()` then fails:** WHY: `mjpegServerFramerate: 0` is treated as "off" by both UiAutomator2 and XCUITest drivers — no MJPEG server is started. The `startRecordingScreen()` command relies on the MJPEG stream to capture frames; without the stream running it throws `Error: Screen recording is not possible as there is no MJPEG server running`. Fix: use a non-zero framerate (minimum 1); if you genuinely want no MJPEG overhead, omit both MJPEG capabilities entirely (the server still starts on the default port — but consuming no CPU when no client connects), or set `'appium:mjpegServerPort': 0` on drivers that support it to bind to an ephemeral port and then not connect.

## `goog:chromeOptions` with `mobileEmulation` — Chrome DevTools Mobile Emulation in WebView Tests  [community]

When testing Android WebView-based content via ChromeDriver, you can pass `goog:chromeOptions` with `mobileEmulation` to simulate specific mobile device viewports, user agents, and touch events at the ChromeDriver level — independently of the physical device screen.

This is distinct from `browser.emulate('device', ...)` (which is a WDIO-level BiDi command) and from `browser.setViewport()` (which resizes the CSS viewport). The `mobileEmulation` option tells ChromeDriver to pre-configure the WebView as if it were running on a specific device before any test commands are sent.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — Android WebView with Chrome DevTools mobile emulation
const androidWebViewCaps: WebdriverIO.Capabilities = {
  platformName: 'Android',
  'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
  'appium:deviceName': 'Pixel 7',
  'appium:platformVersion': '13',
  'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,
  'appium:chromeOptions': {
    // mobileEmulation: force ChromeDriver WebView to emulate a specific device
    mobileEmulation: {
      deviceName: 'iPhone SE',   // named device from Chrome DevTools device list
    },
  },
};

// OR — custom device metrics (width, height, pixelRatio, touch)
const androidCustomViewportCaps: WebdriverIO.Capabilities = {
  platformName: 'Android',
  'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
  'appium:deviceName': 'Pixel 7',
  'appium:platformVersion': '13',
  'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,
  'appium:chromeOptions': {
    mobileEmulation: {
      deviceMetrics: {
        width:            375,
        height:           667,
        pixelRatio:       2.0,
        touch:            true,   // enables touch events in the emulated viewport
      },
      userAgent: 'Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_0 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15',
    },
  },
};
```

```typescript
// test/specs/responsive-webview.spec.ts — WebView responsive layout test
describe('Responsive WebView — iPhone SE layout', () => {
  it('should render the mobile navigation hamburger menu at 375px width', async () => {
    // Switch to the WebView context where ChromeDriver + mobileEmulation are active
    await switchToWebContext();

    // At 375px (iPhone SE), the nav bar collapses to a hamburger
    const hamburger = await $('button[aria-label="Menu"]');
    await expect(hamburger).toBeDisplayed();

    // The desktop navigation links should be hidden
    await expect($('nav.desktop-links')).not.toBeDisplayed();

    await switchToNativeContext();
  });
});
```

```typescript
// Usage pattern: test multiple viewport breakpoints in a single session via setViewport
// after the initial mobileEmulation opens the WebView at the base size
describe('WebView breakpoint coverage', () => {
  const BREAKPOINTS = [
    { name: 'phone-sm',  width: 375,  height: 667 },
    { name: 'phone-lg',  width: 414,  height: 896 },
    { name: 'tablet',    width: 768,  height: 1024 },
  ];

  for (const bp of BREAKPOINTS) {
    it(`should render correctly at ${bp.name} (${bp.width}×${bp.height})`, async () => {
      await switchToWebContext();
      await browser.setViewport({ width: bp.width, height: bp.height, devicePixelRatio: 2 });
      await browser.refresh();                  // re-render at new viewport
      await expect(browser).toMatchScreenSnapshot(`webview-${bp.name}`);
      await switchToNativeContext();
    });
  }
});
```

**`goog:chromeOptions` / `mobileEmulation` gotchas [community]:**

1. **[community] `appium:chromeOptions` and `goog:chromeOptions` are different keys — only `appium:chromeOptions` is forwarded by UiAutomator2 to ChromeDriver:** WHY: Appium's UiAutomator2 driver strips W3C capability namespace prefixes before passing ChromeDriver options. The W3C-compliant `goog:chromeOptions` key is consumed by the session creation layer; the Appium-specific `appium:chromeOptions` key is forwarded to ChromeDriver. Using `goog:chromeOptions` with mobileEmulation in an Appium session silently does nothing — the WebView opens at the physical device dimensions. Fix: always use `appium:chromeOptions` (with the `appium:` namespace prefix) for WebView session ChromeDriver configuration; `goog:chromeOptions` is only valid for direct ChromeDriver sessions (non-Appium).

2. **[community] `deviceName` strings in `mobileEmulation` are case-sensitive and must exactly match Chrome DevTools device list entries:** WHY: ChromeDriver resolves device names against an internal device database identical to Chrome DevTools → Device Mode. A typo like `'iPhone SE (2020)'` instead of `'iPhone SE'` causes ChromeDriver to fall back to a default 800×600 viewport with no touch emulation — without any error or warning. Fix: verify device names against the [Chrome DevTools devices JSON](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main/third_party/devtools-frontend/src/front_end/emulated_devices/); use `deviceMetrics` for custom sizes rather than relying on named device lookup.

3. **[community] `mobileEmulation` touch mode does not replicate iOS WebKit touch event semantics — click delays differ:** WHY: Chrome's mobile emulation adds a 300ms click delay to simulate the iOS tap-to-click disambiguation introduced in older Mobile Safari. Modern iOS (iOS 13+) and most apps with `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width">` disable this delay. An Android ChromeDriver session with `mobileEmulation` may still apply the 300ms delay for touch events if the page doesn't have the FastClick meta tag. Fix: add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">` to the tested page, or use `browser.action('pointer', { parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' } })` with zero-duration moves to avoid the delay entirely in automation.

## `appium:skipDeviceInitialization` — Fast Session Creation for Pre-Configured Devices  [community]

`appium:skipDeviceInitialization` (UiAutomator2 driver, `boolean`, default `false`) skips the device setup steps that Appium normally runs at the start of each session: unlocking the screen, disabling animations, dismissing onboarding dialogs, and waiting for the package manager to settle. When the device is already in a known-good state (e.g. a persistent emulator kept warm between CI jobs), skipping initialization reduces session startup from 15–30 seconds to 2–5 seconds.

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — fast session creation for warm CI emulator
const androidCiFastCaps: WebdriverIO.Capabilities = {
  platformName: 'Android',
  'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
  'appium:deviceName': 'Pixel_7_API_33',
  'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,
  'appium:newCommandTimeout': 120,
  // Fast path: skip unlock, animation disablement, package manager wait
  'appium:skipDeviceInitialization': true,   // requires device pre-configured externally
  // Still enforce fresh app install so the new .apk is tested
  'appium:enforceAppInstall': true,
  'appium:noReset': false,
};
```

**Pre-requisite CI setup when using `skipDeviceInitialization: true`:**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/mobile-e2e.yml — warm emulator with pre-configuration
- name: Start and pre-configure Android emulator
  uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
  with:
    api-level: 33
    target: google_apis
    arch: x86_64
    avd-name: Pixel_7_API_33
    emulator-options: -no-snapshot-save -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim
    disable-animations: true
    script: |
      # Disable animations (required before skipDeviceInitialization)
      adb shell settings put global window_animation_scale 0
      adb shell settings put global transition_animation_scale 0
      adb shell settings put global animator_duration_scale 0
      # Unlock screen and ensure it stays awake
      adb shell input keyevent 82
      adb shell svc power stayon true
      echo "Emulator pre-configured for skipDeviceInitialization"
```

```typescript
// Benchmark helper — compare session startup time with and without skipDeviceInitialization
export async function measureSessionStartup(label: string): Promise<void> {
  const start = Date.now();
  await $('~home-screen').waitForDisplayed({ timeout: 30_000 });
  const elapsed = Date.now() - start;
  console.log(`[perf] ${label}: first element visible in ${elapsed}ms`);
  // Typical results:
  //   skipDeviceInitialization: false → 18,000–28,000ms
  //   skipDeviceInitialization: true  →  2,000–5,000ms (warm emulator)
}
```

**`appium:skipDeviceInitialization` gotchas [community]:**

1. **[community] `skipDeviceInitialization: true` on a cold emulator causes `TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for device to be ready` within 5 seconds:** WHY: The initialization steps include waiting for the Android package manager to settle (the `pm list packages` probe). On a cold boot, the package manager is not yet ready; skipping the wait causes Appium to proceed immediately and fail when it tries to install the app. Fix: use `skipDeviceInitialization: true` ONLY with persistent warm emulators; include a separate CI step that boots the emulator and waits for `adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed` to return `1` before starting the test job.

2. **[community] Animations must be disabled externally — `skipDeviceInitialization` skips Appium's internal animation disablement step:** WHY: Appium normally calls `adb shell settings put global window_animation_scale 0` (and the transition/animator equivalents) during initialization. With `skipDeviceInitialization: true`, these ADB commands are never run by Appium. If the emulator was started fresh (not from a snapshot with pre-disabled animations), animations remain at 1.0x and `waitForDisplayed` timeouts increase significantly. Fix: always run the three `adb shell settings put global` animation disablement commands in the CI setup step before enabling `skipDeviceInitialization`; or use the capability `'appium:disableWindowAnimation': true` which is applied at a different lifecycle point and is NOT skipped by `skipDeviceInitialization`.

3. **[community] `skipDeviceInitialization` combined with `enforceAppInstall: true` can produce `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` on emulators with signature mismatches:** WHY: When initialization is skipped, Appium does not run the `pm uninstall` step that normally removes a conflicting APK signature. If the emulator has a previous APK installed with a different signing key (debug vs release), `enforceAppInstall` forces reinstall but encounters the incompatible signature. Fix: add `adb uninstall com.example.myapp || true` to the CI setup step before starting the test job; this clears any conflicting APK without requiring Appium's initialization flow to run.

## `appium:androidCoverage` and JaCoCo — Code Coverage for Android Instrumentation Tests  [community]

Appium's UiAutomator2 driver supports triggering JaCoCo coverage dump via the `appium:androidCoverage` and `appium:androidCoverageEndIntent` capabilities when running instrumented Android apps. This enables collecting E2E-level code coverage data alongside functional tests.

**Requirement:** The Android app must be built with JaCoCo instrumentation enabled (`testCoverageEnabled = true` in `build.gradle`) and must implement a coverage flush on the `endIntent`.

```groovy
// android/app/build.gradle — enable JaCoCo instrumentation
android {
    buildTypes {
        debug {
            testCoverageEnabled = true  // enables JaCoCo agent for debug builds
        }
    }
}
```

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — enable coverage collection during the E2E session
const androidCoverageCaps: WebdriverIO.Capabilities = {
  platformName: 'Android',
  'appium:automationName': 'UiAutomator2',
  'appium:deviceName': 'Pixel_7_API_33',
  'appium:app': process.env.ANDROID_APP_PATH!,  // must be a coverage-instrumented .apk
  // Coverage capabilities (UiAutomator2 driver)
  'appium:androidCoverage': 'com.example.myapp/com.example.myapp.InstrumentationCoverageRunner',
  'appium:androidCoverageEndIntent': 'com.example.myapp.END_EMMA',
};
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/mobile-coverage.yml — collect and report coverage
- name: Run E2E tests with coverage
  run: npx wdio run wdio.conf.ts
  env:
    ANDROID_APP_PATH: ./app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
    ENABLE_COVERAGE: 'true'

- name: Pull coverage file from device
  run: |
    adb pull /data/data/com.example.myapp/files/coverage.ec ./coverage/coverage.ec
    # Merge with unit test coverage
    java -jar jacococli.jar merge ./coverage/*.ec --destfile ./coverage/merged.ec
    java -jar jacococli.jar report ./coverage/merged.ec \
      --classfiles ./app/build/intermediates/javac/debug/classes \
      --sourcefiles ./app/src/main/java \
      --html ./coverage-report \
      --xml ./coverage-report/coverage.xml

- name: Upload coverage report
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: android-coverage
    path: coverage-report/
```

```typescript
// test/helpers/coverageHelper.ts — flush coverage at test boundaries

/**
 * Signal the Android app to flush JaCoCo coverage data to disk.
 * Call at the end of each test suite (not each test — flushing is slow).
 *
 * WHY: JaCoCo buffers coverage data in memory; if the app crashes or is force-
 * stopped without flushing, all coverage data is lost. Flushing at suite
 * boundaries ensures partial coverage is preserved even on test failures.
 */
export async function flushAndroidCoverage(packageName: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!browser.isAndroid || !process.env.ENABLE_COVERAGE) return;
  await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
    command: 'am',
    args: ['broadcast', '-a', `${packageName}.END_EMMA`],
  });
  // Wait for flush to complete — coverage file appears in app's files directory
  await browser.waitUntil(async () => {
    const result = await driver.execute('mobile: shell', {
      command: 'ls',
      args: [`/data/data/${packageName}/files/coverage.ec`],
    }) as string;
    return result.includes('coverage.ec');
  }, { timeout: 10_000, timeoutMsg: 'Coverage flush timed out after 10 s' });
}
```

```typescript
// wdio.conf.ts — flush coverage after each suite completes
import { flushAndroidCoverage } from './test/helpers/coverageHelper.js';

afterSuite: async (suite) => {
  await flushAndroidCoverage('com.example.myapp');
},
```

**JaCoCo / `appium:androidCoverage` gotchas [community]:**

1. **[community] `appium:androidCoverage` requires an instrumentation APK separate from the main app APK — using the production APK silently collects zero coverage:** WHY: JaCoCo coverage instrumentation is injected at compile time into the debug build variant when `testCoverageEnabled = true`. The production (release) APK is not instrumented; calling `appium:androidCoverage` with the release APK starts the session normally but the coverage runner class is not present in the APK, so no data is ever written to the coverage file. Fix: always point `appium:app` at the debug APK (`app-debug.apk`) when collecting coverage; add a CI step that verifies the APK contains the InstrumentationCoverageRunner class before running tests.

2. **[community] Coverage file path `/data/data/<package>/files/coverage.ec` is only accessible via `adb pull` if the app is debuggable:** WHY: Android scoped storage restricts file access for non-debuggable apps. The `adb pull` command runs as the `shell` user, which cannot access an app's private data directory unless the app has `android:debuggable="true"` in its manifest. Release APKs and distribution builds typically omit this flag. Fix: ensure the coverage APK is a debug build with `android:debuggable="true"`; alternatively, call `adb exec-out run-as com.example.myapp cat files/coverage.ec > coverage.ec` to read the file via the app's own user context.

3. **[community] JaCoCo merging fails when test and instrumentation APKs were compiled with different JDK versions:** WHY: JaCoCo's `jacococli.jar merge` command requires all `.ec` files to have been produced by the same JaCoCo agent version and format. If unit tests use JaCoCo 0.8.x and E2E tests use JaCoCo 0.8.y (where x ≠ y), the merge throws `IncompatibleClassFileFormatException: Incompatible exec data`. Fix: pin the JaCoCo version in both the `app/build.gradle` and the CI `jacococli.jar` download to the same exact version; use `./gradlew jacocoTestReport` rather than manual merging to let Gradle handle version consistency.

### Community Gotchas (iter 41)

**C70-1** — `appium:enforceAppInstall` combined with `appium:noReset: false` and a signed production keystore on Android API 34+ causes `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE` when the CI build has a lower `versionCode` than the previously installed debug build
Why this matters: On Android 14 (API 34), Google tightened the `adb install -r` behaviour: if the installed APK has a higher `versionCode` than the incoming APK, the install is rejected with `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE` — even for debug/development builds. In a typical trunk-based CI pipeline, the `versionCode` is set to `1` (or a static value) for debug APKs while the previously installed APK from a release pipeline might have `versionCode: 120`. `enforceAppInstall: true` forces the install even if the version matches, but it cannot override the downgrade protection. Appium throws `SessionNotCreatedException` with the error string `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE: Package specifies a version code that is already installed.` (the "already installed" suffix is misleading — it's actually a downgrade rejection). The error appears intermittently depending on whether the CI runner shared state across jobs.
Fix: Ensure debug builds always have a `versionCode` higher than any release build on the test device; in `build.gradle`, set `versionCode = System.currentTimeMillis().intdiv(1000)` for debug builds to guarantee monotonically increasing codes. Alternatively, add `adb uninstall com.example.myapp || true` as a CI setup step to remove all installed versions before running Appium; set `'appium:fullReset': true` (which runs `pm uninstall` via Appium) as the nuclear option, at the cost of a slower session creation.

**C70-2** — `browser.emulate('clock', { now: ... })` in a WDIO v9 hybrid app WebView test does not affect `new Date()` calls inside the **native** layer (Swift/Kotlin) — only the JavaScript WebView clock is frozen
Why this matters: Teams testing time-sensitive features (subscription expiry banners, countdown timers, "X days remaining" labels) use `browser.emulate('clock', { now: pastDate })` to simulate a specific point in time. In a React Native or hybrid app, the displayed date string is often rendered by native Swift/Kotlin code (via a `Date` formatter bridged from the native layer) rather than by JavaScript. `browser.emulate('clock')` only intercepts `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `Date` calls that occur in the WebView JavaScript context via the BiDi protocol — it has zero effect on native-layer date calls. The native label displays the real system time while the JS mock time is in the past, causing the test assertion to fail with a real date vs expected mock date mismatch that appears as a flaky test. The failure is intermittent because on fast CI machines the test finishes before the next minute change but on slow machines the real-clock minute differs from the mocked minute.
Fix: For native-layer time assertions, use `appium:settings` API to override the device system time (Android: `adb shell date MMDDhhmm[[CC]YY][.ss]`; iOS Simulator: `xcrun simctl spawn booted defaults write com.apple.preferences.clock UseSystemTimezone -bool false && ...`). Wrap the system time override in a fixture that restores the original time in an `after()` hook. For a cleaner approach, add a debug API to the app that accepts a mock timestamp header via its HTTP client interceptor, and set the header from the test using `browser.url({ headers: { 'X-Mock-Time': timestamp } })`.

**C70-3** — `appium:mjpegServerFramerate` set to a value above the physical screen refresh rate on some Android emulators causes the MJPEG server to emit duplicate frames, inflating video file sizes by 3–5x
Why this matters: If `appium:mjpegServerFramerate` is set to 30fps on an Android emulator running at 60Hz but the emulator's CPU is throttled (common in CI), the UiAutomator2 MJPEG server attempts to capture 30 frames per second but the screen renderer only produces unique frames every 100–200ms. The duplicate detection algorithm in the MJPEG encoder (introduced in UiAutomator2 v2.34) checks pixel-level hash equality with a 1ms debounce; on throttled emulators the CPU takes longer than 1ms to hash a full-resolution frame, so the debounce expires before the comparison completes and duplicate frames are emitted. A 60-second test run produces a 400–600MB video file instead of the expected 80–120MB. The CI job then fails not from a test error but from the artifact upload step hitting the 500MB size limit.
Fix: Set `appium:mjpegServerFramerate` to 5–10fps on CI (not 30fps); the human eye perceives smooth motion at 12fps so 10fps captures all meaningful state changes while reducing file size by 67%. Add a post-test video size check to CI: `[ $(stat -c%s recording.mp4) -gt 104857600 ] && echo "WARNING: recording exceeds 100MB — reduce mjpegServerFramerate" || true`. For UiAutomator2 v2.34+, the duplicate frame issue is fixed but CPU throttling still makes 30fps impractical in CI; keep the cap at 10fps regardless of driver version.
